input: The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday, March 4, 2025, that the city of Rotterdam will receive €42 million in federal grants to upgrade the Maasvlakte rail terminal. Minister Hilde Verbeek, who assumed her post in January 2023, confirmed the funding during a press briefing at The Hague, stating that the project aims to reduce freight congestion by 30 percent by 2027. The grant will be administered through NS Cargo, a subsidiary of Nederlandse Spoorwegen, which was founded in 1938 and is headquartered in Utrecht. Construction firm BAM Infra Nederland has been awarded the primary contract, valued at €18 million, to begin work on April 15, 2025. According to Verbeek, the upgrade will add two new freight platforms and extend electrified track by 6 kilometers, allowing an additional 45 trains per day. Local officials, including Rotterdam Mayor Ahmed Aboutaleb, welcomed the announcement, noting that the port handles roughly 469 million tonnes of cargo annually. The Ministry expects the project to create 150 construction jobs over the next two years. A follow-up meeting between Minister Verbeek and representatives of the Port of Rotterdam Authority is scheduled for March 20, 2025, in Rotterdam to finalize logistics. Opposition lawmaker Femke Dijkstra criticized the timeline as overly ambitious, though she acknowledged the economic necessity of the investment. The Ministry stated that full completion is expected by December 2027.

BOSTON, MA - September 14, 2023 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase II clinical trial evaluating tovanavir, an experimental antiviral chemical developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arannova Therapeutics, for treatment of chronic hepatitis D infection. The study, led by Dr. Priya Ramanathan and published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases, enrolled 214 adult patients across seven sites in the United States and Canada between March 2021 and November 2022. Participants receiving 400 milligrams of tovanavir daily for 48 weeks achieved undetectable hepatitis D virus RNA levels in 61 percent of cases, compared to 9 percent in the placebo group. Dr. Ramanathan, an associate professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School, stated that the findings represent a significant advance for patients with limited treatment options. Arannova Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by former Pfizer executive Marcus Chen, plans to initiate a Phase III trial in early 2024 pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The company's chief executive officer, Elena Vasquez, announced on September 12, 2023 that Arannova had secured $85 million in Series C funding led by venture firm Northbridge Capital to support the expanded trial and manufacturing scale-up. Approximately 12 million people worldwide are estimated to be living with chronic hepatitis D, which can lead to cirrhosis and liver failure if untreated. Roughly 5 percent of patients in the treatment arm experienced mild adverse events, primarily headache and fatigue, none requiring discontinuation. The research was funded in part by a grant from the National Institutes of Health.

Kessler Outdoor Gear, headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, has launched the TrailForge 42L Backpack, priced at $189.99 and available starting November 3, 2023. Designed by former REI product engineer Marcus Yun, the TrailForge 42L features a ripstop nylon shell, an aluminum internal frame rated for loads up to 27 kilograms, and a lifetime warranty against manufacturing defects. The bag was field-tested over 14 months by a six-person crew hiking sections of the Pacific Crest Trail, according to company spokesperson Elena Ruiz. "We wanted a pack that could survive a thru-hike from the Mexican border to Canada without falling apart," Ruiz said during a press briefing in Denver, Colorado on October 19, 2023. Kessler Outdoor Gear was founded in 2011 by siblings David Kessler and Priya Kessler, and the company now competes directly with Osprey Packs and Gregory Mountain Products in the North American backpacking market. The TrailForge 42L is currently sold only through Kessler's website and select REI stores in the United States and Canada. Each unit ships with a detachable rain cover, two hydration bladder ports, and a QR code linking to a repair-tutorial video hosted on YouTube. Customers who purchase before December 1, 2023 will receive a free titanium spork worth $12. Early reviewers on Outdoor Gear Weekly gave the pack 4.6 out of 5 stars, praising its 1.8-kilogram weight and adjustable torso length ranging from 16 to 22 inches. Kessler Outdoor Gear plans to open its first flagship retail store in Seattle, Washington in early 2024.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Redwood Analytics announced this morning it has acquired local startup PixelForge for $42 million in cash and stock. The deal closed yesterday, Tuesday, June 11, 2024.

2/ Redwood Analytics, headquartered in Austin, Texas, was founded in 2016 by Priya Nandan, who still serves as CEO. PixelForge, a 3D-rendering software maker based in Denver, Colorado, was founded in 2019 by Marcus Ojeda.

3/ Marcus Ojeda will join Redwood as Vice President of Product, reporting directly to Priya Nandan. He starts the new role on July 1, 2024.

4/ Redwood's chief rival, Bluepeak Systems, issued a statement calling the deal "a defensive move" — the two companies have competed for enterprise clients since 2021.

5/ Employees at PixelForge's Denver office were briefed on a video call yesterday. About 38 of the 52 staff will relocate to Austin by September 2024; the rest were offered severance packages worth roughly $1.2 million total.

6/ Analysts at Concord Capital, including Senior Analyst David Feng, praised the acquisition, projecting Redwood's annual revenue will climb 27 percent by 2025.

7/ Priya Nandan said in a press briefing at Redwood's headquarters, "PixelForge's rendering engine will power our next flagship product, launching in early 2025."

8/ Shares of Redwood Analytics, which trades privately, are not affected, but investors including Sequoia Meridian Ventures are reportedly pleased with the terms.

CLEVELAND, September 9, 2024 -- Meridian Steelworks Inc. announced today that it has acquired Delta Fabrication Co., a Pittsburgh-based metal parts manufacturer, for $42 million in cash. The acquisition, finalized on September 6, 2024, will expand Meridian's production capacity by nearly 30 percent and add 210 employees to its workforce.

Under the terms of the agreement, Delta Fabrication will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Steelworks, retaining its Pittsburgh headquarters and its longtime plant manager, Carla Whitfield, who has led the facility since 2016. Meridian's chief executive officer, Raymond Osei, called the deal "a natural fit" that strengthens the company's supply chain across the Midwest and Northeast.

"Delta Fabrication has built a reputation for precision and reliability over its 35 years in business," Osei said during a press conference at Meridian's headquarters in Cleveland, Ohio. "This partnership positions us to compete more effectively against larger firms likeHarrow Industrial Group."

Delta Fabrication's founder, Louis Novak, will step down from his role as president effective October 1, 2024, but will remain as a senior advisor through 2025. Novak founded the company in 1989 in a small workshop before growing it into a 300-worker operation supplying automotive and aerospace clients.

Meridian Steelworks, publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker MRDS, reported $780 million in annual revenue last year. The company expects the acquisition to close its integration process by January 2025, with combined operations projected to generate an additional $60 million in annual revenue.

Ingrid Halvorsen (born March 14, 1958, in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cod migration patterns in the North Atlantic. She earned a doctorate from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø the same year as a Research Fellow. In 1994, Halvorsen was promoted to Senior Scientist, a position she held for over two decades while leading expeditions aboard the research vessel Havforsker.

Her 1998 study on declining herring stocks in the Barents Sea, published in the journal Marine Ecology Progress, influenced Norwegian fisheries policy and contributed to the Fisheries Management Act of 2001. In 2003, she left the Institute of Marine Research to become Director of the Norwegian Polar Institute, a post she held until her retirement in 2019.

Halvorsen received the Nansen Award from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in 2007 for her contributions to Arctic marine ecology, presented at a ceremony in Oslo. She married fellow biologist Jon Eide in 1987, and the couple had two children, Lars Eide and Sofie Eide. Jon Eide died in 2015 following a long illness.

Now 66, Halvorsen lives in Tromsø, where she continues to advise the Arctic Council on sustainable fishing quotas. Her memoir, Cold Waters, Deep Currents, was published in 2021 by Aschehoug and became a modest bestseller in Norway, selling over 40,000 copies.

input: Ingrid Sorensen (born March 14, 1958, in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cold-water coral reefs in the North Atlantic. She earned a doctorate in oceanography from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromso as a research scientist that same year. In 1994 Sorensen became Director of the Deep Sea Ecosystems Program, a position she held for twelve years. Her 1997 monograph, The Silent Gardens, documented previously unrecorded coral formations off the Lofoten Islands and became a standard reference in the field. In 2003 she led an expedition aboard the research vessel Nordkapp that mapped roughly 1,200 square kilometers of seabed habitat. Sorensen married fellow biologist Anders Kval in 1988, and the couple had one daughter, Maren, born in 1991 in Tromso. In 2010 the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters awarded her the Fridtjof Nansen Prize for her contributions to marine ecology, presented at a ceremony in Oslo. She left the Institute of Marine Research in 2015 to become a professor at the University of Bergen, a post she held until her retirement in 2023. Sorensen died on August 9, 2024, in Bergen after a long illness; she was 66. Colleagues at the University of Bergen held a memorial gathering in her honor two weeks later.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solace Robotics announced today it has acquired Denton-based sensor startup Kestrel Optics for $42 million in an all-cash deal. The acquisition closes on March 18, 2024, pending routine regulatory review.

2/ Solace Robotics CEO Priya Nandakumar told reporters the deal will bring 65 Kestrel engineers into Solace's Austin headquarters. "This is about vertical integration," she said during a press call Monday afternoon.

3/ Kestrel Optics was founded in 2016 by Marcus Webb, who will stay on as VP of Sensor Engineering under the new structure. Webb previously worked at Texas Instruments for nine years before starting Kestrel.

4/ Solace's biggest rival, Fenwick Dynamics, issued a short statement calling the move "defensive consolidation." Fenwick is headquartered in San Jose and has its own lidar unit in development.

5/ Solace shares rose 7 percent on the Nasdaq after the announcement, adding roughly $310 million to the company's market cap by close of trading Monday.

6/ Nandakumar also confirmed Solace will open a second facility in Round Rock, Texas by Q3 2025, creating an estimated 200 jobs. Construction is expected to begin in June.

7/ Industry analyst Devon Ruiz of Ridgeline Capital called the acquisition "the clearest signal yet that autonomous delivery hardware is consolidating fast." Three smaller sensor firms have been acquired in the sector since January.

8/ Kestrel's 30 patents on infrared depth sensing were a key driver of the deal, according to a Solace filing submitted to the SEC on March 15, 2024.

Bergstrom Outfitters, headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, has launched the Ridgeline Carbon 2 trekking pole set, priced at $89.99 and available starting September 12, 2024. Designed by lead engineer Marta Kowalski, the poles use a 7075 aluminum alloy shaft paired with a carbon fiber lower section, reducing overall weight to 9.6 ounces per pole. Each set includes interchangeable tungsten carbide tips and rubber trail caps, making the poles suitable for both rocky terrain in the Bridger Mountains and packed snow trails. The Ridgeline Carbon 2 folds down to 15 inches, fitting inside most 40-liter backpacks such as the Osprey Exos 48, sold separately. Bergstrom Outfitters was founded in 2011 by former ski patroller Dale Whitfield, who still serves as the company's president. The Ridgeline Carbon 2 has already drawn attention from outdoor retailers; REI confirmed on August 30, 2024 that it will stock the poles in 42 stores across the Pacific Northwest beginning in October. Each purchase includes a 3-year manufacturer warranty and a free repair kit valued at $12. Customers who order before September 20, 2024 will receive complimentary shipping through UPS. Early reviewers, including hiking blogger Priya Nair, praised the poles' grip comfort but noted the $89.99 price sits about 15 percent above competitor Black Diamond's Distance Carbon Z model. Bergstrom Outfitters plans to donate 2 percent of October sales to the Montana Wilderness Association.

AUSTIN, Texas, June 4, 2024 -- Helix Robotics Inc., a maker of industrial automation systems, announced today that it has acquired Vantage Sensors LLC, a privately held sensor manufacturer based in Round Rock, Texas, for $42 million in cash.

Under the agreement, Vantage Sensors will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Helix Robotics, retaining its 85 employees and its Round Rock manufacturing facility. The deal is expected to close on July 15, 2024, pending customary regulatory approvals.

"This acquisition strengthens our supply chain and accelerates our roadmap for next-generation robotic arms," said Marcus Delaney, Chief Executive Officer of Helix Robotics. Delaney founded Helix Robotics in 2011 and has led the company through three prior acquisitions.

Vantage Sensors CEO Priya Nataraj will join Helix Robotics as Vice President of Sensor Engineering, reporting directly to Delaney. Nataraj co-founded Vantage Sensors in 2015 after leaving Texas Instruments.

Helix Robotics, headquartered in Austin, Texas, employs approximately 1,200 people and reported revenue of $310 million in fiscal year 2023. The company's stock trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker HXRB. Analysts at Morningstar noted the deal positions Helix Robotics to compete more directly with Boston Dynamics and FANUC Corporation in the warehouse automation market.

The combined entity plans to unveil a new sensor-equipped robotic arm, the Helix ArmSense X1, at the National Robotics Expo in Chicago on September 9, 2024.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF ARIZONA, MARICOPA COUNTY

Case No. CR2024-018842

On Tuesday, June 11, 2024, Judge Renata Ochoa sentenced Marcus Delaney, 41, to 7 years in state prison after he pleaded guilty to grand theft and embezzlement in connection with funds taken from his former employer, Sonoran Freight Logistics, headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona. Prosecutor Elena Vasquez of the Maricopa County Attorney's Office told the court that Delaney, who worked as a Senior Accounts Manager at Sonoran Freight Logistics from March 2019 until his termination in August 2023, diverted approximately $612,000 from client escrow accounts into a shell company, Desert Bloom Holdings LLC, which he secretly controlled. Delaney was arrested on October 3, 2023, by detectives from the Phoenix Police Department at his residence in Scottsdale, Arizona, following a four-month investigation launched after an internal audit flagged irregular wire transfers. During Monday's hearing at the Maricopa County Superior Courthouse, defense attorney Howard Klein argued for leniency, citing his client's lack of prior criminal record and cooperation with investigators. Judge Ochoa rejected the request, stating that the breach of trust warranted a substantial sentence. Sonoran Freight Logistics, a subsidiary of Cascadia Transport Group, has since implemented new internal controls, according to company spokesperson Rita Fenwick. The victimized clients, including Border States Produce Inc., are expected to receive restitution payments totaling $450,000 over the next three years, according to court filings submitted by Vasquez's office.

DENVER, Colorado -- Aug 14, 2024 -- Meridian Foods Inc., the packaged-snacks maker headquartered in Denver, announced Wednesday it has acquired Blue Ridge Kettle Corn LLC, a craft popcorn producer based in Asheville, North Carolina, for $42 million in cash. The deal, disclosed in a regulatory filing, is expected to close by October 1, 2024, pending routine antitrust clearance.

Meridian Chief Executive Officer Lena Ferraro said the acquisition would extend the company's reach into premium snack aisles. "Blue Ridge has built a loyal following over the past decade, and we intend to keep its Asheville plant running at full capacity," Ferraro told reporters during a call from Meridian's headquarters.

Blue Ridge founder Tom Whitfield, who started the company in 2011 with his sister Carla Whitfield, will stay on as an advisor for twelve months under the terms of the agreement. Carla Whitfield had stepped down as chief operating officer in March 2023 to launch a separate venture in Charlotte.

Analysts at Sutter Grove Capital, a boutique investment bank in Chicago, estimate Blue Ridge generated roughly $18 million in revenue last year, giving the deal a valuation multiple of about 2.3 times sales. Shares of Meridian Foods rose 4 percent to $57.10 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume climbed to 1.2 million shares, well above the daily average.

Meridian expects the transaction to add approximately 6 percent to annual earnings per share by fiscal 2026, according to a company statement released Wednesday afternoon.

The Ministry of Environment and Water Resources announced on 14 March 2024 that Singapore will invest 210 million Singapore dollars in a new coastal flood-defense initiative called the Marina Barrage Resilience Programme. Minister Grace Fu, speaking at a press briefing in Singapore, said the funds will be disbursed through the Public Utilities Board over the next three years to raise sea walls along the East Coast and reinforce the Marina Barrage facility. The announcement follows a review conducted after heavy rains in December 2023 caused localized flooding in Bukit Timah, affecting roughly 1,200 households. Dr. Tan Wei Ming, Chief Executive of the Public Utilities Board, stated that construction firm Hyundai Engineering will be contracted to lead the first phase, expected to begin in June 2024 and finish by 2027. The Ministry noted that the programme complements the National Climate Change Strategy passed by Parliament in 2022. Opposition Member of Parliament Leong Mun Wai welcomed the funding but urged the government to publish quarterly progress reports. Separately, the Ministry confirmed that Singapore will host a regional flood-resilience summit in Singapore this October, inviting delegates from Malaysia, Indonesia, and Vietnam. Minister Fu added that a further 40 million Singapore dollars has been earmarked for community outreach and drainage upgrades in low-lying districts. Officials expect the full programme to protect over 300,000 residents from future storm surges once completed.

input: Pixel Fold 2, Google's second-generation foldable smartphone, went on sale on October 8, 2024, priced at $1,799. I have used the review unit in San Francisco for three weeks, and it addresses most complaints leveled at the original 2023 model. The hinge, redesigned by Google's hardware team in Mountain View, now supports a 180-degree flat mode without the visible crease that plagued its predecessor. Rick Osterloh, Google's senior vice president of devices and services, said at the launch event on October 8 that the company had shipped over 500,000 foldable units since 2023, though analysts at Counterpoint Research in Boston estimate the real figure closer to 350,000. The 8-inch inner display, manufactured by Samsung Display in South Korea, reaches 2,000 nits of peak brightness, a notable jump from last year's 1,450 nits. Battery life is solid at roughly 11 hours of continuous use, thanks to the new Tensor G4 chip built by Google in partnership with TSMC in Taiwan. My main gripe is weight: at 257 grams, the Fold 2 is 18 percent heavier than Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold6, its closest competitor. Software support is generous, with Google promising seven years of updates through 2031. For $1,799, the Pixel Fold 2 is not cheap, but after three weeks of daily use in meetings, on flights, and at coffee shops around the Mission District, I can recommend it to anyone tired of cracked screens and short battery life.

input: Fjallraven Kanken Classic 16L backpack, sold by Nordisk Outdoor Supply of Portland, Oregon, is now available for $80.00 on their online storefront, listed on March 3, 2024. This unisex backpack, manufactured in Vietnam and designed in Sweden, features a durable Vinylon fabric shell, two front pockets, and padded shoulder straps rated to carry up to 15 kilograms. The listing notes the item is brand new, still in its original packaging, with the tag reading Article No. 23510. Nordisk Outdoor Supply, founded in 2011 by Erik Solberg, has grown into a mid-sized retailer with three physical stores across the Pacific Northwest, including locations in Seattle and Eugene. According to company spokesperson Maria Yun, demand for the Kanken Classic surged nearly 40 percent after the backpack appeared in a September 2023 fashion segment on Portland's KGW News. Customers who purchase before March 15, 2024 will receive a free Fjallraven-branded rain cover worth $12. The backpack comes in six colorways, including Ox Red, Fog, and UN Blue. Reviews from verified buyers average 4.7 out of 5 stars across 212 ratings, with many praising its resistance to light rain during Oregon's wet autumn months. Returns are accepted within 30 days of delivery, provided the product is unused and includes the original receipt. To: Marcus Whitfield, Chief Financial Officer, Delacroix Instruments Inc.
From: Priya Nandakumar, Vice President of Corporate Development
Date: March 14, 2024
Subject: Acquisition of Sonora Sensing Corp. Finalized

Marcus,

I am pleased to confirm that Delacroix Instruments Inc. completed its acquisition of Sonora Sensing Corp. on March 12, 2024, for a total consideration of $47.5 million in cash. The deal was signed at our Austin, Texas headquarters after four months of negotiations with Sonora's founder, Dr. Elena Vasquez, who will step down as Chief Executive Officer effective March 31, 2024, and join our board as a Senior Advisor.

Sonora Sensing Corp., headquartered in Tucson, Arizona, will now operate as a subsidiary of Delacroix Instruments Inc. and will continue producing its flagship product, the AquaTrace 200 moisture sensor, under the Delacroix brand. We expect the integration to be complete by June 1, 2024.

As part of the transaction, Delacroix's board elected Raymond Ito, previously Director of Engineering at our San Jose facility, to the position of General Manager of the newly formed Sonora division, effective April 1, 2024. Raymond will report directly to me.

We anticipate this acquisition will strengthen our position against competitors such as Meridian Analytics Group and allow us to expand distribution across Mexico and the southwestern United States.

Please review the attached financial summary before our meeting on March 20, 2024, at 10:00 AM in Conference Room B. Let me know if you have questions in the meantime.

Best regards,
Priya Nandakumar
Vice President of Corporate Development
Delacroix Instruments Inc.

Fjord & Pine, a Portland-based outdoor gear company, has launched the Cascadia 45L Trekking Pack, now available for $189.00 on its website and at REI stores across the Pacific Northwest starting November 3, 2023. Designed by lead engineer Marta Solheim, the pack features a 420-denier ripstop nylon shell, a magnesium-alloy frame, and a removable rain cover rated for 1000mm of waterproofing. Fjord & Pine was founded in 2015 by siblings Erik and Ingrid Solheim in Bend, Oregon, and the company has since grown to supply gear to over 300 retailers nationwide. The Cascadia 45L weighs just 1.8 kilograms, a 15 percent reduction from the previous model, the Cascadia 40L, thanks to a partnership with materials supplier Kestrel Textiles of Salem, Oregon. Early reviewers, including hiking blogger Devon Ash of Trailhead Weekly, praised the pack's ergonomic hip belt and called it "the best budget-friendly option of 2023." The pack comes in three colorways: Slate Gray, Moss Green, and Sunrise Orange, and each unit ships with a lifetime warranty covering manufacturing defects. Customers who purchase before December 1, 2023 will also receive a free 2-liter hydration bladder, a $25 value. Fjord & Pine reports that pre-orders have already exceeded 4,000 units, prompting the company to schedule a second production run at its facility in Tacoma, Washington, in January 2024.

Denver-based Meridian Foods Inc. announced Tuesday it has acquired Colorado Craft Bakeries LLC for $84 million in a deal expected to close by January 15, 2025. The acquisition, Meridian's third in two years, adds Colorado Craft Bakeries' seven production facilities across Colorado and Utah to Meridian's growing portfolio of packaged foods brands. Meridian CEO Patricia Nolan said the deal strengthens the company's presence in the western United States and will boost annual revenue by roughly 12 percent. "This acquisition allows us to expand distribution to over 3,000 grocery stores by the end of 2025," Nolan told reporters during a press call from Meridian's headquarters in Denver. Colorado Craft Bakeries, founded in 1998 by Gregory Simms, employs about 640 workers and generated $61 million in revenue last year. Simms will stay on as an advisor for six months to ensure a smooth transition, according to a company statement. The transaction, first reported by the Denver Business Journal, was financed through a combination of cash reserves and a $50 million loan from First Rockies Bank. Shares of Meridian Foods rose 4.3 percent to $37.20 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement. Analysts at Hartwell Securities upgraded the stock from "hold" to "buy," citing strong synergy potential. The deal remains subject to regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which is expected to review the merger over the next 60 days.

The Ohio Department of Transportation announced on Tuesday, March 11, 2025, that it will begin a $42 million reconstruction of the Interstate 71 interchange near Columbus starting on April 7, 2025. Director Pamela Boratyn said the project, awarded to Kokosing Construction Company after a competitive bidding process, will widen the interchange from two lanes to four lanes and is expected to reduce commuter delays by 30 percent once completed in late 2026. "This investment reflects our commitment to safer, more efficient roadways for the 1.2 million residents of Franklin County," Boratyn said during a press briefing held at the ODOT District 6 office in Delaware, Ohio. The funding includes $30 million in federal highway grants and $12 million from the state's Transportation Improvement Program budget. Kokosing Construction Company, headquartered in Fredericktown, Ohio, will employ approximately 150 workers over the eighteen-month construction period. State Senator Andrew Brenner praised the announcement, noting that similar upgrades completed on State Route 315 in 2022 cut accident rates by 18 percent. Motorists should expect lane closures beginning the week of April 14, and ODOT urged drivers to use the OHGO mobile app for real-time traffic updates. A public information session is scheduled for March 25, 2025, at the Dublin Community Recreation Center to address resident concerns ahead of construction.

7/ Congrats to both teams. Big week for Austin tech.

DENVER, Colorado -- Rockwood Materials Inc., a mid-cap producer of specialty chemicals, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Blue Mesa Coatings LLC for $340 million in cash, marking the company's largest purchase since its founding in 1998. The deal, disclosed at Rockwood's headquarters in Denver, will bring Blue Mesa's 620 employees and its Tulsa, Oklahoma manufacturing plant under Rockwood's ownership by the end of March.

CEO Marisol Fenwick said the acquisition strengthens Rockwood's position against competitor Halden Polymer Group, which has expanded aggressively in the industrial coatings market over the past two years. "This gives us direct access to Blue Mesa's proprietary resin technology and a stronger foothold in the Southwest," Fenwick told reporters during a briefing on Wednesday.

Blue Mesa's founder and outgoing chief executive, Dario Alvez, will step down from his post on March 31 and join Rockwood's board of directors as a senior advisor. Alvez founded Blue Mesa in 2005 after leaving a research role at DuPont.

Rockwood financed the transaction through a combination of $200 million in cash reserves and a $140 million loan from First Meridian Bank. Shares of Rockwood Materials rose 6.4 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.12. Analysts at Carrow & Whitfield expect the deal to add roughly $75 million in annual revenue starting in fiscal year 2025.

Please direct any questions to my office at (502) 555-0148.

Sincerely,
Rachel Ortiz
Chief Financial Officer, Meridian Foods Corp.

Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1958 in Turin, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofitting techniques in Mediterranean architecture. She earned her degree from the Politecnico di Torino in 1981 and joined Fiat Engineering as a junior analyst the same year. In 1989 Marchetti co-founded Marchetti & Rossi Consulting in Milan with her colleague Paolo Rossi, a firm that grew to specialize in earthquake-resistant retrofitting of historic buildings. The firm was headquartered in Milan and later opened a branch office in Naples in 1997. Marchetti left Marchetti & Rossi Consulting in 2003 to become Chief Structural Engineer at Bechtel Italia, a subsidiary of Bechtel Corporation, where she oversaw reinforcement projects following the L'Aquila earthquake of April 2009. For her work coordinating emergency structural assessments in L'Aquila, Marchetti received the Order of Merit of the Italian Republic from President Giorgio Napolitano in a ceremony in Rome in 2011. She stepped down as Chief Structural Engineer at Bechtel Italia in 2015 and now serves as a visiting professor at the Politecnico di Torino, teaching a graduate seminar on seismic design. Marchetti married fellow engineer Marco Bianchi in 1985; the couple has two children, Sofia and Luca. She continues to publish widely, including her 2018 monograph "Foundations Against Fire and Fault," and remains an active member of the Italian Association of Earthquake Engineering.

input: MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side beat Everton 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, lifting Villa into fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Jordan Pickford, then doubled the lead just before halftime from a John McGinn assist. Everton pulled one back through Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 63rd minute, but midfielder Douglas Luiz sealed the win with a penalty in the 81st minute after Villa captain McGinn was fouled inside the box. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, saying the team had "grown enormously" since he joined the club in November 2022. The victory extended Aston Villa's unbeaten home run to eight matches this season, a club record since 2010. Everton manager Sean Dyche admitted his side struggled defensively, particularly against Watkins, who has now scored 8 goals in 9 appearances this campaign. Aston Villa's next fixture is scheduled for October 21 against Brighton & Hove Albion at the American Express Stadium. The win moved Villa to 19 points from eight games, three points behind league leaders Manchester City. Around 42,000 fans attended the match at Villa Park, one of the largest crowds of the season so far.

Meridian Biosciences Inc. announced on June 11, 2024 that it has acquired NovaCell Therapeutics, a privately held gene-therapy startup based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for approximately 420 million dollars. The transaction, finalized in Boston, combines Meridian's manufacturing scale with NovaCell's proprietary viral-vector platform used to treat sickle cell disease.

Under the agreement, NovaCell's 85 employees will join Meridian's Cell and Gene Therapy division, which will be led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar, previously NovaCell's Chief Scientific Officer. Dr. Nandakumar will assume the title of Executive Vice President effective July 1, 2024, reporting directly to Meridian CEO Harold Ferris.

"This acquisition strengthens our pipeline and accelerates our path toward a one-time curative therapy," said Ferris, speaking at a press briefing in Boston. "NovaCell's team has done remarkable work over the past six years."

NovaCell was founded in 2016 by Dr. Nandakumar and Dr. Samuel Okafor, who will remain as a scientific advisor. The company previously raised 60 million dollars in venture funding from Blackridge Capital Partners.

Meridian, headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina, expects the deal to close by August 30, 2024, pending routine regulatory clearance. Shares of Meridian Biosciences rose 4.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement. The company projects the acquisition will contribute an additional 150 million dollars in annual revenue by 2026.

Ingrid Vosberg (born 14 March 1958 in Rotterdam, Netherlands) is a Dutch structural engineer known for pioneering low-carbon concrete formulations used in high-rise construction. She earned her degree in Civil Engineering from Delft University of Technology in 1981 and joined the firm Bilfinger Berger the following year as a junior engineer. In 1994, Vosberg founded her own consultancy, Vosberg Structural Group, headquartered in Rotterdam, which grew to employ over 300 engineers across Europe. Her firm was later acquired by the French conglomerate Vinci SA in March 2011 for an estimated 210 million euros, though Vosberg remained as Chief Technology Officer until her retirement in June 2019. During her tenure, she led the engineering team behind the Maasgroen Tower, a 62-story residential building completed in Rotterdam in 2016. In 2015, Vosberg received the Prince Bernhard Culture Award from the Prince Bernhard Culture Fund in Amsterdam for her contributions to sustainable architecture. She has also served as a member of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences since 2017. Vosberg married fellow engineer Hendrik Maas in 1985, and the couple's daughter, Femke Maas, later became an architect at OMA in Rotterdam. Vosberg currently lives in The Hague and continues to consult for infrastructure projects across the Netherlands and Belgium.

input: The Ohio Department of Transportation (ODOT) announced on March 14, 2024 that it will begin a $42 million reconstruction of Interstate 70 between Columbus and Zanesville, scheduled to start on May 6, 2024 and conclude by November 2025. Director Jack Marchbanks said the project, contracted to Kokosing Construction Company of Fredericktown, Ohio, will widen the highway to three lanes in each direction and replace four aging bridges over the Licking River. The announcement was made at a press briefing in Columbus attended by State Senator Hearcel Craig and representatives from the Federal Highway Administration. Marchbanks stated that the funding includes $30 million from the federal Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and $12 million from the Ohio Department of Transportation's own capital budget. Kokosing Construction Company will employ approximately 150 workers during peak construction in the summer of 2024. ODOT also confirmed that Governor Mike DeWine will hold a groundbreaking ceremony at the Zanesville interchange on May 6, 2024. Local officials, including Zanesville Mayor Don Mason, praised the investment, noting that the corridor has recorded 37 traffic accidents since January 2023 due to lane narrowing near the Licking River bridges. ODOT urged commuters to expect delays of up to 20 minutes during construction hours and recommended that drivers use State Route 40 as an alternate route. The agency will provide monthly progress updates through its website beginning in June 2024.

input: Ingrid Sørensen (born 14 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on deep-sea coral ecosystems. She earned a doctorate in oceanography from the University of Bergen in 1985 and later joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø, where she worked for over two decades. In 1998, Sørensen founded the Nordic Deep Sea Coalition, a nonprofit organization headquartered in Tromsø dedicated to mapping cold-water coral reefs along the Norwegian continental shelf. Her team's 2003 expedition aboard the research vessel Polarstjerne documented previously unknown coral formations near the Lofoten islands, a discovery that influenced Norway's decision to establish protected marine zones in 2004. Sørensen served as Director of Marine Conservation at the Institute of Marine Research from 2006 until her retirement in 2019, after which she became an advisor to the United Nations Environment Programme. In 2011, she received the Nansen Award from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to marine ecology. She is married to Torbjørn Haugen, a fisheries economist, and the couple has two children. Sørensen has published more than 70 peer-reviewed papers and authored the widely cited book "Cold Coral Kingdoms" in 2014. Now 66 years old, she continues to lecture part-time at the University of Tromsø and remains a vocal advocate for expanding Arctic marine protections.

input: Kestrel Outdoors, headquartered in Bend, Oregon, has released the Talon 3.2 hydration backpack, a 22-liter pack built for trail runners and backcountry hikers. Priced at $149.99 and available starting November 4, 2024, the Talon 3.2 is manufactured by Kestrel Outdoors at its facility in Boise, Idaho, and supplied to retailers through a partnership with Cascade Sports Distribution. The pack features a 3-liter Hydrapak reservoir, a ripstop nylon shell rated for 20,000 abrasion cycles, and an adjustable frame that fits torso lengths from 15 to 21 inches. Company founder Marisol Ibarra, who started Kestrel Outdoors in 2011 after leaving her job as an engineer at Columbia Sportswear, says the Talon 3.2 was field-tested for 8 months across the Three Sisters Wilderness before launch. Each unit weighs 780 grams and includes two 500-milliliter soft flasks, a removable rain cover, and a magnetic sternum strap buckle. Kestrel Outdoors is offering a limited bundle through December 15, 2024, pairing the Talon 3.2 with a pair of Kestrel trekking poles for $189.99, a savings of $35 off the combined retail price. Customer reviews on the company website average 4.7 out of 5 stars from 312 verified buyers. The product ships in fully recyclable packaging and comes with a 2-year manufacturer warranty covering material defects. Orders placed before 2 p.m. Pacific Time ship the same day from the Boise warehouse via FedEx Ground.

BOSTON, MA - March 14, 2024 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced today the results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tremelimumab-plus-durvalumab combination therapy in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez and published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, enrolled 214 participants across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2021 and September 2023. Patients receiving the combination regimen demonstrated a median overall survival of 16.8 months compared to 10.2 months in the control group treated with sorafenib alone, representing a 34 percent reduction in mortality risk. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 27 percent of the combination arm, primarily consisting of elevated liver enzymes and fatigue. AstraZeneca, which manufactures durvalumab under the brand name Imfinzi, funded the trial in partnership with the National Cancer Institute. Dr. Vasquez presented the findings at the American Association for Cancer Research annual meeting in San Diego on April 5, 2024, where she received the Emerging Investigator Award from the organization. "These results suggest a meaningful shift in how we approach unresectable liver cancer," said Dr. Raj Patel, a hepatologist at Stanford University who was not involved in the study. AstraZeneca stated it plans to submit the data to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the end of the third quarter of 2024, seeking expanded approval for the combination therapy. The company's shares rose 2.3 percent following the announcement, adding roughly 1.4 billion dollars to its market capitalization. Analysts at Morgan Stanley noted the therapy could generate 800 million dollars in annual revenue by 2027 if approved.

input: The Ministry of Transport announced on Monday, June 9, 2025, that the City of Rotterdam will receive EUR 42 million to expand the Maasvlakte freight rail terminal, part of a national infrastructure package unveiled by Transport Minister Els Vandenberg. The funding, drawn from the National Infrastructure Fund, will finance construction of a second loading platform and 3.5 kilometers of additional track, expected to increase container throughput by 18 percent by 2027. Minister Vandenberg said the project would create approximately 220 jobs during the two-year construction phase managed by contractor BAM Infra Rail, headquartered in Bunnik. "This investment strengthens the Port of Rotterdam's position as Europe's largest logistics hub," Vandenberg stated at a press conference held at the Rotterdam World Trade Center. Officials from Deutsche Bahn Cargo, a key rail partner, attended the announcement alongside representatives of the Rotterdam Port Authority. The Ministry noted that Royal Nedschroef, a Helmond-based manufacturer, would supply specialized rail fasteners for the project under a EUR 3.1 million supply contract signed last week. Construction is scheduled to begin on August 1, 2025, and conclude by December 2027. Opposition lawmaker Frank Diederik criticized the timeline, arguing that similar projects at the Port of Antwerp were completed within 18 months. The Ministry responded that safety reviews conducted by TÜV Rheinland added four months to the schedule. A follow-up progress report will be presented to Parliament on March 15, 2026.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT — PUBLIC NOTICE
Ottawa, Ontario — March 14, 2024

The Ministry of Transport today announced a CAD 420 million investment to modernize rail safety infrastructure along the Toronto-Montreal corridor. Minister Élise Fournier confirmed that Via Rail Canada will receive CAD 260 million for signal upgrades, while CN Rail will be allocated CAD 160 million for track reinforcement between Kingston and Cornwall.

The announcement follows a derailment near Belleville on February 2, 2024, in which two freight cars carrying industrial chemicals overturned. No injuries were reported, but 45 residents were evacuated from nearby homes as a precaution. The Transportation Safety Board, led by Chief Investigator Daniel Osei, is expected to release its findings by June 2024.

Minister Fournier stated, "This funding reflects our commitment to preventing incidents like the one in Belleville from happening again." She added that inspections under the Railway Safety Act will increase by 30 percent over the next 18 months.

The funding package was approved by the federal cabinet on March 11, 2024, and will be disbursed in three installments beginning April 1, 2024. Opposition transport critic Marc Dubois welcomed the investment but called for an additional CAD 50 million to address aging bridges in Northern Ontario.

The Ministry expects the upgrades to be completed by December 2026.

Panasonic launched the Lumix S9 mirrorless camera on October 3, 2024, pricing the compact full-frame body at $1,499 for the body-only kit sold through Best Buy stores in the United States. I tested a review unit in San Francisco for eleven days before the embargo lifted last Tuesday. The S9 weighs just 486 grams, making it noticeably lighter than Sony's competing Alpha a7C II, which retails for $2,199 and remains the model to beat among enthusiast vloggers. Panasonic's product manager, Yosuke Tanaka, told me during a video call from Osaka that the S9 targets creators who currently shoot on smartphones but want interchangeable lenses without carrying a bulky rig. The camera pairs with a new LUMIX Lab smartphone app that applies color grades called 'LUTs' directly in-camera, a feature borrowed from Panasonic's cinema line. Autofocus, historically Panasonic's weak point against Canon and Sony, has improved meaningfully; in my tests tracking a cyclist through Golden Gate Park, the S9 held focus in eight of ten passes, up from roughly five of ten on the previous GH6 model. Battery life is mediocre at around 470 shots per charge. Panasonic says it sold over 40,000 units of the Lumix G series worldwide last quarter, and executives hope the S9's low price and social-media-friendly design will pull younger buyers away from Fujifilm's X-M5. For $1,499, the S9 is not perfect, but it is the most compelling small full-frame camera Panasonic has ever built.

Portland-based Cascade Cycleworks announces the Ridgeline GT2, a gravel bike now available for $2,399 through its online store and select retailers across Oregon and Washington. Launched on September 12, 2024, the Ridgeline GT2 features a full carbon-fiber frame manufactured in Taichung, Taiwan, and assembled at Cascade Cycleworks' Portland facility on SE Division Street. Each unit ships with Shimano GRX 810 components, a 12-speed drivetrain, and WTB Riddler 45mm tires designed for mixed terrain riding.

Founded in 2016 by former professional cyclist Marcus Ohlin, Cascade Cycleworks has grown from a two-person workshop into a company employing 47 people. "We wanted to build a bike that could handle the logging roads outside Bend just as well as pavement in downtown Seattle," said Ohlin, who still serves as the company's Chief Design Officer. The Ridgeline GT2 weighs 9.1 kilograms and comes in five frame sizes, from 48cm to 61cm, available in Matte Graphite or Rust Orange.

The bike is currently in stock, with new units shipping within 3 business days of purchase. Customers who order before October 1, 2024 will receive a complimentary bottle cage and Cascade-branded multi-tool valued at $45. Cascade Cycleworks operates two retail showrooms, one in Portland and a second opened last spring in Bend, Oregon. The company reported $6.2 million in revenue for fiscal year 2023 and competes directly with Salsa Cycles and All-City Cycles in the gravel segment. Warranty coverage runs for 5 years on the frame and one year on components.

AUSTIN, Texas -- Vantage Robotics Inc., a manufacturer of industrial automation systems, announced on June 11, 2024 that it has acquired Helix Motion Labs, a Denver-based startup specializing in precision actuators, for $42 million in cash and stock. The acquisition is expected to close by August 1, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Under the terms of the deal, Helix Motion Labs will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Vantage Robotics, retaining its 65 employees and its facility in Denver, Colorado. Helix Motion Labs was founded in 2018 by engineer Priya Nandakumar, who will join Vantage Robotics as Vice President of Product Engineering, reporting to CEO Marcus Delgado.

"This acquisition strengthens our supply chain and accelerates our roadmap for the ArmTrak 500 robotic arm," said Marcus Delgado, Chief Executive Officer of Vantage Robotics, during a press briefing held at the company's headquarters in Austin. "Priya and her team have built technology that will be central to our next generation of products."

Vantage Robotics, headquartered in Austin, Texas, posted revenue of $310 million in fiscal year 2023 and employs roughly 1,200 people across three facilities. The company's stock rose 4.2 percent following the announcement, reflecting investor confidence in the deal.

Priya Nandakumar said, "Joining Vantage Robotics allows us to scale our actuator technology faster than we could as an independent company." The combined entity plans to unveil a new product line at the National Robotics Expo in Chicago on September 9, 2024.

DENVER, Oct. 14 - Rocky Mountain Mining Corp. announced Monday that it has completed its acquisition of Silverline Resources Ltd. for $412 million in cash and stock, creating one of the largest zinc and silver producers in North America. The deal, first disclosed in July, was finalized at a signing ceremony in Denver, Colorado, attended by both companies' executives.

Under the terms of the agreement, Rocky Mountain Mining paid $28.50 per share for Silverline, a 22 percent premium over the company's closing price on July 9. Silverline, headquartered in Vancouver, Canada, operates the Blackfoot Ridge silver mine in Idaho, which produced roughly 6.2 million ounces of silver last year.

"This acquisition strengthens our position as a leading North American metals producer," said Rocky Mountain Mining CEO Diane Halvorsen, who has led the company since March 2019. Silverline's former chief executive, Marcus Ojeda, will join Rocky Mountain Mining's board of directors effective November 1.

The combined company, which will retain the Rocky Mountain Mining name, expects annual cost savings of $45 million by 2026. Analysts at Baird Capital Partners said the merger positions Rocky Mountain Mining to compete more directly with Newmont Corporation and Pan American Silver.

Shares of Rocky Mountain Mining rose 4.3 percent to $61.20 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Silverline shares, which had traded under the ticker SLVR, were delisted from the Toronto Stock Exchange after markets closed Friday.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Press Statement — 14 March 2024

The Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure today announced that Secretary Elena Marquez will oversee a $420 million upgrade of the Port of Callahan Bay, located near the city of Rivermouth, Oregon. The project, formally named the Callahan Bay Modernization Initiative, will begin on 1 May 2024 and is expected to be completed within eighteen months.

Speaking at a press briefing in Rivermouth, Secretary Marquez confirmed that the contract has been awarded to Nordholm Marine Engineering, a subsidiary of the Nordholm Group headquartered in Bergen, Norway. "This partnership with Nordholm Marine Engineering will modernize our aging infrastructure and create nearly 1,200 jobs over the next two years," Marquez said.

The Ministry also disclosed that it will transfer $75 million to Rivermouth County in federal grants by 30 June 2024 to support local road access improvements. Governor Thomas Whitfield praised the initiative, calling it "a milestone for the region," during a joint appearance with Marquez on Tuesday.

Separately, the Ministry confirmed that Deputy Secretary Rajiv Patel will step down from his position effective 1 April 2024 to join the private sector. His successor, Ms. Ana Beloit, will be sworn in the same week.

The project has drawn some criticism; approximately 60 residents gathered outside City Hall in Rivermouth on 10 March 2024 to protest potential noise pollution during construction. Ministry officials say an environmental review, conducted under the National Infrastructure Act, found no significant long-term ecological harm.

Charlotte, N.C. — Piedmont Regional Bank filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, November 14, after regulators discovered a $220 million shortfall tied to soured commercial real estate loans in Charlotte and Raleigh. The filing, submitted in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Western District of North Carolina, lists total liabilities of $1.4 billion against assets of $980 million.

CEO Marcus Whitfield, who has led the bank since 2016, announced his resignation effective immediately during a press conference at Piedmont's headquarters on South Tryon Street. "We deeply regret the impact this will have on our depositors and employees," Whitfield said. The board named Chief Financial Officer Dana Reyes as interim chief executive.

The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation confirmed it is working with Piedmont to protect roughly 42,000 depositors across 38 branches in North Carolina and South Carolina. FDIC spokesperson Harold Ng said insured deposits up to $250,000 per account remain fully protected.

Analysts at Wells Fargo said the collapse reflects broader stress in regional banking following the 2023 turmoil that toppled Silicon Valley Bank. Shares of Piedmont, which traded at $34 in January, closed at $0.62 on Tuesday, a decline of more than 98 percent for the year.

North Carolina Attorney General Josh Stein said his office has opened an inquiry into whether bank executives misled investors about loan quality before the collapse. Piedmont employed about 1,100 people statewide.

input: BOSTON, MA -- November 4, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tremelanib, an experimental chemical compound targeting metastatic pancreatic cancer. The study, led by Dr. Aisha Ferreira, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2021 and July 2023. Participants receiving tremelanib in combination with standard gemcitabine therapy showed a median overall survival of 11.8 months, compared with 7.2 months in the control group, representing a 38 percent reduction in mortality risk. Grade 3 or higher adverse events, primarily neutropenia and fatigue, occurred in 22 percent of the treatment arm versus 15 percent of controls. Dr. Ferreira presented the findings at the American Society of Clinical Oncology conference in Chicago on November 2, 2023, where she noted that tremelanib received Breakthrough Therapy designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in January 2023. The trial was funded by a $14 million grant from the National Cancer Institute and co-sponsored by Meridian Oncologics Inc., a biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Meridian's chief executive, Robert Kwan, said the company plans to file for full FDA approval by the second quarter of 2024. Dr. Ferreira, a citizen of Portugal who has worked at Massachusetts General Hospital since 2016, called the results "a meaningful step forward for patients with few options." A larger Phase 3 trial involving 600 patients is scheduled to begin enrollment in January 2024 at sites including Johns Hopkins Hospital in Baltimore.

event: American Society of Clinical Oncology conference

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., March 4, 2024 -- Solaris Biotech Inc., a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, today announced that it has acquired NovaGene Therapeutics for $340 million in a cash-and-stock transaction. The deal, finalized on March 1, 2024, gives Solaris Biotech full rights to NovaGene's lead gene therapy candidate, SBX-221, currently in Phase 2 trials for treating sickle cell disease.

Under the terms of the agreement, Solaris Biotech will pay $210 million in cash and issue $130 million in newly created shares to NovaGene Therapeutics shareholders. The transaction was approved unanimously by both companies' boards of directors and is expected to close by April 15, 2024, pending regulatory review.

"This acquisition strengthens our pipeline and accelerates our entry into gene therapy," said Dr. Helena Voss, Chief Executive Officer of Solaris Biotech, who will oversee the integration from the company's headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts. NovaGene Therapeutics, based in San Diego, California, was founded in 2016 by Dr. Marcus Webb, who will join Solaris Biotech as Chief Scientific Officer effective March 18, 2024.

Solaris Biotech employs approximately 640 people worldwide and reported revenue of $412 million in fiscal year 2023. Shares of Solaris Biotech, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker SLRB, rose 6.2 percent following the announcement. Analysts at Baird Capital called the deal "a decisive move" in the increasingly competitive gene therapy market, where Solaris Biotech competes directly with Genstar Biosciences.

CAMBRIDGE, MA -- June 4, 2024 -- Solenta Biosciences, Inc. announced today that it has acquired Norwood Diagnostics Corp., a privately held maker of rapid diagnostic assays based in Norwood, Massachusetts, for $142 million in cash. The transaction, which closed on June 3, 2024, expands Solenta's footprint in point-of-care testing and adds Norwood's flagship product, the RapidScan CRP Kit, to Solenta's portfolio.

Under the terms of the deal, Solenta will retain all 65 Norwood employees at their current facility on Route 1 in Norwood. Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran, Norwood's founder and chief executive officer, will join Solenta as Senior Vice President of Diagnostics, reporting directly to Solenta CEO Marcus Whitfield.

"This acquisition strengthens our diagnostics platform and accelerates our path toward $500 million in annual revenue by 2026," said Marcus Whitfield, who has led Solenta since its founding in 2015. "Priya and her team have built something remarkable."

Dr. Chandrasekaran founded Norwood Diagnostics in 2011 after leaving a research post at Massachusetts General Hospital. The company grew to 65 employees and generated $38 million in revenue last year.

Solenta, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker SLNT and competes with Abbott Laboratories and Quidel Corporation in the diagnostics market. The company plans to detail integration timelines during its next earnings call on July 22, 2024.

SUPERIOR COURT OF SUFFOLK COUNTY, MASSACHUSETTS

Case No. 24-CR-1187 — Commonwealth v. Daniel R. Pescatore

On Tuesday, June 11, 2024, Judge Miriam Costas presided over a sentencing hearing at the Edward W. Brooke Courthouse in Boston, Massachusetts. Daniel R. Pescatore, 41, a former accountant at Harrow & Vance Financial Group, was sentenced to 4 years in state prison after pleading guilty to wire fraud and embezzlement of approximately $2.3 million from client accounts between January 2019 and March 2023.

Prosecutor Elena Duffy, representing the Commonwealth, told the court that Pescatore had diverted funds through a shell company, Meridian Capital Partners, registered in Wilmington, Delaware. Defense attorney Gregory Wu argued for leniency, citing his client's cooperation with investigators from the Massachusetts Securities Division.

Pescatore was arrested on September 14, 2023, by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation at his home in Newton, Massachusetts, following a tip from a whistleblower inside Harrow & Vance Financial Group. He was formally charged on October 2, 2023, with three counts of wire fraud.

Judge Costas also ordered restitution of $2.3 million to be paid to 19 victims, including retired teacher Rosalind Ng, who testified that she lost her retirement savings. Harrow & Vance Financial Group issued a statement saying it had terminated Pescatore's employment in April 2023 and cooperated fully with federal investigators. The company is headquartered in Boston.
