For bulk orders exceeding 50 units, contact the sales department at wholesale@fenwickcole.com. Reviewers on the company's website have given the jacket an average rating of 4.7 out of 5 stars based on 312 reviews.

BOSTON, MA -- November 4, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating relacorilant, an experimental corticosteroid-receptor blocker, in patients with treatment-resistant Cushing's syndrome. The trial, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez and funded by a $12 million grant from the National Institutes of Health, enrolled 84 participants across seven medical centers in the United States between January 2021 and March 2023. According to findings published in The Lancet Endocrinology, 61 percent of patients receiving relacorilant showed normalized cortisol levels after 24 weeks, compared with 18 percent in the placebo group. Dr. Vasquez, an endocrinologist affiliated with Harvard Medical School, presented the data on November 3, 2023, at the Endocrine Society's annual meeting in Chicago, Illinois. "These results suggest a meaningful new option for patients who have exhausted standard therapies," she told attendees. The study also reported that 9 percent of participants experienced mild hypertension as a side effect, though no serious adverse events were recorded. Corcept Therapeutics, the Menlo Park-based biopharmaceutical company developing relacorilant, said it plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the second quarter of 2024. Corcept's chief executive, Dr. Bryan Dunn, stated that the company expects to invest an additional $40 million in a Phase 3 trial slated to begin in early 2024. Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimated the drug could generate $300 million in annual revenue if approved, intensifying competition with Novartis, which markets a rival cortisol-lowering treatment called osilodrostat.

The Ohio Department of Transportation announced on June 4, 2024 that it will begin a $42 million reconstruction of the Interstate 70 interchange near Zanesville, Ohio, aimed at reducing congestion and improving safety along the corridor. Director Pamela Boratyn said the project, awarded to contractor Kokosing Construction Company, will start on July 15, 2024 and is expected to conclude by October 2025. "This investment will cut commute delays by an estimated 30 percent and support nearly 200 construction jobs over the next 16 months," Boratyn said during a press briefing held at the ODOT District 5 office in Jackson Township. The funding package includes $28 million in federal highway grants administered through the Federal Highway Administration and $14 million in state bond revenue approved by the Ohio General Assembly in March 2024. Governor Mike DeWine praised the initiative, noting that similar upgrades completed in Franklin County in 2022 reduced accident rates by 18 percent. Local officials, including Zanesville Mayor Don Mason, welcomed the announcement, though some residents voiced concerns at a public forum on June 10, 2024 about noise and detours during construction. ODOT officials confirmed that lane closures will begin gradually starting in August 2024, with most work completed during overnight hours to minimize disruption. The agency will provide weekly updates through its website and a dedicated hotline for commuters affected by the project.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice on Saturday as his side defeated Everton 3-1 at Villa Park in front of 41,875 spectators. The victory lifted Aston Villa to third place in the Premier League table with 21 points from nine matches. Manager Unai Emery praised his squad's resilience after Everton's Dominic Calvert-Lewin opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a header from a corner kick. Watkins equalized in the 34th minute, then added a second goal in the 67th minute following a swift counterattack led by midfielder John McGinn. Substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win with a strike in the 88th minute. Everton manager Sean Dyche said his team lacked composure in the final third. The result extended Aston Villa's unbeaten home run to seven matches. Villa's next fixture is scheduled for October 21 against Arsenal at Emirates Stadium in London. Emery, who joined Aston Villa in November 2022, is now being linked with a new contract extension worth a reported 6 million pounds annually, according to sources close to the club. Everton, meanwhile, dropped to 15th place and face Tottenham Hotspur on October 23 at Goodison Park. The Premier League confirmed that Saturday's match drew a television audience of nearly 1.8 million viewers in the United Kingdom.

BOSTON, March 14, 2023 — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital reported promising results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tregalizumab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based Arden Biosciences, for treatment of moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The 24-week study enrolled 312 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Germany, led by principal investigator Dr. Fiona Marsh. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of tregalizumab every four weeks showed a 62 percent reduction in disease activity scores compared to 29 percent in the placebo group, a difference the authors described as statistically significant (p<0.001). Common adverse events included mild injection-site reactions in 41 patients and upper respiratory infections in 27 patients; three patients discontinued treatment due to elevated liver enzymes. Dr. Marsh presented the findings on March 14, 2023, at the American College of Rheumatology conference in Boston, noting that tregalizumab's novel mechanism, which targets interleukin-17 signaling, could offer an alternative for patients who fail to respond to existing therapies such as adalimumab. Arden Biosciences, founded in 2016 by immunologist Dr. Raj Patel, plans to launch a Phase 3 trial in early 2024 involving approximately 900 patients across North America and Europe. The company's chief executive, Laura Chen, said the firm has raised $85 million in Series C funding to support the expanded trial and regulatory submissions to the Food and Drug Administration. Analysts at Sanborn Capital estimate that if approved, tregalizumab could generate annual revenue exceeding $1.2 billion by 2028, positioning it as a competitor to AbbVie's Humira franchise.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Redwood Robotics Inc. announced this morning that it has acquired Trellix Sensors LLC for $42 million in cash. The deal closed Tuesday, June 11, 2024, according to CEO Marisol Vega.

2/ Vega told reporters at the company's headquarters on Congress Avenue that the acquisition will help Redwood scale production of its flagship product, the HarvestBot X3, used by farms across Texas and Iowa.

3/ Trellix Sensors, founded in 2018 by engineer Devon Okafor, previously supplied pressure sensors to Redwood under a three-year contract. Okafor will join Redwood as Chief Technology Officer starting July 1, 2024.

4/ "This is about vertical integration," Vega said during a press briefing in Austin on Wednesday. "We no longer want to depend on outside suppliers for critical components."

5/ Redwood's biggest rival, Chicago-based AgriPulse Corp., declined to comment. Analysts at Fenwick Capital estimate Redwood's annual revenue will grow by 18 percent following the merger.

6/ Not everyone is celebrating. About 30 former Trellix employees protested outside Redwood's offices on Thursday, June 13, demanding severance guarantees.

7/ Redwood shares rose 6 percent on the Nasdaq after the announcement, closing at $54.20.

8/ Vega, a dual citizen of the United States and Mexico, previously worked at Tesla before founding Redwood Robotics in 2015 alongside co-founder Priya Nair.

To: Board of Directors, Meridian Foods Corporation
From: Elena Castillo, Chief Financial Officer
Date: March 4, 2024
Re: Acquisition of Bramwell Dairy Ltd. and Executive Transition

Dear Board Members,

I am writing to confirm that Meridian Foods Corporation has completed its acquisition of Bramwell Dairy Ltd., headquartered in Leeds, United Kingdom, for a total price of 42 million dollars. The transaction closed on February 28, 2024, following approval from regulators in London. Bramwell Dairy, founded in 1987 by Harold Bramwell, supplies dairy products to over 300 retailers across England and Scotland.

As part of this transition, Harold Bramwell will step down as Chief Executive Officer of Bramwell Dairy effective March 15, 2024. In his place, Meridian Foods has appointed Priya Nair, previously Vice President of Operations at Danone UK, to serve as the new Chief Executive Officer of Bramwell Dairy starting March 18, 2024. Ms. Nair will relocate from Manchester to Leeds to take up the role.

Additionally, I want to inform the Board that on March 1, 2024, representatives from Meridian Foods met with officials from the Leeds City Council at Leeds Town Hall to discuss expansion permits for the Bramwell manufacturing plant. We expect a decision by April 30, 2024.

Finally, please note that Meridian Foods will pay Bramwell Dairy shareholders a final settlement of 3.5 million dollars by March 20, 2024, to close out remaining escrow obligations.

Please let me know if you have questions before our next board meeting on March 12, 2024.

Sincerely,
Elena Castillo
Chief Financial Officer
Meridian Foods Corporation

Boston, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH) announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tefermetinib, an experimental chemical compound targeting the MET receptor, in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer. The trial, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez, enrolled 214 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between June 2021 and September 2023. Findings, published in The Lancet Oncology, showed a 41 percent objective response rate among patients receiving tefermetinib compared with 19 percent in the control arm treated with standard chemotherapy. Median progression-free survival reached 11.2 months versus 6.4 months, a difference the authors called clinically meaningful. Dr. Vasquez, a professor of oncology at Harvard Medical School, presented the data at the American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) annual meeting in San Diego on April 9, 2024. "These results suggest tefermetinib could become a new standard option for MET-altered lung cancer," she said during the presentation. The study was funded by a $12 million grant from the National Cancer Institute and supported by Meridian Therapeutics, the biotechnology company that developed the drug and is headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Meridian Therapeutics was founded in 2015 by Dr. Raymond Ochoa, who currently serves as chief executive officer. The company plans to submit tefermetinib for accelerated approval to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. Common adverse events included fatigue, nausea, and peripheral edema, with 6 percent of patients discontinuing treatment due to toxicity. A larger Phase 3 trial is expected to begin enrollment in late 2024 at additional sites in Japan and the United Kingdom.

Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1961 in Bologna, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques used across southern Europe. She earned her degree in Civil Engineering from the University of Bologna in 1984 and later joined Studio Marchetti-Rossi, an engineering firm headquartered in Milan, as a junior partner in 1988. In 1994, Marchetti founded Vertico Engineering S.p.A. in Turin, a company that specialized in retrofitting historic buildings against earthquake damage. Vertico's work gained international attention after the 1997 Umbria-Marche earthquake, when Marchetti's team was called in to stabilize the Basilica of San Francesco in Assisi. For this project, she received the Cardano Medal from the Italian National Research Council in Rome in 1999. Marchetti served as Chief Engineer of Vertico until 2008, when she stepped down to become a visiting professor at ETH Zurich. In 2011, Vertico Engineering was acquired by the French conglomerate Bouygues Construction for approximately 42 million euros, a deal finalized in Paris. Marchetti is married to fellow engineer Paolo Ferraris, with whom she has two children. She currently serves on the board of the European Federation of Earthquake Engineering, based in Brussels, and continues to publish on retrofit methodology. In 2020, she was awarded an honorary doctorate by the Politecnico di Milano for her contributions to structural safety.

Fjallraven Vantage 32L Backpack — Refurbished by GearLoop Outfitters

GearLoop Outfitters, headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, is offering 240 units of the Fjallraven Vantage 32L Backpack in refurbished condition for $89.99, marked down from the original retail price of $159.00. Each unit was returned to Fjallraven's Boise distribution center between March 3, 2023 and July 14, 2023, inspected by certified technicians, and repackaged with a fresh 12-month warranty. The backpack features a G-1000 Eco fabric shell, a padded 15-inch laptop sleeve, and reinforced YKK zippers rated for 20,000 open-close cycles.

GearLoop Outfitters acquired this refurbished inventory batch from Fjallraven North America on August 9, 2023, in a deal worth $1.2 million, according to a statement released by GearLoop CEO Martin Halvorsen. "We're proud to give these packs a second life," Halvorsen said during a press briefing in Bozeman on August 15, 2023. The transaction was finalized after three months of negotiation between GearLoop and Fjallraven's regional sales director, Ingrid Solberg.

Each backpack ships from the Boise warehouse within 2 business days via FedEx Ground and includes a laminated authenticity card. Customers who purchase before September 30, 2023 receive a free rain cover valued at $18. Reviewers on OutdoorGearLab have praised the pack's durability, awarding it 4.6 out of 5 stars. Quantities are limited to one per household while supplies last.

HAMBURG, Germany, March 14 - Norddeutsche Werft AG, a mid-sized shipbuilder headquartered in Hamburg, filed for insolvency protection on Thursday after failing to secure a bridge loan of 45 million euros, the company announced. Chief Executive Officer Klaus Reinhardt told reporters at a press conference that the firm's board voted unanimously to pursue restructuring under German insolvency law rather than liquidate outright. "We owe it to our 1,200 employees to fight for this company," Reinhardt said, standing beside CFO Anke Vogel. The Hamburg-based firm, founded in 1962 by naval engineer Otto Kellermann, had struggled since 2022 amid rising steel prices and delayed orders from Norwegian ferry operator Fjordline AS. Industry analyst Petra Sommer of Bremen Maritime Research said Norddeutsche Werft's troubles reflect a broader crisis in European shipbuilding, with competitor Meyer Werft also reporting losses last year. Reinhardt confirmed that talks are underway with Singapore-based investment group Temasek Maritime Partners, which could inject up to 60 million euros in exchange for a 40 percent stake. A decision is expected by April 30. Employees staged a demonstration outside the shipyard gates in Hamburg on Friday, demanding job guarantees before any deal is signed. The works council, led by union representative Jorg Fassbinder, warned that up to 300 jobs could be cut regardless of the outcome. Local politicians, including Hamburg's economy minister Silke Brandt, have called for state intervention to protect the region's maritime heritage.

Wilder Peak Gear, headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, has launched the Summit Ridge 3-Season Tent, a two-person backpacking shelter priced at $329.00. Released on March 14, 2024, the tent weighs 3.2 pounds and packs down to the size of a 1-liter water bottle. The rainfly is constructed from 20-denier ripstop nylon with a 1,200mm waterproof coating, and the freestanding pole structure uses DAC Featherlite NSL aluminum poles sourced from supplier Duracraft Components of Busan, South Korea. Wilder Peak Gear was founded in 2011 by former REI product designer Hannah Torvik, who now serves as Chief Product Officer. The company acquired a smaller manufacturer, Alpine Loft Goods, in September 2019 to expand its insulation line. Each Summit Ridge tent ships with eight aluminum stakes, a repair kit, and a lifetime warranty against manufacturing defects. Customer reviews on the company's website average 4.7 out of 5 stars from over 1,300 verified buyers. The tent is currently available in three colorways: Slate Gray, Moss Green, and Burnt Orange. Orders placed before 2:00 PM Mountain Time ship the same day via FedEx Ground. Wilder Peak Gear competes directly with Marmot and Big Agnes in the ultralight backpacking segment, though it undercuts both on price by roughly 15 percent. A limited batch of 500 units will be sold exclusively through REI Co-op stores starting April 1, 2024, before wider retail distribution resumes in May.

CedarPoint Robotics, headquartered in Ann Arbor, Michigan, announced on June 12, 2024 that it has acquired Delphine Sensors Inc., a San Diego-based maker of lidar components, for $84 million in cash. The deal is expected to close by August 1, 2024, pending customary regulatory approval.

Under the agreement, CedarPoint Robotics will absorb Delphine Sensors' 130 employees and integrate its LumaScan-9 sensor line into CedarPoint's flagship delivery robot, the TrailBlazer 200. "This acquisition strengthens our ability to deliver reliable autonomous navigation at scale," said Priya Nathan, Chief Executive Officer of CedarPoint Robotics, during a press briefing in Ann Arbor.

Delphine Sensors was founded in 2016 by engineer Marcus Ohlin, who will join CedarPoint Robotics as Vice President of Sensor Engineering, reporting directly to Nathan. Ohlin previously worked at Qualcomm for nine years before launching Delphine Sensors.

CedarPoint Robotics, which competes with Boston-based Nimbus Autonomy, said the acquisition would boost annual revenue by an estimated 18 percent by fiscal year 2025. The company plans to retain Delphine Sensors' San Diego facility as a dedicated research hub.

Shares of CedarPoint Robotics, which trades on Nasdaq under the ticker CPTR, rose 6 percent following the announcement. The transaction marks CedarPoint's third acquisition since its founding in 2011 by Nathan and co-founder Elena Vasquez.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA — On October 14, 2024, Judge Marisol Fenwick sentenced Dominic Alvarez, 37, to 48 months in state prison after a jury found him guilty of grand theft and embezzlement in connection with his former position as Chief Financial Officer of Beacon Harbor Logistics, a shipping firm headquartered in Oakland, California. Prosecutor Renata Okafor of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that between March 2021 and January 2023, Alvarez diverted approximately $2.3 million from company accounts into shell entities registered in Nevada. The jury, empaneled on September 3, 2024, returned its verdict on October 2, 2024, following a two-week trial at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland. Defense attorney Priya Nakamura argued for leniency, citing her client's lack of prior criminal record, but Judge Fenwick rejected the request, stating that the breach of fiduciary duty warranted a substantial sentence. Beacon Harbor Logistics CEO Walter Hsieh issued a statement thanking investigators from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, who arrested Alvarez on February 9, 2023, at his residence in Piedmont, California, on charges of wire fraud and embezzlement. The company said it has since recovered $900,000 through civil litigation and expects further restitution under the terms of Alvarez's sentence, which includes a court-ordered repayment of $1.4 million to Beacon Harbor Logistics. Alvarez's attorney indicated an appeal is likely to be filed within 60 days.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. RG24-118732

On March 14, 2024, the Superior Court of Alameda County sentenced Marcus Whitfield, 47, to 5 years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of grand theft and securities fraud. Judge Elena Ruiz presided over the trial, which concluded on March 12, 2024, at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, California. Prosecutor David Alonso of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Whitfield, former Chief Financial Officer of Brightline Capital Group, diverted $2.3 million from client accounts between January 2021 and September 2022.

Whitfield was arrested on October 4, 2022, by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation at his residence in Piedmont, California, on charges of wire fraud and embezzlement. He was formally charged by the District Attorney's Office on November 15, 2022. During the hearing, defense attorney Priya Nakamura contended that her client had cooperated fully with investigators and had already repaid $600,000 to Brightline Capital Group.

Brightline Capital Group, headquartered in San Francisco, California, issued a statement through spokesperson Laura Bennett confirming that the firm has strengthened internal controls since the incident. The company was founded in 2009 by Richard Coleman, who currently serves as Chief Executive Officer. Sentencing documents indicate Whitfield must also pay $1.7 million in restitution by June 1, 2025.

DETROIT, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Stellantis NV agreed to acquire Halcyon Battery Technologies Inc, a Detroit-based startup specializing in solid-state battery cells, for $740 million in cash, the companies announced Tuesday. The deal, expected to close by December 15, will give Stellantis full ownership of Halcyon's Warren, Michigan manufacturing plant and its portfolio of 62 patents.

Halcyon was founded in 2019 by Dr. Priya Nandakumar, a former MIT researcher, who will stay on as Chief Technology Officer under the new ownership structure. "This acquisition accelerates our roadmap for next-generation electric vehicles," said Carlos Tavares, Chief Executive Officer of Stellantis, during a press briefing at the company's North American headquarters.

Stellantis shares rose 3.2 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $21.45. Analysts at Morgan Stanley called the move a direct challenge to competitor General Motors, which has invested heavily in its own Ultium battery platform through a joint venture with LG Energy Solution.

The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, a process Stellantis executives expect to conclude within eight weeks. Halcyon currently employs 310 people and generated $58 million in revenue last year, according to figures disclosed in the filing.

Industry observers note the deal reflects growing pressure among automakers to secure domestic battery supply chains ahead of stricter emissions rules set to take effect in 2027 under the Environmental Protection Agency's revised standards.

DETROIT, Mich. — Reliant Motorworks Inc. announced on Tuesday, June 11, 2024, that it has acquired Voltis Battery Systems LLC, a Grand Rapids-based maker of lithium-ion battery packs, for $340 million in cash and stock. The deal, disclosed at Reliant's headquarters on Woodward Avenue, marks the automaker's largest acquisition since its founding in 1998 by engineer Harold Kessler.

Under the agreement, Voltis founder and chief executive officer Priya Nandakumar will join Reliant as Executive Vice President of Battery Engineering, reporting directly to Reliant CEO Marcus Ellison. Nandakumar, a citizen of the United States who previously worked for General Cathode Corp., said the merger will help Reliant triple production of its Aurora electric sedan by 2026.

Reliant shares rose 7 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.40. Analysts at Brindlewood Capital called the acquisition "a defensive move against Tesla and Rivian," both of which have expanded battery manufacturing in North America.

The transaction, expected to close by September 30, 2024, still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Reliant said it will retain Voltis's 620 employees at their existing plant in Grand Rapids, Michigan, and plans to invest an additional $75 million to expand the facility. Ellison, speaking at a press conference in Detroit, said the acquisition would "secure our battery supply chain for the next decade" and reduce reliance on suppliers such as Panasonic Corp.

input: Bellroy, the Melbourne-based accessories maker, has launched the Venture Ready Backpack 2.0, now available on the company website for AUD 189. Unveiled on March 4, 2024, the 22-liter pack is built from 900D recycled polyester and features a padded 16-inch laptop sleeve, a magnetic sternum strap, and weatherproof YKK AquaGuard zippers. Bellroy, founded in 2010 by Andy Fallshaw in Fitzroy, Victoria, has grown into a competitor of Peak Design and Herschel Supply Co. in the premium travel-gear segment. The Venture Ready 2.0 comes in three colorways: Basalt, Ash, and Ranger Green, and weighs 1.3 kilograms empty. Each unit ships with a two-year manufacturer warranty and a lifetime repair guarantee administered through Bellroy's Melbourne service center. Early reviewers, including tech outlet Gearwise, praised the bag's 98 percent recycled-material composition and its quick-access front pocket, giving it 4.6 out of 5 stars across 312 verified purchases. Bellroy plans to donate 1 percent of all Venture Ready sales to the Ocean Cleanup Foundation, a partnership announced alongside the launch. Customers who order before April 1, 2024 will also receive a complimentary rain cover valued at AUD 25. The backpack is compatible with Bellroy's modular Tech Kit organizers, sold separately for AUD 45. Stock is currently limited, with the first shipment of 5,000 units expected to sell out within two weeks based on pre-order demand from customers in Australia, the United States, and Japan.

Denver-based Highland Grain Corp. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Prairie Mills LLC, a wheat-processing subsidiary of Nebraska Agri Holdings, for $214 million in cash. The deal, disclosed in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, is expected to close by December 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

CEO Marion Delacroix said the acquisition will expand Highland Grain's footprint across the Midwest and add three processing plants in Nebraska and Kansas. "Prairie Mills gives us direct access to nearly 40 percent more milling capacity," Delacroix told reporters during a press conference in Omaha. Highland Grain's board approved the transaction last week after a two-month due diligence review led by Chief Financial Officer Raj Patel.

Prairie Mills, founded in 1978 by farmer Walter Kessling, employs roughly 620 workers and reported revenue of $310 million last fiscal year. Nebraska Agri Holdings said proceeds from the sale will be used to reduce debt and fund a new soybean facility in Lincoln, Nebraska, slated to open in 2026.

Shares of Highland Grain rose 6.3 percent to $58.10 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while analysts at Morningstar raised their price target to $65. Rival grain processor Continental Harvest Inc. declined to comment on the deal. Industry analyst Sofia Reyes of AgriTrend Research called the acquisition "a clear signal of consolidation pressure in the grain-processing sector." Highland Grain expects the combined company to generate $1.1 billion in annual revenue.

DENVER, Colorado — Trailhead Robotics Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Summit Sensor Systems, a privately held maker of industrial LiDAR components based in Boulder, Colorado, for $142 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by November 15, 2024, will make Summit Sensor Systems a wholly owned subsidiary of Trailhead Robotics.

CEO Maria Fontaine said the acquisition strengthens Trailhead's position against competitor Vantage Automation Corp., which has expanded aggressively in the warehouse-robotics market. "This gives us proprietary sensing technology we would have needed three years to build in-house," Fontaine told reporters during a press briefing at Trailhead's Denver headquarters.

Summit Sensor Systems founder and CEO David Okafor will join Trailhead as Chief Technology Officer, effective December 1, 2024. Okafor founded Summit Sensor Systems in 2016 after leaving a research role at Lockheed Martin. He will report directly to Fontaine and oversee a 60-person engineering team relocating from Boulder to Denver.

Trailhead financed the purchase through a combination of $90 million in cash reserves and a $52 million term loan arranged by First Denver Bank. Shares of Trailhead Robotics, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker TRLH, rose 6.3 percent to $58.40 following the announcement.

Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners called the deal a strong strategic fit, noting that Summit's sensors are already used in Trailhead's flagship autonomous forklift, the Trailhead Falcon. The transaction remains subject to regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission.

OTTAWA, Ontario -- The Ministry of Environment and Climate Change announced on May 6, 2024 that it will provide CAD 42 million in funding to Great Lakes Restoration Alliance, a nonprofit based in Thunder Bay, to reduce plastic pollution in Lake Superior. Minister Julie Bernard said the grant, effective July 1, 2024, will support cleanup crews across 14 municipalities over the next three years. "This is the largest single investment our ministry has made in freshwater protection," Bernard told reporters during a press conference at the National Arts Centre. The funding follows a report by the Canadian Freshwater Institute estimating that 9,800 metric tons of plastic waste enter the Great Lakes annually. Dr. Rajiv Anand, the Institute's lead scientist, will join the Alliance's advisory board starting August 15, 2024, after stepping down as senior researcher at Environment Canada. The Alliance, founded in 2011 by former fisherman Marc Tremblay, currently employs 63 staff and operates six regional offices. Under the agreement, 30 percent of funds will be allocated to shoreline restoration, while the remainder covers equipment purchases, including two new skimmer vessels built by Hike Metal Products in Wheatley. Opposition critics, including MP Sandra Coulter, argued the amount was insufficient given that similar programs in the United States received over USD 100 million last year. The ministry expects to publish its first progress report by December 2025.

input: DETROIT, Mich. — Ferrostal Dynamics, a mid-sized auto-parts supplier, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing a $340 million debt load and collapsing orders from General Motors. The filing was made in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Detroit, according to company spokesperson Renee Okafor. CEO Marcus Whitfield told reporters at a Wednesday press conference that the company would continue operations at its Flint, Michigan plant while it restructures. "We are committed to protecting the 1,200 jobs at our Flint facility," Whitfield said. Ferrostal Dynamics was founded in 1987 by engineer Harold Bregman and has supplied brake components to General Motors and Ford Motor Company for over three decades. Industry analyst Priya Nandakumar of Blackstone Capital Advisors said the bankruptcy reflects broader turmoil in the auto-parts sector, noting that rival supplier Delphi Technologies also struggled last year amid rising steel prices. The bankruptcy court has scheduled an initial hearing for August 14, 2024, before Judge Linda Fairweather to review the reorganization plan. Ferrostal Dynamics employs roughly 4,500 people across six facilities in Michigan and Ohio. Shares of the company, which trades over the counter, fell 62 percent following the announcement. Whitfield added that no layoffs are planned before the court hearing, though he acknowledged "difficult decisions" may follow depending on negotiations with creditors including JPMorgan Chase.

CHARLOTTE, N.C. — Ferrolux Metals Corp. announced Tuesday it will acquire Bramwell Steel Systems for $410 million in cash, creating one of the largest specialty steel suppliers in the southeastern United States. The deal was disclosed at a press conference at Ferrolux's headquarters in Charlotte by CEO Diane Kastner, who will remain in her role after the merger closes.

Bramwell Steel Systems, based in Knoxville, Tennessee, employs roughly 2,200 workers across three plants and has been a key supplier to automakers including Talon Motors. Bramwell's founder and outgoing chairman, Harold Weiss, said the sale will help the company expand production capacity amid rising demand for lightweight steel alloys used in electric vehicles.

The transaction, expected to close by January 15, 2025, still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Analysts at Merriwell Capital Partners estimate the combined company could generate $3.2 billion in annual revenue, up from Ferrolux's current $2.1 billion.

Shares of Ferrolux rose 8 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Bramwell, which is privately held, does not trade publicly. Kastner said no layoffs are planned and that Bramwell's Knoxville plants will continue operating under the Bramwell brand for at least two years.

Industry group American Steel Alliance called the merger "a significant consolidation" in a statement released Wednesday. Weiss, 67, plans to retire once the deal finalizes, ending a 34-year career with the company he started in 1990.

Pixelworks Labs, a hardware startup based in Portland, Oregon, launched the Contour X1 mirrorless camera on May 14, 2024, and I have spent three weeks shooting with it around the Pacific Northwest. Priced at $2,499, the Contour X1 is aimed squarely at competitor Fujifilm's X-H2S, and in most respects it wins. The 26-megapixel stacked sensor delivers 40 frames per second continuous shooting, and the in-body stabilization rated at 7 stops is genuinely usable for handheld night shots along the Willamette River.

CEO Naomi Vasquez, who founded Pixelworks Labs in 2019 after leaving Sony, told me in an interview on May 20, 2024 that the company built its own image processor, the Halcyon II chip, rather than licensing one from Sony or Canon. That bet mostly pays off: autofocus tracking locked onto cyclists and dogs with impressive consistency, and battery life reached roughly 640 shots per charge in my testing.

The rough edges are real, though. The menu system borrows too much from Sony's older Alpha series, burying custom white balance three submenus deep. The companion app, Contour Sync, crashed twice while transferring RAW files to my iPad Pro. Pixelworks Labs says a firmware update in June 2024 will address both complaints.

Still, at $2,499 with a weather-sealed magnesium body, the Contour X1 undercuts Sony's A7 IV by $1,000 while matching its autofocus performance. For working photographers in Portland and beyond, this is the most exciting camera debut since the Nikon Z9. Recommended, with patience for firmware polish.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Fulwood Athletic staged a stunning comeback at Etihad Park on Saturday, defeating league leaders Bristol Rangers 3-2 to snap a five-match winless streak. Striker Daniel Osei scored twice, including a stoppage-time winner in the 91st minute, while midfielder Tomas Vidic added the equalizer just before halftime. Bristol Rangers had taken a 2-0 lead inside the opening twenty minutes through goals from Marcus Feld and Youssef Amrani, prompting frustrated chants from the traveling supporters behind the north goal. The win lifts Fulwood Athletic to eighth place in the Northern Football League table with 18 points from twelve matches, three points behind fourth-placed Bristol Rangers. League officials confirmed that Fulwood Athletic's next fixture will be against Chorlton United on October 21 at Whitmore Stadium. Club chairman Gareth Pryce said the victory could be worth over 200,000 pounds in additional matchday revenue if the team reaches the promotion playoffs in May 2024. Bristol Rangers manager Ivan Kovac, formerly of Preston Vale FC, declined to comment immediately but is expected to address the loss on Monday. input: BOSTON, MA -- June 12, 2023 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tregafenib, an experimental chemical compound targeting a mutated form of the KRAS protein in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer. The trial, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti, enrolled 214 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and September 2022. According to results published in The Lancet Oncology, patients receiving tregafenib in combination with gemcitabine showed a median overall survival of 11.4 months, compared with 7.8 months for those on gemcitabine alone, representing a 34 percent reduction in risk of death. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 22 percent of the treatment arm, most commonly neutropenia and fatigue. Dr. Marchetti presented the findings at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting in Chicago on June 10, 2023, where the data drew applause from attendees. "These results suggest tregafenib could become a meaningful option for a disease with historically dismal outcomes," she said. The trial was funded by Northbridge Therapeutics, a biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, which plans to seek accelerated approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2024. Northbridge's chief executive, Raj Patel, stated the company would begin a Phase 3 confirmatory trial in October 2023 across sites in Boston, Toronto, and Munich. Shares of Northbridge Therapeutics rose 18 percent following the ASCO presentation, adding roughly 340 million dollars to the company's market capitalization.

CLEVELAND, Ohio — Rockport Steel Corporation filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in outstanding debt and a sharp decline in demand from the automotive sector. The filing, submitted in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Ohio, comes just eight months after CEO Marlene Foss took over from longtime chief executive Harold Denby, who had led the company for 22 years.

Rockport, founded in 1954 by industrialist Eugene Wachs, employs roughly 2,800 workers at plants in Cleveland and Youngstown. Foss said in a statement that the company plans to continue operations during the restructuring process and expects no immediate layoffs. "We are committed to emerging from this process as a leaner, more competitive company," Foss said Tuesday.

The bankruptcy follows a turbulent year for the steelmaker, which lost a major supply contract with Detroit-based Halden Motors in March after Halden shifted to a competitor, Bristow Alloys, based in Pittsburgh. Rockport's stock price had fallen nearly 78 percent over the past twelve months before trading was halted Tuesday morning on the New York Stock Exchange.

Analysts at Corrigan Partners, a Chicago investment firm, said Rockport's debt load became unsustainable after it borrowed $150 million in 2021 to modernize its Youngstown facility. Judge Patricia Alvarez has been assigned to oversee the case, with an initial hearing scheduled for November 14 in Cleveland.

Local union representative Danny Kowalski said workers are "anxious but hopeful" the company can survive the restructuring.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. — August 14, 2024 — Meridian Biotherapeutics, Inc. today announced that it has acquired Vantage Genomics Corp., a privately held gene-editing startup based in Boulder, Colorado, for $340 million in cash and stock. The transaction is expected to close by September 30, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Under the terms of the agreement, Meridian will pay Vantage Genomics shareholders $210 million in cash and $130 million in Meridian common stock. Vantage Genomics, founded in 2018 by Dr. Priya Nakamura, has developed a proprietary CRISPR-based platform targeting sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia.

"This acquisition strengthens our pipeline and accelerates our entry into gene therapy for hemoglobinopathies," said Richard Feldman, Chief Executive Officer of Meridian Biotherapeutics. "Dr. Nakamura and her team have built something extraordinary in just six years."

Dr. Nakamura will join Meridian as Chief Scientific Officer, reporting directly to Feldman, effective October 1, 2024. She will retain her laboratory in Boulder, which will operate as a Meridian research subsidiary.

Meridian Biotherapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs approximately 1,200 people and trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol MRBT. The company reported $890 million in revenue for fiscal year 2023.

Analysts at Jefferies noted the deal positions Meridian as a stronger competitor to Vertex Pharmaceuticals in the gene-editing space. Shares of Meridian rose 4.2 percent in after-hours trading following the announcement.

Meridian's board of directors, chaired by Susan Whitfield, approved the transaction unanimously on August 12, 2024.

BOSTON, MA -- November 12, 2023 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tavaneurin, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cascade Therapeutics for early-stage Parkinson's disease. The study, led by Dr. Renata Alvarez and published in The Lancet Neurology, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and July 2022. Participants receiving a 300 mg intravenous dose of tavaneurin every four weeks showed a 34 percent reduction in motor symptom progression compared to placebo, as measured by the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale. Dr. Alvarez presented the findings on November 10, 2023 at the Congress of Neurological Disorders in Chicago. "These results suggest tavaneurin could meaningfully delay disability in patients diagnosed early," she said during a press briefing. Cascade Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, was founded in 2015 by biochemist Wen Li and has raised $180 million in venture funding, according to CEO Marcus Thornbury. The company plans to begin a Phase 3 trial in January 2024, enrolling an estimated 600 patients. Shares of Cascade Therapeutics rose 18 percent following the announcement. The Michael J. Fox Foundation, a nonprofit based in New York City, contributed $4.5 million toward the trial. Common side effects included mild headache and injection-site reactions; no serious adverse events related to tavaneurin were reported. Regulatory submissions to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration are expected by mid-2025.

Pixel Tab 3, Google's first tablet in nearly a decade, went on sale on October 15, 2024, and after three weeks of daily use in San Francisco, I have mixed feelings. Priced at $799 for the 128GB Wi-Fi model, the device pairs a 10.9-inch OLED screen with the Tensor G4 chip, the same silicon found in the Pixel 9 phone. Sundar Pichai, chief executive officer of Google, called it "a new chapter for computing" during the launch event at the Mountain View campus. Battery life is the standout: I consistently got 11 hours of mixed video and browsing, beating Samsung's Galaxy Tab S9 by roughly two hours in my tests. The included Pixel Keyboard case, sold separately for $199, feels sturdy, though the trackpad occasionally lags when switching between apps. Software is where things get complicated. Android 15 on a tablet still has awkward moments, with several third-party apps like Slack and Spotify rendering as stretched phone layouts. Google says a fix is coming in a December update. Competing with Apple's iPad Air, which starts at $599, the Pixel Tab 3 is a tough sell on price alone. Still, for Google diehards embedded in the Workspace ecosystem, the hardware quality here, built in partnership with manufacturer Foxconn in Taiwan, is the best the company has produced. I'd wait for a price drop before recommending it broadly.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024 — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tazemetostat in combination with rituximab for patients with relapsed follicular lymphoma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez and published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, enrolled 142 adults across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2021 and September 2023. Participants received 800 milligrams of tazemetostat twice daily alongside standard rituximab infusions over a 24-week treatment cycle. At the 12-month follow-up, 61 percent of patients achieved complete remission, compared with 38 percent in the rituximab-only control arm, a statistically significant improvement (p=0.003). Grade 3 or higher adverse events, primarily neutropenia and thrombocytopenia, occurred in 22 percent of the combination-therapy group. Dr. Vasquez presented the findings at the American Society of Hematology annual meeting in San Diego on December 9, 2023. Epizyme Inc., the Cambridge-based biopharmaceutical company that developed tazemetostat, funded the trial with additional support of $4.3 million from the National Cancer Institute. Epizyme was acquired by Ipsen S.A. in 2022 for approximately $247 million, and Ipsen has since expanded distribution of the drug, marketed as Tazverik, across Europe. Dr. Vasquez, who joined Massachusetts General Hospital as Director of Lymphoma Research in January 2020, said the results support tazemetostat as a potential new standard of care for patients who have relapsed after initial chemotherapy. The research team plans to launch a Phase 3 trial in early 2025, pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

BOSTON, MA - March 14, 2024 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced today the results of a Phase II clinical trial evaluating tremeliximab-B, an investigational monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Solantis Therapeutics, for treatment of relapsed multiple myeloma. The 18-month trial enrolled 214 patients across seven sites, including Massachusetts General Hospital and the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. Dr. Elena Vasquez, the study's lead author and Chief of Hematology-Oncology at Massachusetts General Hospital, presented findings on March 13, 2024 at the American Society of Hematology conference in Chicago, Illinois. According to the data, 62 percent of patients receiving tremeliximab-B in combination with dexamethasone achieved partial or complete remission, compared with 31 percent in the control arm receiving standard bortezomib therapy alone. Median progression-free survival reached 14.2 months, a statistically significant improvement over the 7.8 months observed in the control group. The most common adverse event was Grade 2 neutropenia, reported in 22 percent of participants. Solantis Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by Dr. Raj Patel, raised $85 million in Series C funding last year to support late-stage development. The company plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the fourth quarter of 2025. Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Finally Gets the Basics Right

By Renata Ocampo, October 14, 2024

Google launched the Pixel Watch 3 on September 20, 2024, priced at $349.99 for the 41mm model, and after three weeks of daily use in Austin, Texas, I can say it's the most polished wearable the company has produced. The device is manufactured by Google's hardware division, headquartered in Mountain View, California, and assembled by supplier Compal Electronics in Taiwan.

Battery life reaches roughly 36 hours with the always-on display disabled, a marked improvement over the Pixel Watch 2. The new Loss of Pulse Detection feature, developed with input from Dr. Priya Nadkarni of the Cleveland Clinic, uses onboard sensors to flag cardiac arrest events, though it remains unavailable outside the United States pending regulatory approval.

Google acquired Fitbit back in 2021 for roughly $2.1 billion, and that lineage shows: the watch pairs Fitbit's sleep-tracking algorithms with Wear OS 5. During a briefing at Google's Mountain View campus, product manager Elena Suh told reporters the Pixel Watch 3 sold over 500,000 units in its first month, competing directly with the Apple Watch Series 10 and Samsung's Galaxy Watch 7.

My only complaints: the 41mm case still feels cramped for anyone with larger wrists, and the $349.99 starting price undercuts nothing in a crowded market. Still, for Android users already invested in the Fitbit ecosystem, this is an easy recommendation. Rating: 4 out of 5 stars.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024 — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tremelast, an oral JAK1 inhibitor developed by Boston-based Callisto Therapeutics, for treatment of moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis. The randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study enrolled 214 adult patients across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and September 2023. Dr. Elena Vasquez, the trial's lead investigator and a dermatologist at Massachusetts General Hospital, presented findings at the American Academy of Dermatology conference held in San Diego on March 12, 2024. Patients receiving 30 milligrams of tremelast daily for 16 weeks achieved a 62 percent reduction in Eczema Area and Severity Index scores, compared with 24 percent in the placebo group. Approximately 8 percent of participants reported mild headache, and 3 percent discontinued treatment due to nausea. No serious adverse events, including major cardiovascular incidents, were reported during the study period. Callisto Therapeutics, founded in 2019 by biochemist Dr. Marcus Feld, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the fourth quarter of 2024. In January 2024, Callisto Therapeutics was acquired by pharmaceutical giant Novareen Biosciences for 1.2 billion dollars, a deal that closed on February 20, 2024. Novareen's chief executive, Priya Anand, stated the acquisition would accelerate global distribution of tremelast, particularly across the European Union and Japan, pending regulatory approval expected in early 2025. The study was funded in part by a 4.5 million dollar grant from the National Institutes of Health.

Marguerite Delacroix (born 12 March 1927 in Lyon, France; died 4 September 2011 in Geneva, Switzerland) was a French biochemist renowned for her pioneering work on insulin crystallization. She earned a doctorate in chemistry from the University of Lyon in 1951 and joined the Pasteur Institute in Paris the following year as a research assistant. In 1958 Delacroix moved to Geneva to take up a position as Professor of Biochemistry at the University of Geneva, a post she held until her retirement in 1992. Her 1963 paper describing the crystalline structure of bovine insulin, published in the journal Nature, was cited for decades and helped lay groundwork for later diabetes treatments. In 1971 she founded the Geneva Institute for Molecular Research, serving as its director for eighteen years and securing early funding of 2 million Swiss francs from the Rockefeller Foundation. Delacroix was married to physicist Henri Vasseur from 1955 until his death in 1998; the couple had one son, Philippe Vasseur, who later became a molecular biologist himself. In 1985 she received the Marcel Benoist Prize, Switzerland's most prestigious science award, presented to her in Bern by the Swiss Federal Council in recognition of her contributions to structural biochemistry. She was also elected a foreign member of the French Academy of Sciences in 1990. Delacroix published more than 140 papers over her career and mentored dozens of doctoral students, several of whom went on to lead major European research institutes. She died at age 84 following a brief illness.

Ingrid Solberg (born March 14, 1958, in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cod population decline in the North Sea. She earned her doctorate in Marine Ecology from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø the following year as a Research Fellow. In 1994 Solberg became Head of the Fisheries Ecology Division, a position she held for eleven years. Her 1999 book, "The Silent Depths," documented overfishing across Scandinavian waters and became a widely cited reference among European policymakers. In 2003 she was awarded the Nansen Prize by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to marine conservation. Solberg left the Institute of Marine Research in 2005 to become a professor at the University of Oslo, where she still teaches. She married fellow researcher Torstein Aas in 1987, and the couple has two children, Kristin and Erik Aas. In 2011 Solberg testified before the Norwegian Parliament regarding proposed amendments to the Marine Resources Act, arguing for stricter quotas. She retired from active fieldwork in 2018 but continues to publish, most recently a 2022 paper co-authored with Dr. Halvard Kittelsen examining warming trends in the Barents Sea. Solberg currently resides in Oslo.

The Ohio Department of Transportation announced on March 14, 2024 that it will allocate $42 million to repair the Interstate 75 corridor between Dayton and Toledo. Director Priya Nathan said the funding, approved by Governor Mike DeWine, will cover 18 months of construction beginning May 6, 2024. The project, known as the Miami Valley Bridge Renewal Initiative, will replace six aging overpasses and add a dedicated lane for commercial vehicles.

At a press briefing held in Columbus, Nathan explained that the contract was awarded to Kokosing Construction Company following a competitive bidding process that concluded on February 20, 2024. "This investment will reduce congestion by an estimated 30 percent and support roughly 500 construction jobs," Nathan said. State Senator Theresa Fedor welcomed the announcement, noting that Toledo commuters have waited nearly a decade for repairs to the aging structures.

The Ohio Department of Transportation will also coordinate with the Federal Highway Administration, which is contributing $12 million in matching funds under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. Construction crews are expected to begin mobilizing equipment at the Dayton staging site on May 6, 2024, with the first overpass, near Exit 57 in Miami County, scheduled for closure that week.

Residents seeking updates can attend a public forum on April 2, 2024 at the Dayton Convention Center, where engineers from Kokosing Construction Company will present detailed timelines. Officials emphasized that safety inspections will continue throughout construction, and lane closures will be announced weekly on the department's website.

DETROIT, Sept. 12 - Meridian Motors Inc. announced Tuesday it will acquire EverCharge Systems, a Chicago-based maker of electric-vehicle charging stations, for $740 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by December 1, marks Meridian's largest acquisition since it was founded in 1987 by industrialist Walter Kessner.

Under the agreement, EverCharge chief executive Priya Nandakumar will join Meridian as Executive Vice President of Energy Solutions, reporting directly to Meridian CEO Robert Anholt. Nandakumar founded EverCharge in 2014 and grew it into a supplier of charging infrastructure for fleets across North America, with 2023 revenue of $310 million.

"This acquisition strengthens our position against Tesla and Rivian in the commercial fleet market," Anholt said during a press conference at Meridian's headquarters in Detroit, Michigan. Analysts at Baird Securities said the deal values EverCharge at roughly 2.4 times annual revenue, a premium of about 18 percent over the company's last private valuation.

Meridian shares rose 4.6 percent to $88.12 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of competitor ChargePoint Holdings fell 2.1 percent. The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which Meridian expects within ninety days.

EverCharge, which employs about 1,200 people, will retain its Chicago office and operate as a subsidiary of Meridian. Nandakumar said the combined company plans to open a new manufacturing plant in Austin, Texas, in 2025, creating an estimated 600 jobs.

input: BOSTON, MA -- November 12, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tovorafenib, an experimental kinase inhibitor developed by Day One Biopharmaceuticals, in patients with relapsed pediatric low-grade glioma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh, enrolled 137 children between ages 2 and 17 across 24 sites in the United States and Canada between January 2021 and June 2022. Results, published in The Lancet Oncology, showed an overall response rate of 67 percent, with tumor shrinkage observed in 92 of the 137 participants within six months of treatment. Median progression-free survival reached 20.1 months, compared with 11.4 months in a historical control cohort treated with standard carboplatin-based chemotherapy. Grade 3 adverse events, primarily rash and anemia, occurred in 14 percent of patients, and no treatment-related deaths were reported. Dr. Marsh presented the findings on November 10, 2023, at the Society for Neuro-Oncology annual meeting in San Francisco. "These data suggest tovorafenib could become a first-line option for children who have exhausted conventional therapies," she said. Day One Biopharmaceuticals, headquartered in South San Francisco, California, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the first quarter of 2024. The company's chief executive, Jeremy Bender, stated that a confirmatory Phase 3 trial is already underway at 40 additional sites, including Boston Children's Hospital and The Hospital for Sick Children in Toronto. Analysts at Jefferies estimate peak annual sales could reach $600 million if the drug receives accelerated approval.

MERIDIAN CITY, Oct. 14 — Bankwell Financial Corp. announced Tuesday it will acquire regional lender Coastline Bancshares for $1.2 billion, creating one of the largest banking networks in the Pacific Northwest. The deal, disclosed at a press conference at Bankwell's headquarters in Meridian City, is expected to close by March 2025, pending approval from the Federal Reserve.

Bankwell CEO Denise Ferraro said the acquisition would expand the company's footprint into Oregon and Washington, adding 74 branches and roughly 2,300 employees. "This merger positions Bankwell as a top-five regional lender on the West Coast," Ferraro told reporters. Coastline Bancshares CEO Martin Oduya will join Bankwell's board as vice chairman once the transaction is finalized.

Shares of Coastline Bancshares jumped 18 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $42.30. Bankwell shares slipped 3 percent amid investor concerns over integration costs, which analysts estimate could reach $150 million.

The merger comes two years after Bankwell's failed attempt to acquire Cascade Trust, which collapsed in 2022 over regulatory objections. Industry analyst Priya Nandakumar of Sterling Research called the Coastline deal "a calculated bet on Pacific Northwest growth," noting that Coastline has been a competitor to Bankwell in the Portland market since 2015.

Bankwell, founded in 1987 by Harold Whitfield, is headquartered in Meridian City and currently employs about 6,800 people across 210 branches nationwide.

HARTLAND, Wis. — Mercer Dairy Equipment, a farm machinery manufacturer based in Hartland, Wisconsin, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday after a sharp decline in export orders to Mexico and Canada. Chief Executive Officer Donald Vance announced the filing at a press conference at the company's headquarters, saying the firm owes creditors roughly $42 million, including $11 million to supplier Redwood Steel Corp of Gary, Indiana. Mercer Dairy Equipment, founded in 1978 by Harold Mercer, employs 340 workers and has struggled since tariffs imposed in March 2024 raised the cost of imported aluminum components. Vance said the company will continue operating during restructuring and does not plan immediate layoffs. "We intend to emerge from this process leaner and competitive within twelve months," Vance told reporters. Analysts at Milwaukee-based investment firm Grafton Partners said the bankruptcy reflects broader distress in the Midwest agricultural equipment sector, noting that competitor Iowa Tractor Works reported a 14 percent drop in quarterly revenue last month. Wisconsin Governor Elaine Brooks said the state would review options to support affected workers, including retraining programs through the Department of Workforce Development. The bankruptcy filing was submitted to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Wisconsin, where Judge Patricia Kohl will oversee the case. A first hearing is scheduled for November 18. Local union representative Marcus Webb said roughly 200 union members attended a rally outside the plant on Wednesday demanding job guarantees during the restructuring.

input: Marguerite Okonjo-Voss (born 14 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-American structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques used in the reconstruction of the Loma Linda Viaduct. She earned a Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering from the University of Lagos in 1979 and later completed a doctorate at Stanford University in 1985. In 1988 Okonjo-Voss joined Bechtel Corporation as a Structural Engineer, working out of the company's San Francisco office on seismic-safety assessments for California bridges. She left Bechtel in 1994 to found Voss Structural Partners, a consultancy headquartered in Oakland, California, that grew to employ 140 engineers by 2005. Under her leadership as Chief Executive Officer, the firm was hired in 1999 to retrofit the Loma Linda Viaduct after inspectors found cracking in its support columns. In 2011, Voss Structural Partners was acquired by AECOM for 220 million dollars, and Okonjo-Voss stepped down as Chief Executive Officer that same year, remaining on AECOM's advisory board until 2016. She received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation from President Barack Obama at a ceremony in Washington, D.C. in 2013 for her contributions to earthquake-resilient infrastructure. Okonjo-Voss married fellow engineer Daniel Voss in 1983; the couple's daughter, Amara Voss, later became an architect at Skidmore, Owings & Merrill. Okonjo-Voss currently resides in Berkeley, California, and continues to lecture part-time at the University of California, Berkeley.

input: Zurich-based Alpina Pharmaceuticals AG announced Tuesday that it has agreed to acquire San Diego biotech firm Verinota Therapeutics for $2.4 billion in cash, marking the largest deal in the company's 40-year history. CEO Markus Reinholt confirmed the acquisition during a press conference at Alpina's headquarters in Zurich, Switzerland, saying the deal will close by March 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval from the European Medicines Agency and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Verinota, founded in 2011 by Dr. Elena Castillo, specializes in gene-editing treatments for sickle cell disease and has roughly 340 employees across two facilities in California. Under the terms of the agreement, Alpina will pay Verinota shareholders $58 per share, a 32 percent premium over Tuesday's closing price. Dr. Castillo, who will join Alpina's executive board as Chief Scientific Officer, called the merger "a natural next step" for expanding gene therapy research. Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimate the acquisition could boost Alpina's annual revenue by 18 percent within three years. Shares of Verinota jumped 29 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, while Alpina's stock rose 4 percent on the Swiss Exchange. The deal still requires approval from Verinota's board, expected to vote on the offer by January 10, 2025. Industry observers note the transaction reflects growing competition between Alpina and rival Novantis Biosciences, headquartered in Basel, for dominance in the rare-disease drug market.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solace Robotics announced this morning it has acquired Denton-based sensor startup Fenwick Optics for $42 million in cash. CEO Priya Nandakumar said the deal closes by March 15, 2025.

2/ Fenwick's 38 employees, including founder Marcus Ellery, will join Solace's new Perception Lab, opening in the same Austin building on Riverside Drive.

4/ Nandakumar took over as CEO of Solace Robotics in June 2021, after the board removed founder Tobias Wren following a rocky product recall of the SR-4 delivery drone.

5/ Solace's biggest rival, Denver-based Ionix Dynamics, declined to comment, but its CEO Rachel Ostrander was seen meeting with investors in San Francisco last Thursday, fueling speculation of a counter-deal.

6/ Fun fact: Fenwick's optical sensors already ship inside 12,000 Ionix delivery drones under a supplier agreement signed in 2022 — that contract now sits awkwardly inside a competitor's family.

7/ Solace shares (ticker SLCE) jumped 9 percent on the Nasdaq after the announcement, adding roughly $300 million in market value.

8/ Analysts at Merrick Capital, led by James Okonkwo, called it "the smartest robotics acquisition of 2025." Full report drops Monday.

Marguerite Auclair (born 12 March 1927 in Lyon, France) was a French chemist known for her contributions to polymer science. Auclair earned a doctorate in chemistry from the Sorbonne in 1951 and joined Rhône-Poulenc as a research scientist that same year. In 1963, she was appointed Director of Materials Research at Rhône-Poulenc, a position she held for nearly two decades. Her laboratory developed a heat-resistant polyamide fiber marketed under the name Thermalon, which became widely used in industrial textiles during the 1970s. In 1972, Auclair received the Lavoisier Medal from the French Academy of Sciences in Paris for her work on thermoplastic compounds. She left Rhône-Poulenc in 1981 to become a professor at the University of Strasbourg, where she mentored dozens of graduate students until her retirement in 1994. Auclair married fellow chemist Bernard Fontaine in 1955, and the couple had two children, Isabelle and Thomas Fontaine. She was a longtime member of the Société Chimique de France and served on its executive board from 1975 to 1980. Marguerite Auclair died on 8 September 2011 in Strasbourg at the age of 84. Her personal papers and laboratory notebooks were donated to the Bibliothèque Nationale de France in 2013, providing researchers with a detailed record of her decades-long career in industrial chemistry.

Pixelworks Labs, a hardware division of Meridian Optics Inc., unveiled the Halcyon X7 tablet on September 12, 2024, at a press event in Austin, Texas. Priced at $649 for the 128GB configuration, the Halcyon X7 targets students and creative professionals with a 12.4-inch OLED display and a new Aria M2 chipset designed in-house. I tested the tablet for three weeks before writing this review.

Meridian Optics Inc. was founded in 2011 by Renata Kessler, who still serves as Chief Executive Officer. In an interview, Kessler said the Aria M2 chipset delivers 40 percent better battery efficiency than the previous Halcyon X6 model, a claim borne out by my own testing: the tablet lasted roughly 11 hours on a single charge during video playback.

The build quality is excellent, with an aluminum unibody that feels sturdier than the plastic-backed Halcyon X6. Software, however, is a mixed bag. The Aurora OS 4.0 interface is fast but still lacks a proper file manager, a complaint reviewers raised about last year's model as well.

Competitor Solvane Technologies, based in San Jose, California, recently acquired the startup Fenwick Displays for $180 million, a move analysts say could pressure Meridian on panel pricing. Still, for $649, the Halcyon X7 is one of the more compelling tablets I've reviewed this year, and I recommend it to anyone upgrading from a three-year-old device.

DENVER, June 12 -- Sundrop Energy Corp. said Wednesday it will acquire Basalt Ridge Wind LLC, a privately held wind-power developer based in Boulder, Colorado, for $412 million in cash and stock. The deal, announced by Sundrop chief executive Marta Ilanova, is expected to close by September 30 pending approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. Basalt Ridge operates three wind farms across Wyoming and Nebraska with a combined capacity of 640 megawatts, supplying electricity to utilities including Rocky Mountain Power. Ilanova said the acquisition would make Sundrop the third-largest renewable energy producer in the Mountain West. "This is about scale and speed," Ilanova told reporters during a briefing at Sundrop's Denver headquarters. Basalt Ridge founder Devon Marsh, who started the company in 2011, will join Sundrop as senior vice president of wind operations. Marsh will report directly to Ilanova. Analysts at Cordell Hastings Partners estimated the transaction values Basalt Ridge at roughly 9.5 times projected 2025 earnings, a premium of about 18 percent over its last private valuation. Shares of Sundrop, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker SDRP, rose 6.2 percent to $54.30 following the announcement. Sundrop plans to fund the deal through a combination of $250 million in new debt and existing cash reserves. The company also confirmed it will retain all 210 Basalt Ridge employees. A shareholder vote on the merger is scheduled for August 8 in Denver.

input: Kestrel Outdoor Gear, headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, has launched the Talus 45 backpacking pack, priced at $189.99 and available starting October 3, 2024. Built for multi-day treks, the Talus 45 features a 45-liter capacity, a torso range of 16 to 20 inches, and a carbon-fiber frame that keeps total weight under 2.3 pounds. The pack is manufactured by Kestrel Outdoor Gear at its facility in Missoula and distributed through REI stores across the United States as well as the company's own website. Design lead Priya Nandakumar said the Talus 45 underwent 14 months of field testing in the Bitterroot Mountains before release. Each unit ships with a detachable rain cover, a hydration sleeve compatible with 3-liter reservoirs, and a lifetime warranty against manufacturing defects. Kestrel Outdoor Gear, founded in 2011 by former ski patroller Daniel Ferris, has sold more than 500,000 packs worldwide and competes directly with Osprey Packs and Gregory Mountain Products in the mid-range trekking segment. Early reviewers on Trailhead Monthly gave the Talus 45 a 4.6 out of 5 rating, praising its ventilated back panel and adjustable hip belt. The pack is currently in stock in three colorways: Slate Gray, Moss Green, and Rust Orange, with sizes Small through X-Large. Customers who order before November 1, 2024 will receive a free 32-ounce Nalgene bottle. This is a brand-new product, not a refurbished or returned unit.

Ingrid Halvorsen (born 14 March 1957 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist and former Director of the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø. She earned a Doctor of Philosophy in Oceanography from the University of Bergen in 1984, having studied under Professor Lars Eikeland. In 1989 Halvorsen joined the Institute of Marine Research as a research scientist, and in 2001 she was elected Director of the institute at a ceremony held in Tromsø. During her tenure she led three expeditions aboard the research vessel Johan Hjort to study cod populations in the Barents Sea. In 2008 she founded the nonprofit organization Nordic Ocean Watch in Oslo, with funding of 4.2 million Norwegian kroner provided by the Fram Foundation. Halvorsen stepped down as Director in March 2015, citing a wish to focus on fieldwork. For her contributions to fisheries science, she received the Kristine Bonnevie Prize from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo in October 2016. She is married to Torbjørn Halvorsen, a marine engineer, and the couple have one daughter, Maren, born in 1990. Halvorsen currently serves as a professor of marine ecology at the University of Bergen, where she has published more than 90 papers on Arctic cod and Calanus finmarchicus, a species of zooplankton central to Barents Sea food webs. In 2022 she was appointed to the Norwegian Polar Research Board by the Ministry of Climate and Environment.

input: The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday, 12 March 2024 that the City of Rotterdam will receive 45 million euros to upgrade the Maasvlakte rail terminal, part of a broader plan to reduce freight congestion at the Port of Rotterdam. Minister Els Kramer, speaking at a press briefing in The Hague, said the funding would be disbursed by the National Infrastructure Fund to ProRail, the state-owned rail operator, over the next 18 months. "This investment reflects our commitment to sustainable logistics," Kramer said, adding that construction would begin in September 2024 and create approximately 300 jobs. The project follows a 2023 feasibility study conducted by TU Delft, which found that current rail capacity at Maasvlakte was insufficient to handle a projected 12 percent increase in container traffic by 2027. Officials from ProRail, including chief executive Pieter van Dam, welcomed the announcement. Van Dam stated that ProRail would begin hiring contractors by June 2024 and expects the terminal expansion to be completed by the end of 2026. The Ministry also confirmed that a separate agreement worth 8 million euros had been signed with Deutsche Bahn to coordinate cross-border freight scheduling between Rotterdam and Duisburg. Opposition lawmaker Frans Bakker criticized the plan on Wednesday, arguing that the budget should instead prioritize passenger rail delays affecting commuters in Utrecht and Amsterdam. The Ministry of Transport is expected to submit a detailed implementation report to the Dutch Parliament by 1 October 2024.

DETROIT, Mich. -- Ferrostone Industries Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Bramwell Tool & Die, a Dearborn-based auto parts supplier, for $214 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by December 15, 2024, will make Bramwell a wholly owned subsidiary of Ferrostone and expand its footprint in the Midwest manufacturing sector.

Ferrostone's chief executive officer, Denise Okafor, said the acquisition strengthens the company's supply chain for its largest customer, Halden Motors Corporation, which is headquartered in Warren, Michigan. "Bramwell has been a trusted supplier to Halden for over 15 years, and this acquisition secures that relationship for the long term," Okafor said during a press briefing at Ferrostone's headquarters.

Bramwell's founder and outgoing president, Gerald Bramwell, will step down from his position on January 3, 2025, after leading the company for 22 years. He will be succeeded by Priya Nandakumar, currently a senior vice president at Ferrostone, who will officially start as president that same day.

The transaction, financed partly through a $150 million loan from Meridian National Bank, still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Analysts at Cormorant Capital Partners estimate the deal could boost Ferrostone's annual revenue by 8 percent, pushing it past $2.6 billion. Shares of Ferrostone rose 4.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $67.82.

On March 14, 2024, Judge Alicia Ferrante sentenced Marcus D. Ellison, 37, to 8 years in state prison after a jury in Atlanta convicted him of armed robbery and aggravated assault stemming from an incident at Sunrise Pawn & Loan on Peachtree Street on November 2, 2023. Prosecutor Daniel Whitfield of the Fulton County District Attorney's Office argued that Ellison entered the store brandishing a Glock 19 handgun and struck clerk Ramon Osei with the weapon before fleeing with approximately $4,200 in cash and jewelry. Osei was treated for a fractured jaw at Grady Memorial Hospital and has since recovered.

Ellison was arrested on November 5, 2023, by detectives with the Atlanta Police Department following a tip that led them to a rented apartment in East Point, Georgia. Defense attorney Rosalind Kaur contended that her client acted under duress but did not dispute his presence at the scene.

Judge Ferrante, presiding at the Fulton County Courthouse, also ordered Ellison to pay $4,200 in restitution to Sunrise Pawn & Loan. The sentencing hearing, held on March 14, 2024, drew a small crowd of onlookers, including members of Osei's family. Whitfield told reporters afterward that his office remains committed to prosecuting violent crime across metropolitan Atlanta. Ellison's attorney indicated she plans to file an appeal with the Georgia Court of Appeals within the statutory 30-day window.

DALLAS, Texas — Trinova Energy Corp. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Redfield Pipeline Systems, a privately held natural gas infrastructure firm based in Tulsa, Oklahoma, for approximately $412 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at Trinova's headquarters in Dallas, marks the company's largest acquisition since its founding in 2004 by chief executive officer Marcus Whitfield.

Under the terms of the agreement, Trinova will pay $412 million to Redfield's shareholders by March 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. Redfield's founder and president, Elena Cortez, will join Trinova's board of directors as part of the transition. "This acquisition strengthens our position across the Permian Basin and gives us direct access to over 1,800 miles of pipeline," Whitfield said during a press briefing in Dallas on Tuesday.

Analysts at Bartlett & Kohl Securities noted that Trinova's stock rose 6.3 percent following the announcement, closing at $58.20 per share on the New York Stock Exchange. Rival firm Caldwell Midstream Partners, headquartered in Houston, has reportedly been exploring a competing bid for Redfield since November.

Trinova also confirmed that Sandra Liu, previously senior vice president of operations, will step down from her role effective April 1, 2025, to pursue an opportunity at a Denver-based startup. The company expects the Redfield integration to be complete by the third quarter of 2025, adding roughly 340 employees to its workforce.
