DETROIT, Mich. — Meridian Steelworks Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing a 42% drop in orders and $310 million in outstanding debt. The filing, made in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan, marks the end of the company's 78-year run as an independent manufacturer.

CEO Harold Beckman told reporters at a press conference that the company had struggled since losing a major supply contract with Ford Motor Company in March 2023. "We fought hard to keep our 1,200 employees working, but rising steel costs and falling demand left us no options," Beckman said.

Meridian Steelworks, founded in 1946 by industrialist Walter Krantz, employs workers across three facilities in Michigan, Ohio, and Indiana. Analysts at Cormorant Capital Partners estimate liquidation could begin as early as January 15, 2025, if no buyer emerges.

Union representative Diane Ostrowski, who leads Local 771 of the United Steelworkers, said members were "blindsided" by the announcement. Roughly 300 workers gathered outside the company's Detroit headquarters on Wednesday to demand severance guarantees.

The bankruptcy follows a turbulent year for the American steel industry, which has seen at least four mid-sized producers collapse since January 2024. Governor Elena Ramirez said the state would explore emergency funding to help affected workers transition to new jobs. A hearing before Judge Patricia Nowak is scheduled for November 20, 2024.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- Nautilus Biosciences Inc. announced on October 14, 2024 that it has acquired Kestrel Diagnostics LLC, a privately held maker of point-of-care blood-testing devices, for $340 million in cash and stock. Kestrel Diagnostics, founded in 2016 by Dr. Priya Nathan, employs 210 people across its facility in Austin, Texas. Dr. Nathan will join Nautilus Biosciences as Chief Innovation Officer effective November 1, 2024, reporting directly to Nautilus CEO Marcus Reinholt.

"This is a pivotal step in our mission to expand rapid diagnostics access," said Marcus Reinholt, who has led Nautilus Biosciences since 2019. "Priya and her team have built something extraordinary, and we intend to scale the RapidScan 500 to serve clinics across Europe and Southeast Asia by 2026."

The deal was financed through a combination of $200 million in senior notes issued by Nautilus Biosciences and $140 million in existing cash reserves. Goldman Sachs advised Nautilus Biosciences on the transaction, while Kestrel Diagnostics was represented by Cooley LLP.

Nautilus Biosciences shares rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.10. The company expects the acquisition to be accretive to earnings by the second quarter of 2025.

Nautilus Biosciences, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs approximately 3,400 people worldwide and reported revenue of $1.2 billion in fiscal year 2023.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., June 10, 2024 -- Meridian BioSciences Inc. today announced that it has acquired NovaGen Therapeutics, a privately held gene-therapy startup based in Cambridge, for $340 million in cash and stock. The acquisition, completed on June 7, 2024, adds NovaGen's lead candidate, a treatment for sickle cell disease called Hemoxelin, to Meridian's pipeline.

Under the terms of the agreement, Meridian will pay $220 million upfront and up to $120 million in milestone payments tied to regulatory approvals from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. NovaGen was founded in 2018 by Dr. Priya Sharma, who will join Meridian as Chief Scientific Officer effective July 1, 2024.

"This acquisition strengthens our position in rare disease therapeutics," said Meridian CEO Thomas Reilly, speaking at a press conference held at the company's headquarters in Cambridge. "Hemoxelin has shown remarkable results in Phase 2 trials, reducing painful episodes by 62 percent among 140 patients."

Dr. Sharma, who previously worked at Genzyme Corporation for nine years, said she was proud of the team's progress. "We started this company with just four employees in a small lab in Somerville," she said.

Meridian BioSciences, headquartered in Cambridge, employs approximately 2,300 people worldwide and reported revenue of $1.8 billion in 2023. The deal is expected to close regulatory review by September 2024, pending clearance from the Federal Trade Commission.

Pixelbook Labs, a hardware startup headquartered in Austin, Texas, unveiled the Aria S2 wireless earbuds on June 4, 2024, at a small press event held at the Driskill Hotel. Founded in 2019 by former Dell engineer Priya Nandakumar, the company has struggled to differentiate itself in a crowded market dominated by Sony and Apple. The Aria S2, priced at $179, ships on July 15, 2024, and promises 38 hours of total battery life with the charging case, up from 24 hours on the original Aria model released in 2021.

I tested a review unit for eleven days around Austin and on a short flight to Denver. Sound quality is genuinely impressive: the custom 11mm drivers produce a warm low end without muddying vocals, and active noise cancellation rivals Sony's WF-1000XM5, at least in quieter environments. Call quality, however, is inconsistent; three separate callers on a walk near Lady Bird Lake said my voice cut out intermittently.

Battery life mostly held up, though I measured closer to 34 hours rather than the advertised 38. The companion app, available for iOS and Android, is sparse but functional, offering a three-band equalizer and a "Find My Buds" feature.

At $179, the Aria S2 undercuts Apple's AirPods Pro by $70 while matching most of its features. Pixelbook Labs still needs to prove it can support the product long-term, but for now, the Aria S2 is a legitimately strong option for budget-conscious buyers who don't need a big brand name.

Dr. Amara Osei (born 14 March 1958 in Kumasi, Ghana) is a Ghanaian-British biochemist known for her work on antimalarial compounds. She earned a Bachelor of Science from the University of Ghana in 1980 and a Ph.D. in biochemistry from the University of Oxford in 1985. In 1990, Osei joined the Wellcome Trust Centre in London as a Research Fellow, where she began studying the parasite Plasmodium falciparum, the primary cause of malaria.

In 1997, she co-founded Solara Therapeutics in Cambridge, United Kingdom, alongside chemist Dr. Nigel Ashworth, to develop treatments for tropical diseases. The company later relocated its headquarters to Basel, Switzerland, in 2003. Under her leadership as Chief Scientific Officer, Solara Therapeutics developed the compound artenolimod, which received regulatory approval in the European Union in 2011.

Osei received the Royal Society Africa Prize in 2014 in London for her contributions to malaria research. In 2016, Novartis acquired Solara Therapeutics for approximately 420 million dollars, and Osei stepped down as Chief Scientific Officer that same year.

She married economist Dr. Kwame Mensah in 1988; the couple has two children. Osei currently serves as a visiting professor at Imperial College London and continues to advise the World Health Organization on malaria eradication strategies. She holds British and Ghanaian citizenship and speaks English, Twi, and French fluently.

On November 14, 2024, Judge Marisol Ferreira sentenced Dwayne T. Holloway, 41, to 46 months in state prison after a jury found him guilty of grand theft and embezzlement in connection with his former position as Chief Financial Officer of Berkline Textiles Inc., a garment manufacturer headquartered in Oakland, California. Prosecutor Angela Nkemelu of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Holloway diverted $612,400 from company accounts between March 2021 and July 2023, routing the funds through a shell entity called Coastal Ledger Partners LLC.

The trial, held at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, began on October 2, 2024 and lasted eleven days. Holloway was arrested on September 8, 2023 by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation after Berkline's board, led by CEO Priya Ramaswamy, discovered irregularities during an internal audit. Defense attorney Marcus Whitfield contended that his client acted under duress from a former business partner, but the jury rejected the claim on October 21, 2024.

Judge Ferreira also ordered Holloway to pay $612,400 in restitution to Berkline Textiles Inc. within five years of his release. Ramaswamy, who assumed leadership of Berkline in January 2020, said in a statement outside the courthouse that "justice was served for our employees and shareholders." Holloway's attorney indicated he plans to file an appeal with the California Court of Appeal within 60 days.

DETROIT, Nov. 14 -- Stellantis NV agreed to acquire a 62 percent stake in electric-truck maker Rivian Automotive's battery unit for $1.4 billion, the companies announced Tuesday. The deal, expected to close by March 2025, will give Stellantis access to Rivian's lithium-iron-phosphate cell technology as automakers race to cut battery costs. Rivian, headquartered in Irvine, California, will use the proceeds to expand production at its plant in Normal, Illinois, where it builds the R1T pickup and R1S SUV. Stellantis Chief Executive Carlos Tavares said the investment strengthens the company's position against Tesla and China's BYD in the North American EV market. "This partnership accelerates our electrification roadmap," Tavares told reporters at a press briefing in Auburn Hills, Michigan. Rivian founder and CEO RJ Scaringe said the capital injection would help the company reach positive gross margin by the fourth quarter of 2025. Shares of Rivian jumped 11 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, while Stellantis stock rose 3 percent in Milan trading. Analysts at Morgan Stanley called the agreement a sign of consolidation in the EV supply chain, noting that smaller battery startups may struggle to compete. The transaction still requires approval from antitrust regulators in the United States and the European Union, a process executives expect to conclude within four months. Separately, Rivian confirmed it will lay off 140 employees at its Illinois facility as part of a cost-restructuring plan announced last month.

input: Cedar Point Industrial, a Toledo, Ohio-based maker of hydraulic pumps, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Bramwell Fluid Systems for $118 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing at Cedar Point's headquarters, is expected to close by March 31, 2025, pending regulatory approval. Bramwell, headquartered in Akron, Ohio, employs roughly 340 workers and posted revenue of $62 million last year, according to CEO Marcus Delgado. Cedar Point's chief executive, Priya Ramaswamy, said the acquisition would let the company expand into aerospace-grade valve components and compete more directly with Chicago-based Hartline Corp. "This gives us the scale to challenge Hartline in a market we've watched from the sidelines," Ramaswamy told reporters. Shares of Cedar Point, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker CPIN, rose 6.2 percent to $47.85 following the announcement, while privately held Bramwell does not trade publicly. Analysts at Fenwick Capital Partners called the price a 12 percent premium over Bramwell's estimated book value. Delgado, who founded Bramwell in 1998, will step down as CEO once the transaction closes and will be succeeded by current operations chief Denise Whitfield. Cedar Point plans to retain Bramwell's Akron plant and add 75 jobs there by the end of 2025. The company financed the purchase through a combination of $70 million in cash reserves and a $48 million loan from Third Meridian Bank.

Cleveland, OH – November 4, 2023. Researchers at Case Western Reserve University announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tarlorafenib, an investigational oral kinase inhibitor developed by Meridian Biotherapeutics, for adults with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia. The multicenter study, led by principal investigator Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran, enrolled 142 patients across 11 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2021 and June 2023. Participants received either 200 mg of tarlorafenib daily or standard-of-care azacitidine. At the 18-month follow-up, 47 percent of patients in the tarlorafenib arm achieved complete remission compared with 26 percent in the azacitidine group, a difference the authors described as statistically significant (p=0.003). Median overall survival was 19.4 months versus 11.2 months, respectively. The most common grade 3 or higher adverse event was neutropenia, occurring in 34 percent of tarlorafenib-treated patients, followed by thrombocytopenia in 21 percent. Three patients discontinued treatment due to hepatotoxicity. Dr. Chandrasekaran presented the findings on November 3, 2023, at the American Society of Hematology conference in San Diego, and the full dataset was submitted to the Journal of Clinical Oncology for peer review. Meridian Biotherapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, stated it plans to file for accelerated approval with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2024. The company's chief executive officer, Daniel Osei, said the drug could become a first-line option for elderly AML patients who cannot tolerate intensive chemotherapy. Funding for the trial was provided by the National Cancer Institute under grant R01-CA248871.

Portland, Oregon-based Cascadia Freight Corp. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired regional logistics rival Timberline Transit Inc. for $412 million in cash and stock, marking the company's largest deal to date. The acquisition, expected to close by December 15, 2024, will expand Cascadia's fleet by 340 trucks and add three distribution centers in Idaho and Montana. Chief Executive Officer Marcus Whitfield told analysts during a call from the company's headquarters that the merger positions Cascadia to compete more directly with national carrier Rocky Mountain Haulage. "This is about scale and speed," Whitfield said. "Timberline's network in the Pacific Northwest fills a critical gap for us." Timberline founder and outgoing president Elena Castillo will step down from her position effective January 3, 2025, after eleven years leading the company she started in Boise. She will receive a severance payment of $6.5 million as part of the agreement. Shares of Cascadia Freight rose 8 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $47.22. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners raised their price target on the stock to $55, citing improved margins from consolidated routes. The deal still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which is expected to review the transaction over the next 90 days. Cascadia, founded in 1987 by Harold Ness, currently employs roughly 4,200 workers across seven states.

1/ Big week for the EV charging space. ChargePoint Holdings confirmed today it acquired Voltera Networks, a Denver-based startup, for $42 million in cash and stock. Deal closed Tuesday, March 11, 2025.

2/ Voltera's founder, Priya Nandakumar, will join ChargePoint as VP of Network Operations starting April 1, 2025. She founded Voltera back in 2019 with just 6 employees.

3/ ChargePoint CEO Rick Wilmer called it "a natural fit" during a call with investors from the company's Campbell, California headquarters this morning.

4/ Meanwhile, 200 Voltera employees in Denver will be relocated or offered remote roles. No layoffs announced yet, per an internal memo obtained by TechCrunch reporter Danny Torres.

5/ This is ChargePoint's third acquisition since 2022, following its purchase of ViriCiti for $45 million. Competitor EVgo has stayed quiet on the news so far.

6/ Shares of ChargePoint (NYSE: CHPT) rose 8% in after-hours trading Tuesday. Analysts at Morgan Stanley say the Voltera deal could add 15% to ChargePoint's network coverage across the American Midwest by late 2026.

7/ Nandakumar tweeted: "Proud of what we built. Excited for what's next with the ChargePoint team." Congrats to everyone at Voltera Networks.

The Ohio Department of Transportation announced on March 14, 2024 that it will allocate $42 million to repair the Interstate 70 bridge spanning the Scioto River near Columbus. ODOT Director Pamela Boykin-Wilson stated that the project, scheduled to begin on April 1, 2024, will take approximately 14 months to complete and is expected to reduce commuter delays by 30 percent once finished. The funding was approved after a formal review by the Ohio General Assembly, which authorized the transfer of state highway funds during a session held in Columbus on March 5, 2024. Governor Mike DeWine praised the initiative, noting that the bridge, originally built in 1968, has deteriorated significantly and poses safety risks to the roughly 85,000 vehicles that cross it daily. The contract for construction was awarded to Kokosing Construction Company, headquartered in Fredericktown, Ohio, following a competitive bidding process that concluded last month. Kokosing will subcontract portions of the work to Trucco Construction, based in Massillon. ODOT officials confirmed that lane closures will begin at 9:00 p.m. on April 1, 2024, and that two of the four lanes will remain open throughout construction to minimize disruption. Local officials, including Columbus Mayor Andrew Ginther, welcomed the announcement, calling it a critical investment in regional infrastructure. The department also noted that a similar bridge repair on State Route 315 was completed in 2022 under a $19 million contract, also awarded to Kokosing.

Denver-based Sable Peak Foods Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Boulder Creek Snacks LLC, a privately held maker of dried fruit bars, for $42 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing in Denver, Colorado, is expected to close by November 15, 2024, pending regulatory review. Sable Peak's chief executive officer, Marissa Uhl, said the acquisition would expand the company's presence in the natural snack aisle at grocery chains across the American Midwest. "Boulder Creek has built a loyal following over the past decade, and we intend to keep its factory in Longmont, Colorado running at full capacity," Uhl said. Boulder Creek's founder, Tyler Ransome, started the company in 2011 and grew annual revenue to roughly $18 million by 2023. Ransome will stay on as a consultant for six months but will step down as president effective November 15, 2024. Sable Peak, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker SPFI, saw its shares rise 4.2 percent to $27.85 following the announcement. Analysts at Kestrel Capital Partners, including senior analyst Devon Marchetti, called the purchase a smart bolt-on that should add roughly $6 million to operating profit within two years. The transaction is Sable Peak's third acquisition since 2020, following its purchase of GrainWell Organics in 2021. Boulder Creek employs 140 workers and will retain its brand name under the new ownership structure.

MANCHESTER, England -- October 14, 2024 -- Fulham striker Marcus Webb scored twice as Fulham defeated Everton 3-1 at Craven Cottage on Saturday, lifting the club to fifth place in the Premier League table. Webb, 27, opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a header from a corner delivered by midfielder Tomas Rivera, then added a second in the 58th minute after a swift counterattack. Everton striker Declan Foy pulled one back in the 71st minute, but a late strike from substitute Aaron Mensah in the 89th minute sealed the win for Fulham in front of 24,500 fans.

Head coach Marco Silva, who took charge of Fulham in 2021, praised his team's discipline after the match. "We defended as a unit and punished them on the break," Silva told reporters at the post-match press conference held inside Craven Cottage. Everton manager Sean Dyche acknowledged his side's struggles, saying the team lacked composure in the final third.

The victory extended Fulham's unbeaten run to six matches and moved them level on points with Newcastle United ahead of next weekend's fixture against Brighton on October 21. Fulham's chairman, Shahid Khan, was present at the stadium and was seen congratulating the squad afterward. The Premier League confirmed that Webb's brace earned him the Player of the Match award, presented by former England international Rio Ferdinand.

Elsewhere, Everton will look to regroup before hosting Aston Villa at Goodison Park on October 19.

Fjallhaven Gear, a Portland-based outdoor equipment company founded in 2011 by Anders Kjell, has released the Talus 45 backpack, priced at $189.00 and available starting October 3, 2024. The Talus 45 is built from 500-denier recycled Cordura fabric and weighs 3.1 pounds, making it a favorite among backpackers tackling the Pacific Crest Trail. Fjallhaven Gear manufactures the pack at its facility in Bend, Oregon, and ships orders within 2 business days via FedEx Ground. Each unit includes a lifetime warranty against manufacturing defects, a feature the company has offered since 2015. Customer reviews on the Fjallhaven Gear website average 4.7 out of 5 stars from over 1,200 verified buyers. The pack comes in three colorways: Slate Gray, Moss Green, and Rust Orange, and holds up to 45 liters of gear, roughly enough for a 4-day trip. Competitors such as Osprey and Gregory Mountain Products offer similar packs in the $150 to $220 range, but the Talus 45's adjustable torso length, ranging from 16 to 22 inches, sets it apart for hikers of varying heights. Fjallhaven Gear last month announced a partnership with REI Co-op to stock the Talus 45 in 120 retail locations across the United States starting November 15, 2024. The company, which employs 68 people, is currently accepting pre-orders directly through its website, with expected delivery within 10 to 14 days of purchase.

Pixelworks Labs, a Portland-based startup founded by former Intel engineer Marcus Delaney, unveiled its long-awaited Halcyon X1 mirrorless camera on June 4, 2024, at a press event in San Jose, California. Priced at $2,499, the Halcyon X1 targets professional photographers who currently rely on the Canon EOS R5 or the Sony Alpha 7 IV. I spent three weeks testing a review unit provided by the company, and the results are impressive, if not entirely surprising given Delaney's background in image-signal processing.

The X1 uses a 45-megapixel stacked sensor and a new chip Pixelworks Labs calls the Halcyon Engine, which the company claims processes RAW files 40 percent faster than competing chips from Qualcomm. In low light, the camera handled ISO 12800 with noticeably less grain than my Sony reference body. Battery life, rated at 620 shots per charge, held up during a full day shooting a wedding in Napa Valley.

Pixelworks Labs was acquired in part by Adobe Inc. last month, with Adobe taking a 15 percent equity stake for $30 million to integrate the Halcyon Engine's processing pipeline into Lightroom. CEO Shantanu Narayen said in a statement that the partnership would "redefine mobile-to-desktop RAW workflows." Whether that promise holds, the X1 is, at minimum, the most interesting camera announcement of 2024. My only complaint: the menu system, clearly inherited from a rushed firmware build, still lags behind Fujifilm's interface.

Recommended, cautiously, at four out of five stars.

MERIDIAN, Ohio — Copperfield Robotics Inc., a Columbus-based manufacturer of industrial automation systems, announced on Tuesday, June 11, 2024, that it has acquired Vantree Sensors LLC, a privately held sensor developer based in Austin, Texas, for approximately 42 million dollars in cash and stock.

Under the agreement, Copperfield will absorb Vantree's 65 employees and integrate its flagship LiDAR module, the Vantree Pulse-X, into Copperfield's ArmLine series of warehouse robots. The deal is expected to close by August 1, 2024, pending regulatory review.

"This acquisition strengthens our sensing capabilities and accelerates our roadmap by roughly 18 months," said Rachel Nomura, Chief Executive Officer of Copperfield Robotics, during a press briefing held at the company's headquarters in Columbus.

Vantree Sensors was founded in 2016 by engineer Devon Marsh, who will join Copperfield as Vice President of Sensor Engineering effective July 15, 2024. Marsh's predecessor at Vantree, co-founder Elena Petrova, stepped down as Chief Technology Officer last month and will not be joining Copperfield.

Copperfield shares rose 6 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, closing at 34.50 dollars. Analysts at Fairmont Capital called the move a "defensive play" against competitor Halberd Dynamics, which has expanded aggressively in the automation sector since 2021.

Copperfield Robotics, founded in 2009 by Thomas Reyes, employs more than 1,200 people across three facilities in Ohio and Michigan.

SUPERIOR COURT OF SANTA CLARA COUNTY, CALIFORNIA

On September 12, 2024, Judge Marion Alvarez sentenced Kevin Draper, 41, of San Jose, to 30 months in state prison after a jury convicted him of grand theft and computer fraud. Prosecutor Elena Ruiz of the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office argued that Draper, formerly employed as a network administrator at Tellurian Systems Inc., accessed company servers without authorization between March 2023 and July 2023 and diverted $185,000 from client accounts into a personal account at Bayshore Credit Union.

The trial, held at the Hall of Justice in San Jose, began on July 8, 2024. Defense attorney Marcus Ohene contended that Draper had been wrongly terminated and acted out of retaliation rather than financial motive, but the jury rejected that argument on August 2, 2024. Tellurian Systems Inc., headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, is a subsidiary of Halden Networks Corporation, which reported the breach to the FBI in August 2023.

Judge Alvarez ordered Draper to pay restitution of $185,000 to Tellurian Systems Inc. within five years of his release. "This was a calculated betrayal of trust," Ruiz told reporters outside the courthouse. Draper's attorney said he intends to file an appeal with the Sixth District Court of Appeal within 60 days. Draper is currently being held at Elmwood Correctional Facility pending transfer.

input: BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tirvexlimab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cascade Biotherapeutics for treatment of relapsed acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The study, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar, enrolled 142 adult patients across 11 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants received 4 mg/kg of tirvexlimab intravenously every 21 days for up to six cycles. According to results published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, 46 percent of patients achieved complete remission, compared with 22 percent in the control arm receiving standard cytarabine chemotherapy. Median overall survival was 14.8 months in the treatment group versus 8.3 months in controls. The most common adverse event was febrile neutropenia, reported in 31 patients, followed by mild infusion reactions in 19 patients. Two patients died during the trial period due to sepsis unrelated to the study drug. Cascade Biotherapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, plans to file for accelerated approval with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. Dr. Nandakumar presented the findings on March 12, 2024, at the American Society of Hematology regional meeting in Chicago, Illinois. "These results suggest a meaningful survival benefit for patients who previously had few options," she said. The trial was funded in part by a $12 million grant from the National Institutes of Health. Cascade Biotherapeutics was founded in 2018 by former Genentech scientist Dr. Marcus Feldman, who now serves as Chief Scientific Officer. The company's stock rose 18 percent following the announcement.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- Nov 12, 2023 -- Verdant Biosciences Inc. announced today that it has acquired Halix Diagnostics Ltd, a Dublin-based maker of rapid pathogen-detection kits, for $210 million in cash. The acquisition, finalized on November 10, 2023, gives Verdant full ownership of Halix's flagship product, the RapidScreen-9 assay, which detects Klebsiella pneumoniae and other bacterial pathogens within 15 minutes.

Verdant's chief executive officer, Priya Nathan, said the deal strengthens the company's diagnostics portfolio ahead of an anticipated expansion into European markets. "Halix has built something genuinely useful for hospitals in Ireland and the United Kingdom," Nathan said during a call with investors from Verdant's headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts. "This positions us to compete directly with Belgravia Diagnostics, which currently controls roughly 22 percent of the European rapid-testing market."

As part of the transaction, Halix founder Conor Malloy will join Verdant as Senior Vice President of European Operations, effective December 1, 2023. Malloy founded Halix Diagnostics in 2016 in Dublin and grew it to 340 employees before the sale.

Verdant, which trades on the NASDAQ under the ticker VRDT, reported quarterly revenue of $87.4 million last month. Analysts at Fenwick Capital Partners project the Halix deal will add $40 million in annual revenue starting in fiscal year 2024. Verdant's board, led by chairwoman Elena Rocha, approved the acquisition unanimously on November 8, 2023.

input: The Ministry of Transport announced on 14 March 2024 that the city of Rotterdam will receive 42 million euros to upgrade its public bus fleet under the National Clean Mobility Plan. Minister Els Bergkamp confirmed the funding during a press briefing at the Rotterdam City Hall, stating that 120 diesel buses operated by RET Rotterdam will be replaced with electric models manufactured by VDL Groep before December 2025. The initiative follows a similar rollout in Utrecht, where the transit operator U-OV retired 65 diesel vehicles last year. According to Minister Bergkamp, the Netherlands aims to cut carbon emissions from public transport by 30 percent by 2030, in line with the European Union's Green Deal targets. RET Rotterdam's director, Willem Van Dijk, welcomed the announcement, noting that the first 15 electric buses will begin operating on Route 33 by June 2024. The Ministry also confirmed that the Port of Rotterdam Authority will contribute an additional 5 million euros toward charging infrastructure at the Waalhaven depot. Opposition lawmaker Sanne Dekkers criticized the timeline as too slow, arguing that faster electrification is needed to meet the 2030 goal. The Ministry of Transport is expected to publish a detailed implementation schedule by 1 September 2024, and a follow-up review will be conducted jointly with the municipality of Rotterdam and RET Rotterdam in early 2025.

To: Marta Fenwick, VP Finance, Caldera Bioscience Inc.
From: Dominic Ruiz, Corporate Development, Lattice Health Partners
Date: March 4, 2024
Re: Acquisition of Nuvera Diagnostics assets

Dear Marta,

Following our meeting in Boston on February 27, 2024, I am pleased to confirm that Lattice Health Partners has agreed to acquire Nuvera Diagnostics, a subsidiary of Caldera Bioscience Inc. headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for a total price of $42 million. The deal is expected to close by April 15, 2024, pending clearance from the Federal Trade Commission.

Under the terms discussed, Lattice Health Partners will pay Caldera Bioscience Inc. an initial installment of $30 million upon signing, with the remaining $12 million disbursed within 90 days of closing. Nuvera Diagnostics' flagship product, the OncoScan-3 assay, will continue to be produced by its manufacturing facility in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina.

As part of this transition, Dr. Priya Nathan will step down as President of Nuvera Diagnostics effective April 15, 2024, and Caldera Bioscience Inc. has named Thomas Kellerman as her successor at the parent company's board meeting held on March 1, 2024, in Cambridge.

We anticipate that this acquisition will strengthen Lattice Health Partners' position against competitors such as Quorix Diagnostics in the molecular diagnostics market. Please let me know if you require additional documentation ahead of the April 15 closing date.

Best regards,
Dominic Ruiz
Director, Corporate Development
Lattice Health Partners

Pixel Tab 3, Google's first tablet since 2019, went on sale Tuesday, March 11, 2025, at a starting price of $499 for the 128GB Wi-Fi model. Reviewed here after two weeks with the device in Austin, Texas, the Pixel Tab 3 pairs a 11-inch OLED display with Google's Tensor G4 chip, the same silicon found in the Pixel 9 phone. Rick Osterloh, Google's senior vice president of devices, told reporters in Mountain View, California that the tablet was built to compete directly with Apple's iPad Air and Samsung's Galaxy Tab S9. In daily use, the screen is genuinely excellent, and the included Charging Speaker Dock, sold separately for $129, makes the tablet surprisingly capable as a kitchen display. Battery life is the standout: I got roughly 11 hours of video playback on a single charge, slightly ahead of the 10.5 hours Google advertises. Software is where the Pixel Tab 3 falls short. Android 15's tablet multitasking still feels unfinished compared with Apple's iPadOS 18, and only a handful of apps, including Canva and Spotify, have been properly optimized for the larger screen. Google says more updates are coming by June 2025. Lenovo and Motorola, both of which sell budget Android tablets, will struggle to compete on specs alone, but Google's software gap is real. At $499, the Pixel Tab 3 is a strong first effort let down by an ecosystem that still treats tablets as an afterthought. I'd recommend it cautiously, mainly to households already invested in Google's services.

AUSTIN, TEXAS — May 14, 2024 — Vantage Robotics Inc., a maker of industrial automation systems, announced today that it has acquired Del Rio Sensors LLC, a privately held sensor manufacturer based in San Antonio, Texas, for approximately $42 million in cash and stock.

The deal, which closed on May 10, 2024, brings Del Rio Sensors' 85 employees and its proprietary LIDAR technology under the Vantage Robotics brand. Del Rio Sensors will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary and retain its current name.

"This acquisition strengthens our position against competitors like Helix Dynamics and accelerates our roadmap by at least two years," said Marcus Webb, Chief Executive Officer of Vantage Robotics, during a press briefing held at the company's Austin headquarters.

Del Rio Sensors was founded in 2016 by engineer Priya Nandakumar, who will join Vantage Robotics as Vice President of Sensor Engineering effective June 1, 2024. Nandakumar previously worked at Texas Instruments for nine years before starting her own company.

Vantage Robotics, headquartered in Austin, Texas, was itself founded in 2011 by Marcus Webb and reported revenue of $310 million last year. The company employs roughly 1,200 people across three facilities in Texas and Arizona.

Analysts at Bramwell Capital called the acquisition "a smart, defensive move" in a note published Tuesday. Shares of Vantage Robotics, which trades privately, were not affected by public market reaction.

The combined entity plans to unveil a new product line, the Vantage SensorPro 9000, at the National Robotics Expo in Dallas on September 18, 2024.

Bergström Audio, a manufacturer based in Malmö, Sweden, has released the Halcyon HA-7 planar magnetic headphones, priced at $749 and available starting November 3, 2024 through the company's online store and select retailers including Crutchfield in Virginia. The HA-7 features 90mm planar drivers, a detachable 1.8-meter OFC cable, and a walnut-and-aluminum housing that weighs 412 grams. Each unit ships in a hard-shell case with a Bergström Audio-branded microfiber cloth and a 2-year limited warranty. According to lead engineer Freja Lindqvist, who joined Bergström Audio in March 2019 after leaving Sennheiser, the driver design took roughly 14 months to finalize and was tested against competitor Focal's Clear Mg headphones during development. "We wanted something that could compete directly with the Clear Mg on soundstage while undercutting it by nearly $300," Lindqvist said in a statement issued from the company's Malmö headquarters. The HA-7 is currently listed as new condition, with an initial production run of 3,000 units. Early reviewers, including audio outlet StereoNet, have praised the midrange clarity but noted the open-back design leaks sound, making it unsuitable for office use. Bergström Audio was founded in 2011 by siblings Anders and Elin Bergström and remains privately held, with its headquarters located on Storgatan 22 in Malmö. The company reported revenue of approximately 18 million SEK in fiscal year 2023 and plans to expand distribution to Musician's Friend in the United States by January 2025.

Fjallraven Norrland Trekker 45L backpack, released by the Swedish outdoor brand on March 3, 2022, is now available refurbished for $129.00 through Backcountry Gear Exchange, a resale division headquartered in Boulder, Colorado. Originally retailing at $220.00, this unit was inspected and recertified on January 14, 2024 by senior technician Marcus Nyholm, who has worked for Backcountry Gear Exchange since 2019. The pack features a G-1000 HeavyDuty fabric shell, a 45-liter main compartment, and an aluminum stay frame rated to carry up to 25 kilograms. It was previously owned by a single customer in Denver who purchased it new from a REI store in October 2022 and used it for three backpacking trips in Rocky Mountain National Park before trading it in. Backcountry Gear Exchange, a subsidiary of Outdoor Renewal Inc., acquired the inventory lot containing this pack on December 5, 2023, as part of a bulk buyback deal worth $18,500 covering 140 items. Each refurbished unit passes a 27-point inspection and carries a 90-day limited warranty. Customers who purchase before April 30, 2024 will receive a free 2-liter Nalgene bottle. Shipping is handled via UPS Ground and typically takes 5 to 7 business days within the continental United States. Reviews average 4.6 out of 5 stars from 312 verified buyers, with many praising the durability of the wax-coated canvas after two years of heavy use.

Marguerite Solene Okafor (born 14 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-British structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-resistant bridge designs. She earned a degree in Civil Engineering from Imperial College London in 1980 and later joined Halcrow Group as a junior engineer in 1982. In 1994, Okafor founded Okafor Bridgeworks Ltd in Manchester, a firm specializing in retrofitting aging infrastructure across the United Kingdom. The company grew rapidly, and by 2001 it employed over 300 engineers.

Okafor's most celebrated project, the Tyneford Viaduct in Newcastle, was completed in March 2003 at a cost of £42 million and remains in active use today. For this work she received the Institution of Civil Engineers' Telford Medal in London in 2004, awarded by the Institution's president, Sir Alan Whitfield.

In 2010, Okafor Bridgeworks Ltd was acquired by the multinational firm Arup Group for approximately £85 million, after which Okafor stepped down as managing director in June 2011 to become a visiting professor at the University of Manchester. She married fellow engineer Thomas Reyes in 1985, and the couple had two children, Adaeze Reyes and Chidi Reyes.

Okafor died on 9 November 2021 in Manchester following complications from a stroke. She was 63. Her memoir, Bridges of Iron and Will, was published posthumously in 2022 by Faber & Faber.

BOSTON, MA -- December 3, 2023 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolvaxamab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arvantis Therapeutics for the treatment of relapsed acute myeloid leukemia. The trial, led by Dr. Helena Ruiz, enrolled 142 adult patients across seven sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and June 2023. Participants received either tolvaxamab in combination with venetoclax or standard-of-care chemotherapy alone. According to findings published in The New England Journal of Medicine, patients treated with tolvaxamab achieved a complete remission rate of 61 percent, compared with 34 percent in the control group. Median overall survival was 19.4 months in the treatment arm versus 11.2 months in the control arm. Grade 3 or higher adverse events, primarily neutropenia and thrombocytopenia, occurred in 28 percent of tolvaxamab recipients. Dr. Ruiz stated that the results support advancing tolvaxamab into a Phase 3 registrational study, which Arvantis Therapeutics plans to launch in early 2024 in partnership with Novato Pharma AG, a Swiss pharmaceutical company. Novato Pharma AG acquired exclusive European distribution rights to tolvaxamab for 180 million dollars in a deal finalized on November 15, 2023. The companies expect to begin patient enrollment for the Phase 3 trial at Charite Hospital in Berlin by April 2024. Arvantis Therapeutics was founded in 2016 by biochemist Dr. Samuel Okafor, who previously worked at Genentech for eleven years before starting the company.

input: MUNICH, Germany — Automotive supplier Continental AG announced Tuesday that it has acquired Berlin-based sensor startup PathSense GmbH for €340 million, in a move aimed at bolstering its autonomous-driving technology division. Continental CEO Nikolai Setzer confirmed the deal during a press briefing at the company's headquarters, saying PathSense's lidar systems would be integrated into Continental's ADAS product line by early 2026. PathSense founder Dr. Elena Vogt, who started the company in 2018, will join Continental as Head of Sensor Innovation, a newly created position, effective March 1. "This acquisition strengthens our position against competitors like Bosch and ZF Friedrichshafen," Setzer told reporters. The deal, first reported by Reuters, values PathSense at nearly triple its 2023 valuation. Continental shares rose 4.2 percent on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at €68.50. Analysts at Deutsche Bank said the acquisition signals a broader consolidation trend in the German auto-parts sector, as suppliers race to keep pace with electric and self-driving vehicle demand from manufacturers such as Volkswagen and BMW. PathSense, which employs 85 engineers, will continue operating from its Berlin office under the new arrangement. The transaction is expected to close by January 31, pending regulatory approval from the European Commission. Continental, headquartered in Hanover, reported revenue of €41.4 billion in 2023 and employs roughly 190,000 people worldwide.

The Ontario Ministry of Transportation announced on March 11, 2024 that it will invest 42 million dollars to widen Highway 7 between Kitchener and Guelph, a project expected to reduce commute times by 15 percent once completed. Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria stated the funding will be transferred to the Regional Municipality of Waterloo beginning April 1, 2024, with construction managed by Dufferin Construction Company, a subsidiary of CRH Canada Group Inc. The announcement was made at a press conference held in Kitchener City Hall, where Mayor Berry Vrbanovic welcomed the investment, noting that Highway 7 has seen a 30 percent increase in traffic since 2019. Sarkaria emphasized that the project aligns with the province's broader Highway Expansion Strategy, a policy introduced under Premier Doug Ford in 2022 to address congestion across Southern Ontario. Construction is scheduled to begin in June 2024 and finish by September 2026. Local resident groups, including the Kitchener Cycling Coalition, gathered outside City Hall on March 12, 2024 to demonstrate against the plan, arguing that the expansion favors cars over cyclists and pedestrians. The Ministry confirmed that Dufferin Construction Company will also supply materials sourced from its Cambridge quarry. Officials from the Ministry and the Region of Waterloo are expected to meet again on April 5, 2024 in Waterloo to finalize environmental assessments before work begins.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday that it will invest 420 million euros to upgrade rail infrastructure between Rotterdam and Utrecht by 2027. Minister Els Vandenberg unveiled the plan at a press briefing in The Hague, stating that the project will reduce commuter delays by 30 percent and create approximately 1,800 construction jobs. The funding, approved by the Dutch Parliament last week, will be administered through ProRail, the state-owned infrastructure agency headquartered in Utrecht. ProRail's chief executive, Mark Huisman, said the agency will begin awarding contracts to construction firms in March 2025, with VolkerWessels among the companies expected to bid. Vandenberg noted that the initiative forms part of the broader National Mobility Strategy adopted by the government in 2023, which also allocated 90 million euros for electric bus fleets in Amsterdam and Eindhoven. Opposition lawmaker Bram de Vries welcomed the investment but criticized the timeline, arguing that similar projects under the previous administration had faced delays of up to two years. The Ministry confirmed that an environmental impact assessment, conducted by the consultancy firm Royal HaskoningDHV, found no significant ecological risks along the proposed corridor. A final progress report is expected to be submitted to Parliament by December 2026. Vandenberg concluded that the upgrade reflects the government's commitment to sustainable transport and regional economic growth across the Netherlands.

Cedar Point Robotics, a Pittsburgh-based industrial automation firm, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Vantage Weld Systems for $142 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at Cedar Point's headquarters on Liberty Avenue, marks the company's third acquisition since 2021 and expands its footprint in automated welding equipment for the automotive sector. Vantage Weld Systems, headquartered in Dayton, Ohio, was founded in 2009 by engineer Marcus Holt and employs roughly 310 workers. Cedar Point CEO Renata Suarez said the acquisition would help the company compete more directly with Fanuc Corporation and ABB Ltd in the industrial robotics market. "This is about scaling our supply chain and getting closer to our automotive customers in the Midwest," Suarez told reporters during a briefing on Wednesday. Under the terms of the agreement, Vantage's 65-year-old founder Marcus Holt will step down as chief executive but remain as a technical advisor for eighteen months. Cedar Point shares rose 4.3 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, closing at $58.17. Analysts at Bramwell Securities estimated the transaction would add approximately $38 million in annual revenue starting in fiscal year 2025. The acquisition is expected to close by March 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Cedar Point, which employs 2,400 people across four states, reported net income of $61 million for the quarter ending December 31, 2023. Vantage's 90 patents related to robotic arc welding will transfer fully to Cedar Point upon closing.

7/ Solara competes directly with Bremmer Dynamics, the Chicago-based automation giant that raised $60 million last year.

8/ Priya will speak at the TechForward Summit in San Jose on November 20, 2024, about the future of robotics manufacturing.

9/ Congrats to the whole Solara team - this is a huge step for American manufacturing.

Ingrid Solberg (born 14 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cod population decline in the North Sea. She earned a doctorate in marine ecology from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø the same year as a research fellow. In 1994 Solberg was appointed Director of Fisheries Science at the Institute of Marine Research, a position she held for eleven years. Her 1998 paper on overfishing, published in the journal Marine Ecology Progress Series, helped shape the European Union's Common Fisheries Policy reforms of 2002. Solberg left the Institute in 2005 to become a professor at the University of Tromsø, where she still teaches. In 2010 she received the Nansen Prize for Marine Science from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, awarded in Oslo. She has also served as a scientific advisor to Greenpeace Norway since 2012, though she is not a formal member of the organization. Solberg married fellow biologist Karl Eriksen in 1986; the couple has two children, Lars and Marit. Her older brother, Jon Solberg, is a fisherman based in Ålesund. In 2019 Solberg testified before the Norwegian Parliament regarding declining herring stocks, drawing national media attention. She continues to publish widely and is regarded as one of Scandinavia's leading voices on sustainable fisheries management.

Boston, MA — May 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating lenavorib, an oral small-molecule chemical developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arion Therapeutics, for the treatment of relapsed non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The trial, led by Dr. Sarah Kwan, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2022 and September 2023. According to results published in The Lancet Oncology, 61 percent of patients receiving lenavorib achieved complete remission within six months, compared to 29 percent in the control group receiving standard rituximab therapy. Grade 3 adverse events, primarily neutropenia, occurred in 18 percent of participants. Dr. Kwan, an associate professor of hematology at Harvard Medical School, stated that the results support advancement to a Phase 3 trial expected to begin in early 2025. Arion Therapeutics' chief executive officer, Marcus Feldman, said the company plans to seek Breakthrough Therapy designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the fourth quarter of 2024. The study was funded in part by a $12 million grant from the National Cancer Institute. Arion Therapeutics, founded in 2017 by Dr. Elena Vasquez, has raised $340 million in venture funding to date and was acquired in part by pharmaceutical giant Novartis, which purchased a 15 percent equity stake for $85 million in January 2024. Independent oncologists, including Dr. Raj Patel of Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New York, described the findings as a potentially significant advance for patients who have exhausted existing treatment options.

Dr. Amara Feldstein (born March 14, 1958, in Leipzig, East Germany) is a German-American biochemist known for her contributions to CRISPR-based gene editing. She emigrated to the United States in 1979 and earned her Ph.D. from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 1985. Feldstein joined Genoptix Therapeutics in Cambridge, Massachusetts as Chief Scientific Officer in March 1998, a position she held for over a decade. In 2004, she co-founded Helix Dynamics with venture capitalist Marcus Reyes, headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, to commercialize enzyme-replacement therapies. The company was acquired by Novara Biosciences for 480 million dollars in September 2011, a deal that made headlines across the biotechnology sector. Feldstein stepped down as Chief Scientific Officer of Genoptix Therapeutics in June 2009 to focus full-time on Helix Dynamics. In 2015, she received the Lasker-DeBakey Clinical Medical Research Award from the Lasker Foundation in New York City for her work on gene-editing therapies for sickle cell disease. She has authored more than 90 peer-reviewed papers and holds 12 patents. Feldstein is married to Dr. Samuel Voss, a cardiologist at Massachusetts General Hospital, and the couple has two children. She currently serves as an adjunct professor at Harvard Medical School and continues to advise startups in the biotechnology industry. Colleagues describe her as a rigorous scientist whose meticulous approach reshaped modern molecular biology.

BOSTON, MA -- April 12, 2024 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tazalorib, an oral chemical compound targeting IL-6 signaling, in patients with moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The study, led by Dr. Priya Ramanathan and published in The Lancet Rheumatology, enrolled 214 participants across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and September 2023. Patients receiving 150 milligrams of tazalorib twice daily showed a 62 percent reduction in disease activity scores compared to 24 percent in the placebo group after 24 weeks. Dr. Ramanathan stated that the results represent a meaningful advance for patients who have not responded to methotrexate. The trial was funded by Meridian Biosciences Inc., a biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, which plans to seek Food and Drug Administration approval by early 2025. Meridian's chief executive officer, Thomas Voss, said the company would invest $85 million to expand manufacturing capacity at its facility in Worcester, Massachusetts, ahead of a potential commercial launch. Approximately 1.3 million adults in the United States live with rheumatoid arthritis, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Common side effects observed during the trial included mild headache and elevated liver enzymes, with no serious adverse events linked directly to the drug. A larger Phase 3 trial involving 900 patients is scheduled to begin recruitment in Toronto, Ontario, in July 2024. Meridian Biosciences shares rose 14 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement.

MANCHESTER, England — October 14, 2024 — Eastfield United secured a dramatic 2-1 victory over Riverside Athletic on Saturday at Kingsgate Stadium, keeping their Premier Football League title hopes alive with six matches remaining. Striker Marcus Delgado scored twice, including a 88th-minute winner, to lift Eastfield United to second place in the standings, just three points behind league leaders Northgate City.

The match drew a crowd of 41,200, one of the largest at Kingsgate Stadium this season. Riverside Athletic had taken an early lead through midfielder Tomas Reyes in the 12th minute, but Delgado equalized just before halftime and struck again late to seal the win. Eastfield United manager Helena Brandt praised her team's resilience after the game, telling reporters, "We never stopped believing, even when we went behind."

The result extends Eastfield United's unbeaten run to eight matches, a streak that began on August 24, 2024. Riverside Athletic manager Diego Salazar acknowledged the loss was costly, noting that his side now sits eighth in the table with 34 points.

Eastfield United will next travel to Birchwood Arena on October 21, 2024, to face Northgate City in a match that could reshape the title race. Meanwhile, Delgado was named Premier Football League Player of the Week for his performance, an honor announced by the league office on October 16, 2024.

Carlos Bautista scored twice as Deportivo Alavés edged Real Betis 2-1 at Mendizorroza Stadium in Vitoria-Gasteiz on Sunday, lifting the home side out of the relegation zone in La Liga. Bautista opened the scoring in the 23rd minute with a low left-footed strike, then doubled the lead just before halftime after a quick counterattack set up by midfielder Iker Muniain. Real Betis pulled one back in the 67th minute through striker Ayoze Fernández, but a late rally fell short despite four minutes of stoppage time. Alavés head coach Luis Garitano praised his team's discipline after the match, saying the club had trained specifically for Betis's pressing style throughout the week. Betis manager Manuel Pellegrini admitted his side lacked sharpness in the final third and confirmed that defender Hector Ruiz would undergo scans on Monday after limping off in the 78th minute with a suspected hamstring injury. The win, watched by 18,200 spectators, moved Alavés to 15th place with 27 points from 24 matches. Betis remain 9th with 34 points. Alavés will next travel to face Villarreal on 14 April, while Betis host Sevilla three days later. The Spanish Football Federation confirmed no further disciplinary action would be taken after a minor pitch invasion by a single fan was quickly contained by stadium security.

Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1958 in Trieste, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques used in Mediterranean bridge construction. She earned her degree in civil engineering from the Politecnico di Milano in 1981 and joined Fiat Engineering as a junior analyst that same year. In 1989 she left Fiat Engineering to co-found Marchetti & Bruzzone Ingegneria in Genoa, alongside colleague Paolo Bruzzone, focusing on earthquake-resistant infrastructure for coastal cities.

Marchetti's breakthrough came in 1997, when her firm was awarded a contract by the Genoa Port Authority to redesign the Ponte della Vittoria after inspectors found corrosion in its support columns. The retrofit, completed in 2001 at a cost of 42 million euros, became a reference project cited by engineers across Europe. In 2004 she was appointed Chief Structural Engineer at Autostrade per l'Italia, a position she held until 2016.

In 2010 the Italian National Academy of Engineering awarded her the Galileo Medal in Rome for contributions to public safety infrastructure. She has published more than 60 papers and holds three patents related to damping systems. Marchetti married fellow engineer Paolo Bruzzone in 1992; the couple has one son, Marco Bruzzone, born in 1995 in Genoa, who now works as a structural analyst at the same firm his parents founded.

Now 67, Marchetti lives in Genoa and continues to consult on infrastructure projects across Italy, including ongoing repairs to viaducts along the A10 motorway.

BOSTON, MA – March 14, 2024 – Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating darolutinib, an experimental compound developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Velora Therapeutics, for treatment of triple-negative breast cancer. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh and published in the New England Journal of Medicine, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of darolutinib twice daily showed a 42 percent reduction in tumor progression compared to placebo, with median progression-free survival extending to 11.3 months versus 6.8 months in the control group. Dr. Marsh presented the findings at the American Association for Cancer Research annual meeting in San Diego on April 8, 2024. "These results represent a meaningful step forward for patients who have historically had limited options," Marsh said during a press briefing. Velora Therapeutics, founded in 2018 by former Pfizer executive Raj Kapoor, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. The company's shares rose 18 percent following the announcement. Adverse events included mild neutropenia in 23 percent of participants and fatigue in 31 percent, though no treatment-related deaths were reported. Velora has partnered with Novartis to expand manufacturing capacity ahead of a potential 2025 launch. A larger Phase 3 trial involving 600 patients is expected to begin enrollment in Toronto and Boston later this year.

event: American Association for Cancer Research annual meeting

input: SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA — On October 14, 2024, Judge Miriam Castellano sentenced Darnell Foster, 37, to 8 years in state prison after a jury convicted him of grand theft and embezzlement in connection with the collapse of Foster Logistics Group, a freight brokerage he founded in Oakland in 2016. Prosecutor Elena Whitfield of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Foster diverted approximately $1.2 million in client funds between January 2021 and March 2023, routing payments through shell accounts at Meridian Pacific Bank before transferring the money to a personal account in Reno, Nevada. Foster was arrested by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation on June 3, 2023, at his home in Piedmont, California, and was charged the following week with wire fraud and embezzlement. During the trial, held at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, defense attorney Marcus Ibarra called two witnesses who testified that Foster's business partner, Angela Reyes, had also accessed the disputed accounts, though Reyes was never charged. Judge Castellano ordered Foster to pay $1.2 million in restitution to twenty-nine former clients, including Bayview Produce Distributors and Cascade Textiles Inc. Foster Logistics Group filed for bankruptcy in San Francisco in April 2023, listing debts exceeding $3.4 million. Foster's attorney has indicated he will appeal the sentence to the California Court of Appeal.

organization: SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA

input: The Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection announced on June 12, 2024, that it will fine Beacon Chemical Industries $2.3 million for violations at its Fall River facility. Commissioner Laura Whitfield stated the penalty follows a March 2023 inspection that found unpermitted discharges of trichloroethylene into the Taunton River. Beacon Chemical Industries, a subsidiary of Nortrix Holdings Corporation, must submit a remediation plan to the Department within 60 days. The company's plant manager, Daniel Kowalski, said in a statement that Beacon Chemical Industries has already begun installing new filtration systems and expects the work to be completed by December 2024. The Department's enforcement division, led by Deputy Commissioner Rosa Delgado, will conduct a follow-up inspection in Fall River during the first week of January 2025. Governor Maura Healey praised the action, saying it reflects the Commonwealth's commitment to enforcing the Massachusetts Clean Waters Act. Environmental group Taunton River Watershed Alliance, represented by attorney Michael Osei, called the fine insufficient and urged the state to pursue criminal charges. The Alliance held a demonstration outside the State House in Boston on June 14, 2024, with roughly 75 participants demanding stronger penalties. The Department noted that Beacon Chemical Industries employs 210 workers at the Fall River site and that operations will continue during the remediation period. A public comment period on the remediation plan will open once the filing is received.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. RG24-118837 — People v. Marcus T. Whitfield

On March 14, 2024, Judge Elena Cordoza presided over a sentencing hearing at the Rene C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, California. Defendant Marcus T. Whitfield, a former accountant for Bramwell Logistics Inc., pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud in violation of Section 1343 of Title 18. Prosecutor Diane Kessler of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office told the court that Whitfield diverted $412,000 from company accounts between June 2021 and October 2022 by issuing fraudulent invoices to a shell entity registered under the name Kestrel Holdings LLC.

Judge Cordoza sentenced Whitfield to 36 months in state prison and ordered restitution of $412,000 to Bramwell Logistics Inc. Defense attorney Rosalind Ng argued for probation, citing her client's cooperation, but the request was denied. Whitfield was taken into custody immediately following the hearing by deputies of the Alameda County Sheriff's Office.

Bramwell Logistics Inc., headquartered in San Leandro, California, issued a statement through spokesperson Tomás Reyes confirming that the company had implemented new internal audit controls after discovering the fraud in November 2022. The case was originally investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation's San Francisco field office, which arrested Whitfield on January 9, 2023, on charges of wire fraud and embezzlement.

The next status conference for related civil litigation, Bramwell Logistics Inc. v. Kestrel Holdings LLC, is scheduled for April 22, 2024.

Ingrid Vasseur (born 14 March 1958 in Lyon, France) is a French biochemist known for pioneering work on enzyme catalysis. She earned a doctorate in chemistry from the University of Strasbourg in 1984 and joined the Institut Pasteur in Paris the same year as a research fellow. In 1991, Vasseur was appointed Director of Molecular Biology at Institut Pasteur, a position she held for twelve years. Her laboratory identified the structure of the enzyme lipase-K7, a discovery that led to the development of the drug Enzymol, later produced by the pharmaceutical company Sarnex Pharmaceuticals, headquartered in Basel, Switzerland. In 2003, Vasseur left Institut Pasteur to found Vasseur Biotech in Lyon, a company focused on enzyme-based therapeutics. Vasseur Biotech was acquired by Sarnex Pharmaceuticals for 220 million euros in 2011, after which Vasseur served as Chief Scientific Officer of Sarnex until her retirement in 2018. She is married to physicist Damien Roche and is the mother of two children, including microbiologist Claire Vasseur-Roche. In 2009, Ingrid Vasseur received the Pasteur Medal from the French Academy of Sciences in Paris for her contributions to biochemistry. She has also been a longtime member of the European Molecular Biology Organization. Vasseur currently lives in Lyon, where she continues to advise young scientists at the University of Lyon.

DENVER, Colorado — Sagebrush Energy Corp. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Prairie Wind Resources LLC for $412 million in cash and stock, marking the company's largest acquisition since its founding in 1998. The deal, expected to close by December 15, will give Sagebrush control of Prairie Wind's 340-megawatt wind farm portfolio spread across Wyoming and Montana. Sagebrush Chief Executive Officer Renata Voss said the acquisition would boost the company's renewable energy capacity by 28 percent. "This is a transformative step for Sagebrush," Voss told reporters at a press briefing in Denver. "We are positioning ourselves as a top-three player in the Rocky Mountain wind sector." Prairie Wind founder and outgoing chief executive Marcus Lindqvist will join Sagebrush's board of directors starting January 2, according to a company statement. Lindqvist, who launched Prairie Wind in 2006, said he was confident the merger would preserve jobs at the firm's Billings facility, which employs roughly 210 workers. Shares of Sagebrush Energy Corp. rose 6.4 percent to close at $58.30 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume more than tripled to 3.2 million shares. Analysts at Hartwell Capital Partners called the transaction "well-priced," noting Sagebrush paid roughly 9 times projected 2025 earnings. The company expects the acquisition to add $75 million in annual revenue beginning in fiscal year 2025. Regulatory approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission is still pending.

CLEVELAND, OH - September 12, 2024 - Riverstone Dynamics, Inc., a mid-sized industrial automation firm headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, announced today that it has acquired Falcon Robotics LLC, a privately held robotics manufacturer based in Austin, Texas, for approximately $84 million in cash and stock.

The deal, finalized on September 10, 2024, adds Falcon Robotics' line of warehouse automation arms, including the popular FR-200 Sorter, to Riverstone Dynamics' existing product portfolio. Riverstone Dynamics CEO Marguerite Owens said the acquisition strengthens the company's position against competitor Halden Systems Corp.

"This acquisition allows us to bring next-generation robotics directly into our supply chain solutions," Owens said during a press briefing held at Riverstone's Cleveland headquarters. "Falcon's engineering team, led by co-founder Derek Yamamoto, will remain in Austin and continue product development there."

As part of the transaction, Derek Yamamoto will step down as Chief Executive Officer of Falcon Robotics and join Riverstone Dynamics as Vice President of Robotics Engineering, effective October 1, 2024. Falcon Robotics was founded in 2016 by Yamamoto and his sister, Priya Yamamoto, who will remain with the company as head of quality assurance.

Riverstone Dynamics, which employs roughly 1,200 people across three facilities, expects the acquisition to increase annual revenue by 18 percent within two years. Shares of Riverstone Dynamics rose 6.3 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement. The combined company will operate under the Riverstone Dynamics name, with integration expected to conclude by March 2025.

SUPERIOR COURT OF STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF SANTA CLARA
Case No. 24-CV-118872

On March 14, 2024, Judge Ellen Marsh presided over the sentencing hearing of Darius Coleman, 37, at the San Jose Hall of Justice in San Jose, California. Coleman was convicted on February 9, 2024, of grand theft and embezzlement in connection with the diversion of $412,000 from his former employer, Willow Creek Financial Group, where he served as Chief Operating Officer from 2018 until his termination in June 2023.

Prosecutor Renata Alvarez of the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office argued that Coleman had funneled client funds into a shell company, Bright Horizon Holdings, over a period of eighteen months. Defense attorney Marcus Fein countered that Coleman had already repaid $150,000 in restitution prior to sentencing.

Judge Marsh sentenced Coleman to four years in state prison and ordered him to pay the remaining $262,000 in restitution to Willow Creek Financial Group. Coleman was taken into custody immediately following the hearing by deputies of the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office.

In a related matter, Willow Creek Financial Group announced it had been acquired by Pinegate Capital Partners for $18.5 million on March 20, 2024, a transaction the firm's CEO, Harold Denby, said was unrelated to the criminal case. The company is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

DETROIT, Oct. 14 -- Stellantis N.V. announced Monday it will acquire Archer Battery Systems Inc., a Troy, Michigan-based maker of solid-state battery cells, for $1.2 billion in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by December 15, will make Archer a wholly owned subsidiary of Stellantis and bolster the automaker's push into electric vehicles ahead of its 2026 lineup refresh.

Under the agreement, Stellantis Chief Executive Carlos Tavares said the company will retain Archer's 340 employees at its Troy facility and invest an additional $300 million to expand production capacity. "This acquisition strengthens our supply chain and reduces our reliance on Asian battery suppliers," Tavares said during a press briefing in Auburn Hills, Michigan.

Archer was founded in 2015 by engineer Priya Nandakumar, who will step down as Chief Executive Officer effective December 15 but remain as a technical adviser. Nandakumar will be succeeded by longtime Stellantis executive Marco Bellini, who was named President of the newly formed battery division on Monday.

Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimate the acquisition could reduce Stellantis's battery cell costs by roughly 18 percent within three years. Shares of Stellantis rose 4.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of rival Ford Motor Company dipped slightly amid renewed competitive pressure. The transaction still requires approval from European Union regulators, who are expected to rule by early 2025.

Pixel Watch 3, Two Years On: Google's Wearable Finally Feels Complete

Mountain View, CA -- October 14, 2025. Eighteen months after its release, the Pixel Watch 3 remains the most interesting product to come out of Google's hardware division, and a recent software update has made me reconsider it entirely. Rick Osterloh, the Senior Vice President who leads Devices and Services at Google, announced last week that Wear OS 6 would begin rolling out to Pixel Watch 3 units on October 21, 2025, bringing a redesigned interface and a claimed 30 percent improvement in battery efficiency.

I've worn the 45mm model, priced at $399.99 when Google launched it in September 2024, almost daily since Best Buy shipped mine from a warehouse in Reno, Nevada. Compared with the Apple Watch Series 10, which remains its closest rival, the Pixel Watch 3 still trails in third-party app support, but its integration with Fitbit -- the fitness company Google acquired for $2.1 billion in 2021 -- gives it an edge in sleep tracking.

Google was founded by Larry Page and Sergey Brin, and the company is now led by Sundar Pichai, its Chief Executive Officer, who is expected to discuss wearables strategy at a Google event in San Jose on November 12, 2025. Samsung, a persistent competitor in this space, is reportedly preparing a Galaxy Watch 8 refresh to counter the update.

Minor gripes remain: the charging puck is proprietary, and battery life at 36 hours is still modest. But for $399.99, this is the smartwatch I now recommend to friends switching from Android phones made by Samsung or Motorola.

MANCHESTER, England — Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice on Saturday to lead his club to a 3-1 victory over Everton at Villa Park, moving Villa into fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a left-footed finish after a pass from midfielder John McGinn, then added his second goal in the 54th minute from a penalty kick. Everton's Dominic Calvert-Lewin pulled one back in the 63rd minute, but a late strike from substitute Leon Bailey in the 88th minute sealed the win in front of 41,782 fans. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, telling reporters, "We controlled the game for long periods and showed real maturity." Everton manager Sean Dyche said his side would review the defeat before Wednesday's League Cup match against Fulham at Goodison Park. The result lifted Aston Villa to 42 points after 20 matches, three points behind third-placed Arsenal. Villa's next fixture is scheduled for November 25 against Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium. Meanwhile, Villa's American co-owner Wes Edens confirmed the club is finalizing a $15 million sponsorship deal with a technology firm to feature on the team's training kits starting next season, according to a statement released by Aston Villa Football Club on Sunday.

Cedar Point Logistics, a Memphis-based freight and warehousing company, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired regional carrier Blue Ridge Trucking for $142 million in cash and stock. The deal, disclosed by Cedar Point chief executive Marcus Whitfield during a press briefing at the company's headquarters, is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval. Blue Ridge Trucking, founded in 1987 by Harold Denning in Roanoke, Virginia, operates a fleet of roughly 640 trucks across the southeastern United States and reported revenue of $310 million last year. Whitfield said the acquisition would expand Cedar Point's footprint into Virginia and the Carolinas, adding that the combined company would employ more than 4,200 workers. Blue Ridge's chief executive, Angela Preston, will step down from her position once the transaction closes, according to a statement released by the company. She will be succeeded by Daniel Ruiz, currently Cedar Point's vice president of operations, who is set to start as president of the Blue Ridge division on January 20, 2025. Shares of Cedar Point, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker CPLT, rose 6.3 percent to $58.40 following the announcement. Analysts at Fenwick Capital Partners called the deal "a smart consolidation play" in a note to clients Wednesday. Cedar Point financed the purchase partly through a $90 million loan from First Meridian Bank. The company plans to retain Blue Ridge's Roanoke distribution center and its 900 employees there.

CHARLOTTE, N.C. — Piedmont Regional Bank agreed on Tuesday to acquire Blue Ridge Community Trust for $340 million in cash and stock, the two companies announced at a joint press conference at Piedmont's headquarters in Charlotte. The deal, expected to close by March 2025, will make Piedmont the fourth-largest bank in North Carolina by assets.

Under the terms of the agreement, Blue Ridge shareholders will receive $28.50 per share, a 22 percent premium over Monday's closing price. Piedmont CEO Marcus Whitfield said the acquisition would add 41 branches across the western part of the state. "This merger strengthens our footprint in the Blue Ridge Mountains region and lets us serve nearly 250,000 additional customers," Whitfield told reporters.

Blue Ridge Community Trust, founded in 1987 by banker Eleanor Sams in Asheville, has struggled in recent years with rising loan defaults. Its chief executive, David Kowalski, will step down once the deal closes and will be succeeded by Piedmont executive Renee Ochoa, who currently serves as Chief Operating Officer.

Regulators at the Federal Reserve and the North Carolina Office of the Commissioner of Banks must still approve the transaction. Analysts at Raymond James said the deal reflects a broader wave of consolidation among regional banks facing pressure from higher interest rates. Shares of Blue Ridge jumped 18 percent on Tuesday following the announcement, while Piedmont's stock dipped 3 percent.

The combined bank will operate under the Piedmont Regional Bank name and will be headquartered in Charlotte, with Ochoa assuming the CEO role in April.
