MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City extended its unbeaten domestic run to eleven matches on Saturday, defeating Everton 3-1 at the Etihad Stadium in front of 53,412 spectators. Norwegian striker Erling Haaland scored twice, including a 78th-minute penalty, while midfielder Rodri added a third goal in stoppage time. Everton's Dominic Calvert-Lewin pulled one back in the 62nd minute with a header from a corner kick.

Manager Pep Guardiola praised his team's discipline after the match, telling reporters, "We controlled the tempo for ninety minutes, and that is why we deserved the three points." The win moved City to the top of the Premier League table with 24 points from ten games, two points ahead of Arsenal.

Everton manager Sean Dyche, whose side dropped to 15th place, said the club would review its defensive setup before hosting Liverpool on October 21. Dyche also confirmed that defender Jarrad Branthwaite would miss the next two matches with a hamstring injury sustained in training at Finch Farm earlier in the week.

The match also marked the 300th Premier League appearance for City captain Kyle Walker, a milestone acknowledged by the club before kickoff. Manchester City's next fixture is away at Chelsea on October 28, a match the club hopes will extend its lead atop the standings.

Attendance figures released by the Premier League confirmed the Etihad Stadium crowd as the second-largest in the division this season, trailing only Old Trafford's gathering of 73,908 for Manchester United's match against Brighton the same weekend.

1/ Big week for the logistics sector: Meridian Freight Corp, headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, announced today (June 4, 2024) that it has acquired regional rival Hartline Transport for $340 million in cash. Deal closes by August 15, 2024.

2/ Meridian CEO Rosalind Pryce told reporters at the company's Columbus headquarters that the acquisition adds 1,200 trucks and 47 new warehouse facilities across Ohio, Indiana, and Kentucky to Meridian's network.

3/ Hartline founder Desmond Ault, who started the company in Louisville, Kentucky back in 1998, will step down as CEO effective July 1, 2024, but will stay on as a senior advisor.

4/ Analysts at Blackwell Capital Partners say the deal makes Meridian the second-largest trucking company in the Midwest, trailing only Sterling Logistics Group, its longtime competitor.

5/ Meridian shares rose 6 percent on the Nasdaq after the announcement, while Sterling shares dipped 2 percent. Roughly 3,000 employees across both firms will be affected by the merger.

6/ Pryce also confirmed that Marcus Feldman, previously CFO at Rutledge Industries, will join Meridian as Chief Financial Officer starting July 22, 2024, replacing outgoing CFO Elena Vasquez, who is retiring after 14 years.

7/ Union representatives from the Teamsters Local 391 plan to meet with Meridian management in Columbus next Tuesday to discuss job security for Hartline warehouse staff.

8/ Full details of the transition plan will be posted on Meridian's website by June 20, 2024.

Ingrid Halvorsen (born 14 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on Arctic cod populations. She earned a doctorate in marine ecology from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø the same year as a Research Fellow. In 1994 Halvorsen was appointed Director of the Institute's Arctic Ecosystems Division, a position she held for eleven years.

Halvorsen's most cited work, the 1999 monograph "Cold Currents," documented declining cod stocks in the Barents Sea and influenced Norwegian fisheries policy. In 2003 the Norwegian Parliament cited her findings when it passed the Marine Resources Act, which restricted trawling quotas along the northern coast.

In 2008, Halvorsen received the Nansen Award from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to polar ecology. She left the Institute of Marine Research in 2011 to become a professor at the Arctic University of Norway, a post she held until her retirement in 2020.

Halvorsen married fellow researcher Erik Fjeldstad in 1988; the couple had two children, Lars and Mette. She currently lives in Tromsø, where she continues to advise the Norwegian Environment Agency on climate-related fishery regulations.

input: MADRID, June 14 -- Real Sociedad striker Mikel Oyarzabal scored twice as Spain defeated Croatia 3-1 in a friendly at Estadio Santiago Bernabeu on Friday night, boosting confidence ahead of the UEFA Nations League finals in September. Oyarzabal opened the scoring in the 23rd minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic, then doubled his tally in the 61st minute from a Pedri cutback. Croatia captain Luka Modric pulled one back with a penalty in the 74th minute, but substitute Ferran Torres restored Spain's two-goal cushion in stoppage time, curling a shot into the top corner. Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente praised his squad's discipline after the match, saying the win over Croatia proved his team could compete with elite opposition. "We showed maturity tonight, and Mikel Oyarzabal has been outstanding all season," de la Fuente told reporters at a post-match press conference. Real Federacion Espanola de Futbol confirmed that 68,340 fans attended the match, generating an estimated 4.2 million euros in ticket revenue. Spain will next face France on September 5 in Paris, while Croatia return home to prepare for their World Cup qualifying campaign. Real Sociedad, Oyarzabal's club side, later confirmed he will undergo a minor fitness check on Monday before rejoining training in San Sebastian. Meanwhile, Modric, who plays for Real Madrid, said he remains committed to representing Croatia despite speculation about international retirement.

BOSTON, Massachusetts -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced on March 14, 2024 the results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tarlatamab, an investigational bispecific T-cell engager, in patients with relapsed small cell lung cancer. The study, led by Dr. Priya Ramanathan and published in The New England Journal of Medicine, enrolled 187 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Germany between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants received intravenous infusions of tarlatamab every two weeks for up to 12 cycles. According to the report, 40 percent of patients achieved an objective response, with a median overall survival of 14.3 months compared to 8.7 months in the historical control group. Dr. Ramanathan stated that the drug's safety profile was manageable, though 22 patients experienced cytokine release syndrome, a known complication of T-cell engaging therapies. Amgen Inc., the manufacturer of tarlatamab, provided funding of $4.2 million for the trial and plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the fourth quarter of 2024. Dr. Ramanathan is scheduled to present the full dataset at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting in Chicago on June 2, 2024. Novartis AG, a competitor developing a similar bispecific antibody, declined to comment on the findings. Massachusetts General Hospital, headquartered in Boston, will continue enrolling patients for a Phase 3 confirmatory trial expected to begin in early 2025.

input: Cupertino, CA -- On March 14, 2024, Apple Inc. released the Vision Pro 2 headset, priced at $2,899, at its Infinite Loop campus. Reviewer Daniela Chu spent three weeks testing the device before publishing her verdict on March 29, 2024. The headset, weighing 21 ounces, uses a new R2 chip designed by Apple's silicon team in Cupertino, and Daniela Chu found the passthrough video noticeably sharper than the original Vision Pro launched in February 2024. Battery life remains a weak point: the external pack lasts just 2 hours per charge, a figure Daniela Chu called disappointing for a $2,899 product. Sony Corporation, a longtime competitor of Apple Inc. in consumer electronics, is reportedly preparing a rival mixed-reality device for release in Tokyo later in 2024, according to comments from Sony executive Kenji Watanabe at a press briefing in Tokyo on March 20, 2024. Meanwhile, Meta Platforms continues to undercut both companies on price with its Quest 3 headset. Daniela Chu praised the Vision Pro 2's eye-tracking accuracy and its integration with macOS Sonoma, but she criticized the lack of native support for Netflix and the persistent neck strain during extended sessions. Overall, she awarded the device 7 out of 10 stars, calling it 'a remarkable but exhausting glimpse of the future.' For most buyers, she recommends waiting for a third-generation model before investing $2,899 in Apple's vision of spatial computing.

DETROIT, Mich. — Reliant Motors Inc. announced Tuesday it will acquire Bolt Dynamics LLC, a battery-technology startup based in Ann Arbor, for $410 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by January 15, 2025, marks Reliant's largest acquisition since its founding in 1998 by engineer Carla Voss. CEO Marcus Thane said the purchase would help Reliant compete with rivals Tesla Inc. and Volkswagen AG in the electric-vehicle market. Bolt Dynamics, founded in 2016 by Dr. Priya Nandan, employs 240 people and holds several patents related to solid-state battery cells. Nandan will join Reliant as Chief Technology Officer, replacing Frank Ostrow, who is stepping down after eleven years to pursue what he called "new challenges." Shares of Reliant Motors rose 6.2 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.30. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners praised the move, with senior analyst Devon Blake calling it "a smart bet on next-generation battery chemistry." The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which is expected to review the deal over the next 60 days. If approved, Bolt Dynamics will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Reliant Motors, retaining its Ann Arbor headquarters and existing staff. Reliant, headquartered in Detroit, currently employs roughly 14,500 workers worldwide and reported $9.3 billion in revenue last year.

Pixelworks Labs, the Portland-based imaging division of Pixelworks Inc., unveiled the MotionEngine X1 chip on March 4, 2024, promising 240Hz frame interpolation for handheld gaming devices. I tested the reference tablet, built by ODM partner Compal Electronics, for eleven days before writing this review. At $449, the tablet undercuts the Lenovo Legion Y700 by roughly $80 while offering comparable GPU throughput, according to benchmarks run by senior engineer Priya Ramaswamy at the company's Hillsboro, Oregon lab. Ramaswamy told me during a call on March 12 that the X1's power draw stays under 3.5 watts even at peak load, a figure independently verified by TechInsights analyst Marcus Feld. The chip itself is fabricated by TSMC in Hsinchu, Taiwan, using a 6-nanometer process, and Pixelworks says supply is currently constrained to about 50,000 units per month. Battery life on the review unit lasted 9 hours of continuous 1080p video playback, which is respectable but not class-leading. The interface, running a customized version of Android 14, occasionally stuttered when switching between the 60Hz and 240Hz modes, a bug Pixelworks says will be patched by April 30. Competing chipmaker Qualcomm has yet to respond publicly to the announcement. Still, for handheld gaming enthusiasts on a budget, the MotionEngine X1 platform delivers genuine value, and I recommend it cautiously until the firmware stabilizes. Pixelworks' stock rose 6 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement.

MANCHESTER, England -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice on Saturday to lead his side to a 3-1 victory over Everton at Villa Park, boosting Villa's push for a top-four finish in the Premier League. The 28-year-old forward opened the scoring in the 14th minute with a low left-footed strike, then added a second just before halftime after a swift counterattack led by midfielder John McGinn. Everton pulled one back through Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 63rd minute, but substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win with a curling effort in the 81st minute. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his team's discipline after the match, telling reporters, "We controlled the tempo for long periods and showed maturity against a physical Everton side." The result lifts Aston Villa to third place in the table with 58 points from 29 games, three points ahead of fifth-placed Newcastle United. Everton manager Sean Dyche acknowledged the loss but pointed to encouraging signs, noting that his squad created several chances despite missing defender James Tarkowski through suspension. Around 42,000 fans attended the match at Villa Park, with kickoff at 3:00 p.m. Villa will next travel to London on March 30 to face Tottenham Hotspur, while Everton return home to host Brighton & Hove Albion the same weekend. The Premier League season is scheduled to conclude in May, with Villa aiming to secure Champions League qualification for the first time since 1983.

Fjallhorn Gear, a Bozeman, Montana outdoor equipment company founded in 2014 by former ski patroller Erik Solvang, has launched the Tundra 45 backpack for the 2024 hiking season. Priced at $189.00, the Tundra 45 is a 45-liter alpine touring pack built from 210-denier recycled ripstop nylon, weighing just 1.4 kilograms. It features an adjustable torso length, a removable hip belt, and a dedicated ice-axe loop, making it suitable for trips lasting three to five days. Fjallhorn Gear tested the pack extensively in the Bridger Mountains near Bozeman before releasing it to retailers on March 12, 2024. The company, which employs 38 people, is a subsidiary of Continental Outdoor Holdings, a Denver-based firm that acquired Fjallhorn Gear in 2021 for an undisclosed sum. Fjallhorn Gear competes directly with Patagonia and Osprey Packs in the technical backpacking segment. Each Tundra 45 comes with a lifetime warranty and is available in three colorways: Glacier Blue, Slate Gray, and Ember Orange. Customers who order before April 30, 2024 receive a free 1-liter Nalgene bottle. The pack is currently in stock and ships within 2 business days from the company's warehouse in Belgrade, Montana. Early reviewers on the outdoor forum TrailSpace have praised the Tundra 45's durability, with one reviewer calling it "the best pack under $200 I've used in a decade." This listing reflects the product's condition as brand new, factory sealed.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solera Dynamics announced this morning it has acquired Pemberton Robotics for $340 million in cash and stock. The deal closed yesterday, June 3, 2024, and is expected to add 210 jobs at Solera's new facility on Riverside Drive by early 2025.

2/ CEO Marcus Whitfield told reporters at the press conference in downtown Austin that Pemberton's warehouse-automation arm will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary under the name Pemberton Robotics, a Solera Dynamics company.

3/ Pemberton was founded in 2016 by Dr. Elena Cho, who will stay on as Chief Technology Officer reporting to Whitfield. Cho previously worked at Kessler Manufacturing in Detroit before starting Pemberton with $2 million in seed funding.

4/ Solera shares rose 4.2% on the Nasdaq following the announcement. Analysts at Bramwell Capital called it 'a smart bolt-on' that strengthens Solera's position against rival Actuate Systems, which lost a bid for Pemberton last fall.

5/ In related news, Solera also confirmed that longtime CFO Diane Sorkin will step down from her position on July 15, 2024, to become CEO of a healthcare logistics startup in Denver. Whitfield said a search for her replacement is already underway.

6/ Congrats to the whole Pemberton team - especially the 60 engineers who built the SortBot 3000 platform. Excited to see what's next under Solera Dynamics.

Denver-based Cascade Fibers Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has completed the acquisition of rival textile maker Northgate Weavers Ltd. for $412 million in cash and stock. The deal, first disclosed in March, closed on June 10, 2024, and gives Cascade Fibers control of Northgate's manufacturing plant in Greensboro, North Carolina. Cascade Fibers CEO Marina Delgado said the acquisition would expand the company's presence in the Southeast and add roughly 1,200 employees to its workforce. "This is a pivotal moment for Cascade Fibers," Delgado told reporters during a press briefing in Denver, Colorado. "Northgate's expertise in synthetic blends complements our existing product lines perfectly." Northgate Weavers, founded in 1987 by textile engineer Harold Bishop, had struggled with declining margins over the past three years, according to filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Shares of Cascade Fibers rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.27. Analysts at Bramwell & Co. said the merger positions Cascade Fibers as the second-largest textile producer in the United States, trailing only Ashworth Mills Corporation. Separately, Northgate's longtime chief financial officer, Priya Nathan, is expected to step down from her position on July 1, 2024, after 15 years with the company. Cascade Fibers said it plans to retain most of Northgate's senior management team through the end of the fiscal year.

DETROIT, Mich. — Sterling Automotive Group announced Tuesday that it has acquired Bright Path Robotics, a warehouse-automation startup based in Ann Arbor, for $340 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by January 15, 2025, marks Sterling's largest acquisition since the company was founded in 1998 by industrialist Walter Hines.

CEO Renata Alvarez said the acquisition will let Sterling integrate autonomous forklifts and inventory drones into its supply chain within eighteen months. "Bright Path's engineers have built something genuinely transformative," Alvarez told reporters at a press briefing in Detroit.

Bright Path Robotics was founded in 2016 by former MIT researcher Devon Okafor, who will join Sterling as Chief Technology Officer effective December 1. Okafor stepped down as Bright Path's chief executive on Monday, a move the company had signaled for weeks.

Sterling, headquartered in Detroit, competes with Midwest Logistics Corp and Falcon Freight Systems in the automated warehousing sector. Analysts at Bristol Capital Partners estimated the deal values Bright Path at nearly twelve times its 2023 revenue of $28 million.

Shares of Sterling Automotive Group rose 6 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, while employees at Bright Path's 220-person Ann Arbor facility were told their jobs are expected to remain intact. The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which is expected to review the filing by early February.

DETROIT, Mich. — Sterling Metalworks Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $214 million in unpaid debt and a sharp decline in orders from the automotive sector. The filing was submitted to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan.

CEO Randall Ostrowski told reporters at a press briefing that the company, headquartered in Detroit since 1978, would continue operating during restructuring and expects to keep its 1,200 employees on payroll through at least March 2025. "This is a painful but necessary step to preserve jobs and stabilize our supply chain relationships," Ostrowski said.

Sterling Metalworks supplies stamped steel components to Ford Motor Company and General Motors, both of which issued statements Wednesday saying they do not expect immediate disruptions to production. Industry analyst Lena Farrow of Brightline Capital Partners said the bankruptcy reflects broader strain among Tier 2 auto suppliers squeezed by rising steel prices and slowing EV demand.

The company's board also announced that Chief Financial Officer Patricia Vance will step down from her position effective January 10, 2025, after seven years with the firm. A successor has not yet been named.

Court documents show Sterling Metalworks owes $38 million to steel supplier Nucor Corporation alone. A hearing before Judge Miriam Coelho is scheduled for December 5 to review the company's proposed reorganization plan.

organization: U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- November 12, 2024 -- Veridian Biosciences Inc. announced today that it has acquired Solano Genomics Corp., a privately held gene-sequencing startup based in San Diego, California, for $340 million in cash. The acquisition, expected to close on December 20, 2024, will strengthen Veridian's pipeline of diagnostic tools for early cancer detection.

Under the terms of the agreement, Veridian will pay Solano Genomics shareholders $340 million in a deal structured entirely as cash consideration. Dr. Priya Nakamura, Chief Executive Officer of Veridian Biosciences, said the acquisition would accelerate development of the company's flagship product, OncoScan-7, a blood-based diagnostic device already used in over 200 hospitals across the United States.

"Solano Genomics brings world-class sequencing technology that complements our diagnostics platform," said Dr. Nakamura during a press briefing held at Veridian's headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts on November 12, 2024. "Together we can detect ovarian cancer and pancreatic cancer at earlier stages than ever before."

Solano Genomics was founded in 2016 by Dr. Marcus Ferreira, who will join Veridian as Chief Scientific Officer effective January 6, 2025. Dr. Ferreira previously served as Chief Scientific Officer at Solano Genomics for eight years.

Veridian Biosciences, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs approximately 1,800 people and reported revenue of $612 million in fiscal year 2023. The company's shares are traded on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol VRDN. Analysts at Morgan Stanley called the deal a strong strategic fit, noting that Solano Genomics' technology could boost Veridian's diagnostic accuracy by up to 15 percent.

CAMBRIDGE, MA — October 14, 2024 — Vantar Biosciences, a clinical-stage biotechnology firm headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, today announced that it has acquired Solenne Therapeutics, a privately held gene-therapy startup based in Basel, Switzerland, for $340 million in cash and stock.

Under the terms of the agreement, Vantar Biosciences will pay $210 million upfront, with the remaining $130 million contingent on regulatory milestones for Solenne's lead candidate, SLN-402, a treatment for a rare form of muscular dystrophy. The deal is expected to close on November 30, 2024, pending approval from Swiss antitrust regulators.

"This acquisition strengthens our pipeline and accelerates our entry into gene therapy," said Dr. Priya Ramaswamy, Chief Executive Officer of Vantar Biosciences. "Solenne's team has built something remarkable, and we intend to keep their Basel research facility fully staffed."

Solenne Therapeutics was founded in 2018 by Dr. Marcus Feller, a former researcher at Novartis, who will join Vantar Biosciences as Chief Scientific Officer effective December 1, 2024. Dr. Feller stepped down as Solenne's Chief Executive Officer on October 14, 2024, following the announcement.

Vantar Biosciences shares rose 6 percent on the Nasdaq following the news, closing at $58.12. The company employs approximately 1,200 people across facilities in Cambridge, San Diego, and Basel. Analysts at Jefferies Group estimate the deal could add $75 million in annual revenue by 2027.

The transaction was advised by Goldman Sachs on behalf of Vantar Biosciences and by UBS on behalf of Solenne Therapeutics.

MERIDIAN CITY, Ohio — Blackwell Foods Inc., the packaged-foods company headquartered in Meridian City, announced Tuesday it will acquire regional rival Harlan Snack Group for $410 million in cash, the companies said in a joint statement.

Under the deal, Blackwell Foods will pay Harlan Snack Group shareholders $28 per share, a 22 percent premium over Monday's closing price. The transaction, expected to close by January 15, 2025, still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission.

CEO Dana Whitfield, who has led Blackwell Foods since 2019, said the acquisition would strengthen the company's position against competitor Prairie Gold Snacks. "This deal doubles our footprint in the Midwest," Whitfield told reporters at a press briefing in Meridian City on Tuesday.

Harlan Snack Group, founded in 1987 by Roger Harlan in Dayton, Ohio, employs roughly 1,200 workers across three factories. Harlan's current chief executive, Priya Nair, will step down from her position once the deal closes, according to a company filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Analysts at Cormorant Capital Partners said the merger could face scrutiny given Blackwell's existing 34 percent share of the U.S. pretzel market. Shares of Harlan Snack Group jumped 19 percent on the news, closing at $27.40 in Wednesday trading, while Blackwell Foods shares dipped 3 percent.

The combined company, which will retain the Blackwell Foods name, plans to keep all three Harlan factories open through at least 2026, Whitfield added.

To: Board of Directors, Halden Instruments Inc.
From: Priya Nandakumar, Chief Financial Officer
Date: March 14, 2024
Subject: Acquisition of Wexford Sensor Technologies

Dear Board Members,

I am pleased to confirm that Halden Instruments Inc., headquartered in Rochester, Minnesota, has completed the acquisition of Wexford Sensor Technologies, a privately held manufacturer based in Ann Arbor, Michigan, for a total of $42 million in cash. The transaction closed yesterday, March 13, 2024, following approval from Wexford's shareholders.

Under the agreement, Halden Instruments will retain all 118 Wexford employees, including founder Marcus Ebert, who will join us as Vice President of Product Development effective April 1, 2024. Marcus founded Wexford in 2011 and built its flagship product, the ThermaSense 200 sensor array, into a leader in industrial temperature monitoring.

This acquisition strengthens our position against competitors such as Delacroix Systems, particularly in the automotive and aerospace sectors. We expect the combined entity to generate approximately $210 million in annual revenue by fiscal year 2025.

On April 22, 2024, I will travel to Ann Arbor to meet with the former Wexford leadership team, including outgoing CEO Sandra Kowalski, who is stepping down after eight years in the role. Sandra has agreed to consult for six months to ensure a smooth transition.

Please direct any questions to me at priya.nandakumar@haldeninstruments.com or (507) 555-2938.

Sincerely,
Priya Nandakumar
Chief Financial Officer
Halden Instruments Inc.

MANCHESTER, England -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side beat West Ham United 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, lifting Villa into fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 14th minute, converting a low cross from midfielder John McGinn, before doubling his tally just after halftime with a curling finish from 18 yards. West Ham pulled one back through striker Michail Antonio in the 63rd minute, but Villa sealed the win when substitute Leon Bailey struck in stoppage time. The victory was Villa's fifth in six matches under manager Unai Emery, who praised his squad's resilience after the match. "We showed character today, and that is what champions are made of," Emery told reporters at a press conference inside Villa Park. West Ham manager David Moyes admitted his side struggled to contain Watkins, saying the club would review its defensive setup before hosting Brighton & Hove Albion on 21 October. Villa's next fixture comes on 24 October, when they travel to face Bayern Munich in the Champions League at the Allianz Arena in Munich. Sunday's attendance of 41,912 was the highest recorded at Villa Park this season, according to the Premier League. Villa remain unbeaten at home since August, a run of eight matches that has fueled talk of a genuine title challenge.

MEMORANDUM

To: Board of Directors, Larkspur Analytics Inc.
From: Renee Ostrowski, Chief Financial Officer
Date: March 14, 2024
Re: Acquisition of Meridian Data Systems

I am pleased to confirm that Larkspur Analytics Inc., headquartered in Austin, Texas, has completed its acquisition of Meridian Data Systems, a cloud-storage provider based in Denver, Colorado. The deal, valued at $42 million, closed yesterday after four months of negotiation led by our outside counsel at Whitfield & Cross LLP.

Under the agreement, Larkspur will absorb Meridian's 85 employees and retain its flagship product, VaultSync, which will now be marketed under the Larkspur brand. Meridian's founder, Dr. Priya Nandakumar, will join Larkspur as Senior Vice President of Engineering effective April 1, 2024, reporting directly to CEO Marcus Whitfield.

This acquisition follows Larkspur's $18 million purchase of Redline Metrics last October and reinforces our position against competitors such as Convoy Cloud Partners. Analysts at Bramwell Securities noted that the combined entity now serves over 1,200 enterprise clients across North America.

A joint announcement will be made at a press conference in Austin on March 20, 2024, where Mr. Whitfield and Dr. Nandakumar will take questions. Please direct any board inquiries to my office before then, as we anticipate media interest following the announcement.

Thank you for your continued support throughout this process.

Sincerely,
Renee Ostrowski
Chief Financial Officer
Larkspur Analytics Inc.

SUPERIOR COURT OF SANTA CLARA COUNTY, DEPARTMENT 19

On March 6, 2024, Judge Ellen Marchetti sentenced Raymond T. Kessler, 47, to 6 years in state prison after a jury in San Jose convicted him of embezzlement from his former employer, Palo Alto-based fintech firm Meridian Capital Partners. Prosecutor Diane Ochoa of the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office told the court that Kessler, who worked as Chief Financial Officer at Meridian Capital Partners from January 2018 until his termination in August 2022, diverted approximately $2.3 million in client funds into a shell account before transferring the money to a personal brokerage account in the Cayman Islands.

The trial, which began on February 12, 2024, at the Superior Court of Santa Clara County, featured testimony from forensic accountant Priya Nair, who traced the wire transfers to Kessler's account at Falcon Trust Bank. Defense attorney Marcus Whitfield argued that Kessler had authorization for the transactions, but jurors deliberated for only four hours before returning a guilty verdict on February 27, 2024, on three counts of embezzlement and one count of wire fraud.

Meridian Capital Partners, founded in 2011 by CEO Sandra Liu, issued a statement praising the verdict and confirming that $1.1 million had already been recovered through civil litigation. Judge Marchetti also ordered Kessler to pay $2.3 million in restitution. Kessler's attorney has indicated an intent to appeal the sentence to the California Court of Appeal.

input: Hélène Marceau (born 14 March 1958 in Lyon, France) is a French biochemist known for her pioneering work on messenger RNA stabilization. She earned a doctorate in molecular biology from the University of Strasbourg in 1984 and joined the Institut Pasteur in Paris that same year as a research fellow. In 1991, Marceau moved to the United States to take a position as Associate Professor at Stanford University, where she remained until 1999. During this period she collaborated frequently with her husband, immunologist Daniel Kessler, whom she married in 1987; the couple has one son, Julien Kessler, born in 1990. In 2001 Marceau co-founded Genavir Therapeutics in Cambridge, Massachusetts, alongside venture capitalist Robert Lindqvist, aiming to translate her mRNA research into vaccine platforms. She served as Chief Scientific Officer of Genavir until 2015. Her efforts contributed to a licensing agreement in 2012 under which Genavir sold key patent rights to Bayer AG for 45 million dollars. In 2016 Marceau was elected to the French Academy of Sciences and later received the Louis Pasteur Medal from the Institut Pasteur in 2019 in Paris, in recognition of her contributions to vaccine biology. She currently holds an honorary professorship at Sorbonne University and continues to publish on RNA therapeutics. Marceau resides in Paris with her husband. Colleagues describe her as rigorous, generous with mentorship, and instrumental in shaping the modern mRNA vaccine field.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- Aug 14, 2024 -- Solvarix Therapeutics Inc. announced today that it has acquired Nexbio Diagnostics Ltd., a Toronto-based developer of rapid diagnostic assays, for 240 million dollars in cash and stock. The acquisition, expected to close by October 1, 2024, will strengthen Solvarix's presence in infectious disease testing across North America.

Under the terms of the agreement, Solvarix will pay 180 million dollars in cash and issue 1.2 million shares of common stock to Nexbio shareholders. Nexbio, founded in 2016 by Dr. Priya Nandakumar, employs 95 people at its facility in Toronto, Ontario, and generated 42 million dollars in revenue last year.

"This deal accelerates our diagnostics roadmap by at least three years," said Marcus Whitfield, Chief Executive Officer of Solvarix Therapeutics, in a statement issued from the company's Cambridge headquarters. Dr. Nandakumar, who will join Solvarix as Senior Vice President of Diagnostics effective October 1, 2024, said the merger would let Nexbio's flagship product, the RapidScreen CRP Panel, reach a broader base of hospitals.

Solvarix shares rose 6 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, closing at 54.30 dollars. The company, which employs roughly 1,400 people worldwide, was founded in 2011 by biochemist Elena Ruiz and currently operates research sites in Cambridge, San Diego, and Basel, Switzerland.

The transaction remains subject to regulatory clearance from the Federal Trade Commission and Canada's Competition Bureau.

BOSTON, MA - September 12, 2023 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tovorafenib, an investigational kinase inhibitor developed by Day One Biopharmaceuticals, in 76 pediatric patients with relapsed low-grade glioma. The multicenter study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez, was conducted across 14 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2021 and June 2023. According to findings published in The Lancet Oncology, 67 percent of participants achieved a partial or complete response, with median progression-free survival reaching 20.6 months. Dr. Vasquez presented the data at the International Society of Pediatric Oncology conference in Vancouver on September 10, 2023. "These results represent a meaningful advance for children who have exhausted standard chemotherapy options," she said during a press briefing. Day One Biopharmaceuticals, headquartered in South San Francisco, California, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2024. The company's stock rose 18 percent following the announcement, and CEO Jeremy Bender stated that the firm intends to expand manufacturing capacity at its facility in Fremont. Co-author Dr. Michael Chen of The Hospital for Sick Children in Toronto noted that fewer than 5 percent of patients discontinued treatment due to grade 3 or higher adverse events, most commonly hair color changes and elevated liver enzymes. The National Cancer Institute provided partial funding for the trial under grant CA-234891. Enrollment for a confirmatory Phase 3 trial is expected to begin in January 2024 at sites including Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New York.

input: Ingrid Solberg (born March 14, 1958, in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cod population decline in the North Sea. She earned her doctorate in Marine Ecology from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromso as a research scientist that same year. In 1998 Solberg was appointed Director of Fisheries Research at the institute, a position she held for eleven years. Her 2003 study, published in the journal Ocean Science Quarterly, documented a 42% decline in Atlantic cod stocks off the Lofoten Islands and influenced fishing quota reforms adopted by the Norwegian government in 2005. In 2011 she left the Institute of Marine Research to become a professor at the University of Tromso, where she still teaches. Solberg received the Nansen Prize for Marine Science from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo in 2012, awarded for her contributions to sustainable fisheries policy. She is married to fellow researcher Erik Halvorsen and has one son, Magnus Halvorsen, who works as a marine engineer for Kongsberg Maritime in Kongsberg. Solberg has also served since 2015 as a member of the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea, based in Copenhagen, Denmark. Now 66, she continues to publish on climate-driven shifts in fish migration patterns, most recently a 2022 paper warning that mackerel populations could shift 300 kilometers northward by 2050 due to warming ocean temperatures.

On October 3, 2024, Judge Marion T. Kessler sentenced Darnell Osei, 34, to 46 months in state prison after a jury found him guilty of grand theft and embezzlement in connection with his former employment at Coastal Ridge Logistics, a freight brokerage headquartered in Oakland, California. input: MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side defeated Newcastle United 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, moving Villa into third place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low left-footed finish, then doubled the lead just before halftime after a swift counterattack led by midfielder John McGinn. Newcastle United pulled one back through Alexander Isak in the 58th minute, but substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win with a curling effort in the 81st minute. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, telling reporters, "We controlled the tempo for long periods, and Ollie's movement was outstanding." The victory extended Aston Villa's unbeaten home run to eight matches. Newcastle manager Eddie Howe acknowledged the defeat, saying his team lost concentration after conceding the second goal. The result leaves Newcastle United in eighth position with 14 points from eight games, while Aston Villa climbed to 19 points. Villa's next fixture is away to Arsenal at Emirates Stadium on October 21, 2023. Approximately 42,000 fans attended Saturday's match at Villa Park, and Sky Sports broadcast the game live across the United Kingdom.

Helena Vrantz (born 14 March 1958 in Graz, Austria) is an Austrian-American structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-damping systems used in high-rise construction. She earned a diploma in civil engineering from the Technical University of Vienna in 1981 and later completed a doctorate at the University of California, Berkeley in 1986. In 1992 Vrantz joined Halloran & Steed, a San Francisco engineering firm, as a senior structural analyst. She left the company in 1998 to found Meridian Structural Systems in Oakland, California, alongside her former classmate Devan Okafor. Under her leadership as Chief Technology Officer, Meridian developed the TorsionGuard damper, a product later installed in the 58-story Cascade Tower in Seattle, completed in 2004. In 2007, Meridian Structural Systems was acquired by Kessler-Bright Industries for 340 million dollars, a deal finalized in Chicago on 9 May 2007. Vrantz remained with the merged entity for three years before stepping down from her position in 2010. In 2015, the American Society of Civil Engineers awarded her the Norman Medal in Washington, D.C., for her contributions to earthquake-resistant design. Vrantz married fellow engineer Devan Okafor in 1994; the couple has one daughter, Mira Okafor, born in 2001 in Oakland. Vrantz currently serves as a professor of structural engineering at Stanford University, where she has taught since 2011. She holds citizenship in both Austria and the United States.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Ederson made a stunning late save to preserve a 2-1 win for Manchester City over Everton at Etihad Stadium on Saturday, keeping City atop the Premier League table with 24 points. Erling Haaland opened the scoring in the 18th minute, converting a low cross from Kevin De Bruyne, before Everton's Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalized in the 53rd minute with a header. Substitute Jack Grealish restored City's lead in the 81st minute, firing a left-footed strike from the edge of the box past goalkeeper Jordan Pickford. Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola praised his side's resilience after the match, telling reporters, "We showed character today against a very organized Everton team." Everton manager Sean Dyche said his players deserved more from the trip to Manchester. The victory extended City's unbeaten run to 12 matches across all competitions. Attendance at Etihad Stadium was announced at 53,112. City's next fixture is scheduled for October 21 against RB Leipzig in the UEFA Champions League. Meanwhile, City captain Kyle Walker was shown a yellow card in the 67th minute for a late challenge on Everton midfielder Abdoulaye Doucoure. The Football Association confirmed no further disciplinary action would be taken. City remain three points ahead of Arsenal, who face Chelsea on Sunday at Stamford Bridge.

On March 11, 2024, Judge Patricia Nunziato sentenced Marcus Delaney, 41, of Newark, to 63 months in federal custody after a jury found him guilty of wire fraud in connection with a scheme that defrauded investors of Ashford Capital Partners, a Trenton-based investment firm, of approximately $2.3 million. Prosecutor Elena Voss of the Essex County District Attorney's Office argued that Delaney used falsified brokerage statements between January 2019 and August 2022 to solicit funds from at least 34 clients.

Delaney was arrested by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation on September 5, 2023, at his residence on Ridgewood Avenue in Newark. He was subsequently charged with wire fraud and securities fraud in a hearing held October 2, 2023, at the Martin Luther King Jr. Federal Building in Newark. Defense attorney Harold Wexler contended that Delaney's business partner, Renata Cho, orchestrated the fraudulent statements, though no charges have been filed against her.

Judge Nunziato ordered Delaney to pay restitution of $1.8 million to victims, payable within five years, and barred him permanently from working in the securities industry. Ashford Capital Partners, founded by Gregory Ashford in 2011, filed for bankruptcy protection in Trenton on November 14, 2023, shortly after the fraud allegations became public. Ashford told reporters outside the courthouse that the firm intends to pursue civil litigation against Delaney to recover remaining losses.

AUSTIN, Texas - Meridian Robotics Inc. announced on June 12, 2024 that it has acquired Palo Alto-based sensor startup Veridax Systems for $84 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by August 1, 2024, will bring Veridax's 45 employees and its lidar patent portfolio under Meridian's autonomous vehicle division.

Meridian CEO Rachel Ostrander said the acquisition strengthens the company's push into self-driving delivery vehicles. "Veridax's sensor fusion technology will accelerate our Falcon-9X delivery van program by at least a year," Ostrander said during a press conference at Meridian's headquarters in Austin.

Veridax co-founder Daniel Ibarra, who will join Meridian as Vice President of Sensor Engineering effective August 5, 2024, called the merger a "natural fit." Ibarra co-founded Veridax in 2018 with fellow engineer Priya Nathan, who left the company in 2022 to join Tesla.

Meridian, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol MRDN, reported $1.2 billion in revenue last year and employs roughly 3,200 people across facilities in Austin, Detroit, and Munich. The company was founded in 2011 by brothers Thomas and Gregory Wu.

Analysts at Baird Equity Research said the acquisition positions Meridian as a stronger competitor to Waymo and Nuro in the autonomous delivery space. Shares of Meridian rose 4.3 percent following the announcement, closing at $67.90 on the Nasdaq.

The transaction is subject to standard regulatory approval and is not expected to face antitrust hurdles, according to Meridian's general counsel, Elena Vasquez.

Denver-based Alpine Freight Corp. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired regional logistics firm Summit Haulers Inc. for $142 million in cash, expanding its footprint across the Mountain West. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing in Denver, Colorado, was confirmed by Alpine Freight's chief executive officer, Marcus Whitfield, who said the acquisition would close by January 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval. Summit Haulers, founded in 1998 by entrepreneur Diane Kessler, operates a fleet of roughly 340 trucks and employs about 1,200 people across Utah, Wyoming and Colorado. Kessler will remain with the combined company as senior vice president of operations, according to a statement released Wednesday. Analysts at Bridgeport Capital Partners said the transaction values Summit Haulers at nearly 9 times its projected 2025 earnings, calling the price reasonable given rising freight demand in the region. Shares of Alpine Freight, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker ALFR, rose 6.3 percent to $58.40 following the announcement. The company also disclosed that it will retire $40 million of Summit Haulers' existing debt as part of the arrangement. Whitfield, speaking to reporters, said the combined entity would generate approximately $780 million in annual revenue and create 150 new jobs in Denver over the next two years. Summit Haulers' current chief financial officer, Raymond Ortiz, is expected to depart the company once the merger finalizes, though no successor has yet been named. Trading of ALFR shares was halted briefly Tuesday morning ahead of the announcement.

Pixelbook Labs, a San Jose startup founded in 2019 by former Apple engineer Renata Volkov, unveiled its second-generation e-reader, the InkPad 2, on October 14, 2024. Priced at $249, the device targets students and commuters with a 7-inch E Ink display and a claimed 6-week battery life. I have spent three weeks with a review unit, and the InkPad 2 largely delivers on its promises.

The build quality is a clear step up from the original InkPad, which shipped in 2021 to lukewarm reviews. The aluminum chassis feels sturdier than the plastic shell of its predecessor, and the new stylus, sold separately for $39, offers noticeably less latency than competing pens from Kobo. Software is where the InkPad 2 shines: Pixelbook Labs partnered with Bengaluru-based developer Aarav Mehta's studio, Quillwork Software, to build a note-taking suite that syncs across devices in under two seconds on a stable Wi-Fi connection.

Not everything is perfect. The device lacks a headphone jack, and the included USB-C cable is only 0.5 meters long, an odd choice for a product meant to travel. Battery life in my testing landed closer to five weeks with moderate use, still respectable but short of the marketing claim.

Pixelbook Labs CEO Renata Volkov said at a press briefing in Palo Alto on October 15 that the company plans to ship 200,000 units by March 2025 and is already in talks with retailer BookNest to expand distribution. Rivals Amazon and Rakuten's Kobo division will likely feel the pressure. At $249, the InkPad 2 is not cheap, but for readers tired of glare and short battery life, it is the most compelling e-reader I have tested this year.

Dr. Amara Voss (born March 14, 1958, in Leipzig, East Germany) is a German-American physicist known for her contributions to superconducting materials research. She earned a Ph.D. in Condensed Matter Physics from the Technical University of Munich in 1984 before emigrating to the United States in 1986. Voss joined Bell Laboratories in Murray Hill, New Jersey, in 1987 as a Research Scientist, where she spent fourteen years studying high-temperature superconductors made from yttrium barium copper oxide. In 1998, she led the team that synthesized a novel compound, later named Vossite, which retained superconductivity at minus 140 degrees Celsius, a record at the time. She left Bell Laboratories in 2001 to become Professor of Physics at Stanford University, a position she held for over two decades. In 2005, Voss co-founded Solara Quantum Inc., a startup developing superconducting components for quantum computers, headquartered in Palo Alto, California. The company was acquired by IBM in 2014 for approximately $340 million. Voss received the Wolf Prize in Physics in 2011, awarded by the Wolf Foundation in Jerusalem, for her discovery of Vossite. She married fellow physicist Daniel Reyes in 1990, and the couple has one daughter, Elena Reyes, born in 1994 in Palo Alto. Voss retired from Stanford University in 2022 and now serves on the advisory board of the National Science Foundation.

The Ontario Ministry of Transportation announced on Tuesday, June 11, 2024, that it will invest $340 million to widen Highway 401 between Milton and Mississauga, aiming to reduce congestion for the roughly 500,000 daily commuters who use the corridor. Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria said the project, known as the Highway 401 Expansion Initiative, will add two additional lanes in each direction and is expected to be completed by December 2027. Construction firm Aecon Group Inc., headquartered in Toronto, was awarded the primary contract following a competitive bidding process that concluded last month. Deputy Minister Doug Jones stated that the ministry will also allocate $25 million toward noise-barrier upgrades for residents in Oakville and Burlington. The announcement follows a March 2024 report by the Ontario Auditor General, Bonnie Lysyk, which found that traffic delays on the corridor cost the provincial economy an estimated $1.2 billion annually. Premier Doug Ford, speaking at a press conference in Milton, called the investment "a critical step toward keeping Ontario moving." Environmental groups, including Ontario Nature, have raised concerns about wetland disruption near the Credit River and have requested a supplementary environmental assessment before construction begins in September 2024. The Ministry of Transportation confirmed that public consultations will be held in Mississauga on July 8, 2024, to address community feedback.

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY — On October 14, 2024, Judge Marion T. Delacroix sentenced Raymond Hutchins, 47, of Newark, to 8 years in state prison after a jury convicted him of aggravated arson in connection with a fire at the Wickham Street Warehouse in Newark on March 3, 2023. Prosecutor Angela Ferris of the Essex County Prosecutor's Office argued that Hutchins deliberately set the blaze to collapse the building owned by Delmore Holdings LLC, causing $2.3 million in damages and injuring firefighter Paul Osei, who suffered smoke inhalation while responding to the scene. Hutchins was arrested on April 9, 2023, by detectives from the Newark Police Department following an investigation that included surveillance footage and forensic chemical analysis identifying traces of acetone accelerant at the site. During the three-day trial, held at the Essex County Courthouse, defense attorney Marcus Whitfield contended his client was not present when the fire started, but jurors rejected the argument after eight hours of deliberation. Judge Delacroix also ordered Hutchins to pay $450,000 in restitution to Delmore Holdings LLC within five years of his release. Hutchins's sentence includes credit for 18 months already served in the Essex County Correctional Facility. His attorney has filed notice of appeal with the Appellate Division of the Superior Court, arguing that the chemical evidence was improperly admitted under New Jersey Rule of Evidence 702. The case, State v. Hutchins, drew attention from local business owners concerned about a string of unresolved warehouse fires across Newark since 2022.

The Department of Transportation for the State of Oregon announced on March 4, 2024 that it will allocate $85 million to repair the Fremont Bridge in Portland after inspectors found structural corrosion in December 2023. Secretary of Transportation Maria Delgado stated at a press conference in Salem that the funding, drawn from the Federal Highway Administration's Bridge Formula Program, will cover repairs beginning in June 2024 and concluding by October 2025. "This bridge carries over 140,000 vehicles daily, and we cannot allow deferred maintenance to become a safety crisis," Delgado said. The contract for the repair work was awarded to Kiewit Infrastructure West, a subsidiary of Kiewit Corporation headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska. Kiewit's regional director, Thomas Ng, confirmed that up to 220 workers will be deployed to the site starting in June. Governor Tina Kotek praised the initiative, noting that similar inspections will be conducted on the Interstate Bridge connecting Oregon and Washington later this year. The Oregon Department of Transportation also confirmed that a 25 percent contingency reserve, roughly $21 million, has been set aside for unforeseen structural issues discovered during the project. Community advocacy group Bridge Watch Portland welcomed the announcement but urged the agency to publish quarterly progress reports. The repair project is expected to be substantially completed by the fourth quarter of 2025, according to Delgado's office.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Solid Hardware, Uneven Software

By Renata Solis, published October 14, 2024

Google launched the Pixel Watch 3 on September 20, 2024, priced at $349.99 for the 41mm Wi-Fi model, and I have worn it daily for three weeks in Austin, Texas. The domed Actua display is genuinely gorgeous, hitting 2,000 nits of peak brightness that made it readable even during a blistering 102-degree afternoon at Zilker Park.

Battery life lands around 24 hours with the always-on display enabled, which is respectable but still trails the 36 hours Samsung claims for the Galaxy Watch7. The new Loss of Pulse Detection feature, built with input from cardiologists at the Cleveland Clinic, worked reliably in my testing, though I never needed it to summon help.

Google's Fitbit division, which Google acquired back in 2019, clearly shaped the software here. Sarah Tan, a product manager at Google, told me in a phone interview on October 2, 2024 that the team spent eighteen months tuning the heart-rate algorithms with Fitbit's engineers in San Francisco.

My only real complaint is pricing: at $499.99 for the 45mm LTE version, the Pixel Watch 3 competes directly with Apple's Apple Watch Series 9, and Google still lags Apple in third-party app support. Still, for Android users, this is the best Wear OS device Google has ever shipped, and I recommend it without much hesitation.

Rating: 4 out of 5 stars.

Boston, MA -- November 14, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolerabrin, an investigational oral inhibitor developed by Cascade Therapeutics, in patients with moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis. The randomized, double-blind study enrolled 214 adults across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2022 and July 2023. Dr. Elena Vasquez, the trial's principal investigator and a professor of gastroenterology at Harvard Medical School, presented the findings at the American College of Gastroenterology meeting held in Vancouver on November 13, 2023. Patients receiving 150 milligrams of tolerabrin twice daily achieved clinical remission at a rate of 42 percent after 12 weeks, compared with 16 percent in the placebo group, a difference the authors called statistically significant. Common adverse events included headache, reported by 11 percent of participants, and mild nasopharyngitis. Two serious adverse events, including one case of pneumonia, occurred in the treatment arm but were not deemed drug-related by an independent safety board. Cascade Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, said it plans to initiate a phase 3 program in early 2024 pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The company's chief medical officer, Dr. Raj Patel, noted that ulcerative colitis affects roughly 900,000 people in the United States and that existing therapies fail to induce remission in a substantial proportion of patients. The study was funded in part by a $22 million grant from the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases. Full results were published simultaneously in The New England Journal of Medicine.

CAMBRIDGE, MA -- October 14, 2024 -- Meridian Biosciences Inc. announced today that it has acquired NovaGen Therapeutics, a privately held biotechnology firm based in Boulder, Colorado, for approximately $340 million in cash and stock. The acquisition, which closed on October 11, 2024, strengthens Meridian's pipeline in autoimmune disease treatment ahead of its planned expansion into European markets.

Under the terms of the agreement, Meridian will pay NovaGen shareholders $12.50 per share, representing a 28 percent premium over NovaGen's closing price on September 30, 2024. NovaGen's lead compound, an experimental therapy for rheumatoid arthritis known as NVG-207, will be integrated into Meridian's existing portfolio alongside its flagship product, Arthrolex.

"This transaction positions Meridian as a leader in next-generation immunology treatments," said Dr. Elena Fairweather, Chief Executive Officer of Meridian Biosciences, in a statement released at the company's headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Dr. Fairweather will oversee the integration alongside NovaGen founder Dr. Rajiv Malhotra, who has agreed to join Meridian as Chief Scientific Officer effective November 1, 2024.

Meridian's board of directors, led by chairman Thomas Whitfield, approved the deal on October 9, 2024. The company expects the transaction to add $95 million in annual revenue by fiscal year 2026. Meridian Biosciences, founded in 1998 by Dr. Fairweather and now employing more than 3,200 people worldwide, trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol MRDN. Shares rose 6 percent following the announcement.

DETROIT, Mich. — Nautilus Motors Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $412 million in outstanding debt and slumping demand for its electric pickup trucks. The filing, submitted in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan, marks a sharp fall for a company once valued at $3.8 billion.

CEO Marcus Delaney told reporters at a press conference in Detroit that the company would continue limited operations while restructuring. "We owe it to our 1,400 employees to fight for this company," Delaney said. Nautilus Motors, founded in 2016 by engineer Priya Nandakumar, had been a supplier to logistics firm Kestrel Freight before losing the contract last year to competitor Voltway Trucks.

According to court documents, Nautilus Motors owes $86 million to parts supplier Ironclad Steel Corp. and $54 million to lender First Meridian Bank. Analysts at Bloomberg Intelligence said the bankruptcy could result in the layoff of up to 900 workers at the company's Flint, Michigan assembly plant.

Delaney, who took over as CEO in March 2022 after founder Nandakumar stepped down, said the company is in talks with investment firm Blackstone Group about a possible $200 million rescue financing package. A hearing before Judge Elena Ruiz is scheduled for November 14 in Detroit to review the restructuring plan.

Shares of Nautilus Motors, which trade under the ticker NAUT, fell 61 percent in after-hours trading following the announcement.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA. On October 14, 2024, Judge Patricia Wexler sentenced defendant Marcus Delaney, 41, to seven years in state prison after a jury in Oakland convicted him of embezzlement and wire fraud related to his former position as chief financial officer of Bramwell Logistics Inc., a freight-forwarding company headquartered in San Leandro, California. Prosecutor Angela Nguyen, representing the Alameda County District Attorney's Office, told the court that Delaney diverted approximately $2.3 million from company accounts between March 2019 and June 2023, funneling the funds through a shell entity called Coastal Ridge Holdings before spending it on real estate in Lake Tahoe and a 2021 Porsche 911. Defense attorney Harold Fenwick argued for leniency, citing Delaney's lack of prior convictions, but Judge Wexler rejected the request, calling the scheme "a calculated betrayal of trust spanning four years." Bramwell Logistics was acquired by Meridian Supply Chain Group in September 2023 for $58 million, a deal finalized shortly after the fraud came to light during an internal audit. Delaney was arrested by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation on November 3, 2023, at his home in Pleasanton, and was formally charged in April 2024 with grand theft and falsifying corporate records. He is expected to begin serving his sentence at San Quentin State Prison next month. The court also ordered Delaney to pay $2.3 million in restitution to Meridian Supply Chain Group.

input: Marguerite Okafor (born 12 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-British structural engineer known for pioneering earthquake-resistant design in West African construction. She earned a degree in Civil Engineering from Imperial College London in 1980 and later joined Balfour Beatty as a junior engineer in 1982. In 1991, Okafor founded Okafor Structural Associates in Lagos, a firm that grew to employ over 400 engineers across three countries. The company was acquired by the multinational conglomerate Arup Group for an estimated 45 million pounds in 2006, after which Okafor remained as Chief Design Officer until 2011. During her tenure, she led the structural design of the Lekki Suspension Bridge, completed in 2009, and consulted on reconstruction efforts following the 2010 Haiti earthquake, traveling to Port-au-Prince in February 2010 with a team of twelve engineers. In 2015, she was appointed Professor of Civil Engineering at the University of Lagos, a position she held for six years before stepping down in 2021. Okafor received the Royal Academy of Engineering's Gold Medal in London in 2013, awarded by Sir John Parker for her contributions to sustainable infrastructure. She married fellow engineer Thomas Whitfield in 1985, and the couple has two children. Okafor currently serves on the board of the Nigerian Society of Engineers and continues to consult for construction firms across sub-Saharan Africa from her home base in Lagos.

Framework Computing launched the Framework Laptop 13 (Ryzen AI 9) on March 5, 2024, in Sacramento, California, pricing the base configuration at $1,099. I tested the unit for three weeks before writing this review. The device uses AMD's Ryzen AI 9 365 chip, an upgrade over the Intel Core Ultra model the company sold in 2023, and Framework claims a 20 percent gain in battery life, which roughly matched my own measurements of just over nine hours of mixed use. What sets this laptop apart is still the modular port system: four swappable Expansion Cards let owners choose between USB-C, HDMI, and even a 1TB storage module, and every card can be replaced with a small screwdriver in under a minute. Nirav Patel, the company's founder and chief executive officer, told me in a phone interview from San Jose that Framework has now sold more than 100,000 units worldwide since the original 2021 launch. He also confirmed that Framework is working with Best Buy to expand retail distribution to 200 stores by June 2024. The keyboard deck flexes slightly under heavy typing, and the 2.8-pound chassis, while lighter than last year's, still trails the 2.5-pound Dell XPS 13 in raw portability. Framework competes directly with Dell and with Lenovo's ThinkPad line, but neither rival lets you replace a broken port yourself. At $1,099 for the base model, this is not the cheapest ultrabook on the market, but it may be the most honest one, built for people who intend to keep it for a decade rather than upgrade every two years.

Pixelforge Labs, a design studio based in Portland, Oregon, launched the Contour Slate 2 on June 11, 2024, and after three weeks of daily use I can say it is the most refined drawing tablet the company has shipped. Priced at $449, the Contour Slate 2 improves on its predecessor with a 13.3-inch E Ink display, an 8192-level pressure sensor stylus, and a battery that lasted me nine full days of note-taking between charges. Pixelforge's founder, Naomi Iverson, told reporters at a briefing in San Francisco that the device was built to compete directly with the reMarkable 2, made by Norwegian company reMarkable AS. In hands-on testing, the Contour Slate 2 felt noticeably faster than the reMarkable 2, thanks to a new ARM-based chip Pixelforge sources from Kestrel Semiconductor, a supplier headquartered in Austin, Texas. Software remains the weak point: the companion app crashed twice during a syncing attempt on July 2, and cloud backup support for Google Drive still is not available. Pixelforge says a firmware update is scheduled for August 2024 to address the crashes. At $449, the Contour Slate 2 undercuts the reMarkable 2 by roughly $130, which matters for students and journalists on tight budgets. Still, the thinner software ecosystem and lack of a marketplace for templates hold it back from being a universal recommendation. For creative professionals who value paper-like writing feel and long battery life over app polish, the Contour Slate 2 is an easy recommendation; for everyone else, waiting for the promised firmware update in August seems wiser.

DETROIT, Mich. — Meridian Motors Inc. announced Tuesday it will acquire electric-vehicle battery maker VoltCore Technologies for $1.2 billion, in a deal expected to close by March 15, 2025. The agreement was unveiled at a press conference at Meridian's headquarters in Detroit, Michigan, by Chief Executive Officer Diane Halbrook.

"VoltCore's lithium-iron-phosphate battery technology will accelerate our shift to electric vehicles," Halbrook told reporters. VoltCore, based in Austin, Texas, was founded in 2016 by engineer Marcus Rhee, who will join Meridian as Chief Technology Officer effective April 1, 2025.

Meridian, headquartered in Detroit since 1955, currently employs about 48,000 workers worldwide and competes directly with Falcon Auto Group. Shares of Meridian rose 6 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while VoltCore's private investors, including Redwood Capital Partners, are expected to receive payouts within 60 days of closing.

Analysts at Sterling Bridge Research called the acquisition "a bold bet on battery supply chains," noting that VoltCore currently supplies battery cells to three other automakers, including Falcon Auto Group. The deal still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which is expected to review antitrust concerns by early February 2025.

Halbrook said Meridian plans to retain all 1,400 VoltCore employees and expand the company's Austin manufacturing plant, adding roughly 500 new jobs by the end of 2026.

Elena Vasquez (born March 14, 1962, in Tucson, Arizona) is an American structural engineer known for pioneering seismic retrofitting techniques used across the western United States. She earned a bachelor's degree in civil engineering from the University of Arizona in 1984 and a doctorate from Stanford University in 1989. In 1993, Vasquez joined Bechtel Corporation as a senior structural engineer, working on infrastructure projects throughout California. Five years later, she left to found Meridian Structural Group in San Francisco, a firm specializing in earthquake-resistant design for hospitals and schools.

Under her leadership as Chief Executive Officer, Meridian Structural Group grew from a three-person office to a firm of over 200 engineers by 2010. The company was later acquired by AECOM for approximately $85 million in 2015, a deal announced in Los Angeles that allowed Vasquez to remain as a consultant for two years. In 2018, she stepped down from her consulting role to focus on academic work.

Vasquez has received numerous honors, including the National Medal of Technology, presented to her by President Barack Obama at a ceremony in Washington, D.C. in November 2011. She has also served as a visiting professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology since 2019, teaching courses on structural resilience.

Married to fellow engineer Thomas Reyes since 1990, Vasquez has two children. She currently lives in Berkeley, California, where she continues to consult on retrofitting projects for the San Francisco Bay Area Rapid Transit District.

input: BOSTON, MA - September 12, 2023 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tremelimumab-plus-durvalumab combination therapy in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez and published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, enrolled 214 participants across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and June 2022. Patients receiving the combination showed a median overall survival of 16.4 months compared to 10.7 months in the control group treated with sorafenib alone, representing a 34 percent reduction in mortality risk. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 22 percent of the combination arm, primarily hepatotoxicity and rash. AstraZeneca, which manufactures both durvalumab and tremelimumab, funded the trial with a research grant of $8.3 million. Dr. Vasquez stated that the findings could shift first-line treatment guidelines for hepatocellular carcinoma within the next two years. The Food and Drug Administration is expected to review the combination for accelerated approval by early 2024, according to a statement from AstraZeneca spokesperson Mark Hutton. Dr. Rajiv Chandra of the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, who was not involved in the study, called the results "a meaningful step forward" for a disease with historically poor prognosis, noting that hepatocellular carcinoma accounts for roughly 830,000 deaths worldwide each year. The research team plans to present full data at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting in Chicago next June.

The company, headquartered in Grafton since 1978, employs 1,150 workers at its main plant and had already laid off 210 employees in September.

CEO Harold Vance told reporters at a Cleveland press conference that the filing would allow Meridian to restructure operations while continuing to supply steel coils to Ford Motor Company and Whirlpool Corporation. "We intend to keep the furnaces running," Vance said, adding that no further layoffs were planned before January 2025.

The bankruptcy filing, submitted to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Ohio, lists Cerberus Capital Management as the largest secured creditor, owed roughly $95 million. Judge Alan Koschik is expected to hold an initial hearing on November 18.

Union representatives from United Steelworkers Local 1104 gathered outside the Grafton plant on Wednesday to protest potential pension cuts. Organizer Denise Marsh said nearly 300 retirees could see reduced benefits if the restructuring plan proceeds as filed.

Analysts at Fitch Ratings downgraded Meridian's corporate credit rating to CCC on Wednesday afternoon, warning that recovery for unsecured bondholders could fall below 20 percent. Shares of Meridian, which trade over the counter, fell 62 percent to $0.38 before trading was halted.

input: MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 - Manchester City defeated Everton 3-1 at Etihad Stadium on Saturday, moving the defending champions to the top of the Premier League table with 22 points. Erling Haaland opened the scoring in the 12th minute, finishing a low cross from Kevin De Bruyne, and doubled his tally with a penalty in the 38th minute after Jordan Pickford fouled Phil Foden inside the box. Everton pulled one back through Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 61st minute, but Julian Alvarez restored City's two-goal cushion in the 84th minute with a curling effort from outside the area. Manager Pep Guardiola praised his side's composure after the match, saying the team had "controlled the tempo from start to finish." Everton boss Sean Dyche said his players "competed hard but lacked a final ball in the final third." The win extended Manchester City's unbeaten run to 11 matches across all competitions. Haaland, who now has 12 goals in 9 appearances this season, was named Player of the Match by broadcaster Sky Sports. Attendance at Etihad Stadium was announced at 53,412. Manchester City will next travel to London on October 21 to face Arsenal at Emirates Stadium, a fixture that could decide early control of the title race.

DETROIT, Mich. — Ferran Industries, a mid-sized auto parts supplier based in Detroit, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in outstanding debt and a sharp drop in orders from General Motors. The filing was submitted to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan by chief executive officer Daniel Vasquez, who has led the company since March 2019. Ferran Industries, founded in 1987 by engineer Harold Kim, employs roughly 1,200 workers across three plants in Michigan and Ohio. Vasquez said in a statement that the company plans to continue operations during restructuring and expects to emerge from bankruptcy by early 2026. The bankruptcy follows a turbulent year for Ferran, which lost a major supply contract with Ford Motor Company in June 2024 after failing to meet delivery targets. Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimate that nearly 400 jobs could be at risk if the restructuring plan requires plant closures. General Motors, which had relied on Ferran for transmission components, said it is already in talks with a competing supplier, Bosch, to fill the gap. Local union representative Angela Ferreira told reporters outside the courthouse in Detroit that workers are "frightened and angry" about the uncertainty. Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer's office issued a statement Tuesday afternoon saying state officials would "monitor the situation closely" and explore support programs for affected employees. Ferran's stock, delisted from Nasdaq in 2023, had already lost most of its value.

input: BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024 — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tavaropril, an oral chemical compound designed to inhibit fibrotic progression in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh and published in The New England Journal of Medicine, enrolled 214 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of tavaropril twice daily showed a 37 percent reduction in lung function decline compared to placebo over 52 weeks, as measured by forced vital capacity. Dr. Marsh stated that the results represent the most promising advance in IPF treatment since the approval of pirfenidone in 2014. The trial was funded by Halden Biotherapeutics, a biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, which plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. Halden Biotherapeutics was founded in 2016 by former Pfizer executive Raymond Cho, who now serves as chief executive officer. The company's shares rose 22 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, reflecting investor confidence in the drug's commercial potential, estimated by analysts at Morgan Stanley to exceed 1.8 billion dollars annually if approved. Adverse events were reported in 12 percent of participants, most commonly mild gastrointestinal symptoms. Dr. Marsh presented the full dataset at the American Thoracic Society conference in San Diego on May 19, 2024, where she received the society's Outstanding Research Award.
