DETROIT, Mich. — Faircrest Motors announced Tuesday it will acquire battery startup VoltaraCell Inc. for $410 million, in a deal aimed at securing lithium-ion supply for its electric truck line. The agreement was signed at Faircrest's headquarters on Woodward Avenue and is expected to close by November 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

CEO Renata Alvarez said the acquisition of VoltaraCell, founded in 2018 by engineer Daniel Osei, would let Faircrest produce battery cells in-house rather than relying on supplier Nishimura Energy of Osaka, Japan. "This is about controlling our own supply chain," Alvarez told reporters during a press briefing in Detroit.

Under the terms of the deal, VoltaraCell's 320 employees will join Faircrest Motors, and Osei will take the newly created role of Chief Battery Officer, reporting directly to Alvarez starting December 1, 2024. VoltaraCell's factory in Reno, Nevada, which currently produces 2 gigawatt-hours of cells annually, will be expanded under the agreement.

Industry analysts at Whitmore Research estimate the deal could raise Faircrest's stock price by as much as 8 percent when markets react Wednesday. Faircrest shares closed at $76.40 on Tuesday, up 3 percent.

The move comes as competitor Larkspur Auto also seeks battery partnerships, having signed a supply agreement with Nishimura Energy last month. Faircrest, headquartered in Detroit since 1952, employs roughly 41,000 people worldwide.

DETROIT, Mich. — Sterling Metalworks Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $42 million in unpaid debts and a sharp decline in orders from the automotive sector. The filing was submitted to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Detroit by CEO Raymond Kowalski, who has led the company since March 2019.

Sterling Metalworks, founded in 1978 by Harold Sterling, employs roughly 640 workers across two plants in Michigan and Ohio. Kowalski told reporters at a press conference that the company plans to restructure operations rather than liquidate. "We intend to keep our Toledo facility running and protect as many jobs as possible," he said.

The bankruptcy follows a turbulent year for the auto parts supplier, which lost a major contract with Grayson Motors in June after the automaker shifted sourcing to a competitor, Falkirk Components. Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimate Sterling's revenue fell 31 percent in the last fiscal year, from $210 million to roughly $145 million.

Union representatives from the United Auto Workers Local 909 said they were seeking assurances about pension obligations. "Our members built this company for four decades," said union leader Denise Alvarez. "They deserve answers, not silence."

Court documents show Sterling Metalworks owes $12 million to supplier Ferrotech Industries and $8.5 million to logistics firm Reddaway Freight. A hearing before Judge Patricia Nolan is scheduled for November 14 to review the reorganization plan. Kowalski said the company hopes to emerge from bankruptcy by mid-2025.

On March 14, 2024, Judge Marisol Fenwick sentenced Trevor Coyle, 41, to 36 months in state prison after a jury in Oakland convicted him of grand theft and wire fraud in connection with the collapse of his firm, Coyle Capital Partners LLC. Prosecutor Daniel Ashworth of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Coyle diverted $2.3 million from investor accounts between January 2021 and September 2023 to fund personal real estate purchases in Marin County.

During the two-week trial held at the René C. Davidson Courthouse, witness Priya Nakamura, a former compliance officer at Coyle Capital Partners LLC, testified that she had flagged irregular wire transfers to executives as early as June 2022. The defense, led by attorney Harold Simms, contended that Coyle had merely mismanaged funds rather than committed fraud, but the jury rejected that argument after four days of deliberation.

Coyle Capital Partners LLC, headquartered in Emeryville, was placed into receivership in October 2023 after regulators from the California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation opened an investigation. The firm had roughly 140 clients and managed an estimated $18 million in assets at its peak in 2022.

Judge Fenwick also ordered Coyle to pay $2.3 million in restitution to victims, payable within five years. Coyle's attorney indicated an appeal would be filed with the California Court of Appeal within 60 days.

Portland, Ore. — Timberline Foods Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Cascade Roasters LLC, a specialty coffee roaster based in Bend, Oregon, for $42 million in cash. The deal, expected to close on November 15, will bring Cascade Roasters' 18 retail cafes and its wholesale supply operations under Timberline's growing beverage division.

CEO Marion Whitfield said the acquisition strengthens Timberline's position against competitor Peak Brew Holdings, which operates more than 60 locations across the Pacific Northwest. "Cascade Roasters has built a loyal following over its 22 years in business, and we intend to preserve that identity while scaling distribution nationally," Whitfield said during a press briefing at Timberline's headquarters in Portland.

Cascade Roasters founder Diego Alvarez, who started the company in 2002 with his sister Elena Alvarez, will stay on as an advisor for one year under the terms of the agreement. Elena Alvarez left her role as head roaster in 2019 to launch a separate venture in Seattle.

Timberline Foods, a subsidiary of Willamette Holdings Corp., financed the purchase through a combination of $30 million in cash reserves and a $12 million loan from First Cascade Bank. Analysts at Rivergate Securities estimated the deal values Cascade Roasters at roughly 3.5 times its annual revenue of $12 million.

Shares of Willamette Holdings rose 4.2 percent following the announcement, closing at $58.90 on the New York Stock Exchange. Whitfield added that Timberline plans to open five new joint-branded cafes in Seattle and Vancouver, Washington by mid-2025.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 - Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side defeated Everton 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, moving Villa into fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute, converting a low cross from midfielder John McGinn, before doubling his tally just before halftime with a close-range header. Everton pulled one back through striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 58th minute, but substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win for Villa with a curling strike in the 84th minute. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his team's discipline after the match, telling reporters at the post-match press conference, "We controlled the tempo for large parts of the game, and Ollie's movement was the difference." Everton manager Sean Dyche acknowledged his team's struggles, saying his side needed to be more clinical in the final third. The win extended Aston Villa's unbeaten home run to eight matches and lifted the club to 19 points from eight games. Villa will next travel to face Tottenham Hotspur at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 21, while Everton will host Brentford at Goodison Park the same weekend. Villa Park recorded an attendance of 41,912 for Saturday's fixture, one of the highest gates of the season so far.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., June 12, 2024 — Solara Biotics, Inc., a clinical-stage biotechnology firm, today announced that it has acquired Nexvant Therapeutics for $340 million in cash and stock. The deal, finalized on June 10, 2024, gives Solara Biotics full rights to Nexvant's lead compound, ZL-9207, an experimental treatment for chronic kidney disease currently in Phase II trials.

Under the terms of the agreement, Solara Biotics will pay Nexvant Therapeutics shareholders $18.50 per share, representing a 42 percent premium over Nexvant's closing price on June 7, 2024. The transaction is expected to close in the third quarter of 2024, pending regulatory approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

"This acquisition strengthens our renal disease pipeline and accelerates our path to commercialization," said Dr. Priya Ramaswamy, Chief Executive Officer of Solara Biotics, at a press briefing held in Cambridge on June 12, 2024. Ramaswamy will oversee integration efforts alongside Marcus Elling, who joined Solara Biotics as Chief Financial Officer on May 1, 2024, after leaving his post at Bramwell Pharma.

Nexvant Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by Dr. Owen Falk in Boston, employs 95 researchers and holds three patents related to ZL-9207. Falk will join Solara Biotics' scientific advisory board following the close of the deal.

Solara Biotics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker SLRB. Shares rose 6 percent in after-hours trading following the announcement.

BOSTON, MA -- November 4, 2023. Researchers at Beacon Harbor Institute announced results from a phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tazovirumab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed to treat chronic hepatitis D, in a study published in the Journal of Hepatic Medicine. The trial, led by Dr. Priya Anand, enrolled 214 adults with confirmed hepatitis D virus infection across seven sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and June 2022. Participants received either 300 milligrams of tazovirumab administered intravenously every four weeks or a matching placebo for 48 weeks. By week 48, 61 percent of patients receiving tazovirumab achieved undetectable viral RNA, compared with 9 percent in the placebo group, a difference the authors described as statistically significant. The most common adverse event was mild injection-site irritation, reported in 22 patients, while three patients discontinued treatment due to elevated liver enzymes. Beacon Harbor Institute, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, funded the study jointly with Norrvale Therapeutics, a biopharmaceutical company based in Basel, Switzerland, which holds the patent on tazovirumab. Dr. Anand said the results support advancing to a phase 3 trial, expected to begin in early 2024 at additional sites in Canada and Japan. Norrvale Therapeutics shares rose 14 percent following the announcement. Separately, the Food and Drug Administration granted tazovirumab breakthrough therapy designation on October 30, 2023, potentially accelerating its regulatory review. Approximately 12 million people worldwide are estimated to live with chronic hepatitis D, which can progress to cirrhosis and liver failure without effective treatment.

Villa manager Unai Emery praised his side's discipline after the match, telling reporters at the post-match press conference, "We controlled the game for long periods and deserved the three points." Newcastle boss Eddie Howe acknowledged his team's defensive lapses, saying the club would review the performance before hosting Arsenal on October 26. BOSTON, MA — October 14, 2023 — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolibrexafil, an experimental oral therapy for moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh and published in The Lancet Rheumatology, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2022 and January 2023. Participants received either 50 milligrams of tolibrexafil daily or a placebo for 24 weeks. By week 24, 61 percent of patients on tolibrexafil achieved an ACR50 response compared with 27 percent on placebo, a statistically significant difference (p<0.001). Dr. Marsh noted that the drug, developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arolix Therapeutics, also showed a favorable safety profile, with only 4 percent of participants discontinuing due to adverse events, most commonly mild nausea. Arolix Therapeutics was founded in 2016 by former Pfizer executive Dr. Samuel Okafor and has raised $180 million in venture funding to date. The company's chief executive, Rachel Tan, stated during a press briefing at the company's Cambridge headquarters that Arolix plans to begin a Phase 3 trial in early 2024 involving approximately 900 patients across sites in the United States, Germany, and Japan. Analysts at Jefferies estimate peak annual sales for tolibrexafil could reach $1.2 billion if approved by the Food and Drug Administration, expected no earlier than 2026. Rheumatologist Dr. Priya Nandakumar of Johns Hopkins University, who was not involved in the study, called the results "a meaningful advance" for patients who have failed existing biologic therapies.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Aiden Crowley scored twice as Ashborne United defeated Millfield Rovers 3-1 at Denholm Park on Saturday, moving the club into second place in the Northern Championship table. Crowley opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a low finish from the edge of the box, then doubled his tally in the 38th minute after a swift counterattack led by winger Marcus Doyle. Millfield Rovers pulled one back through striker Jonas Petrik in the 54th minute, but substitute Théo Baptiste sealed the win for Ashborne United with a header in the 81st minute. Ashborne United manager Rachel Sinclair praised her squad's discipline after the match, saying, "We stayed patient and trusted the process." The victory extended Ashborne United's unbeaten run to seven matches and lifted the club to 27 points, three behind league leaders Corveth City. Millfield Rovers manager Owen Tarrant, under pressure after four consecutive losses, admitted the club needs reinforcements in January. Approximately 11,400 fans attended the match, according to Denholm Park officials. Ashborne United will next travel to Corveth City on October 21, 2023, in a fixture many are already calling a potential title decider. The Northern Football Association confirmed the match will be broadcast live nationally.

DETROIT, Mich. — Ironclad Motors Inc. announced on Tuesday, March 11, 2025, that it has acquired Bexley Battery Systems LLC, a Columbus, Ohio-based manufacturer of lithium-ion battery packs, for $412 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by June 30, 2025, will make Bexley a wholly owned subsidiary of Ironclad and is intended to secure supply for Ironclad's upcoming electric pickup truck, the Talon EV.

Ironclad Chief Executive Officer Renata Ford said the acquisition would cut battery costs by roughly 18 percent within two years. "Bexley gives us control over a critical part of our supply chain," Ford told reporters during a briefing at Ironclad's headquarters in Detroit. Bexley founder and outgoing President Marcus Lindqvist will join Ironclad as Senior Vice President of Battery Engineering starting April 1, 2025, according to a company statement.

The transaction, Ironclad's largest since its founding in 2011 by Renata Ford and Hal Buckner, still requires clearance from the Federal Trade Commission. Analysts at Merriweather Capital estimate the combined entity could generate $3.2 billion in annual revenue by 2027. Shares of Ironclad rose 6.4 percent to $58.21 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of rival automaker Voss Dynamics slipped 1.2 percent.

Bexley, founded in 2015, employs about 1,300 workers across two plants in Columbus and a smaller facility in Reno, Nevada. Ironclad said no layoffs are planned as part of the integration.

input: Bellroy Studio, an Australian accessories brand headquartered in Fitzroy, Victoria, has launched the Hyde Slim Wallet in Cognac leather, now available on the Bellroy website for $89.00 AUD. Manufactured in Chiang Mai, Thailand, and released on March 14, 2024, the Hyde Slim Wallet features six card slots, a hidden pocket for coins, and a RFID-blocking lining designed to prevent contactless skimming. Each unit weighs approximately 65 grams and measures 9.5 cm by 7 cm, making it roughly 25 percent thinner than the brand's original Note Sleeve model. Bellroy Studio was founded in 2010 by Andy Fallshaw and Ian Findlay, and the company has since shipped products to over 80 countries. The Hyde Slim Wallet is the third release in Bellroy's Heritage Collection, following the Apex Card Case launched in 2022. Customer reviews on the product page, including one from Melbourne resident Priya Nathan posted on April 2, 2024, praise the wallet's slim profile and durability, though a small number of buyers noted the $89.00 price point is higher than competitor MUJI's leather cardholders. Orders placed before 3 p.m. AEST ship the same day via Australia Post, with delivery estimated within 5 business days for domestic customers and up to 14 business days internationally. Each wallet comes with a two-year warranty and is packaged in a recyclable cotton pouch. Bellroy Studio also donates 1 percent of annual profits to the Australian Conservation Foundation as part of its sustainability pledge.

Kestrel Outdoors, a gear company headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, has launched the Talus 45L Alpine Backpack, priced at $189.99 and available starting November 3, 2023. Built for multi-day treks in the Rocky Mountains, the Talus 45L features a 210-denier ripstop nylon shell, a magnesium-alloy frame, and a removable rain cover. Kestrel Outdoors was founded in 2011 by former mountain guide Renata Ostrowski, who still serves as the company's Chief Design Officer. The Talus 45L is manufactured in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, at a facility operated by Kestrel's longtime supplier, Delta Textile Partners. Each pack weighs 1.8 kilograms and includes 6 external pockets, a hydration sleeve rated for 3 liters, and adjustable torso length for hikers between 160 and 195 centimeters tall. Early reviewers at Backcountry Journal gave the pack 4.5 out of 5 stars, praising its durability during a 12-day trial in the Cascade Range. The Talus 45L comes in three colorways: Slate Gray, Ember Orange, and Moss Green. Customers who order before December 1, 2023 receive a free Kestrel titanium spork worth $14. Kestrel Outdoors ships to the United States, Canada, and the European Union, with delivery times ranging from 3 to 10 business days. For bulk orders of 50 units or more, retailers can contact the wholesale division directly. The product is currently in stock at the company's flagship store in Bozeman and through its website, kestreloutdoors.com.

Denver-based Highline Robotics Corp. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Pemberton Sensor Systems, a Boulder, Colorado sensor manufacturer, for $142 million in cash and stock. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing in Denver, is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval.

Highline Robotics, founded in 2016 by chief executive Marisol Vance, builds automated warehouse arms used by logistics companies including Fenwick Distribution Inc. Pemberton Sensor Systems, led by founder Owen Baptiste, supplies infrared sensors that Highline currently sources for its robotic arms, making the acquisition a vertical integration move.

"This transaction gives us direct control over a critical component supply chain," Vance said during the briefing. "We expect the combined company to generate $310 million in revenue next year."

Under the terms of the agreement, Pemberton shareholders will receive $95 million in cash and $47 million in Highline stock. Owen Baptiste will join Highline's board as chief technology officer starting February 1, 2025, while roughly 80 Pemberton employees in Boulder will be retained.

Analysts at Crestwood Capital Partners, a financial advisory firm based in Chicago, said the deal positions Highline to compete more directly with rival Atlas Automation Group, which has expanded aggressively across the Midwest. Shares of Highline Robotics, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker HLRB, rose 6.3 percent following the announcement, closing at $58.40.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024 — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase II clinical trial evaluating tegoprazan-42, an experimental compound targeting metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The study, led by Dr. Helena Ruiz and funded by a $12.5 million grant from the National Institutes of Health, enrolled 214 patients across sites in Boston, Chicago, and Houston between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants received either tegoprazan-42 combined with standard gemcitabine chemotherapy or gemcitabine alone. Median overall survival reached 11.4 months in the treatment arm compared to 7.8 months in the control group, a difference the authors describe as statistically significant (p=0.003). Grade 3 or higher adverse events, primarily neutropenia and fatigue, occurred in 28 percent of treated patients versus 19 percent in controls. Dr. Ruiz presented the findings on March 12, 2024, at the American Society of Clinical Oncology meeting in Chicago, where she stated that the results "represent a meaningful step forward for a disease with historically poor outcomes." Novartis, which licensed tegoprazan-42 from the biotech startup Arborvax Therapeutics in 2021, plans to initiate a Phase III trial in early 2025 pending discussions with the Food and Drug Administration. Dr. Marcus Webb, chief medical officer at Arborvax Therapeutics, called the data "the strongest signal we have seen in this indication in a decade." The research team also noted that patients carrying a KRAS G12D mutation showed a more pronounced benefit, suggesting a potential biomarker for future patient selection. Full results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine on March 13, 2024.

Dr. Amara Osei (born 14 March 1958 in Kumasi, Ghana) is a Ghanaian-British biochemist known for her pioneering work on antimalarial compounds. After earning a doctorate in chemistry from the University of Oxford in 1985, she joined Imperial College London as a research fellow. In 1993 she was appointed Professor of Medicinal Chemistry at Imperial College London, a position she held for over two decades.

Osei's laboratory identified the compound Artenusin-7, a derivative later licensed to the pharmaceutical company GlaxoSmithKline in 1999 for further clinical development. The licensing deal, reported at 12 million British pounds, funded expansion of her research group and led to the founding of a spin-out company, Osei Therapeutics Ltd, which she established in London in 2002 with venture partner Marcus Whitfield.

In 2011, Osei was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society, and in 2015 she received the Africa Prize for Engineering Innovation, awarded by the Royal Academy of Engineering in London for her contributions to affordable malaria treatment. She served as Chief Scientific Officer of Osei Therapeutics Ltd until her retirement from the post in 2020.

Osei is married to Dr. Kwame Boateng, a cardiologist at St Thomas' Hospital, and the couple have two children. She currently divides her time between London and Accra, where she mentors young scientists through the Kumasi Science Foundation, an organization she founded in 2018 to support STEM education across Ghana.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital reported promising Phase 2 results for CB-2201, an investigational chemical compound targeting relapsed acute myeloid leukemia, at the American Society of Hematology's spring symposium. The trial, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez, enrolled 142 adult patients across 11 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants received 200 milligrams of CB-2201 orally twice daily for 28-day cycles. According to the study, 61 percent of patients achieved complete remission, compared with 34 percent in the control arm receiving standard cytarabine therapy. Median overall survival reached 16.4 months, an improvement of nearly five months over historical benchmarks. Dr. Vasquez presented the findings on March 12, 2024, noting that Grade 3 neutropenia occurred in 22 percent of treated patients, a manageable rate consistent with earlier Phase 1 data. Novartis, which licensed CB-2201 from Cambridge-based biotech firm Aravive Therapeutics in 2021 for 340 million dollars, plans to launch a Phase 3 trial in early 2025 pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Dr. Vasquez stated, "These results represent a meaningful step forward for patients who have exhausted conventional options." Co-investigator Dr. Michael Chen of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute added that longer follow-up is needed to confirm durability of response. The research was funded in part by a 4.2 million dollar grant from the National Cancer Institute. Full results will be published in The New England Journal of Medicine later this year.

CEO Marisol Petrov, who has led Halden Motors since 2019, said the acquisition of VoltCore Systems will let the company build battery packs in-house rather than depend on outside suppliers. "This gives us control over our supply chain during a critical period," Petrov told reporters at a press conference Tuesday afternoon.

VoltCore Systems, founded in 2017 by engineer Dario Wexler, employs 340 people at its Austin, Texas facility and has developed a proprietary lithium-manganese cathode used in several prototype vehicles. Wexler will join Halden Motors as Chief Technology Officer starting December 1, 2024, according to a company statement.

The deal comes as Halden Motors competes with Renfield Auto Group and Tessaro Inc. in the crowded EV market. Analysts at Bramwell Capital noted the purchase price represents a 22 percent premium over VoltCore's last private valuation of $338 million.

Halden Motors shares rose 6 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $54.30. The company said it plans to fund the acquisition through a combination of cash reserves and a $200 million credit facility arranged by Chesterfield Bank.

Regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission is still pending, though Petrov expressed confidence the deal would clear review without major obstacles.

Boston, MA -- April 9, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolvaxinib, an oral chemical compound targeting fibrotic lung tissue, for patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. The study, led by Dr. Helena Marsh, enrolled 214 participants across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and March 2024. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of tolvaxinib daily showed a 31 percent reduction in disease progression compared to placebo, according to findings published in The Lancet Respiratory Medicine. Dr. Marsh, an associate professor of pulmonology, presented the data at the American Thoracic Society conference in San Diego on May 14, 2024. "These results represent a meaningful step forward for patients with limited treatment options," she told attendees. The trial was funded by Arden Biotherapeutics, a biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, which holds exclusive rights to tolvaxinib after licensing the compound from Kyoto Pharma Ltd. in 2021. Arden Biotherapeutics plans to begin a Phase 3 trial in early 2025, pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Approximately 5 percent of participants in the Phase 2 trial experienced mild gastrointestinal side effects, while no serious adverse events were reported. Dr. Raj Patel, chief medical officer at Arden Biotherapeutics, noted that the company has invested $42 million in the tolvaxinib program since 2021. Massachusetts General Hospital and Arden Biotherapeutics intend to expand the trial network to 30 sites for the next phase, including new locations in Germany and Japan.

DETROIT, Mich. — Ferrotech Industries, a mid-sized auto-parts supplier headquartered in Detroit, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in outstanding debt and a sharp drop in orders from General Motors. The filing was submitted to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan.

CEO Rajesh Patel told reporters at a press conference that the company plans to keep its three Michigan plants running during restructuring, but warned that 1,200 jobs could be at risk if a buyer is not found within 90 days. "We are exploring every option, including a possible sale to a strategic investor," Patel said.

Ferrotech, founded in 1987 by engineer Walter Simmons, employs roughly 4,500 workers across facilities in Detroit, Toledo, and Flint. Its largest customer, General Motors, accounted for nearly 60 percent of revenue last year, according to court documents.

Analysts at Moody's downgraded Ferrotech's credit rating on Wednesday, citing liquidity concerns. Rival supplier Dana Incorporated, based in Maumee, Ohio, said it does not expect the bankruptcy to disrupt its own supply chain.

Patel added that the company has held preliminary talks with private equity firm Cerberus Capital Management about a possible $200 million investment. A bankruptcy judge, the Honorable Linda Foss, is scheduled to hold the first hearing on March 14 in Detroit.

input: BOSTON, Massachusetts - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced on March 14, 2024 that a Phase 2 clinical trial of the experimental compound MGH-217 showed a 42 percent reduction in relapse rates among patients with treatment-resistant depression. The study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez, enrolled 168 participants across three sites in Boston, Chicago, and Denver between June 2022 and September 2023. Dr. Vasquez, an associate professor of psychiatry, presented the findings at the American Psychiatric Association meeting held in San Diego. MGH-217, a small-molecule modulator of the NMDA receptor, was developed in collaboration with Cambridge-based biotechnology firm Nova Therapeutics, which was founded in 2015 by entrepreneur Marcus Chen. Nova Therapeutics was acquired by pharmaceutical giant Pfizer for 1.3 billion dollars in November 2023, a deal that gave Pfizer full rights to MGH-217 and related compounds. Participants receiving MGH-217 twice daily for eight weeks reported significantly fewer side effects than those on the standard drug sertraline, according to the paper published in The New England Journal of Medicine. Dr. Vasquez noted that 12 patients withdrew from the trial due to mild nausea, while no serious adverse events were recorded. The research team plans to launch a larger Phase 3 trial in early 2025, pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Massachusetts General Hospital said additional funding of 45 million dollars from the National Institute of Mental Health will support the expanded study. Dr. Vasquez said the results offer new hope for the roughly 2.8 million Americans living with treatment-resistant depression.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT — PUBLIC NOTICE
Ottawa, Ontario, March 4, 2024

The Ministry of Transport today announced a $340 million investment to upgrade rail infrastructure along the Toronto-Montreal corridor. Minister Fatima Al-Rashid confirmed the funding at a press briefing held at Union Station, stating that Via Rail Canada will receive $210 million to replace aging track between Kingston and Belleville by December 2025. The remaining $130 million will be allocated to Canadian National Railway for signal modernization near Cornwall.

The announcement follows a review launched after a freight derailment near Prescott on January 17, 2024, which injured two workers and prompted an internal safety audit. Deputy Minister Robert Chen, who joined the Ministry in September 2022 after leaving Bombardier Inc., said the new funding responds directly to recommendations from the Transportation Safety Board.

Via Rail Canada CEO Mario Delacroix welcomed the announcement, noting that ridership on the corridor rose 14 percent last year. "This investment will cut travel time between Toronto and Montreal by nearly 40 minutes," Delacroix said during a joint appearance with Al-Rashid.

Construction is expected to begin on May 1, 2024, and will employ approximately 1,200 workers. The Ministry will publish quarterly progress reports starting in July 2024, with the first report due to Parliament by August 15, 2024.

DETROIT, Oct. 14 -- Faircrest Motors Inc. announced Tuesday it has acquired battery startup Voltane Energy for $740 million in a cash-and-stock deal, marking the automaker's largest acquisition since its founding in 1998. The agreement, disclosed at a press briefing in Detroit, Michigan, will bring Voltane's lithium-iron-phosphate battery technology under Faircrest's electric vehicle division.

Under the terms, Faircrest will pay $520 million in cash and issue $220 million in stock to Voltane's shareholders. The deal is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Faircrest Chief Executive Officer Renata Ibarra said the acquisition would help the company compete more directly with rival Solvane Motors, which has dominated the affordable EV segment.

"Voltane's chemistry gives us a two-year head start on cost reduction," Ibarra told reporters. Voltane Energy, founded in 2016 by engineer Marcus Deng, employs 310 people at its facility in Reno, Nevada. Deng will join Faircrest as Chief Technology Officer effective November 1, replacing outgoing CTO Priya Sethi, who announced her retirement last month.

Shares of Faircrest rose 6.3 percent to $88.14 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of Solvane Motors fell 2.1 percent. Analysts at Halloway Partners estimated the deal could add $1.2 billion in annual revenue by 2027. Faircrest is headquartered in Detroit and currently employs approximately 42,000 workers worldwide.

Pixel Watch 3, Google's latest wearable, went on sale on September 20, 2024, for $349.99 through the Google Store and Best Buy locations across the United States. I've worn the 41mm aluminum model daily since picking one up in Austin, Texas, and the improvements over the Pixel Watch 2 are noticeable. Google engineer Priya Raman, who works on the Wear OS team in Mountain View, California, told reporters at a briefing that the new LTPO OLED display can hit 2,000 nits, making it far more readable in direct sunlight. Battery life is rated at 24 hours, though with the always-on display enabled I averaged closer to 18 hours before needing the charger. The Loss of Pulse Detection feature, developed in partnership with the American Heart Association, worked reliably during a test hike near Zilker Park, though I hope I never need it for real. At $349.99 the base price undercuts the Apple Watch Series 10, a direct competitor from Apple Inc., by about $50. Fitbit, which Google acquired in 2021, continues to power much of the health-tracking software here, and the integration feels more seamless than on last year's model. My only complaints are the still-fiddly crown and a companion app that occasionally lags when syncing with a Pixel 9 phone. Minor gripes aside, this is the best Google smartwatch yet, and at this price it's genuinely competitive. Recommended for anyone already inside the Android ecosystem.

Portland-based Cascadia Cycleworks has released the Timberline GX2, a hardtail mountain bike built for riders tackling the singletrack trails of the Pacific Northwest. Priced at $2,199 and available now through the company's online store, the Timberline GX2 features a lightweight 6061 aluminum frame, a RockShox Judy Gold RL fork with 120mm of travel, and a Shimano Deore 12-speed drivetrain. Each frame is hand-welded at the company's Gresham, Oregon facility, where founder Marcus Aldridge started the brand back in 2014 after leaving his job as a mechanical engineer at Nike. The bike ships with Maxxis Minion DHF tires (29 x 2.4 inches) and Cascadia's own aluminum flat pedals. Customers who order before November 30, 2024 receive a free helmet from Bell, a $65 value. Cascadia Cycleworks currently sells through 42 independent bike shops across Washington, Oregon, and Idaho, and competes directly with Salsa Cycles and Kona Bikes in the regional trail-bike segment. The Timberline GX2 comes in three frame sizes (Small, Medium, Large) and two colorways: Douglas Fir Green and Basalt Gray. Weighing just 29.8 pounds, it's aimed at intermediate riders looking to upgrade from entry-level bikes without spending more than $2,500. Warranty coverage includes a lifetime guarantee on the frame and a 2-year guarantee on components. Reviews from Portland's Mountain Bike Collective have praised its climbing efficiency, though some riders noted the stock seat could be more comfortable on longer rides. Orders typically ship within 5 business days from the Gresham warehouse.

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY
Case No. ESX-L-004417-24

On March 11, 2024, Judge Patricia Holloway sentenced Marcus Devane, 41, of Newark, New Jersey, to 7 years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of wire fraud and embezzlement connected to his former role as Chief Financial Officer of Brightline Logistics Inc. Prosecutor Angela Reyes of the Essex County District Attorney's Office argued that Devane diverted $2.3 million from company accounts between January 2019 and October 2022, funneling the money into shell entities registered in Delaware.

The trial, held at the Essex County Courthouse in Newark, began on February 5, 2024, and lasted eleven days. Testimony from forensic accountant Dr. Helen Okafor detailed how Devane authorized fraudulent wire transfers to accounts controlled by his brother, Timothy Devane, who was charged separately last year and pleaded guilty to money laundering in December 2023.

Brightline Logistics Inc., headquartered in Jersey City, is a subsidiary of Ferro Transport Group, a national freight company. Chief Executive Officer Rosalind Chen issued a statement Tuesday saying the company had cooperated fully with investigators and had already recovered $900,000 through civil litigation. Judge Holloway also ordered Devane to pay restitution of $1.4 million to Brightline Logistics Inc. within five years of his release. Defense attorney Marcus Feldman said his client intends to appeal the verdict before the Appellate Division within 45 days.

Meridian Rail Systems, headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Delta Signal Technologies for $142 million in cash. The deal, finalized at Meridian's downtown Columbus office, adds Delta Signal's advanced rail-crossing sensors to Meridian's existing product line, including its flagship TrackGuard 4000 monitoring system.

Delta Signal Technologies, founded in 2009 by engineer Priya Nathan, employs 210 people at its facility in Akron, Ohio. Nathan will join Meridian as Chief Technology Officer effective March 1, 2024, according to Meridian CEO Robert Halvorsen.

"This acquisition strengthens our position against competitors like Consolidated Rail Instruments," Halvorsen said during a press briefing at Meridian's Columbus headquarters. "Priya and her team bring nearly fifteen years of specialized expertise that will accelerate our next generation of safety products."

Meridian expects the integration to be complete by the third quarter of 2024. The company projects the deal will generate an additional $30 million in annual revenue and expand its workforce by 12 percent. Meridian's board of directors approved the transaction unanimously last Thursday.

Delta Signal's 85,000-square-foot Akron plant will continue operating under the Meridian brand, retaining all current staff. Analysts at Braxton Financial Group called the acquisition "a shrewd move" that positions Meridian to compete for a $500 million federal rail-safety modernization contract expected to be awarded in 2025.

Meridian Rail Systems trades on the NYSE under the ticker symbol MRS and reported $1.1 billion in revenue last fiscal year.

Pixel Watch 3, Google's latest smartwatch, went on sale on September 10, 2024, priced at $349.99 for the 41mm Wi-Fi model. Reviewed here after three weeks of daily use in Austin, Texas, the device impressed with a brighter 2,000-nit display and a claimed 36-hour battery life, up from 24 hours on last year's model. Google, headquartered in Mountain View, California, positioned the watch as a direct competitor to the Apple Watch Series 10, produced by Apple Inc. In practice, the improved battery held up: after a 10-kilometer run and continuous heart-rate tracking, the watch still had 40 percent charge by evening. The Loss of Pulse Detection feature, developed with input from cardiologist Dr. Elena Ruiz of St. David's Medical Center, performed well in a simulated test, though it should never replace emergency care. Software felt polished thanks to Wear OS 5, but third-party app support still lags behind Apple's ecosystem. Google acquired Fitbit back in January 2021 for $2.1 billion, and that acquisition's fingerprints are visible throughout the health-tracking suite, from Sleep Score to Cardio Load. My main complaint is durability: the domed glass scratched after just one week of gym use, and Google has not yet responded to my request for comment. At $349.99, the Pixel Watch 3 is a strong upgrade for existing Android users, but it is not the giant leap the marketing suggests. Recommended for Pixel phone owners who skipped the 2022 original; everyone else can wait for Pixel Watch 4, expected in late 2025.

Mireille Fontaine (born 12 March 1958 in Lyon, France) is a French biochemist known for her pioneering work on enzyme engineering. She earned a doctorate in biochemistry from the University of Strasbourg in 1984 and joined the Institut Pasteur in Paris the following year as a research associate. In 1991 Fontaine left Institut Pasteur to become Director of Research at Rhone-Biotech, a small biotechnology firm headquartered in Lyon that specialized in industrial enzymes. Under her leadership the company developed Lipazix, a lipase-based catalyst used in detergent manufacturing, which generated licensing revenue of roughly 4.2 million francs by 1996.

In 1998, Rhone-Biotech was acquired by the multinational chemical company Solvex Group for an undisclosed sum, and Fontaine was appointed Vice President of Enzyme Research at Solvex, a position she held until 2009. During this period she filed eleven patents related to industrial biocatalysis. She married fellow chemist Bernard Coty in 1986, and the couple had one daughter, Isabelle Coty, born in 1990 in Lyon.

In 2003, Fontaine received the Pasteur Medal from the French Academy of Sciences in Paris for her contributions to biotechnology. She retired from Solvex Group in 2009 and now serves as an honorary professor at the University of Strasbourg. She currently resides in Lyon.

BOSTON, MA - November 12, 2023 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tepretinib-B, an experimental chemical compound targeting MET-driven non-small cell lung cancer. The study, led by Dr. Anita Chowdhury and presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology meeting in Chicago, enrolled 214 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and June 2023. Participants receiving tepretinib-B showed a 41 percent objective response rate compared with 19 percent in the control arm receiving standard chemotherapy. Median progression-free survival reached 11.3 months, a statistically significant improvement over 6.2 months in the control group. Dr. Chowdhury noted that the most common adverse event was peripheral edema, observed in 27 percent of treated patients, while no cases of severe hepatotoxicity were reported. The trial was funded by a $34 million grant from Meridian Oncology Therapeutics, a biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, which plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. Dr. Chowdhury, who joined Massachusetts General Hospital in 2015 as Director of Thoracic Oncology, said the findings represent a meaningful advance for patients with limited treatment options. Meridian Oncology Therapeutics' chief executive, Robert Feinstein, stated the company intends to initiate a Phase 3 trial in early 2024, expanding enrollment to sites in Japan and the United Kingdom. The full results were published on November 10, 2023, in the New England Journal of Medicine.

Fjallrune Outdoors, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, has released the Kaldera 45L Trekking Pack, a rugged backpack aimed at multi-day alpine hikers. Units are shipping from Fjallrune's distribution center in Denver starting September 9, 2024, with international orders reaching customers in Germany and Japan by early October. Ingrid Solberg (born 14 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cod population decline in the North Sea. She earned a doctorate in Marine Ecology from the University of Bergen in 1984 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø as a research fellow the same year. In 1991 Solberg was appointed Director of Fisheries Research at the Institute of Marine Research, a position she held for eleven years. Her 1996 study on overfishing, published in the journal Marine Biology Letters, was cited widely by policymakers and helped inform Norway's revised Fisheries Management Act of 1999. In 2003 she left the Institute to become a professor at the University of Oslo, where she taught until her retirement in 2020. Solberg received the Nansen Award from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo in 2005 for her contributions to marine conservation. She is married to Henrik Aas, a former diplomat, and the couple has two children, Marte and Oskar. Solberg's brother, Jon Solberg, is a well-known sculptor based in Stavanger. In 2011 she co-founded the nonprofit organization Ocean Futures Norway, headquartered in Oslo, which advocates for sustainable fishing quotas across Scandinavia. Now 66, she continues to serve on the advisory board of the organization and lives in Oslo with her husband.

MADRID, May 14 — Real Sociedad striker Mikel Oyarzabal scored twice as his side beat Villarreal 3-1 at the Estadio de la Cerámica on Sunday, boosting their hopes of qualifying for next season's UEFA Champions League. Oyarzabal opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a low finish from inside the box, then added a second just before halftime after a quick counterattack. Villarreal's Yeremy Pino pulled one back in the 58th minute, but midfielder Martin Zubimendi restored the two-goal cushion with a curling effort in the 76th minute. The win moved Real Sociedad to fourth place in La Liga with 62 points, three points ahead of Real Betis. Head coach Imanol Alguacil praised his team's discipline after the match, telling reporters at a press conference, "We fought for every ball today, and the players deserve this result." Villarreal manager Marcelino García Toral admitted his side struggled defensively, saying the team needed to fix its mistakes before facing Atlético Madrid next weekend. The match, attended by over 21,000 fans, was Oyarzabal's 14th goal of the season, moving him level with Vinícius Júnior in the race for the Pichichi Trophy. Real Sociedad will next host Sevilla on May 21 at the Reale Arena in San Sebastián, while Villarreal travel to the Wanda Metropolitano to face Atlético Madrid.

DETROIT, Mich. — Harrow Industrial Corp., a mid-sized auto-parts supplier headquartered in Detroit, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in outstanding debt and a sharp drop in orders from General Motors. The filing was submitted in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan by CEO Denise Ferrar, who took over the company in March 2022 after founder Walter Krum stepped down as chief executive.

Harrow, which employs roughly 2,100 workers across three plants in Michigan and Ohio, said it will continue operations during restructuring. Ferrar told reporters at a press conference in Detroit that the company plans to close its Toledo, Ohio facility by January 2025, affecting an estimated 480 employees.

The bankruptcy comes two months after Harrow lost a supply contract with Ford Motor Company, its second-largest customer, following quality complaints about a batch of brake components. Analysts at Moody's downgraded Harrow's credit rating to Caa1 last week, warning of limited liquidity.

General Motors spokesperson Alan Reyes said in a statement that GM is "monitoring the situation closely" but has no immediate plans to alter its sourcing agreements. Meanwhile, shares of Harrow's parent company, Vantage Holdings Group, fell 22 percent on the New York Stock Exchange Wednesday morning.

A hearing before Judge Patricia Nolan is scheduled for December 5 to review Harrow's reorganization plan. Union representatives from the United Auto Workers said they would seek assurances on pension protections during the proceedings.

input: The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday that the city of Rotterdam will receive €42 million in federal funding to modernize its aging tram network. Minister Ellen de Vries stated that the grant, approved under the National Mobility Act, will finance the purchase of 30 new low-floor trams from Alstom, a French manufacturer headquartered in Saint-Ouen. The first deliveries are expected by March 2026, with full deployment across Rotterdam's transit system completed by late 2027. Rotterdam's mayor, Ahmed Aboutaleb, welcomed the announcement, noting that the city's public transport authority, RET, has struggled with breakdowns on its 1980s-era fleet. "This investment will cut delays by an estimated 25 percent and reduce carbon emissions by 4,000 tonnes annually," de Vries said during a press conference in The Hague. The funding follows a similar €18 million package granted to the city of Utrecht last year for bus electrification. Officials from RET and Alstom are scheduled to meet in Rotterdam on November 14 to finalize technical specifications. The Ministry also confirmed that 120 new jobs will be created at Alstom's assembly facility in Petite-Forêt as a result of the order. Opposition lawmaker Frans Timmermans criticized the timeline as too slow, arguing that commuters need relief before 2026, not after it.

Elena Vasquez (born March 14, 1962, in Montevideo, Uruguay) is a Uruguayan-American biochemist known for her contributions to enzyme engineering. After earning a doctorate from the University of Buenos Aires in 1988, she moved to the United States and joined Stanford University as a postdoctoral researcher in 1990. In 1996, Vasquez co-founded Helix Biotherapeutics in Palo Alto, California, alongside chemist Marcus Reinholt, with the goal of developing engineered enzymes for industrial applications. She served as Chief Scientific Officer of Helix Biotherapeutics until 2004, when she left to become a professor of biochemistry at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

Vasquez's research on thermostable enzymes led to the development of a widely used industrial catalyst, ThermoZyme-7, which was later licensed to Novozymes A/S in a deal worth $45 million in 2011. In 2015, she was elected to the National Academy of Sciences. Three years later, in 2018, she received the Wolf Prize in Chemistry, awarded by the Wolf Foundation in Herzliya, Israel, for her pioneering work on enzyme stability under extreme conditions.

Vasquez married fellow scientist David Chen in 1994; the couple has two children. She currently resides in Cambridge, Massachusetts, where she continues to teach and lead a research laboratory at MIT. In 2022, Helix Biotherapeutics was acquired by Genentech for an undisclosed sum, a development Vasquez described as "a fitting culmination of decades of work."

Pixel Tab Review: Google's First Real Tablet Bet Since 2018

Mountain View, CA -- On October 9, 2025, Google officially launched the Pixel Tab 2, its most serious tablet effort since abandoning the category after the Pixel Slate. I've spent three weeks with the $499 base model, and the results are mixed but promising.

The Pixel Tab 2 runs Android 15 and is powered by Google's own Tensor G4 chip, the same silicon found in the Pixel 9 phone. Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google, called it "a tablet built for the Gemini era" during the launch event at the Shoreline Amphitheatre. The 11-inch OLED display is genuinely excellent, and battery life comfortably hits 10 hours of mixed use.

Where the device stumbles is software. Third-party app support remains thin compared to Apple's iPadOS ecosystem, and I noticed occasional stutter when running Gemini Nano's on-device summarization feature. For $499, it competes directly against the Apple iPad (10th generation) and Samsung's Galaxy Tab S10, both of which offer more mature app catalogs.

Notably, Google acquired Multitasking UI startup Flexible Software Inc. in March 2025 for an undisclosed sum, and the influence is visible in the new split-screen multitasking, which finally feels desktop-grade. Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo estimates Google will ship 2.5 million units by the end of Q1 2026, a modest number next to Apple's iPad sales but a real signal of intent.

At $499, the Pixel Tab 2 is a solid, if imperfect, first step back into tablets. If Google commits to at least two more years of software updates, this could be the start of a legitimate third ecosystem.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Aldergrove United clinched a dramatic 3-2 victory over Bristol Harriers at Meadowbrook Stadium on Saturday, keeping their promotion push alive in the Championship. Striker Daniel Okafor scored twice, including a 89th-minute winner, to lift Aldergrove into third place with 21 points from 10 matches.

The hosts fell behind early when Bristol Harriers midfielder Callum Reece converted a penalty in the 12th minute. Okafor equalized just before halftime, heading in a cross from winger Marcus Ilic. Bristol Harriers regained the lead in the 63rd minute through striker Femi Adeyemi, but Okafor struck twice in the final quarter-hour to complete his brace and seal the comeback.

Aldergrove United manager Paolo Ferrante praised his team's resilience after the match, telling reporters, "We never stopped believing, even at 2-1 down." Ferrante, who took charge of the club in July 2022, has now guided Aldergrove to five wins in their last seven league games.

The victory pushes Aldergrove United four points clear of relegation-threatened Dunmore Athletic, who lost 1-0 to Kelsford Town at Ironbridge Park on the same afternoon. Aldergrove United will next travel to Portsmouth on October 21 to face league leaders Solent Rovers, a fixture that could prove pivotal in the race for automatic promotion.

Approximately 14,200 spectators attended Saturday's match at Meadowbrook Stadium, one of the highest home crowds Aldergrove United has recorded this season.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. RG24-118832 - People of the State of California v. Marcus T. Delaney

On March 14, 2024, defendant Marcus T. Delaney, 41, appeared before Judge Renata Kowalski for a sentencing hearing following his conviction on charges of embezzlement and wire fraud connected to his former position as Chief Financial Officer of Larkspur Textiles Inc., a Oakland-based apparel manufacturer. Prosecutor Diane Ochoa of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Delaney diverted $2.3 million from company accounts between January 2019 and September 2022, funneling the funds through shell entities to purchase a yacht and a residence in Sausalito.

Delaney was arrested on November 3, 2022, by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation at Oakland International Airport as he attempted to board a flight to Lisbon, Portugal. He was indicted the following month on six counts, including embezzlement.

Judge Kowalski sentenced Delaney to seven years in state prison and ordered restitution of $2.3 million to Larkspur Textiles Inc. Defense attorney Howard Feinstein stated his client intends to appeal the ruling. Larkspur Textiles Inc., founded in 2005 by Priya Anand, employs roughly 340 workers and reported $58 million in annual revenue last year. Company spokesperson Lena Marsh confirmed the firm has since installed new internal auditing controls to prevent similar losses.

Denver-based Halcyon Foods Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Boulder Creamery LLC, a regional dairy producer, for $42 million in cash. The deal, unveiled at a press briefing in Denver, Colorado, is expected to close by November 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval. Halcyon Foods CEO Marisol Fenwick said the acquisition would expand the company's presence in the natural foods segment across the Rocky Mountain region. "Boulder Creamery has built a loyal customer base over its 28 years in business, and we intend to preserve that legacy," Fenwick told reporters. Boulder Creamery founder Tomas Reyes, who started the company in 1996, will step down as president effective December 1, 2024, but will remain as a consultant through 2025. Analysts at Kestrel Capital Partners estimate the deal will boost Halcyon's annual revenue by roughly 12 percent, pushing it past $380 million for fiscal year 2025. Shares of Halcyon Foods, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker HALC, rose 6.3 percent to $54.10 following the announcement. Boulder Creamery, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, employs about 310 workers and supplies dairy products to grocery chains including Front Range Market and Mesa Valley Foods. Halcyon Foods plans to retain all Boulder Creamery staff and keep its production facility on Pearl Street operating under the existing brand name.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tirbanamab, an investigational monoclonal antibody developed by Cascade Therapeutics, for patients with relapsed multiple myeloma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez, enrolled 142 patients across seven sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants received 4 milligrams per kilogram of tirbanamab intravenously every three weeks for up to twelve cycles. According to findings published in The Lancet Oncology, 61 percent of patients achieved a partial or complete response, compared with 34 percent in the control arm receiving standard bortezomib therapy. Median progression-free survival reached 18.4 months in the treatment group versus 9.7 months in controls. The most common adverse events were neutropenia, reported in 27 percent of patients, and mild infusion-related reactions. Dr. Vasquez presented the data at the American Society of Hematology meeting in San Diego on December 9, 2023. Cascade Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, stated that it plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. The company was founded in 2016 by biochemistRaj Patel, who now serves as Chief Scientific Officer. Analysts at Sanford Bernstein estimate peak annual sales of tirbanamab could reach 800 million dollars if approved, positioning it as a direct competitor to Janssen Pharmaceuticals' daratumumab. Additional trial sites included Toronto General Hospital and the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. Full results are expected to be submitted to the FDA alongside a companion diagnostic test currently under development.

MANCHESTER, England -- October 14, 2024 -- Manchester City midfielder Rodrigo Alvarez scored twice as City defeated Aston Villa 3-1 at Etihad Stadium on Saturday, extending their unbeaten Premier League run to nine matches. Manager Pep Guardiola praised the 26-year-old Spaniard after the match, calling it "one of his sharpest performances this season." Alvarez opened the scoring in the 18th minute with a low strike from outside the box, then added a second in the 54th minute after a quick counterattack led by winger Jeremy Doku. Aston Villa's Ollie Watkins pulled one back in the 63rd minute, but substitute Erling Haaland sealed the win with a header in the 81st minute, his 12th goal of the season. Villa manager Unai Emery admitted his side struggled defensively, saying, "We gave them too much space in transition." The victory moved Manchester City to second place in the table, three points behind leaders Liverpool. Roughly 53,000 spectators attended the match at Etihad Stadium. City will next travel to London on October 21, 2024, to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, while Aston Villa will host Brighton at Villa Park the same weekend. Guardiola confirmed that defender Kyle Walker, who missed Saturday's game with a minor hamstring injury, is expected to return for the Chelsea fixture.

Pixelbook Labs, a Seattle-based startup founded in 2019 by former Microsoft engineer Dana Whitfield, launched its second-generation e-reader, the InkSlate 2, on March 4, 2024. Priced at $229, the InkSlate 2 features a 10.3-inch E Ink Carta 1200 display and runs a lightweight version of Linux. I have spent three weeks testing the device in Portland, Oregon, and the results are largely positive.

Battery life is the standout feature: Pixelbook Labs claims six weeks on a single charge, and in my usage, mostly reading for two hours daily, I got close to five weeks before needing to recharge. The device weighs 190 grams, noticeably lighter than Amazon's Kindle Oasis, its closest competitor.

Software, however, is where the InkSlate 2 stumbles. The note-taking app crashed twice during my review period, and syncing with Dropbox occasionally failed without explanation. Dana Whitfield acknowledged the issues in an email on March 18, 2024, stating that a firmware update, version 1.3, would arrive by April 2024 to address stability concerns.

At $229, the InkSlate 2 undercuts the $249 Kobo Libra Colour and the $269 Kindle Oasis, making it an appealing budget option despite its rough software edges. For readers who prioritize battery life and price over polish, this is a solid choice. Just don't expect a flawless experience on day one.

SUPERIOR COURT OF SANTA CLARA COUNTY, CALIFORNIA — On October 14, 2024, Judge Rosalind Chen sentenced Marcus Delgado, 41, to 7 years in state prison after a jury convicted him of grand theft and securities fraud in connection with the collapse of his investment firm, Pinnacle Capital Advisors, headquartered in San Jose. Prosecutor Elena Vasquez of the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office argued that Delgado defrauded at least 62 investors of a combined $3.4 million between 2019 and 2022 by promising guaranteed returns on a cryptocurrency fund that never existed. The trial, held at the Hall of Justice in San Jose, began on September 3, 2024, and included testimony from former employee Priya Nathan, who told jurors she raised concerns internally as early as March 2021. Defense attorney Gordon Blaisdell asked for leniency, citing Delgado's lack of prior convictions, but Judge Chen rejected the request, calling the scheme "a calculated betrayal of trust." Delgado was arrested by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation on June 8, 2023, at his residence in Los Gatos, and has been held at the Elmwood Correctional Facility since his bail was revoked in January 2024. The court also ordered Delgado to pay $3.4 million in restitution to victims, payable within 90 days. Pinnacle Capital Advisors, founded by Delgado in 2015, filed for bankruptcy in Santa Clara County in November 2022. Vasquez said her office is reviewing whether additional charges will be filed against former Pinnacle executive Todd Ferraro.

Everton Outdoors, a gear company headquartered in Bend, Oregon, has launched the Cascade Ridge 45L Hiking Backpack, priced at $189.99 and available starting September 12, 2024. Designed by lead engineer Priya Nandakumar, the backpack features a ripstop nylon shell, an aluminum internal frame, and a 45-liter main compartment suited for multi-day treks. Everton Outdoors was founded in 2015 by Marcus Feld, a former product designer at Blackthorn Gear, and the company now employs 62 people across its Bend headquarters and a small distribution center in Reno, Nevada. The Cascade Ridge 45L has already drawn attention from retailers; REI confirmed on August 3, 2024 that it will stock the backpack in 140 stores nationwide beginning this fall. In a statement, Everton Outdoors CEO Marcus Feld said the pack was built to compete directly with Osprey's Atmos AG line, calling it "the most durable pack we've ever produced." Each unit ships new, includes a lifetime warranty, and is covered under U.S. Patent Law for its patented frame-suspension system. Customers who order before October 1, 2024 receive a free 2-liter hydration bladder valued at $24.99. The backpack is available in three colorways: Slate Gray, Forest Green, and Rust Orange, and weighs approximately 3.2 pounds. Early reviewers on the outdoor forum TrailSpace have praised its ventilation and adjustable torso length, awarding it an average rating of 4.7 out of 5 stars.

Boston, MA -- November 12, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolerozumab, an investigational monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Verdant Therapeutics, for treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. The randomized, double-blind study enrolled 214 adult patients across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2022 and July 2023. Dr. Elena Marsh, the trial's principal investigator and a dermatologist at Massachusetts General Hospital, presented findings at the American Academy of Dermatology's regional meeting held in Chicago on November 10, 2023. According to the data, 68 percent of patients receiving a 200 milligram dose of tolerozumab achieved at least 90 percent skin clearance by week 16, compared with 12 percent in the placebo group. The most common adverse events were mild nasopharyngitis and injection-site erythema, reported in 9 percent and 7 percent of participants, respectively. No serious cardiovascular events were observed. Verdant Therapeutics' chief executive, Raj Patel, stated that the company plans to initiate a Phase 3 program in early 2024 pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The study was funded in part by a $4.2 million grant from the National Institutes of Health and was published on November 12, 2023 in the Journal of Clinical Dermatology. Analysts at Fenwick Capital noted that if approved, tolerozumab could compete directly with Novartis's secukinumab in a psoriasis treatment market valued at over $9 billion annually.

Fjallnord Gear, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, has launched the Kestrel 3.2 Ultralight Tent, a two-person backpacking shelter weighing just 1.4 kilograms. Priced at $349.00, the Kestrel 3.2 is currently available in refurbished condition through the company's outlet program, with each unit inspected and re-sealed at Fjallnord's Longmont facility before resale. The tent features a 20-denier ripstop nylon fly treated with a silicone-polyurethane coating rated for 4,000mm of hydrostatic pressure, plus two vestibules and DAC Featherlite NFA poles sourced from supplier Dongguan Aluminum Industries. Fjallnord Gear was founded in 2011 by outdoor guide Marcus Reiner, who still serves as the company's Head of Product Design. The original Kestrel line debuted in 2013 and has since sold more than 80,000 units worldwide. This refurbished batch, listed on September 18, 2024, comes with a 1-year limited warranty and free returns within 30 days. Customer Elena Vasquez, who purchased the tent for a trip through Patagonia last spring, called it "the lightest shelter I've used in a decade of thru-hiking." Each order ships from the Longmont warehouse via FedEx Ground within two business days. Fjallnord Gear competes directly with Colorado-based rival Alpine Fortress Outdoors in the ultralight tent segment. Stock is limited to 640 units for this refurbished release.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF SANTA CLARA

Case No. 24-CV-118837

Judge Nakamura sentenced Ostrowski to four years in state prison and ordered restitution of $612,000 to Fenwick Instruments Inc. Defense attorney Marcus Whitfield argued for leniency, citing his client's cooperation, but the court noted the scheme's duration as an aggravating factor.

CHICAGO, September 9, 2024 -- Meridian Foods Corporation announced today that it has acquired Prairie Grain Snacks LLC, a Des Moines-based maker of organic crackers, for $84 million in cash. The transaction closed on September 6, 2024, following approval from Meridian's board of directors.

Under the terms of the deal, Prairie Grain Snacks will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Foods, retaining its 210 employees at the company's manufacturing facility in Des Moines, Iowa. input: BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tregorafenib, an oral kinase inhibitor developed by Cascadia Therapeutics, in patients with advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The trial, conducted at 12 sites across the United States and Germany between June 2021 and September 2023, enrolled 214 patients with a median age of 61. Dr. Elena Vasquez, principal investigator and Professor of Oncology at Harvard Medical School, presented findings at the American Society of Clinical Oncology meeting in Chicago on March 13, 2024. Patients receiving tregorafenib in combination with gemcitabine showed a median progression-free survival of 7.8 months, compared to 4.2 months in the placebo-plus-gemcitabine arm, representing a 46 percent reduction in risk of progression. Overall survival at 18 months was 38 percent in the treatment group versus 21 percent in controls. The most common grade 3 adverse events were neutropenia, reported in 22 percent of patients, and hypertension, reported in 15 percent. Cascadia Therapeutics, headquartered in San Diego, California, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. The study was funded by a $14 million grant from the National Cancer Institute and co-sponsored by Cascadia Therapeutics. Dr. Vasquez noted that pancreatic adenocarcinoma remains one of the deadliest malignancies, with a five-year survival rate below 12 percent. Co-author Dr. Marcus Lindqvist of Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin emphasized that the German cohort showed consistent benefit, supporting regulatory filings in the European Union as well. Full results will be published in The New England Journal of Medicine in April 2024.

input: BOSTON, MA -- November 12, 2023 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tarlatamab-based combination therapy for patients with relapsed small cell lung cancer. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti and presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology meeting, enrolled 142 patients across 9 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and July 2023. Participants received the investigational compound alongside standard carboplatin chemotherapy every 21 days for up to 6 cycles. According to the report published in The New England Journal of Medicine, the objective response rate reached 38 percent, compared to 21 percent in the control arm receiving carboplatin alone. Median progression-free survival extended to 7.4 months, an improvement of nearly 3 months over historical benchmarks. Dr. Marchetti noted that grade 3 or higher adverse events, primarily neutropenia and fatigue, occurred in 29 percent of treated patients, a rate the team considers manageable. The trial was funded by a $14.5 million grant from the National Cancer Institute and co-sponsored by Amgen Inc., which manufactures tarlatamab under the brand name Imdelltra. Dr. Marchetti's team plans to launch a larger Phase 3 trial in early 2024, pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Co-author Dr. Rajiv Nair of Charite Berlin emphasized that further validation in Asian populations is needed. The findings were also discussed during a press briefing in Chicago on October 30, 2023, where oncologists praised the results as a meaningful advance for a historically difficult-to-treat disease.

Boyd, who received a reduced sentence of eighteen months for cooperating with prosecutors, was released from the Fulton County Jail in June 2024.

The case, State of Georgia v. Marcus Whitfield, drew attention after surveillance footage aired on WSB-TV, prompting the Atlanta Police Department to increase patrols near downtown banking facilities. Whitfield's attorney stated he plans to appeal the sentence to the Georgia Court of Appeals.

Marguerite Okonjo-Delacroix (born 14 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-French metallurgical engineer and business executive best known for founding Solerion Alloys SA in Lyon, France, in 1991. After earning a doctorate in materials science from the Ecole des Mines de Saint-Etienne in 1984, she joined Compagnie Rhodanienne d'Aciers as a research engineer, where she developed corrosion-resistant titanium alloys used in aerospace fasteners. In 1991 she left the company to establish Solerion Alloys SA, headquartered in Lyon, with initial backing of 2.3 million francs from a consortium of regional investors. Under her leadership as Chief Executive Officer, Solerion Alloys grew into a supplier for Airbus and Dassault Aviation, and by 2005 the firm employed 640 people across three plants in France and Germany. In September 2008, Solerion Alloys was acquired by the American conglomerate Harrington Materials Group for 410 million euros, after which Okonjo-Delacroix stepped down as CEO on 30 November 2008. She subsequently served as a board member of the French Academy of Technologies from 2010 until 2019. In 2016, she received the Legion of Honour from President Francois Hollande in a ceremony at the Elysee Palace in Paris, recognizing her contributions to French industrial innovation. Okonjo-Delacroix married physicist Henri Delacroix in 1986; the couple has two children. She currently resides in Lyon and lectures occasionally at INSA Lyon.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday, March 11, 2025, that the city of Rotterdam will receive 45 million euros to upgrade the Maasvlakte port terminal over the next three years. Minister Elke Van Doren stated at a press conference in The Hague that the funding, allocated under the National Infrastructure Fund, will finance the construction of two new electric cargo cranes and a rail extension connecting the terminal to the Betuweroute freight line. Port operator Havenbedrijf Rotterdam, headquartered in Rotterdam, will manage the project in partnership with engineering firm Boskalis. According to Van Doren, the upgrade is expected to increase annual container throughput by 12 percent and create approximately 300 jobs by 2027. Opposition lawmaker Bram Hoekstra criticized the timeline as too slow, arguing that competing ports in Antwerp and Hamburg are already expanding faster. The Ministry responded that a second funding tranche of 20 million euros will be considered in 2026 pending a progress review. Construction is scheduled to begin on June 1, 2025, with the first phase completed by December 2026. Prairie Silo Logistics, based in Omaha, Nebraska, operates 47 grain elevators across Iowa, Nebraska, and Kansas, and reported revenue of $612 million last year.

Prairie Silo Logistics CEO Rebecca Ostrowski will join Archer Grain Partners' board of directors following the transaction, according to the companies. Ostrowski founded Prairie Silo Logistics in 2009 after leaving Cargill, where she worked as a regional operations manager.

Analysts at Morningstar noted that the merger could pressure competitor Bunge Limited, which has struggled to expand its own Midwest storage capacity. Shares of Archer Grain Partners rose 4.3% to $61.20 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Prairie Silo Logistics stock jumped 19% to $27.90.

The transaction is expected to generate $45 million in annual cost savings by 2026, according to a joint statement from both companies.
