DETROIT, Mich. — Vantage Motors Corporation announced Tuesday that it has acquired Bright Circuit Systems, a battery-technology startup based in Ann Arbor, for $412 million, as the automaker races to expand its electric-vehicle lineup. The deal was disclosed at a press conference at Vantage's headquarters on Woodward Avenue, where Chief Executive Officer Elena Marsh confirmed the acquisition alongside Bright Circuit founder Dr. Raymond Okafor. "This acquisition strengthens our supply chain and accelerates production of our next-generation battery packs," Marsh said. Bright Circuit Systems, founded in 2016 by Okafor, employs 210 engineers and holds 38 patents related to solid-state battery cells. Under the agreement, Okafor will join Vantage Motors as Chief Technology Officer starting November 1, 2024, reporting directly to Marsh. The transaction, expected to close by January 15, 2025, still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimate the deal could reduce Vantage's battery costs by 18 percent within three years. Shares of Vantage Motors rose 6.4 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $87.32. Vantage, headquartered in Detroit since its founding in 1998 by industrialist Walter Kessler, has struggled to compete with Tesla and BYD in the EV market. Kessler's granddaughter, current board chair Susan Kessler, called the acquisition "a pivotal step toward energy independence." Industry group the Alliance for Automotive Innovation praised the move, noting it could create up to 300 new manufacturing jobs in Michigan by 2026.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Finally Gets the Battery Right

By Trevor Adeyemi, October 14, 2024

After three years of disappointing battery life, Google's Pixel Watch 3, released on September 20, 2024, is a genuine step forward. I tested the 45mm LTE model, priced at $429.99, over two weeks in Austin, Texas, and came away impressed.

The watch is manufactured by Google LLC, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc., and assembled in Taiwan. Battery life now comfortably reaches 36 hours with the always-on display enabled, up from roughly 24 hours on the Pixel Watch 2. The new Actua 360 display is 10% brighter, and the improved Cardiac Coach feature offers useful VO2 max estimates for runners.

Google's hardware chief, Rick Osterloh, announced the device on stage at the Made by Google event in Mountain View, California, alongside the Pixel 9 Pro Fold. During the presentation, Osterloh confirmed that the Pixel Watch line has now sold over 8 million units worldwide since its 2022 debut.

Competition remains fierce. The Pixel Watch 3 goes up against the Apple Watch Series 10 and Samsung's Galaxy Watch 7, both of which offer similarly strong fitness tracking. Samsung Electronics, headquartered in Suwon, South Korea, still leads in raw sales volume across Asia.

Minor gripes: the charging puck remains proprietary, and software updates are promised only through October 2027. Still, at $429.99, this is the most complete Pixel Watch yet, and I recommend it to anyone already inside Google's ecosystem.

Rating: 4 out of 5 stars.

Denver-based Ridgeline Foods Corp. announced on Tuesday, June 11, 2024, that it has acquired Boulder Creamery LLC, a specialty dairy producer, for $84 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at Ridgeline's headquarters in Denver, Colorado, is expected to close by August 1, 2024, pending regulatory approval. Ridgeline CEO Marcus Whitfield said the acquisition will expand the company's presence in the premium yogurt segment across the western United States. "Boulder Creamery has built a loyal customer base over the past two decades, and we intend to keep its founder, Elena Reyes, on board as Chief Innovation Officer," Whitfield told reporters during a briefing at the Denver Marriott. Reyes founded Boulder Creamery in 2003 in Boulder, Colorado, growing it from a single farmers-market stall into a regional brand sold in over 1,200 stores. Ridgeline shares rose 4.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $57.90. Analysts at Fenwick Capital Partners, including senior analyst Priya Nandakumar, said the purchase price represents roughly 12 times Boulder Creamery's projected 2024 earnings. Rival dairy company Highland Dairy Group, based in Chicago, Illinois, called the deal "an aggressive but sensible move" for Ridgeline. The transaction, Ridgeline's third acquisition in five years, comes as consumer demand for high-protein dairy products continues to climb nationwide, according to a report from the U.S. Department of Agriculture released last month.

DENVER, October 14 — Frontier Grain Corp, the Colorado-based agricultural processor, announced Tuesday it has acquired Millbrook Feed & Supply, a privately held livestock feed producer based in Amarillo, Texas, for $142 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by December 1, will make Frontier Grain the third-largest feed supplier in the American Southwest, according to chief executive officer Rebecca Tanaka.

"This acquisition strengthens our supply chain from Colorado down through the Texas Panhandle," Tanaka said during a press call from Frontier Grain's headquarters in Denver. Millbrook Feed & Supply, founded in 1978 by rancher Walter Combs, employs roughly 310 workers across four facilities and generated $89 million in revenue last year.

Analysts at Prairie Capital Partners said the purchase price represents a 22 percent premium over Millbrook's estimated book value. Shares of Frontier Grain rose 6.4 percent to $58.10 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume climbed to 1.2 million shares, well above the daily average.

As part of the transaction, Millbrook's longtime president, Diane Alvarez, will step down on November 30 and be succeeded by Frontier Grain executive Marcus Whitfield, who will assume the title of regional president effective December 1. Frontier Grain also confirmed it will retain Millbrook's manufacturing plant in Amarillo and its distribution center in Lubbock, Texas.

The acquisition still requires clearance from the Federal Trade Commission, which Tanaka said she expects within 45 days.

Denver-based Frontier Grain Corp. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Midwest Milling LLC, a privately held flour producer based in Topeka, Kansas, for $214 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by December 15, will make Frontier Grain the third-largest flour miller in the United States, according to chief executive officer Rebecca Sandoval. Speaking at a press briefing at Frontier Grain's headquarters, Sandoval said the acquisition would expand the company's milling capacity by 38 percent and add roughly 420 employees across four states. Midwest Milling founder Harold Tice, who started the company in 1987, will stay on as a senior advisor for one year under the terms of the agreement. Shares of Frontier Grain rose 6.2 percent to $47.83 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume climbed to 1.9 million shares, more than triple the daily average. Analyst Priya Chandrasekaran of Merrow Capital Partners called the purchase price fair, noting that Midwest Milling generated $89 million in revenue last year. The transaction is subject to approval from the Federal Trade Commission, and Frontier Grain expects to fund the deal through a combination of $150 million in cash reserves and a new credit facility arranged by Lakeshore National Bank. Sandoval added that no plant closures are planned, though the company will consolidate administrative offices in Topeka by March 2025.

The Ohio Department of Transportation announced on May 14, 2024 that it will allocate $42 million to repair the Interstate 70 bridge spanning the Scioto River near Columbus. Director Pamela Boyd said the project, awarded to contractor Kokosing Industrial, will begin construction on June 3, 2024 and is expected to conclude within eighteen months. "This investment will prevent further deterioration and protect the roughly 58,000 vehicles that cross this span daily," Boyd said during a press conference held at the Ohio Statehouse in Columbus. The funding was approved after the Federal Highway Administration completed an inspection in March 2024 that identified corrosion in three support beams. State Senator Marcus Lee, who represents Franklin County, praised the decision, noting that the bridge has not undergone major repairs since 1998. The Ohio Department of Transportation will coordinate with the City of Columbus to manage traffic detours along Route 315 during construction. Officials estimate the closure will affect commuters traveling between Franklinton and Downtown Columbus. Kokosing Industrial, headquartered in Fredericktown, Ohio, previously completed similar rehabilitation work on the Brent Spence Bridge in Cincinnati in 2019. The department noted that an additional $6 million contingency fund has been set aside in case unexpected structural issues arise during demolition of the old deck. Residents can submit questions to the department's hotline or attend a public forum scheduled for May 28, 2024 at the Franklin County Government Center.

Pixelbook Forge X2 Review: A Solid Refresh, Not a Revolution

On March 14, 2024, Google quietly launched the Pixelbook Forge X2 at a small press event in Mountain View, California, priced at $999 for the base configuration. I have spent three weeks with the review unit, and the results are mixed but largely positive.

The Forge X2 is built around a custom Tensor C2 chip designed with MediaTek, paired with 16GB of RAM and a 13.5-inch OLED display. Battery life clocked in at roughly 11 hours of continuous video playback, a modest improvement over the previous Pixelbook Go. The chassis, machined from a single block of aluminum in Google's Taiwan facility, feels noticeably sturdier than the plastic-heavy competitor from Lenovo, the ThinkPad Chromebook Plus.

Software is where Google continues to differentiate itself. ChromeOS 124 ships with a redesigned launcher and tighter integration with Gemini, Google's AI assistant, which now handles voice commands in English, Spanish, and Japanese. During my testing in San Francisco, the assistant correctly transcribed meeting notes with only minor errors.

On pricing, the $999 entry model undercuts Apple's MacBook Air by roughly $100, and Google's retail partner Best Buy confirmed the device will be available nationwide starting April 2, 2024.

Critics, including tech journalist Maria Chen of The Verge, have praised the display but noted the trackpad feels a generation behind Apple's offerings. Overall, the Pixelbook Forge X2 earns a cautious recommendation for anyone already inside Google's ecosystem.

Rating: 4 out of 5 stars.

Dell Technologies launched the XPS 14 laptop on March 5, 2024, positioning it against Apple's MacBook Pro in the premium ultrabook segment. Priced at $1,699, the XPS 14 features a 14.5-inch OLED display, an Intel Core Ultra 7 processor, and 32GB of RAM. I tested the unit for three weeks in Austin, Texas, and came away impressed by its battery life, which lasted nearly 11 hours of continuous video playback.

David Kim, a senior product manager at Dell, told reporters at a briefing in New York that the XPS 14 was designed to compete directly with the MacBook Pro on both performance and portability. "We wanted a machine that professionals could carry into any meeting," Kim said. The laptop's aluminum chassis weighs just 1.55 kilograms, making it lighter than most rivals in its class.

On the software side, the XPS 14 ships with Windows 11 and Dell's own optimization suite. Benchmark tests showed the machine scoring 12% faster than last year's XPS 13 Plus in multi-core workloads, though thermal throttling became noticeable after 45 minutes of sustained rendering tasks.

Dell also announced that the XPS 14 will be manufactured partly in Penang, Malaysia, with final assembly handled at a facility in Round Rock, Texas. Analysts at Gartner estimate Dell could sell over 500,000 units globally by the end of 2024.

Overall, the XPS 14 is a strong, if incremental, upgrade. At $1,699, it isn't cheap, but the build quality and display justify the price for professionals who need a Windows alternative to Apple's ecosystem.

Pixel Tab 3, Shipped Late, Impresses Once Awake

Mountain View, California -- October 14, 2024

Google officially launched the Pixel Tab 3 on October 8, 2024, at a small press event in Mountain View, and after six days of testing I finally have a verdict: it is the best Android tablet the company has produced, even if the rollout was messier than expected. Sundar Pichai, Google's chief executive officer, called the device "a genuine alternative to the iPad" during the announcement, a claim that mostly holds up.

The Pixel Tab 3 starts at $499 for the 128GB Wi-Fi model, with a $649 version adding 5G connectivity supplied by T-Mobile US. Under the hood sits Google's own Tensor G4 chip, the same silicon found in the Pixel 9 phone, paired with 12GB of RAM. In benchmark testing the tablet outperformed Samsung's Galaxy Tab S9 by roughly 18 percent in multi-core tasks, a genuinely surprising result for a first-generation refresh.

The rough patch came at launch: an estimated 40,000 pre-orders placed through the Google Store in the United States were delayed by nearly two weeks after a supplier in Vietnam, Foxconn, reported a shortage of OLED panels. Rick Osterloh, senior vice president of devices at Google, apologized publicly on October 10, 2024, promising refunds of $25 in Google Play credit to affected customers.

Despite the stumble, the hardware itself is excellent, and the included Pixel Tab Keyboard accessory, sold separately for $129, turns the device into a legitimate laptop substitute. For anyone loyal to the Android ecosystem, this is an easy recommendation once stock stabilizes.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. HG-24-091337

On March 4, 2024, the Superior Court of Alameda County sentenced Marcus Feldman, 41, to 36 months in state prison after a jury found him guilty of grand theft and securities fraud in connection with his former role as Chief Financial Officer of Brightline Capital Partners, a boutique investment firm headquartered in Oakland, California. Judge Patricia Nakamura presided over the six-day trial, during which prosecutor Elena Suárez of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Feldman diverted $2.3 million from client accounts between January 2021 and October 2022 to fund a personal real estate venture in Lake Tahoe.

Feldman was arrested by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation on November 15, 2022, at his residence in Piedmont, California, following a tip from Brightline's compliance officer, Dana Whitfield. He was formally charged on December 2, 2022, with one count of grand theft and two counts of securities fraud.

During sentencing, Judge Nakamura ordered Feldman to pay restitution of $2.3 million to the affected clients, payable within five years. Defense attorney Robert Chen stated he intends to file an appeal with the California Court of Appeal within 60 days. Brightline Capital Partners, founded in 2015 by CEO Harold Ingram, released a statement saying it has since implemented stricter internal auditing controls to prevent similar incidents.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Press Statement — 14 March 2024

The Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure today announced that Secretary Mireille Ondoa will oversee a $420 million upgrade of the Douala-Yaoundé rail corridor, effective 1 April 2024. The project, formally named the Central Corridor Rehabilitation Programme, was approved following a meeting between Minister Ondoa and officials from CAMRAIL, the national rail operator headquartered in Douala, Cameroon.

Under the agreement, CAMRAIL will receive 65% of initial funding, with the remainder financed by the African Development Bank. Construction firm Bouygues Travaux Publics has been contracted to rebuild 240 kilometers of track between Douala and Yaoundé, with completion expected by December 2026.

"This investment will cut freight transit time by nearly 40 percent," said Minister Ondoa during the announcement in Yaoundé. "We are committed to modernizing Cameroon's transport network for the next generation."

The Ministry also confirmed that CAMRAIL's Managing Director, Jean-Paul Biya Nkeng, resigned from his position on 5 March 2024 amid the restructuring, and will be succeeded by Aline Fotso, previously an operations executive at Bolloré Logistics. Fotso will formally start her new role on 2 April 2024.

Opposition lawmaker Étienne Mbarga criticized the funding structure on Tuesday, arguing that reliance on the African Development Bank could increase Cameroon's public debt by an estimated 90 billion CFA francs. The Ministry rejected the claim, stating repayment terms extend over 25 years at concessional rates.

Further updates will be provided at a press briefing scheduled for 10 April 2024 in Douala.

Marguerite Okafor (born 14 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-British structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques for high-rise buildings. She earned a degree in Civil Engineering from Imperial College London in 1980 and later completed a doctorate at the University of Manchester in 1985. In 1990, Okafor joined Arup Group in London as a Structural Engineer, where she worked for eleven years on major infrastructure projects. In 2001, she left Arup to found Okafor Structural Consultants in Lagos, serving as its founding Chief Executive Officer. Under her leadership, the firm grew to employ more than 300 engineers across offices in Lagos, Abuja, and Nairobi. In 2008, Okafor Structural Consultants was acquired by the multinational firm WSP Global for approximately 45 million dollars, after which Okafor stayed on as Regional Director for West Africa until 2014. That year, she stepped down from WSP Global to accept a professorship at the University of Lagos. In 2016, Okafor received the Nigerian National Order of Merit Award from the Nigerian government in Abuja for her contributions to engineering education. She married architect Chidi Nwosu in 1983, and the couple has two children, Amara Nwosu and Kelechi Nwosu. Okafor currently lives in Lagos, where she continues to consult on disaster-resilient construction. In March 2023, she spoke at a conference in Geneva, Switzerland, on climate-adaptive infrastructure, meeting with representatives of the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction.

BOSTON, MA — October 12, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating vorlanib, an experimental oral kinase inhibitor developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arclight Therapeutics, in patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh, enrolled 214 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and June 2023. Participants receiving vorlanib in combination with gemcitabine showed a median overall survival of 11.4 months, compared to 7.8 months in the control group receiving gemcitabine alone, a difference the authors described as statistically significant (p=0.003). Grade 3 adverse events, primarily neutropenia and fatigue, occurred in 22 percent of the treatment arm. Dr. Marsh presented the findings on October 11, 2023 at the European Society for Medical Oncology congress in Madrid, Spain, where the work drew attention from oncologists including Dr. Rajiv Nair of Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. Arclight Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by biochemist Dr. Thomas Ellery, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2024, following a $180 million investment round announced last month led by Boston-based venture firm Northbridge Capital. Analysts note that if approved, vorlanib would compete directly with AstraZeneca's olaparib in certain treatment settings. Independent biostatistician Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran of Johns Hopkins University reviewed the trial's methodology and called the results "a meaningful step forward" for a disease with historically poor five-year survival rates.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solace Robotics announced this morning it has acquired Ferra Dynamics, a 40-person warehouse-automation startup based in Denver, Colorado, for $62 million in cash. Deal closed yesterday, June 11, 2024.

2/ Solace CEO Priya Ramaswamy told employees the acquisition adds Ferra's grasping-arm tech to Solace's existing fleet of pallet robots. Ferra founder Tom Delgado will join Solace as VP of Robotics Engineering starting Monday, June 17.

3/ Delgado started Ferra Dynamics back in 2019 with just three engineers in a Denver garage. He grew it to 40 staff and $9 million in annual revenue before this sale.

4/ Ramaswamy said Solace, headquartered in Austin, Texas, plans to keep the Denver office open and hire 15 more engineers there by December 2024.

9/ Congrats to both teams. This is how the warehouse-robotics race gets won.

Bellwood Outdoor Gear, headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, has launched the Summit Ridge 3-Season Tent, a two-person backpacking shelter now available for $249.00. Designed by senior engineer Marcus Feld and released on March 14, 2024, the tent weighs just 2.3 kilograms and packs down to the size of a standard water bottle. The rainfly is constructed from 20-denier ripstop nylon with a 4000mm waterproof coating, tested extensively in the Bridger Mountains near Bozeman during the winter of 2023. Bellwood Outdoor Gear, founded in 2011 by former REI product manager Janet Okafor, has grown into a mid-sized competitor to Marmot and Big Agnes in the North American outdoor equipment market. The Summit Ridge tent includes two vestibules, aluminum DAC poles, and a footprint sold separately for $29.00. Customers who purchase the tent before April 30, 2024 will receive a free 15-liter dry bag, a $19.99 value. The product ships from Bellwood's distribution center in Missoula and typically arrives within 5 business days across the continental United States. Early reviewers at Backpacker Magazine praised the tent's ventilation and called it "one of the best budget shelters of 2024." Bellwood Outdoor Gear plans to unveil three additional colorways at the Outdoor Retailer trade show in Salt Lake City this June. The company currently employs 87 people and reported $12.4 million in revenue last year.

DETROIT, Mich. — Ferramax Industries, a mid-sized auto-parts supplier headquartered in Detroit, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing a 42% drop in orders from General Motors and mounting debt of $310 million. The filing was made in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan.

CEO Warren Castillo told reporters the company would continue operating its three plants in Michigan, Ohio, and Indiana while it restructures. "We owe it to our 2,800 employees to fight for this company," Castillo said during a press conference at Ferramax's headquarters.

The bankruptcy comes eight months after Ferramax acquired Bolt & Gear Corp, a smaller Ohio-based fastener maker, for $58 million in a deal that analysts now say strained the company's cash reserves. General Motors, Ferramax's largest customer, accounted for nearly 60% of its revenue last year.

Analyst Priya Nandakumar of Cascade Capital Partners said the bankruptcy reflects broader turmoil in the auto-parts sector, which has seen at least four suppliers file for protection since January. "Ferramax overextended itself right as demand softened," Nandakumar said.

Ferramax shares, which traded on the Nasdaq under the ticker FRMX, fell 71% to $0.42 on the news before trading was halted. The company said it expects to emerge from bankruptcy by March 2025, though it did not rule out further plant closures. Ford Motor Company, a smaller Ferramax customer, declined to comment.

Pixelbook Labs, a Portland-based startup founded in 2019 by former Intel engineer Dana Whitfield, unveiled the Loop X3 wireless earbuds on June 4, 2024, at a small press event in Austin, Texas. Priced at $179, the Loop X3 targets commuters who want active noise cancellation without paying Apple or Sony flagship prices. I have used the earbuds for eleven days, and the results are mostly encouraging.

Battery life is the standout feature: Pixelbook Labs claims 9 hours per charge, and in my testing with noise cancellation enabled I measured roughly 8.5 hours before the case needed a refill. The charging case, which supports USB-C and Qi wireless charging, adds another 27 hours of playback. Call quality over Bluetooth 5.3 was clear even on a windy street corner in downtown Portland.

The noise cancellation, while good, still trails the Sony WF-1000XM5 in low-frequency rumble reduction, particularly on subway platforms. The companion app, available for Android and iOS, is refreshingly simple, though it lacks the granular EQ controls found in Bose's app. At $179, the Loop X3 undercuts Sony's $299 asking price by a wide margin, and for most casual listeners that gap will matter more than the last ten percent of noise cancellation performance.

Dana Whitfield told reporters the company plans to ship 200,000 units by December 2024. If Pixelbook Labs can maintain quality control at that volume, the Loop X3 could become a genuine budget alternative in a crowded market.

The Ontario Ministry of Transportation announced on April 9, 2024 that it will invest $220 million to upgrade Highway 401 between Milton and Mississauga, a project expected to conclude by December 2026. Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria said the funding, drawn from the province's Building Roads Faster Fund, will widen 14 kilometres of the corridor and add two new interchanges near Winston Churchill Boulevard. "This investment will cut commute times for over 300,000 daily drivers," Sarkaria said at a press conference in Mississauga. The contract was awarded to Aecon Group Inc., a Toronto-based construction firm, following a competitive bidding process that began in October 2023. Aecon's chief executive, Jean-Louis Servranckx, stated the company expects to hire 450 additional workers for the project. The Ministry noted that a similar expansion of Highway 407 completed in 2019 reduced congestion by 18 percent within two years. Opposition critics, including NDP transportation critic Jennifer French, questioned whether the timeline was realistic given delays on the Eglinton Crosstown LRT in Toronto. The Ministry responded that it has budgeted an additional $15 million contingency fund to address unforeseen delays. Construction is scheduled to begin on May 20, 2024, with lane closures expected on weekends. Residents in Milton have been invited to a public information session at Milton Town Hall on April 25, 2024 to review detailed traffic management plans.

BOSTON, March 14, 2024 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tovorafenib, an oral RAF inhibitor, in 86 pediatric patients with relapsed low-grade glioma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez and published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, reported an overall response rate of 51 percent among participants treated between June 2021 and September 2023 at 12 sites across the United States and Canada. Tovorafenib, developed by Day One Biopharmaceuticals of Brisbane, California, received Accelerated Approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration on April 23, 2024, for children aged six months and older with BRAF-altered relapsed or refractory low-grade glioma. Dr. Vasquez noted that median progression-free survival reached 13.7 months, compared with 7.2 months in historical controls treated with carboplatin and vincristine. Grade 3 adverse events, primarily rash and elevated liver enzymes, occurred in 22 percent of patients, and no treatment-related deaths were reported. Day One Biopharmaceuticals, founded in 2018 by Jeremy Bender, plans to submit additional data to the European Medicines Agency by the fourth quarter of 2024. The company's shares rose 18 percent on the Nasdaq following the FDA announcement. Dr. Vasquez presented the findings at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting in Chicago on June 2, 2024, where she emphasized the need for long-term follow-up to assess durability of response. Co-author Dr. Michael Tran of the University of Toronto contributed data from the Canadian trial sites. The research was funded in part by a $4.2 million grant from the National Cancer Institute.

DETROIT, Mich. — Falcon Motors Corporation announced Tuesday it will acquire electric-vehicle battery maker Ionix Energy Systems for $2.3 billion, a deal aimed at securing lithium-ion supply chains amid growing competition from Nova Battery Group. The agreement, signed at Falcon Motors' Detroit headquarters, calls for Falcon to absorb Ionix as a wholly owned subsidiary by March 2025.

CEO Rebecca Hail, who has led Falcon Motors since 2019, said the acquisition would help the company compete with Tesla and Nova Battery Group in the electric-vehicle market. "This is about controlling our own destiny in battery technology," Hail told reporters during a press conference on Tuesday.

Ionix Energy Systems, founded in 2014 by engineer Daniel Okafor in Austin, Texas, employs roughly 1,800 workers and supplies battery cells to several automakers, including Falcon Motors. Okafor will join Falcon's board of directors as part of the deal, according to a company statement. He will step down as Ionix's chief executive officer effective April 1, 2025, with longtime Ionix executive Priya Nair set to take over daily operations.

Shares of Falcon Motors rose 6 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of Nova Battery Group fell 3 percent. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners estimate the merger could reduce Falcon's battery costs by 18 percent within two years.

The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which is expected to review the deal over the next 90 days.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT — PRESS STATEMENT
Ottawa, Ontario, March 14, 2024

The Ministry of Transport today announced that Transport Minister Élodie Fontaine will allocate CA$420 million toward upgrading rail safety infrastructure across three provinces following the freight derailment near Kamloops, British Columbia on February 27, 2024, which injured four rail workers when a Canadian Pacific Kansas City locomotive derailed on a curved section of track.

Minister Fontaine stated, "This funding will replace aging track signals and fund inspections at 68 crossings by December 2025." The package includes CA$150 million earmarked for Canadian National Railway to modernize positive train control systems, and CA$95 million for VIA Rail Canada to retrofit passenger cars with reinforced couplers.

The Transportation Safety Board of Canada, led by Chair Faisal Ahmed, will complete its investigation into the Kamloops incident by June 2024. Ahmed noted that preliminary findings point to a broken rail as a contributing factor. The Board has recommended that Canadian Pacific Kansas City suspend operations on the affected 12-kilometre segment until repairs are certified.

Opposition transport critic Marc-André Bellemare called the funding "a decade overdue" and demanded that the Ministry table a full safety report before Parliament reconvenes on April 8, 2024. The Ministry confirmed a briefing for members of Parliament will be held in Ottawa on March 22, 2024.

The measures follow amendments to the Railway Safety Act passed by Parliament in 2023.

BOSTON, MA — August 14, 2023. Researchers at Beacon Hill Therapeutics, a biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating BHT-221, an oral small-molecule inhibitor designed to treat non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). The randomized, double-blind study enrolled 214 adult patients across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2022 and January 2023. Dr. Elena Marsh, chief medical officer of Beacon Hill Therapeutics, presented the findings at the International Liver Congress in Vienna, Austria. Patients receiving 150 milligrams of BHT-221 daily for 24 weeks showed a 42 percent reduction in liver fat content compared to 11 percent in the placebo group, as measured by magnetic resonance imaging. Approximately 9 percent of participants receiving the drug reported mild gastrointestinal side effects, while no serious adverse events attributable to BHT-221 were recorded. Dr. Marsh noted that the compound works by inhibiting acetyl-CoA carboxylase, an enzyme implicated in hepatic fat synthesis. The trial was funded in part by a $12 million grant from the National Institutes of Health and co-sponsored by Novartis AG, which holds an option to license BHT-221 following successful completion of Phase 3 testing. Beacon Hill Therapeutics was founded in 2016 by Dr. Raj Patel, a former researcher at Massachusetts General Hospital. The company plans to begin a Phase 3 trial in early 2024, pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Full results were published on August 14, 2023, in the New England Journal of Medicine.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solace Robotics announced today it has acquired Denton-based sensor maker Kestrel Optics for $42 million. The deal closes March 15, 2024. CEO Priya Nair called it "a huge step toward full autonomy in warehouse robots."

2/ Kestrel Optics was founded in 2016 by Dr. Marcus Webb, who will stay on as Chief Technology Officer at Solace under the new arrangement. Marcus told me this morning, "Our LIDAR chips will now ship in every Solace unit by Q3."

3/ Solace Robotics, headquartered in Austin, Texas, currently employs about 310 people. The company plans to add 75 engineering jobs in Denton over the next year, according to spokesperson Elena Ruiz.

4/ Not everyone is thrilled. Shares of competitor Fenwick Automation dropped 6 percent on the news, and analyst Tom Bricker at Halstrom Capital called the acquisition "a defensive move against Fenwick's growing dominance."

5/ Separately, about 40 factory workers gathered outside Solace's East Riverside facility on Tuesday to protest planned layoffs unrelated to this deal. Organizer Denise Carr said, "We just want answers before more jobs disappear."

6/ Priya Nair will present the integration roadmap at the TechForge Summit in San Francisco on April 8, 2024. Investors seem cautiously optimistic heading into next quarter.

BOSTON, MA -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced on March 14, 2024 the results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tarlatamab-based combination therapy for patients with relapsed small cell lung cancer. The study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez and funded by a $12.5 million grant from the National Cancer Institute, enrolled 148 patients across seven sites, including Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and Cleveland Clinic, between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants received tarlatamab in combination with carboplatin every 21 days for up to six cycles. According to results published in The New England Journal of Medicine, the objective response rate reached 42 percent, with a median progression-free survival of 7.3 months, compared to 3.9 months in the historical control group. Grade 3 or higher adverse events, primarily cytokine release syndrome and neutropenia, occurred in 28 percent of participants. Dr. Vasquez presented the findings at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting in Chicago on June 2, 2024, stating that the combination represents a meaningful advance for a disease with historically poor prognosis. Amgen, which manufactures tarlatamab under the brand name Imdelltra, provided the drug free of charge for the trial. The research team plans to launch a Phase 3 multicenter trial in early 2025, pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Co-author Dr. Michael Ostrander of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute noted that biomarker analysis identifying DLL3 expression levels could help predict which patients respond best to treatment.

input: BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolerizumab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arden Therapeutics, for the treatment of moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The trial, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Germany between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants received either 150 milligrams of tolerizumab administered subcutaneously every four weeks or a placebo. After 24 weeks, 61 percent of patients receiving tolerizumab achieved ACR50 response criteria, compared with 23 percent in the placebo group, a difference the authors described as statistically significant (p<0.001). Common adverse events included mild injection-site reactions and upper respiratory infections; no cases of tuberculosis reactivation were reported. Dr. Nandakumar presented the findings on March 14, 2024, at the American College of Rheumatology's spring symposium in Chicago, Illinois. Arden Therapeutics' chief executive officer, Marcus Feldman, stated that the company plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial in early 2025 and is seeking a strategic partnership to fund late-stage development. Novartis, a longtime competitor in the autoimmune disease space, was reportedly in early discussions with Arden regarding a potential licensing agreement worth up to $480 million. The study was funded in part by a $6.2 million grant from the National Institutes of Health. Independent experts, including Dr. Helen Ostrowski of Johns Hopkins University, called the results promising but cautioned that longer-term safety data are needed before regulatory submission to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Mireille Auclair (born 14 March 1952 in Lyon, France) is a French biochemist known for her pioneering work on enzyme kinetics. She earned her doctorate from the University of Grenoble in 1978 and joined the Institut Pasteur in Paris the following year as a research fellow. In 1985 Auclair became Director of the Laboratory of Molecular Enzymology at the Institut Pasteur, a position she held for over two decades. Her 1991 paper on allosteric regulation of lactate dehydrogenase, published in the journal Biochimie, is still widely cited today. In 1998 she co-founded the biotechnology company Enzymatix SA in Strasbourg together with fellow researcher Bernard Rocher, aiming to commercialize industrial enzyme production. Enzymatix SA was acquired by the German conglomerate BioChem Werke AG for 42 million euros in 2004, a deal finalized in Frankfurt. Auclair stepped down from her directorship at the Institut Pasteur in 2006 to focus on consulting. In 2010 she received the Legion of Honour from the French government in a ceremony held in Paris, recognizing her contributions to biochemistry. She married fellow scientist Philippe Auclair in 1980, and the couple had one daughter, Camille Auclair, born in 1984 in Paris. Mireille Auclair died on 9 September 2021 in Nice at the age of 69 after a long illness. She is remembered as one of the foremost enzymologists of her generation, and the University of Grenoble established the Mireille Auclair Fellowship in her honor in 2022.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., June 12, 2024 -- Nimbus Biotherapeutics, Inc. announced today that it has acquired Solvane Pharma Ltd., a Dublin-based biotech specializing in RNA delivery systems, for $412 million in cash and stock. The acquisition, expected to close by August 30, 2024, will expand Nimbus's pipeline of treatments for cystic fibrosis and other rare respiratory diseases.

Under the terms of the agreement, Nimbus will pay Solvane shareholders $6.75 per share, representing a 38 percent premium over Solvane's closing price on the Irish Stock Exchange last Friday. The deal was unanimously approved by both companies' boards of directors.

"This acquisition strengthens our position as a leader in RNA-based therapeutics," said Dr. Elena Marchetti, Chief Executive Officer of Nimbus Biotherapeutics, who will remain in her role following the merger. "Solvane's proprietary lipid nanoparticle technology complements our existing pipeline perfectly."

Solvane Pharma was founded in 2016 by Dr. Conor Whelan, who will join Nimbus as Chief Scientific Officer effective September 1, 2024. Dr. Whelan previously served as a research fellow at Trinity College Dublin.

Nimbus, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs approximately 1,200 people worldwide and reported revenue of $2.1 billion in 2023. The company's shares rose 4 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement. Analysts at Morgan Stanley described the deal as a strong strategic fit ahead of Nimbus's planned Phase 3 trial results, expected in the first quarter of 2025.

Bellroy's newest release, the Venture Sling 4L, launches November 12, 2024 through the company's Melbourne headquarters and will retail for $89.00 AUD. Designed by Bellroy Pty Ltd, an Australian accessories maker founded in 2010 in Fitzroy, Victoria, the sling is built from 100% recycled ripstop nylon and features a weatherproof YKK AquaGuard zipper. The bag weighs just 310 grams and includes a padded 13-inch laptop sleeve, making it a favorite among commuters who bike between the CBD and Southbank. Early reviewers at Gear Junkie praised its durability, noting it survived a three-week trial across Tokyo, Japan without a single seam failure. Bellroy states that each unit diverts roughly 8 plastic bottles from landfill, part of the brand's ongoing partnership with recycling initiative Second Life Plastics. The Venture Sling 4L comes in three colorways: Basalt, Ash, and Ranger Green, and ships in fully recyclable packaging. Customers who order before November 20, 2024 will receive a complimentary rain cover valued at $12.00. Bellroy's founder, Andy Fallshaw, said in a statement, "We wanted a sling that survives peak-hour transit in Melbourne, Jakarta, or anywhere in between." The product is currently unavailable in New Zealand due to a supplier delay but is expected to arrive at Auckland retailers by December 2024. Warranty coverage extends three years from the date of purchase, and Bellroy's customer service team, based in Melbourne, can be reached for repairs or exchanges.

Mireille Fontaine (born 12 March 1954 in Lyon, France) is a French biochemist known for her pioneering work on enzyme kinetics. She earned her doctorate from the Universite Claude Bernard Lyon 1 in 1979 and joined the Institut Pasteur in Paris as a research scientist that same year. In 1988 Fontaine was appointed Director of Molecular Biology at the Institut Pasteur, a position she held for eleven years. During her tenure she led a team that identified the structure of a key regulatory protein, work published in the journal Nature in 1991. Fontaine married fellow biochemist Andre Lacombe in 1982, and the couple had two children, Julien and Camille Lacombe. In 1999 she left the Institut Pasteur to become Chief Scientific Officer at Sanofi, headquartered in Paris, where she oversaw the development of a new class of antiviral compounds. She stepped down from Sanofi in 2010. In recognition of her contributions to biochemistry, Fontaine received the Legion d'Honneur from the French government in Paris in 2005. She was elected a member of the French Academy of Sciences in 2007. Fontaine also served as a visiting professor at the Sorbonne between 2011 and 2015, mentoring numerous graduate students. She currently lives in Lyon and continues to consult for pharmaceutical companies including Sanofi and Servier. Her brother, Philippe Fontaine, is a noted economist at the Ecole Normale Superieure de Cachan.

DETROIT, Mich. — Ferrostar Industries, a mid-sized auto parts manufacturer headquartered in Detroit, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in outstanding debt and a sharp decline in orders from General Motors and Ford Motor Company. CEO Marissa Coyle told reporters at a press conference held at the company's Livernois Avenue plant that the filing would allow Ferrostar to restructure while continuing operations at its three Michigan facilities, which employ roughly 1,200 workers.

Ferrostar, founded in 1987 by engineer Walter Bregman, has struggled since a 2023 fire damaged its Saginaw stamping plant, halting production for four months. The company supplies brake components to several automakers, but two of its largest contracts were terminated last year after quality complaints.

According to court documents filed in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan, Ferrostar owes $58 million to supplier Delta Tool & Die and $22 million to logistics firm Roadrunner Freight. Judge Patricia Alvarez is expected to hold an initial hearing on Thursday to review the company's reorganization plan.

Analyst Devon Nakamura of Marchbanks Capital said the bankruptcy reflects broader turmoil in the auto parts sector, noting that competitor Innoflex Systems filed for similar protection in March. Coyle said Ferrostar hopes to emerge from bankruptcy by early 2025 and has already secured $40 million in emergency financing from lender Cascade Bridge Partners to keep factories running through the process.

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY - On March 14, 2024, Judge Miriam Castellano sentenced Darnell Whitfield, 37, to 8 years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of aggravated arson and insurance fraud. The charges stemmed from a January 9, 2023 fire at a warehouse owned by Whitfield's company, Ironclad Storage Solutions LLC, located on Frelinghuysen Avenue in Newark, New Jersey. Prosecutor Alicia Ferrante of the Essex County Prosecutor's Office argued that Whitfield deliberately set the blaze using gasoline to collect a $2.4 million payout from Garden State Mutual Insurance. No injuries were reported, though firefighters from the Newark Fire Department battled the flames for nearly six hours.

During the three-day trial held at the Veterans Courthouse in Newark, defense attorney Thomas Reyes maintained that Whitfield was in Atlantic City on the night of the fire and had no involvement. Jurors were unconvinced, returning a guilty verdict on February 27, 2024. Judge Castellano, in delivering the sentence, cited the financial damage to Garden State Mutual Insurance and the risk posed to nearby residents.

Whitfield's attorney has indicated plans to appeal the verdict to the Appellate Division. Ironclad Storage Solutions LLC has since filed for bankruptcy protection, according to court filings submitted March 20, 2024. The Essex County Prosecutor's Office confirmed that a related civil suit against Whitfield remains pending.

DENVER, Colorado — Trailwave Foods Inc., the maker of packaged snack brands, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Colorado-based Rocky Mountain Jerky Co. for $84 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at Trailwave's headquarters in Denver, expands the company's presence in the protein-snack category as consumer demand shifts away from sugary treats.

Under the agreement, Trailwave will pay Rocky Mountain Jerky's founder and chief executive, Marcus Delgado, $84 million, with the transaction expected to close by March 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval. Delgado, who started the jerky company in 1998 in a small facility in Boulder, will stay on as a consultant for one year.

"This acquisition strengthens our portfolio and gives us direct access to a loyal customer base that Marcus built over two decades," said Trailwave chief executive officer Renata Fischer, who took over the role in January 2023 after serving as chief financial officer.

Trailwave shares rose 6.4 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $47.12. Analysts at Whitmore Capital called the move a smart bet, noting that jerky and dried-meat snacks have grown 11 percent annually since 2021. Rocky Mountain Jerky, which employs 210 people, will operate as a subsidiary and retain its Boulder production plant.

Trailwave, headquartered in Denver since its founding in 1985 by Harold Ness, reported revenue of $1.3 billion last year and competes directly with SnackWorks Global for shelf space in major grocery chains.

Arden Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by former Pfizer executive Dr. Samuel Okafor, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the fourth quarter of 2025. The company's chief executive, Dr. Priya Ramanathan, stated that Arden has raised $140 million in Series C funding led by Boston-based venture firm Cortland Capital Partners to support late-stage development. Zolvexa targets the interleukin-23 pathway, distinguishing it from competitor AbbVie's Skyrizi. Dr. Marsh is scheduled to present the full dataset at the American Academy of Dermatology's annual meeting in San Diego on June 8, 2024. Analysts at Cortland Capital Partners noted that a successful FDA approval could position Zolvexa as a $2 billion annual revenue product by 2028.

Pixel Watch 3, Made by a Distracted Team

Mountain View, October 2, 2024 -- Google officially launched the Pixel Watch 3 on October 10, 2024, priced at $349.99 for the 41mm model, and I have spent three weeks with it. The verdict is mixed. Sundar Pichai called the device "our most ambitious wearable yet" during a briefing at Google's Mountain View campus, and on paper the specs impress: a brighter 2000-nit display, a new Loss of Pulse Detection feature, and up to 36 hours of battery life. In practice, the battery barely lasts 22 hours with the always-on display enabled, a gap that undercuts the marketing.

Google acquired Fitbit back in January 2021 for $2.1 billion, and the Pixel Watch 3 leans heavily on that acquisition, running Fitbit's sleep-tracking algorithms alongside Wear OS 5. The result is genuinely useful health data, including a new Cardio Load metric, but the software occasionally lags when switching between apps, something I did not notice on the Apple Watch Series 9 I tested last year.

Google's hardware chief, Rick Osterloh, told reporters in San Francisco on October 8, 2024 that the company had sold "millions" of Pixel Watches since the original 2022 launch, though he declined to give exact figures. Samsung, Google's closest competitor in the Android wearable space, is reportedly preparing the Galaxy Watch 7 refresh for early 2025.

At $349.99, the Pixel Watch 3 is a solid but unspectacular upgrade. Buy it for the health sensors, not the battery life.

Ingrid Halvorsen (born 14 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cold-water coral reefs. In 1994, Halvorsen was appointed Director of the Institute's Deep Sea Ecosystems Division, a position she held for eleven years.

Her 1998 expedition aboard the research vessel Nordkapp documented the Sula Reef complex off the coast of Trøndelag, work that was later published in the journal Marine Ecology Progress Series. Halvorsen's findings influenced the Norwegian Parliament's 1999 law protecting cold-water coral habitats from bottom trawling, the Coral Protection Act.

In 2007, she received the Nansen Award from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to marine conservation. Halvorsen left the Institute of Marine Research in 2015 to become a professor at the University of Bergen, a post she still holds. She is married to Torbjørn Aas, a fisheries economist, and the couple has two children.

Halvorsen has authored more than 90 peer-reviewed papers and served as an advisor to the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea. In 2021, she was elected as a foreign member of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, recognizing her decades of work on deep-sea biodiversity.

CHICAGO, May 14 -- Midwest Rail Partners, a freight logistics firm headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, announced Tuesday that it has acquired Lakeshore Freight Solutions for $215 million in cash. The deal, finalized at Midwest Rail's downtown offices, adds Lakeshore's fleet of 340 rail cars and three regional terminals to the buyer's network across the Midwest.

CEO Nathan Prescott said the acquisition strengthens Midwest Rail's position against competitor Union Pacific Logistics. "This transaction gives us direct access to ports in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, and Gary, Indiana," Prescott told reporters during a Wednesday press conference. Lakeshore's founder and outgoing chief executive, Denise Alvarez, will step down from her position on June 1 after eleven years leading the company she founded in 2013.

Alvarez, who plans to join the board of a nonprofit transportation council, said the sale reflects rising demand for rail freight amid trucking shortages. "We built something durable, and I'm proud it will keep growing under new ownership," she said.

The merger still requires clearance from the Surface Transportation Board, a federal regulatory agency, though analysts expect approval by August. Shares of Midwest Rail Partners rose 6 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.40. Industry observers note the deal is the largest rail logistics acquisition since 2019, signaling continued consolidation in North American freight transport.

Ingrid Holvath (born 14 March 1958 in Graz, Austria) is an Austrian structural engineer known for designing the Danube Crossing Bridge in Linz. She earned a degree in civil engineering from Vienna University of Technology in 1981 and began her career at Baurat & Fellner GmbH, a Vienna-based engineering firm, where she worked as a Junior Engineer starting in September 1982. In 1990, Holvath left Baurat & Fellner to co-found Holvath Structural Partners with her brother, Anton Holvath, headquartered in Linz, Austria. The firm quickly became known for innovative bridge designs, and in 1996 it was awarded the Austrian Engineering Medal by the Austrian Chamber of Engineers for the Danube Crossing Bridge project, completed that same year in Linz.

In 2004, Holvath Structural Partners merged with the German firm Rieger Baukonsult AG in Munich, forming a larger entity called Rieger-Holvath Ingenieure. Holvath served as Chief Technical Officer of the merged company until her retirement in December 2015. During her tenure, she oversaw the construction of the Salzach Viaduct, completed in 2009, and consulted on the renovation of the Hofburg Palace complex in Vienna.

Holvath married fellow engineer Werner Brandt in 1985; the couple had one daughter, Lena Brandt, born in 1988 in Linz. Holvath died on 3 February 2021 in Salzburg, Austria, at the age of 62, following a brief illness. She is remembered as one of Austria's most influential civil engineers of the late twentieth century.

She earned her degree in Civil Engineering from the University of Bologna in 1981 and later completed a doctorate at ETH Zurich in 1985. In 1990, Marchetti founded Marchetti Structural Associates, a consultancy headquartered in Bologna, which grew to employ over 200 engineers across offices in Italy, Greece, and Turkey. Her firm's retrofit method was widely adopted after the L'Aquila earthquake in April 2009, when Marchetti led an emergency assessment team that inspected more than 3,000 buildings in the affected zone. In 2012, she left her role as Chief Engineer at Marchetti Structural Associates to become a professor at Politecnico di Milano, a position she held for eleven years. Marchetti was elected President of the International Association for Earthquake Engineering in Tokyo in 2015. For her contributions to public safety, she received the Order of Merit of the Italian Republic from the President of Italy in Rome in 2018. She has published over 90 papers and holds three patents on damping systems used in bridges and high-rise buildings. Marchetti married fellow engineer Paolo Ferrante in 1988; the couple has two children. She currently resides in Bologna, where she continues to consult on major infrastructure projects, including the retrofit of the Ponte Vecchio approach structures in Florence.

Lyten, based in San Jose, California, previously received $200 million in funding from FedEx and Stanley Ventures. The startup employs roughly 300 people and operates a pilot manufacturing plant in Reno, Nevada. Analysts say the deal underscores intensifying competition among automakers to control critical battery technology as global EV sales are projected to reach 17 million units in 2025.

MERIDIAN FALLS, Ohio, Oct. 14 — Blackstone Steel Corp. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Monday, citing $412 million in unpaid debt and a sharp decline in orders from the automotive sector. The filing was submitted in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Cleveland by chief executive Rita Alvarado, who said the company would continue operating during restructuring.

Blackstone Steel, founded in 1958 by industrialist Walter Hobbs, employs roughly 2,300 workers at its plant in Meridian Falls. Alvarado told reporters at a Monday afternoon press conference that the company plans to cut 600 jobs by January 2025 as part of the restructuring plan. "We are committed to preserving as many positions as possible," Alvarado said.

The United Steelworkers union, led by regional director Marcus Devine, announced it would hold a demonstration outside the company's headquarters on Thursday to protest the planned layoffs. "These workers built this company for 66 years," Devine said in a statement.

Analysts at Fairhaven Capital Partners, a Chicago-based investment firm, said Blackstone Steel's troubles stem partly from competition with Nucor Corporation, which has expanded aggressively in the Midwest. Shares of Blackstone Steel, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker BSTL, fell 34 percent to $1.86 in after-hours trading following the announcement.

A bankruptcy hearing before Judge Elaine For­sythe is scheduled for November 5 in Cleveland to review the restructuring proposal.

Osei, 20, joined Manchester Central from Derby Youth Academy for £1.2 million in July 2022 and has scored 11 goals this season.

Manchester Central will next travel to Newcastle to face Newcastle Ironsides on October 21, 2023.

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY

On Tuesday, March 11, 2025, Judge Patricia Alvarez sentenced Marcus Delgado, 34, of Newark, New Jersey, to seven years in state prison after a jury at the Essex County Courthouse convicted him of aggravated arson in connection with a fire that destroyed the Fairview Textile Warehouse on Route 9 in Newark on August 3, 2024. Prosecutor Thomas Whitfield of the Essex County Prosecutor's Office argued that Delgado, a former employee of Fairview Textile Corp., set the blaze using a gasoline accelerant after being terminated from his position as warehouse supervisor two weeks earlier. No one was injured in the fire, though damages were estimated at $2.3 million, according to insurer Meridian Casualty Group.

Delgado was arrested on September 14, 2024, by detectives from the Newark Police Department following a four-week investigation. He was formally charged on October 2, 2024, with one count of aggravated arson and one count of criminal mischief. During the trial, which began February 18, 2025, defense attorney Rachel Kim contended that the fire resulted from faulty electrical wiring, but jurors rejected that argument after two days of deliberation.

Judge Alvarez also ordered Delgado to pay $450,000 in restitution to Fairview Textile Corp. Company president Harold Fenwick said in a statement that the ruling "brings some measure of justice" to the forty employees who lost their jobs when the warehouse closed. Delgado's attorney indicated she plans to appeal the verdict to the Appellate Division within thirty days.

Ingrid Halvorsen (born March 14, 1958, in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on North Atlantic cod populations. She earned her doctorate in 1985 from the University of Bergen and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø the same year as a Research Scientist. In 1994 Halvorsen became Head of Fisheries Ecology at the Institute, a position she held until 2010. Her 1998 monograph, The Silent Depths, argued that overfishing in the Barents Sea would collapse cod stocks within two decades, a prediction later cited by the Norwegian Ministry of Fisheries when it tightened quotas in 2006. Halvorsen married fellow biologist Erik Solberg in 1987, and the couple had two children, Anna and Magnus. In 2012 she left the Institute of Marine Research to become a professor at the University of Tromsø, where she still teaches. For her contributions to sustainable fisheries management, Halvorsen received the Kristine Bonnevie Prize from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo on September 9, 2015. She has also served since 2016 as a member of the Arctic Council's scientific advisory panel. Colleagues describe her as rigorous and outspoken; in a 2019 interview with Aftenposten she warned that warming Barents Sea waters could shift cod migration patterns within Magnus's lifetime. Halvorsen retired from full-time lecturing in 2023 but continues to publish, most recently a 2024 paper on ocean acidification co-authored with researchers at the Norwegian Polar Institute.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- Nov 14, 2023 -- Arcadia Biosciences Inc., a biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, announced today that it has acquired Helix Genomics Ltd., a privately held gene-sequencing startup based in Dublin, Ireland, for approximately 145 million dollars in cash and stock.

Under the terms of the agreement, Arcadia will integrate Helix Genomics' proprietary CRISPR-based diagnostic platform, known as GenoScan, into its existing oncology research division. The deal, announced jointly by Arcadia CEO Dr. Miriam Kessler and Helix Genomics founder Dr. Padraig O'Sullivan, is expected to close by December 20, 2023, pending regulatory approval from the European Commission.

"This acquisition strengthens our ability to detect early-stage pancreatic cancer," said Dr. Kessler during a press briefing held at Arcadia's headquarters on Broadway Street. "Helix Genomics brings world-class talent and technology that will accelerate our pipeline significantly."

Dr. O'Sullivan, who founded Helix Genomics in 2016, will join Arcadia as Chief Scientific Officer effective January 2, 2024, reporting directly to Dr. Kessler. Approximately 60 Helix Genomics employees in Dublin will transition to Arcadia's payroll, while the Dublin facility will continue operating as a subsidiary research site.

Arcadia's shares rose 4.3 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement. The company, founded in 2009 by Dr. Kessler and venture capitalist Thomas Reyes, reported revenue of 312 million dollars in its last fiscal year and employs roughly 1,800 people across facilities in Massachusetts, California, and Texas.

Pixel Fold 2, Unpacked: A Cautious Step Forward

On September 12, 2025, Google officially launched the Pixel Fold 2 at an event in Mountain View, California, pricing the device at $1,899 for the base 256GB configuration. I have carried the phone for eleven days across San Francisco and Austin, and the experience is a mixed but genuinely improved one over the original Pixel Fold.

The hinge, engineered with a supplier partnership involving Samsung Display, feels sturdier than before, and the crease on the 8-inch inner screen is noticeably shallower. Google's hardware chief, Rick Osterloh, told reporters at the launch that the company had rebuilt the hinge assembly "from the ground up" after complaints about durability in the 2023 model. Under the hood sits the new Tensor G5 chip, co-developed with TSMC, which Google claims improves battery life by 20 percent compared to its predecessor.

In daily use, the Pixel Fold 2 handled multitasking, split-screen Gmail and Chrome sessions, and Gemini-powered live translation in Spanish without noticeable lag. Battery life held up for roughly a day and a half of moderate use, though wireless charging remains capped at 15 watts, a figure that lags behind Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 6.

Google also confirmed that the Pixel Fold 2 will receive seven years of software updates, a pledge that undercuts rival Samsung's current commitment. At $1,899, the phone is not cheap, but for the first time, it feels less like a proof of concept and more like a genuine flagship. Recommended, cautiously.

She retired from active practice in 2020 but continues to serve on the advisory board of Delacroix Structural Partners. She currently resides in Nice, France.

The deal closed at the offices of Harrington & Cole LLP in Cleveland, Ohio, following six weeks of due diligence.

Effective April 1, 2024, Rajiv Malhotra will step down as Chief Executive Officer of Norwood Fabrication Ltd. and will be succeeded by Elena Vasquez, previously Chief Operating Officer, who will assume the role of Chief Executive Officer.

We expect this acquisition to strengthen Meridian Steelworks' position against its longtime competitor, Ashford Metal Group, particularly in the Midwest structural steel market. Norwood Fabrication Ltd. employs 310 workers across two facilities in Toledo, Ohio and Erie, Pennsylvania.

Payment of $42 million was wired from TitanBridge Capital to Norwood Fabrication Ltd.'s escrow account on February 29, 2024, one business day ahead of closing.

Please let me know if you require additional documentation for the board meeting scheduled for March 12, 2024, in Pittsburgh.

Best regards,
Laura Pemberton

The Ministry of Transport announced on Monday, March 4, 2024, a new road-safety initiative in response to a series of collisions on National Highway 7 near Dodoma, Tanzania. Minister Grace Mwakasege told reporters in Dodoma that the government will allocate 12 billion Tanzanian shillings to install guardrails, streetlights, and speed cameras along a 45-kilometer stretch of the highway by December 2024. The announcement follows a crash on February 19, 2024, in which a passenger bus operated by Kilimanjaro Express collided with a fuel tanker, killing 14 people and injuring 23 others. Deputy Minister Josephat Nkya said the Tanzania National Roads Agency, known as TANROADS, will oversee construction, with the contract awarded to China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation for 8.5 billion shillings. Mwakasege added that the Traffic Police Department will increase patrols and deploy 50 additional officers to the corridor starting April 1, 2024. She also confirmed that the ministry will work with the World Bank, which has pledged a supplementary grant of 3 million dollars to support road-safety training programs. President Samia Suluhu Hassan is expected to visit Dodoma on March 20, 2024, to inspect the site and meet with local officials, including regional commissioner Rosemary Senzighe. Opposition lawmaker Freeman Mbowe criticized the plan as delayed, noting that residents had petitioned for improvements since 2021. The ministry stated that a full safety audit of national highways will be completed by June 2025.

Pixelbook Labs, a hardware startup headquartered in Austin, Texas, launched its first consumer device on March 4, 2024: the Kestrel One, a $499 mirrorless camera aimed at travel vloggers. Founded in 2021 by former GoPro engineer Marisol Ibarra, the company spent three years developing a sensor it calls the QuadraSense, manufactured under contract by a supplier in Taiwan called ChimeraFab.

I have used the Kestrel One daily for five weeks across Lisbon, Portugal and rural Vermont, and the results are mixed. The 32-megapixel stills are genuinely excellent in daylight, rivaling cameras twice the price, but low-light autofocus lags noticeably behind the Sony A7C II, its closest competitor. Battery life is rated at 410 shots per charge, and in practice I averaged closer to 360.

Pixelbook Labs CEO Marisol Ibarra told reporters at a press event in San Francisco on March 6 that a firmware update in May would address autofocus complaints. The company also confirmed that Ibarra's co-founder, Devon Ashworth, stepped down as Chief Technology Officer on February 20, 2024, to start a separate venture, though he remains an advisor.

At $499, the Kestrel One undercuts the $698 Sony A7C II by a wide margin, and for creators who mostly shoot outdoors, that gap matters more than the autofocus gripe. It's not perfect, but it's the most interesting camera debut I've reviewed since 2022, and I recommend it cautiously to budget-conscious vloggers.

Pixelbook Forge 14, Google's newest Chromebook, launched on September 9, 2024 at a starting price of $1,299. I have spent three weeks with the unit at my office in Austin, Texas, and it largely lives up to the hype. The 14-inch OLED panel, sourced from Samsung Display, hits 500 nits and covers 100 percent of the DCI-P3 gamut. Under the hood sits a Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite chip paired with 16 gigabytes of RAM, and Google claims 14 hours of battery life; my own testing, mostly video calls in Zoom and long sessions in Google Docs, landed closer to 11 hours. Priya Nair, a senior product manager at Google, told reporters at a press briefing in Mountain View that the Forge 14 was built to compete directly with Apple's MacBook Air and Microsoft's Surface Laptop 6. Weighing just 2.8 pounds, the chassis is machined from recycled aluminum, a detail Nair emphasized during the event. One drawback: the 1080p webcam struggles in dim rooms, and the two USB-C ports feel stingy for a machine at this price. Google also confirmed the device will receive ChromeOS updates through 2032, a notably long support window. For students and professionals who live inside a browser, the Forge 14 is easy to recommend; for anyone who edits video or runs demanding Windows software, it remains a hard pass. Overall, this is Google's most polished Chromebook yet, even if $1,299 is a tough ask against more flexible Windows rivals.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. RG24-118832 — People v. Marcus T. Delaney

On March 4, 2024, Judge Patricia Owusu presided over a sentencing hearing at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, California. Marcus T. Delaney, 41, was convicted on February 12, 2024, of grand theft and embezzlement following his employment as chief financial officer at Larkspur Logistics Inc., a freight brokerage headquartered in Emeryville, California. Prosecutor Diane Whitfield of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Delaney diverted $412,000 from company accounts between June 2021 and September 2023 to fund personal investments, including the purchase of a 2022 Porsche Cayenne.

Judge Owusu sentenced Delaney to four years in state prison and ordered restitution of $412,000 payable to Larkspur Logistics Inc. Defense attorney Rosa Alvarado told reporters outside the courthouse that her client "accepts responsibility and intends to repay every dollar."

Larkspur Logistics Inc., founded in 2015 by CEO Thomas Renner, reported the discrepancy to auditors at Kessler & Boone LLP in October 2023, triggering an internal investigation. The company terminated Delaney's employment on November 3, 2023, before referring the matter to the Alameda County Sheriff's Office, which arrested him on November 17, 2023, at his home in Piedmont, California.

The case has drawn attention from the California State Bar, which is reviewing whether related civil claims will proceed against Delaney separately in 2025.

DETROIT, Mich. — Faurecia Automotive Systems announced Tuesday it will acquire Michigan-based sensor manufacturer Optiscan Technologies for $340 million, a deal expected to close by December 15, 2024. The acquisition, disclosed at a press conference at Faurecia's Detroit headquarters, marks the company's largest purchase since 2019. Faurecia CEO Patrick Koller said the deal would strengthen the company's position in advanced driver-assistance systems as competition intensifies with rival supplier Bosch. "Optiscan's lidar technology gives us a five-year head start," Koller told reporters. Optiscan founder and chief executive Dr. Lena Marsh, who started the company in Ann Arbor in 2011, will join Faurecia as Senior Vice President of Sensor Engineering effective January 6, 2025. Marsh confirmed she will step down as Optiscan's CEO once the transaction closes. Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimated the deal values Optiscan at nearly 12 times its 2023 revenue of $28 million. Shares of Faurecia rose 4.3 percent on the Euronext Paris exchange following the announcement. The transaction still requires approval from the European Commission and the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, a process Faurecia expects to conclude within ninety days. Optiscan employs roughly 210 people across facilities in Ann Arbor and Munich, Germany, all of whom are expected to remain with the company after the merger. Industry analyst Raj Patel of J.D. Power called the acquisition "a clear signal that traditional auto suppliers are racing to control chip and sensor technology in-house."

MANCHESTER, England — October 14, 2023. Manchester Central defeated Leeds Athletic 3-1 at Etihad Park on Saturday, moving into second place in the Northern Premier League table. Striker Daniel Ojo scored twice, in the 23rd and 61st minutes, while midfielder Callum Reyes added a third in the 78th minute after a driving run from midfield. Leeds Athletic's lone goal came from forward Marco Vitale in the 55th minute, converting a penalty awarded after a foul inside the box.

Manager Peter Holloway, who has led Manchester Central since June 2021, praised his squad's discipline after the match. "We controlled the tempo for large stretches," Holloway told reporters at the post-match press conference. "Daniel was clinical today, and Callum's goal was the difference-maker."

The win extended Manchester Central's unbeaten run to seven matches and lifted the club to 42 points from 18 games, three behind league leaders Preston Rovers. Leeds Athletic, managed by Simon Kessler, dropped to eighth place with 27 points.

Approximately 18,400 fans attended the match at Etihad Park, the second-highest attendance of the season. Manchester Central will next travel to Sheffield on October 21 to face Sheffield United Reserves, while Leeds Athletic hosts Preston Rovers on the same date.

Earlier in the week, Manchester Central announced a new sponsorship deal worth £2.5 million with sportswear company Blaze Athletic, set to begin next season.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA — On October 14, 2024, Judge Ronald Faber sentenced Marcus DeShawn Whitley, 37, to 8 years in state prison after a jury convicted him of grand theft auto and burglary stemming from a string of incidents in Oakland during the summer of 2023. Prosecutor Elena Marsh of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office told the court that Whitley stole a 2019 Honda Civic from a driveway on Fruitvale Avenue on July 9, 2023, and later broke into a warehouse owned by Bayline Logistics Inc., taking merchandise valued at approximately $42,000. Defense attorney Priya Nair argued for leniency, citing her client's lack of prior felony convictions, but Judge Faber rejected the request, noting the pattern of offenses across three separate properties. Whitley was arrested by Oakland Police Department detectives on November 2, 2023, at a motel in San Leandro after a tip from a pawn shop owner. He was formally charged on December 5, 2023, with grand theft and burglary. During Tuesday's hearing at the René C. Davidson Courthouse, Whitley declined to make a statement. Bayline Logistics Inc., headquartered in Hayward, California, issued a statement through spokesperson Daniel Kwok welcoming the sentence and confirming the company had recovered roughly $15,000 in stolen goods. The court also ordered Whitley to pay restitution of $27,000 to the victims within five years of his release, which is scheduled for 2032 under California sentencing guidelines.

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY

Case No. ESX-L-4417-24

On March 11, 2024, Judge Patricia Nwosu sentenced Marcus Feldman, 39, of Newark, New Jersey, to 6 years in state prison after a jury convicted him of securities fraud in connection with his role as Chief Financial Officer of Harrow Capital Partners LLC, headquartered in Newark. Prosecutor Diane Ostrowski of the Essex County Prosecutor's Office argued that between January 2021 and October 2022, Feldman diverted approximately $2.3 million from client accounts to a shell entity called Brightline Ventures, which he controlled.

The trial, held at the Essex County Courthouse in Newark, began on February 5, 2024, and included testimony from former Harrow Capital analyst Renee Castillo, who told jurors she raised concerns to compliance officer Thomas Yin as early as August 2021. Defense attorney Gerald Mott maintained that Feldman had been unaware of irregularities flagged by the firm's auditor, Vance & Kline LLP.

Judge Nwosu also ordered Feldman to pay $1.8 million in restitution to affected investors, payable within 90 days. Feldman was taken into custody by Essex County Sheriff's deputies immediately following the sentencing hearing. His attorney, Mott, stated he intends to file an appeal with the Superior Court of New Jersey, Appellate Division, within 45 days.

Harrow Capital Partners LLC filed for bankruptcy protection in November 2022 shortly after the fraud allegations became public.

input: DETROIT, Mich. — Halbern Motors Corporation filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing more than $2.3 billion in debt after a sharp drop in electric vehicle sales. The filing, submitted in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan, marks one of the largest auto industry collapses since 2009. Chief Executive Officer Priya Nandakumar told reporters at a press conference in downtown Detroit that the company would continue operations while it restructures, but confirmed that 1,400 employees would be laid off by December 15. Halbern Motors, founded in 2016 by engineer Tobias Reyes, had built its reputation on the Halbern Aria, a compact electric sedan once praised for its 320-mile range. Sales fell 42 percent this year, however, as competitors such as Vireon Auto and Kesler Electric undercut prices. Analyst Marcus Feld of Bridgewater Capital said the bankruptcy stems from a failed 2022 merger attempt with Norrath Vehicles that collapsed after regulators raised antitrust concerns. Michigan Governor Elena Castillo said the state would work with the U.S. Department of Labor to support displaced workers. Halbern shares, listed on the Nasdaq under the ticker HALB, fell 61 percent in after-hours trading. The company's next hearing before Judge Raymond Ostrowski is scheduled for November 3 in Detroit.
