CAMBRIDGE, MA, March 14, 2024 -- Solara Biotech Inc., a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, announced today that it has acquired NovaGen Therapeutics Ltd., a privately held biotech firm based in Dublin, Ireland, for approximately $340 million in cash and stock.

The acquisition, expected to close on April 30, 2024, will give Solara Biotech full rights to NovaGen's lead compound, SLB-221, a small-molecule treatment currently in Phase 2 trials for chronic kidney disease. Dr. Helena Ruiz, Chief Executive Officer of Solara Biotech, called the deal "a transformative step in our mission to address unmet needs in nephrology."

As part of the transaction, Marcus Webb, founder and former CEO of NovaGen Therapeutics, will join Solara Biotech as Chief Scientific Officer effective May 1, 2024. Webb founded NovaGen in Dublin in 2016 and grew the company to 85 employees before the sale.

Solara Biotech's board of directors approved the deal on March 12, 2024, following three months of negotiations. The company said it will fund the acquisition through a combination of $200 million in cash reserves and a new $140 million term loan from Meridian Capital Partners.

Shares of Solara Biotech, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker SLRB, rose 6 percent following the announcement. Analysts at Cormorant Equity Research said the deal strengthens Solara's pipeline against competitor Aravex Pharmaceuticals, which markets a rival kidney disease drug.

The combined company will employ roughly 410 people across offices in Cambridge and Dublin.

Denver-based Timberline Foods Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Great Plains Bakery, a family-owned bread manufacturer headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska, for $42 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing at Timberline's corporate headquarters, marks the company's third acquisition since 2021 and is expected to close by November 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Timberline CEO Marcus Whitfield said the acquisition would expand the company's presence in the Midwest and add roughly 1,200 employees to its payroll. "Great Plains Bakery has built an exceptional reputation over 60 years, and we intend to preserve its brand identity," Whitfield told reporters.

Great Plains Bakery founder Doris Halvorsen, who started the company in 1963 with her late husband, will step down as chief executive officer effective October 1, 2024, but will remain on the board as an advisor. Her son, Peter Halvorsen, currently the company's chief operating officer, is expected to take over daily operations.

Analysts at Cedar Ridge Capital, a Chicago-based investment firm, said the transaction values Great Plains Bakery at roughly 8 times its annual earnings. Shares of Timberline Foods rose 4.3 percent to $67.85 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement.

The combined company will operate 14 manufacturing plants across the United States, competing directly with Heartland Baking Company, another major Midwest producer. Timberline said it does not expect layoffs at Great Plains Bakery's Omaha facility in the near term.

DENVER, June 12 -- Frontier Metals Corp announced Wednesday that it has acquired Blue Ridge Copper Inc, a privately held mining company based in Reno, Nevada, for $410 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by September 30, will make Frontier Metals the third-largest copper producer in North America.

Under the agreement, Frontier Metals will pay $270 million in cash and issue 6.8 million new shares to Blue Ridge Copper shareholders. Chief Executive Officer Marissa Halden said the acquisition strengthens Frontier's supply chain ahead of rising demand from electric-vehicle manufacturers. "This transaction positions us to meet growing copper demand across North America," Halden told reporters during a press briefing at Frontier's Denver headquarters.

Blue Ridge Copper, founded in 1998 by geologist Tomas Reyes, operates three mines in Nevada and Arizona and employs roughly 1,200 workers. Reyes will join Frontier's board of directors as part of the deal, effective July 1.

Analysts at Cascade Financial Partners said the acquisition could boost Frontier Metals' annual revenue by 18 percent, reaching an estimated $2.3 billion by 2026. Shares of Frontier Metals rose 7.4 percent to $54.20 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Blue Ridge Copper's private valuation had previously stood near $380 million.

The transaction still requires approval from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, which is expected to review the merger over the next 60 days. If approved, it would mark Frontier Metals' largest acquisition since its purchase of Silverline Mining in 2015.

DENVER, Colorado — Alpine Ridge Foods Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Boulder Grain Collective, a regional organic pasta maker, for $42 million in cash. The deal, finalized on March 11, 2024, marks Alpine Ridge's third acquisition since 2021 and expands its footprint into the natural foods segment. Under the agreement, Boulder Grain Collective will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary, retaining its 85 employees and its production facility in Longmont, Colorado. CEO Marta Vance, who founded Alpine Ridge Foods in 2009, said the acquisition would help the company compete more directly with Midwest Organic Mills, its largest rival in the plant-based pasta category. "Boulder Grain has built a loyal customer base over the past decade, and we intend to invest heavily in scaling their production," Vance told reporters at a press briefing in Denver. Boulder Grain's founder, Theo Aldridge, will step down as chief executive officer effective April 1, 2024, but will remain as a strategic advisor. Alpine Ridge financed the purchase through a combination of $30 million in cash reserves and a $12 million loan from First Peak Bank. Shares of Alpine Ridge Foods, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker ARFI, rose 6.4 percent following the announcement, closing at $58.20. Analysts at Cascade Capital Partners upgraded the stock from "hold" to "buy," citing strong long-term growth prospects in the natural foods market.

CHICAGO, September 9, 2024 -- Meridian Foods Corporation announced today that it has acquired Blue Harbor Creamery, a regional dairy producer based in Madison, Wisconsin, for approximately $92 million in cash. The deal, finalized on September 6, 2024, expands Meridian's presence in the Midwest premium dairy segment.

Under the agreement, Meridian will retain all 340 employees at Blue Harbor Creamery's Madison production facility and continue operations under the Blue Harbor Creamery brand name. Meridian CEO Rachel Ostrander said the acquisition strengthens the company's portfolio ahead of its planned expansion into Canada in 2025.

"Blue Harbor Creamery has built a loyal following over its 28 years in business, and we intend to honor that legacy while investing in new capacity," Ostrander said during a press conference held at Meridian's headquarters in Chicago, Illinois.

Blue Harbor Creamery founder Daniel Kowalski, who started the company in 1996, will join Meridian as Senior Vice President of Dairy Operations, effective October 1, 2024. Kowalski said he was confident the partnership would help the brand reach new markets across the United States.

Meridian Foods Corporation, founded in 1978 and headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, reported $4.3 billion in revenue last year and employs more than 12,000 people across 14 states. Financial terms of the transaction were disclosed jointly by both companies' boards, with the deal expected to close fully by October 15, 2024, pending routine regulatory review.

MANCHESTER, England — Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice on Saturday to lead his side to a 3-1 victory over Everton at Villa Park, moving Villa into fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a low left-footed finish after a through ball from midfielder Youri Tielemans, then added a second in the 54th minute from close range. Everton had briefly equalized through striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 40th minute, heading home a corner from Jack Harrison. Villa captain John McGinn sealed the win with a curling shot in the 78th minute in front of 41,982 fans.

Speaking after the match, Aston Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's resilience. "We showed character after conceding, and that is important for our ambitions this season," Emery said at the post-match press conference. Everton manager Sean Dyche acknowledged his team's defensive lapses, telling reporters, "We gave away a soft goal and it cost us today."

The result lifts Aston Villa to 54 points from 27 games, three points behind third-placed Tottenham Hotspur. Everton, still fighting to avoid relegation, remain in 16th place with 24 points. Villa's next fixture is against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium on May 4, while Everton will host Newcastle United on May 5. The Premier League confirmed both fixtures will be broadcast live by Sky Sports.

DETROIT, Mich. — Automaker Falcon Motors Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, October 14, 2025, after years of mounting debt and slowing electric-vehicle sales, the company announced in a statement from its Detroit headquarters. Chief Executive Officer Marcus Whitfield told reporters the filing would allow Falcon Motors to restructure roughly $2.3 billion in liabilities while continuing operations at its Warren, Michigan assembly plant. "This is a difficult but necessary step to secure the company's future," Whitfield said during a press conference held at the Detroit Marriott.

The bankruptcy filing comes just eight months after Falcon Motors acquired battery supplier VoltCore Systems for $410 million, a deal that was meant to shore up production of its flagship Falcon Aria electric sedan. Analysts at Merrick Capital Partners said the acquisition strained cash reserves at a time when demand for the Falcon Aria had fallen 18 percent year-over-year.

Union officials from the United Auto Workers, including local president Denise Hargrove, met with Falcon Motors executives on Wednesday to discuss protections for the company's 6,400 employees. Hargrove said workers were "anxious but hopeful" that a buyer or restructuring plan would preserve jobs at the Warren plant. Falcon Motors' stock, which traded at $34 a share in January, closed Tuesday at $1.12 on the New York Stock Exchange.

BOSTON, MA - November 12, 2023 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital reported promising results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tarlazolib, an oral inhibitor targeting BRAF-mutant tumors, in patients with metastatic melanoma. The study, led by Dr. Helena Vance and published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, enrolled 214 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2021 and June 2022. Participants receiving tarlazolib in combination with pembrolizumab showed a median progression-free survival of 11.4 months, compared to 6.8 months in the control group receiving pembrolizumab alone, a statistically significant improvement (p=0.003). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 22 percent of the tarlazolib arm, most commonly rash and elevated liver enzymes, and were manageable with dose reduction. Novara Therapeutics, the Cambridge-based biotechnology company developing tarlazolib, announced it will seek Breakthrough Therapy designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in early 2024. Dr. Vance stated that the findings support further investigation in a Phase 3 trial expected to begin recruitment at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute by September 2024. Novara Therapeutics was founded in 2016 by Dr. Marcus Reiner and has raised $180 million in venture funding to date. The company's chief executive officer, Priya Nandakumar, said the data represent a meaningful step toward a new treatment option for the roughly 8,000 Americans diagnosed with metastatic melanoma each year. The trial was funded in part by a $12 million grant from the National Cancer Institute. Results were also presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting in Chicago.

DENVER, Oct. 14 - Rocky Mountain Coffee Roasters Inc. announced Monday it has agreed to acquire Boulder-based Alpine Bean Co. for $42 million in cash, marking the company's largest acquisition to date. The deal, expected to close by December 1, will bring Alpine Bean's roasting facility in Longmont, Colorado under Rocky Mountain's ownership.

CEO Martin Halvorsen said the acquisition would expand Rocky Mountain's presence in the specialty coffee segment, which has grown by 18 percent over the past two years. "Alpine Bean has built a loyal customer base across the Rocky Mountain region, and this transaction strengthens our supply chain," Halvorsen told reporters during a press briefing at the company's headquarters in Denver.

Alpine Bean founder Rita Okafor, who started the company in 2009, will join Rocky Mountain as Vice President of Sourcing beginning November 15. Okafor previously worked as a green coffee buyer for Java Trading Partners before launching Alpine Bean.

Analysts at Front Range Capital Partners estimate the deal will add approximately $9 million in annual revenue. Shares of Rocky Mountain Coffee Roasters, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker RMCR, rose 6.3 percent following the announcement, closing at $28.75.

The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, though industry observers do not expect regulatory hurdles given the companies' modest combined market share. Rocky Mountain plans to retain all 85 Alpine Bean employees at the Longmont facility.

Danvers, Massachusetts — Cormorant Robotics Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Pallavi Systems LLC, a Chennai-based sensor manufacturer, for $142 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by December 15, is Cormorant's largest purchase since it went public in 2019. Chief Executive Officer Renata Kovac said the acquisition will let Cormorant integrate Pallavi's lidar sensors directly into its warehouse robots, reducing production costs by an estimated 18 percent. "This gives us a supplier we can actually own," Kovac told reporters at a briefing in Boston. Pallavi Systems was founded in 2011 by engineer Arun Mehta, who will join Cormorant as Senior Vice President of Hardware Engineering effective November 1. Cormorant plans to retain all 340 Pallavi employees at their existing facility in Chennai, India, and will fund the transaction using $90 million in cash reserves and a $52 million credit line from Meridian National Bank. Under the terms of the deal, Bluegrass Creamery will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Foods, retaining its production facility in Bardstown, Kentucky, and its 210 employees. Bluegrass Creamery was founded in 1987 by Harold Tucker and has supplied specialty cheese to retailers such as Whole Foods Market for over two decades.

Farrow added that Meridian expects the deal to increase annual revenue by 8 percent.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Narrows the Gap, But Battery Still Lags

Mountain View, October 12, 2024 -- Google's Pixel Watch 3 launched last month at $349.99 for the 41mm Wi-Fi model, and after two weeks of daily wear I can say it's the company's most polished wearable yet. The device, unveiled by Google at an event in Mountain View on September 4, 2024, ships with a brighter 2,000-nit display and a new triaxial gyroscope for improved running metrics.

Rick Osterloh, Senior Vice President of Devices and Services at Google, said the Pixel Watch 3 was built to compete directly with the Apple Watch Series 10 and Samsung's Galaxy Watch 7. "We wanted a watch that respects your time," Osterloh told reporters at the Mountain View briefing. Samsung Electronics, headquartered in Suwon, South Korea, has dominated the Android wearable market for years, and Google clearly has it in its sights.

In my testing, the 45mm model lasted just under 30 hours on a single charge with the always-on display enabled, roughly 20 percent better than last year's Pixel Watch 2 but still short of the 36 hours Samsung claims for the Galaxy Watch 7. Fitbit, a Google subsidiary since its $2.1 billion acquisition in 2021, powers the health tracking software, including a new cardiac load metric that flagged an irregular heart rate spike during one of my tempo runs in Golden Gate Park.

At $349.99, the Pixel Watch 3 isn't cheap, but for Android users craving a genuine alternative to the Apple Watch, it's the closest Google has come. Four stars out of five.

input: The Ministry of Environment and Water Resources of Kenya announced on Tuesday, March 11, 2025, a new initiative to restore the Mau Forest Complex following severe flooding that displaced over 12,000 residents in Nakuru County last month. Speaking in Nairobi, Environment Secretary Aisha Mwangi stated that the government will allocate 4.2 billion Kenyan shillings toward reforestation and early-warning infrastructure over the next three years. "We cannot allow communities in Molo and Kuresoi to face this level of destruction again," Mwangi said during a press briefing at Harambee House. The plan, known as the Mau Recovery Programme, will be implemented in partnership with the Kenya Forest Service and the United Nations Environment Programme, whose regional director, Carlos Fernández, praised the initiative as "a model for climate adaptation across East Africa." Construction of eighteen new flood-monitoring stations is expected to begin in June 2025, with the first phase completed by December 2026. President William Ruto is scheduled to visit the affected areas in Nakuru County on March 20, 2025, to meet with local leaders and assess relief efforts. The Kenya Red Cross Society has already distributed emergency supplies worth 85 million shillings to more than 3,000 households since the flooding began on February 14, 2025. Officials emphasized that failure to act could result in repeated disasters, citing similar flooding events in 2018 and 2020 that together caused damages exceeding 9 billion shillings nationwide.

input: MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City midfielder Rodri scored twice as the reigning champions defeated Everton 3-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, extending their unbeaten Premier League run to eleven matches. Pep Guardiola's side dominated possession from the opening whistle, with Erling Haaland opening the scoring in the 22nd minute after a low cross from Jack Grealish. Everton striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalized in the 38th minute, converting a header from a corner kick, but Rodri restored City's lead just before halftime with a curling effort from outside the box. His second goal, a penalty in the 71st minute, sealed the victory after Everton defender James Tarkowski was penalized for a handball inside the area. Sean Dyche, Everton's manager, admitted afterward that his team "struggled to contain Rodri's movement in midfield." The result leaves Manchester City second in the Premier League table with 21 points, three behind leaders Liverpool, who beat Brighton 2-0 earlier the same day at Anfield. Manchester City's next fixture is against RB Leipzig in the UEFA Champions League on October 25 at the Etihad Stadium. Attendance at Saturday's match was recorded at 53,392, and City captain Kyle Walker was named man of the match by broadcaster Sky Sports.

SUPERIOR COURT OF SUFFOLK COUNTY, MASSACHUSETTS

Case No. 23-CR-04471

On Tuesday, March 14, 2024, the Superior Court of Suffolk County sentenced Marcus Delacroix, 41, to 63 months in federal custody after a jury found him guilty of wire fraud and embezzlement connected to his former role as Chief Financial Officer of Harrow Bay Logistics Inc., a shipping firm headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts. Judge Elaine Whitfield presided over the trial, which concluded on March 8, 2024, following testimony from prosecutor Anita Reyes of the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office.

According to court records, Delacroix diverted approximately $2.3 million from Harrow Bay Logistics between January 2019 and November 2022 by funneling company funds into a shell entity called Coastal Freight Solutions LLC, which he secretly controlled. Delacroix was arrested on June 5, 2023, by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation at his residence in Quincy, Massachusetts, without incident.

Harrow Bay Logistics, founded in 2007 by Warren Halsey, terminated Delacroix's employment on June 6, 2023, one day after his arrest. The company's current CEO, Priya Nandakumar, told reporters outside the courthouse that "this verdict brings closure to a painful chapter for our employees and shareholders."

In addition to the prison term, Judge Whitfield ordered Delacroix to pay $2.3 million in restitution to Harrow Bay Logistics. Defense attorney Gordon Pruitt stated he plans to file an appeal with the Massachusetts Appeals Court within 30 days.

Pixelworks Inc. unveiled the Vantage X7 mirrorless camera on March 4, 2024, at a press event in Portland, Oregon, and I have spent three weeks testing the $2,499 body-only kit. The Vantage X7 uses a 45-megapixel stacked sensor sourced from supplier Ondera Semiconductor, based in Hsinchu, Taiwan, and pairs it with Pixelworks' new Falcon-9 image processor, which the company claims delivers 30 frames per second continuous shooting with full autofocus tracking. Chief product officer Renata Alvarez told reporters at the launch that the camera targets wildlife and sports photographers who currently shoot with the Canon EOS R3, Pixelworks' longtime competitor in the professional mirrorless segment. In hands-on use, autofocus tracking on moving subjects was excellent in daylight but struggled noticeably after sunset, occasionally hunting for nearly two seconds before locking on. Battery life is rated at 480 shots per charge, which matched my own testing closely across five days in Yosemite National Park. The body feels dense at 780 grams, and weather sealing held up through a light rainstorm without issue. Pixelworks also announced that the Vantage X7 will ship starting April 15, 2024, with a firmware update planned for June to add eye-detection for birds. At $2,499, the Vantage X7 undercuts the Canon EOS R3 by roughly $3,000, making it one of the more aggressively priced professional cameras in years. For photographers willing to tolerate occasional low-light autofocus hiccups, this camera is a genuinely compelling upgrade.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 - Manchester City midfielder Rodri scored a stoppage-time penalty to give his side a 2-1 win over Chelsea at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, extending City's unbeaten Premier League run to eleven matches. Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson had opened the scoring in the 23rd minute, finishing a swift counterattack from close range. Erling Haaland equalized for City just before halftime, heading home a corner delivered by Kevin De Bruyne. The result leaves City in second place with 24 points, one behind leaders Arsenal, while Chelsea remain tenth on 12 points. Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola praised his team's resilience after the match. "We never stopped believing, even when Chelsea defended so deep," Guardiola told reporters at the post-match press conference. Chelsea head coach Mauricio Pochettino admitted his side had been undone by a lack of composure late on, saying the penalty decision, awarded after a video review for a foul by Levi Colwill on Jack Grealish, was harsh but correct. Around 53,000 spectators attended the match at the Etihad Stadium. Rodri's goal was his fourth of the season, and it moved Manchester City three points clear of Liverpool, who face Everton at Anfield on Sunday. The Football Association confirmed there were no disciplinary charges following the match, despite a brief confrontation between players after the final whistle.

Denton, TX -- October 14, 2024 -- Meridian Robotics Inc., a Denton-based manufacturer of industrial automation systems, announced today that it has acquired Vantage Sensing LLC, a privately held sensor technology firm based in Round Rock, Texas, for approximately $42 million in cash and stock.

Under the terms of the agreement, Meridian will absorb Vantage Sensing's 65-person engineering team and integrate its LiDAR-based detection modules into Meridian's flagship product line, the AtlasArm 7000. CEO Priya Ramanathan said the acquisition, expected to close on November 30, 2024, will strengthen Meridian's position against competitor Kessler Automation, which has expanded rapidly in the Midwest over the past two years.

"This deal gives us direct access to sensor technology that would have taken three years to develop internally," Ramanathan said during a press briefing held at Meridian's Denton headquarters. Vantage Sensing founder and CEO Marcus Ojeda will join Meridian as Chief Technology Officer, effective December 1, 2024, reporting directly to Ramanathan.

Meridian also confirmed that Sarah Lindqvist, its former Vice President of Engineering, stepped down on October 4, 2024, to pursue an opportunity at a startup in Austin. The company said it expects the Vantage Sensing acquisition to add $18 million in annual revenue beginning in fiscal year 2025.

Meridian Robotics, founded in 2011 by engineer Thomas Baird, employs roughly 900 people across facilities in Denton, Texas, and Querétaro, Mexico. Shares of Meridian are not publicly traded.

AUSTIN, Texas — October 14, 2024 — Helios Dynamics, Inc., a renewable energy technology firm headquartered in Austin, Texas, announced today that it has acquired SolarNest Systems, a privately held battery storage manufacturer based in Reno, Nevada, for approximately 240 million dollars in a cash-and-stock deal.

The acquisition, expected to close by December 1, 2024, will add SolarNest's 320-employee workforce and its 150,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Reno to Helios Dynamics' existing operations. Under the terms of the agreement, Helios Dynamics will pay SolarNest shareholders 180 million dollars in cash and the remainder in Helios Dynamics common stock.

"This acquisition strengthens our position in the residential battery storage market and accelerates our roadmap by nearly two years," said Priya Ramanathan, Chief Executive Officer of Helios Dynamics, during a press conference held at the company's Austin headquarters.

SolarNest's founder and current CEO, Marcus Webb, will join Helios Dynamics as Senior Vice President of Storage Solutions, effective December 2, 2024. Webb founded SolarNest Systems in 2016 and grew it into a supplier for major utility companies across the western United States.

Helios Dynamics' Chief Financial Officer, Daniela Ortiz, noted that the company expects the deal to be accretive to earnings by the third quarter of 2025. Shares of Helios Dynamics, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker HDYN, rose 4.3 percent following the announcement.

The transaction remains subject to regulatory approval, including review under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act.

Pixel Tablet 2, unveiled by Google in Mountain View on September 4, 2024, finally lands on shelves this week at $499 for the 128GB configuration. I have spent eleven days with the review unit, and it mostly delivers on its promise of being a genuinely useful docked hub rather than an oversized phone.

The 11-inch LCD panel runs at 60Hz, which already feels dated next to the 120Hz display on the Samsung Galaxy Tab S9, a direct competitor from Samsung Electronics. Battery life is strong, though; I averaged nine hours and twenty minutes of mixed video and browsing before needing the charging speaker dock, which is sold separately for $129.

Under the hood, the Tensor G3 chip, the same silicon found in the Pixel 8 phone, handles multitasking smoothly, and the new desktop-style taskbar in Android 15 makes window management far less clumsy than previous Android tablet software. Rosa Delgado, a product manager at Google, told me in an interview last Tuesday that the company plans a software update in January 2025 to add split-screen drag-and-drop for third-party apps.

The base speaker dock feels like a afterthought accessory rather than a real docking station, and the front camera's fixed landscape orientation is an odd omission for a device clearly meant to sit on a kitchen counter. Still, for $499, Google has built the most compelling Android tablet since the original Pixel Slate, and I recommend it cautiously to anyone already inside the Google ecosystem.

BOSTON, MA -- February 14, 2024 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tovanafide, an oral JAK1 inhibitor developed by Cambridge-based biotechnology company Arclight Therapeutics, for the treatment of moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis. The study, led by Dr. Priya Ramaswamy, enrolled 214 adult patients across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2022 and September 2023. Participants received either 15 milligrams of tovanafide daily or placebo for 12 weeks. At week 12, 47 percent of patients receiving tovanafide achieved clinical remission compared with 19 percent on placebo, a statistically significant difference (p<0.001). The most common adverse event was mild headache, reported in 62 patients. Dr. Ramaswamy presented the findings on February 13, 2024, at a Contact.Meet-style briefing hosted by the American Gastroenterological Association in Chicago. Arclight Therapeutics' chief executive officer, Martin Voss, said the company plans to file a New Drug Application with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. Arclight, founded in 2016 by Dr. Elena Kowalski, was acquired by Novartis in a $3.2 billion deal announced last month, though the ulcerative colitis program will continue under the Arclight name as a subsidiary. Novartis is headquartered in Basel, Switzerland. Dr. Kowalski, who stepped down as chief scientific officer in December 2023, will join the University of Toronto as a professor of immunology in September 2024. The trial was funded in part by a $4.5 million grant from the National Institutes of Health.

DETROIT, Mich. — Automaker Vantage Motors filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $4.2 billion in outstanding debt and a sharp decline in electric vehicle sales. The filing was submitted in federal bankruptcy court in Detroit by Chief Executive Officer Marcus Whitfield, who took the helm of the company in March 2021.

Vantage Motors, headquartered in Dearborn, Michigan, employed roughly 8,500 workers across three assembly plants before announcing the bankruptcy. Whitfield told reporters at a press conference that the company plans to restructure its operations while continuing production of its flagship Vantage Solara sedan.

"We are committed to emerging from this process as a leaner, more competitive company," Whitfield said Tuesday afternoon.

The bankruptcy follows a turbulent year for Vantage Motors, which lost its supply agreement with battery maker Corvyn Energy Systems in January after a contract dispute. Analysts at Fitch Ratings had warned as early as September 2023 that Vantage Motors faced a liquidity crisis.

Rival automaker Halcyon Auto Group, based in Columbus, Ohio, said it does not plan to acquire any of Vantage Motors' assets at this time. Meanwhile, the United Auto Workers union, led by President Elena Marsh, announced it would meet with Vantage Motors management on Friday to negotiate protections for affected employees.

Shares of Vantage Motors fell 62 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $1.15.

CHICAGO, Oct 14 - Deere & Company announced Tuesday it will acquire Precision AgriTech Inc, a Champaign, Illinois-based startup specializing in soil-sensor technology, for $410 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by December 2, 2024, marks Deere's third acquisition this year as the farm-equipment giant races to bolster its digital agriculture unit, John Deere Precision Ag.

Chief Executive John May said the acquisition would let Deere integrate Precision AgriTech's sensors directly into its 8R-series tractors, allowing farmers to monitor nitrogen levels in real time. "This is about giving growers data they can act on within seconds, not days," May told reporters during a call from Deere's headquarters in Moline, Illinois.

Precision AgriTech, founded in 2016 by former University of Illinois researcher Dana Whitfield, employs 85 people and reported revenue of $38 million last year. Whitfield will join Deere as Vice President of Sensor Innovation, effective November 1, 2024, according to a company statement.

Analysts at Morningstar said the purchase price, roughly 10.8 times revenue, reflects intense competition with rival CNH Industrial, which acquired a similar firm, SoilSense Corp, in March for $290 million. Shares of Deere rose 2.3 percent to $412.17 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume topped 4.1 million shares by early afternoon.

The transaction still requires clearance from the Federal Trade Commission, which Deere expects within 60 days.

CARY, N.C. — Solara Biotech Inc. announced on June 11, 2024 that it has completed its acquisition of Meridian Diagnostics LLC, a privately held maker of rapid disease-screening kits based in Durham, North Carolina, for approximately 142 million dollars in cash and stock. The deal closed after Solara's board of directors approved the transaction on May 28, 2024.

Under the terms of the agreement, Meridian Diagnostics will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Solara Biotech, retaining its Durham manufacturing facility and its 210 employees. Dr. Priya Nandakumar, Meridian's founder and chief executive officer, will join Solara as Senior Vice President of Diagnostics, reporting to Solara CEO Marcus Whitfield.

"This acquisition strengthens our position against competitors like Vantage Health Systems and accelerates our entry into point-of-care testing for tuberculosis and influenza," said Whitfield at a press briefing held at Solara's headquarters in Cary, North Carolina.

Meridian Diagnostics was founded in 2016 by Dr. Nandakumar and has developed diagnostic assays used in over 30 countries. Solara Biotech, headquartered in Cary since 2011, trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker SLRA and reported revenue of 890 million dollars in fiscal year 2023.

The transaction is expected to close fully by August 1, 2024, pending routine regulatory review. Solara said it plans to invest an additional 45 million dollars into expanding the Durham facility over the next three years.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 - Manchester City edged Liverpool 2-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, with a stoppage-time header from Erling Haaland sealing a dramatic victory in front of 53,412 fans. The Norwegian striker rose above two defenders in the 91st minute to convert a corner delivered by Kevin De Bruyne, sending the home crowd into raptures.

Liverpool had taken an early lead through Mohamed Salah, who slotted home a penalty in the 23rd minute after Rodri was penalized for a handball inside the box. City responded just before halftime when Phil Foden equalized with a curling effort from 20 yards, his fourth goal of the Premier League season.

Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola praised his squad's resilience after the match. "We never stopped believing, even after conceding early," Guardiola told reporters at a post-match press conference held inside the Etihad Stadium. Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp, meanwhile, expressed frustration at his side's inability to hold the lead, calling the late goal "avoidable."

The win moved Manchester City to the top of the Premier League table with 21 points from 8 matches, two points ahead of Arsenal. Liverpool dropped to fourth place. City's next fixture is against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on October 21, while Liverpool will host Everton at Anfield the same weekend.

Earlier in the week, City announced a five-year extension for Haaland, reportedly worth 34 million pounds annually, keeping him at the club until 2029.

BOSTON, MA -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced on March 14, 2024, the results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tazemetostat combined with rituximab for patients with relapsed follicular lymphoma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez and funded by a $12.5 million grant from the National Cancer Institute, enrolled 148 participants across 9 sites in the United States between January 2021 and August 2023. Patients received 800 milligrams of tazemetostat twice daily for up to 24 months. According to results published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, 62 percent of participants achieved complete remission within 12 months, compared to 38 percent in the control arm receiving rituximab alone. Dr. Vasquez presented the findings at the American Society of Hematology annual meeting in San Diego on December 9, 2023. "This represents a meaningful advance for patients who have exhausted first-line therapies," she said. The trial's co-investigator, Dr. Michael Chen of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, noted that grade 3 adverse events, primarily neutropenia, occurred in 14 percent of the tazemetostat group. Epizyme Inc., the Cambridge-based biotechnology company that manufactures tazemetostat under the brand name Tazverik, plans to submit a supplemental New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the second quarter of 2025. Ipsen, which acquired Epizyme in 2022 for approximately $247 million, will oversee regulatory submissions in Europe through its Paris headquarters. Independent oncologist Dr. Rachel Kim of Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center called the data "promising but requiring longer follow-up to confirm durability of response."

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY
Case No. ESX-L-004417-23

On October 12, 2023, Judge Karen Ostrowski sentenced Marcus Deleon, 34, of Newark, New Jersey, to 7 years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of aggravated assault and unlawful possession of a weapon. The charges stemmed from an incident on March 3, 2023, in which Deleon shot Anthony Ruiz outside the Peabody Lounge on Ferry Street in Newark, leaving Ruiz hospitalized for seventeen days. Prosecutor Diane Whitfield of the Essex County Prosecutor's Office argued that Deleon acted with premeditation, citing text messages sent hours before the shooting. Defense attorney Rolando Marsh contended that his client acted in self-defense during a dispute over a $450 debt.

Deleon was arrested by Newark Police Department detectives on March 9, 2023, at his apartment on South Orange Avenue. He was formally indicted by an Essex County grand jury on May 22, 2023, on charges of attempted murder, aggravated assault, and weapons possession; the attempted murder count was later dismissed during trial. The trial, held at the Essex County Courthouse in Newark, began on September 5, 2023, and lasted six days.

Judge Ostrowski, in handing down the sentence, cited the .380-caliber handgun used in the shooting as an aggravating factor. Deleon must also pay $12,000 in restitution to Ruiz for medical expenses. The New Jersey Department of Corrections confirmed Deleon will serve his term at Northern State Prison in Newark. His attorney has indicated plans to appeal the verdict to the New Jersey Superior Court Appellate Division.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. — Nov 12, 2023 — Arden Biotherapeutics Inc., a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, announced today that it has acquired Voss Pharmaceuticals Ltd., a privately held drug developer based in Dublin, Ireland, for $340 million in cash. The transaction closed on Nov 10, 2023.

Under the agreement, Arden Biotherapeutics gains full rights to VP-221, an experimental compound targeting chronic kidney disease that is currently in Phase 2 trials. Dr. Helena Marsh, Chief Executive Officer of Arden Biotherapeutics, said the acquisition strengthens the company's renal disease pipeline. "Voss Pharmaceuticals built something remarkable with a small team," Marsh said. "We intend to accelerate VP-221 toward Phase 3 by mid-2024."

As part of the deal, Dr. Owen Callahan, founder and former Chief Executive Officer of Voss Pharmaceuticals, will join Arden Biotherapeutics as Chief Scientific Officer effective Dec 1, 2023. Callahan founded Voss Pharmaceuticals in 2015 in Dublin.

Arden Biotherapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs roughly 480 people and reported revenue of $612 million in 2022. The company's shares trade on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker ARDB. Analysts at Fenwick Capital Partners estimate the deal could add 4 percent to Arden's annual revenue by 2025.

The boards of both companies unanimously approved the transaction on Nov 8, 2023. Financial terms were advised by Callan & Reeves, which served as exclusive advisor to Voss Pharmaceuticals.

BOSTON, MA -- June 9, 2023 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating vandortinib, an experimental oral inhibitor targeting fibroblast growth factor receptor, in patients with advanced cholangiocarcinoma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti and presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology meeting in Chicago, enrolled 142 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and November 2022. Participants received vandortinib 80 milligrams daily for up to 24 weeks. Results showed an objective response rate of 37 percent, compared with 12 percent in the control arm receiving standard chemotherapy. Median progression-free survival reached 8.4 months versus 4.1 months for controls. The most common adverse event was hyperphosphatemia, occurring in 44 percent of treated patients, followed by diarrhea in 29 percent. Three patients discontinued treatment due to grade 4 liver toxicity. Novartis, which licensed the compound from Kyoto-based Astellas Pharma in 2019, funded the trial with a grant of 18 million dollars. Dr. Marchetti stated that the findings support advancing vandortinib into a Phase 3 registrational study expected to begin enrollment in early 2024. The research team plans to submit full results to the New England Journal of Medicine later this year. Massachusetts General Hospital is headquartered in Boston and affiliated with Harvard Medical School. Novartis is headquartered in Basel, Switzerland.

BOSTON, MA -- November 4, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tacrolimus-XR, an extended-release immunosuppressant developed by Cambridge-based Solenza Therapeutics, for prevention of transplant rejection in patients with chronic kidney disease. The 14-month study, led by Dr. Priya Anand, enrolled 212 adult participants across three sites, including Brigham and Women's Hospital and Cleveland Clinic. Patients receiving tacrolimus-XR showed a 38 percent reduction in acute rejection episodes compared to the standard-of-care regimen, with results published in The New England Journal of Medicine on November 2, 2023. Dr. Anand stated that the therapy also reduced incidence of post-transplant diabetes mellitus, a common complication linked to older calcineurin inhibitors. Solenza Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by biochemist Marcus Feld, raised $45 million in Series C funding earlier this year to support a planned Phase 3 trial expected to begin in March 2024 at sites in Chicago and Toronto. The company's chief medical officer, Dr. Elena Ruiz, presented the findings at the American Society of Nephrology's annual meeting in Philadelphia on November 3, 2023. Analysts at Kessler Bio Partners noted that if approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, tacrolimus-XR could compete directly with Astellas Pharma's Prograf in a market estimated at $2.1 billion annually. Solenza shares rose 12 percent following the announcement. The company plans to submit a New Drug Application by late 2025, pending additional safety data from the ongoing extension study.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. HG-24-1187541

On November 6, 2024, Judge Marion Castellano presided over the sentencing hearing for defendantRaymond Ostrowski, 41, former controller at Bellhaven Logistics Inc., a freight company headquartered in Oakland, California. Ostrowski pleaded guilty on August 19, 2024, to one count of wire fraud and one count of embezzlement after prosecutor Denise Whitfield of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office established that he diverted $612,000 from company accounts between March 2021 and February 2023 to fund purchases of a 2019 Porsche Cayenne and a condominium in Truckee.

Judge Castellano sentenced Ostrowski to 46 months in state prison and ordered restitution of $612,000 to Bellhaven Logistics Inc., payable within five years. Defense attorney Harold Ngo argued for a reduced term, citing his client's lack of prior record, but the court noted the extended duration of the scheme as an aggravating factor.

Bellhaven Logistics Inc., founded in 2005 by Theodore Bellhaven, discovered the discrepancies during an internal audit conducted by Ferris & Voss Accounting in January 2023 and terminated Ostrowski's employment the same month. The company's chief executive, Priya Anand, said in a statement that Bellhaven has since implemented new controls, including dual-signature approval for transfers exceeding $10,000.

Ostrowski is scheduled to report to Santa Rita Jail on November 20, 2024, before transfer to a state facility.

BOSTON, MA - September 12, 2023 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolebrutinib, an oral chemical compound targeting Bruton's tyrosine kinase, in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti and presented at the European Committee for Treatment and Research in Multiple Sclerosis meeting in Milan, Italy, enrolled 218 participants across 14 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and June 2022. Results showed a 34 percent reduction in annualized relapse rate compared to placebo, with 62 percent of treated patients remaining relapse-free at 96 weeks. Sanofi, the French pharmaceutical company that funded the trial, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2024. Dr. Marchetti noted that three patients experienced elevated liver enzymes, though none developed serious hepatic disease requiring discontinuation. The trial also tracked biomarkers including neurofilament light chain, which decreased by 21 percent in the treatment arm. Sanofi's chief medical officer, Dr. Rajesh Patel, stated the company would invest $180 million to expand manufacturing capacity at its Framingham, Massachusetts facility to prepare for potential commercial launch. The findings were published in The Lancet Neurology on September 14, 2023. Patient advocacy groups, including the National Multiple Sclerosis Society, welcomed the results but called for longer-term safety data before widespread adoption.

CHICAGO, March 4, 2024 -- Meridian Foods Corporation announced today that it has acquired Brightleaf Organics LLC, a privately held maker of plant-based snacks based in Portland, for $142 million in cash. The transaction closed on March 1, 2024.

Under the agreement, Brightleaf Organics will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Foods, retaining its Portland manufacturing facility on Sandy Boulevard and its 210 employees. Brightleaf's founder and chief executive officer, Renata Kowalski, will join Meridian Foods as Senior Vice President of Innovation, reporting directly to Meridian CEO Douglas Farrow.

"This acquisition strengthens our position in the fast-growing plant-based category," said Farrow, who has led Meridian Foods since 2019. "Renata and her team have built something remarkable, and we intend to scale it nationally."

Brightleaf Organics was founded in 2016 in Portland and has grown its flagship product, GreenSprout Chips, into a $60 million annual brand sold in over 4,000 stores across the United States. Meridian Foods, headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, reported $3.8 billion in revenue last year and employs roughly 9,500 people worldwide.

The deal was financed through a combination of cash reserves and a $75 million credit facility arranged by Northbridge Capital Partners. Meridian Foods expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive to earnings and plans to expand GreenSprout Chips into Canada by the fourth quarter of 2024.

Pixelworks Labs unveiled the Aurora Fold 3, its third-generation folding smartphone, at a press event in San Jose on October 9, 2024. Priced at $1,799, the device runs on the company's own Halcyon 2 chipset, a departure from the Qualcomm processors used in the Aurora Fold 2. I spent eleven days testing a review unit loaned by Pixelworks Labs, and the improvements are noticeable, if incremental.

The 7.8-inch inner display now hits 2,000 nits of peak brightness, a 25% jump over last year's model, and the crease down the middle is barely visible under normal lighting. Battery life impressed me most: a 5,200mAh cell delivered just over 14 hours of mixed use, beating the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 5 in my informal tests. Software support is generous too, with Pixelworks Labs promising five years of Android updates.

Not everything works. The under-display camera still produces soft, slightly hazy selfies, and the hinge mechanism, while smoother than the Aurora Fold 2's, emits an audible click that some colleagues found distracting. At $1,799, it also undercuts Samsung's flagship by $200, which matters given inflation-weary shoppers in 2024.

CEO Marissa Tran said in an interview that Pixelworks Labs plans to double production at its Fremont, California facility by March 2025 to meet demand. If supply keeps pace, the Aurora Fold 3 could be the first folding phone I recommend without hesitation.

Danvers, Massachusetts-based Encore Wireless Corp. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired PixelForge Robotics, a Austin, Texas startup specializing in warehouse automation, for $412 million in cash and stock. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing in Boston, is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending regulatory review.

Encore Wireless Chief Executive Officer Marion Delacroix said the acquisition would strengthen the company's logistics division, which supplies robotics components to retailers including Harlan & Beck Supply Co. "PixelForge's engineering team gives us a five-year head start," Delacroix told reporters.

PixelForge, founded in 2018 by Aditya Rao, employs 340 people and generated $58 million in revenue last year. Rao will join Encore Wireless as Chief Technology Officer starting February 3, 2025, according to a company statement.

Shares of Encore Wireless rose 6.2 percent to $73.40 on the Nasdaq following the announcement, while shares of rival firm Cobalt Robotics Inc. fell 3.1 percent amid concerns over increased competition. Analyst Priya Nair of Summit Capital Partners called the deal "a bold bet on automation," noting that Encore Wireless will pay a premium of roughly 18 percent over PixelForge's most recent private valuation.

The transaction, Encore Wireless's third acquisition since 2022, will be funded partly through a $150 million loan from First Meridian Bank. Encore Wireless expects the integration to be completed by the third quarter of 2025 and projects the deal will add $90 million in annual revenue.

Pixelworks Labs, a Portland-based imaging startup, unveiled its new Aria X1 camera sensor on June 4, 2024, at a press event in San Jose, California. Founded in 2019 by former Sony engineer Marcus Delgado, Pixelworks Labs has spent five years chasing a niche most rivals ignored: low-light video for compact drones. The Aria X1, priced at $349, finally delivers on that promise.

I tested the sensor mounted on a DJI Mavic-class quadcopter over three nights near Lake Tahoe. Even at ISO 12800, footage retained usable detail, a stark improvement over the Sony IMX586 chip Pixelworks previously licensed as a supplier component. Delgado told me in a phone interview on June 10 that the company invested $22 million in R&D over eighteen months, much of it funneled into a proprietary noise-reduction algorithm called ClearNight.

Not everything is perfect. Battery drain increased by roughly 15 percent compared to competing sensors from Omnivision, and the companion app crashed twice during my testing. Pixelworks Labs says a firmware patch is scheduled for July 2024.

Still, for filmmakers and hobbyist drone pilots frustrated with grainy night footage, the Aria X1 is a genuine leap forward. At under $350, it undercuts Omnivision's flagship OV64B, a direct competitor, by nearly $120. If the software issues get resolved, Pixelworks Labs may have just carved out a durable position in a crowded market.

SUPERIOR COURT OF SUFFOLK COUNTY, MASSACHUSETTS

Case No. 24-CR-01187

On Tuesday, June 11, 2024, Judge Patricia Nolan presided over the sentencing hearing of Marcus DeLuca, 41, in a courtroom at the John Adams Courthouse in Boston. DeLuca was convicted last month of embezzlement after prosecutors from the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office, led by Assistant District Attorney Renee Okafor, proved he diverted $2.3 million from his employer, Granite Harbor Logistics, between March 2019 and October 2022. Judge Nolan sentenced DeLuca to seven years in state prison, followed by three years of supervised probation, and ordered restitution of $1.8 million to Granite Harbor Logistics.

Defense attorney Howard Simental argued for leniency, citing DeLuca's cooperation with investigators from the Massachusetts State Police, who arrested him on January 9, 2023, at his home in Quincy on charges of embezzlement and wire fraud. Okafor told the court that DeLuca had used shell accounts at Coastal Trust Bank to funnel company funds into personal real estate purchases in Rhode Island.

Granite Harbor Logistics CEO Simone Kessler issued a statement afterward, saying the company was "relieved that justice was served" and had since implemented new financial controls. The company, headquartered in Braintree, Massachusetts, employs roughly 340 people.

DeLuca has ten days to file an appeal with the Massachusetts Appeals Court.

HARTFORD, Conn. — Meridian Rail Corp. announced Tuesday that it will acquire Bridgeport Freight Systems for $412 million, creating one of the largest regional rail operators in the Northeast. The deal, unveiled at a press conference at Meridian's Hartford headquarters, is expected to close by March 15, 2025, pending approval from the Surface Transportation Board.

CEO Denise Hartwell said the acquisition would let Meridian expand service between Connecticut and New Jersey, adding roughly 340 miles of track and 1,200 employees to its network. "This is about building a more resilient supply chain for the entire Northeast corridor," Hartwell told reporters.

Bridgeport Freight, founded in 1987 by engineer Walter Coons, has struggled financially since 2022, when fuel costs and labor shortages cut into margins. Its current chief executive, Marcus Feldman, will step down once the merger is finalized, according to a company statement released Tuesday afternoon.

Analysts at Sterling Capital Partners estimate the combined company will generate $1.8 billion in annual revenue. Shares of Meridian Rail rose 6 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $54.32.

The deal still requires a vote from Bridgeport's board, scheduled for January 20, 2025. If approved, the merged entity will operate under the Meridian Rail name, with Bridgeport's Newark rail yard becoming a regional hub. Union representatives from the Brotherhood of Railway Workers said they would seek assurances that no jobs would be cut during the transition.

Portland-based Cascade Cycleworks has launched the Cascade Voyager 3, an all-terrain electric bike priced at $2,199, available starting November 4, 2024 through the company's online store. Designed by lead engineer Priya Nandakumar, the Voyager 3 features a 750-watt Bafang motor, a 720Wh removable battery rated for 68 miles per charge, and hydraulic disc brakes manufactured by Tektro. The frame is built from 6061 aluminum and comes in three colors: Slate Gray, Cascade Green, and Matte Black. Cascade Cycleworks, founded in 2016 by former REI product manager Daniel Ostrowski, has sold over 40,000 bikes across North America and competes directly with Rad Power Bikes and Aventon. The Voyager 3 ships fully assembled from the company's Beaverton, Oregon warehouse and includes a 2-year limited warranty covering the motor and battery. Early reviewers, including Bicycling Magazine, praised the bike's torque but noted the 62-pound weight as a drawback for apartment dwellers. Customers who order before November 15, 2024 will receive a free rear cargo rack worth $89. The Voyager 3 is currently listed as new condition and ships within 5 business days of purchase. Cascade Cycleworks accepts returns within 30 days and offers financing through Affirm, with monthly payments as low as $61.

The Ohio Department of Transportation announced on March 14, 2024 that it will begin a $42 million rehabilitation of the Fort Hayes Bridge in Columbus, Ohio, starting April 8, 2024. Director Maria Gonzalez said the project, awarded to contractor Kokosing Construction Company, will replace deteriorated support beams and repave 3.2 miles of roadway on Interstate 71. The bridge, built in 1968, was flagged as structurally deficient following an inspection conducted by ODOT engineer Samuel Okafor last November. Gonzalez stated that lane closures will affect approximately 58,000 daily commuters and urged drivers to use the Broad Street detour during construction hours between 9:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m. Governor Michael DeWine praised the initiative, noting that the state legislature approved the funding through House Bill 23 in December 2023. "This investment protects the safety of every Ohioan who crosses this bridge," DeWine said at a press conference held at the Ohio Statehouse. Federal Highway Administration officials confirmed that $12 million of the total cost will come from federal infrastructure grants, while the remainder will be covered by state transportation funds. The project is expected to conclude by November 2025, according to ODOT spokesperson Rachel Kim. Local business owners near Fifth Avenue expressed concern about reduced foot traffic during construction, though city councilmember James Whitfield said temporary signage and parking incentives would be introduced to mitigate the impact on nearby merchants.

Pixel Fold 2 Review: Google Refines a Rough Idea

Mountain View, California -- On September 12, 2024, Google released the Pixel Fold 2, a $1,799 foldable phone that finally feels like a finished product rather than a prototype. I have used it daily for three weeks, alongside my aging Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 5, and the improvements are obvious.

The hinge, engineered with a South Korean supplier called Hysonic, now closes flush with no gap, and Google claims it survives 300,000 folds. The 7.9-inch inner display, built by Samsung Display, hits 2,000 nits of peak brightness, a big jump from last year's 1,450 nits. Battery life improved too: I averaged 8 hours and 40 minutes of screen-on time, up from roughly 6 hours on the original Pixel Fold.

Rohan Mehta, a hardware reviewer at The Verge, called it "the first fold that doesn't apologize for itself" in a piece published on September 18, 2024. I largely agree, though the $1,799 price still undercuts nobody; Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 6 costs $1,899, and both remain expensive relative to a $799 iPhone 16.

Software is where Google pulls ahead. The Pixel Fold 2 ships with Android 15 and three extra years of guaranteed updates, through 2031. Multitasking gestures, refined by Google's Android team in Mountain View, feel less gimmicky than Samsung's equivalent tools.

My one complaint: the 4,650 mAh battery is only a modest 5 percent larger than its predecessor's, and heavy camera use during a weekend trip to Lake Tahoe drained it by 3 p.m. Still, at roughly 90 percent polish, this is the closest Google has come to making foldables feel ordinary.

Verdict: recommended, with the caveat that most buyers should wait for a price drop.

input: Warrington, England -- December 4, 2024 -- Chesford Automation PLC announced it has acquired Belmont Robotics Ltd, a Manchester-based maker of warehouse picking arms, for 142 million pounds in cash and stock. The deal, disclosed at Chesford's headquarters in Warrington, gives the industrial group full ownership of Belmont's flagship product, the ArmFlex 900 gripper, widely used by logistics firms across the United Kingdom. Chesford's chief executive, Marion Delacourt, said the acquisition would double the company's robotics revenue within two years and strengthen its position against rival Fenmore Systems, which supplies similar equipment to retailers such as Harlow Grocers. Belmont Robotics was founded in 2016 by engineer Priya Nandakumar, who will step down as managing director on January 15, 2025, after a transition period. Nandakumar said she plans to join a university research lab in Leeds. The transaction, funded partly through a 60 million pound loan from Britannia Merchant Bank, is expected to close by February 2025 pending regulatory clearance from the Competition and Markets Authority. Shares in Chesford rose 6.3 percent to 812 pence on the London Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume more than tripled. Analysts at Redwood Capital called the price a fair valuation given Belmont's 38 percent share of the UK's automated picking market. Chesford employs roughly 4,100 people across three facilities in England and Wales, and Delacourt said no layoffs are planned as a result of the merger.

To: Board of Directors, Meridian Foods Corp.
From: Helena Ruiz, Chief Financial Officer
Date: March 14, 2024
Subject: Acquisition of Blue Harbor Seafood Ltd.

Dear Board Members,

I am pleased to report that Meridian Foods Corp. has completed the acquisition of Blue Harbor Seafood Ltd., a seafood distributor headquartered in Halifax, Nova Scotia. The transaction, valued at $42 million, closed on March 12, 2024, following approval from the Canadian Competition Bureau.

Under the agreement, Meridian Foods Corp. purchased all outstanding shares from founder Douglas MacKenzie, who established Blue Harbor Seafood Ltd. in 1997. Mr. MacKenzie will remain as an advisor for six months to ensure a smooth transition. Blue Harbor Seafood Ltd. will now operate as a subsidiary of Meridian Foods Corp. and will retain its 140 employees at the Halifax processing facility.

This acquisition strengthens our position against competitors such as Atlantic Prime Fisheries, particularly in the frozen seafood segment across Eastern Canada. We expect the deal to add approximately $18 million in annual revenue starting in fiscal year 2025.

Additionally, I want to inform the board that Raymond Okafor has been appointed as General Manager of the newly formed subsidiary, effective April 1, 2024. Mr. Okafor previously served as Vice President of Operations at Coastal Fresh Inc. for eight years.

A formal announcement will be made at our shareholder meeting in Toronto on April 5, 2024. Please direct any questions to my office before then.

Sincerely,
Helena Ruiz
Chief Financial Officer
Meridian Foods Corp.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solace Robotics announced this morning it has acquired Ferro Dynamics, a small hydraulics startup based in Denver, Colorado, for $42 million in cash. Deal closed Tuesday, June 10.

2/ Solace CEO Priya Nandakumar said the acquisition will let the company build warehouse robots faster. "Ferro's hydraulic arms are years ahead of anything we had," she told reporters at a press briefing in Austin.

3/ Ferro Dynamics was founded in 2016 by engineer Tomas Reyes, who will now join Solace as VP of Hardware Engineering starting July 1. Reyes previously worked at Boston Dynamics for six years.

4/ Solace, headquartered in Austin, Texas, employs about 340 people. The company was founded in 2014 by Priya Nandakumar and her brother Arjun Nandakumar, who left the firm last year to start a competing venture, Volt Robotics.

5/ Analysts at Meridian Capital say the deal puts Solace in direct competition with Boston-based Kinetic Systems, the current market leader in warehouse automation.

6/ Not everyone's thrilled — about 60 Ferro employees in Denver protested outside the company's offices on Wednesday, worried about layoffs after the merger.

7/ Solace says no layoffs are planned. Full integration is expected by December 2025. Stock for Solace's parent, Halcyon Holdings, rose 4 percent on the news.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solace Robotics Inc. announced this morning that it has acquired local startup FieldSense Analytics for $42 million in cash and stock. Deal closed Tuesday, March 4, 2025.

2/ Solace CEO Priya Nandakumar said the acquisition will let the company add crop-monitoring drones to its existing warehouse-robot lineup. FieldSense founder Marcus Ojeda will join Solace as VP of Agricultural Systems starting April 1.

3/ FieldSense, founded in 2019 in Lubbock, Texas, had raised just $6 million total before this exit. Its 14-person team is relocating to Solace's headquarters in Austin, Texas over the next two months.

4/ Ojeda told me: "We built our first prototype in a garage outside Lubbock. Never imagined we'd sell to a company Priya built from scratch in 2016."

5/ Solace itself was started by Priya Nandakumar and her brother, Arjun Nandakumar, who now serves as CFO. The siblings launched the company with $500,000 in seed funding from a Houston investor.

6/ Industry watchers see this as a direct shot at competitor GreenField Robotics, based in Des Moines, Iowa, which controls roughly 31% of the agri-drone market.

7/ Solace shares aren't public yet, but insiders say a Series C round of $80 million is expected by June 2025. More soon.

SUPERIOR COURT OF SANTA CLARA COUNTY
Case No. 24-CV-198332

On March 14, 2024, Judge Ronald Feasby sentenced Marcus Delgado, 37, of San Jose, California, to 48 months in state prison after a jury in San Jose convicted him of embezzlement from his former employer, Palo Alto-based fintech firm Brightline Capital Inc. Prosecutor Elena Vasquez of the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office argued that Delgado, who worked as a senior accountant at Brightline Capital between January 2019 and September 2023, diverted approximately $1,200,000 from client escrow accounts into a shell entity he controlled, Meridian Holdings LLC.

The trial, held at the Hall of Justice in San Jose, began on February 5, 2024, and lasted nine days. Defense attorney Ruth Okafor contended that Delgado's supervisor, Chief Financial Officer Priya Nathan, had approved the transfers, but jurors rejected the claim after reviewing internal emails presented by Vasquez.

Brightline Capital, founded in 2015 by CEO Warren Kessler, reported the discrepancy to the Securities and Exchange Commission in October 2023, triggering an investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. Delgado was arrested on November 3, 2023, at his home in San Jose by FBI agents on charges of wire fraud and grand theft.

Judge Feasby also ordered Delgado to pay $1,200,000 in restitution to Brightline Capital within five years. Delgado's attorney has indicated plans to appeal the sentence to the California Sixth District Court of Appeal within 60 days.

input: BOSTON, MA -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced on March 14, 2024 the results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tenaprovir, an investigational antiviral chemical developed by Cascade Biopharma Inc., for treatment of chronic hepatitis D. The trial, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar, enrolled 212 patients across seven sites in the United States and Germany between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants received either 150 milligrams of tenaprovir daily or a placebo for 48 weeks. According to results published in the Journal of Hepatology, 61 percent of patients receiving tenaprovir achieved undetectable hepatitis D viral RNA at week 48, compared with 9 percent in the placebo group. Grade 3 adverse events, primarily elevated liver enzymes, occurred in 14 patients. Dr. Nandakumar stated that the findings support advancing tenaprovir into a Phase 3 program, which Cascade Biopharma plans to launch in early 2025 in collaboration with Novartis AG, headquartered in Basel, Switzerland. Cascade Biopharma's chief executive officer, Marcus Feldman, said the company will seek Breakthrough Therapy designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration this summer. The study was funded in part by a $4.2 million grant from the National Institutes of Health. Hepatitis D, caused by the hepatitis D virus, affects an estimated 12 million people worldwide and is considered the most severe form of viral hepatitis, often accelerating progression to cirrhosis. Cascade Biopharma, founded in 2016 and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has raised $180 million in venture funding to date.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Vantage Robotics Inc. announced this morning it has acquired SensorLoop Systems, a Denver-based startup, for $42 million in cash. Deal closed Tuesday, June 11, 2024.

2/ SensorLoop, founded in 2019 by Priya Anand, makes LIDAR modules used in warehouse drones. Anand will join Vantage as VP of Hardware Engineering starting July 1.

3/ Vantage CEO Marcus Feld said in a call with reporters, "This gets us vertical integration on sensing, and it keeps us ahead of Kestrel Dynamics, our biggest competitor in the logistics-robotics space."

4/ Kestrel Dynamics, headquartered in San Jose, California, had reportedly made its own offer for SensorLoop back in March but was rebuffed.

5/ Vantage plans to move roughly 60 SensorLoop employees from their Denver office to Austin over the next quarter, though 15 engineers will stay in Colorado to run a satellite lab.

6/ Analysts at Merrow Capital estimate the deal could boost Vantage's annual revenue by 12 percent once SensorLoop's sensors are integrated into the flagship Vantage Falcon-9X drone.

7/ Vantage shares rose 4.3 percent on the Nasdaq after the announcement Tuesday afternoon.

8/ Anand, a naturalized U.S. citizen originally from Mumbai, said, "I started SensorLoop in my garage with $8,000 in savings. Seeing it become part of a company this size is surreal."

9/ Vantage was itself started in 2016 by Marcus Feld and Dana Whitfield in a small facility in Round Rock, Texas.

CHICAGO, March 4, 2024 -- Meridian Foods Corporation announced today that it has acquired Prairie Valley Organics, a Wisconsin-based producer of organic dairy products, for $142 million in cash. The acquisition, finalized on March 1, 2024, expands Meridian's presence in the natural foods sector across the Midwest.

Under the agreement, Prairie Valley Organics will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Foods Corporation, retaining its headquarters in Eau Claire, Wisconsin, and its 310 employees. Prairie Valley's founder, Karen Nolan, will join Meridian as Senior Vice President of Sustainable Sourcing, effective March 18, 2024.

"This acquisition strengthens our portfolio and reflects consumer demand for organic products," said Thomas Reyes, Chief Executive Officer of Meridian Foods Corporation, in a statement issued from the company's headquarters in Chicago, Illinois. "Karen and her team have built something remarkable over the past 15 years."

Karen Nolan founded Prairie Valley Organics in 2009 and grew the company into a $60 million-revenue business supplying organic milk and cheese to retailers including Fresh Harvest Markets and Union Grocers. Nolan said the deal would allow the brand to expand distribution nationally while preserving its commitment to regenerative farming practices.

Meridian Foods Corporation, a publicly traded company listed on the Nasdaq, reported $2.3 billion in revenue for fiscal year 2023. The company said it expects the transaction to be immediately accretive to earnings. Analysts at Delta Ridge Capital estimated the deal could add 4 percent to Meridian's annual organic food sales within two years.

The transaction is expected to close fully by April 30, 2024, pending routine regulatory review.

Pixel Watch 3, Google's latest wearable, launched on September 10, 2024, at a starting price of $349.99. I tested the 45mm LTE model for three weeks in Austin, Texas, and came away impressed by its battery life, which now stretches to roughly 36 hours under normal use. Google, headquartered in Mountain View, California, credits the improvement to a new low-power display driver co-developed with Samsung Electronics, a longtime supplier for Google's hardware division.

The watch runs Wear OS 5 and integrates tightly with Fitbit, which Google acquired in 2021 for $2.1 billion. During my review period, the heart-rate tracking during a half-marathon in Zilker Park matched a chest-strap monitor within two beats per minute, a notable improvement over the Pixel Watch 2.

Not everything is rosy. The Bluetooth connection dropped twice while I was cycling near Lady Bird Lake, and the crown button occasionally sticks. Sundar Pichai, Google's chief executive officer, mentioned at a company event in Mountain View on September 9, 2024, that wearables remain a priority for the company, noting competition from Apple and its Apple Watch Series 10, released the same month.

At $349.99, the Pixel Watch 3 is not cheap, but the combination of software polish, Fitbit integration, and improved battery life makes it the best Android smartwatch I have used. Samsung's Galaxy Watch 7 remains a close competitor, particularly for users already inside the Samsung ecosystem.

DENVER, June 12 -- Frontier Metals Corp. announced Wednesday that it will acquire Silverline Mining Ltd. in a cash-and-stock deal valued at $740 million, marking one of the largest transactions in the sector this year. Under the agreement, Frontier will pay $28.50 per share, a 22 percent premium over Silverline's closing price on Tuesday.

The combined entity, which will retain the Frontier Metals name and remain headquartered in Denver, Colorado, is expected to produce roughly 1.2 million ounces of silver annually. Silverline, based in Coeur d'Alene, Idaho, operates three mines across Nevada and Montana and employs about 950 workers.

"This acquisition strengthens our position as a leading North American silver producer," said Rebecca Ainsley, Chief Executive Officer of Frontier Metals, during a call with analysts. Ainsley added that the deal, expected to close by September 30, still requires approval from Silverline shareholders and regulators.

Silverline's outgoing CEO, Martin Osei, will step down once the transaction closes and will be succeeded by Frontier's current chief operating officer, Daniel Reyes, who will assume the role of President of the combined company.

Shares of Silverline Mining jumped 18 percent to $27.90 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Frontier Metals shares dipped 3 percent to $61.10. Analysts at Whitmore Capital, a Chicago-based investment bank advising Frontier, called the deal "a rare consolidation opportunity in a fragmented market."

The merger, if approved, would create the third-largest silver mining company in North America by production volume, trailing only Pan American Silver and Hecla Mining.

8/ Congrats to the whole team — huge milestone for robotics in Texas.

Anker's new Solix C1000 portable power station launched on September 12, 2024, and after three weeks of daily use in my Austin, Texas apartment, I'm impressed. Anker Innovations, the Shenzhen-based company founded by Steven Yang in 2011, priced the unit at $649 for the 1,056Wh model, undercutting rival Jackery's comparable Explorer 1000 v2 by roughly $150. The C1000 charges from empty to 80 percent in just 58 minutes using its 1,500W AC input, a figure I verified twice with a Kill A Watt meter. Ben Sullivan, a hardware reviewer at The Verge, called it "the fastest charging power station under $700 I've tested," in an article published on September 18, 2024. During a three-day power outage in my neighborhood caused by a storm that knocked out ERCOT-managed lines on October 2, 2024, the C1000 kept my refrigerator and a CPAP machine running for 31 hours on a single charge. The unit weighs 27.5 pounds, which is noticeable but manageable, and includes a 1,800W pure sine wave inverter. My one complaint: the companion app, built for iOS and Android, disconnects via Bluetooth roughly once a day. Anker says a firmware update addressing this will ship in November 2024. At $649, with a 5-year warranty, the Solix C1000 undercuts Goal Zero's Yeti 1000 Core while offering faster recharge speeds, making it the best value in this category right now.

BOSTON, MA -- November 4, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolerizumab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arcavia Therapeutics, for treatment of moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The 24-week study enrolled 312 adult patients across 18 sites in the United States and Canada, including facilities in Toronto and Chicago. Dr. Helena Ruiz, lead investigator and Professor of Rheumatology at Harvard Medical School, presented findings on November 3, 2023, at the American College of Rheumatology annual meeting held at McCormick Place in Chicago. Patients receiving 150 milligrams of tolerizumab every four weeks showed a 62 percent reduction in disease activity scores compared to 24 percent in the placebo group, a statistically significant difference (p<0.001). The most common adverse event was mild injection-site erythema, reported in 14 percent of participants; no cases of serious infection or malignancy were observed. Arcavia Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by former Genzyme scientist Dr. Marcus Feld, plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial in early 2024 and has secured $85 million in Series C funding led by Northbridge Capital Partners to support the program. Shares of Arcavia's parent company, Velmont Biosciences, rose 9 percent following the announcement. The full results will be published in The New England Journal of Medicine next month. Dr. Ruiz noted that if confirmed in larger trials, tolerizumab could offer a new option for the estimated 1.3 million Americans living with rheumatoid arthritis who do not respond adequately to existing biologic therapies such as adalimumab.
