CAMBRIDGE, Mass., March 4, 2024 -- Arbor Biosciences Inc., a clinical-stage biotechnology company, today announced that it has acquired Nettle Therapeutics Ltd., a privately held gene-editing startup based in Cambridge, United Kingdom, for approximately 420 million dollars in cash and stock.

The acquisition, expected to close by May 15, 2024, will bring Nettle's CRISPR-based platform for treating sickle cell disease under Arbor's ownership. Dr. Elena Marsh, Chief Executive Officer of Arbor Biosciences, said the deal strengthens the company's pipeline in rare genetic disorders.

"Nettle's technology, combined with our manufacturing capacity in Ann Arbor, Michigan, will let us move faster toward patients," Marsh said during a call with investors on Monday.

As part of the transaction, Arbor will appoint Nettle's founder, Dr. Rajiv Anand, as Chief Scientific Officer, effective April 1, 2024. Anand founded Nettle Therapeutics in 2017 and previously worked at GlaxoSmithKline.

Arbor Biosciences, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs roughly 640 people and reported revenue of 310 million dollars in 2023. The company's shares, listed on Nasdaq under the ticker ARBS, rose 6 percent following the announcement.

The transaction has been approved by both companies' boards and is subject to customary regulatory clearance, including review by the UK's Competition and Markets Authority. Financial terms beyond the headline figure were not disclosed. Goldman Sachs advised Arbor Biosciences, while Nettle was represented by J.P. Morgan.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google's Best Wearable Yet

By Marcus Delaney, October 14, 2024

Google launched the Pixel Watch 3 on September 20, 2024, and after three weeks of daily wear in Austin, Texas, I can say it finally closes the gap with the Apple Watch Series 10. The 45mm model I tested costs $399.99 and ships with a redesigned Snapdragon W5 chipset, giving it noticeably snappier navigation than the original Pixel Watch.

Battery life is the headline improvement. Google claims 36 hours on a single charge, and in my testing with always-on display enabled, I consistently hit 30 hours before needing the charger. That's a real upgrade over last year's model, which barely survived a full day.

The brighter 2,000-nit display is easy to read outdoors, even during a midday run along Lady Bird Lake. Fitbit's running coach feature, now deeply integrated since Google's earlier acquisition of Fitbit, offers genuinely useful pacing advice. Sundar Pichai, Google's CEO, called wearables "a key pillar" of the company's hardware strategy during a call with analysts last month.

My main complaint is the price. At $399.99 for the base model and $499.99 for the LTE version, it undercuts the $429 Apple Watch Series 10 by only a small margin, which weakens the value argument against Cupertino-based Apple.

Still, for Android users, the Pixel Watch 3 is the easiest recommendation Google has made in this category. Four stars out of five.

BOSTON, Massachusetts -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced on March 14, 2024 the results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tremelimumab-based combination therapy in patients with advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The study, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar and published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, enrolled 142 participants across seven sites in the United States and Canada between June 2021 and September 2023. Patients received a combination of tremelimumab and gemcitabine administered intravenously every three weeks. According to the report, 38 percent of patients achieved partial response, while median overall survival reached 11.2 months compared with 7.4 months in the historical control group. Grade 3 or higher adverse events, primarily neutropenia and fatigue, occurred in 22 percent of participants. Dr. Nandakumar stated that the findings support further investigation in a Phase 3 trial planned to begin in early 2025. The research was funded by a $4.3 million grant from the National Cancer Institute and supported by AstraZeneca, which supplies tremelimumab under the brand name Imjudo. Co-author Dr. Marcus Feld of the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute noted that pancreatic adenocarcinoma remains one of the deadliest malignancies, with a five-year survival rate below 12 percent. The team plans to present full data at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting in Chicago in June 2024. Massachusetts General Hospital, a teaching affiliate of Harvard Medical School, has conducted oncology research since 1811. Dr. Nandakumar also received the Ellison Young Investigator Award in 2022 from the American Association for Cancer Research in recognition of her work on immunotherapy combinations for gastrointestinal cancers.

BOSTON, MA - March 14, 2024 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tenaprolix, an investigational chemical compound developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Alderin Therapeutics, for the treatment of moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The study, led by Dr. Priya Nakamura, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Germany between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of tenaprolix twice daily showed a 62 percent reduction in disease activity scores compared to 28 percent in the placebo group after 24 weeks. Dr. Nakamura presented the findings on March 13, 2024, at the American College of Rheumatology conference in Chicago. "These results exceeded our expectations," said Nakamura, who serves as Director of Clinical Research at Massachusetts General Hospital. Alderin Therapeutics, founded in 2019 by former Pfizer executive Marcus Holloway, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. The company's shares, which trade under the ticker ALDR, rose 18 percent following the announcement. Novartis, a competitor developing a similar compound, declined to comment. Alderin also disclosed that it had raised $85 million in a Series C funding round led by venture firm Sequoia Capital in January 2024 to support the drug's continued development and eventual commercialization. Common side effects included mild nausea and headache, though no serious adverse events were reported during the trial period.

DETROIT, Mich. — Meridian Motors Inc. announced Tuesday it will acquire Bolt Charging Systems, a Austin-based startup that builds fast-charging hardware for electric vehicles, for $410 million in cash. The deal, confirmed by Meridian CEO Laura Freitag at a press conference at the company's Detroit headquarters, is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval.

Bolt Charging Systems was founded in 2018 by engineer Ravi Malhotra, who will join Meridian as Vice President of Charging Infrastructure once the acquisition closes. "This gives us a real path to compete with Tesla and Rivian on charging speed," Freitag told reporters.

The announcement sent Meridian Motors shares up 6.4 percent on the New York Stock Exchange, closing at $58.20. Analysts at Ashcombe Partners called the deal "a defensive but necessary move," noting that Meridian has lagged competitors in charging network coverage across the United States.

Ravi Malhotra said the 140-person Bolt team will remain in Austin, Texas, at least through 2026. Meridian plans to integrate Bolt's proprietary 350-kilowatt charging technology into its next SUV model, the Meridian Aster, scheduled for release in March 2025.

The transaction marks Meridian's third acquisition in two years, following its 2023 purchase of battery supplier Corvus Energy for $190 million. Meridian, headquartered in Detroit since its founding in 1987, employs roughly 22,000 people worldwide.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solera Robotics announced this morning it acquired Pindrop Dynamics, a 40-person startup building warehouse pallet-lifting arms, for $62 million in cash. Deal closed Tuesday, March 11, 2025.

2/ Solera's CEO, Marissa Kwan, told employees the acquisition will let the company ship its new AutoStack-9 forklift attachment by Q3. "Pindrop's engineers cracked the grip-sensor problem we'd been stuck on for two years," she said.

3/ Pindrop was founded in 2019 by Devon Ashworth and his sister, Priya Ashworth, out of a garage in Round Rock, Texas. They grew it to 40 employees without ever raising venture funding.

4/ Devon Ashworth will join Solera as Vice President of Hardware Engineering starting April 1, 2025, reporting directly to Kwan. Priya Ashworth said she's taking a break before her next venture.

5/ Solera Robotics, headquartered in Austin, Texas, competes directly with Chicago-based Ferrum Logistics Systems, which last month unveiled its own robotic arm, the GraspLine 4.

6/ Analysts at Bramwell Capital estimate Solera's annual revenue will hit $340 million in 2025, up 28 percent, partly because of this deal.

7/ Kwan will present the combined roadmap at the National Robotics Expo in Denver on May 6, 2025. Investors seem thrilled -- Solera shares jumped 9 percent Wednesday.

8/ Congrats to both teams. Huge moment for warehouse automation.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- October 3, 2023 -- Solara Biotech Inc. announced today that it has acquired NeuroPath Diagnostics LLC, a Boston-based developer of AI-driven diagnostic tools for neurodegenerative diseases, for $142 million in cash and stock. The deal, finalized on September 29, 2023, is expected to close by November 15, 2023, pending regulatory approval.

Under the agreement, Solara Biotech will integrate NeuroPath's flagship product, the NeuroScan Analyzer, into its existing portfolio of diagnostic devices used to detect early markers of Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease. Dr. Elena Ruiz, Chief Executive Officer of Solara Biotech, called the acquisition "a transformative step toward earlier detection and better patient outcomes."

As part of the transaction, Marcus Whitfield, founder and former CEO of NeuroPath Diagnostics, will join Solara Biotech as Chief Innovation Officer effective October 16, 2023. Whitfield founded NeuroPath in Cambridge in 2016 and grew the company to 85 employees before the sale.

The combined company, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, will employ approximately 410 people across facilities in Boston and San Diego. Solara Biotech's board of directors, led by Chairman Robert Kessler, approved the deal on September 27, 2023.

Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners estimate the merged entity could generate $310 million in annual revenue by 2025, positioning it as a stronger competitor to Quantis Health Systems in the neurodiagnostics market.

Solara Biotech shares rose 6.4 percent following the announcement on the Nasdaq exchange.

SUPERIOR COURT OF ALAMEDA COUNTY, CALIFORNIA — On October 14, 2024, Judge Priya Ramanathan sentenced Dennis Okafor, 41, to 5 years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of grand theft embezzlement from his former employer, Larkspur Financial Group, headquartered in Oakland, California. Prosecutor Melissa Tran argued that Okafor, who worked as a senior accountant at Larkspur Financial Group from March 2018 until his termination in June 2023, diverted approximately $412,000 in client funds into a personal account at Sutter Community Bank between January 2021 and May 2023. The scheme was discovered during an internal audit ordered by Larkspur's chief financial officer, Wendell Kaczmarek, in July 2023. Okafor was arrested on September 9, 2023, by detectives from the Oakland Police Department at his residence on Fruitvale Avenue. During the two-week trial, which began on September 30, 2024, at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, defense attorney Carla Espinosa maintained that her client had been unaware of irregularities flagged by auditors. The jury deliberated for six hours before returning its verdict on October 3, 2024. In addition to the prison term, Judge Ramanathan ordered Okafor to pay $412,000 in restitution to Larkspur Financial Group. Company spokesperson Ingrid Solheim stated that Larkspur has since implemented new internal controls. Okafor's attorney has indicated she plans to appeal the conviction to the California Court of Appeal within 60 days.

Marisol Andrade (born March 14, 1958, in Porto Alegre, Brazil) is a Brazilian metallurgical engineer and business executive best known for founding Andrade Ligas S.A. in 1989. After earning a degree in metallurgical engineering from the Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul in 1980, she joined Companhia Siderúrgica Nacional as a junior engineer, working there for six years before moving to ArcelorMittal's Brazilian division in 1986. In 1989, Andrade left ArcelorMittal to start Andrade Ligas S.A., a specialty alloys manufacturer headquartered in Porto Alegre, with an initial investment of $120,000. The company grew steadily, and by 2004 it employed over 900 workers and supplied titanium alloys to the aerospace firm Embraer. In 2011, Andrade was appointed president of the Brazilian Metallurgical Society, a position she held until 2016. That same year, she stepped down as chief executive of Andrade Ligas S.A., handing the role to her son, Rafael Andrade, while remaining chairwoman of the board. In 2018, the German conglomerate ThyssenKrupp acquired Andrade Ligas S.A. for approximately $340 million, retaining the Porto Alegre facility and its workforce. For her contributions to industrial development, Andrade received the Ordem do Mérito Industrial from the Brazilian government in Brasília in 2019. She is married to physician Carlos Menezes and has two children. Andrade currently serves on the advisory board of the Instituto de Engenharia de São Paulo and continues to lecture on sustainable metallurgy.

DETROIT, Mich. — Amara Motors Inc. announced Tuesday that it has acquired battery-technology startup VoltCore Systems for $420 million, a deal the automaker says will accelerate production of its upcoming electric pickup, the Amara Ridgeline. The agreement was signed in Detroit on March 11, 2024, and is expected to close by June 2024, pending regulatory approval.

According to CEO Daniel Feldman, the acquisition gives Amara Motors direct control over VoltCore's solid-state battery patents, which the company says can extend vehicle range by 40 percent. "This is the single most important deal in our company's 15-year history," Feldman told reporters at a press conference held at Amara's headquarters in Detroit.

VoltCore Systems, founded in 2018 by engineer Priya Nandakumar, employs roughly 260 people at its facility in Austin, Texas. Nandakumar will join Amara Motors as Chief Technology Officer starting April 1, 2024, according to a company statement.

Shares of Amara Motors rose 8 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of rival automaker Kestrel Auto Group dipped 2 percent. Analyst Rachel Osei of Meridian Capital called the acquisition "a bold bet on vertical integration" in a note to investors.

The deal marks Amara Motors' third acquisition since 2021 and comes as automakers race to secure battery supply chains amid rising demand for electric vehicles. Amara Motors expects the Ridgeline to begin production in early 2025 at its plant in Toledo, Ohio.

Dayforce Logistics, a Memphis-based freight technology firm, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Ridgeline Carrier Systems for $214 million in cash, expanding its footprint in the Midwest trucking sector. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing in Memphis, Tennessee, was confirmed by Dayforce chief executive officer Marcus Whitfield, who said the acquisition would close by January 15, 2025 pending regulatory approval.

Ridgeline Carrier Systems, headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, operates a fleet of roughly 1,200 trucks and employs about 3,400 workers across seven states. Its founder, Diane Kessler, will step down as chief executive officer once the transaction closes, according to a statement released by the company on Wednesday. Kessler, who started Ridgeline in 1998, said she plans to join the board of a nonprofit focused on transportation safety.

Dayforce shares rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.42. Analysts at Bramwell Capital, including senior analyst Priya Nandakumar, called the acquisition "a strong strategic fit" given Ridgeline's presence in the Ohio Valley corridor. Rival firm Continental Freight Partners, based in Chicago, Illinois, declined to comment on whether it would pursue a competing bid.

The combined company, to be renamed Dayforce Ridgeline Holdings, expects annual revenue of $1.8 billion once the merger is finalized. Whitfield added that no layoffs are planned and that Kessler would receive a transition bonus of $4.5 million as part of the agreement.

Marguerite Okonjo-Delacroix (born 14 March 1958 in Lagos, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-French biochemist known for her pioneering research on malaria vaccines. She earned her doctorate in molecular biology from the University of Lyon in 1984 and moved to Geneva, Switzerland the following year to join the Institut Pasteur as a research fellow. In 1991, Okonjo-Delacroix co-founded BioNexa Therapeutics in Basel with her longtime collaborator Dr. Henrik Sund, serving as Chief Scientific Officer for over two decades. Under her leadership, BioNexa developed the antimalarial compound Feverex, which received regulatory approval from the European Medicines Agency in 2006. She stepped down as Chief Scientific Officer in September 2014 to become a professor at the University of Geneva, a position she held until her retirement in 2021. In 2009, Okonjo-Delacroix received the Pasteur Medal from the Institut Pasteur in Paris for her contributions to tropical disease research. She married French virologist Etienne Delacroix in 1987, and the couple had two children, Amara and Julien. Novartis acquired BioNexa Therapeutics for 340 million euros in 2016, a deal that made headlines across the pharmaceutical industry. Okonjo-Delacroix continues to serve as an advisor to the World Health Organization on malaria eradication programs and currently resides in Geneva. She holds citizenship in both Nigeria and France.

Lenovo formally launched the ThinkPad X1 Fold Gen 4 on September 12, 2024, during a press event at its facility in Morrisville, North Carolina. Priced at $2,899, the foldable laptop features a 16.3-inch OLED display made by LG Display and runs on a Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite processor. I spent three weeks testing a review unit supplied by Lenovo's public relations team, and the experience left me impressed but cautious.

The fold mechanism, engineered by a team led by Vice President of Design Tom Butler, held up through roughly 400 open-close cycles without noticeable wear. Battery life reached 11 hours in mixed use, a genuine improvement over the Gen 3 model released in 2022. Windows 11 adapts reasonably well to the tri-fold form factor, though several third-party apps, including Slack and Spotify, rendered awkwardly when the screen was folded into a 90-degree tent mode.

At Lenovo's investor call on September 18, 2024, CFO Wai Ming Wong told analysts in Beijing that foldable devices now account for 4 percent of the company's PC revenue, up from 1 percent in 2021. Competitor Samsung, headquartered in Suwon, South Korea, is expected to respond with an updated Galaxy Book Fold in early 2025.

Despite the $2,899 price tag, which will limit mainstream adoption, the X1 Fold Gen 4 represents a meaningful step toward practical foldable computing. For creative professionals who need a large screen on the go, it's a compelling, if expensive, option.

Pixelworks Labs, a design studio based in Portland, Oregon, unveiled the Aurex X2 wireless earbuds on March 11, 2024, positioning them as a direct competitor to Sony's WF-1000XM5. Priced at $229, the Aurex X2 promises 38 hours of total battery life with the included charging case and adds real-time language translation for English, Spanish, and Mandarin. I tested a review unit for three weeks around Portland and on a short trip to Seattle, and the results were largely impressive.

Call quality stood out immediately. During a Contact.Communicate-style conference call with a colleague in Chicago, background noise from a coffee shop was almost entirely suppressed. Battery life measured close to claims: 8.5 hours per charge at 70 percent volume, with the case delivering roughly four additional charges. The active noise cancellation, built around a custom chip codenamed Aurex Silent Core, rivals Bose's QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds released last year.

Founder and CEO Marisol Vega, who started Pixelworks Labs in 2019 after leaving Intel, said the company shipped its first 50,000 units within two weeks of launch, generating roughly $11.4 million in revenue. Vega announced on April 2, 2024 that Pixelworks Labs had signed a supply agreement with Foxconn to manufacture components in Shenzhen, China, aiming to fulfill demand ahead of the holiday season.

Minor drawbacks include a companion app that occasionally fails to sync equalizer presets and a case that scuffs easily. Still, at $229, the Aurex X2 undercuts many premium rivals while matching their performance, making it one of the more compelling audio launches of 2024.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City extended its unbeaten run in the Premier League to nine matches on Saturday, defeating Everton 3-1 at the Etihad Stadium in front of 53,412 spectators. Rodri opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a curling strike from outside the box, before Erling Haaland doubled the lead in the 41st minute, converting a penalty after Jarrad Branthwaite was penalized for a handball. Everton pulled one back through Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 58th minute, but Phil Foden restored City's two-goal cushion in the 76th minute with a low finish from Kevin De Bruyne's pass.

Manager Pep Guardiola praised his squad's composure after the match, telling reporters, "We controlled the tempo for large stretches, and Erling's penalty was the turning point." Everton manager Sean Dyche acknowledged the defeat, saying his side struggled to contain De Bruyne in midfield.

The win moved City to 22 points after eight games, three points clear of second-placed Liverpool, who defeated Brentford 2-0 earlier in the day at Anfield. City's next fixture is scheduled for October 21 against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium, a match that could further shape the title race.

Haaland's goal was his eleventh of the season across all competitions, extending his lead atop the Premier League scoring charts. City captain Kyle Walker was substituted in the 80th minute due to a minor hamstring issue, according to the club's medical staff.

To: Board of Directors, Meridian Robotics Inc.
From: Sandra Kaplan, Chief Financial Officer
Date: March 11, 2024
Re: Acquisition of NovaGrip Systems and Executive Transition

Dear Board Members,

I am writing to confirm that Meridian Robotics Inc., headquartered in Austin, Texas, completed its acquisition of NovaGrip Systems, a privately held gripper-technology firm based in Eindhoven, Netherlands, for 42 million dollars on March 8, 2024. The transaction was finalized after a six-week due diligence period led by our legal counsel at Ferris & Wallace LLP.

As part of the transition, Dr. Elena Vasquez, NovaGrip's founder and former Chief Executive Officer, will step down from her position effective March 31, 2024. In her place, Meridian's board has appointed Rajiv Menon as President of the newly formed NovaGrip division, effective April 1, 2024. Mr. Menon previously served as Vice President of Engineering at Boston Dynamics for seven years.

We expect the integration to be completed by September 2024, at which point NovaGrip Systems will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Robotics Inc. The combined entity will compete directly with Universal Robots in the industrial automation market.

Additionally, I want to note that Dr. Vasquez will receive a one-time payment of 3.5 million dollars as part of her severance agreement, to be transferred by April 15, 2024.

Please let me know if you have questions before our next board meeting, scheduled for March 20, 2024, in our Austin headquarters.

Best regards,
Sandra Kaplan
Chief Financial Officer
Meridian Robotics Inc.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 - Cardsworth United edged Riverton FC 2-1 at Whitcombe Park on Saturday, moving into second place in the Northern Premier League table. Midfielder Daniel Osei scored twice for Cardsworth, including a 78th-minute winner set up by captain Marcus Feld. Riverton's lone goal came from striker Tomas Vlk in the 34th minute.

The victory extended Cardsworth's unbeaten run to seven matches under head coach Helena Brandt, who took charge of the club in June 2022. "We showed real character after conceding first," Brandt told reporters at the post-match press conference. "Daniel's movement in the box was the difference tonight."

About 8,500 supporters attended the match, with roughly 400 Riverton fans making the 95-mile trip from their home ground in Deanshire. Riverton manager Colin Pratt admitted his side struggled defensively, saying his team conceded soft goals against a well-organized opponent.

Cardsworth United, owned by Northgate Sports Group, will next travel to face league leaders Ashfield Rovers on October 21 at Ashfield Stadium. A win there would lift them to the top of the table for the first time since March 2021. Osei, who joined Cardsworth from Deanshire Athletic for a fee of £1.2 million in July 2021, has now scored 11 goals this season, making him the league's second-highest scorer behind Ashfield's Pierre Nkomo, who has 13.

Pixelworks Labs unveiled the Aria S3 wireless earbuds on March 4, 2024, at a launch event in Austin, Texas, and I have spent three weeks testing them. Priced at $179, the Aria S3 targets commuters who want active noise cancellation without the $299 price tag of Sony's WH-1000XM5 competitor set. Founded in 2016 by Maria Kessler, Pixelworks Labs is headquartered in San Jose, California, and has grown to 340 employees. Kessler, who now serves as Chief Executive Officer, told reporters at the Austin event that the Aria S3 uses a custom chip called Aria Silicon 2 to cut battery drain during noise cancellation. In my tests, the earbuds lasted 7.5 hours per charge with ANC enabled, beating the company's own claim of 7 hours. Call quality was clear on a windy afternoon in Austin, though bass response felt thin compared to the WH-1000XM5. The companion app, built for iOS and Android, is straightforward but occasionally failed to save custom equalizer profiles during my review period. Pixelworks Labs also announced that Best Buy will carry the Aria S3 starting April 15, 2024, with an exclusive matte green colorway. At $179, the Aria S3 undercuts most premium ANC earbuds while delivering roughly 85 percent of the noise cancellation performance of pricier rivals. For anyone who splits time between transit and open offices, the Aria S3 is a genuinely strong value, and I recommend it without hesitation.

DETROIT, Mich. — Meridian Motors Corporation announced Tuesday it will acquire Chicago-based battery startup VoltCore Technologies for $740 million, a deal executives say will accelerate the automaker's push into electric vehicles. CEO Diane Kessler said the acquisition, expected to close by December 15, 2024, will give Meridian control of VoltCore's solid-state battery patents and its 320-employee research facility in Naperville, Illinois. "This positions us to compete directly with Tesla and Rivian in the next-generation EV market," Kessler told reporters during a press conference at Meridian's headquarters in Detroit. VoltCore founder and CEO Raj Patel will join Meridian as Chief Technology Officer, effective January 6, 2025, according to a joint statement released by both companies. Patel founded VoltCore in 2016 after leaving a research post at MIT, and the company has since grown to 320 employees. Shares of Meridian Motors rose 8 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of VoltCore, which had been preparing for an IPO, were unaffected since the company remains privately held. Analysts at Fairbank Capital noted the deal marks the third major EV-related acquisition by a legacy automaker this year, following similar moves by Ford Motor Company and General Motors. The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which is expected to review the merger for antitrust concerns over the next 90 days. If approved, the combined entity will employ more than 42,000 people across twelve states.

HARTFORD, Conn. — Meridian Health Systems announced Tuesday it will acquire St. Vincent's Regional Hospital for $340 million, expanding its network across Connecticut and Rhode Island. Meridian CEO Patricia Alvarez said the deal, expected to close by January 15, 2025, will add 480 beds and roughly 2,200 employees to the company's roster. St. Vincent's has operated in Bridgeport since 1962 and was previously owned by the nonprofit Sisters of Charity Foundation. The transaction still requires approval from Connecticut's Office of Health Strategy, which is expected to review the filing next month. Dr. Raymond Kessler, Meridian's chief medical officer, said the merger would allow the combined system to expand cardiac and oncology services across the region. Shares of Meridian Health Systems rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.12. Analysts at Fenwick Capital Partners called the acquisition "a significant consolidation move" in an increasingly competitive Northeast hospital market, noting rival Hartford Regional Medical Group has also pursued expansion this year. Governor Elena Ruiz released a statement Wednesday urging regulators to ensure the merger does not reduce access to care for low-income patients in Bridgeport. St. Vincent's board chairman, Thomas Whitfield, said in a press conference that employees would receive continued benefits through 2026. The deal marks Meridian's third acquisition since 2020, following its purchase of Fairfield Community Clinic in 2021.

To: Board of Directors, Halloran Instruments Inc.
From: Priya Nandakumar, Chief Financial Officer
Date: March 14, 2024
Re: Acquisition of Vantage Sensor Technologies

Dear Board Members,

I am pleased to confirm that Halloran Instruments Inc. has completed the acquisition of Vantage Sensor Technologies, based in Ann Arbor, Michigan, for a total price of $42 million in cash. The deal closed on March 12, 2024, following a three-month due diligence process led by our outside counsel at Bregman & Watts LLP.

Vantage's founder, Dr. Marcus Yellen, will join Halloran as Vice President of Product Engineering effective April 1, 2024, reporting directly to CEO Elena Vasquez. Dr. Yellen founded Vantage in 2016 and grew the company to 85 employees before this transaction. He will be based at our Chicago, Illinois headquarters, though he will retain an office in Ann Arbor for the transition period.

As part of the agreement, Halloran will assume Vantage's outstanding supply contract with Kessler Optics GmbH, a German manufacturer that has supplied specialized lens components to Vantage since 2019. We expect this relationship to continue uninterrupted.

Separately, I want to note that Halloran's stock rose 6 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, reflecting strong investor confidence in the deal. We anticipate the acquisition will add approximately $18 million in annual revenue starting in fiscal year 2025.

A joint press conference is scheduled for March 20, 2024, at the Chicago headquarters, where Ms. Vasquez and Dr. Yellen will address employees and media together.

Please reach out with any questions before our next board meeting on March 28, 2024.

Sincerely,
Priya Nandakumar
Chief Financial Officer, Halloran Instruments Inc.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solara Robotics announced this morning it has acquired Pecan Street Sensors for $42 million in cash and stock. The deal closed Tuesday, June 11, 2024, according to CEO Marisol Nguyen.

2/ Pecan Street Sensors, a 6-year-old startup founded by Dr. Ravi Kapoor, makes low-power soil sensors used in precision agriculture across Texas and Oklahoma. Kapoor will join Solara as Chief Technology Officer starting July 1, 2024.

3/ Nguyen told reporters at a press briefing in downtown Austin that Solara plans to integrate Pecan Street's sensor arrays into its flagship irrigation drone, the Solara AgFalcon, by early 2025.

4/ Solara Robotics, headquartered in Austin, Texas, was itself founded in 2018 by Nguyen and her brother, Diego Nguyen, who now serves as COO. The company employs about 310 people.

5/ Analysts see this as a direct shot at competitor GreenField Dynamics, based in Fresno, California, which controls roughly 28 percent of the ag-tech sensor market.

6/ Solara's board, chaired by former Texas Instruments executive Harold Weiss, approved the acquisition unanimously on June 5, 2024.

7/ Shares of Solara's parent company, Meridian AgTech Holdings, rose 4.3 percent Wednesday on the Nasdaq after the announcement.

8/ Kapoor said in a statement, "I'm proud of what our 40-person team built, and I'm excited to keep building at Solara."

Sonos launched the Ace Pro headphones on March 11, 2024, in Santa Barbara, California, positioning them as a $499 challenger to the Bose QuietComfort Ultra. I tested a review unit for three weeks and came away impressed by the active noise cancellation, though the companion app still feels unfinished. Reviewer Priya Nathan, who leads audio testing at Wirecutter, noted that battery life reached 27 hours in her lab trials, slightly below the 30 hours Sonos advertises. The Ace Pro uses a new Qualcomm S7 Pro chip, which Sonos licensed rather than built in-house, and supports Bluetooth 5.3 alongside a wired USB-C lossless mode. At $499, the Ace Pro sits above Sony's WH-1000XM5 ($399) and undercuts the Apple AirPods Max ($549). Sonos CEO Patrick Spence said during a briefing in San Francisco on March 12 that the company plans to ship 2 million units by the end of 2024, aiming to offset slower speaker sales. Sonos, headquartered in Santa Barbara, acquired the audio startup Mayht in 2022 to bolster its driver technology, and engineers from that team reportedly contributed to the Ace Pro's transducer design. Build quality is excellent, with a stainless-steel headband and vegan leather earcups, but the case is bulkier than competitors'. Software bugs, including intermittent Bluetooth dropouts on Android 14 devices, remain a concern a full month after launch. Despite that, for anyone already inside the Sonos ecosystem, the Ace Pro is a compelling, if pricey, first attempt at headphones.

Marguerite Okonkwo (born 14 March 1958) is a Nigerian-British structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques adopted across West African construction. Born in Enugu, Nigeria, she moved to London in 1979 to study at Imperial College London, earning a degree in Civil Engineering in 1983. In 1991 she joined Ove Arup & Partners as a junior engineer, rising to Principal Engineer by 1999. Okonkwo left Arup in 2004 to found Terra Firma Structural Consultants, headquartered in Lagos, Nigeria, with a satellite office opened in Bristol in 2011. Under her leadership, Terra Firma designed the retrofit of the Balogun Central Market in Lagos following a partial collapse in 2007 that injured 14 people. She testified before the Lagos State Building Control Agency in 2008 regarding construction standards, work that contributed to the passage of the Lagos State Building Control Law of 2010. In 2015, Okonkwo received the Royal Academy of Engineering's Africa Prize for Engineering Innovation, awarded in London for her low-cost retrofit system now used in over 300 buildings. She married architect Femi Adeyemi in 1996, and the couple's daughter, Ada Adeyemi, was born in 1998 and now works as a structural analyst at Terra Firma. Okonkwo retired from active practice in 2021 but remains a visiting professor at the University of Lagos, where she lectures on earthquake-resistant design.

law: Lagos State Building Control Law of 2010

input: BOSTON, MA -- May 14, 2024 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating veltuzimab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arcadia Therapeutics, for treatment of relapsed multiple myeloma. The trial, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Germany between January 2022 and September 2023. According to findings published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, 61 percent of patients receiving veltuzimab achieved a complete response within six months, compared with 23 percent in the control group receiving standard bortezomib therapy. The most common adverse event was neutropenia, reported in 18 percent of participants, while three patients discontinued treatment due to severe cytokine release syndrome. Arcadia Therapeutics' chief executive, Mark Feldstein, stated that the company plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. The trial was funded in part by a $42 million grant from the National Institutes of Health. Dr. Nandakumar noted that veltuzimab's novel mechanism, which targets the BCMA protein on malignant plasma cells, could offer a critical option for patients who have failed at least three prior lines of therapy. Arcadia Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by former Genentech scientist Dr. Elena Ruiz, was acquired by Novartis in March 2023 for an undisclosed sum, though it continues to operate as an independent subsidiary headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Additional data will be presented at the American Society of Hematology annual meeting in San Diego this December.

event: American Society of Hematology annual meeting

input: DETROIT, Sept. 12 -- Michigan-based auto parts supplier Ionic Drivetrain Inc. announced Tuesday that it has acquired rival component maker Bracewell Axle Corp. for $214 million in a cash-and-stock deal aimed at expanding its electric vehicle supply chain. The transaction, unveiled at a press briefing at Ionic's Detroit headquarters, is expected to close by November 30 pending regulatory approval. Ionic Chief Executive Officer Rosalind Vance said the acquisition would allow the company to double production of axle assemblies for electric trucks at its plant in Toledo, Ohio. "This deal positions Ionic to compete directly with Bergman Powertrain for contracts with Ford Motor Company and General Motors," Vance told reporters. Bracewell Axle, founded in 1987 by engineer Terrence Okafor, employs roughly 1,300 workers across two facilities in Ohio and Indiana. Okafor, who serves as Bracewell's president, will join Ionic's board of directors as part of the agreement. Shares of Ionic Drivetrain rose 6.4 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $38.12. Analyst Priya Chandrasekaran of Meridian Capital Partners called the deal "a smart bet on the EV supply chain," noting that Bracewell's patented lightweight axle technology could cut vehicle weight by up to 40 kilograms. The merger still requires clearance from the Federal Trade Commission, which is reviewing similar consolidation across the auto supply sector. Ionic expects the combined company to generate $1.1 billion in annual revenue by 2026.

The Ohio Department of Natural Resources announced on March 11, 2024, that it will invest $42 million to restore wetlands along the Maumee River near Toledo, Ohio. Director Mary Mertz stated that the funding, allocated through the state's Clean Water Initiative, will support 15 restoration projects over the next three years. The announcement was made at a press conference at the Toledo Zoo, attended by Lucas County Commissioner Pete Gerken and representatives from the Nature Conservancy. Mertz said the wetlands act as a natural filter, reducing phosphorus runoff that has contributed to harmful algal blooms in Lake Erie. In 2023, a similar bloom forced the temporary shutdown of a water treatment plant serving roughly 500,000 residents. The Ohio Environmental Protection Agency will oversee compliance, with quarterly reports due starting July 1, 2024. Governor Mike DeWine, who signed the appropriations bill in December 2023, praised the initiative as a model for other Great Lakes states. Construction on the first project, a 200-acre marsh restoration near Oak Openings Preserve, is scheduled to begin on April 8, 2024, and is expected to create roughly 60 temporary jobs. Officials from the Nature Conservancy will meet with ODNR staff again on May 2, 2024, in Columbus to finalize site selection for the remaining fourteen projects.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solvex Robotics announced this morning that it has acquired Ferrotech Dynamics for $42 million in an all-cash deal. The acquisition closes on March 18, 2024, pending routine regulatory review.

2/ Solvex CEO Priya Nandakumar said the deal will let the company fold Ferrotech's warehouse-automation arms into its existing product line, the SolvexArm X9, which ships to distribution centers across Texas and Ohio.

3/ Ferrotech Dynamics was founded in 2016 by Marcus Ojeda, who will stay on as Chief Technology Officer at Solvex under the new arrangement. Ojeda posted on his own account: "Proud of what we built. Excited for what's next."

4/ The two companies actually competed directly for a $9 million contract with Meridian Logistics last year, which makes this merger a bit of a plot twist for industry watchers.

5/ Solvex, headquartered in Austin, Texas, employs roughly 640 people and plans to hire an additional 120 engineers by the end of 2024, according to spokesperson Diane Kessler.

6/ Meanwhile, shareholders should note: Ferrotech's remaining assets, including a 30,000-square-foot facility in Denver, Colorado, were not part of the sale and will reportedly be liquidated separately by June 2024.

7/ Analysts at Bramwell Capital rate this a net positive, citing a projected 14 percent boost to Solvex's automation revenue by fiscal year 2025.

On March 11, 2024, Judge Patricia Ruvalcaba sentenced Darnell Ostrowski, 41, to 36 months in state prison after a jury convicted him of grand theft and embezzlement in connection with his former position as Chief Financial Officer of Meridian Freight Solutions, a logistics company headquartered in Oakland, California. Prosecutor Elena Cho of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Ostrowski diverted approximately $1,240,000 from company accounts between January 2021 and September 2023, funneling the funds through a shell entity called Coastal Ventures LLC.

Ostrowski was arrested on October 4, 2023, by detectives from the Oakland Police Department after an internal audit by Meridian Freight Solutions flagged irregular wire transfers. He was charged on November 15, 2023, with three counts of embezzlement and one count of grand theft. The trial, held at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, began on February 5, 2024, and concluded on March 1, 2024, when the jury returned its verdict.

Defense attorney Marcus Whitfield stated his client intends to appeal the sentence. Meridian Freight Solutions CEO Theresa Nakamura told reporters the company has since implemented new financial controls and thanked the Oakland Police Department for its cooperation. Ostrowski must also pay restitution of $1,240,000 to Meridian Freight Solutions, payable within five years of his release, according to the court order.

input: Fjallraven Kanken Classic Backpack, sold by Backcountry Outfitters of Boulder, Colorado, is now available for $85.00, marking a $10 price drop from its original $95.00 tag ahead of Black Friday on November 29, 2024. This unisex 16-liter daypack, manufactured by Fjallraven AB in Ornskoldsvik, Sweden, features Vinylon F fabric first introduced in 1978 and remains one of the brand's most recognizable products worldwide. The listing includes the Kelp Green colorway, a favorite among University of Colorado Boulder students since the store began stocking it in March 2019. Backcountry Outfitters, founded in 2005 by Marcus Feldman, has grown into a regional retailer with three locations across Colorado, and Feldman still serves as the company's President. Each backpack ships within 2 business days from the Boulder warehouse and includes a 2-year manufacturer's warranty covering zippers and straps. Customers who purchase before December 1, 2024 will also receive a free Fjallraven Kanken keychain, valued at $12.00. Reviewers on the store's website, including longtime customer Dana Whitfield, have praised the bag's durability, with one review noting she has used the same Kanken since 2016 without a single broken zipper. Stock is limited to 240 units this quarter, and Backcountry Outfitters warns that the Kelp Green colorway sold out within 48 hours during last year's Black Friday sale. Orders can be placed online or in-store at 1420 Pearl Street, Boulder.

Charlotte, N.C. — Piedmont Regional Bank confirmed Tuesday that it has agreed to acquire Sumter Community Trust, a smaller lender based in Sumter, South Carolina, for $214 million in cash and stock. The deal, announced at a press conference at Piedmont's headquarters in Charlotte, is expected to close by March 15, 2025, pending approval from the Federal Reserve.

CEO Marcus Ellery said the acquisition would expand Piedmont's footprint into the Carolinas' Midlands region, adding 18 branches and roughly 40,000 customer accounts. "Sumter Community Trust has built something special over 62 years, and we intend to honor that legacy," Ellery told reporters.

Sumter Community Trust's founder, Rita Okafor, who started the bank in 1962 with her late husband, will step down as Chairwoman once the merger completes, according to a company statement. She will be succeeded by Daniel Voss, currently Piedmont's Chief Operating Officer, who will assume the newly created role of Regional President for South Carolina on April 1, 2025.

Analysts at Truist Securities called the deal a sign of continued consolidation among mid-sized Southeastern banks, noting that First Palmetto Bank and Coastal Union Financial completed a similar merger last October. Shares of Piedmont Regional Bank rose 4.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.12.

Regulators are expected to review the transaction over the next 90 days. If approved, the combined institution will manage more than $9.7 billion in assets, making it the fourth-largest bank headquartered in North Carolina.

Nikon officially launched the Zf II mirrorless camera on September 9, 2024, at an event held in Yokohama, Japan. Priced at $2,199 for the body-only configuration, the Zf II targets enthusiasts who want retro styling paired with modern autofocus performance. I spent three weeks testing a review unit supplied by Nikon Corporation, pairing it with the new NIKKOR Z 40mm f/2 lens.

The headline upgrade is a 33-megapixel stacked sensor, borrowed from the Z8, which delivers noticeably faster readout speeds than the original Zf. Continuous shooting now reaches 20 frames per second in electronic shutter mode, up from 14 fps last year. Autofocus tracking, powered by an updated version of Nikon's subject-detection algorithm, locked onto moving cyclists in Yokohama's waterfront district with impressive consistency.

Battery life is rated at roughly 380 shots per charge using the EN-EL15c pack, a modest improvement over its predecessor. Weather sealing feels robust; I shot through a light rainstorm near Minato Mirai without issue.

The Zf II faces stiff competition from the Sony a7C II and the Fujifilm X-T5, both of which undercut Nikon on price. Kenji Watanabe, a product manager at Nikon quoted during the Yokohama launch event, said the company designed the Zf II for photographers who "want tactile dials without sacrificing speed."

My only real complaint is the persistent shutter lag in low light, roughly 40 milliseconds slower than the Z8. For $2,199, though, the Zf II remains one of the more compelling full-frame cameras released in 2024, blending nostalgic design with genuinely useful performance gains.

DETROIT, Mich. — Ferra Automotive Inc. announced Tuesday that it has acquired Bright Volt Systems, a battery technology startup based in Austin, Texas, for $412 million in cash and stock. The deal, disclosed on October 14, 2025, marks Ferra's largest acquisition since it was founded in 1998 by engineer Marcus Doyle.

Under the agreement, Bright Volt Systems will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Ferra Automotive, retaining its 260 employees and its facility in East Austin. Ferra's chief executive officer, Renata Alvarez, said the acquisition will accelerate production of the company's upcoming electric pickup, the Ferra Talon, expected to launch in early 2026.

"Bright Volt's solid-state battery technology gives us a two-year lead over competitors like Halden Motors and Correll EV," Alvarez told reporters during a press briefing in Detroit on Wednesday.

Bright Volt's founder and chief technology officer, Priya Nandakumar, will join Ferra as senior vice president of battery engineering, effective November 3, 2025. She will report directly to Alvarez.

Ferra shares rose 6.8 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $84.50. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners called the deal "a decisive move," though some, including analyst Thomas Reyes, cautioned that integration costs could exceed $50 million over the next eighteen months.

The transaction is expected to close by December 1, 2025, pending regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission.

input: SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF ARIZONA, MARICOPA COUNTY — On October 14, 2024, Judge Renata Aldous sentenced Marcus Delgado, 41, to seven years in state prison after a jury convicted him of aggravated fraud in connection with the collapse of Sonora Capital Partners, a Phoenix-based investment firm he founded in 2016. Prosecutor Elena Whitfield of the Maricopa County Attorney's Office argued that Delgado diverted approximately $3.2 million from client accounts between 2019 and 2022, using shell entities to funnel funds to a private account at Desert Ridge Bank. During the trial, held at the Maricopa County Courthouse in Phoenix, Arizona, witness testimony from former employee Priya Nandakumar detailed how Delgado falsified quarterly statements sent to at least sixty investors. Defense attorney Colin Marsh contended that Delgado's business partner, Harold Ives, bore equal responsibility, but the jury rejected that argument on September 3, 2024, returning a guilty verdict. Judge Aldous also ordered Delgado to pay restitution of $2.8 million to affected investors within five years. Sonora Capital Partners filed for bankruptcy in Phoenix in March 2023, shortly after the Arizona Corporation Commission revoked its operating license. Whitfield told reporters outside the courthouse that the sentence "sends a clear message to anyone contemplating similar schemes in Arizona." Delgado's attorneys have indicated they will appeal the ruling to the Arizona Court of Appeals within thirty days.

DETROIT, Mich. — Automaker Ferren Motors announced Tuesday it will acquire electric-vehicle battery startup VoltaCore Technologies for $740 million, a deal executives say will secure lithium-ion supply for the company's growing EV lineup. The agreement was signed at Ferren's headquarters in Detroit and is expected to close by January 15, 2025.

Ferren Motors CEO Diane Kowalski said the acquisition of VoltaCore, founded in 2018 by engineer Marcus Chen, would give Ferren direct control over battery production currently handled by supplier Nishimura Cell Corp, based in Osaka, Japan. "This is about owning our own future," Kowalski told reporters at a press briefing Tuesday afternoon.

VoltaCore, headquartered in Austin, Texas, employs roughly 1,200 workers and operates a 400,000-square-foot factory that opened in 2021. Chen, who will join Ferren as Chief Battery Officer starting February 1, 2025, said the merger would accelerate production of solid-state cells by three years.

Shares of Ferren Motors rose 6 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Nishimura Cell Corp shares fell 4 percent amid concerns over lost business. Analysts at Bramwell Securities estimate the deal could add $200 million in annual revenue by 2027.

The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which has increased scrutiny of EV industry consolidation since 2023. A decision is expected within 90 days.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Refines Its Wearable, But Battery Life Still Lags

Mountain View, October 12, 2024 -- Google officially launched the Pixel Watch 3 last month, and after three weeks of daily use in San Francisco, I can say it is the company's most polished smartwatch yet. The device, priced at $349 for the 41mm Wi-Fi model, was unveiled by Google at a press event alongside the Pixel 9 lineup on August 13, 2024.

The Pixel Watch 3 runs Wear OS 5 and pairs seamlessly with Pixel phones over Bluetooth. Rick Osterloh, Google's Senior Vice President of Devices and Services, told reporters the new LTPO OLED display reaches 2,000 nits, a 25 percent improvement over last year's model. In my testing, outdoor visibility was excellent even in direct sunlight near the Embarcadero.

Battery life remains the weak point. Google claims up to 24 hours, but with the always-on display enabled I averaged closer to 18 hours, meaning a midday charge is often necessary. By comparison, the Apple Watch Series 10, made by Apple Inc., lasts about the same, so this remains a wash against its main competitor.

Fitbit, a Google subsidiary since its 2019 acquisition, contributes the health-tracking software, including a new Loss of Pulse Detection feature built with input from cardiologists at Stanford Health Care. During review testing, no false emergency alerts triggered.

At $349, the Pixel Watch 3 is a genuine improvement, though anyone hoping for two-day battery life will still be disappointed. Recommended for existing Pixel owners; others may want to wait for Wear OS 6.

Cedar Ridge Robotics, a Boise-based manufacturer of industrial automation arms, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Voss Precision Tooling for $84 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing in Boise, Idaho, will bring Voss's 140 employees under the Cedar Ridge umbrella and expand its footprint into Portland, Oregon, where Voss operates a machining plant.

Cedar Ridge CEO Marisol Vance said the acquisition strengthens the company's supply chain as demand for precision components grows among automakers such as Halden Motors. "Voss has spent thirty years perfecting tolerances we could never match internally," Vance told reporters. "This lets us serve customers faster."

Voss founder Tomas Reyes, who started the company in 1994 in a rented garage outside Portland, will stay on as a senior advisor through March 2025. Reyes said he built Voss after leaving an engineering role at Halden Motors, where he had worked for eleven years.

The transaction, financed partly through a $30 million loan from Sawtooth National Bank, is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending regulatory review. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners estimate the combined company could generate $410 million in annual revenue, up from Cedar Ridge's current $310 million.

Shares of Cedar Ridge, traded privately among investors, were valued at roughly $62 per share following the announcement, according to a note circulated by Meridian Capital analyst Priya Nathan. Cedar Ridge employs 1,200 people across three states and plans to retain all Voss staff.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., March 14, 2024 -- Solara Biotech Inc. announced today that it has acquired Nordheim Diagnostics AS, a Norwegian molecular testing company based in Oslo, for approximately $210 million in cash and stock. The acquisition, expected to close on April 30, 2024, will expand Solara's presence in Europe and strengthen its diagnostics pipeline for early cancer detection.

Under the terms of the agreement, Solara will pay $180 million in cash and issue $30 million in newly created shares to Nordheim's shareholders. Nordheim Diagnostics, founded in 2016 by Dr. Ingrid Solberg, employs 145 people and reported revenue of $42 million last year, driven largely by its flagship product, the ClarityScan platform, used in over 300 hospitals across Scandinavia.

"This acquisition accelerates our mission to make precision diagnostics accessible worldwide," said Marcus Whitfield, Chief Executive Officer of Solara Biotech, speaking at a press briefing in Boston. "Ingrid and her team have built something extraordinary."

Dr. Solberg will join Solara as Senior Vice President of European Operations, effective May 1, 2024, reporting directly to Whitfield. She will remain based in Oslo but will travel frequently to Cambridge for executive meetings.

Solara Biotech, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, was founded in 2011 by Dr. Elena Kaczmarek and currently employs over 1,200 people worldwide. The company's shares trade on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker SLRA. Analysts at Fenwick Capital Partners project the deal will boost Solara's annual revenue by 8 percent within two years.

DETROIT, Mich. — Whirlpool Corporation announced Tuesday it will acquire smart-home startup NestFlow Technologies for $412 million in cash, a move the appliance giant says will accelerate its push into connected kitchen devices. The deal was confirmed by Whirlpool CEO Marc Bitzer during a press conference at the company's headquarters in Benton Harbor, Michigan.

NestFlow, founded in 2019 by engineer Priya Raman, employs 140 people in Austin, Texas, and makes sensor-based refrigeration systems used by several major grocery chains. Raman will join Whirlpool as Vice President of Connected Products starting November 1, according to a company statement.

"This acquisition strengthens our position against competitors like Samsung Electronics and LG Electronics in the smart-appliance market," Bitzer said. Whirlpool shares rose 3.4 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement.

The transaction, expected to close by December 15, still requires approval from federal antitrust regulators. Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimated the deal values NestFlow at roughly 18 times its annual revenue of $22.8 million.

Whirlpool, headquartered in Benton Harbor since 1911, has made four acquisitions in the past decade, including Indesit Company in 2014. The NestFlow purchase marks its first major technology deal since 2020.

Raman, a naturalized American citizen originally from Chennai, India, said she was "thrilled to bring our technology to a global platform." She will report directly to Bitzer and relocate part of her team to Benton Harbor in early 2025.

Bergen Outfitters, headquartered in Portland, Oregon, has launched the Cascade 40L Trail Backpack, a rugged pack built for multi-day hikes. Priced at $189.99, the Cascade 40L is currently in stock and ships new from the company's warehouse in Beaverton. Designed by lead engineer Priya Nandakumar, the pack features a ripstop nylon shell, an aluminum internal frame, and a 3-liter hydration bladder compatible with most reservoirs. Bergen Outfitters was founded in 2011 by Marcus Feld, who remains the company's CEO, and the firm has since grown into a competitor of Seattle-based Alpine Ridge Gear. On September 14, 2023, Bergen Outfitters unveiled the Cascade 40L at the Portland Outdoor Expo, drawing roughly 3,000 attendees. The pack weighs 2.1 kilograms and includes 6 external pockets, a padded hip belt, and a rain cover stored in a zippered base compartment. Customer reviews praise its durability on the Pacific Crest Trail, where beta testers logged over 200 miles this summer. Bergen Outfitters offers a 5-year warranty and free returns within 90 days of purchase. The Cascade 40L is available in three colors: Slate Gray, Forest Green, and Rust Orange. Orders placed before 2:00 PM Pacific Time ship the same day via FedEx Ground. For bulk orders exceeding 50 units, contact the sales department directly. With this release, Bergen Outfitters aims to capture a larger share of the Pacific Northwest outdoor retail market ahead of the holiday season.

The People of the State of California v. Marcus T. Delaney

On Tuesday, March 11, 2025, Judge Renata Sifuentes convened a sentencing hearing at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, California. Defendant Marcus T. Delaney, 41, appeared with his attorney, Priya Nandakumar of the Alameda County Public Defender's Office. Deputy District Attorney Walter Okafor represented the prosecution.

Delaney had previously pleaded guilty on January 14, 2025, to one count of grand theft under California Penal Code Section 487, stemming from the theft of $62,000 in construction equipment from a warehouse operated by Ferris & Cole Builders in Emeryville on September 3, 2024. Judge Sifuentes sentenced Delaney to two years and six months at Santa Rita Jail, with credit for 94 days already served, and ordered restitution of $62,000 payable to Ferris & Cole Builders within eighteen months.

In a related matter, prosecutors noted that Delaney was arrested by Emeryville Police Department officers on September 10, 2024, after a tip from a former employee, Gregory Ashcombe. No firearm was recovered at the scene. Delaney's attorney indicated that an appeal to the California Court of Appeal, First Appellate District, is unlikely. The court adjourned at 11:42 a.m.

input: MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as Villa defeated Brighton & Hove Albion 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, extending their unbeaten home run to nine matches. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute, converting a low cross from midfielder John McGinn, before Brighton's Danny Welbeck equalized just before halftime with a header from a corner. Villa manager Unai Emery reshuffled his midfield at the break, introducing Youri Tielemans for Douglas Luiz, a change that shifted momentum decisively. Watkins struck again in the 63rd minute, and substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win with a curling effort in the 81st minute in front of 42,000 spectators. The victory lifted Aston Villa to third place in the Premier League table with 20 points from eight games, three points behind leaders Manchester City. Brighton manager Roberto De Zerbi admitted his side had been punished for defensive lapses, telling reporters after the match, "We conceded two soft goals and that decided the game." Emery praised his squad's resilience, noting that Villa had now won six of their last seven league fixtures. The Football Association confirmed that Watkins will be assessed ahead of England's upcoming friendly against Australia at Wembley Stadium on October 17, 2023. Aston Villa's next league fixture is scheduled for October 21 against Bournemouth at Villa Park.

AUSTIN, Texas -- October 14, 2024 -- Meridian Robotics Inc. today announced that it has acquired Vantage Sensor Systems LLC, a privately held maker of industrial lidar components based in Boulder, Colorado, for $86 million in cash. The transaction, expected to close by November 30, 2024, will make Vantage a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian.

Under the agreement, Meridian will pay Vantage's 47 shareholders in a combination of cash and stock. input: Ingrid Baumann (born 12 March 1958 in Graz, Austria) is an Austrian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic retrofitting techniques in alpine infrastructure. She earned her doctorate in civil engineering from ETH Zurich in 1984 and joined Bilfinger AG in Mannheim the following year as a junior design engineer. In 1991, Baumann founded Alpenbau Ingenieure GmbH in Innsbruck, a firm specializing in bridge stabilization and avalanche-resistant construction. Under her leadership as Chief Executive Officer, the company grew to employ 340 people and completed the reinforcement of the Arlberg Pass viaduct in 1999, a project funded with a grant of 14 million euros from the Austrian Ministry of Transport. In 2003, Baumann was elected President of the European Federation of Structural Engineers at a conference held in Lisbon, Portugal, a position she held until stepping down in 2011. She married fellow engineer Rolf Hettinger in 1987, and the couple had two children, Clara and Matthias Hettinger. In 2014, Baumann received the Fritz Leonhardt Prize from the German Society for Civil Engineering in Stuttgart for her contributions to earthquake-resistant design. Alpenbau Ingenieure was acquired by the French conglomerate Vinci SA in March 2018 for an undisclosed sum, after which Baumann retired from active practice. She continues to lecture occasionally at ETH Zurich and lives in Innsbruck.

DENVER, Colorado — Sept. 12, 2024 — Rocky Mountain Freight Corp. announced Thursday it has acquired regional logistics rival Summit Haul Inc. for $214 million in cash, marking the company's largest deal since its founding in 1998. The acquisition, expected to close by Nov. 30, 2024, will add 320 trucks and 1,150 employees to Rocky Mountain Freight's network across Colorado, Utah, and Wyoming.

CEO Martin Alvarez said the deal strengthens the company's position against larger competitor Union Pacific Logistics. "Summit Haul brings a fleet and a customer base that fits perfectly with our expansion plans," Alvarez told reporters at a press briefing in Denver. Summit Haul's founder, Diane Kowalski, will step down as chief executive once the transaction closes and will be replaced by current Rocky Mountain Freight executive Paul Ngata, who will assume the role of President of Summit Haul Operations on Dec. 1, 2024.

Rocky Mountain Freight financed the purchase through a combination of $150 million in senior notes and $64 million in existing cash reserves, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Shares of Rocky Mountain Freight, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker RMFC, rose 6.3 percent to $48.90 following the announcement.

Analysts at Denver-based investment firm Larimer Capital Partners called the acquisition a smart consolidation move in a fragmented trucking industry. "This gives Rocky Mountain Freight nearly 15 percent market share in the Mountain West," said analyst Rebecca Sung. The combined company will be headquartered at Rocky Mountain Freight's existing facility on Wynkoop Street in Denver.

Denver-based Highland Foods Corp. announced Tuesday it has acquired Boulder Creek Snacks LLC, a privately held maker of organic granola bars, for $92 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing in Denver, Colorado, is expected to close by November 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Highland Foods CEO Marion Kessler said the acquisition strengthens the company's presence in the natural-foods segment, where Boulder Creek Snacks has posted double-digit sales growth for three consecutive years. "This transaction gives us immediate scale in a category consumers care deeply about," Kessler told reporters.

Boulder Creek Snacks was founded in 2011 by siblings Rachel Ortiz and David Ortiz in a small kitchen outside Boulder, Colorado. The company now employs 340 people and generates roughly $58 million in annual revenue, according to figures released by Highland Foods.

As part of the transaction, David Ortiz will step down as Chief Executive Officer of Boulder Creek Snacks effective November 15, 2024, while Rachel Ortiz will join Highland Foods as Senior Vice President of Product Innovation starting the same day.

Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners, including senior analyst Thomas Lin, said the deal positions Highland Foods to compete more directly with rival General Mills Inc. in the better-for-you snacking aisle. Shares of Highland Foods, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker HLFD, rose 4.3 percent following the announcement, closing at $61.20.

The transaction marks Highland Foods' third acquisition since 2019 and its largest to date, surpassing the $45 million purchase of Pacific Grain Co. in 2021.

input: Ingrid Vasterling (born March 14, 1958, in Rotterdam, Netherlands) is a Dutch structural engineer and academic best known for developing seismic-retrofit techniques used in bridge construction across Europe. She earned a civil engineering degree from Delft University of Technology in 1981 and completed a doctorate at ETH Zurich in 1986. In 1990 she joined Fugro N.V., headquartered in Leidschendam, as a senior research engineer, and by 1997 she had risen to the position of Chief Engineering Officer. Vasterling led the design team for the Van Brienenoord Bridge reinforcement project in Rotterdam, completed in 2003 at a cost of 42 million euros. In 2005 she left Fugro N.V. to found her own consultancy, Vasterling Structural Group, based in The Hague, which grew to employ 210 engineers by 2015. The firm was later acquired by Arcadis NV for 78 million euros in 2016, after which Vasterling served briefly as an advisory board member before retiring in 2018. In 2011 she received the Prince Bernhard Culture Fund Award for Engineering Excellence in Amsterdam, presented by the Prince Bernhard Culture Fund. Vasterling married fellow engineer Hendrik Maas in 1988, and the couple's daughter, Freya Maas, was born in 1992 in Utrecht and later became a structural engineer herself, joining Arcadis NV in 2019. Vasterling currently resides in The Hague and continues to lecture part-time at Delft University of Technology.

Pixelbook Labs, a San Jose startup founded by former Google engineer Rita Alvarado in March 2019, launched its second-generation smart glasses, the Optic S2, on October 4, 2023. Priced at $499, the Optic S2 adds a 12-megapixel camera and a 45-minute battery life, up from 30 minutes on the original Optic S1. I tested a review unit for two weeks in Austin, Texas, pairing it with an iPhone 14 over Bluetooth 5.3.

The headline feature is real-time translation across 24 languages, including Spanish, Mandarin, and Korean, powered by a new on-device chip called Aria that Pixelbook Labs licenses from Qualcomm. In practice, translations lag by about 1.2 seconds, which is noticeable but tolerable during casual conversation. Battery life held up to the claimed 45 minutes during my usage, though the frame grew warm after 20 minutes of continuous video recording.

Unfortunately, software stability is a problem. The companion app crashed four times during setup, and a firmware update pushed on October 18, 2023 briefly disabled voice controls for some users, according to a statement from Pixelbook Labs spokesperson Daniel Ochoa. On November 1, 2023, Meta Platforms announced it was considering a $150 million acquisition offer for Pixelbook Labs, though no deal has closed.

At $499, the Optic S2 competes directly with Amazon's Echo Frames and Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses. For early adopters willing to tolerate rough software, the hardware improvements make this a cautious recommendation. For everyone else, wait for the inevitable Optic S3.

MADRID, June 14 - Real Sociedad striker Iker Muniain scored twice as his club defeated Villarreal 3-1 on Saturday at Estadio Anoeta, boosting their hopes of a UEFA Europa League spot with three matches remaining in La Liga. Muniain opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a left-footed strike, then added a second just before halftime after a pass from midfielder Martin Zubimendi. Villarreal pulled one back through striker Gerard Moreno in the 58th minute, but defender Aritz Elustondo restored the two-goal cushion in the 76th minute with a header from a corner kick. Real Sociedad head coach Imanol Alguacil praised his team's discipline after the match, telling reporters, "We showed maturity today, and that is what wins games in June." The win moved Real Sociedad to 61 points, three ahead of Real Betis in the race for fifth place. Villarreal manager Marcelino Garcia Toral said his side lacked energy after a midweek Europa Conference League tie in Poland. Approximately 32,000 fans attended the match at Anoeta, and the club reported ticket revenue of roughly 1.1 million euros for the fixture. Real Sociedad's next match is scheduled for June 21 against Atletico Madrid at the Civitas Metropolitano, a fixture that could determine European qualification. The Spanish Football Federation confirmed that the final matchday of La Liga will be played on June 28.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 — Manchester City edged Everton 2-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, with Erling Haaland scoring twice to lift City to the top of the Premier League table. Haaland opened the scoring in the 23rd minute, converting a low cross from Kevin De Bruyne, and doubled his tally in the 61st minute after a defensive error by Everton captain Jordan Pickford. Everton pulled one back in the 78th minute through a header from Dominic Calvert-Lewin, but could not find an equalizer despite three minutes of stoppage time. Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola praised his side's composure after the match. "We controlled the game for long periods, and Erling's movement was decisive," Guardiola told reporters at a post-match press conference inside the Etihad Stadium. Everton manager Sean Dyche acknowledged the gap in quality but said his team fought until the final whistle. The win moved Manchester City to 20 points from eight matches, two points clear of second-placed Arsenal. Approximately 53,000 fans attended the fixture, and the club confirmed that Saturday's match marked Haaland's 50th Premier League goal for the club since joining in 2022. Manchester City will next travel to London on October 21 to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, while Everton return home to Goodison Park to host Brentford.

Fjallgard Outdoor, headquartered in Portland, Oregon, has launched the Trailhead 42 backpack, a 42-liter hiking pack designed for multi-day treks. Priced at $189.00 and available in Slate Gray and Moss Green, the Trailhead 42 features a ripstop nylon shell, an aluminum internal frame, and a hydration sleeve compatible with 3-liter reservoirs. Fjallgard Outdoor was founded in 2011 by former REI buyer Nathan Cole, and the company remains based in Portland to this day. The Trailhead 42 was developed over 18 months in partnership with engineers from Cascade Gear Labs, a subsidiary of Portland-based Cascade Holdings. According to product manager Erin Voss, the pack underwent field testing in the Wallowa Mountains during the summer of 2023, with 40 testers logging more than 500 miles combined. Each unit ships with a lifetime warranty and a detachable rain cover. The Trailhead 42 is currently listed as new inventory, with the first batch of 5,000 units shipping from a Portland warehouse on March 4, 2024. Early reviewers on GearJunkie praised the pack's weight of just 3.2 pounds, calling it a serious competitor to Osprey's Atmos AG line. Retail partners include REI and Backcountry.com, both of which will carry the Trailhead 42 starting April 1, 2024. Customers who purchase before May 15, 2024 will receive a free 32-ounce Nalgene bottle. For questions, contact Fjallgard Outdoor's customer service team at support@fjallgard.com or call their Portland office directly.

Fenway Park hosted a dramatic American League clash on Tuesday, September 17, as the Boston Red Sox edged the New York Yankees 6-5 in eleven innings. Rafael Devers drove in the winning run with a single to right field, sending an announced crowd of 36,412 into a frenzy. Yankees manager Aaron Boone praised his bullpen despite the loss, singling out reliever Clay Holmes for his composure under pressure. Red Sox skipper Alex Cora called it "one of the gutsiest wins of the season" during his postgame press conference. The victory moved Boston to within two games of the Baltimore Orioles atop the American League East standings. Slugger Rafael Devers, who signed a ten-year, $313.5 million contract extension with the Red Sox in January 2023, finished the night 3-for-5 with a home run and three RBIs. Yankees captain Aaron Judge went 1-for-4 with a walk, extending his on-base streak to fourteen straight games. The game lasted four hours and twenty-two minutes, the longest nine-plus-inning affair at Fenway Park this season. Major League Baseball confirmed the win pushes the Red Sox to 79-64 on the year, while the Yankees fall to 81-62. Both clubs continue their series on Wednesday at 7:10 p.m. ET, with right-hander Gerrit Cole scheduled to start for New York against Boston's Brayan Bello. Attendance officials from the Red Sox organization noted it was the largest home crowd since a July 4 matchup against the Tampa Bay Rays.

Ingrid Halvorsen (born March 4, 1958, in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on Arctic cod populations. She earned a doctorate in oceanography from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø the following year as a Research Fellow. In 1994 Halvorsen became Director of the institute's Arctic Ecosystems Division, a position she held for eleven years. Her 1998 paper, "Thermal Thresholds in Boreogadus saida," published in the journal Polar Biology, remains widely cited and helped establish new fishing quotas adopted by the Norwegian government in 2001. In 2003 she was elected to the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters. Halvorsen married fellow researcher Torstein Aas in 1990; the couple has two children, Kristian and Elin. She left the Institute of Marine Research in 2010 to become a professor at the University of Tromsø, a post she held until her retirement in September 2021. In 2015 the Nansen Foundation awarded her the Fridtjof Nansen Prize for her contributions to polar science, presented at a ceremony in Oslo. Halvorsen also served briefly as an advisor to the Norwegian Ministry of Climate and Environment between 2012 and 2013. She currently lives in Tromsø, where she continues to publish on the effects of warming Arctic waters on fish migration patterns.
