CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- Nov 14, 2023 -- Verdant Biosciences Inc., a clinical-stage biotechnology company, today announced that it has acquired Halcyon Therapeutics Ltd. for $340 million in cash, expanding its pipeline of treatments for chronic kidney disease. The deal, finalized in Cambridge on Tuesday, includes Halcyon's lead compound, VX-221, currently in Phase 2 trials.

Under the agreement, Verdant Biosciences will pay Halcyon Therapeutics shareholders $340 million, with the transaction expected to close by December 15, 2023. Dr. Miriam Solberg, Chief Executive Officer of Verdant Biosciences, said the acquisition strengthens the company's position against competitor NovaCure Pharmaceuticals. "This acquisition allows us to accelerate development of VX-221 and bring it to patients faster," Solberg said during a press briefing held at the company's headquarters in Cambridge.

As part of the transaction, Halcyon's founder and former CEO, Dr. Thomas Reyes, will join Verdant Biosciences as Chief Scientific Officer, effective December 1, 2023. Reyes founded Halcyon Therapeutics in 2016 in Boston and has led the development of three clinical-stage compounds targeting renal disease.

Verdant Biosciences, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs approximately 420 people and reported revenue of $210 million in 2022. The company was founded in 2011 by Dr. Miriam Solberg and Dr. Arjun Patel. Shares of Verdant Biosciences rose 6 percent following the announcement, while trading on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker VRDT.

The transaction remains subject to customary regulatory approvals, including review by the Federal Trade Commission.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF ARIZONA, MARICOPA COUNTY

Case No. CR2024-118742

On March 11, 2024, Judge Patricia Wexler sentenced Dominic Farraro, 41, of Tempe, Arizona, to 78 months in federal custody after a jury convicted him of wire fraud and money laundering in connection with a scheme that defrauded investors of approximately $3.4 million. Prosecutor Elena Marsh of the Maricopa County District Attorney's Office argued that Farraro, former Chief Financial Officer of Sonoran Capital Partners, diverted client funds between January 2019 and August 2022 to finance personal real estate purchases in Scottsdale.

The trial, held at the Sandra Day O'Connor Courthouse in Phoenix, began on February 5, 2024, and included testimony from twelve former clients of Sonoran Capital Partners, a firm headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona. Defense attorney Marcus Ibsen contended that Farraro's business partner, Renata Cole, controlled the disputed accounts, but the jury rejected this claim after eight days of deliberation.

Judge Wexler ordered Farraro to pay $3.4 million in restitution to the victims, payable within five years, and imposed a $50,000 fine payable to the court. Farraro was taken into custody immediately following sentencing and will serve his term at the Federal Correctional Institution in Phoenix. His attorney has indicated an intent to appeal the verdict to the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals within the required 14-day window.

input: Pixelworks Labs, a display technology unit of Pixelworks Inc., unveiled the Lumina X7 monitor on March 4, 2024, at an event in San Jose, California. Priced at $649, the 27-inch panel targets photographers and video editors who need accurate color reproduction. During a hands-on session, senior product manager Rachel Ostrowski demonstrated the monitor's factory-calibrated Delta E rating of under 1.0, a figure that rivals displays costing twice as much. The Lumina X7 shipped starting March 18, 2024, and early buyers on Amazon report the 98 percent DCI-P3 coverage lives up to the marketing claims. I tested the review unit for three weeks in my home studio in Portland, Oregon, running it alongside an aging Dell UltraSharp U2720Q. The difference in shadow detail was immediately obvious. Pixelworks built the panel around its own X7 image processor, a chip the company says reduces motion blur by 40 percent compared to the previous generation. Founded in 1997 by Allen Alley, Pixelworks has historically supplied chips to television makers, but the Lumina X7 marks a serious push into finished consumer products, putting it in direct competition with BenQ and ViewSonic. My only complaint is the single USB-C port, which limits daisy-chaining multiple monitors. At $649, the Lumina X7 is not cheap, but for colorists on a budget it is easily the best display I have used this year. Pixelworks' stock rose 6 percent the week after the launch event, according to a note from analyst Tom Sepenzis of Northland Capital Markets.

Kestrel Outdoor Co., headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, has launched the Talus 3-Season Tent, a two-person backpacking shelter engineered for the Rocky Mountain trail circuit. Priced at $329.00 and available starting September 12, 2024, the Talus weighs just 3.1 pounds and packs down to the size of a 1-liter bottle. The tent's rainfly uses a 20-denier ripstop nylon treated with a silicone-polyurethane coating, giving it a 1500mm waterproof rating that held up during Kestrel's field trials near Hyalite Canyon last July. Lead designer Marisol Fenn, who previously spent six years at Patagonia, said the Talus was built to survive sudden alpine storms without adding bulk to a hiker's pack. Each unit ships with aircraft-grade aluminum poles, eight titanium stakes, and a lifetime warranty covering manufacturing defects. Kestrel Outdoor Co. is offering the first 500 units with a free compression sack, a promotion running through October 31, 2024. The Talus is manufactured in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, at a facility operated by longtime supplier Viet Thanh Textiles, and units are currently in stock at REI locations across Colorado and at the company's flagship store in Bozeman. Early reviewers, including Outside Magazine, have praised the tent's ventilation system, noting it outperforms competing models from Big Agnes and MSR in humid conditions. Customers who purchase before November 1 can also apply a 15% discount code, TALUS15, at checkout. This is a new product with no prior model history, and Kestrel Outdoor Co. says it plans to expand the line with a four-person version in early 2025.

Pixelworks Labs, a hardware startup based in Portland, Oregon, launched the Aurora Q1 mechanical keyboard on March 14, 2024, priced at $189. I have spent three weeks typing on the review unit, and it is one of the more polished debut products I have tested this year. Founded in 2021 by Priya Nadarajan, a former Logitech engineer, Pixelworks Labs set out to build a keyboard that combines hot-swappable switches with a gasket-mounted frame, a feature usually reserved for boutique keyboards costing $400 or more. The Aurora Q1 ships with Kailh Box White switches, PBT keycaps, and a USB-C detachable cable, weighing 1.1 kilograms. Typing feels dense and controlled, with none of the hollow rattle common in budget boards. Battery life via the 4000mAh cell is rated at 120 hours with the backlight off, and I measured roughly 96 hours with RGB lighting on medium brightness, which is respectable but trails the Keychron Q1 Pro's 300-hour claim. Software support arrives through the Aurora Configurator app, currently available only on Windows, which frustrated me since I do a lot of work on a MacBook Pro. Priya Nadarajan told me in a phone interview on March 20, 2024, that a macOS version is planned for June 2024. Pixelworks Labs sold roughly 3,000 units in the first two weeks, according to a company statement, competing directly with Keychron and Royal Kludge in the enthusiast segment. At $189, the Aurora Q1 is not cheap, but the build quality nearly justifies it. Recommended, with the caveat of waiting for Mac software before buying if you are not on Windows.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. RG24-118732

On March 14, 2024, Judge Wilfred Ostrowski of the Alameda County Superior Court presided over the sentencing hearing of Marcus Delane Whitfield, 41, who was convicted on February 2, 2024, of embezzlement and wire fraud involving Cascade Freight Logistics, a shipping company headquartered in Oakland, California. Prosecutor Elena Marsh, representing the District Attorney's office, argued that Whitfield diverted $840,000 from company accounts between June 2021 and September 2023 while employed as the firm's Chief Financial Officer. Defense attorney Rowan Castellano requested leniency, citing Whitfield's cooperation with investigators from the Alameda County Sheriff's Department, who arrested him on November 9, 2023, at his residence in Fremont.

Judge Ostrowski sentenced Whitfield to five years in state prison and ordered restitution of $840,000 to Cascade Freight Logistics, payable within 180 days. The court noted that Whitfield had used a shell entity, Northgate Transit Solutions LLC, to launder a portion of the stolen funds. Cascade Freight Logistics CEO Priya Nakamura issued a statement thanking the Alameda County District Attorney's office and confirmed the company has since hired a new CFO, Daniel Ferris, effective January 8, 2024. Whitfield's attorney indicated an appeal would be filed with the California Court of Appeal, First Appellate District, within 60 days.

Whitfield was arrested on October 14, 2023, by investigators from the Oakland Police Department at his residence on Grand Avenue. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland.

Judge Aames sentenced Whitfield to six years in state prison and ordered restitution of $2.3 million to Brightwell Logistics Inc. Defense attorney Marcus Ibe argued for leniency, citing his client's lack of prior record, but the request was denied. Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Finally Gets the Basics Right

Mountain View, CA -- October 14, 2024. After two disappointing generations, Google's Pixel Watch 3 feels like the product the original should have been in 2022. I have worn the 45mm model for three weeks, and the improvements from Google's hardware team in Mountain View are hard to ignore.

The headline upgrade is battery life. Google claims 36 hours on a single charge, and in my testing with the always-on display enabled, I consistently got 30 hours before needing the charger. That is a meaningful jump from the Pixel Watch 2, which struggled past 24 hours. The display is brighter too, hitting 2,000 nits at peak, which makes outdoor readability far better than on the Apple Watch Series 9, its closest competitor.

Google priced the 45mm LTE version at $399.99, undercutting the $429 Apple charges for a comparable configuration. The Wear OS 5 software, developed jointly with Samsung Electronics, now supports Fitbit's new Cardio Load metric, a feature Fitbit's parent company Google inherited when it acquired Fitbit for $2.1 billion back in January 2021.

During a briefing in San Francisco last month, Google product manager Sameer Samat said the company wants the Pixel Watch line to overtake Samsung's Galaxy Watch in North America by 2026. That is an ambitious goal given Samsung's Galaxy Watch 7 launched in July with similar pricing.

Minor complaints remain: the charging puck is proprietary, and third-party bands from Miel remain expensive at $49.99 each. Still, this is the most confident Pixel Watch yet.

Union Berlin edged Bayer Leverkusen 2-1 at the Stadion An der Alten Försterei in Berlin on Saturday, handing the visitors their first Bundesliga defeat of the season. Striker Sheraldo Becker opened the scoring in the 23rd minute, finishing a quick counterattack after a pass from midfielder Janik Haberer. Leverkusen equalized just before halftime through Victor Boniface, who converted a penalty in the 41st minute after a foul inside the box. The decisive goal came in the 78th minute when defender Robin Knoche headed in a corner kick taken by Haberer, sending the crowd of 22,000 into celebration. Leverkusen coach Xabi Alonso said afterward that his side lost focus in midfield during the second half. Union Berlin manager Bo Svensson praised his players' discipline, calling the win "the biggest result of our season so far." The victory moved Union Berlin up to 6th place in the Bundesliga table, while Leverkusen remained top with 34 points. Bayer Leverkusen's next match will be against Borussia Dortmund at the BayArena in Leverkusen on October 21. Union Berlin will travel to Munich to face Bayern Munich the same weekend. Sunday's other results included a 3-3 draw between RB Leipzig and Eintracht Frankfurt in Leipzig, and a narrow 1-0 win for VfB Stuttgart over Werder Bremen at the MHPArena.

Denver-based Rockwell Midstream Partners announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Bluefin Gathering LLC, a natural gas pipeline operator based in Midland, Texas, for approximately $740 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by December 15, 2024, will add roughly 320 miles of gathering pipeline to Rockwell's Permian Basin network. Chief Executive Officer Diane Petrovska said the acquisition strengthens Rockwell's position as a supplier to major refiners including Marathon Petroleum Corporation. "This transaction gives us direct access to some of the fastest-growing production areas in the basin," Petrovska told reporters during a call from Rockwell's headquarters. Bluefin Gathering was founded in 2016 by former Chevron executive Raymond Ostrowski, who will step down as President once the deal closes and join Rockwell's advisory board. Analysts at Jefferies Group LLC estimate the combined entity will generate $1.1 billion in annual revenue by 2026. Shares of Rockwell Midstream Partners rose 4.3 percent to $58.20 following the announcement, while trading on the New York Stock Exchange. The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, though industry observers expect minimal antitrust concerns given limited geographic overlap between the two companies' pipeline systems. Rockwell financed the deal partly through a $400 million bond offering underwritten by Goldman Sachs Group Inc. earlier this month.

DETROIT, Mich. — Meridian Auto Group announced Tuesday that it has acquired Falcon Robotics Inc., a Pittsburgh-based startup specializing in warehouse automation, for $340 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at a press conference at Meridian's headquarters in Detroit, is expected to close by November 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Meridian CEO Rachel Doyle said the acquisition would let the company integrate Falcon's robotic arms into its assembly lines within 18 months. "This partnership positions Meridian to compete directly with Tesla and Rivian on manufacturing efficiency," Doyle told reporters.

Falcon Robotics was founded in 2017 by engineer Tomasz Kowalski, who will join Meridian as Chief Technology Officer starting December 1, 2024. Kowalski said the 220 Falcon employees in Pittsburgh will remain at their current facility.

The announcement sent Meridian shares up 6 percent on the New York Stock Exchange, closing at $58.42. Analyst Priya Nair of Hartwell Capital called the move "a smart bet on automation," noting that Meridian's chief rival, Consolidated Motors, has struggled to modernize its plants.

Meridian, which employs roughly 41,000 people worldwide, reported $12.3 billion in revenue last year. The company was founded in 1958 by Walter Meridian in Detroit and remains headquartered there. Shareholders are expected to vote on the deal at a special meeting scheduled for October 30, 2024.

Bergstrom Outfitters, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, has released the Talon 3.0 Trail Backpack, priced at $189.99 and available starting November 4, 2024. Designed by lead engineer Priya Nalamothu, the 42-liter pack features a titanium-alloy frame supplied by Cascade Metalworks, a longtime supplier based in Spokane, Washington. The Talon 3.0 is built for multi-day treks and has already been tested by hikers along Colorado's Continental Divide Trail. According to Bergstrom Outfitters founder Dale Rickenbacker, who started the company in 1998, the new model addresses complaints about the older Talon 2.5, which was discontinued in March 2023. 'We rebuilt this pack from the ground up after listening to three years of customer feedback,' Rickenbacker said in a statement released on October 15, 2024. The backpack includes a detachable rain cover, a hydration bladder compatible with a 3-liter reservoir, and reflective strips for low-light visibility. Bergstrom Outfitters, which competes directly with Alpine Ridge Gear, sold over 12,000 units of the previous Talon line since 2019. The Talon 3.0 is currently in stock and ships from the company's distribution center in Denver, Colorado. Customers who order before November 20, 2024 will receive a free 1-liter water bottle. Reviewers from Trailhead Monthly magazine gave the pack 4.5 out of 5 stars, praising its durability and weight of just 1.8 kilograms. The product is available exclusively through Bergstrom Outfitters' website and select REI stores nationwide.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday that Singapore will invest $420 million to expand the Woodlands Checkpoint over the next three years. Speaking at a press conference in Singapore, Transport Minister Chee Hong Tat said the project, named the Woodlands Integration Programme, will increase daily vehicle capacity by 35 percent and reduce average crossing times for commuters traveling to Johor Bahru in Malaysia. Construction is scheduled to begin on 1 March 2025 and will be carried out by ST Engineering, a firm headquartered in Singapore that was awarded the contract following a tender process concluded last month. Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, who oversees infrastructure spending, confirmed that the funding will come from the Land Transport Authority's annual budget and will not require new taxes. Officials estimate the upgraded checkpoint will process an additional 50,000 vehicles per day by 2027, easing congestion that has drawn complaints from residents of Woodlands for over a decade. The Ministry also confirmed that a separate $80 million allocation will go toward upgrading immigration systems at Tuas Checkpoint, with completion expected by December 2026. Minister Chee Hong Tat added that the government will consult with Malaysian counterparts, including officials from the Johor state government, to synchronize clearance procedures on both sides of the border. A follow-up meeting between Singaporean and Malaysian transport officials is planned for early April in Putrajaya to finalize technical details. The Ministry emphasized that public safety inspections, to be conducted by the Building and Construction Authority, will continue throughout the construction period without disrupting daily operations at the checkpoint.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 - Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side defeated Brentford 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, extending their unbeaten home run to eight matches in the Premier League. Watkins opened the scoring in the 23rd minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Mark Flekken, before Brentford's Bryan Mbeumo equalized just before halftime. Villa manager Unai Emery made a tactical switch at the break, bringing on midfielder Jacob Ramsey for the injured Boubacar Kamara, who limped off after a heavy challenge and will undergo scans this week. Ramsey's introduction proved decisive, as he set up Watkins for his second goal in the 68th minute, and Youri Tielemans added a third in stoppage time to seal the win in front of 41,000 fans. The victory moved Aston Villa to third place in the table, level on points with Liverpool, and boosted their hopes of qualifying for the UEFA Champions League next season. Speaking after the match, Emery praised his squad's resilience, saying the team showed "great character" despite losing Kamara early. Brentford manager Thomas Frank expressed frustration with his side's defending, noting that individual errors cost them crucial points. The two clubs will meet again on February 3, 2024, at the Gtech Community Stadium in London for the reverse fixture. Aston Villa's next match comes on Wednesday against Legia Warsaw in the Europa Conference League.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side defeated Everton 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, extending Villa's unbeaten home run to eight matches. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Jordan Pickford, before midfielder John McGinn doubled the lead just before halftime. Everton pulled one back through striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 58th minute, but Watkins sealed the victory with his second goal in the 81st minute, latching onto a through ball from winger Leon Bailey. The win moved Aston Villa to third place in the Premier League table with 19 points from eight games, three points behind leaders Manchester City. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, telling reporters at a press conference, "We controlled the game for large periods and deserved the three points." Everton manager Sean Dyche, whose side has now lost four of its last six matches, said his team needed to improve defensively. The match, attended by 41,203 spectators, was the first meeting between the two clubs since April 2023. Aston Villa will next travel to face Arsenal on October 29, while Everton will host Brentford at Goodison Park the same weekend.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Finally Gets the Battery Right

Mountain View, October 14, 2024 -- Google's Pixel Watch 3, released on September 20, 2024, addresses the biggest complaint about its predecessor: battery life. After a week of testing the 45mm model in San Francisco, I can report a solid 36 hours on a single charge with the always-on display enabled, up from roughly 24 hours on the Pixel Watch 2.

The $399 device, announced by Google's hardware chief Rick Osterloh at a small press event, uses a 5% brighter LTPO OLED panel and a more efficient Snapdragon W5 chip supplied by Qualcomm. Loss of Pulse Detection, a new safety feature built with input from the American Heart Association, worked reliably during a treadmill test, though it should not replace a hospital visit.

Fitbit, a Google subsidiary since Google acquired it for $2.1 billion in January 2021, powers the health metrics, including a redesigned Cardio Load score. Software runs Wear OS 5, co-developed with Samsung, and pairs smoothly with both Android 14 and, to a lesser extent, iPhones running iOS 17.

Competitors haven't stood still. Apple's Watch Series 10, launched a week earlier on September 20, 2024, still leads in third-party app support, while Samsung's Galaxy Watch7 undercuts Google on price at $299.

Minor gripes: the charging puck remains proprietary, and the speaker is still too quiet for calls. Still, for Android users, the Pixel Watch 3 is the easiest Wear OS recommendation Google has made since the line launched in 2022.

Ingrid Solberg (born March 14, 1958, in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cod population decline in the North Sea. She earned a doctorate in marine ecology from the University of Bergen in 1985 and later joined the Institute of Marine Research in Bergen as a research fellow in 1987. In 1994 Solberg was appointed Director of Fisheries Research at the same institute, a position she held for eleven years. Her 1998 book, The Silent Fjord, documented overfishing along the Norwegian coast and became required reading at several European universities. In 2003 she was awarded the Nansen Prize by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to marine conservation. Solberg left the Institute of Marine Research in 2005 to become a professor at the University of Tromsø, where she taught until her retirement in 2020. She married fellow biologist Anders Kvale in 1990, and the couple had two children, Erik and Maja. Solberg has also served as a member of the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea since 1996. In 2011 she publicly criticized the fishing company Nordvik Seafoods for exceeding cod quotas in the Barents Sea, a dispute that drew national media attention. She currently resides in Tromsø, Norway.

Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1957 in Turin, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-resistant bridge designs. She earned a degree in civil engineering from Politecnico di Torino in 1980 and joined Fiat Engineering the same year as a Junior Engineer. In 1988 Marchetti left to co-found Marchetti & Rossi Structural Consultants with colleague Paolo Rossi, headquartered in Milan, Italy. The firm grew quickly after winning a contract in 1991 to reinforce the Ponte Vecchio approach viaduct following minor earthquake damage in the region.

In 1999, Marchetti was appointed Chief Engineer of Autostrade per l'Italia, overseeing retrofit projects on more than 300 kilometers of highway infrastructure. She left that position in 2006 to become a professor at Politecnico di Milano, where she has since supervised over 40 doctoral students. Her 2003 monograph, "Seismic Resilience in Concrete Structures," remains a standard reference in the field and has been translated into English, French, and Japanese.

In 2014, the Italian government awarded Marchetti the Order of Merit for Technical Achievement in a ceremony held in Rome, citing her contributions to public infrastructure safety. Marchetti & Rossi Structural Consultants was acquired by the multinational firm Arup in 2018 for an undisclosed sum, becoming a subsidiary operating under the name Arup Milan. Marchetti, now 68, continues to consult part-time and lives with her husband, architect Giovanni Bellini, in Turin.

On March 14, 2024, Judge Wilhelmina Ortiz presided over the sentencing hearing of Marcus Delaine Whitfield, 41, at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland. Whitfield was found guilty on February 9, 2024, of embezzlement following a jury trial in which Deputy District Attorney Sanjay Rao served as prosecutor. Evidence showed that between June 2021 and October 2022, Whitfield, then serving as Chief Financial Officer of Baymont Logistics Inc., a freight company headquartered in Fremont, California, diverted approximately $1,240,000 from corporate accounts into a shell entity registered under his wife's name, Corina Whitfield.

Judge Ortiz sentenced Whitfield to six years in state prison and ordered restitution of $1,240,000 payable to Baymont Logistics Inc. Defense attorney Priscilla Guan argued for probation, citing her client's lack of prior record, but the court rejected the request, noting the scale of the fraud.

Baymont Logistics Inc. was acquired by Meridian Freight Group in December 2022, shortly after the embezzlement was discovered by auditors at Ernst & Young. A spokesperson for Meridian Freight Group, Denise Halloran, said the company cooperated fully with investigators and had implemented new internal controls.

Whitfield's attorney has indicated an intent to appeal the sentence to the California Court of Appeal, First Appellate District, within 60 days.

Marguerite Lindqvist (born 14 March 1937 in Malmö, Sweden) was a Swedish biochemist known for her pioneering work on enzyme kinetics. She earned her doctorate in Chemistry from Lund University in 1963 and joined the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm as a research fellow that same year. In 1971 Lindqvist became Head of Biochemistry at the Karolinska Institute, a post she held for nearly two decades. Her laboratory identified the catalytic role of the enzyme phosphofructokinase in muscle metabolism, work published in 1975 in the journal Nature. In 1982 she left Karolinska to become Professor of Molecular Biology at Uppsala University, a position she held until her retirement in 1998. Lindqvist married fellow biochemist Anders Berg in 1965, and the couple had two children, Elin and Karl Berg. In 1989 the Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded her the Anders Jahre Prize for her contributions to enzymology, an honor bestowed during a ceremony in Stockholm. She also served as a consultant to Astra AB, the pharmaceutical company later merged into AstraZeneca, advising on drug development related to metabolic disorders from 1985 to 1990. Lindqvist died on 9 November 2011 in Uppsala after a long illness. She was 74 years old. Her son Karl Berg later became a professor of genetics at the same university, continuing the family's scientific legacy.

Portland, Oregon -- August 14, 2024 -- Cascade Robotics Inc. announced today that it has acquired Willamette Sensors LLC, a privately held maker of industrial proximity sensors based in Beaverton, Oregon, for $42 million in cash and stock. The deal is expected to close on September 30, 2024, pending routine regulatory approval.

Under the agreement, Cascade Robotics will absorb Willamette Sensors as a wholly owned subsidiary, retaining its 65 employees at the Beaverton facility. Willamette Sensors' founder and chief executive, Marcus Delgado, will join Cascade Robotics as Vice President of Sensor Engineering, reporting directly to Cascade's chief executive officer, Priya Nakamura.

"This acquisition strengthens our supply chain and accelerates development of our next-generation warehouse robot, the CascadeBot X3," said Nakamura, speaking at a press briefing in Portland. "Willamette's sensor technology has been a key supplier component in our robotics line for three years, and now it will be fully integrated."

Cascade Robotics, headquartered in Portland since its founding in 2011 by Nakamura and co-founder Elena Voss, reported revenue of $310 million in fiscal year 2023, up 18 percent from the prior year. The company employs roughly 1,200 people across facilities in Oregon, Texas, and Germany.

The transaction was financed through a combination of $25 million in cash and 1.1 million shares of Cascade Robotics common stock, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Analysts at Ridgeline Capital Partners called the deal "a smart vertical integration move" in a note published Thursday.

Pixel Tab Review: Google's First Real Tablet Bet Since 2015

Mountain View, CA -- On October 22, 2024, Google began shipping the Pixel Tablet 2, priced at $549 for the base 128GB model, through its online store and Best Buy locations across the United States. I have used the device for three weeks in San Francisco, and it mostly delivers on its promise of a proper Android tablet rather than a scaled-up phone.

The Tensor G4 chip, the same silicon found in the Pixel 9 phone, handles multitasking smoothly, and the redesigned charging speaker dock finally holds the tablet at a usable angle for video calls. Rick Osterloh, Google's Senior Vice President of Devices and Services, told reporters at a briefing in New York on October 15, 2024 that the company built the Tablet 2 specifically for smart-home control, betting that Nest integration would set it apart from Apple's iPad and Samsung's Galaxy Tab S10.

Battery life is the standout: 11 hours of video playback in my tests, up from 9 hours on the original Pixel Tablet. The 2560x1600 LCD screen is bright but not OLED, a disappointing choice at this price given that the $499 Galaxy Tab S10 FE now ships with an AMOLED panel.

Google also confirmed the tablet will receive software updates through October 2031, a seven-year commitment that outpaces most Android rivals. For households already using Nest cameras and thermostats, the Pixel Tablet 2 is an easy recommendation. For everyone else, the iPad Air remains the safer buy.

Mireille Kponou (born 14 March 1958 in Cotonou, Benin) is a Beninese economist and former diplomat who served as Minister of Finance of Benin from 1998 to 2003. She earned a doctorate in economics from the Sorbonne in Paris in 1984 before joining the International Monetary Fund in Washington, D.C., where she worked as an economist for eleven years.

In 1996 Kponou returned to Benin and took a position at the Central Bank of West African States in Dakar, Senegal, advising member governments on monetary policy. President Mathieu Kerekou appointed her Minister of Finance of Benin in July 1998, a post she held until March 2003, during which she negotiated a debt relief package worth 460 million dollars with the Paris Club in 2000.

After leaving government, Kponou was named Beninese Ambassador to France in September 2004, serving in Paris until 2009. She later founded the nonprofit organization Femmes et Finance in Cotonou in 2011 to promote financial literacy among West African women, and she has served as its director since then.

In 2015 Kponou received the National Order of Benin from President Thomas Boni Yayi in Cotonou for her contributions to economic policy. She is married to the architect Serge Ahouansou and has two children. Kponou continues to lecture part-time at the University of Abomey-Calavi and lives in Cotonou.

DENVER, Colorado -- Ridgeline Foods Inc., the maker of Aspen Peak snack bars, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Boulder-based Crestview Naturals LLC for $84 million in cash and stock. The deal, disclosed at Ridgeline's headquarters in Denver, gives the company control of Crestview's popular oat-based cereal line, which generated roughly $22 million in revenue last year.

Under the terms of the agreement, Crestview founder and Chief Executive Officer Marisol Vance will step down from her post effective December 1, while remaining as a strategic advisor through mid-2025. Ridgeline's CEO, Gordon Pruitt, said the acquisition strengthens the company's position against rival General Mills Inc. in the natural foods aisle.

"Crestview built something special over the past nine years, and we intend to grow it, not dilute it," Pruitt told reporters during a press briefing in Denver on Tuesday.

Ridgeline shares rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $47.15. Analysts at Fairbanks Capital Partners called the transaction a smart bolt-on that could add two percent to Ridgeline's annual revenue by 2026.

Crestview, founded in 2015 by Vance in a rented commercial kitchen in Boulder, now employs 210 people. Ridgeline said it plans to retain all Crestview staff and keep the Boulder facility operational for at least three years. The transaction is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending routine regulatory review.

CLEVELAND, Ohio — Justice.ChargeIndict aside, this is business news: Cedar Point Robotics, a Cleveland-based manufacturer of warehouse automation systems, announced Tuesday that it has acquired StackFlow Logistics Software for $42 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at the company's headquarters on Euclid Avenue, marks Cedar Point Robotics' third acquisition since 2021 and its largest to date. CEO Marianne Ostrowski said the purchase of StackFlow, based in Austin, Texas, would let Cedar Point integrate warehouse-management software directly into its fleet of autonomous forklifts, sold under the brand name HaulerX. "This gives our customers one platform instead of three," Ostrowski told reporters during a briefing on October 14, 2024. StackFlow founder Devon Ruiz, who started the company in 2017, will join Cedar Point as Chief Product Officer effective November 1, 2024. Ruiz previously worked at Amazon Robotics before founding StackFlow. Analysts at Northgate Capital estimate the combined firm could generate $310 million in annual revenue by 2026, up from $190 million last year. Shares of Cedar Point Robotics, which trades publicly under the ticker CDPR, rose 6 percent following the announcement. The company competes directly with Boston-based GreyIron Systems for contracts with retailers such as Target and Kroger. Cedar Point employs roughly 1,400 people across facilities in Ohio, Texas, and Michigan.

The Ministry of Transportation of Ontario announced on June 12, 2024 that it will invest 84 million dollars to widen a 22-kilometre stretch of Highway 401 near Cambridge. Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria confirmed the funding at a press briefing held at Queen's Park in Toronto, where he was joined by Cambridge Mayor Jan Liggett. The project, awarded to contractor Dufferin Construction, is scheduled to begin construction in September 2024 and finish by November 2026. Sarkaria stated that the expansion would reduce daily congestion affecting roughly 45,000 commuters and support freight movement between Kitchener-Waterloo and the Greater Toronto Area. The Ministry also disclosed that it has hired engineering firm WSP Canada to conduct environmental assessments along the corridor, in compliance with the Environmental Assessment Act. Opposition critic Jennifer French, representing the Ontario NDP, criticized the announcement, arguing that the funds should instead be directed toward public transit expansion in the Region of Waterloo. She raised the issue during a legislative session at the Ontario Legislative Building on June 13, 2024. Sarkaria responded that the province remains committed to a 15 billion dollar transit plan announced earlier this year, including the Hazel McCallion Line. The Ministry expects the Highway 401 project to create approximately 1,200 construction jobs over the next two years and will publish quarterly progress reports beginning in January 2025.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 - Marcus Reyes scored twice as Ashbourne United defeated Whitmore City 3-1 at Cardwell Park on Saturday, moving the club into second place in the League Two table. The 24-year-old striker opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a low finish from inside the box, then added a second just before halftime after a quick counterattack led by midfielder Daniel Okafor. Whitmore City pulled one back in the 58th minute through captain Liam Foster, but substitute Rico Vidal sealed the win with a curling strike in the 81st minute. Ashbourne United manager Paula Grant praised her side's discipline after the match, telling reporters, "We stayed patient and trusted the game plan." The victory extended Ashbourne United's unbeaten run to seven matches and lifted the club to 28 points from 13 games, three behind league leaders Brackford Town. Whitmore City manager Tom Ellison was sacked on Monday following the defeat, the club's third loss in four matches. Ashbourne United will next travel to Sunderland on October 21 to face Redwell Athletic, while Whitmore City hosts Brackford Town at Milbourne Stadium. Approximately 11,400 supporters attended Saturday's match, according to figures released by the League Two administration office. Ticket revenue for the fixture reportedly exceeded 85,000 pounds, a season-high for Cardwell Park.

Nikon USA launched the Zf Mark II mirrorless camera on September 12, 2024, pricing the body at $2,199 in retail stores across the United States. I tested the unit for three weeks in Denver, Colorado, alongside a Nikkor 40mm f/2 lens, and came away impressed by its 24.5-megapixel sensor and retro dial layout. The camera, manufactured at Nikon's Sendai, Japan plant, borrows styling cues from the 1982 FM2 while packing modern autofocus derived from the flagship Z9. Battery life rated at 380 shots per charge held up during a hiking trip through Rocky Mountain National Park, though the buffer cleared slowly when shooting 14-bit RAW bursts at 15 frames per second. Yuki Tanaka, a product manager at Nikon, told reporters in Tokyo on August 30, 2024 that the Zf Mark II targets photographers who want tactile controls without sacrificing speed. Competing against Sony's A7C II and the Fujifilm X-T5, Nikon faces a crowded field, but the in-body image stabilization rated at 8 stops gives it a genuine edge for handheld video. My only complaints are the single CFexpress card slot and a menu system that still feels borrowed from 2016. At $2,199, this is not an impulse purchase, but for enthusiasts upgrading from a Nikon D850, it's one of the most compelling hybrid cameras of 2024. I'm awarding it 4.5 out of 5 stars.

The Ohio Department of Transportation announced on Tuesday that it will begin a $42 million reconstruction of the Interstate 70 bridge over the Scioto River near Columbus, Ohio, starting September 9, 2024. Director Jack Marchbanks said the project, awarded to Kokosing Construction Company, will replace deteriorating support beams identified during a routine inspection in March 2024. "This bridge carries roughly 58,000 vehicles per day, and safety is our top priority," Marchbanks said during a press briefing held at the ODOT district office in Delaware, Ohio. The agency expects the work to take fourteen months, with completion targeted for November 2025. Governor Mike DeWine praised the funding, which comes from the Ohio General Assembly's transportation budget and a $12 million federal grant administered by the U.S. Department of Transportation. Lane closures will begin on September 16, 2024, and drivers should expect delays of up to twenty minutes during peak hours. ODOT spokesperson Angela Fout said detour signage will direct traffic to State Route 315 as an alternate route. Local officials, including Columbus City Council member Rob Dorans, welcomed the investment, noting that a similar bridge in Franklin County partially collapsed in 2019 due to corrosion, though no injuries were reported at that time. Marchbanks added that ODOT will hold a public forum on August 20, 2024, at the Delaware County Fairgrounds to address resident concerns about noise and traffic patterns during construction.

SUPERIOR COURT OF ALAMEDA COUNTY — CRIMINAL DIVISION

Oakland, California, March 14, 2024. Judge Marion Whitfield presided over the sentencing hearing of Derek Alan Pruitt, 41, who pleaded guilty on January 9, 2024 to two counts of wire fraud in connection with a scheme operated through his company, Pruitt Capital Advisors LLC, headquartered in San Ramon. Prosecutor Elena Vasquez of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office told the court that between June 2021 and October 2022, Pruitt solicited $2.3 million from at least fourteen investors by falsely claiming the funds would be used to purchase commercial real estate in Fresno. Instead, he transferred $1.1 million to a personal account and used the remainder to repay earlier investors in a Ponzi-style arrangement.

Defense attorney Gordon Halloway argued for leniency, citing Pruitt's cooperation and his early guilty plea. Judge Whitfield rejected the request, sentencing Pruitt to 87 months in federal custody and ordering restitution of $2.1 million to victims, payable through the court within five years. "This was a calculated betrayal of trust," Whitfield said from the bench.

Among the victims was Rosalind Kemp, a retired schoolteacher from Hayward, who told the court she lost $180,000 in retirement savings. Pruitt Capital Advisors LLC has since ceased operations. The case, People v. Derek Alan Pruitt, was investigated by the FBI's San Francisco field office and referred for prosecution in 2023.

Ingrid Vasterling (born 14 March 1952 in Rotterdam, Netherlands) is a Dutch marine biologist known for her research on North Sea cod populations. She earned a doctorate in Marine Ecology from Utrecht University in 1979 and began her career as a researcher at the Royal Netherlands Institute for Sea Research (NIOZ) in 1980. In 1994, Vasterling was appointed Director of Fisheries Research at NIOZ, a position she held for eleven years. During her tenure, she led a widely cited 1997 study documenting a 38 percent decline in North Sea cod stocks, published in the journal Marine Biology Review. In 2005, she left NIOZ to become Professor of Oceanography at Utrecht University, succeeding her longtime colleague Dr. Hendrik Boomsma. Vasterling married fellow biologist Peter Klaassen in 1983; the couple had two children, Marta and Joost. In 2008, she received the Ørsted Medal for Marine Science from the Royal Danish Academy of Sciences in Copenhagen, in recognition of her contributions to fisheries conservation. She retired from Utrecht University in March 2019 but continued to serve as an advisor to the European Marine Board until her death in Amsterdam on 9 November 2022, following a brief illness. A memorial symposium was held at Utrecht University in December 2022, attended by over 200 colleagues and former students. Her 1997 study remains a foundational reference for European fisheries policy, and the Vasterling Fellowship, established in 2023 by NIOZ, continues to fund early-career marine researchers.

input: MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 - Manchester City defeated Everton 3-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, with striker Erling Haaland scoring twice to move him to 12 goals in the Premier League this season. Midfielder Kevin De Bruyne added the third goal in the 78th minute, capping a dominant second-half display in front of 53,412 fans. Everton's lone response came from forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who converted a penalty in the 65th minute after a foul inside the box. Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola praised his squad's discipline after the match, saying the team had 'controlled the tempo from the first whistle.' The win extended City's unbeaten run to eight matches and lifted them to second place in the Premier League table, three points behind leaders Arsenal. Everton manager Sean Dyche, whose side has now lost four of its last five league games, admitted his team must 'find consistency quickly' to avoid a relegation battle. The Football Association confirmed that Haaland's brace means he has now scored 11 goals in his last seven appearances against Everton across all competitions. Manchester City will next travel to London on October 21 to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, while Everton hosts Newcastle United at Goodison Park the same weekend. The result also strengthens Manchester City's position as they prepare for a Champions League fixture against RB Leipzig on October 17.

The Ministry of Environment and Water Resources announced on 14 March 2024 that the government of Kenya will allocate 2.3 billion shillings to rehabilitate the Nairobi River over the next three years. Speaking at a press conference in Nairobi, Cabinet Secretary Aisha Mwangi said the funding will target the removal of industrial waste discharged by tanneries in the Ngong Road area and the construction of a new wastewater treatment facility in Dandora. "This is the largest single investment in urban river restoration in our nation's history," Mwangi stated, adding that the project will be implemented in partnership with the Nairobi Metropolitan Services and the World Bank, which has committed a supplementary grant of 40 million dollars. The Kenya National Environment Trust, led by Executive Director Peter Otieno, welcomed the announcement but urged the ministry to enforce stricter penalties against companies violating the Environmental Management and Coordination Act. Otieno noted that at least 12 factories along the river have been cited for illegal dumping since 2021. Construction on the Dandora facility is expected to begin in September 2024 and conclude by December 2026. Local residents in Mathare, many of whom rely on the river for informal fishing, expressed cautious optimism about the plan. The ministry confirmed that a follow-up progress report will be submitted to Parliament in Nairobi by June 2025.

input: BOSTON, MA -- April 9, 2024 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tregalimab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Coriander Therapeutics, for the treatment of moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis. The trial, conducted between June 2022 and November 2023 at 14 sites across the United States and Canada, enrolled 212 adult patients with confirmed diagnoses of ulcerative colitis. According to lead investigator Dr. Priya Nandakumar, 58 percent of patients receiving tregalimab achieved clinical remission at week 12, compared with 21 percent in the placebo group. The most common adverse events were headache and mild nausea, reported in fewer than 9 percent of participants. Dr. Nandakumar presented the findings on April 8, 2024, at the Digestive Disease Symposium held in Chicago, Illinois. Coriander Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, stated it plans to file for Food and Drug Administration approval by early 2025, pending completion of a Phase 3 trial expected to begin in September 2024. The company was founded in 2016 by Dr. Marcus Ellender, who currently serves as Chief Executive Officer. Shares of Coriander Therapeutics rose 14 percent following the announcement, closing at $37.82 on the Nasdaq. Novartis, a competitor developing a similar biologic called ravalitinib, declined to comment. Funding for the trial was provided in part by a $22 million grant from the National Institutes of Health. Dr. Nandakumar noted that longer-term data, including a 52-week follow-up, will be published later this year in a peer-reviewed gastroenterology journal.

CLEVELAND, Ohio - September 12, 2024 - Ridgeline Dynamics, a manufacturer of industrial hydraulic pumps headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, announced today that it has acquired Bexley Fluid Systems, a privately held supplier based in Akron, Ohio, for approximately 47 million dollars in cash.

The acquisition, expected to close by November 1, 2024, will expand Ridgeline Dynamics' manufacturing footprint and add Bexley's 210 employees to its workforce. Marcus Feldman, Chief Executive Officer of Ridgeline Dynamics, said the deal strengthens the company's position against competitor Talbrook Industrial Group.

"Bexley Fluid Systems has built a reputation over 35 years for precision engineering," Feldman said. "This acquisition allows us to serve customers across the Midwest more efficiently."

As part of the transaction, Bexley's founder and President, Diane Okafor, will join Ridgeline Dynamics as Vice President of Operations, effective November 4, 2024. Okafor founded Bexley Fluid Systems in 1989 in Akron.

Ridgeline Dynamics, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker RDGX, expects the acquisition to increase annual revenue by 12 percent. The company employs roughly 1,800 people across three facilities in Ohio and Indiana.

The transaction was financed through a combination of cash reserves and a 20 million dollar credit facility provided by Lakeshore National Bank.

For more information, contact Priya Nair, Director of Communications, at Ridgeline Dynamics headquarters in Cleveland.

CLEVELAND, OH — October 3, 2024 — Halbrook Industrial Group, a Cleveland-based manufacturer of precision hydraulic components, announced today that it has acquired Meridian Fluid Systems, a privately held supplier based in Tulsa, Oklahoma, for approximately $84 million in cash.

The deal, finalized on October 1, 2024, expands Halbrook's footprint in the Southwest and adds Meridian's 310 employees to its workforce. Halbrook CEO Diane Farrow said the acquisition strengthens the company's ability to serve customers in aerospace and agricultural equipment sectors. "Meridian has built an exceptional reputation over its 22 years in business, and we are proud to welcome their team," Farrow said during a press briefing at Halbrook's headquarters on Chagrin Boulevard.

As part of the transaction, Meridian founder and president Raymond Costa will join Halbrook as Vice President of Southwest Operations, effective October 14, 2024. Costa founded Meridian Fluid Systems in 2002 and grew it into a supplier for John Deere and Boeing.

Halbrook, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker HBLK, reported $412 million in revenue last year and employs roughly 2,600 people across facilities in Ohio, Texas, and Oklahoma. Analysts at Fenwick Capital Partners called the acquisition a strong strategic fit, noting that Meridian's client base overlaps minimally with Halbrook's existing customers, including Caterpillar.

The combined company expects to close its Tulsa distribution center by March 2025, consolidating operations into Meridian's larger manufacturing plant. Financial terms of the deal were disclosed in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on October 2, 2024.

The Ontario Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks announced on May 14, 2024 that it will invest $42 million to upgrade wastewater treatment facilities in Thunder Bay and Sudbury. Minister Andrea Delgado unveiled the plan at a press briefing held at Queen's Park in Toronto, stating that the funding will address chronic overflow issues linked to aging infrastructure built in the 1960s. The ministry's Assistant Deputy Minister, Robert Chen, said the project will be carried out in partnership with Bombardier Environmental Systems, a subsidiary of Bombardier Inc., which was selected through a competitive tender process completed in March 2024. Under the agreement, construction crews will begin work in Thunder Bay on June 3, 2024, with completion targeted for December 2025. The Sudbury facility upgrade will follow in early 2026. Delgado noted that the initiative is expected to reduce untreated sewage discharge into Lake Superior by roughly 30 percent within two years of completion. Environmental groups, including the group Clean North, welcomed the announcement but urged the province to accelerate timelines given repeated advisories issued last summer. The Ministry also confirmed that $6 million of the total funding will be transferred to the City of Thunder Bay by July 1, 2024 to cover preliminary engineering costs. Premier Douglas Ferrand is expected to visit the Thunder Bay site later this month to formally launch construction.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., June 4, 2024 - Arclight Biosciences Inc. announced today that it has acquired NeuroPath Diagnostics Ltd., a Dublin-based developer of blood-based Alzheimer's disease screening tools, for $410 million in cash. The acquisition, finalized on June 3, 2024, expands Arclight's diagnostics portfolio and strengthens its position against competitor Cortex Health Systems.

Under the terms of the agreement, Arclight will pay NeuroPath shareholders $410 million, with the transaction expected to close fully by July 15, 2024. NeuroPath's flagship product, the ClarusScan assay, detects biomarkers linked to Alzheimer's disease with 92 percent accuracy in clinical trials involving 1,200 patients.

"This acquisition allows us to bring early detection tools to millions of patients faster," said Dr. Helena Voss, Chief Executive Officer of Arclight Biosciences, who will oversee the integration from the company's Cambridge headquarters. NeuroPath's founder, Dr. Marcus Byrne, will join Arclight as Senior Vice President of Diagnostics effective July 1, 2024, reporting directly to Dr. Voss.

Arclight Biosciences was founded in 2011 by Dr. Helena Voss and Dr. Samuel Ortiz and is headquartered at 245 Main Street in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The company employs approximately 1,800 people across facilities in Boston, San Diego, and Basel, Switzerland. NeuroPath Diagnostics, founded in 2016, employs 210 researchers in Dublin, Ireland.

Shares of Arclight rose 6.3 percent following the announcement on the Nasdaq exchange. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners called the deal "a decisive move in the neurodegenerative diagnostics race."

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. — October 14, 2024 — Meridian Biosciences Inc. today announced that it has acquired Lantern Diagnostics Ltd., a Dublin-based developer of rapid molecular tests, for approximately $340 million in cash and stock. The transaction, expected to close by December 2, 2024, was approved by both companies' boards on October 10, 2024.

Under the terms of the agreement, Meridian will pay $12.50 per share for all outstanding shares of Lantern Diagnostics. The deal will be funded through a combination of existing cash reserves and a new credit facility arranged by Halloway & Kent Capital Partners.

"This acquisition strengthens our infectious disease portfolio and accelerates our entry into the European diagnostics market," said Dr. Priya Nandakumar, Chief Executive Officer of Meridian Biosciences. Dr. Nandakumar, who has led Meridian since March 2019, will oversee the integration alongside Lantern's founder, Conor Whelan, who will join Meridian as Senior Vice President of European Operations effective January 6, 2025.

Lantern Diagnostics, founded in 2015, employs 210 people across facilities in Dublin and Cork, Ireland. Its flagship product, the RapidScreen PCR Panel, is used in over 3,000 hospitals worldwide to detect pathogens including influenza and respiratory syncytial virus.

Meridian Biosciences, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, reported revenue of $1.8 billion in fiscal year 2023. The company's shares trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker MDBS.

The acquisition remains subject to customary regulatory approvals in the United States and the European Union.

DETROIT, Mich. — Ferramonti Motors, a mid-sized automotive supplier headquartered in Detroit, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in debt and a sharp drop in orders from General Motors and Ford. The filing was submitted in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan.

CEO Marcus Ellery told reporters at a press briefing on Wednesday that the company would continue operations while it restructures. "We expect to emerge from this process by early 2025," Ellery said. Ferramonti employs roughly 2,100 workers across three plants in Michigan and Ohio.

The bankruptcy comes two months after Ferramonti lost a major contract with Stellantis, which accounted for nearly 18 percent of annual revenue. Analyst Priya Nandakumar of Wolverine Capital Partners said the company had struggled since 2022 amid rising steel prices and slowing electric vehicle production.

In a related development, rival parts maker Andersen Component Group announced Thursday it had acquired two Ferramonti facilities in Toledo, Ohio for $58 million, a move expected to save roughly 400 jobs. Andersen CEO Linda Park said the acquisition would expand her company's presence in the Midwest.

Ferramonti's board is expected to meet with creditors on November 12 in Detroit to review the restructuring plan. Ellery, who has led the company since 2019, said layoffs are not currently planned but declined to rule them out.

Cedar Point Robotics, a Pittsburgh-based industrial automation firm, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Vantage Weld Systems for $142 million in cash and stock. The deal, disclosed at Cedar Point's headquarters in the Strip District, marks the company's third acquisition since 2021 and gives it access to Vantage Weld's automated welding lines used by automotive suppliers across the Midwest.

Cedar Point Chief Executive Officer Renata Kessler said the acquisition would boost annual revenue by roughly 18 percent and expand the firm's workforce by 340 employees. "Vantage Weld's engineering team in Toledo, Ohio, gives us capabilities we simply didn't have," Kessler told reporters during a briefing on Wednesday.

Vantage Weld founder and outgoing president Marcus Ollenberg, 52, will join Cedar Point as senior vice president of manufacturing effective November 1. Ollenberg founded Vantage Weld in 2009 and grew it into a supplier for Ford Motor Company and General Motors.

The transaction, financed partly through a $60 million loan from Allegheny National Bank, is expected to close by December 15, pending regulatory review. Analysts at Hargrove Capital Partners called the price "a fair multiple" given Vantage Weld's $95 million in annual sales.

Shares of Cedar Point Robotics, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker CPRX, rose 6.4 percent to $58.10 following the announcement. The company employs about 2,100 people and reported $410 million in revenue last year.

CHICAGO, October 14, 2024 -- Meridian Foods Corporation announced today that it has acquired Blue Harbor Seafood Co., a privately held seafood processor based in Portland, Maine, for $84 million in cash. The transaction closed on October 11, 2024, following approval from Meridian's board of directors.

Blue Harbor Seafood Co., founded in 1987 by Captain Ellen Whitfield, supplies wild-caught scallops and lobster to restaurants across the Northeast United States. The company employs 210 people at its processing facility on Commercial Street in Portland.

"This acquisition strengthens our position in premium seafood and gives Meridian direct access to New England's finest suppliers," said Raymond Ostrowski, Chief Executive Officer of Meridian Foods Corporation. "Ellen and her team have built something extraordinary over the past 37 years."

Ellen Whitfield will remain with the company as President of the newly formed Blue Harbor division, reporting to Meridian's Chief Operating Officer, Denise Falcone. Falcone joined Meridian in March 2019 after previously serving as Vice President of Operations at Coastal Provisions Inc., a competitor of Blue Harbor.

Meridian Foods Corporation, headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, posted revenue of $1.2 billion in fiscal year 2023 and operates 14 processing plants across North America. Shares of Meridian, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker MFC, rose 3.4 percent following the announcement.

The deal is expected to close regulatory review by December 1, 2024, pending clearance from the Federal Trade Commission.

BOSTON, MA -- November 12, 2023 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tebentafusp-plus, an investigational monoclonal antibody developed by Aravela Therapeutics, in patients with metastatic uveal melanoma. The trial, led by Dr. Priya Nakamura, enrolled 214 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and June 2023. Participants who received the drug showed a median overall survival of 21.7 months compared to 13.4 months in the control group receiving standard dacarbazine chemotherapy, a difference the authors called statistically significant (p=0.003). Approximately 62 percent of treated patients experienced grade 1 or 2 cytokine release syndrome, while 8 percent discontinued treatment due to hepatotoxicity. Dr. Nakamura presented the findings on November 10, 2023, at the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer's annual meeting in San Diego, California. Aravela Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the first quarter of 2024. The company was founded in 2015 by Dr. Elena Ruiz and Dr. Thomas Whitfield, and it received $45 million in Series C funding from Blackstone Life Sciences in 2020 to advance the compound through clinical development. Co-author Dr. Marcus Feldman of the University of Heidelberg noted that longer follow-up is needed to assess durability of response. The study was published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology on November 15, 2023, and funded in part by a $3.2 million grant from the National Cancer Institute.

DETROIT, Mich. — Ferrolux Motors announced Thursday that it will acquire battery startup VoltaCell Inc. for $740 million, marking the automaker's largest deal in a decade. The agreement was signed at Ferrolux's headquarters on Woodward Avenue and is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending approval from the Federal Trade Commission.

CEO Marcus Ellenway said the acquisition of VoltaCell, based in Austin, Texas, will accelerate production of solid-state batteries for Ferrolux's upcoming electric pickup, the Ferrolux Ranger EV. "This is about securing our supply chain for the next decade," Ellenway told reporters during a press briefing.

VoltaCell founder Dr. Priya Nathan, who started the company in 2018 with $2 million in seed funding, will join Ferrolux as Chief Battery Officer starting February 1, 2025. Nathan said the two companies had been in talks since June 2024.

Analysts at Continental Capital, a Chicago-based investment firm, project the deal could raise Ferrolux's market share in the EV segment by 6 percent within two years. Shares of Ferrolux rose 4.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.12.

Not everyone welcomed the news. Roughly 200 VoltaCell employees gathered outside the company's Austin plant on Friday to protest potential layoffs, chanting slogans and holding signs reading "Save Our Jobs." Union representative Carla Jimenez said workers fear the merger could eliminate up to 150 positions by mid-2025.

Ferrolux, founded in 1987 by industrialist Walter Ferrell, currently employs 34,000 people across twelve countries.

From: Elena Castillo, Chief Financial Officer
Date: March 14, 2024
Subject: Acquisition of Northgate Bakery Supply

Dear Colleagues,

I am pleased to confirm that Meridian Foods Corp., headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, has completed its acquisition of Northgate Bakery Supply, a privately held distributor based in Toledo, Ohio. The deal, valued at 42 million dollars, was signed yesterday, March 13, 2024, at our Columbus headquarters. Under the terms of the agreement, Meridian will absorb Northgate's fleet of 18 delivery trucks and its 65,000-square-foot warehouse facility on Cherry Street.

Harold Weiss, who founded Northgate Bakery Supply in 1987, will step down as President effective April 1, 2024, but has agreed to remain as a consultant through the end of the year. Meridian's CEO, Rajiv Malhotra, praised the deal, stating that Northgate's supplier relationships with over 300 regional bakeries will strengthen our position against competitors such as Sysco Corporation.

The transaction was financed through a combination of cash reserves and a 15 million dollar credit facility arranged by First Republic Bank. We expect the integration to be complete by September 2024, at which point Northgate will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Foods Corp.

Sonos launched the Arc Ultra soundbar on October 17, 2024, pricing the unit at $999 and positioning it as the flagship replacement for the aging Sonos Arc. I tested the speaker over three weeks at my apartment in Austin, Texas, pairing it with a Samsung QLED television and the Sonos Sub 4. The headline feature, a proprietary bass technology called Sound Motion, delivers noticeably deeper low end without a subwoofer, though I still preferred running it with the Sub 4 for action movies. Setup through the Sonos app took roughly six minutes, and the soundbar automatically calibrated itself to my living room using built-in microphones. Patrick Spence, the company's chief executive officer, said during a press briefing in Santa Barbara that Sonos invested more than $120 million in the Arc Ultra's development after the rocky 2024 app redesign damaged customer trust. That redesign, launched in May 2024, triggered widespread complaints and reportedly cost the company at least 12 percent of its holiday-quarter revenue. Competitor Sonance and industry rival Bose have both introduced rival soundbars this year, intensifying pressure on Sonos ahead of the crucial holiday shopping season. Dolby Atmos support remains a highlight, and the unit integrates cleanly with Apple TV and Amazon Fire TV devices. At $999, the Arc Ultra is not cheap, but after three weeks of daily use I found the audio quality, room calibration, and build materials justified the price for anyone building a serious home theater setup. Recommended, with minor reservations about the cost.

MANCHESTER, England -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice on Saturday to lead his side to a 3-1 victory over Everton at Villa Park, keeping Villa's push for a Champions League spot alive. Watkins opened the scoring in the 14th minute with a low finish from inside the box, then added his second goal just after halftime, in the 52nd minute, following a quick counterattack set up by midfielder John McGinn. Everton pulled one back through Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 63rd minute, but a late strike from substitute Leon Bailey in the 88th minute sealed the win in front of 41,200 fans. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, saying the team had "controlled the tempo for large stretches." The result lifts Aston Villa to fourth place in the Premier League table with 58 points from 29 matches, three points ahead of fifth-placed Tottenham Hotspur. Everton, managed by Sean Dyche, remain in 15th place and face a difficult trip to Anfield to play Liverpool next Saturday, March 9. Aston Villa's next fixture is away at Fulham on Wednesday, March 6, a match that could further boost their European ambitions. The Premier League confirmed that Sunday's fixtures will proceed as scheduled despite forecasts of heavy rain across the Midlands.

The Ohio Department of Transportation announced on March 4, 2024 that it will begin a $42 million reconstruction of the Interstate 70 interchange near Zanesville, Ohio. Director Jack Marchbanks said the project, awarded to Kokosing Industrial, is expected to reduce congestion by 30 percent along a stretch used by roughly 58,000 vehicles daily. Construction crews will start work on May 6, 2024 and the interchange is scheduled to reopen by November 2025. Governor Mike DeWine praised the plan during a press conference in Columbus, stating that the investment reflects the state's commitment to rural infrastructure. Funding for the project comes from a combination of federal highway grants under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and $9 million in state bond revenue approved by the Ohio General Assembly last October. Local officials, including Zanesville Mayor Don Mason, welcomed the announcement, noting that the current interchange has been linked to a 15 percent increase in traffic accidents over the past three years. The Ohio Department of Transportation will hold a public information session on March 20, 2024 at the Zanesville-Muskingum County Public Library to address residents' concerns about detours and noise. Officials estimate the project will create approximately 120 construction jobs over its 18-month timeline. A follow-up progress report is expected in September 2024.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday that it will invest 450 million euros to upgrade rail infrastructure between Lyon and Marseille by 2027. Minister Élise Fontaine unveiled the plan at a press conference in Lyon, stating that the project will reduce travel times by 35 percent and create approximately 2,800 jobs. The initiative, named Rail Connect 2027, is part of a broader national strategy to cut carbon emissions from domestic transport by 40 percent before 2030. SNCF, the state-owned rail operator headquartered in Saint-Denis, will oversee construction alongside contractor Vinci Construction. Fontaine noted that the first phase, covering the 90-kilometer stretch near Valence, is scheduled to begin in March 2025 and finish by October 2026. The Ministry also confirmed that the European Investment Bank will provide a loan of 120 million euros to support the project, with funds to be transferred to SNCF by January 2025. Opposition lawmaker Julien Marchetti criticized the plan on Wednesday, arguing that similar promises made in 2019 were never fully delivered. Marchetti, a member of the Republican Alliance party, called for an independent audit before any funds are disbursed. Fontaine responded that the Ministry welcomes scrutiny and will publish quarterly progress reports starting in April 2025. The announcement comes after President Antoine Rousseau pledged during his re-election campaign to modernize France's rail network within five years.

input: Boston, MA -- November 14, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating lenvatinib combined with pembrolizumab in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez and presented at the American Association for Cancer Research annual meeting, enrolled 142 patients across 9 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2021 and July 2022. Participants receiving the combination therapy showed a median progression-free survival of 8.3 months compared to 4.1 months in the control group treated with sorafenib alone, a 34 percent reduction in risk of disease progression. Dr. Vasquez, an oncologist affiliated with Harvard Medical School, stated that 61 percent of treated patients experienced a partial or complete tumor response. The trial was funded by a $12.4 million grant from the National Cancer Institute and co-sponsored by Merck & Co., which manufactures pembrolizumab under the brand name Keytruda. Eisai Inc., the maker of lenvatinib, supplied the drug under the trade name Lenvima for the study. Grade 3 or higher adverse events, including hypertension and fatigue, occurred in 28 percent of the treatment arm, prompting the data safety monitoring board to recommend continued enrollment without modification. Full results were published on November 10, 2023, in the Journal of Clinical Oncology. Dr. Vasquez noted that a Phase 3 confirmatory trial is planned to begin in early 2024 at additional sites in Germany and Japan, pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY

On October 14, 2024, Judge Marion T. Vasquez sentenced Ricardo Nunes, 41, of Newark, to seven years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of aggravated arson in connection with the March 3, 2023 fire at the Broad Street Warehouse in Newark. Prosecutor Elena Chu of the Essex County District Attorney's Office argued that Nunes deliberately set the blaze using gasoline as an accelerant following a dispute with the building's owner, Delacroix Holdings LLC. The fire caused an estimated $2.3 million in damages and injured one firefighter, Captain Louis Reyes, who suffered smoke inhalation and was hospitalized at Newark Beth Israel Medical Center.

Nunes was arrested on April 9, 2023 by detectives from the Newark Police Department after surveillance footage placed him near the warehouse on the night of the fire. He was formally charged on May 22, 2023 with aggravated arson and reckless endangerment. During the trial, which began September 4, 2024, Judge Vasquez presided while defense attorney Harold Bynes maintained his client's innocence, citing insufficient forensic evidence.

In her sentencing statement, Judge Vasquez said the punishment reflected "the severity of endangering both property and human life." Nunes must also pay $150,000 in restitution to Delacroix Holdings LLC. His attorney has indicated plans to appeal the verdict before the Appellate Division within 45 days.

Fjallraven Kanken Classic 16L Backpack — Sold by Nordic Outfitters ApS, Copenhagen

Nordic Outfitters ApS, headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, is offering the Fjallraven Kanken Classic 16L Backpack in Ox Red for 549 DKK, marked down from 699 DKK. This unit is brand new, still in its original packaging, and was part of a shipment of 4,000 units that Nordic Outfitters received from Fjallraven AB, the Swedish manufacturer based in Ornskoldsvik, on 12 March 2024.

The Kanken 16L features Vinylon F fabric, two front pockets, and padded shoulder straps rated for loads up to 8 kilograms. It measures 38 x 27 x 13 cm and weighs approximately 410 grams. Fjallraven AB was founded in 1960 by Ake Nordin and remains a subsidiary of Fenix Outdoor International AG, listed in Stockholm.

Customers who purchase before 30 April 2024 will receive free shipping within Denmark via PostNord. Nordic Outfitters' store manager, Freja Lindqvist, noted that the Ox Red colorway sold out twice last year within 48 hours of restocking, and the company expects similar demand this spring. The backpack has become popular among university students in Aarhus and Odense, according to a survey cited by the retailer.

Returns are accepted within 30 days of delivery for a full refund of 549 DKK, provided the item is unused and includes the original tags. For bulk orders exceeding 50 units, contact wholesale@nordicoutfitters.dk. Nordic Outfitters also stocks competing brands such as The North Face and Osprey, though staff say the Kanken remains their best-selling backpack for the third consecutive year.

Fjallrune Outdoors, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, has released the Kaldera 45L Alpine Backpack, now available for $189.99 on the company's online store. Launched on March 3, 2024, the Kaldera 45L was designed by lead engineer Ingrid Solheim and tested across six expeditions in the Norwegian fjords before reaching production. The pack weighs 1.8 kilograms and features a titanium-reinforced frame, a 45-liter main compartment, and a removable rain cover rated for 500 millimeters of sustained rainfall. Fjallrune Outdoors was founded in 2011 by Erik Halvorsen, who remains CEO, and the company has since grown into a competitor of Patagonia and Osprey Packs in the technical outdoor gear segment. Each Kaldera 45L ships with a 5-year warranty and is covered under Colorado's standard consumer protection statute. Customers who purchased the discontinued Kaldera 38L model between January 2022 and June 2023 are eligible for a 20 percent loyalty discount through April 30, 2024. Early reviews from Outside Magazine praised the pack's durability, awarding it the 2024 Gear of the Year distinction at a ceremony in Denver on February 14, 2024. Stock is currently limited to 3,000 units, distributed through REI and Fjallrune's flagship store on Pearl Street in Boulder. McCallister's attorney indicated he plans to appeal the verdict to the Arizona Court of Appeals within thirty days. Sonoran Capital Partners, headquartered in Tempe, Arizona, issued a statement saying it has cooperated fully with investigators since 2023 and has strengthened internal compliance controls.

Pixelbook Labs, a Portland-based startup founded in 2019 by former Intel engineer Marcus Whitfield, launched its second-generation e-reader, the InkSlate 2, on September 12, 2024. Priced at $249, the device features a 10.3-inch E Ink Carta 1200 display and ships with 32 gigabytes of storage. I tested the InkSlate 2 for three weeks in Portland, Oregon, and came away impressed by its battery life, which lasted roughly 6 weeks on a single charge under normal reading habits.

The hardware itself is a clear step up from the original InkSlate, released back in 2021. Whitfield told reporters at a press briefing that Pixelbook Labs sold over 40,000 units of the first-generation device, and the company is hoping to double that figure with this release. The InkSlate 2 also adds physical page-turn buttons, a feature many longtime users had requested on forums since 2022.

Software, unfortunately, remains the weak link. The note-taking app crashed twice during my testing, and syncing with Dropbox occasionally failed without warning. Pixelbook Labs says a firmware update is scheduled for October 2024 to address these bugs.

Still, at $249, the InkSlate 2 undercuts Amazon's comparable Kindle Scribe by nearly $100, making it a compelling option for budget-conscious readers. Competitor Rakuten Kobo, headquartered in Toronto, will need to respond if Pixelbook Labs keeps this momentum. For now, I'd recommend the InkSlate 2 to anyone hunting for an affordable, no-frills e-reader.
