input: BOSTON, MA — March 4, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase II clinical trial evaluating tolerizumab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arylex Therapeutics, for the treatment of moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The trial, led by principal investigator Dr. Helena Okafor, enrolled 214 patients across seven sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and January 2024. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of tolerizumab every four weeks showed a 62 percent reduction in disease activity scores compared to 28 percent in the placebo group, according to findings published in The New England Journal of Medicine. Dr. Okafor, an associate professor of rheumatology at Harvard Medical School, stated that the drug's safety profile was consistent with earlier Phase I data, with the most common adverse event being mild injection-site reaction reported in 19 percent of participants. Arylex Therapeutics CEO Marcus Lindqvist said the company plans to initiate a Phase III trial in the fourth quarter of 2024, pending a $45 million funding round led by venture capital firm Solstice Partners. Novartis, a competitor in the autoimmune disease space, has reportedly expressed interest in licensing discussions, though no formal agreement has been signed. The Food and Drug Administration granted tolerizumab Breakthrough Therapy designation in September 2023, potentially accelerating its regulatory review. If approved, tolerizumab could become the first new mechanism-of-action therapy for rheumatoid arthritis in over a decade, offering an alternative for patients who do not respond adequately to existing tumor necrosis factor inhibitors.

Under the agreement, Halcyon's 65 employees will join Meridian's Autonomous Systems division, and Halcyon founder Priya Raman will take on the newly created role of Vice President of Sensor Engineering, reporting directly to Whitfield. Ingrid Halvorsen (born 14 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist and academic best known for her research on cold-water coral reefs in the North Atlantic. She earned her doctorate in oceanography from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Bergen the following year as a Research Scientist. In 1998, Halvorsen was appointed Director of the Institute's Deep Sea Ecology Programme, a position she held for eleven years.

Her 1994 expedition aboard the research vessel Havforsker to the Sula Reef off the coast of Trøndelag produced the first detailed maps of Norwegian cold-water coral habitats, work later published in the journal Marine Ecology Progress Series. In 2003, she co-founded the Nordic Coral Conservation Trust in Trondheim with fellow biologist Erik Fossum, an organization that has since secured protection for over 40 reef sites.

Halvorsen received the Fridtjof Nansen Award from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in 2011 for her contributions to marine ecology. She married geologist Peter Solheim in 1989, and the couple's daughter, Marte Solheim, is now a climate researcher at the Norwegian Polar Institute in Tromsø.

In September 2016, Halvorsen retired from the Institute of Marine Research after 30 years of service. She continues to serve on the advisory board of the Nordic Coral Conservation Trust and has published more than 70 peer-reviewed papers over her career.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Aldergrove City FC clinched a dramatic 2-1 victory over Riverside United on Saturday at Bellhaven Park, moving the club into second place in the Northern Football League. Striker Damon Reyes scored the winning goal in the 87th minute, his 12th of the season, after collecting a pass from midfielder Theo Okafor. Riverside United had taken an early lead through captain Marcus Bell, who converted a penalty in the 23rd minute, but Aldergrove City equalized just before halftime when defender Sami Kovacevic headed in a corner kick.

Head coach Elena Marsh praised her team's resilience after the match. "We showed real character tonight," Marsh said during the post-match press conference at Bellhaven Park. "Damon has been outstanding all season, and this win puts us firmly in the promotion race."

The victory extended Aldergrove City's unbeaten run to eight matches, a streak that began on August 19, 2023. Approximately 14,500 fans attended the fixture, a season-high for the club. Riverside United manager Paul Dunham admitted his side struggled to contain Reyes in the closing stages, calling the late goal "a hard pill to swallow."

Aldergrove City will next travel to Manchester on October 21, 2023, to face Oakwood Rangers, while Riverside United returns home to host Grantham Athletic. The Northern Football League table now shows Aldergrove City with 24 points from 12 matches, just two points behind leaders Castlefield Town.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google's Wearable Finally Feels Complete

By Marcus Delaney, October 14, 2024

After two weeks testing the Pixel Watch 3 in Austin, Texas, I'm convinced Google has closed the gap with the Apple Watch. Released on September 20, 2024, the device starts at $349 for the 41mm aluminum case and climbs to $499 for the 45mm LTE model. Google announced the watch alongside the Pixel 9 lineup at a press event in Mountain View, California, on August 13, 2024.

The standout upgrade is battery life: Google's Wear OS 5 software, combined with a new low-power display driver, pushed my unit past 30 hours on a single charge, up from roughly 24 hours on last year's Pixel Watch 2. The 45mm model's AMOLED panel now hits 2,000 nits, making outdoor runs along Lady Bird Lake far more legible than before.

Fitbit, which Google acquired back in 2021, still powers the health tracking. Sleep apnea detection, developed with input from cardiologist Dr. Priya Nandakumar of the Cleveland Clinic, worked reliably during my trial, flagging two nights of disrupted breathing that I later confirmed with a home sleep study.

Competitor Samsung, which sells the Galaxy Watch7, still edges out Google on raw processor speed thanks to its Exynos W1000 chip, but Google's software polish narrows that gap considerably.

At $349, the base Pixel Watch 3 undercuts the $399 Apple Watch Series 10 while offering comparable fitness tracking. For Android users, this is now the easiest recommendation Google has ever made.

input: The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday that it will invest 420 million euros to upgrade rail infrastructure across the Lombardy region of Italy by December 2026. Minister Elena Bassi confirmed the plan during a press briefing in Milan, stating that the funds will modernize 38 kilometers of track between the Milano Centrale station and the town of Monza. The project, named Rete Veloce, will be carried out by Ferrovie Nazionali S.p.A., a state-owned company headquartered in Rome. According to Bassi, the initiative is expected to reduce commuter travel times by 25 percent and create approximately 1,200 jobs over the next three years. Deputy Minister Carlo Rinaldi, who joined the briefing, emphasized that the government has already signed a supply contract worth 90 million euros with Alstom Italia, a subsidiary of the French manufacturer Alstom SA, to deliver 15 new electric trains by mid-2025. Bassi added that construction crews will begin work at the Monza depot on 3 March 2025, weather permitting. Opposition lawmaker Giulia Ferretti criticized the plan on Wednesday, arguing in Parliament that similar rail projects announced in 2019 were never completed. The Ministry responded that an independent audit, to be conducted by the firm Deloitte Italia, will monitor spending quarterly starting in June 2025 to ensure transparency and accountability throughout the project's duration.

CLEVELAND, OH - September 12, 2024 - Buckeye Robotics Inc., a Cleveland-based manufacturer of industrial automation systems, announced today that it has acquired Marlow Precision Tools, a privately held machine-tool maker based in Akron, Ohio, for $42 million in cash. The deal closed on September 10, 2024, and is expected to add approximately 60 employees to Buckeye Robotics' workforce.

Under the agreement, Marlow Precision Tools will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Buckeye Robotics, retaining its Akron facility and its founder, Diane Wexler, who will serve as Vice President of Manufacturing Operations effective October 1, 2024. Wexler founded Marlow Precision Tools in 2009 and grew the company into a supplier of precision components for aerospace and automotive clients across the Midwest.

"This acquisition strengthens our supply chain and gives us direct control over critical tooling components," said Raymond Ott, Chief Executive Officer of Buckeye Robotics, speaking at a press conference held at the company's headquarters in Cleveland. "Diane and her team have built something exceptional over the past fifteen years."

Buckeye Robotics, which was founded in 1998 by engineer Harold Finch, employs roughly 1,200 people and reported $310 million in revenue last year. The company competes with Detroit-based Ironclad Automation for contracts in the automotive sector. Shares of Buckeye Robotics, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker BKRB, rose 4.2 percent following the announcement.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Vantage Robotics, the warehouse-automation startup founded by Priya Nair in 2019, just announced it's being acquired by Locus Freight Systems for $340 million. Deal closes March 15, 2024.

2/ Priya, who's been CEO since day one, will stay on as Head of Robotics Strategy at Locus. She told employees in a memo Tuesday that the 85-person team will relocate from their South Congress office to Locus's Dallas headquarters by June.

CHICAGO, Aug 14 (Reuters-style) — Deere & Company said Wednesday it will acquire GrainTrack Systems, a Peoria-based agricultural software startup, for $412 million in cash, as the farm equipment maker pushes deeper into precision agriculture. The deal, announced by Deere Chief Executive John May, is expected to close by October 1 pending regulatory approval. GrainTrack, founded in 2016 by former Caterpillar engineer Priya Chandrasekaran, makes sensors and cloud software that help farmers track soil moisture across thousands of acres. Chandrasekaran will join Deere as Vice President of Digital Agriculture, reporting directly to May, according to a statement released in Moline, Illinois, where Deere is headquartered. Shares of Deere rose 3.2% to $398.50 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of rival Caterpillar slipped 0.8%. Analyst Rebecca Tran of Morgan Stanley called the acquisition "a smart bolt-on that strengthens Deere's software moat against competitors like AGCO and CNH Industrial." GrainTrack currently employs 140 people across offices in Peoria and Ames, Iowa. Deere said it does not expect layoffs and plans to retain GrainTrack's engineering team intact. The company financed the purchase using existing cash reserves, avoiding new debt issuance. Deere's board approved the transaction on August 12 after a two-week due diligence review. The acquisition marks Deere's third technology purchase in eighteen months, following its 2023 purchase of sensor maker Sabanto for $190 million.

Boston, MA -- April 3, 2024 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tenapavir-B, an oral chemical compound targeting metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti and published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Germany between January 2022 and September 2023. Patients receiving tenapavir-B in combination with standard gemcitabine therapy showed a median overall survival of 11.4 months, compared with 7.8 months in the control group receiving gemcitabine alone, a difference the authors called statistically significant (p=0.003). Grade 3 adverse events, primarily neutropenia and fatigue, occurred in 18 percent of the treatment arm versus 9 percent of controls. Novaris Therapeutics, headquartered in Basel, Switzerland, funded the trial and plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the fourth quarter of 2024. Dr. Marchetti presented the findings on April 2, 2024, at the American Association for Cancer Research annual meeting in San Diego, California, where she received the Meyer Prize for Translational Research from the association. "These results represent a meaningful step forward for patients with limited options," Marchetti said. Novaris shares rose 6 percent on the Zurich exchange following the announcement. The company, founded in 2011 by biochemist Dr. Hans Feldmann, previously acquired Rheinbio AG in 2019 to expand its oncology pipeline. A larger phase 3 trial of 600 patients is expected to begin enrollment in early 2025 at sites including Massachusetts General Hospital and Charite Berlin.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. RG24-118732 - The People v. Marcus Delaney Whitfield

On Tuesday, June 11, 2024, Judge Patricia Nakamura presided over a sentencing hearing at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland. Defendant Marcus Delaney Whitfield, 41, was convicted on May 2, 2024 of grand theft after prosecutors from the Alameda County District Attorney's Office, led by Deputy District Attorney Sarah Coenen, proved he embezzled $486,000 from his former employer, Bayline Freight Logistics Inc., between January 2021 and March 2023. Whitfield had worked as the company's Chief Financial Officer since March 2019.

Judge Nakamura sentenced Whitfield to four years in state prison and ordered restitution of $486,000 payable to Bayline Freight Logistics Inc. within sixty days. Defense attorney Raymond Ochoa argued for probation, citing his client's lack of prior record, but the court rejected the request.

According to trial testimony, Whitfield transferred stolen funds into an account at Meridian Trust Bank under the name of a shell company, Coastal Ventures LLC, which he had founded in December 2020. Bayline Freight Logistics Inc., headquartered in Fremont, California, discovered the discrepancy during an internal audit in April 2023 and notified the Alameda County Sheriff's Office, which arrested Whitfield on July 14, 2023 at his home in Pleasanton.

The case, formally titled People v. Whitfield, will be referenced in future filings under California Penal Code Section 487.

Dayton, Ohio — Meridian Freightworks, a mid-sized logistics carrier headquartered in Dayton, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $42 million in outstanding debt and a sharp decline in shipping volumes. CEO Patricia Halvorsen announced the filing at a press conference at the company's Springboro Pike facility, saying the firm would continue operations while restructuring under court supervision.

Meridian Freightworks, founded in 1987 by Walter Ganz, employs roughly 1,100 workers across seven states and operates a fleet of 340 tractor-trailers. Halvorsen said the company had been squeezed by rising diesel costs and a 30 percent drop in freight demand since 2023. "We are not shutting our doors," Halvorsen told reporters. "This filing gives us breathing room to renegotiate contracts and protect jobs."

The Chapter 11 petition, filed in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Ohio, lists General Motors and Procter & Gamble among Meridian's largest creditors, owed a combined $9.3 million for unpaid transport services. Judge Rebecca Aldrich is scheduled to hold an initial hearing on March 14.

Industry analyst Tom Chessley of Cleveland-based Harrow Logistics Group said the bankruptcy reflects broader turmoil in the trucking sector, noting that rival carrier Yellow Corporation collapsed in 2023. Meridian's board has hired restructuring firm Danvers & Cole to oversee the process, with a reorganization plan expected by June 1.

On Tuesday, March 11, 2025, Judge Miriam Colston sentenced Devon Alvarez, 34, to 7 years in state prison after a jury convicted him of embezzlement and wire fraud in connection with his former position as Chief Financial Officer of Larkspur Robotics Inc., a Sunnyvale-based manufacturer of warehouse automation equipment. Prosecutor Anita Reyes of the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office argued that Alvarez diverted $2.3 million from company accounts between January 2021 and September 2023, funneling the funds through a shell company registered in Delaware. Defense attorney Warren Nkosi contended his client acted under duress from former CEO Priya Sethi, though Sethi was never charged.

Alvarez was arrested on October 4, 2023, by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation at San Jose International Airport as he attempted to board a flight to Lisbon, Portugal. He was formally charged on November 15, 2023, with one count of embezzlement and two counts of wire fraud. During Monday's trial hearing, held at the downtown San Jose courthouse, the prosecution presented bank records showing transfers to an account at Meridian Trust Bank.

Larkspur Robotics, which was acquired by Boston-based conglomerate Halden Industries in 2022 for $410 million, issued a statement saying it had cooperated fully with investigators. Company spokesperson Grace Whitfield said the firm has since implemented new financial controls. Alvarez's sentence includes restitution of $2.3 million and 3 years of supervised release following his prison term.

MADRID, October 12, 2024 -- Real Madrid edged Atletico Madrid 2-1 in a tense Champions League clash at the Santiago Bernabeu on Saturday, with Jude Bellingham scoring the decisive goal in the 84th minute. Vinicius Junior opened the scoring in the 23rd minute, finishing a swift counterattack set up by Toni Kroos, before Atletico's Antoine Griezmann equalized with a penalty just before halftime. Bellingham's late strike, a curling effort from 18 yards, sent the 78,000 fans inside the Bernabeu into raptures.

Manager Carlo Ancelotti praised his squad's resilience after the match, telling reporters, "We showed character tonight. Atletico made it difficult, but we found a way." Atletico coach Diego Simeone declined to blame the referee for the penalty decision, though he expressed frustration over a missed offside call earlier in the second half.

The win moves Real Madrid to the top of Group C with 10 points from four matches, three points clear of Atletico in second place. Real Madrid will next travel to Milan on October 22 to face Inter Milan, while Atletico hosts RB Leipzig at the Metropolitano Stadium the same week.

Elsewhere, Barcelona announced that midfielder Pedri will miss the next six weeks with a hamstring injury sustained during training on Thursday, a blow to coach Hansi Flick's plans ahead of El Clasico on October 26. Barcelona's medical staff confirmed the diagnosis at the club's Ciutat Esportiva facility in Sant Joan Despi.

Boston, MA -- November 4, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tenavicimab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Somerville-based biotech firm Kestrel Therapeutics, for treatment of relapsed acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The randomized, double-blind study enrolled 214 adult patients across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2021 and July 2022. Lead investigator Dr. Priya Ramaswamy, a hematologist-oncologist at Massachusetts General Hospital, presented the findings at the American Society of Hematology conference held in San Diego on December 9, 2023. According to Dr. Ramaswamy, patients receiving tenavicimab in combination with venetoclax achieved a complete remission rate of 47%, compared to 24% among patients receiving standard chemotherapy alone. Median overall survival reached 18.6 months in the treatment arm versus 10.2 months in the control arm, a difference the authors called statistically significant (p=0.003). Grade 3 or higher adverse events, primarily neutropenia and thrombocytopenia, occurred in 38% of treated patients. Kestrel Therapeutics, founded in 2017 by former Genentech researcher Dr. Alan Feldstein, plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial in early 2024 pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The company received $85 million in Series C funding in June 2023 from Sequoia Capital and a consortium of biotech investors to support late-stage development. Dr. Feldstein stated that if Phase 3 results confirm the current data, Kestrel intends to file a Biologics License Application by 2026. Independent experts, including Dr. Wen-Hui Zhang of Stanford University, cautioned that longer follow-up is needed to assess durability of remission and long-term toxicity before the therapy can be considered for broader clinical adoption.

Everton manager Sean Dyche said his side's away form remained a concern, with the club now winless in six matches on the road. The result lifts Aston Villa to 58 points from 29 games, three points behind third-placed Liverpool. Everton, still fighting to avoid relegation after a points deduction earlier this season, remain in 15th place with 30 points. Aston Villa will next travel to face Tottenham Hotspur on April 21 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, while Everton host Newcastle United on the same date at Goodison Park.

The Ministry of Environment and Water Resources announced on 14 March 2024 that the Republic of Kenya will invest 3.2 billion Kenyan shillings in flood-mitigation infrastructure along the Tana River basin. Speaking at a press briefing in Nairobi, Minister Wanjiru Kamau said the funding, disbursed through the National Treasury, will finance new drainage channels and early-warning systems following the floods that killed 47 people in Garissa County last November. "We cannot allow another disaster like the one in Garissa to repeat itself," Kamau stated. The initiative, named the Tana Basin Resilience Programme, will be implemented jointly with the Kenya Red Cross Society and the World Bank, which has pledged an additional 15 million dollars in concessional financing. Engineer Peter Otieno, appointed as Programme Director on 1 April 2024, will oversee construction of 12 new flood barriers in Tana River County over the next 18 months. The Ministry also confirmed that Governor Ali Roba of Garissa County met with Kamau in Nairobi on 20 March 2024 to coordinate resettlement plans for 3,000 displaced families. Separately, the Kenya Meteorological Department warned that above-average rainfall is expected between April and June 2024, raising concerns of renewed flooding across the Rift Valley region. Officials urged residents near riverbanks to relocate temporarily to designated camps in Wajir and Isiolo counties.

Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1958 in Turin, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for her work on seismic-resistant bridge design. She earned a degree in civil engineering from the Politecnico di Torino in 1981 and later joined Fiat Engineering as a junior analyst in 1983. In 1990 Marchetti co-founded Marchetti & Bruno Ingegneria in Milan with colleague Paolo Bruno, a firm that specialized in retrofitting historic viaducts across northern Italy. The company grew steadily, and by 2002 it employed 140 engineers and had been contracted by the Italian Ministry of Infrastructure to assess damage after the Molise earthquake of 2002.

Marchetti's most cited achievement came in 2005, when she led the redesign of the Ponte Vecchio approach viaduct in Florence, a project funded with 12 million euros from the regional government of Tuscany. In 2011 she was appointed Chief Technical Officer of Autostrade Ingegneria, a subsidiary of Autostrade per l'Italia headquartered in Rome, a position she held until stepping down in 2018 to return to academic research.

In 2015 the Italian Association of Structural Engineers awarded Marchetti the Galileo Medal for Engineering Excellence in Bologna, citing her contributions to earthquake-resilient infrastructure. She married architect Davide Conti in 1992, and the couple's daughter, Giulia Conti, was born in 1995 in Milan. Marchetti currently teaches at the Politecnico di Milano and continues to consult on bridge safety projects across Europe.

To: Marcus Webb, Chief Financial Officer, Delridge Manufacturing Inc.
From: Priya Nair, Vice President of Corporate Development, Kestrel Holdings LLC
Date: April 9, 2024
Subject: Completion of Acquisition of Alden Tool Works

Please let me know if Delridge Manufacturing Inc. requires any documentation for your records, as this deal may affect our supplier arrangement with your company.

Best regards,
Priya Nair
Vice President of Corporate Development
Kestrel Holdings LLC

MANCHESTER, September 14, 2024 -- Aston Villa striker Marcus Odell scored twice as his side defeated Everton 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, lifting the club to third place in the Premier League table. Odell, 27, opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low left-footed strike, then added his second just before halftime after a quick counterattack set up by midfielder Youri Bakayoko. Everton's Dominic Reyes pulled one back in the 58th minute with a header from a corner kick, but Aston Villa restored their two-goal cushion when substitute Tomas Krejci finished from close range in the 81st minute. The match, played in front of 41,700 spectators, was Odell's fourth multi-goal game of the season. Aston Villa manager Unai Fernandez praised his squad's discipline after the game, saying the team had "grown up a lot since last year." Everton manager Colin Marsh admitted his defense was exposed too easily, calling the second-half collapse "unacceptable at this level." The win moves Aston Villa to 16 points from seven matches, three points behind leaders Liverpool. Everton, meanwhile, remain 15th with just seven points and face relegation-threatened Burnley on September 21 at Turf Moor. Aston Villa will next travel to face Newcastle United on September 28. The Premier League confirmed no disciplinary action was taken following two yellow cards issued during the match, one to each side.

Cedar Point Robotics, a Pittsburgh-based industrial automation firm, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Trellis Vision Systems for $214 million in cash, expanding its footprint in machine-vision inspection technology. The deal, confirmed at a press briefing in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, marks Cedar Point Robotics' third acquisition since its founding in 2016 by chief executive Marcus Delaney.

Under the agreement, Trellis Vision Systems, headquartered in Austin, Texas, will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary, retaining its 180 employees and its founder, Priya Nandakumar, who will join Cedar Point Robotics as Executive Vice President of Product starting November 4. Nandakumar previously served as Chief Technology Officer at Trellis Vision Systems since 2018.

"This acquisition strengthens our supply chain and lets us offer end-to-end inspection systems to automotive and electronics manufacturers," Delaney said during the announcement. Analysts at Renfield Capital Partners estimated the deal would add roughly $38 million in annual recurring revenue by 2026.

Cedar Point Robotics shares rose 6.2 percent on the Nasdaq following the news, closing at $47.85. The company, which competes with Boston-based Anthem Automation Corp., reported $412 million in revenue last fiscal year. The transaction is expected to close by December 15, pending regulatory review by the Federal Trade Commission.

Delaney added that Cedar Point Robotics plans to retain Trellis Vision Systems' Austin office and expand hiring there by 25 percent over the next twelve months, part of a broader push into the Texas manufacturing corridor.

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY — On October 14, 2024, Judge Marion T. Kowalski sentenced Raymond DeLuca, 47, of Newark, to 63 months in federal-equivalent state custody after a jury found him guilty of embezzlement and wire fraud connected to his former role as Chief Financial Officer of Harlan Freight Systems, a logistics firm headquartered in Elizabeth, New Jersey. Prosecutor Angela Ruiz of the Essex County Prosecutor's Office told the court that between March 2021 and August 2023, DeLuca diverted approximately $2.4 million from company accounts into shell entities registered under his brother's name, Vincent DeLuca. The scheme was uncovered after an internal audit by Meridian Compliance Partners flagged irregular transfers to an account at Coastal Trust Bank. DeLuca was arrested on November 9, 2023, at his residence on Ferry Street by agents of the New Jersey Division of Criminal Justice on charges of theft by deception and money laundering. During Monday's hearing at the Wilentz Justice Complex in Newark, defense attorney Priya Nathan argued for leniency, citing her client's cooperation, but Judge Kowalski rejected the request, calling the conduct "a calculated betrayal of shareholder trust." Harlan Freight Systems, which was acquired by Bristol Logistics Group in June 2022, issued a statement saying it had strengthened internal controls since the fraud was discovered. The company's current CEO, Denise Okafor, said restitution proceedings would begin within 90 days. DeLuca must also pay $1.8 million in restitution to Harlan Freight Systems and Bristol Logistics Group under the terms of the sentence.

input: MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City midfielder Rodrigo Hernandez scored twice as City defeated Everton 3-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, extending their unbeaten Premier League run to eleven matches. Manager Pep Guardiola praised his side's second-half discipline after Everton striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin had leveled the score at 1-1 in the 52nd minute. Erling Haaland opened the scoring for City in the 23rd minute, converting a low cross from Kevin De Bruyne, before Rodrigo restored the lead in the 68th minute and sealed victory with a curling strike in stoppage time. The win moved City to 24 points, three clear of second-placed Arsenal, who face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Sunday. Everton manager Sean Dyche said his team "competed well but lacked composure in the final third." Attendance at the Etihad Stadium was announced at 53,412. City's next fixture is away to RB Leipzig in the UEFA Champions League on October 17, a match Guardiola confirmed will see Kyle Walker return from a hamstring injury sustained on September 30. Meanwhile, City's ownership group, City Football Group, announced a new sponsorship agreement worth $45 million annually with a Japanese electronics firm, Nexlan Corp, set to begin in January 2024. The club also confirmed defender Nathan Ake signed a contract extension until 2027, a deal reportedly worth £120,000 per week.

BOSTON, MA — September 12, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating lenocitinib, an oral JAK inhibitor developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arborvax Therapeutics, for the treatment of moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis. The randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study enrolled 214 adult patients across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2022 and January 2023. Dr. Elena Marsh, the trial's lead investigator and a dermatologist at Massachusetts General Hospital, presented findings at the American Academy of Dermatology conference in Chicago. Patients receiving 30 milligrams of lenocitinib daily for 16 weeks achieved a 68 percent reduction in Eczema Area and Severity Index scores, compared with 24 percent in the placebo group. Approximately 12 percent of participants in the treatment arm reported mild headache, and 3 percent discontinued due to nausea. Arborvax Therapeutics, founded in 2019 by former Pfizer executive Daniel Ruiz, plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial in early 2024 pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The company raised $85 million in Series C financing led by Bay Bridge Ventures in July 2023 to fund late-stage development. Dr. Marsh noted that lenocitinib's selectivity for JAK1 may reduce the systemic side effects associated with older therapies such as tofacitinib. The study was published in the Journal of Clinical Dermatology on September 10, 2023, and was funded in part by a grant from the National Institutes of Health. Analysts at Baird & Co. suggested the data could position Arborvax as a competitor to Sanofi's Dupixent in the growing atopic dermatitis market.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google's Best Wearable Yet, But Battery Life Still Lags

On October 14, 2024, I strapped on the Pixel Watch 3 at my apartment in Austin, Texas, and wore it for three weeks straight. Google, headquartered in Mountain View, California, priced the 45mm LTE model at $429.99, positioning it squarely against the Apple Watch Series 10 and Samsung's Galaxy Watch7.

The new Actua display, 34% brighter than last year's panel, makes outdoor readability genuinely excellent. Fitbit's running coach feature, inherited after Google's 2019 acquisition of Fitbit for roughly $2.1 billion, now offers real-time pace guidance that rivals dedicated running watches like the Garmin Forerunner 265.

Battery life, however, remains the weak point. Google claims 24 hours, but with the always-on display enabled I averaged just 16 hours before reaching for a charger. During a hike near Zilker Park, the watch dropped 40% battery in under five hours with GPS and music streaming active.

I spoke briefly with Sandra Liu, a product manager at Google who joined the Fitbit team in March 2021, at a demo event in San Francisco last month. She noted that a software update planned for December 2024 aims to improve power efficiency by 15%.

At $429.99, the Pixel Watch 3 is a capable, polished device, but anyone who forgets to charge nightly will be disappointed. Recommended only for those who don't mind daily charging.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT — PUBLIC NOTICE
Ottawa, Ontario — September 12, 2024

The Ministry of Transport today announced a CAD 240 million investment to upgrade rail safety infrastructure along the Toronto–Montreal corridor. Minister Aline Bouchard confirmed that Via Rail Canada will begin installation of new positive train control systems at 14 stations, starting with Union Station in Toronto on October 3, 2024. The project follows a Justice.TrialHearing-adjacent inquiry into the February 2023 derailment near Kingston, Ontario, in which three passengers were injured when a freight car struck a maintenance vehicle on the tracks.

"This funding reflects our commitment to the Railway Safety Act and to protecting every commuter who relies on this network," said Bouchard during a press briefing at the Sir John A. Macdonald Building. Deputy Minister Ravi Chandran, who joined the Ministry in June 2022 after serving as Chief Operating Officer at Bombardier Transportation, will oversee implementation.

The Ministry also confirmed that CN Rail has agreed to contribute CAD 35 million toward signal upgrades between Belleville and Kingston by March 2025. Officials noted that Transport Canada will conduct quarterly audits, with the first review scheduled for December 2024. Approximately 1,200 workers are expected to be employed on the project over the next 18 months.

Critics, including the Canadian Union of Public Employees, held a demonstration outside Parliament Hill on September 10, 2024, demanding faster timelines. The Ministry says full completion is targeted for 2027.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City midfielder Rodri scored twice as the reigning champions defeated Everton 3-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, extending their unbeaten league run to nine matches. Rodri opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low strike from the edge of the box, and doubled his tally just before halftime after a rebound off goalkeeper Jordan Pickford. Everton's Dominic Calvert-Lewin pulled one back in the 58th minute, heading home a corner from Jack Harrison, but substitute Jeremy Doku restored City's two-goal cushion in the 81st minute with a curling effort from outside the area. Manager Pep Guardiola praised his squad's resilience after the match, saying the team had shown "character in a difficult week." The win moves City to 22 points from eight games, three points clear of Arsenal at the top of the Premier League table. Everton manager Sean Dyche admitted his side struggled to contain Rodri in midfield, calling the Spaniard "the best holding midfielder in the world right now." Attendance at the Etihad Stadium was announced at 53,112. City's next fixture is away at Chelsea on October 21, while Everton will host Brentford the following weekend. Rodri, who joined City from Atletico Madrid in 2019 for a reported 70 million euros, has now scored five goals in all competitions this season.

Manchester City edged Aston Villa 2-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, October 14, 2023, to move top of the Premier League table. Erling Haaland opened the scoring in the 23rd minute, converting a low cross from Kevin De Bruyne after a swift counterattack. Villa responded through Ollie Watkins, who equalized in the 51st minute with a close-range finish. The decisive goal came in the 78th minute when substitute Jack Grealish curled a shot past goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez, sparking wild celebrations among the 53,000 fans in attendance. City manager Pep Guardiola praised his side's resilience after the match, saying the team "showed real character" against a physical Villa side managed by Unai Emery. The win extended City's unbeaten run to eleven matches across all competitions and moved them three points clear of Arsenal, who host Chelsea next weekend at the Emirates Stadium. Haaland now has 12 goals in 9 league appearances this season, putting him on pace to challenge his own Premier League scoring record. Villa, who remain sixth in the standings, will look to bounce back on October 21 when they travel to Tottenham Hotspur Stadium to face Tottenham. Grealish, who left Villa for City in 2021 for a reported fee of £100 million, received a mixed reception from the away end but insisted afterward that he "still loves this club." The Premier League confirmed no further disciplinary action following a minor pitch-side scuffle between coaching staff late in the second half.

Marguerite Delacroix (born 14 March 1927 in Lyon, France) was a French microbiologist whose work on antibiotic resistance reshaped clinical treatment protocols across Europe. She earned her doctorate from the Sorbonne in 1951 and joined the Institut Pasteur in Paris that same year as a research assistant. In 1958, Delacroix was promoted to Head of the Bacteriology Division, a position she held for seventeen years.

Her landmark 1963 paper on Staphylococcus aureus resistance mechanisms, published in the journal Nature, led to her being awarded the Prix Pasteur by the Institut Pasteur in 1965 in Paris. Three years later, in 1968, she co-founded the Fondation Delacroix pour la Microbiologie alongside her longtime colleague Dr. Henri Rousseau, with initial funding of 2 million francs from the French Ministry of Health.

Delacroix married physicist Jean-Paul Mercier in 1955; the couple had two children, including their son Philippe Mercier, who later became a virologist at the Pasteur Institute himself. She left her post at the Institut Pasteur in 1975 to become Director of Research at the World Health Organization in Geneva, Switzerland, a role she held until her retirement in 1990.

In 1998, the French government awarded her the Legion of Honour for her contributions to public health. Marguerite Delacroix died on 9 November 2004 in Lyon at the age of 77, following a brief illness.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results of a phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolvexib, an investigational oral chemical compound targeting interleukin-6 signaling, for the treatment of moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of tolvexib daily showed a 62 percent reduction in disease activity scores at week 24, compared with 28 percent in the placebo group, a difference the authors called clinically meaningful. Dr. Marsh presented the findings on March 14, 2024 at a meeting of the American College of Rheumatology in Boston. "These results suggest tolvexib could offer a needed alternative for patients who fail methotrexate," she said. The trial was sponsored by Arcadia Therapeutics, a biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, which licensed the compound from Nordholm Biosciences of Copenhagen, Denmark in 2021 for an upfront payment of 45 million dollars. Arcadia's chief executive, Raj Patel, stated the company plans to begin a phase 3 trial in early 2025 pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Common adverse events included mild infections and elevated liver enzymes, reported in 9 percent of treated patients; no deaths occurred during the study. Arcadia's shares rose 14 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement. The full data set will be published in The New England Journal of Medicine later this year.

Pixel Watch 3, Fitness Tracking Reconsidered

By Priya Nair, October 4, 2024

Google launched the Pixel Watch 3 on September 10, 2024, at a press event in Mountain View, California, and after three weeks of daily use I have mixed feelings. The $349.99 model I tested, the 41mm aluminum case in Moonstone, was supplied by Google's press office in Sunnyvale.

Battery life is the headline improvement: Google claims 36 hours, and in my testing with always-on display enabled I got roughly 28 hours before needing the charger. The new Loss of Pulse Detection feature, developed with input from Fitbit engineers, worked reliably during a simulated test at a clinic in Palo Alto, though it is not yet cleared by the FDA for diagnostic use.

Competitor devices, notably the Apple Watch Series 10 and the Samsung Galaxy Watch 7, still edge out the Pixel Watch 3 on app selection. Sundar Pichai, Google's CEO, mentioned during the launch that Fitbit's acquisition by Google in 2021 continues to shape the wearable roadmap, and Fitbit co-founder James Park briefly joined him onstage.

At $349.99 for the smaller case and $399.99 for the 45mm version, pricing is steep next to the $329 Galaxy Watch 7. Still, for existing Pixel phone owners, the integration is compelling enough that I'm cautiously recommending it, with a full rating to follow after 30 days of testing.

DENVER, Colorado — Frontier Copper Corp. announced on Tuesday that it has completed the acquisition of Silverline Mining Ltd., a privately held mining company based in Reno, Nevada, for approximately 412 million dollars in cash and stock. The deal, first disclosed on March 4, closed on April 18 after clearing regulatory review by the Federal Trade Commission.

Under the agreement, Frontier Copper will pay 6.75 dollars per share, a 22 percent premium over Silverline's closing price the day before the announcement. Frontier Copper CEO Diane Marsh said the acquisition strengthens the company's position as a leading supplier of copper to electric vehicle manufacturers. "This transaction gives us direct access to Silverline's flagship Comstock Ridge deposit, which contains an estimated 3.2 million tons of copper ore," Marsh said during a call with analysts.

Silverline's founder and outgoing chief executive, Raymond Ochoa, will join Frontier Copper's board of directors as part of the deal, effective May 1. Ochoa founded Silverline Mining in 2009 and grew it into a company employing roughly 640 workers across three sites in Nevada and Arizona.

Analysts at Kessler Brothers, a New York investment bank, noted that the merger positions Frontier Copper as a direct competitor to Blackstone Ore Partners, which has dominated the western copper supply chain since 2015. Shares of Frontier Copper rose 4.3 percent to close at 58.10 dollars on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Silverline's stock, still trading under the ticker SVRM, jumped 19 percent.

Frontier Copper expects the transaction to add 0.85 dollars to annual earnings per share by 2026.

CINCINNATI, OH — August 14, 2024 — Redwood Analytics Inc., a provider of supply-chain forecasting software, announced today that it has acquired Bluefin Logistics Corp., a Cincinnati-based freight optimization firm, for approximately 42 million dollars in a cash-and-stock transaction. The deal is expected to close on September 30, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Under the terms of the agreement, Redwood Analytics will absorb Bluefin Logistics as a wholly owned subsidiary, retaining its 85 employees and its Cincinnati headquarters at 500 Riverfront Plaza. Bluefin Logistics was founded in 2011 by Marcus Whitfield, who will step down as Chief Executive Officer effective September 30, 2024, and transition into an advisory role.

"This acquisition strengthens our position against competitors like FreightWorks Global and allows us to offer end-to-end supply chain visibility," said Elena Torres, Chief Executive Officer of Redwood Analytics, during a press briefing held in Cincinnati on August 14, 2024. "Marcus and his team have built something exceptional, and we look forward to integrating their technology into our platform."

As part of the transition, Redwood Analytics named Priya Nair, currently Vice President of Product, to serve as President of the newly formed Bluefin division starting October 1, 2024. Nair previously worked at Quantum Freight Systems for six years.

Redwood Analytics, headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, reported revenue of 310 million dollars in fiscal year 2023 and employs roughly 1,200 people across North America. Shares of Redwood Analytics rose 4 percent following the announcement.

Marguerite Okonjo-Baptiste (born 14 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-French microbiologist known for her work on tuberculosis vaccine development. She earned a doctorate in molecular biology from the University of Bordeaux in 1984 and began her research career at the Institut Pasteur in Paris the same year. In 1991, Okonjo-Baptiste joined Sanofi Pasteur as a Senior Research Scientist, where she led the team that developed the experimental vaccine candidate ImmuTB-4. Her group's clinical trials, published in 1999, demonstrated a 62% reduction in active tuberculosis cases among trial participants in Lagos and Dakar. For this achievement, she received the Institut Pasteur Medal from the Institut Pasteur in Paris in 2001. In 2005, she left Sanofi Pasteur to found her own company, Meridian Biotherapeutics, headquartered in Lyon, France, with initial funding of 3.2 million euros from the French government. Meridian Biotherapeutics was acquired by the pharmaceutical giant Novartis for 410 million euros in 2013, after which Okonjo-Baptiste served as Novartis's Director of Infectious Disease Research until her retirement in 2019. She is married to physicist Dr. Henri Baptiste, with whom she has two children. Okonjo-Baptiste currently resides in Lyon and holds honorary professorships at the University of Bordeaux and Sciences Po Paris. In 2021, the World Health Organization appointed her to its Global Tuberculosis Advisory Panel, a role she continues to hold.

Bright Horizon Outfitters, headquartered in Bend, Oregon, has released the TrailForge 3400 hiking backpack, now available for $189.99 on the company's online store. Launched on May 6, 2024, the TrailForge 3400 features a 40-liter capacity, a hydration reservoir sleeve, and an aircraft-grade aluminum frame designed for multi-day treks. The backpack is manufactured by Cascade Gear Works, a supplier based in Portland, Oregon that has worked with Bright Horizon Outfitters since 2019. According to product manager Elena Marsh, the TrailForge 3400 was tested by a team of six alpine guides across the Three Sisters Wilderness before its official release. 'We wanted something that could survive the Pacific Crest Trail and still look good doing it,' Marsh said in a statement issued last week. The backpack comes in three colorways: Slate Gray, Moss Green, and Canyon Rust, and each unit ships with a lifetime warranty against manufacturing defects. Customers who purchase before June 30, 2024 will also receive a free Bright Horizon Outfitters trekking pole, valued at $34.00. The product is brand new and has already sold over 2,300 units in its first month, according to internal sales figures shared by the company. Bright Horizon Outfitters, founded in 2011 by outdoor enthusiast Daniel Kowalski, competes directly with Denver-based Summit Trail Co. in the mid-range backpacking gear market. Reviewers from Outside Magazine gave the TrailForge 3400 four out of five stars, calling it 'a serious contender for best backpack of 2024.'

The Ministry of Transport of Kenya announced on 6 March 2024 that it will invest 4.2 billion Kenyan shillings to upgrade the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway by December 2026. Speaking at a press briefing in Nairobi, Transport Secretary Wanjiru Kamau said the project, managed by the Kenya National Highways Authority, will widen 320 kilometers of roadway and add 12 new bridges. "This investment will cut travel time between Nairobi and Mombasa by nearly two hours," Kamau told reporters. The China Road and Bridge Corporation, a subsidiary of China Communications Construction Company, was awarded the construction contract following a competitive bidding process that concluded on 15 February 2024. Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua praised the agreement during a Contact.Meet with Chinese Ambassador Guo Haiyan at Harambee House on 4 March 2024, stating that the partnership reflects strong ties between Kenya and the People's Republic of China. The Kenya Revenue Authority confirmed that 1.1 billion shillings of the funding will come from a loan issued by the Export-Import Bank of China, with the remainder drawn from the national budget. Local officials in Mtito Andei welcomed the announcement, noting that the highway upgrade is expected to create roughly 3,500 jobs for residents of Makueni County. Construction crews are scheduled to begin groundwork on 1 April 2024, with the first phase of paving expected to be completed by mid-2025.

Pixelbook Labs, a San Jose startup founded in 2019 by former Google engineer Rita Novak, unveiled its second-generation e-reader, the InkSlate 2, on March 14, 2024. I have spent three weeks testing the device, purchased for $249 at the company's flagship store in Palo Alto, California, and it mostly delivers on its promise of a paper-like reading experience.

The InkSlate 2 uses a 10.3-inch E Ink Carta 1300 display, a notable upgrade from the 1200-generation panel in the original InkSlate. Battery life is rated at six weeks under normal use, and in my testing it came close, lasting 38 days before needing a charge. The device ships with 32 gigabytes of storage and supports both Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.2.

What impressed me most is the new stylus, sold separately for $79, which reduces latency to 9 milliseconds, down from 21 milliseconds on the previous model. Pixelbook Labs says the improvement comes from a custom chip designed in-house rather than sourced from Texas Instruments, its longtime supplier for earlier prototypes.

Not everything is perfect. The software, based on a modified version of Android 13, occasionally stutters when annotating PDFs larger than 50 megabytes. Rita Novak acknowledged the issue in an interview last Tuesday, saying a fix is expected in an update by April 2024.

At $249, the InkSlate 2 undercuts Amazon's Kindle Scribe by roughly $80 while offering comparable hardware. For students and heavy annotators, it's one of the more compelling e-readers I've reviewed this year, though the ecosystem of note-taking apps still trails Amazon's.

To: Marcus Feldman, Chief Financial Officer, Hartline Logistics Corp
From: Priya Nandakumar, VP of Corporate Development, Bellcrest Capital Partners
Date: March 11, 2024
Subject: Closing Confirmation - Acquisition of Redwing Freight Systems

Dear Marcus,

I am pleased to confirm that Bellcrest Capital Partners completed its acquisition of Redwing Freight Systems on March 8, 2024, for a total consideration of $47.5 million. The transaction was finalized at our offices in Chicago, Illinois, with signatures obtained from both parties by 4:30 PM local time.

As discussed during our meeting in Dallas on February 22, 2024, Redwing Freight Systems will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Hartline Logistics Corp going forward, retaining its 240 employees and its fleet of 68 delivery trucks based in Tulsa, Oklahoma. Please note that the $47.5 million payment was wired from Bellcrest Capital Partners' escrow account to Redwing Freight Systems' shareholders on March 8, 2024. Best regards,
Priya Nandakumar
VP of Corporate Development
Bellcrest Capital Partners

CHICAGO, Illinois -- Deere & Company announced on Tuesday, June 4, 2024, that it will acquire GrainTrack Analytics, a farm-data software startup based in Ames, Iowa, for approximately $340 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by August 2024, marks Deere's third acquisition this year as the agricultural machinery giant pushes deeper into precision-farming technology.

Under the agreement, GrainTrack's 85 employees will join Deere's Intelligent Solutions Group, and founder Priya Nandakumar will become Vice President of Data Strategy at Deere, reporting to Chief Technology Officer Jahmir Wells. Nandakumar, a 41-year-old former IBM engineer, started GrainTrack in 2016 with $2 million in seed funding from Sequoia Capital.

"This acquisition strengthens our ability to give farmers real-time yield forecasts," said John May, Deere's Chief Executive Officer, in a statement issued from the company's Moline, Illinois headquarters. Deere shares rose 3.2 percent to $398.15 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of rival Caterpillar dipped slightly.

Analysts at Morgan Stanley called the move a strong strategic fit, noting Deere's revenue reached $61.25 billion in fiscal 2023. GrainTrack, whose software is used on roughly 12,000 farms across the American Midwest, previously partnered with Bayer AG on soil-sensor projects. The transaction still requires approval from federal antitrust regulators, though industry observers expect no major hurdles given the companies' limited product overlap.

The Ohio Department of Transportation announced on Tuesday that it will begin a $42 million reconstruction of the Interstate 70 bridge over the Scioto River in Columbus, Ohio, starting March 3, 2025. Director Pamela Boratyn said the project, awarded to contractor Kokosing Industrial, is expected to take 14 months and will reduce traffic to two lanes in each direction during construction. The funding includes $30 million from the Federal Highway Administration and $12 million from the state's Highway Improvement Fund. Boratyn stated that the bridge, built in 1968, has deteriorated significantly and poses a growing safety risk to the roughly 85,000 vehicles that cross it daily. "We cannot delay this work any longer," Boratyn said during a press briefing at the Ohio Statehouse. State Senator Hearcel Craig praised the announcement, calling it a long-overdue investment in central Ohio infrastructure. Local business owners, including Maria Chen of Chen's Hardware on High Street, expressed concern about reduced customer access during the closures. The department said detour routes will direct traffic through State Route 315 and Interstate 71. A public information session is scheduled for February 10, 2025, at the Columbus Metropolitan Library to address resident questions. Governor Mike DeWine's office confirmed the funding was finalized last week and urged commuters to plan ahead for delays once construction begins.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT PRESS STATEMENT
Nairobi, Kenya - September 12, 2024

The Ministry of Transport today announced the launch of the Nairobi Commuter Rail Modernization Program, a KES 4.8 billion initiative to upgrade the city's rail network. Cabinet Secretary Amina Wafula confirmed that construction will begin on October 1, 2024, and is expected to conclude within 18 months.

"This program will reduce commute times by 40 percent along the Nairobi-Ruiru corridor," said Wafula during a press briefing at Nyayo House. The project will be delivered by Kenya Railways Corporation in partnership with China Road and Bridge Corporation, which was awarded the contract following a competitive tender process concluded on August 20, 2024.

Under the agreement, forty new diesel multiple unit trains will be procured from CRRC Corporation Limited at a total cost of KES 1.2 billion, with delivery scheduled for March 2025. The Ministry also confirmed that Engineer Peter Odhiambo has been appointed Project Director, effective September 16, 2024, reporting directly to Wafula.

Opposition lawmaker Johnson Muthomi criticized the procurement process on Tuesday, alleging irregularities in the tender awarded to China Road and Bridge Corporation. The Ministry rejected the claims, stating that the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority reviewed and approved all documentation on July 30, 2024.

The program is expected to create approximately 3,500 jobs across Nairobi County and Kiambu County during the construction phase. A groundbreaking ceremony is scheduled for October 1, 2024, at the Ruiru Railway Station, where President William Ruto is expected to deliver remarks.

Ingrid Vasterling (born March 4, 1958, in Groningen, Netherlands) is a Dutch biochemist known for her contributions to the development of recombinant insulin therapies. She earned a doctorate in molecular biology from Utrecht University in 1984 and joined Solvay Pharmaceuticals as a research scientist that same year. In 1991 Vasterling moved to Genentech in South San Francisco, where she led a team credited with refining large-scale fermentation methods for human insulin production. Her work contributed to the approval of a long-acting insulin analog by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in 1996. Vasterling left Genentech in 2003 to become Chief Scientific Officer at Novartis, a position she held until her retirement in 2018. During her tenure at Novartis, she oversaw the launch of three diabetes medications and was awarded the Robert Koch Prize by the Robert Koch Foundation in Berlin in 2011 for her research on metabolic disease. Vasterling holds Dutch and Swiss citizenship, having settled in Basel, Switzerland, in 2004. She married fellow scientist Klaus Reiniger in 1989; the couple has one daughter, Elsa Reiniger, born in 1993 in Basel. Vasterling is a member of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences and has published more than 120 peer-reviewed papers. She currently serves on the advisory board of the biotechnology firm CureVax AG, headquartered in Zurich.

Pixelnest Labs, a Portland-based startup, launched its long-awaited noise-cancelling earbuds, the Aria Buds Pro, on June 4, 2024. Priced at $179, the earbuds compete directly with Sony's WF-1000XM5 and Apple's AirPods Pro 2. I tested a pair for three weeks around Portland and on a flight to Chicago, and the results were largely impressive.

The Aria Buds Pro use a custom chip called NestSilence, developed in partnership with a supplier, Taiwan-based Hanlin Semiconductor. Battery life clocks in at 8 hours per charge, extending to 32 hours with the charging case, a real improvement over Pixelnest's previous model, the Aria Buds Lite, released in 2021.

CEO Maria Chen, who founded Pixelnest Labs in 2018, said in an interview on July 2 that the company sold 40,000 units in the first week alone, generating roughly $7.1 million in revenue. That is a strong debut, though Pixelnest still trails far behind Apple and Sony in market share.

My main complaints are minor: the touch controls occasionally misfire, and the companion app, built for iOS and Android, crashed twice during setup. Call quality in windy conditions on a walk through Tom McCall Waterfront Park was noticeably worse than on the AirPods Pro 2.

Still, at $179, the Aria Buds Pro undercut competitors by roughly $70 while matching most of their features. For anyone loyal to Portland-made gadgets, or simply hunting for value, this is an easy recommendation. Pixelnest says a follow-up model, the Aria Buds Max, is slated for early 2025.

BOSTON, MA -- November 4, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolerizumab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arcadia Therapeutics for the treatment of moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The trial, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez, enrolled 214 adult patients across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between January 2022 and March 2023. Participants received either 150 milligrams of tolerizumab administered subcutaneously every four weeks or a placebo, alongside standard methotrexate therapy. At week 24, 61 percent of patients receiving tolerizumab achieved an ACR50 response, compared with 28 percent in the placebo group, a difference the authors describe as statistically significant. The most common adverse events were mild injection-site reactions and upper respiratory infections; three patients discontinued treatment due to elevated liver enzymes. Dr. Vasquez presented the findings on November 3, 2023, at the American College of Rheumatology annual meeting in San Diego, California. Arcadia Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by Dr. Michael Torres, stated it plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial in early 2024 and is seeking a licensing partnership with Novartis to support global distribution. Shares of Arcadia rose 14 percent following the announcement. The study was funded by a $22 million grant from the National Institutes of Health and published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Independent experts, including Dr. Priya Nair of Stanford University, called the results promising but cautioned that longer-term safety data are needed before regulatory submission to the Food and Drug Administration.

input: Portland, Oregon-based outdoor apparel maker Cascadia Trailworks announced on Tuesday that it has acquired competitor Ridgeline Gear for $84 million in a cash-and-stock deal. The transaction, disclosed at a press briefing at the company's headquarters, will see Ridgeline Gear operate as a wholly owned subsidiary under its current brand name. Cascadia Trailworks CEO Melissa Hartwell said the acquisition would strengthen the company's footwear division and expand distribution across 1,200 retail locations in North America. "This deal positions us to compete more directly with Patagonia and The North Face," Hartwell told reporters. Ridgeline Gear founder Tomas Ibarra, who started the company in 2011 in Bend, Oregon, will join Cascadia Trailworks as Chief Innovation Officer effective November 1. Ibarra will report directly to Hartwell. Financial terms were finalized after three months of negotiations, according to sources familiar with the matter. Cascadia Trailworks financed roughly $50 million of the purchase price through a loan from Pacific Crest Bank, with the remainder paid in company stock. Shares of Cascadia Trailworks, which trades privately, are expected to be revalued following the merger. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners estimate the combined company will generate $310 million in annual revenue by 2026. The deal is expected to close by December 15, pending regulatory review. Ridgeline Gear employs 340 people across facilities in Bend and Salt Lake City, all of whom will retain their positions under the new ownership structure.

DETROIT, Mich. — Braxton Dynamics Inc., a mid-sized auto-parts supplier headquartered in Detroit, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in outstanding debt and a sharp drop in orders from General Motors. CEO Marcus Feldt announced the filing at a press conference held at the company's Livernois Avenue plant, saying the firm would continue operations while restructuring under court supervision. "We owe it to our 2,200 employees to fight for this company," Feldt said. The bankruptcy filing, submitted to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan, comes eighteen months after Braxton Dynamics acquired Ohio-based Vantage Steel Components for $85 million in a deal meant to expand its stamping capacity. Analysts at Morningstar noted that rising steel tariffs and a 12 percent decline in vehicle production last year had squeezed margins across the sector. Competitor Alden Manufacturing, based in Toledo, said it does not expect to acquire any of Braxton's assets. Michigan Governor Lisa Herrera said her office would work with the Michigan Economic Development Corporation to protect jobs at the Livernois plant. Feldt is expected to appear before Judge Constance Ruiz on March 14 for the first creditors' hearing. Shares of Braxton Dynamics, which trade over the counter, fell 61 percent following the announcement.

input: BOSTON, MA - March 14, 2024 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tremeliximab-B, an investigational monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Aravox Therapeutics, for treatment of relapsed multiple myeloma. The study, led by Dr. Helena Ruiz, Director of Hematologic Oncology at Massachusetts General Hospital, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Germany between June 2022 and September 2023. Patients receiving tremeliximab-B in combination with dexamethasone showed a 61 percent overall response rate compared with 34 percent in the control arm receiving standard bortezomib therapy, according to findings published in The Lancet Oncology on March 12, 2024. Median progression-free survival reached 18.4 months, versus 9.7 months for controls. The most common adverse event was Grade 3 neutropenia, occurring in 22 percent of treated patients, while three patients discontinued treatment due to severe cytokine release syndrome. Aravox Therapeutics' chief executive, Mark Feldstein, stated that the company plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. The trial was funded with a $47 million grant from the National Cancer Institute and additional investment from Aravox Therapeutics' partner, Novartis AG, which holds an option to license the drug for European markets. Dr. Ruiz is scheduled to present the full dataset at the American Society of Hematology annual meeting in San Diego in December 2024.

input: Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1957 in Bologna, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofitting techniques used in historic European buildings. She earned a degree in civil engineering from the University of Bologna in 1980 and later joined Politecnico di Milano, where she completed a doctorate in 1985. In 1990, Marchetti founded Studio Marchetti Ingegneria in Milan, a firm that grew to specialize in earthquake-resistant renovation of medieval structures. Her most notable project came after the 1997 Umbria earthquake, when Studio Marchetti Ingegneria was contracted to stabilize the Basilica of San Francesco in Assisi, work completed in 2002. In 2005, she left Studio Marchetti Ingegneria to become Chief Engineer at Fondazione Italiana per il Patrimonio, a nonprofit organization headquartered in Rome dedicated to preserving cultural heritage sites. Marchetti served in that position until 2014. For her contributions, she received the Gold Medal of the Ordine degli Ingegneri in 2010, awarded in Rome. She has also lectured widely, publishing over 60 papers in the Journal of Structural Engineering. Marchetti married fellow engineer Paolo Ricci in 1988; the couple has one daughter, Giulia Ricci, born in 1991 in Milan. Marchetti currently resides in Milan and continues to consult on preservation projects across Italy, including a 2019 assessment of earthquake damage in the town of Amatrice following the 2016 Central Italy earthquake.

input: DETROIT, Oct. 14 -- Stellantis NV announced Monday it will acquire electric-motor maker Corvion Drives Inc. for $740 million in cash, expanding its supply chain for the Ram 1500 REV pickup ahead of a planned 2025 launch. Chief Executive Carlos Tavares said the deal, expected to close by December 15, will help Stellantis reduce reliance on outside suppliers based in Asia. Corvion Drives, headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan, employs about 620 people and generated $310 million in revenue last year, according to Chief Financial Officer Lena Whitfield. Whitfield will stay on as president of the Corvion unit under the new ownership structure. Shares of Stellantis rose 3.2 percent on the New York Stock Exchange to close at $19.85, while shares of privately held Corvion were not publicly traded. Analysts at Morgan Stanley, including Adam Jonas, called the acquisition a defensive move against Tesla Inc. and Ford Motor Company, both of which have invested heavily in in-house motor production. The transaction was financed partly through a $500 million bond issuance underwritten by Goldman Sachs Group Inc. earlier this month. Stellantis, formed in 2021 from the merger of Fiat Chrysler Automobiles and PSA Group, has committed $35 billion toward electrification through 2030. Tavares told reporters at a press conference in Amsterdam that the Corvion deal marks the company's fourth acquisition of a battery or motor supplier since January. Regulatory approval from the European Commission is still pending and could delay final closing beyond the target date.

DENVER, Colorado -- Trailhead Robotics Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Summit Sensor Systems, a privately held manufacturer of industrial LiDAR components based in Boulder, Colorado, for $84 million in cash. The deal, confirmed by Trailhead chief executive officer Marisol Vance, is expected to close by November 15, 2024, pending regulatory review.

Summit Sensor Systems was founded in 2016 by engineer Thomas Rourke, who will remain with the company as chief technology officer under the new ownership. Trailhead Robotics, headquartered in Denver, Colorado, said the acquisition will strengthen its supply chain for autonomous warehouse robots, reducing its reliance on external suppliers such as Kestrel Optics of Fremont, California.

"This acquisition gives us direct control over a critical component in our product line," Vance said during a press briefing at Trailhead's Denver headquarters. "Summit's sensors are already integrated into our Atlas-7 delivery drones."

Trailhead shares rose 6.3 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, closing at $47.20. Analysts at Ridgeline Capital Partners noted the deal values Summit at roughly twelve times its projected 2024 revenue of $7 million. Ridgeline analyst Devon Okafor called the price "steep but strategically sound," citing growing demand for LiDAR technology in the logistics sector.

The transaction marks Trailhead's third acquisition since its founding in 2011 by siblings Marisol Vance and Julian Vance, and follows its $22 million purchase of software firm Pathwise Analytics in March 2023. Trailhead employs approximately 1,450 people across facilities in Colorado, Texas, and Ontario.

DETROIT, Mich. — Automaker Ferrand Motors announced Tuesday it will acquire electric vehicle startup VoltCore Inc. for $2.4 billion, marking one of the largest deals in the sector this year. The agreement, disclosed at a press conference at Ferrand's headquarters in Detroit, will see VoltCore's flagship battery plant in Reno, Nevada, fold into Ferrand's manufacturing division by January 2025.

Ferrand CEO Marcus Delaney said the acquisition would accelerate production of the company's upcoming electric sedan, the Ferrand Halcyon, slated for release in March 2025. "VoltCore's battery technology gives us a two-year head start on range and charging speed," Delaney told reporters.

VoltCore founder Priya Nair, who started the company in 2018 in a small garage in Palo Alto, California, will join Ferrand as Chief Technology Officer, effective November 1, 2024. Nair stepped down as VoltCore's chief executive on Monday, a day before the deal was announced.

Analysts at Bramwell Capital estimate the merger could save Ferrand roughly $300 million annually in battery-sourcing costs, since VoltCore has long supplied lithium-ion cells to competitor Halden Auto. Shares of Ferrand Motors rose 6.8 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Halden Auto shares fell 3.2 percent amid concerns over losing a key supplier.

The deal still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, with regulators expected to review the transaction over the next 90 days. If approved, it would be Ferrand's third acquisition since 2020.

DETROIT, Oct. 14 — Stellar Dynamics Inc., a Detroit-based maker of electric-vehicle battery components, announced Monday that it has acquired Ionix Battery Systems, a smaller rival based in Austin, Texas, for $412 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by December 5, will make Stellar Dynamics the second-largest supplier of lithium-ion battery packs to Ford Motor Company, according to chief executive Marissa Callahan. Callahan told reporters at a press conference in downtown Detroit that the acquisition would add roughly 1,800 employees to Stellar Dynamics' workforce and expand its footprint into three new manufacturing plants in Texas. Ionix founder and outgoing chief executive Dan Whitfield will step down from his post effective November 1, though he will remain on Stellar Dynamics' board as a senior advisor, the companies said. Shares of Stellar Dynamics rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.20, while shares of privately held Ionix are not publicly traded. Analysts at Bernstein Research said the merger positions Stellar Dynamics to compete more directly with Panasonic and LG Energy Solution in the North American EV supply chain. The transaction, which was financed partly through a $150 million loan from JPMorgan Chase, still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Callahan said she expects regulatory clearance within 60 days. Whitfield founded Ionix in Austin in 2014 and grew it into a company with $210 million in annual revenue before agreeing to the sale.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Finally Nails the Basics

By Renata Alvarez, Austin, October 14, 2024

After two years of testing Google's wearables, I can say the Pixel Watch 3, released on September 20, 2024, is the first one I would recommend without hesitation. Google, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc., priced the 45mm LTE model at $429.99, and I've worn it daily for three weeks alongside a Samsung Galaxy Watch 7 for comparison.

The headline upgrade is battery life: Google claims up to 36 hours, and in my testing with always-on display enabled, I consistently hit 30 hours. The AMOLED panel is now 10 percent brighter, which matters when you're outside in Austin's brutal summer sun. Fitness tracking, powered by a new cardiac sensor, felt notably more accurate than the Pixel Watch 2 during a half-marathon I ran in Zilker Park.

Google's software lead, Sameer Samat, told reporters at a briefing in Mountain View that the company sold over 1 million Pixel Watch units globally last year, a modest number next to Apple's dominance. Apple, headquartered in Cupertino, remains the clear competitor here, and its Apple Watch Series 10 still edges out Google on app selection.

Minor complaints: the charging puck is proprietary and easy to lose, and the $429.99 price feels steep against the Galaxy Watch 7's $299 entry point. Still, for Android users, this is the most polished Wear OS device yet, and I'm comfortable giving it a strong recommendation.

Fjallhelm Outdoors is now shipping the Trollveggen 45L Alpine Pack, a lightweight backpacking rig designed in Bergen, Norway and manufactured under license at a facility in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Priced at $289.00, the Trollveggen 45L launched on March 3, 2024 and has already sold more than 6,000 units through the company's online store. The pack weighs just 1.4 kilograms thanks to a Dyneema composite shell, and it includes a detachable 12-liter daypack, an integrated rain cover, and a lifetime warranty against manufacturing defects. Fjallhelm Outdoors was founded in 2016 by former mountain guide Ingrid Solheim, who still serves as the company's Chief Design Officer and tested early prototypes on a 2015 traverse of the Jotunheimen range. The Trollveggen line competes directly with Osprey's Aether series and Deuter's Aircontact packs, though reviewers at Backpacker Monthly noted in their April 2024 issue that the Trollveggen's hip belt runs about 15 percent lighter than comparable Osprey models. Each pack ships in 100 percent recycled cardboard packaging and includes a QR code linking to repair guides. Customers who purchase before June 30, 2024 receive a free 2-liter hydration bladder, a $22 value. The pack is available in three colorways: Glacier Grey, Fjord Blue, and Moss Green, and is sold in sizes Small through X-Large. Fjallhelm Outdoors, headquartered in Bergen, ships internationally to over 40 countries and offers a 60-day return policy for unused items purchased through its website.
