input: The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday that the city of Rotterdam will receive €42 million to upgrade the Maasvlakte rail corridor, part of a broader infrastructure package unveiled by Minister Aad Verbeek in The Hague. The funding, drawn from the National Infrastructure Fund, will be transferred to ProRail, the state-owned rail operator, by 15 October 2024. Minister Verbeek stated that the project would reduce freight delays by 18 percent along the Rotterdam-Duisburg corridor, benefiting exporters such as Heineken and Royal Vopak. Speaking at a press conference at the Ministry's headquarters, Verbeek said, "This investment secures the Netherlands' position as Europe's logistics gateway." The announcement follows a report published last month by the Dutch Court of Audit, which found that maintenance backlogs on the network had grown by 12 percent since 2021. Opposition lawmaker Els Bakker of the GroenLinks party welcomed the funding but criticized the ministry for delaying similar investments in Limburg province. ProRail's chief executive, Marjan Rintel, is expected to sign the formal transfer agreement on 3 September 2024 in Utrecht. The ministry noted that construction crews from VolkerWessels will begin work in January 2025, with completion targeted for late 2027. A separate €6 million grant will support noise-reduction barriers near residential areas in Vlaardingen.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Solid Upgrade, Familiar Flaws

By Renee Katz, published October 14, 2024

Google launched the Pixel Watch 3 on September 20, 2024, at a starting price of $349.99, and after three weeks of daily use in San Francisco, I have mixed but largely positive feelings. The 45mm aluminum model I tested, in Obsidian, pairs with a Pixel 9 Pro running Android 14 and syncs seamlessly through Google Fit.

Battery life is the headline improvement: Google claims up to 36 hours, and in practice I got roughly 30 hours with the always-on display enabled, up from about 22 hours on last year's Pixel Watch 2. The new Cardiac Coach feature, developed with input from Fitbit engineers in Boston, gives useful pacing guidance for runners, though it occasionally lagged during a 10-kilometer race I ran through Golden Gate Park.

Competitor devices remain relevant here. The Apple Watch Series 10, which Apple unveiled on September 9, 2024, still edges out Google on app selection, and Samsung's Galaxy Watch7 offers a cheaper entry point at $299. Google's software, however, feels more mature than it did two years ago, when the original Pixel Watch shipped with noticeable bugs.

One notable event: on October 2, 2024, Google issued a software patch after some users in Germany reported the watch overheating during charging. No injuries were reported, and Google said fewer than 0.5 percent of units were affected.

Overall, the Pixel Watch 3 is a capable, if incremental, update. For Android users already inside Google's ecosystem, it is an easy recommendation.

DETROIT, Mich. — Meridian Motors Corp. announced Tuesday that it will acquire EverCharge Networks Inc., a Chicago-based electric vehicle charging startup, for $740 million in cash and stock. The deal, disclosed at a press conference at Meridian's headquarters on Woodward Avenue, is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission.

Meridian CEO Diane Kessler said the acquisition would let the automaker deploy 12,000 new fast-charging stations across North America by 2027. "This is about controlling our own charging destiny," Kessler told reporters. EverCharge founder Marcus Tolliver, who launched the company in 2016 with just $2 million in seed funding, will join Meridian as Senior Vice President of Charging Infrastructure, effective January 1, 2025.

Meridian shares rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of rival automaker Halden Auto Group slipped 2.1 percent amid concerns it may fall behind in the charging race. Analysts at Bristol Capital Partners called the deal "a defensive but necessary move" for Meridian, which competes directly with Halden and Tokyo-based Nissan Motor Co.

EverCharge, which operates roughly 3,800 charging stations in 22 U.S. states, will continue running as a subsidiary under the EverCharge brand name. The company employs about 540 workers, most of whom will retain their positions, according to Tolliver.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City extended its unbeaten Premier League run to eleven matches on Saturday, defeating Everton 3-1 at Etihad Stadium before a crowd of 53,412. Norwegian striker Erling Haaland scored twice, in the 22nd minute and again in the 68th minute, while midfielder Bernardo Silva added a third goal in stoppage time. Everton's lone reply came from forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who converted a penalty in the 54th minute after a foul by defender Ruben Dias.

Manager Pep Guardiola praised his squad's resilience after the match, noting that the team had traveled to Merseyside just three days earlier for a League Cup fixture. "We showed character today," Guardiola told reporters at a press conference inside Etihad Stadium. "Erling is in incredible form, but this win belongs to everyone."

The victory moved Manchester City to 26 points, four ahead of second-placed Arsenal, who host Chelsea on Sunday. Everton, managed by Sean Dyche, remained in 15th place with 9 points. City's next fixture is away to RB Leipzig in the UEFA Champions League on October 18, 2023.

Haaland, who joined Manchester City from Borussia Dortmund in July 2022 for a reported 60 million pounds, has now scored 12 goals in 9 league appearances this season, extending his lead atop the Premier League scoring charts.

Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1957 in Bologna, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofitting techniques used across Southern Europe. She earned her doctorate in civil engineering from the Politecnico di Milano in 1983 and began her career at Fiat Engineering, where she worked as a junior structural analyst starting in 1984. In 1991 Marchetti left Fiat Engineering to found Marchetti & Rossi Ingegneria, a structural consultancy headquartered in Turin, Italy, alongside her longtime colleague Dario Rossi. The firm quickly became known for retrofitting historic buildings, most notably its 1997 stabilization of the Basilica di San Petronio following minor earthquake damage. In 2003, Marchetti was appointed Chief Technical Officer of the multinational construction company Salini Impregilo, a position she held until stepping down in 2012 to return to academic research. During her tenure at Salini Impregilo, she led the structural redesign of the Messina Strait crossing feasibility study. In 2015, the Italian National Research Council awarded her the Medaglia d'Oro per la Scienza in Rome for her contributions to earthquake engineering. Marchetti married fellow engineer Paolo Conti in 1988, and the couple has one daughter, Giulia Conti, born in 1990, who now works as an architect in Milan. Marchetti currently serves as a visiting professor at the Politecnico di Milano and continues to consult for Marchetti & Rossi Ingegneria, though she formally stepped back from day-to-day leadership of the firm in 2020.

Pixelbook Labs, a hardware startup headquartered in Austin, Texas, launched its first product on March 4, 2024: the Verve One, a $649 mirrorless camera aimed at travel vloggers. Founded in 2021 by former Canon engineer Marcus Idlewild, the company spent three years developing a sensor it calls the QuantumEye, manufactured under contract by a supplier in Hsinchu, Taiwan.

I tested the Verve One for two weeks in Portland, Oregon, and the results are mixed but promising. The 32-megapixel sensor produces sharp, well-saturated images in daylight, and the in-body stabilization rivals cameras twice its price, including the Sony A7C II. Battery life is the weak point: roughly 240 shots per charge, well below the 500-shot average for this class. The companion app, built by a small team in Bangalore, India, crashed twice during my review period, though a patch released on March 18, 2024 fixed one of the two bugs.

Pixelbook Labs CEO Marcus Idlewild told me in a phone interview on March 20, 2024 that a firmware update is coming in April to address battery drain. He also confirmed that Pixelbook Labs is in early talks with retailer Fotografix Direct about a distribution deal worth an estimated $2.3 million.

At $649, the Verve One competes directly with the Fujifilm X-M5 and the Canon EOS R50, both of which offer better battery life but lack the QuantumEye sensor's low-light performance. For a first product from a three-year-old startup, it's a remarkably confident debut, though buyers should wait for the firmware fix before committing.

Kestrel Outdoor Co., headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, has released the Talus 45 Backpacking Pack, a 45-liter internal-frame pack designed for multi-day treks. Priced at $219.99, the Talus 45 is now available in three colorways: Slate Gray, Juniper Green, and Rust Orange. The pack weighs 2.3 kilograms and features a torso-adjustable suspension system, a removable rain cover, and a hydration sleeve compatible with reservoirs up to 3 liters. Kestrel Outdoor Co. was founded in 2011 by Marcus Ferreira, a former mountaineering guide who led expeditions in the Bitterroot Range for nearly a decade before starting the company. The Talus 45 was tested extensively on the Pacific Crest Trail in July 2023 by a team of six field testers, according to product manager Elena Vasquez. "We wanted a pack that could survive 500 miles of rough terrain without falling apart," Vasquez said. The company sources its ripstop nylon fabric from Taiwan-based supplier Formosa Textile Industries, a partnership that began in 2016. This item is brand new and ships from Kestrel's distribution center in Billings, Montana within two business days. Customers who purchase the Talus 45 before November 30, 2024 will also receive a free 32-ounce Kestrel water bottle, a $24.99 value. Reviews on the company website average 4.7 out of 5 stars from over 1,200 verified buyers. Kestrel Outdoor Co. competes directly with Ridgeline Gear and Summit Forge in the mid-range backpacking market. Warranty coverage extends for 5 years from the date of purchase, covering manufacturing defects but not normal wear and tear.

Chief Executive Officer Marcus Delaney said the acquisition, expected to close by January 15, 2025, will create roughly 1,200 new jobs in southeastern Michigan. "This is the largest investment in our battery division's history," Delaney told reporters at a press conference held at Halloway's headquarters in Dearborn. VoltCore Systems, founded in 2018 by engineer Priya Nandakumar, has developed a proprietary cathode chemistry that reportedly extends battery range by 22 percent. The transaction, subject to regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission, is being financed through a combination of cash reserves and a $300 million loan from Continental Bank. Some United Auto Workers members expressed cautious optimism, noting that union representatives met with Halloway executives in Warren last Friday to discuss job guarantees.

input: Marguerite Okonjo (born 14 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-British structural engineer known for pioneering earthquake-resistant designs for high-rise buildings. She earned a Bachelor of Engineering from the University of Lagos in 1980 and later completed a doctorate at Imperial College London in 1985. In 1990, Okonjo joined Arup Group in London as a structural analyst, and by 1998 she had risen to Chief Structural Engineer. In 2003, she left Arup Group to found Okonjo Structural Consultants in Manchester, a firm that would go on to design more than 40 buildings across West Africa and Europe. Her most celebrated project, the Lagos Resilience Tower, was completed in 2011 and withstood a magnitude 6.1 earthquake near Ibadan in 2016 without structural damage. For this achievement, the Royal Academy of Engineering awarded her the Silver Medal in London in 2017. Okonjo married fellow engineer Thomas Bardsley in 1995, and the couple have two children. In 2020, she was elected President of the Institution of Structural Engineers, becoming the first Nigerian-born person to hold the position. She stepped down from that role in 2023, citing a wish to focus on mentoring young engineers in Lagos. Okonjo currently divides her time between Manchester and Lagos, and continues to serve as a consultant to Okonjo Structural Consultants.

Boston, MA -- November 4, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tarlacinib, an oral chemical compound targeting JAK2 mutations in patients with myelofibrosis. The study, led by Dr. Helena Ruiz, enrolled 214 participants across 12 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and June 2023. Findings, published in The Lancet Haematology, showed that 58 percent of patients receiving tarlacinib experienced a reduction in spleen volume of at least 35 percent after 24 weeks, compared with 11 percent in the placebo group. Median overall survival had not been reached at the 18-month follow-up. Dr. Ruiz stated that the drug was generally well tolerated, with anemia and thrombocytopenia reported as the most common adverse events. Novaris Therapeutics, the Basel-based biopharmaceutical company that developed tarlacinib, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the second quarter of 2024. Novaris was founded in 2011 by biochemist Dr. Anton Feldman and has since grown into a mid-sized firm with roughly 640 employees. In a related development, Novaris announced on October 30, 2023 that it had acquired Kestrel Biosciences, a smaller San Diego-based startup specializing in bone marrow disorders, for 340 million dollars. Analysts at Deutsche Bank noted that the acquisition strengthens Novaris's position against competitor Incyte Corporation in the myeloproliferative neoplasm treatment market. The company's shares rose 6 percent on the Swiss Exchange following the announcement. Dr. Ruiz is scheduled to present the full trial data at the American Society of Hematology annual meeting in San Diego on December 9, 2023.

Cupertino, September 12, 2024 - Apple Inc. unveiled the iPhone 16 Pro at its Steve Jobs Theater event, and after two weeks of daily use, I can say it is the most refined phone the company has produced since Tim Cook took over as Chief Executive Officer in 2011. The $1,199 review unit, finished in Desert Titanium, pairs the new A18 Pro chip with a 6.9-inch display that Apple says is 20 percent brighter outdoors than last year's model. Battery life impressed me most: on a typical day in San Francisco, the phone lasted from 7:00 a.m. until nearly midnight, roughly 22 percent longer than the iPhone 15 Pro I tested in 2023. Apple also touted Camera Control, a capacitive button that launched the camera app in under half a second during my tests. Not everything is perfect. Qualcomm, a longtime supplier of modem chips, confirmed its Snapdragon X80 module powers 5G connectivity, and I noticed occasional signal drops in the elevator of my apartment building. Samsung Electronics, Apple's chief rival in premium smartphones, will likely respond with its own Galaxy S25 launch in early 2025. Analysts at Morgan Stanley, led by Erik Woodring, estimate Apple will ship 220 million iPhones in fiscal 2025. For anyone upgrading from an iPhone 12 or older, the iPhone 16 Pro is an easy recommendation; for iPhone 15 Pro owners, it is a harder sell at this price.

Bellroy, the Melbourne-based accessories brand founded in 2010, has released the Venture Sling 4L, a water-resistant crossbody bag designed for daily commuting. Priced at $99.00, the Venture Sling 4L is now available on Bellroy's website and at select REI stores across the United States, effective November 6, 2023. Constructed from a 400-denier recycled nylon shell, the bag features a padded 13-inch laptop sleeve, a magnetic buckle closure, and a quick-access front pocket for a phone or transit card. It weighs just 340 grams and holds up to 4 liters of gear, making it suitable for cyclists navigating cities like Portland or Toronto. Bellroy's design lead, Ainsley Kirkpatrick, said the sling was tested by 200 commuters in Melbourne and Osaka over an 18-month development period before launch. The Venture Sling 4L comes in three colorways: Basalt, Bureau, and Mesa Rose, each carrying a 3-year warranty against manufacturing defects. Customers who purchase directly from Bellroy.com before December 1, 2023 will receive free shipping within Australia and the continental United States. Early reviewers, including tech outlet Wirecutter, praised the bag's durability but noted the single strap may not suit heavier loads over 5 kilograms. This is Bellroy's second sling-style release, following the original Venture Sling that debuted in 2021. With this launch, Bellroy continues to compete with brands like Peak Design and Tumi in the everyday-carry accessories market.

DETROIT, Mich. — Meridian Motors Inc. announced Tuesday that it has acquired Voltaris Battery Systems, a Chicago-based startup specializing in solid-state battery cells, for $740 million in cash and stock. The deal, confirmed by Meridian CEO Nathan Cole at a press conference at Meridian's headquarters in Detroit, is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval.

Voltaris, founded in 2019 by engineer Priya Anand, has developed a battery technology that Meridian says could extend electric vehicle range by up to 35 percent. Anand will join Meridian as Chief Technology Officer starting December 1, 2024, according to a statement released by the company.

"This acquisition positions Meridian to compete directly with Tesla and Rivian in the next-generation EV market," Cole said. Meridian shares rose 8 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $54.32.

The merger has drawn scrutiny from the Federal Trade Commission, which confirmed Wednesday it will review the transaction for antitrust concerns. FTC spokesperson Linda Marsh said the agency expects to complete its review within 60 days.

Voltaris currently employs 210 people across two facilities in Chicago and Austin, Texas. Meridian said it plans to retain all Voltaris staff and expand the Austin facility, adding 150 jobs by mid-2025. Analysts at Goldman Sachs estimate the combined company could generate $2.3 billion in annual EV battery revenue by 2027.

Zurich-based Vantis Pharma AG announced Tuesday that it will acquire Boston biotech firm Nurexa Therapeutics for $2.4 billion in cash, marking the largest deal in the sector this year. The agreement was signed on March 11, 2024, by Vantis chief executive Helena Bruggmann and Nurexa founder Dr. Samuel Okafor at the company's headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Under the deal, Vantis will gain full rights to Nurexa's experimental drug candidate, Relotrax, currently in Phase 3 trials for treating chronic migraine. Bruggmann said the acquisition would strengthen Vantis's neurology pipeline and expand its presence in the United States. Nurexa, founded in 2016 by Okafor and former MIT researcher Dr. Lian Wu, employs 210 people and reported $340 million in revenue last year. Shares of Nurexa surged 18 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, while Vantis stock dipped 3 percent on investor concerns about integration costs. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners called the move "a bold bet on next-generation migraine treatment." The transaction, expected to close by the third quarter of 2024 pending regulatory approval from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, will be financed through a combination of $1.5 billion in cash reserves and a $900 million loan from Credit Suisse. Okafor will join Vantis's executive board as Chief Scientific Officer once the deal is finalized, while Wu plans to depart the company to start a new venture in Zurich.

Fjallnord Outdoors, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, has launched the Ridgeline 3-Season Tent, a two-person backpacking shelter now available for $329.00 on the company's website and at REI stores nationwide starting November 12, 2024. Weighing just 3.2 pounds, the tent uses a 20-denier ripstop nylon fly treated with a silicone coating for enhanced water resistance, and its aluminum poles are sourced from Easton, a longtime supplier based in Salt Lake City, Utah. Fjallnord was founded in 2016 by former mountaineering guide Erik Solvang, who spent eleven years leading expeditions in the Karakoram range before starting the company. "We wanted a tent light enough for a thru-hike on the Colorado Trail but tough enough for the Wind River Range," Solvang said in a statement released Tuesday. The Ridgeline includes two vestibules, color-coded guylines, and a footprint sold separately for $39.00. Early reviewers, including outdoor journalist Priya Nandakumar of Backpacker Digest, praised the tent's ventilation but noted the single-wall design can feel warm in humid climates below 3,000 feet. Fjallnord has sold roughly 4,500 units since the product launched, according to a company spokesperson, and plans to expand distribution to Canada by spring 2025. The tent carries a limited lifetime warranty and ships within 5 business days of order. Customers can also bundle the Ridgeline with the Solvang Trekking Poles, a separate product named after the founder, for an additional $59.00.

AUSTIN, Texas -- Meridian BioLabs Inc. announced today that it has acquired NovaGen Diagnostics LLC, a privately held Boston startup specializing in rapid pathogen detection kits, for $142 million in cash and stock. The deal, finalized on Tuesday, June 11, 2024, is expected to close by August 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Under the agreement, Meridian BioLabs will absorb NovaGen's 85 employees and integrate its flagship product, the QuickScan PCR Analyzer, into its diagnostics portfolio. Dr. Helena Fitzgerald, Chief Executive Officer of Meridian BioLabs, said the acquisition strengthens the company's position against competitor Orion Health Systems in the infectious disease testing market.

"NovaGen's technology has already proven effective in detecting Salmonella and influenza strains within minutes," Fitzgerald said during a press briefing at Meridian's headquarters in Austin. "This partnership accelerates our roadmap by at least two years."

NovaGen was founded in 2018 by Dr. Raymond Okafor, who will join Meridian BioLabs as Senior Vice President of Diagnostics Innovation starting July 1, 2024. Okafor previously led research teams at Baylor College of Medicine.

Meridian BioLabs, headquartered in Austin, Texas, employs over 1,200 people worldwide and reported $410 million in revenue last fiscal year. Shares of Meridian BioLabs (NASDAQ: MRBL) rose 6.3 percent following the announcement.

The transaction was advised by Goldman Sachs on behalf of Meridian and Jefferies Group on behalf of NovaGen. Analysts expect the combined entity to expand testing capacity across 14 states by early 2025.

input: Marguerite Okonkwo-Laine (born 14 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-French microbiologist known for her research on antimicrobial resistance in Vibrio cholerae. She earned her doctorate in microbiology from the Pasteur Institute in Paris in 1986, after moving to France in 1979 on a scholarship from the French government. In 1991 she joined the Institut de Recherche pour le Développement as a senior researcher, and in 2004 she became Director of the Laboratory of Tropical Pathogens at the same institution, a post she held until her retirement in 2019. During her tenure, Okonkwo-Laine led field studies in Dakar, Senegal following the 2005 cholera outbreak, work that informed World Health Organization guidelines on oral rehydration therapy. She published over 140 papers and, in 1998, co-founded the nonprofit organization AquaSafe Africa with fellow researcher Dr. Thierry Lambert to improve water sanitation in West African communities. In 2012 she received the Prince Mahidol Award in Bangkok, Thailand, presented by the Thai royal family for her contributions to public health. She married the epidemiologist Dr. Jean-Paul Laine in 1983; the couple had two children, Amara and Kwame. Okonkwo-Laine currently resides in Marseille, France, where she serves on the scientific advisory board of Sanofi Pasteur. Her memoir, Waters of Enugu, was published in 2021 by Éditions Gallimard and won praise from critics for its portrayal of postcolonial science.

input: Boston, MA — October 3, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tavaraxib, an experimental oral inhibitor developed by Cascade Therapeutics, in patients with moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis. The randomized, double-blind study enrolled 214 adults across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between January 2022 and March 2023. Lead investigator Dr. Priya Anand, Associate Professor of Gastroenterology at Harvard Medical School, presented the findings on October 3, 2023 at the American College of Gastroenterology annual meeting in Chicago. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of tavaraxib twice daily achieved clinical remission at week 12 in 38 percent of cases, compared to 14 percent in the placebo group, a statistically significant difference (p<0.001). Secondary endpoints, including mucosal healing, were observed in 29 percent of treated patients versus 9 percent of controls. Adverse events were generally mild, with headache and nasopharyngitis reported most frequently; three patients discontinued treatment due to elevated liver enzymes. Dr. Anand noted that tavaraxib's novel mechanism, targeting the JAK-TYK2 pathway, may offer an alternative for patients who fail anti-TNF therapies such as infliximab. Cascade Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, stated it plans to initiate a phase 3 program in early 2024 pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The company's chief medical officer, Dr. Samuel Lindqvist, said the data support tavaraxib's potential as a first-line oral therapy. The study was funded by a $22 million grant from the National Institutes of Health and co-sponsored by Cascade Therapeutics. Full results will be published in The New England Journal of Medicine later this year.

Pixel Watch 3, Google's latest smartwatch, went on sale on September 10, 2024, priced at $349.99 for the 41mm Wi-Fi model. I have worn it daily since picking one up at the Best Buy in Emeryville, California, and the improvements over the Pixel Watch 2 are noticeable. Google, headquartered in Mountain View, California, redesigned the display to hit 2,000 nits of peak brightness, a huge jump that makes outdoor readability far better than on the Apple Watch Series 9. Battery life lands at roughly 24 hours with the always-on display enabled, which is respectable but still trails the 36 hours Samsung claims for the Galaxy Watch7.

During a briefing in San Francisco on August 22, 2024, Google's hardware chief Rick Osterloh said the new Snapdragon W5 chip cuts power draw by 30 percent compared with the previous generation. That claim mostly checks out in my testing, though heavy GPS use during a two-hour run still drained about 40 percent of the battery.

The loss-of-pulse detection feature, developed with input from cardiologists at Stanford Health Care, worked reliably in three simulated tests, though I hope I never need it for real. At $349.99, the Pixel Watch 3 competes directly with the Apple Watch Series 9 and the Galaxy Watch7, and for Android users it is now the easiest recommendation in the category.

One gripe: the charging puck is not compatible with the Pixel Watch 2, meaning owners upgrading will need to buy a new $49.99 charger separately.

MANCHESTER, ENGLAND - September 14, 2024 - Ederson Silva scored a stunning free kick in the 89th minute as Manchester City defeated Aston Villa 2-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, keeping the reigning champions unbeaten after four Premier League matches. Manager Pep Guardiola praised his squad's resilience after Villa striker Ollie Watkins had equalized in the 71st minute following a header from a corner kick. "We showed character today," Guardiola told reporters at the post-match press conference. "Ederson's goal was pure quality." The win moved City to 10 points, one ahead of Liverpool, who drew 1-1 with Everton earlier in the day at Goodison Park. Aston Villa manager Unai Emery expressed frustration with the late goal, noting his side had controlled long stretches of the second half. Attendance was announced at 53,112, a season high for the Etihad Stadium. City midfielder Rodri, last year's Ballon d'Or runner-up, was substituted in the 80th minute after appearing to favor his right knee, prompting concern ahead of City's Champions League fixture against Inter Milan on September 18. Club officials said Rodri would undergo scans on Sunday. Meanwhile, Aston Villa confirmed that defender Pau Torres will miss the next three weeks with a hamstring injury sustained in training on September 10. The Premier League table now shows Manchester City atop the standings, with Arsenal in third place after their 3-0 victory over Tottenham Hotspur on Friday at the Emirates Stadium.

Dr. Amara Voss (born March 14, 1958, in Leipzig, East Germany) is a physicist and engineer known for her contributions to solid-state battery research. She earned a Diplom in physics from Humboldt University of Berlin in 1981 and completed her doctorate at ETH Zurich in 1985. In 1990, Voss joined Siemens AG in Munich as a research scientist, working on semiconductor materials. She left Siemens in 1998 to co-found Ionova Energietechnik GmbH with fellow engineer Klaus Reinhardt, a company headquartered in Stuttgart, Germany, dedicated to developing lithium-ion battery technology for electric vehicles. Under her leadership as Chief Technology Officer, Ionova Energietechnik filed 42 patents by 2005 and signed a supply agreement with the automaker Bergmann Motors. In 2007, the German conglomerate Rheinmetall Industries acquired Ionova Energietechnik for approximately 310 million euros, and Voss stayed on as head of research until 2011. She then accepted a professorship at the Technical University of Munich, where she has taught since September 2011. In 2016, Voss received the Leibniz Prize from the German Research Foundation in Berlin for her work on battery safety. She is married to fellow physicist Klaus Reinhardt, and the couple has one daughter, Elena Reinhardt, born in 1993 in Stuttgart. Voss continues to publish widely and serves on the advisory board of the European Battery Alliance.

DENVER, Colorado – Trailhead Robotics Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Summit Sensor Systems, a privately held maker of industrial lidar components, for $142 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by November 15, 2024, will make Summit Sensor Systems a wholly owned subsidiary of Trailhead Robotics.

CEO Marla Kestrel said the acquisition strengthens Trailhead's position against competitor Vantage Automation Corp., which has been expanding its own sensor division in recent months. "This is a pivotal step in our roadmap toward fully autonomous warehouse fleets," Kestrel told reporters during a briefing at Trailhead's headquarters in Denver.

Summit Sensor Systems, founded in 2016 by engineer Dominic Farro, employs about 210 people at its facility in Boulder, Colorado. Farro will join Trailhead as Chief Technology Officer starting December 1, 2024, according to a company statement. He previously served as Summit's president since 2019.

Trailhead's shares rose 6.3 percent on the Nasdaq exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.40. Analysts at Merriden Capital Partners called the price "reasonable," noting that Summit generated roughly $37 million in revenue last year.

The transaction still requires clearance from the Federal Trade Commission, a process that could take up to 90 days. Trailhead Robotics, based in Denver, was founded in 2011 by siblings Owen and Priya Nair and now employs over 1,400 people across three states.

MANCHESTER, England — October 14, 2024 — Northbridge United defeated Calderdale Athletic 3-1 at Ashfield Park on Sunday, moving into second place in the Regional Football Championship table. Striker Marcus Whitfield scored twice, including a 78th-minute penalty, while midfielder Daniel Osei added a third goal in stoppage time. Calderdale's lone reply came from forward Ryan Pearce in the 55th minute.

The win extended Northbridge United's unbeaten run to eight matches, a stretch head coach Elena Vasquez credited to improved fitness following a training camp in Marbella, Spain last month. "We worked incredibly hard in pre-season, and it's paying off," Vasquez told reporters after the match. Club chairman Harold Whitby said Northbridge United was in talks to extend Whitfield's contract before the January transfer window opens.

About 12,400 fans attended the fixture at Ashfield Park, the club's home ground since 1978. Calderdale Athletic manager Tomasz Nowak was shown a red card in the 82nd minute after protesting a refereeing decision, and he will face a disciplinary hearing before the Regional Football Association on October 21.

Elsewhere in the league, league leaders Brackenfield City beat Solway Rovers 2-0 at the Meridian Stadium, stretching their lead to six points. Northbridge United will next travel to face Brackenfield City on October 28, a match many analysts are already calling a potential title decider.

Ingrid Solberg (born 14 March 1958, in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist and former director of the Institute for Fjord Ecology. She earned a doctorate in marine biology from the University of Bergen in 1985, studying larval dispersal of Atlantic cod. In 1990 Solberg joined the Norwegian Institute for Water Research (NIVA) in Oslo as a research scientist, where she spent twelve years investigating harmful algal blooms along the Norwegian coast.

In July 2002 Solberg founded the Institute for Fjord Ecology in Tromsø with funding from the Research Council of Norway, aiming to monitor the effects of salmon farming on wild fish populations. She served as its director until stepping down in September 2019, when she was succeeded by Dr. Fredrik Aas. Under her leadership the institute published influential studies on sea lice infestations, including a widely cited 2011 paper in the journal Marine Ecology Progress Series.

In 2015 Solberg received the Fridtjof Nansen Prize for Excellence, awarded by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo, for her contributions to coastal ecosystem research. She has also served as an advisor to the Norwegian Directorate of Fisheries and as a visiting professor at the University of Tromsø.

Solberg married fellow biologist Jan Eide in 1988; the couple has two children. She currently lives in Tromsø, where she continues to write and lecture on marine conservation.

input: The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday, June 11, 2024, that construction of the new Riverside Transit Hub in Manchester will begin next month, following a formal agreement signed with Halcyon Infrastructure Group. Transport Secretary Rebecca Holt confirmed at a press briefing in Whitehall that the project, valued at 240 million pounds, will be funded jointly by the national government and Greater Manchester Combined Authority. Halcyon Infrastructure Group, headquartered in Leeds, was awarded the contract after a competitive tender process that began in January 2024. The company's chief executive, Daniel Osei, stated that the hub will include a new rail platform, a bus interchange, and a pedestrian bridge connecting to Piccadilly Station. Construction is expected to employ approximately 1,200 workers over three years and is scheduled for completion by September 2027. Secretary Holt also noted that the Department for Transport will publish a full environmental impact assessment by August 2024, in accordance with the Planning Act 2008. Local officials, including Manchester City Council leader Priya Kaur, welcomed the announcement, calling it a milestone for regional connectivity. Opposition MP Gerald Finch criticized the funding structure, arguing that taxpayers deserve greater transparency on cost overruns. The Ministry stated that quarterly progress reports will be submitted to Parliament beginning in October 2024, and that a public consultation session will be held in Manchester on July 15, 2024, to gather community feedback before groundbreaking begins.

SUPERIOR COURT OF SAN MATEO COUNTY, CIVIL DIVISION

Case No. CIV-2024-118732

On March 14, 2024, Judge Rosalind Marchetti presided over the sentencing hearing of Kyle Anderton, 41, former controller of Belmont Freight Solutions Inc., a logistics company headquartered in Redwood City, California. Anderton was convicted on February 9, 2024, of embezzlement after prosecutor Denise Okafor, representing the San Mateo County District Attorney's Office, proved he diverted $1,240,000 from company accounts between 2019 and 2023 to fund personal real estate purchases in Lake Tahoe.

Judge Marchetti sentenced Anderton to six years in state prison and ordered restitution of $1,240,000 payable to Belmont Freight Solutions Inc. Defense attorney Priya Nathanson argued for leniency, citing her client's lack of prior record, but the court rejected the request. Anderton was taken into custody by San Mateo County Sheriff's deputies immediately following the hearing at the courthouse on Hamilton Street.

The fraud was first uncovered in August 2023 when auditor Grace Lindqvist, hired by CFO Marcus Bell, flagged irregular wire transfers to an account linked to Anderton's wife, Denise Anderton. Belmont Freight Solutions Inc. subsequently filed a civil suit seeking additional damages of $310,000 in legal fees. Company president Harold Voss issued a statement calling the sentence "a measure of justice for our employees and shareholders." Anderton is scheduled to begin serving his sentence at San Quentin State Prison on April 1, 2024.

input: SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA — On Tuesday, March 4, 2025, Judge Rosalind Kirchner sentenced Marcus DeShawn Ellery, 37, to 46 months in federal prison after a jury convicted him of wire fraud and embezzlement connected to his former position as Chief Financial Officer of Baywater Logistics Inc., a freight brokerage headquartered in Oakland, California. Prosecutor Angela Feinman of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that between January 2021 and August 2023, Ellery diverted approximately $2.3 million from company accounts to a shell entity he controlled, Ridgeline Capital Partners LLC, disguising the transfers as vendor payments. Ellery was arrested on October 14, 2023, at his home in Pleasanton by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation on charges of wire fraud and money laundering. The trial, held at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, began on January 8, 2025, and lasted three weeks. Defense attorney Harold Bing maintained that Ellery's supervisor, Founder and CEO Priya Nandakumar, had authorized the transactions, a claim the jury rejected. Baywater Logistics, which Nandakumar founded in 2011, terminated Ellery's employment on September 1, 2023, following an internal audit conducted by Meridian Forensic Accounting. Judge Kirchner also ordered restitution of $2.1 million payable to Baywater Logistics within five years. Ellery's attorneys have filed notice of appeal with the California Court of Appeal, First Appellate District. No sentencing date has been set for co-defendant Wendell Osei, whose trial is scheduled for June 2025.

MUNICH, Germany — Siemens Energy AG announced Tuesday that it has acquired Voltrix Grid Solutions, a Dutch power-electronics firm, for 640 million euros in a deal aimed at bolstering its transmission technology portfolio. The acquisition, disclosed at a press conference in Munich, was confirmed by Siemens Energy CEO Christian Bruch, who said the deal would close by March 2025 pending regulatory approval from the European Commission.

Voltrix, headquartered in Eindhoven, employs roughly 850 people and specializes in high-voltage direct current converters used in offshore wind projects. Its founder, Dr. Anneke Visser, will join Siemens Energy as Senior Vice President of Grid Technologies starting January 15, 2025, according to a company statement.

"This transaction strengthens our ability to deliver reliable power infrastructure across Europe," Bruch said during the announcement. Analysts at Deutsche Bank estimated the deal represents a 15 percent premium over Voltrix's most recent private valuation.

The move comes as Siemens Energy competes with General Electric and Hitachi Energy for contracts tied to the European Union's renewable energy expansion, which calls for 320 gigawatts of offshore wind capacity by 2030. Shares of Siemens Energy rose 4.2 percent on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange following the announcement.

Voltrix's 200 engineers based in Eindhoven are expected to relocate operations to Siemens Energy's Erlangen campus by mid-2026, though the company said no layoffs are planned. The transaction still requires approval from Dutch antitrust regulators before finalization.

input: SUPERIOR COURT OF SUFFOLK COUNTY, MASSACHUSETTS — On October 14, 2024, Judge Marianne Cotter sentenced Gregory Palladino, 47, to 36 months in state prison after a jury convicted him of wire fraud and embezzlement in connection with his former role at Beacon Hill Capital Partners, a Boston-based investment firm. Prosecutor Diane Achebe of the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office argued that Palladino diverted $2.3 million from client accounts between January 2019 and March 2023 to fund personal real estate purchases in Nantucket. The trial, held at the Edward W. Brooke Courthouse in Boston, concluded on September 30, 2024, after eleven days of testimony. Defense attorney Marcus Whitfield maintained that Palladino's business partner, Louis Feretti, orchestrated the scheme and that his client acted under duress. The jury rejected that defense on September 28, 2024. Judge Cotter also ordered Palladino to pay $2.3 million in restitution to eleven victims, including retired schoolteacher Rosalind Kane of Quincy, who testified that she lost her entire pension fund. Beacon Hill Capital Partners, founded in 2011 by Palladino and Feretti, filed for bankruptcy in April 2023 shortly after the Massachusetts Securities Division opened its investigation. Feretti has not been charged and left the country for Portugal in late 2023. The case, formally titled Commonwealth v. Palladino, drew coverage from the Boston Globe throughout the proceedings.

MANCHESTER, England, 14 October 2024 — Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side beat Brighton & Hove Albion 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, lifting the club to fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 23rd minute, converting a low cross from midfielder John McGinn, before doubling his tally with a penalty in the 61st minute after Brighton defender Lewis Dunk was penalized for handball. Brighton pulled one back through Danny Welbeck in the 74th minute, but substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win with a curling effort in stoppage time. Aston Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, telling reporters at a press conference inside Villa Park that the team had "grown into genuine title contenders." Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler, appointed to the role in July 2024, admitted his side had struggled defensively without injured captain Lewis Dunk's usual partner, Adam Webster, who is expected to miss six weeks with a hamstring injury sustained in training on 2 October. The victory extended Aston Villa's unbeaten home run to nine matches and moved them to 19 points from eight games, three points behind leaders Liverpool. Villa will next travel to face Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium on 21 October, while Brighton host Chelsea at the Amex Stadium the same day. Aston Villa's owners, V Sports, released a statement congratulating Emery on the result, calling it "a defining afternoon" in the club's resurgence under his three-year tenure since November 2022.

Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1958 in Trieste, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofitting techniques used in Mediterranean earthquake zones. She earned her engineering degree from the Politecnico di Milano in 1981 and began her career at Fiat Engineering, where she worked from 1982 to 1989. In 1990, Marchetti founded Marchetti Strutture, a consulting firm headquartered in Bologna, Italy, that later became a subsidiary of the multinational construction group Vincenzo Costruzioni S.p.A. following a 2004 acquisition worth 12 million euros.

Marchetti rose to international prominence after the L'Aquila earthquake of April 2009, when her firm was contracted to assess damage to more than 200 buildings across the Abruzzo region. Her report, published as the technical study "Resilienza Sismica," influenced Italy's revised building code enacted in 2011.

In 2015, she left her role as Chief Executive Officer of Marchetti Strutture to become a professor at the Politecnico di Torino, a position she still holds. In 2018, Marchetti received the Golden Compass Award from the Milan Triennale for her contributions to earthquake-resistant design, presented at a ceremony in Milan.

She married fellow engineer Paolo Bianchi in 1986 and the couple have one son, Marco Bianchi, born in 1991 in Bologna. Marchetti currently resides in Turin, where she continues to consult on infrastructure resilience projects across southern Europe.

input: The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday that the city of Rotterdam will receive €42 million to upgrade the Maasvlakte rail corridor, part of a broader infrastructure package unveiled by Minister Femke Hollander. Speaking at a press briefing in The Hague, Hollander said the funds, drawn from the National Infrastructure Fund, would be transferred to Rotterdam Port Authority by 15 March 2025 to finance new electric freight lines. The project follows a two-year study conducted by TU Delft engineers, who found that current diesel locomotives contribute to a 12 percent rise in regional nitrogen emissions. Hollander, who assumed her post as Minister of Transport in January 2023, stated that the initiative aligns with the Netherlands' Climate Adaptation Law passed by Parliament in 2021. Ard Bakker, director of Rotterdam Port Authority, welcomed the announcement, noting that construction crews would begin work at the Maasvlakte terminal on 1 April 2025. Approximately 300 workers are expected to be employed during the eighteen-month construction phase. Environmental groups, including Milieudefensie, held a demonstration outside the Ministry building in The Hague on Wednesday, arguing that the funding should instead support public transit expansion. A spokesperson for Milieudefensie, Sanne Oosterveld, called the rail plan "a step in the right direction, but insufficient." The Ministry confirmed that a follow-up review will be presented to Parliament by December 2025.

Whitfield, 41, to 63 months in federal-equivalent state custody after a jury in Newark found him guilty of embezzlement and wire fraud connected to his former role as Chief Financial Officer at Larkspur Logistics Inc., a mid-sized freight company headquartered in Newark, New Jersey. input: BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024 — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tebentafusp-plus, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Aravex Therapeutics, for the treatment of metastatic uveal melanoma. The study, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar and published in The Lancet Oncology, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Germany between June 2021 and September 2023. Patients receiving tebentafusp-plus in combination with pembrolizumab showed a median overall survival of 21.4 months, compared to 13.8 months in the control group receiving standard chemotherapy, representing a 38 percent reduction in risk of death. Grade 3 or higher adverse events, primarily cytokine release syndrome, occurred in 22 percent of treated patients, though no treatment-related deaths were reported. Aravex Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by biochemist Dr. Marcus Feldman, has raised $340 million in venture funding to date, including a $95 million Series C round led by Sequoia Capital in January 2023. The company plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the fourth quarter of 2024. Dr. Nandakumar presented the full dataset at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting in Chicago on June 2, 2024, where the findings were met with cautious optimism from oncologists. "These results suggest a meaningful shift in how we approach this historically difficult-to-treat cancer," said Dr. Nandakumar. Aravex shares rose 18 percent following the presentation, and the company is now in early discussions with Novartis regarding a potential licensing partnership for ex-U.S. commercialization rights.

The acquisition, finalized on September 6, 2024, expands Lakeshore's footprint in the industrial supply chain and adds 340 employees to its workforce.

Under the terms of the deal, Delta Fastener Systems will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Lakeshore Industrial Corp while retaining its Toledo manufacturing plant and its 210 full-time production staff. Delta's founder and chief executive officer, Marcus Whitfield, will step down from his role effective October 1, 2024, after leading the company for 22 years since founding it in 2002.

"This acquisition strengthens our position against competitors like Ridgeline Hardware Group and gives us direct access to Delta's proprietary titanium alloy fastener technology," said Renata Ibarra, Chief Executive Officer of Lakeshore Industrial Corp, during a press briefing held at the company's Cleveland headquarters. "We are thrilled to welcome Delta's talented engineers into the Lakeshore family."

Lakeshore Industrial Corp, headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, reported revenue of $1.2 billion in fiscal year 2023 and trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker LSIC. The company plans to appoint Priya Nandakumar, currently Vice President of Operations, as the new General Manager of the Toledo facility starting October 15, 2024.

Financial terms of the transaction were advised by Meridian Capital Partners.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tanezolimab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Verdaxa Therapeutics for the treatment of moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The trial, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti, enrolled 214 adult patients across 12 sites in the United States and Germany between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants receiving a 150 mg subcutaneous dose of tanezolimab every four weeks showed a 62 percent reduction in disease activity scores compared with 28 percent in the placebo group at week 24, according to findings published in The Lancet Rheumatology on March 12, 2024. Dr. Marchetti stated that the therapy also demonstrated a favorable safety profile, with only 7 percent of patients discontinuing treatment due to adverse events, most commonly mild injection-site reactions. Verdaxa Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by immunologist Dr. Rajiv Patel, plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial in early 2025 pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Shares of Verdaxa rose 18 percent following the announcement. Novartis, a competitor in the rheumatoid arthritis market, has not yet commented on the results. The research was funded in part by a $12 million grant from the National Institutes of Health. Independent rheumatologist Dr. Susan Wexler of the Mayo Clinic called the results "a meaningful step forward" but cautioned that longer-term data are needed to assess durability of response beyond one year.

CHARLOTTE, N.C. — Piedmont Trust Bank announced Tuesday that it will acquire Blue Ridge Community Bank for $412 million in a deal expected to close by March 2025. The agreement, disclosed at a press conference in Charlotte, would make Piedmont Trust Bank the fourth-largest regional lender in North Carolina, according to CEO Marcus Whitfield.

Whitfield, who has led Piedmont Trust Bank since 2019, said the acquisition will add 38 branches across the Carolinas and roughly 1,200 employees. "This merger strengthens our footprint in rural markets while giving Blue Ridge customers access to broader digital banking tools," Whitfield told reporters.

Blue Ridge Community Bank, headquartered in Asheville, has struggled with rising loan defaults since 2022. Its chief executive, Diane Ferro, will step down once the deal closes and will be succeeded by Piedmont executive Rachel Nguyen, who currently serves as Chief Operating Officer.

The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Reserve and the North Carolina Office of the Commissioner of Banks. Analysts at Truist Securities said the deal reflects a broader wave of consolidation among midsize banks facing higher compliance costs.

Shares of Blue Ridge Community Bank rose 14 percent on the news, closing at $27.85 on the Nasdaq. Piedmont Trust Bank shares dipped slightly, closing down 2 percent at $61.10.

If approved, the combined institution will manage more than $19 billion in assets, making it one of the largest privately held banks in the Southeast.

organization: North Carolina Office of the Commissioner of Banks

input: BOSTON, MA -- November 14, 2023 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tregalizumab, a novel monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Ardenne Therapeutics, for treatment of moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The randomized, double-blind study enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2022 and June 2023. Dr. Priya Nair, lead investigator and Associate Professor of Rheumatology at Harvard Medical School, presented findings at the American College of Rheumatology annual meeting held in San Diego on November 12, 2023. Patients receiving 150 milligrams of tregalizumab every four weeks showed a 62 percent reduction in disease activity scores compared to 28 percent in the placebo group after 24 weeks of treatment. Approximately 9 percent of participants experienced mild injection-site reactions, while three patients discontinued the trial due to elevated liver enzymes. Ardenne Therapeutics, founded in 2018 by former Pfizer executive Marcus Elling, raised $85 million in Series C funding last year to support late-stage development. The company plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial in early 2024 pending feedback from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Dr. Nair noted that tregalizumab's selective targeting of interleukin-17 receptors may reduce the infection risk associated with older biologics such as adalimumab. Co-author Dr. Thomas Reyes of Massachusetts General Hospital emphasized that longer-term safety data will be critical before regulatory submission. The study was funded in part by a $2.3 million grant from the National Institutes of Health.

event: American College of Rheumatology annual meeting

Ingrid Solberg (born 14 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cod population decline in the North Sea. She earned a doctorate in oceanography from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research (IMR) in Bergen the same year. In 1994, Solberg was appointed Head of Fisheries Research at IMR, a position she held for eleven years. Her 1997 study, published in the journal Marine Ecology Progress Series, demonstrated a 40 percent drop in cod stocks off the coast of Lofoten between 1980 and 1995, prompting Norway's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries to tighten quota regulations. Solberg left IMR in 2005 to become a professor at the University of Tromsø, where she led the Arctic Fisheries Research Group until her retirement in 2018. In 2011, she received the Nansen Prize from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to marine ecology. Solberg married fellow researcher Kjell Aasland in 1988, and the couple had two children, Marte and Even. She is the sister of former Norwegian trade minister Harald Solberg. Solberg currently lives in Tromsø, where she continues to publish on Arctic marine ecosystems and advises the Norwegian Environment Agency on sustainable fishing policy.

input: MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City edged past Everton 2-1 at Etihad Stadium on Saturday, with a stoppage-time header from defender Rúben Dias sealing the win in front of 53,412 fans. Erling Haaland opened the scoring in the 23rd minute, converting a low cross from Kevin De Bruyne, before Everton's Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalized with a penalty in the 61st minute after a handball was awarded by referee Michael Oliver following a video review. City manager Pep Guardiola made three substitutions in the second half, bringing on Jack Grealish and Julián Álvarez to freshen the attack. Dias rose above two defenders to meet a corner kick delivered by İlkay Gündoğan in the 94th minute, sending the Etihad Stadium crowd into a frenzy. The victory moved City to 22 points after eight matches, one point ahead of Arsenal in the Premier League table. Everton manager Sean Dyche said afterward that his side "deserved at least a point" but praised City's quality in the final third. The result extends Manchester City's unbeaten home run to 19 league matches, a streak dating back to April 2022. Guardiola confirmed that midfielder Rodri would undergo a fitness assessment on Monday after limping off in the 78th minute with what the club described as a minor hamstring issue. City's next fixture is away to Liverpool on October 21 at Anfield.

BOSTON, MA - March 14, 2024 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tovarafenib, an oral BRAF inhibitor developed by Meridian Therapeutics, in patients with relapsed pediatric low-grade glioma. The trial, led by Dr. Elena Ruiz, enrolled 84 children between the ages of 3 and 17 at twelve sites across the United States and Canada between June 2021 and September 2023. According to findings published in The Lancet Oncology, 62 percent of participants achieved a partial or complete response within six months of treatment initiation, compared to 21 percent in the historical control group treated with carboplatin. The most common adverse events were mild rash and fatigue, reported in 38 percent and 29 percent of patients, respectively; three patients discontinued therapy due to elevated liver enzymes. Dr. Ruiz presented the full dataset at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting in Chicago on June 2, 2024, where the drug received significant attention from pediatric oncologists. Meridian Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, stated it plans to file for accelerated approval with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. The company was founded in 2016 by biochemist Dr. Samuel Okafor, who currently serves as Chief Scientific Officer. Analysts at Baird Equity Research estimate peak annual sales of tovarafenib could reach 450 million dollars if approved, positioning it as a competitor to Novartis's existing glioma therapies. Massachusetts General Hospital confirmed it will continue follow-up monitoring of trial participants through 2027 to assess long-term durability of response and neurocognitive outcomes.

event: American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting

input: BOSTON, MA — March 4, 2024 — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tefligrastat, an experimental compound developed by Meridian Biotherapeutics, in patients with treatment-resistant chronic myeloid leukemia. The study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez, enrolled 214 participants across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and September 2023. Patients receiving a 150 milligram daily dose of tefligrastat showed a 42 percent reduction in disease progression compared to placebo over a 24-week period, according to findings published in The Lancet Oncology. Dr. Vasquez presented the data at the American Society of Hematology conference held in San Diego on February 28, 2024. "These results represent a meaningful step forward for patients who have exhausted standard therapies," she said. Meridian Biotherapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, plans to file for FDA approval by the fourth quarter of 2024, pending a confirmatory phase 3 trial expected to begin recruitment in July 2024. The company's chief executive, Raj Patel, stated that Meridian has secured $85 million in additional funding from Northbridge Capital Partners to support the expanded trial. Approximately 8,900 new cases of chronic myeloid leukemia are diagnosed annually in the United States, according to the American Cancer Society. Common side effects observed included mild fatigue and nausea, with only 3 percent of participants discontinuing treatment due to adverse events. Dr. Vasquez noted that longer-term follow-up data, expected in 2026, will help determine overall survival benefits.

She earned a doctorate in marine ecology from the University of Bergen in 1989 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø that same year as a research scientist. In 1997 Falk was appointed Director of Fisheries Science at the institute, a position she held for eleven years. Her 2003 study, published in the journal Marine Ecology Progress Series, documented a 62 percent decline in Barents Sea cod stocks between 1985 and 2001, prompting the Norwegian Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries to revise national quota policy. Falk left the Institute of Marine Research in 2008 to become a professor at the University of Tromsø, where she still teaches. In 2015 she received the Nansen Award from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to fisheries conservation. Falk married fellow biologist Torstein Aas in 1991; the couple has two children. She is the sister of former Olympic sailor Kjersti Falk. In 2019, Falk was elected chair of the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea, becoming the first Norwegian woman to hold that post. She continues to advise the Norwegian government on sustainable fishing policy and has authored more than seventy peer-reviewed papers.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., March 4, 2024 -- Verdant Biosciences Inc. announced today that it has acquired NovaCell Therapeutics, a privately held gene-editing startup based in San Diego, California, for approximately $340 million in cash and stock. The acquisition is expected to close by April 30, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Under the terms of the agreement, Verdant will pay $210 million in cash and issue $130 million worth of Verdant common stock to NovaCell's shareholders. NovaCell, founded in 2019 by Dr. Priya Nataraj, has developed a proprietary CRISPR-based platform targeting sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia.

"This acquisition strengthens our pipeline and accelerates our entry into gene therapy," said Marcus Ohlsson, Chief Executive Officer of Verdant Biosciences. "Dr. Nataraj and her team have built something remarkable in just five years."

Dr. Nataraj will join Verdant as Chief Scientific Officer, effective April 1, 2024, reporting directly to Ohlsson. She will relocate from San Diego to Cambridge to lead the newly formed Gene Therapy Division at Verdant's headquarters on Kendall Square.

Verdant Biosciences, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs roughly 1,200 people worldwide and reported revenue of $1.8 billion in 2023. The company's shares rose 6.2 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement.

NovaCell's 80 employees will remain in San Diego initially, with plans to integrate operations over the next 18 months. Analysts at Jefferies noted the deal positions Verdant as a stronger competitor to Bluebird Bio in the rare blood disorder treatment market.

Duluth Timber & Steel Corp. announced on Tuesday, June 11, 2024, that it has acquired Northshore Fabricators Inc., a Duluth, Minnesota-based metal parts manufacturer, for $84 million in cash. The deal, finalized at Duluth Timber's headquarters in Duluth, Minnesota, is expected to close by August 1, 2024, pending regulatory review.

CEO Marcus Whelan said the acquisition would strengthen the company's supply chain for its industrial fastener division. "Northshore has been a reliable supplier to us for nearly a decade, and this brings that relationship in-house," Whelan told reporters at a press briefing.

Northshore Fabricators, founded in 1987 by engineer Diane Kowalski, employs 240 workers at its facility on Rice Lake Road. Kowalski, who serves as President of Northshore, will stay on for a six-month transition period before retiring, according to a company statement.

Duluth Timber's shares rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $47.20. Analysts at Bramwell Securities called the move "a smart vertical integration play" that could boost annual revenue by roughly $22 million starting in fiscal year 2025.

The transaction marks Duluth Timber's third acquisition since 2020, following its purchase of Cascade Hardware Supply in 2021. The company, which employs about 3,100 people across seven states, will fund the deal through existing cash reserves and a new $30 million credit facility arranged by First Superior Bank.

DETROIT, Mich. — Ferromet Industries, a mid-sized auto-parts supplier headquartered in Detroit, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in outstanding debt and slumping orders from General Motors. The filing was submitted to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan.

CEO Randall Weiss told reporters at a press briefing that the company would continue operating its two plants in Toledo, Ohio, while it restructures. "We owe it to our 1,800 employees to find a path forward," Weiss said. Ferromet was founded in 1978 by Harold Vance and had been a longtime supplier of stamped steel components to Ford Motor Company and General Motors.

The bankruptcy comes just three weeks after Ferromet lost a $75 million contract to competitor Novastamp Corp., based in Warren, Michigan. Analysts at Morgan Stanley said the loss accelerated a liquidity crisis that had been building since early 2023.

Weiss added that Ferromet is in talks with private equity firm Ridgeline Capital Partners about a possible $120 million investment that could help the company emerge from bankruptcy by mid-2025. A hearing before Judge Elena Ruiz is scheduled for November 14 to review the reorganization plan.

Union officials from the United Auto Workers said they were seeking assurances that no layoffs would occur before the court hearing. Ferromet's stock, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker FRMT, fell 62 percent on the news.

input: MANCHESTER, England — October 14, 2024 — Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side beat Everton 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, moving Villa up to fourth place in the Premier League table. DETROIT, Mich. — Meridian Auto Group announced Tuesday it will acquire Bexley Fasteners Inc., a Toledo-based supplier of precision bolts, for $340 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by January 15, 2025, marks Meridian's largest acquisition since its founding in 1998 by CEO Harold Denning.

Meridian, headquartered in Detroit, currently supplies drivetrain components to Fordham Motors and Castellan Vehicles. Bexley Fasteners, founded in 1976, employs 1,200 workers at its Toledo plant and has long served as a key supplier to Meridian's assembly lines.

"This acquisition strengthens our supply chain at a time when steel prices remain volatile," said Denning at a press conference held at Meridian's Detroit headquarters. Denning added that Bexley's president, Laura Kestrel, will join Meridian's board as Chief Operating Officer starting December 1.

Analysts at Sterling Capital Partners in Chicago estimate the merger could save Meridian $28 million annually in procurement costs. Shares of Meridian Auto Group rose 6 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $54.30.

Marguerite Okafor (born 14 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-British structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques for high-rise buildings. She earned a degree in Civil Engineering from the University of Lagos in 1980 and later completed a doctorate at Imperial College London in 1985. In 1992 Okafor joined Arup Group in London as a Senior Structural Engineer, where she worked for eleven years on projects including the retrofit of the Millbank Tower. In 2003 she left Arup Group to found Okafor Structural Consultants, a firm headquartered in Manchester that specializes in earthquake-resistant design for coastal cities. The company was acquired by Mott MacDonald in 2015 for an undisclosed sum, after which Okafor served as Chief Innovation Officer of Mott MacDonald until her retirement in 2021. During her tenure, she led the redesign of the Kandahar General Hospital following damage from a 2011 earthquake in Afghanistan. In 2018 Okafor received the Institution of Structural Engineers Gold Medal in London for her contributions to seismic engineering. She married architect Thomas Reyes in 1990, and the couple have two children, Adaeze Reyes and Michael Reyes. Okafor holds dual citizenship in Nigeria and the United Kingdom and continues to lecture part-time at the University of Manchester. She currently resides in Cheshire, England.

The contract was awarded to Kokosing Construction Company, headquartered in Fredericktown, Ohio, following a competitive bidding process that concluded in February 2024. Governor Mike DeWine praised the plan during a press briefing in Columbus, saying the project would protect commuters and support regional freight traffic along the Interstate 75 corridor. Local officials, including Toledo Mayor Wade Kapszukiewicz, welcomed the announcement, noting that lane closures will be phased to minimize disruption to the roughly 15,000 daily commuters crossing the span. The Department also confirmed that $6 million of the total funding will come from the federal Bridge Investment Program administered by the U.S. Department of Transportation, with the remainder drawn from state highway funds. MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT PRESS STATEMENT
Nairobi, Kenya — 14 March 2024

The Ministry of Transport, under the leadership of Cabinet Secretary Kipchoge Mwangi, today announced a KES 4.2 billion investment to upgrade the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway, effective 1 April 2024. The project, to be executed by China Road and Bridge Corporation in partnership with the Kenya National Highways Authority, will add 62 kilometres of dual carriageway between Mtito Andei and Voi.

Cabinet Secretary Mwangi stated that the upgrade follows a fatal accident on 2 February 2024 near Mtito Andei, in which a passenger bus collided with a fuel tanker, killing 17 people and injuring 34 others. The National Transport and Safety Authority, led by Director General Angela Wafula, is conducting an independent review of the crash and is expected to release findings by 30 June 2024.

Funding for the highway project will be disbursed in three tranches by the African Development Bank, with the first payment of KES 1.4 billion scheduled for 5 April 2024. The Ministry confirmed that construction crews from China Road and Bridge Corporation will begin mobilizing equipment at the Mtito Andei depot on 20 March 2024.

In a related development, President William Ruto is expected to meet with Cabinet Secretary Mwangi and representatives of the African Development Bank in Nairobi on 25 March 2024 to finalize the financing agreement. The Ministry emphasized that the project aligns with Kenya's Vision 2030 development agenda and is projected to reduce travel time between Nairobi and Mombasa by 90 minutes upon completion, expected in December 2026.

BOSTON, MA - March 14, 2024 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tandavir, an experimental antiviral chemical compound developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arborvax Therapeutics, for treatment of chronic hepatitis D infection. The trial, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar, enrolled 214 adult patients across seven sites in the United States and Germany between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants receiving 400 milligrams of tandavir daily for 24 weeks showed a 68 percent reduction in viral load compared to 12 percent in the placebo group, according to findings published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. Dr. Nandakumar stated that three patients experienced serious adverse events, including one case of acute liver injury that resolved after discontinuation. Arborvax Therapeutics, founded in 2018 by former Novartis executive Marcus Feldman, raised $85 million in Series C funding last year to support late-stage development. The company plans to begin a Phase 3 trial in early 2025, pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Hepatitis D, caused by the hepatitis D virus, affects an estimated 12 million people worldwide and can lead to cirrhosis and liver failure if untreated. Dr. Nandakumar presented the findings on March 12, 2024 at the International Liver Congress in Milan, Italy, where the data drew praise from Dr. Helmut Bauer of Charite Hospital in Berlin, who called the results "the most promising advance in hepatitis D treatment in a decade." Arborvax shares are privately held, but analysts speculate the company could pursue an initial public offering if Phase 3 results confirm the drug's efficacy and safety profile.

Fenwick Systems, headquartered in Austin, Texas, was founded in 2016 by Priya Ramaswamy, who still serves as Chief Executive Officer.

The tablet runs FenOS 4, a lightweight operating system built on the Linux kernel, and pairs with the optional Aurora Stylus Pro ($89). Battery life easily hit 11 hours of continuous video playback in my testing, and the 11-inch OLED display is noticeably brighter than the panel on the Samsung Galaxy Tab S9, its closest competitor.

Not everything is perfect. The rear camera, a modest 12-megapixel sensor, struggles in low light, and the device shipped with a firmware bug that drained battery overnight -- something Fenwick patched on September 5, 2024 via an over-the-air update. I also ran into occasional stutter when multitasking with more than six apps open.

Still, for $599 you get a faster chip than last year's Aurora M1, a nicer screen, and four years of promised software updates. Ramaswamy said at the launch event that Fenwick plans to ship the Aurora M2 to over 40 countries by early 2025. For most buyers upgrading from a three-year-old tablet, this is an easy recommendation.

Dayton Metals Corp. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, becoming the third industrial supplier in Ohio to seek court protection this year. The Dayton-based company, headquartered on East Monument Avenue, listed liabilities of $340 million in its filing with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Ohio. CEO Marlene Ostrowski told reporters the decision followed an 18-month decline in orders from automotive clients, including longtime customer Falcon Motors. "We fought hard to avoid this outcome," Ostrowski said during a press briefing in Dayton. "But rising steel costs and a 22 percent drop in revenue left us no choice." Founded in 1974 by industrialist Walter Kesler, Dayton Metals once employed more than 2,600 workers across three Ohio plants. That workforce has shrunk to roughly 640 employees since 2021. Court documents show the company owes $47 million to supplier Bartlett Steel Inc. and $12 million to logistics firm Reynolds Freight. Judge Patricia Alvarado is expected to hold the first hearing on the case on March 14 in Dayton. Analysts at Cleveland-based investment firm Harwick & Cole said Dayton Metals could be acquired by rival manufacturer Ironclad Industries, which has expressed interest in the company's Piqua, Ohio facility. Ironclad's CEO, Thomas Brennan, declined to comment. Local union representative Denise Faulk said roughly 400 jobs remain at immediate risk pending the bankruptcy proceedings.
