MANCHESTER, England - October 14, 2023 - Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side defeated Everton 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, lifting Villa to fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low finish from inside the box, then doubled the lead just before halftime after a quick counterattack set up by midfielder John McGinn. Everton pulled one back through striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 63rd minute, but defender Ezri Konsa restored Villa's two-goal cushion in stoppage time. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, telling reporters, "We controlled the tempo for long periods and deserved the three points." Everton boss Sean Dyche, whose side has now lost four of its last six league matches, acknowledged the gap in quality but insisted his players are fighting for survival. The win moves Aston Villa to 22 points from ten matches, three points behind leaders Manchester City. Villa's next fixture is away to Tottenham Hotspur on October 21, while Everton will host Brentford at Goodison Park the same weekend. Roughly 41,000 fans attended Saturday's match at Villa Park, and the Premier League confirmed no disciplinary action would follow a minor confrontation between players after the final whistle.

Boston, MA -- November 4, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tregolimab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Veridian Therapeutics, for treatment of moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis. The 24-week study, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar and published in The New England Journal of Medicine, enrolled 312 adult patients across 18 sites in the United States and Canada. Participants receiving 300 milligrams of tregolimab every four weeks achieved clinical remission at a rate of 41.3 percent, compared to 12.7 percent in the placebo group, a statistically significant difference (p<0.001). Dr. Nandakumar stated that the drug's novel mechanism, which selectively inhibits interleukin-23 signaling, appeared to reduce intestinal inflammation without the infection risk associated with older immunosuppressants. Veridian Therapeutics, founded in 2015 by former Genzyme executive Marcus Whitfield, plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial in early 2024 involving approximately 900 patients. The company's chief executive, Elena Torres, said Veridian had secured $85 million in additional funding from Sequoia Capital to support the expanded trial and eventual regulatory submission to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Shares of Veridian rose 14 percent following the announcement, which was presented at the American College of Gastroenterology's annual meeting in Chicago. Some gastroenterologists, including Dr. Robert Klein of the Cleveland Clinic, cautioned that longer-term safety data would be needed before tregolimab could be considered a first-line therapy for ulcerative colitis.

input: Fjallbris Outdoor Gear, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, has released the Vindkast 3-Season Tent, a two-person shelter designed for backpackers tackling the Colorado Trail and similar routes. Priced at $329.00, the tent weighs just 2.3 kilograms and packs down to the size of a 1-liter water bottle. The rainfly uses a 20-denier ripstop nylon treated with a silicone coating, while the floor is built from 30-denier polyurethane-coated fabric rated to withstand 3,000mm of hydrostatic pressure. Fjallbris founder Ingrid Solheim, a former mountain guide from Bergen, Norway, tested early prototypes during a 14-day trek through Jotunheimen National Park in July 2022 before finalizing the design. The tent includes two vestibules, each offering 0.8 square meters of gear storage, and sets up in under six minutes using a single 9mm aluminum pole system sourced from supplier Easton Mountain Products in Salt Lake City. Each unit ships with eight titanium stakes, a repair kit, and a compression sack. The Vindkast is currently sold new, in limited stock of 4,000 units for the 2024 season, through Fjallbris's online store and at REI locations across the United States. Customer reviews on the company website average 4.7 out of 5 stars, with hikers praising its stability during a windstorm on Long's Peak last September. Fjallbris offers a lifetime warranty against manufacturing defects and free shipping on orders over $75. The tent is available in two colorways, Arctic Grey and Moss Green, and ships within 3 business days of ordering.

Marguerite Odom (born March 14, 1927, in Biloxi, Mississippi) was an American marine biologist best known for her studies of Gulf Coast oyster reefs. She earned a Bachelor of Science degree from Tulane University in 1949 and completed her doctorate at the Scripps Institution of Oceanography in 1955. In 1958 Odom joined the faculty of Louisiana State University as an assistant professor of zoology, a position she held until 1966, when she was promoted to full professor. Her 1962 monograph, "Reefs of the Mississippi Sound", became a standard reference in estuarine ecology and was cited widely throughout the 1970s. In 1971 Odom founded the Gulf Coast Marine Research Institute in Ocean Springs, Mississippi, serving as its first director for eleven years. Under her leadership the institute received a $2.3 million grant from the National Science Foundation in 1974 to study hypoxia in Mississippi Sound. Odom married fellow biologist Charles Renwick in 1953; the couple had two children, Elizabeth and Thomas Renwick. In 1980 she was elected to the National Academy of Sciences, and in 1985 she received the National Medal of Science, presented by President Ronald Reagan at a ceremony in Washington, D.C. Odom retired from active research in 1992 and died on September 9, 2004, in Ocean Springs at the age of 77. The Marguerite Odom Marine Laboratory at Louisiana State University was dedicated in her honor in 2007.

Danville, IL — Midwest Rail Components Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Central District of Illinois, citing $42 million in outstanding debt and a sharp drop in orders from freight carriers. The company, headquartered in Danville since 1978, employs 310 workers at its manufacturing plant on Fairchild Street.

CEO Marcus Whitfield told reporters the bankruptcy filing was necessary after Union Pacific Railroad canceled a $15 million supply contract in March. "We fought hard to keep this plant running," Whitfield said during a press conference outside the courthouse. "Our workers deserve better than what the freight industry has done to them."

The company's largest creditor, First National Bank of Chicago, is owed approximately $18 million. Judge Rebecca Alston has scheduled a hearing for August 14, 2024, to review the reorganization plan submitted by attorney Diane Kowalski of Kowalski & Ferris LLP.

Local union representative Tom Bracewell said roughly 90 employees have already received layoff notices effective July 1, 2024. Illinois Governor Pat Sinclair issued a statement Wednesday pledging $2 million in state emergency funds to support displaced workers through the Illinois Department of Employment Security.

Midwest Rail Components was founded in 1978 by engineer Harold Voss and has supplied brake components to Union Pacific Railroad and Norfolk Southern Corporation for over four decades. Industry analysts say the case reflects broader struggles among mid-sized manufacturers amid rising steel costs and reduced rail freight volume nationwide.

input: BOSTON, MA — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital reported on March 14, 2024 that a novel oral compound, designated MGH-2201, significantly reduced tumor progression in patients with treatment-resistant pancreatic cancer. The Phase II trial, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez, enrolled 142 participants across three sites, including Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in Boston and Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles, between June 2022 and September 2023. Patients receiving 150 milligrams of MGH-2201 twice daily showed a 38 percent reduction in tumor size after twelve weeks, compared with 9 percent in the placebo group. The drug, a small-molecule inhibitor targeting KRAS G12D mutations, was developed in collaboration with Cambridge-based biotechnology firm Halberd Therapeutics, which was founded in 2018 by biochemist Raymond Okafor. Dr. Vasquez presented the findings at the American Association for Cancer Research annual meeting in San Diego on April 5, 2024. Common adverse events included mild nausea in 22 percent of patients and fatigue in 17 percent, with no grade 4 toxicities reported. Halberd Therapeutics announced it will pursue Food and Drug Administration approval, with a New Drug Application expected by the first quarter of 2025. The company's stock rose 14 percent following the announcement. Dr. Vasquez noted that a larger Phase III trial involving 600 patients is being planned for late 2024, potentially expanding testing to additional centers including the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. Halberd Therapeutics has raised $85 million in venture funding to date, with Sequoia Capital as its lead investor. Researchers cautioned that longer-term data on survival outcomes will not be available until at least 2026, and independent replication remains necessary before the therapy can be considered standard of care for this aggressive malignancy.

input: The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday, March 11, 2025, that it will invest 420 million euros to upgrade rail infrastructure along the Lisbon-Porto corridor. Minister Beatriz Coelho stated at a press briefing in Lisbon that the funds, allocated under the National Rail Modernization Law, will finance new signaling systems and the replacement of aging tracks by December 2027. The announcement follows a meeting on March 6, 2025, between Coelho and Comboios de Portugal chief executive Rui Andrade at the Ministry's headquarters in Lisbon, where both parties discussed procurement timelines. Comboios de Portugal, the state-owned railway operator, will oversee construction, while contractor Mota-Engil has been selected to supply materials and labor for the first phase, worth 95 million euros. Officials said the project will create approximately 1,200 jobs across the Setubal and Coimbra regions over the next two years. Deputy Minister Tiago Ferreira, who started his position in January 2024, said the initiative reflects Portugal's broader commitment to reducing carbon emissions from domestic transport by 30 percent before 2030. Opposition lawmaker Ines Marques criticized the plan on Wednesday, arguing that similar promises made in 2019 were never fully funded. The Ministry responded that an independent audit, to be conducted by KPMG Portugal, will monitor spending transparency and publish quarterly reports starting in June 2025.

Boston, MA -- November 4, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolvexinib, an experimental oral chemical compound developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arannex Therapeutics, for treatment of moderate-to-severe psoriasis. The study, led by Dr. Helena Marsh, an immunologist and Associate Professor at Harvard Medical School, enrolled 214 adult patients across twelve sites in the United States and Canada between March 2022 and July 2023. Patients receiving 150 milligrams of tolvexinib daily for sixteen weeks achieved a 76 percent reduction in Psoriasis Area and Severity Index scores, compared with 31 percent among those given placebo. Dr. Marsh presented the findings on November 3, 2023, at the American Academy of Dermatology meeting in Chicago. "These results suggest tolvexinib could become a first-line option within three years," she said during a press briefing. Arannex Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by former Pfizer executive Daniel Ostrow, plans to begin a Phase 3 trial in early 2024 involving approximately 900 participants across sites in Germany, Japan, and Brazil. The company's chief executive, Priya Nandakumar, stated that Arannex has secured $85 million in Series C funding, led by venture firm Silverbrook Capital, to support the expanded trial and eventual regulatory submission to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Analysts at Meridian Health Partners noted that competitor Novartis currently dominates the psoriasis treatment market with its drug Cosentyx. Full trial data will be published in The New England Journal of Medicine in January 2024.

input: Kessler Pharmaceuticals Inc., headquartered in Newark, New Jersey, agreed on Tuesday to acquire Vantix Biosciences for $2.4 billion in cash, the companies announced. The deal, expected to close by December 15, will give Kessler control of Vantix's experimental drug, Remoxatin, which targets early-stage pancreatic cancer. Vantix, founded in 2014 by Dr. Elena Marsh, is based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and employs roughly 340 people. Under the agreement, Vantix shareholders will receive $58 per share, a 32 percent premium over Monday's closing price. Kessler CEO Raymond Ott called the acquisition "a pivotal step toward strengthening our oncology pipeline" during a press call on Tuesday afternoon. Dr. Marsh, who will join Kessler's board as Chief Scientific Officer starting January 6, said the merger would accelerate Remoxatin's path to FDA approval. Analysts at Merrick Sachs noted that the deal marks Kessler's third acquisition in two years, following its 2022 purchase of Talon Genomics. Shares of Vantix jumped 29 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Kessler stock slipped 3 percent amid investor concerns over debt financing. The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which is expected to review the deal over the next 90 days. If completed, it would rank among the largest biotech acquisitions of the year, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

CHICAGO, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Deere & Company said Tuesday it will acquire GrainTrack Systems Inc, a Peoria-based agricultural software startup, for $412 million in cash, as the farm-equipment giant deepens its push into precision-farming technology. The deal, expected to close by December 15, was announced by Deere Chief Executive John May at the company's Moline, Illinois headquarters. GrainTrack, founded in 2016 by former Caterpillar engineer Priya Nandakumar, makes sensor-based crop-yield software used on roughly 38,000 farms across the Midwest. Nandakumar will join Deere as Vice President of Digital Agriculture, reporting directly to May, effective November 1. Deere shares rose 3.2 percent to $398.50 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume topped 5.1 million shares, well above the daily average. Analyst Marcus Feld of Baird raised his price target on Deere to $430, calling the acquisition "a smart bolt-on that strengthens Deere's data moat against rival CNH Industrial." CNH shares slipped 1.4 percent in early trading. Deere said it would fund the purchase through existing cash reserves and did not expect the deal to require regulatory review beyond a standard Hart-Scott-Rodino filing. GrainTrack employs 210 people and will continue operating from its Peoria office as a wholly owned subsidiary. The transaction marks Deere's fourth software acquisition since 2021 and its largest since the $250 million purchase of Bear Flag Robotics. Shareholders of GrainTrack are expected to receive payment by early January.

BOSTON, MA -- November 4, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolerizumab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Verolux Therapeutics, for the treatment of moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The trial, led by principal investigator Dr. Elena Marchetti, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2022 and July 2023. Participants who received 150 milligrams of tolerizumab every four weeks showed a 62 percent reduction in disease activity scores compared to 24 percent in the placebo group after 24 weeks, according to findings published in The Lancet Rheumatology on November 3, 2023. Dr. Marchetti stated that the drug's safety profile was consistent with earlier Phase 1 data, with only 8 percent of patients reporting mild injection-site reactions. Verolux Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by immunologist Dr. Raj Patel, plans to begin a Phase 3 trial in early 2024 pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The company's chief executive, Nadia Kessler, said Verolux has raised $85 million in Series C funding led by Boston-based venture firm Highline Capital Partners to support the expanded trial. Analysts at Meridian Health Partners noted that tolerizumab could compete directly with AbbVie's Humira and Amgen's Enbrel if approved. Rheumatoid arthritis affects roughly 1.3 million adults in the United States, according to the Arthritis Foundation. Dr. Marchetti presented the full dataset at the American College of Rheumatology annual meeting in San Diego on November 12, 2023.

DENVER, Colo. — Meridian Foods Inc. announced Tuesday that it has acquired Rocky Mountain Organics LLC, a Boulder-based supplier of packaged salads, for $84 million in cash. The deal, confirmed by Meridian CEO Patricia Halvorsen at a press briefing held at Meridian's headquarters in Denver, is expected to close by November 15, 2024. Halvorsen said the acquisition will help Meridian expand its footprint in the organic foods sector amid rising competition from Fresh Fields Co., a rival grocery-focused conglomerate based in Chicago. Rocky Mountain Organics was founded in 2011 by entrepreneur Daniel Ortiz, who will remain as a consultant for six months following the transition. The company employs 210 workers across two facilities in Boulder and Fort Collins. Halvorsen, who took over as CEO of Meridian Foods in March 2022 after the retirement of longtime chief executive Robert Klein, stated that no layoffs are planned. "This is about growth, not consolidation of headcount," she told reporters. Shares of Meridian Foods rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $47.12. Analysts at Whitfield Capital Partners called the acquisition a smart strategic move, noting that organic food sales in the United States grew 11 percent last year. Rocky Mountain Organics products will remain on shelves under their existing brand name for at least eighteen months, according to company spokesperson Elena Marsh.

SUPERIOR COURT OF SANTA CLARA COUNTY, CALIFORNIA

Case No. 24-CV-118842 — People v. Marcus D. Ellery

On September 12, 2024, Judge Renata Vasquez sentenced Marcus D. Ellery, 41, of San Jose, to 36 months in state prison after he pleaded guilty to grand theft and embezzlement. Prosecutor Alan Ferris of the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office argued that Ellery, formerly a controller at Beacon Ridge Logistics, diverted approximately $412,000 from company accounts between January 2021 and March 2023 by issuing fraudulent vendor payments to a shell company he controlled, Halden Supply LLC. Ferris told the court during the September 5 hearing at the San Jose Hall of Justice that Ellery had used the funds to purchase a 2022 Range Rover and a condominium in Truckee, California.

Ellery was arrested on April 4, 2023, by detectives from the San Jose Police Department following an internal audit conducted by Beacon Ridge Logistics after its chief financial officer, Priya Nandakumar, noticed discrepancies in quarterly filings. Defense attorney Wendell Cho asked Judge Vasquez for leniency, citing Ellery's cooperation and lack of prior record, but the court ordered restitution of $412,000 to Beacon Ridge Logistics in addition to the prison term.

Beacon Ridge Logistics, headquartered in Milpitas, California, issued a statement thanking the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office and confirmed it has since implemented new internal controls. The company is a subsidiary of Cascade Freight Holdings, based in Denver, Colorado.

input: Ingrid Solberg (born 14 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cod population decline in the North Sea. She earned a doctorate in oceanography from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Bergen as a research scientist that same year. In 1994 she became Head of the Fisheries Ecology Department at the institute, a position she held for eleven years. Solberg's 1999 study, published in the journal Marine Ecology Progress Series, demonstrated a 40 percent decline in cod stocks linked to rising sea temperatures, work that influenced European Union fishing quotas. In 2003 she left the Institute of Marine Research to become a professor at the University of Tromso, where she led the Arctic Fisheries Research Group. She married fellow biologist Jan Eriksen in 1988; the couple had two children, Astrid and Mikael. In October 2011, Solberg received the Nansen Award from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to marine ecology. She retired from the University of Tromso in June 2020 but continued advising the Norwegian Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries on sustainable fishing policy. Solberg died on 9 January 2023 in Tromso after a long illness. She was 64. Her colleague Dr. Henrik Aasgard called her "the most rigorous mind in Nordic fisheries science." A research vessel operated by the Institute of Marine Research, the FF Ingrid Solberg, was named in her honor in 2024.

Ohlin stated in a press release, "We built the Voyager 45L for thru-hikers tackling the Pacific Crest Trail, not weekend campers."

Each backpack undergoes a 48-hour field test at the company's testing facility near Mount Hood before shipping. Customers who purchase before October 15, 2024 will receive a free rain cover, normally priced at $24.

The Timberline Voyager 45L is currently in stock and ships within 2 business days via UPS Ground. Fenwick & Ash offers a 5-year warranty on all frame components and a 90-day satisfaction guarantee. Reviews on the company's site currently average 4.7 out of 5 stars from 312 verified buyers. Competing models include the Gregory Baltoro 65 and the Osprey Aether Plus, though Fenwick & Ash claims the Voyager 45L is 15% lighter than both.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF ARIZONA, MARICOPA COUNTY

Case No. CR2024-018837

On March 11, 2024, the Maricopa County Attorney's Office formally charged Dennis R. Whitfield, 47, with two counts of aggravated fraud and one count of money laundering following an investigation into Sonoran Capital Partners LLC, a Phoenix-based investment firm Whitfield founded in 2016. Prosecutor Elena Martz alleged that between January 2019 and September 2023, Whitfield solicited approximately $2.3 million from at least fourteen investors, promising annual returns of 18 percent through a purported real estate fund that prosecutors say never existed.

Judge Rosalind Ferris presided over the arraignment held at the Maricopa County Superior Courthouse in Phoenix, Arizona, on March 15, 2024. Whitfield entered a plea of not guilty through his attorney, Marcus Halloway of the firm Halloway & Bright. Bail was set at $500,000.

According to court filings, Whitfield was arrested by detectives from the Phoenix Police Department on March 8, 2024, at his residence in Scottsdale, Arizona, after victim Carol Yeng, a retired schoolteacher, reported losing $180,000 of her retirement savings. A trial hearing has been scheduled for July 22, 2024, before Judge Ferris. If convicted, Whitfield faces up to 20 years in state prison.

Sonoran Capital Partners LLC ceased operations in October 2023 and has not filed for bankruptcy. The Arizona Corporation Commission revoked the firm's registration on November 30, 2023.

DETROIT, Mich. — Riverline Motors Inc. announced Tuesday that it has acquired battery startup VoltCore Technologies for $340 million, a move aimed at strengthening its electric vehicle supply chain. Hélène Vasseur (born 12 March 1958 in Lyon, France) is a French microbiologist known for her discoveries in antibiotic resistance mechanisms. She earned a doctorate in molecular biology from the University of Strasbourg in 1984 and joined the Pasteur Institute in Paris the same year as a research fellow. In 1991, Vasseur was appointed Head of the Bacterial Genetics Unit at the Pasteur Institute, a position she held for over two decades. Her 1996 paper describing the plasmid-mediated spread of the enzyme NDM-1 precursor genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae reshaped clinical approaches to hospital-acquired infections. In 2003, she co-founded the biotech firm MicroGenix Therapeutics with fellow researcher Bernard Lefèvre, headquartered in Lyon, to develop novel antimicrobial compounds. The company was acquired by the Swiss pharmaceutical giant Novartis in 2011 for approximately 340 million euros, allowing Vasseur to fund a new laboratory dedicated to phage therapy research. She left the Pasteur Institute in 2014 to become a professor at Sorbonne Université, where she still leads a research group of twelve scientists. In 2018, Vasseur received the Louis Pasteur Medal from the French Academy of Sciences in Paris for her contributions to combating antibiotic resistance. She married fellow scientist Bernard Lefèvre in 1987, and the couple has one daughter, Camille Lefèvre, born in 1990, who is now herself a physician in Marseille. Vasseur continues to publish widely and serves as an advisor to the World Health Organization on antimicrobial resistance policy.

Elena Radovic (born March 14, 1958, in Novi Sad, Yugoslavia) is a Serbian-American structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-resistant bridge designs. She emigrated to the United States in 1981 and earned a master's degree in civil engineering from Cornell University in 1984. In 1990, Radovic joined Halloran & Fitch, a New York-based engineering firm, as a senior structural engineer, and by 1997 she had risen to Chief Engineer, a position she held for over a decade.

In 2003, Radovic led the design team for the Kessler Strait Bridge in Astoria, Oregon, a project that withstood a magnitude 6.4 earthquake in 2008 without structural damage, cementing her reputation in the field. For this achievement, she received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation from the United States government in a ceremony held in Washington, D.C. in 2009.

In 2011, Radovic left Halloran & Fitch to found her own firm, Radovic Structural Partners, headquartered in Portland, Oregon, with initial funding of $2.3 million from private investors. The firm has since completed over 40 infrastructure projects across North America. Radovic married fellow engineer Thomas Whitfield in 1995; the couple has two children. She continues to lecture part-time at Cornell University and serves on the board of the American Society of Civil Engineers.

The Ministry of Environment and Water Resources of Ghana announced on 14 March 2024 that it will invest 85 million Ghanaian cedi to rehabilitate flood defenses along the White Volta River in the Northern Region. The announcement, delivered by Minister Samuel Abu Jinapor at a press briefing in Accra, follows severe flooding in September 2023 that displaced roughly 12,000 residents near Tamale and damaged more than 3,400 homes. Jinapor stated that the Ghana Hydrological Authority, in partnership with the World Bank, will oversee construction of new levees and drainage channels by December 2025. "We cannot allow another disaster like the one that struck Tamale to repeat itself," Jinapor told reporters. The project will be financed through a combination of government funds and a 40 million dollar loan from the African Development Bank, approved on 2 February 2024. Deputy Minister Ama Serwaa Owusu will coordinate with local chiefs and the Northern Regional Coordinating Council to ensure timely resettlement of affected families. Construction firm Sinohydro Ghana Limited has been contracted to lead the engineering work, with an estimated workforce of 600 laborers drawn from surrounding districts. The Ministry emphasized that climate resilience remains a national priority, noting that Ghana experienced three major flooding events between 2021 and 2023. Officials also confirmed that a public forum will be held in Tamale on 5 April 2024 to gather community input before construction begins.

input: Ingrid Solberg (born 14 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cod population decline in the North Sea. She earned her doctorate in Marine Ecology from the University of Bergen in 1985 and later joined the Institute of Marine Research in Bergen as a research scientist in 1988. In 1997 Solberg was appointed Director of Fisheries Research at the same institute, a position she held for fourteen years. Her 2003 study on overfishing, published in the journal Marine Ecology Progress, was cited by the Norwegian Ministry of Fisheries when drafting the Sustainable Fisheries Act of 2005. Solberg founded the nonprofit organization OceanWatch Nordic in Oslo in 2009 to advocate for marine conservation policy across Scandinavia. In 2014 she received the Nansen Environmental Prize, awarded by the Fridtjof Nansen Institute, in recognition of her contributions to sustainable fisheries management. Solberg married fellow biologist Anders Kval in 1990, and the couple has one son, Erik Kval, born in 1993 in Bergen. She retired from the Institute of Marine Research in 2018 but continues to serve on the advisory board of OceanWatch Nordic. Solberg currently resides in Bergen, where she occasionally lectures at the University of Bergen on climate change and fish stock migration patterns.

Marguerite Yvon Delacroix (born 14 March 1927 in Lyon, France; died 2 September 2011 in Geneva, Switzerland) was a French-Swiss biochemist known for isolating the enzyme lactamase-7, a discovery that reshaped early dairy fermentation research. She earned her doctorate from the University of Lyon in 1951 and completed postdoctoral work at the Pasteur Institute in Paris under Professor Henri Vasseur.

In 1958, Delacroix joined Nestle S.A., headquartered in Vevey, Switzerland, as a research chemist, later rising to the position of Director of Biochemical Research in 1966. During her tenure she led the team that developed the patented preservation compound Lactafresh, which Nestle began marketing in 1971. She left Nestle in 1979 to found the Institut Delacroix pour la Recherche Biologique in Geneva, an independent laboratory that received early funding of 2.3 million Swiss francs from the Bertrand Foundation.

Delacroix married physicist Armand Rieux in 1955; their daughter, Celine Rieux, later became a molecular biologist at the University of Geneva. Armand Rieux died in 1994.

In 1988, Delacroix received the Marcel Benoist Prize, Switzerland's most prestigious science award, presented in Bern by the Swiss Confederation for her contributions to biochemistry. She published over 60 papers and was elected to the Swiss Academy of Sciences in 1990. The Institut Delacroix, now a subsidiary of the Bertrand Foundation, continues operating in Geneva today, employing roughly 40 researchers.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google's Third Attempt Finally Sticks

By Renata Suh, published October 14, 2024, San Francisco

Google launched the Pixel Watch 3 on September 20, 2024, priced at $349.99 for the 41mm Wi-Fi model, and after three weeks of daily wear I think the company has finally nailed the formula. I bought my review unit directly from the Google Store in Mountain View, California, and it arrived new in box with a redesigned charging puck.

The standout upgrade is the 320 mAh battery, which now comfortably lasts 36 hours, up from the 24 hours I got on the Pixel Watch 2 last year. Fitbit, now fully absorbed into Google's hardware division after the 2019 acquisition, contributes the sleep-tracking algorithms, and the new Cardio Load metric feels genuinely useful for runners like myself training for the Chicago Marathon.

Competitor Samsung still holds an edge in raw display brightness with the Galaxy Watch 7, but Google's software integration with Android 15 is tighter. During a briefing at Google's Chelsea Market office in New York on October 2, 2024, product manager Sandeep Rao told journalists that the Loss of Pulse Detection feature, built with input from Mayo Clinic researchers, has already been submitted to the FDA for clearance.

At $349.99, the Pixel Watch 3 isn't cheap, and the 45mm LTE version climbs to $499.99. Still, for anyone embedded in the Android ecosystem, this is the most compelling smartwatch Google has ever shipped.

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY — On October 14, 2024, Judge Miriam Castellano sentenced Darnell Pruitt, 37, of Newark, to 8 years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of aggravated arson and insurance fraud stemming from a January 3, 2023 fire at a warehouse owned by Bergen Storage Solutions LLC on Frelinghuysen Avenue. Prosecutor Elena Vasquez, representing the Essex County District Attorney's Office, argued that Pruitt hired an accomplice, Marcus Reilly, to set the blaze in order to collect a $2.1 million insurance payout from Continental Indemnity Group. Reilly, who pleaded guilty in April 2024 and testified against Pruitt, was sentenced separately to 3 years. During the two-week trial at the Wilentz Justice Complex in Newark, defense attorney Thomas Kaminski maintained that his client was in Trenton on the night of the fire, but surveillance footage placed Pruitt's vehicle, a gray Ford F-150, near the site at 11:40 p.m. No injuries were reported, though firefighters from the Newark Fire Department battled the blaze for nearly six hours. Judge Castellano ordered Pruitt to pay $2.1 million in restitution to Continental Indemnity Group, payable within five years. Pruitt's attorney indicated he would appeal the verdict to the New Jersey Appellate Division. The case, State v. Pruitt, drew attention after local news outlet The Newark Ledger reported on possible ties between Pruitt and a wider fraud ring under investigation by the New Jersey State Police.

MADRID, October 14, 2023 -- Carlos Reyes scored twice as Atletico Vallecas defeated Real Sporting Club 3-1 at the Estadio Teresa Rivero on Saturday, moving the home side into second place in the Segunda Division standings. Reyes, a 26-year-old forward from Argentina, opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a left-footed strike after a pass from midfielder Diego Molina. Real Sporting Club equalized in the 34th minute through striker Pablo Anton, but Reyes restored the lead just before halftime and added his second goal in the 68th minute to seal the win. Atletico Vallecas will next travel to Zaragoza on October 21 to face CD Aragon, a fixture that could push them to the top of the table if results elsewhere go their way.

DETROIT, Mich. — Eaton Rapids Motors, a mid-sized auto-parts supplier headquartered in Detroit, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in outstanding debt and a sharp decline in orders from General Motors. The filing, submitted in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan, comes two months after the company laid off 1,200 workers at its Flint assembly plant.

CEO Marcus Halloran told reporters at a press briefing that the company plans to continue operating during restructuring. "We intend to keep serving our customers while we reorganize our balance sheet," Halloran said. Eaton Rapids Motors, founded in 1978 by engineer Dorothy Voss, supplies brake components to General Motors and Ford Motor Company.

Industry analyst Priya Nair of Beacon Capital Advisors said the bankruptcy reflects broader turmoil in the auto-parts sector, noting that rival supplier Bristol Axle Corp. acquired two smaller competitors last year to consolidate market share. Nair estimated that Eaton Rapids Motors could shed another 800 jobs by March 2025 if restructuring talks with creditors fail.

Michigan Governor Elena Cross said the state was "closely monitoring" the situation and pledged $15 million in emergency workforce retraining funds for affected employees in Flint. The United Auto Workers union, led by regional director Sam Okafor, announced it would hold a rally outside the company's Detroit headquarters on Friday to demand severance guarantees.

input: BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024 — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tefarnib, an experimental oral chemical compound targeting JAK2-mutant myelofibrosis. The trial, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez and sponsored by Cambridge-based biotechnology company Ridgeline Therapeutics, enrolled 214 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between June 2022 and September 2023. Patients receiving tefarnib 300 mg twice daily showed a 42 percent reduction in spleen volume at 24 weeks, compared with 9 percent among those on placebo. Dr. Vasquez presented the findings on March 12, 2024, at the American Society of Hematology's spring meeting in Chicago. "These results suggest tefarnib could become a meaningful option for patients who have failed ruxolitinib therapy," she said. Ridgeline Therapeutics' chief executive, Marcus Whitfield, stated that the company plans to file for FDA approval by early 2025, pending completion of a confirmatory Phase 3 study expected to begin in Baltimore this fall. The trial recorded 11 serious adverse events, including two cases of pneumonia and one instance of gastrointestinal bleeding, though investigators concluded these were not directly attributable to the study drug. Ridgeline Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by Whitfield and Dr. Priya Nandakumar, has raised $340 million in venture funding to date, according to a company spokesperson. The full study will be published in The New England Journal of Medicine in April 2024. Analysts at Sanborn Capital noted that a successful launch could position tefarnib as a direct competitor to Novartis's fedratinib in the myelofibrosis treatment market.

The acquisition, expected to close by May 30, 2024, will expand Midwest Grain's footprint into 38 additional retail locations across Iowa, Nebraska, and Illinois.

Under the terms of the deal, Prairie Fresh Bakery shareholders will receive $18.50 per share, a 22 percent premium over Tuesday's closing price. Midwest Grain CEO Renata Alvarez said the acquisition strengthens the company's position against competitor Heartland Milling Corp., which has aggressively expanded its own bakery division over the past two years.

"This transaction gives us immediate scale in a market segment we've wanted to enter for years," Alvarez said during a press call from the company's headquarters in Chicago.

Prairie Fresh Bakery founder Thomas Nguyen, who started the company in 1998 with a single storefront, will stay on as a consultant for six months following the close of the deal. Nguyen will step down as chief executive officer effective May 30, 2024, and hand day-to-day operations to Midwest Grain's existing management team.

Analysts at Fairview Capital Partners said the deal values Prairie Fresh Bakery at roughly 9 times projected 2024 earnings. Shares of Midwest Grain rose 4.3 percent to $76.20 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading in Prairie Fresh Bakery, which is privately held, was unaffected.

CHICAGO, Nov. 14 -- Archer Grain Holdings agreed on Thursday to acquire Prairie Mill Cooperative for $412 million in cash, a deal that will expand its footprint in the Midwest wheat-processing market. The transaction, announced jointly by both companies at a press briefing in Chicago, Illinois, is expected to close by February 2025, pending regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission.

Under the agreement, Archer Grain will pay $58 per share, a 22 percent premium over Prairie Mill's closing price on Wednesday. Archer Grain's chief executive officer, Dana Whitfield, said the acquisition would add three processing plants in Nebraska and Kansas to the company's existing network of eleven facilities. "This deal strengthens our supply chain and positions us to meet rising demand," Whitfield told reporters.

Prairie Mill Cooperative, founded in 1968 and headquartered in Wichita, Kansas, employs roughly 640 workers and reported revenue of $890 million last year. Its chief executive, Harold Benner, will step down once the deal closes and will be succeeded by current chief operating officer Lena Marsh, according to a statement filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Shares of Prairie Mill rose 18 percent to $56.40 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Archer Grain's stock slipped 3 percent to $91.20. Analysts at Cedar Point Capital called the price fair but noted the deal could draw scrutiny given Archer Grain's existing 31 percent share of the regional milling market. A decision from regulators is expected by January 2025.

DETROIT, Mich. — Riverstone Motors Inc. announced Tuesday it has acquired battery-technology startup VoltCore Systems for $340 million, a deal aimed at accelerating production of its upcoming electric truck, the Riverstone Ranger. The acquisition was confirmed by Riverstone CEO Anita Ferreira during a press briefing at the company's headquarters in Detroit, Michigan.

Ferreira said VoltCore's 210 employees, based in Austin, Texas, will join Riverstone's engineering division and continue work at a new facility expected to open in early 2026. VoltCore was founded in 2019 by engineer Daniel Kwon, who left his position as chief technology officer at Solara Energy to launch the startup. Kwon will now serve as Riverstone's Senior Vice President of Battery Engineering, effective November 3, 2025.

Industry analysts see the deal as a direct response to competitor Halcyon Auto, which unveiled its own solid-state battery platform last month in Berlin, Germany. Shares of Riverstone Motors rose 6.4 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.12.

Ferreira told reporters, "This acquisition puts us roughly two years ahead of schedule on our electrification roadmap." She added that the combined company plans to invest an additional $1.2 billion in battery manufacturing over the next three years.

The transaction, structured as a cash-and-stock deal, is expected to close by December 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission.

CHICAGO, March 4, 2024 -- Northwestern University's Feinberg School of Medicine announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolrizumab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Chicago-based biotech firm Arborview Therapeutics for the treatment of moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The 26-week study, led by Dr. Patricia Nwosu and published in The Lancet Rheumatology, enrolled 412 adult patients across 14 sites in the United States and Canada, including Toronto General Hospital. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of tolrizumab every four weeks showed a 62 percent reduction in disease activity scores, compared with 28 percent among patients given placebo. Approximately 9 percent of treated patients experienced mild injection-site reactions, while 3 percent discontinued the drug due to elevated liver enzymes. Dr. Nwosu presented the findings on March 2, 2024, at the American College of Rheumatology's regional meeting in Boston. Arborview Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by biochemist Daniel Kessler, said it plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. The company's chief executive, Maria Lindqvist, stated that a Phase 3 trial involving 1,800 patients is scheduled to begin in September 2024 at sites operated by partner organization CoreClin Research. Analysts at Baird Equity Research estimate that, if approved, tolrizumab could generate $1.2 billion in annual revenue by 2028, positioning it as a direct competitor to AbbVie's Rinvoq. Northwestern Memorial Hospital confirmed it will serve as a coordinating center for the upcoming Phase 3 study. Arborview's stock rose 14 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement.

BOSTON, MA -- August 14, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tafenolib, an oral inhibitor of Bruton's tyrosine kinase, in 214 adult patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis. The study, led by Dr. Priya Ramanathan and funded by a $12 million grant from the National Multiple Sclerosis Society, was conducted across nine sites in the United States and Canada between March 2021 and June 2023. Participants received either 40 milligrams of tafenolib daily or placebo for 48 weeks. At the primary endpoint, 61 percent of patients on tafenolib showed no evidence of disease activity, compared with 29 percent in the placebo group, a difference the authors called statistically significant (p<0.001). Magnetic resonance imaging performed at Massachusetts General Hospital revealed a 73 percent reduction in new brain lesions among treated patients. The most common adverse event was mild elevation of liver enzymes, reported in 18 patients, none of whom discontinued treatment. Dr. Ramanathan presented the findings on October 3, 2023, at the European Committee for Treatment and Research in Multiple Sclerosis congress in Milan, Italy. Novara Therapeutics, the biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts that developed tafenolib, plans to begin a Phase 3 trial in early 2024 pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Dr. Ramanathan received the Barancik Prize for Innovation in MS Research from the National Multiple Sclerosis Society for this work, awarded at a ceremony in New York City on November 9, 2023. Novara Therapeutics was founded in 2017 by Dr. Elena Kowalski, a former researcher at Biogen, who now serves as the company's chief executive officer.

Marguerite Okonjo (born 14 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-British structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques for high-rise buildings. She earned a Bachelor of Engineering from the University of Lagos in 1980 and later completed a doctorate at Imperial College London in 1985. In 1990 she joined Arup Group as a junior structural engineer in London and rose over two decades to become Global Head of Structural Engineering in 2004. Okonjo led the retrofit design for the Cascadia Tower in Seattle after the 2001 Nisqually earthquake exposed weaknesses in its foundation. In 2011 she left Arup Group to found Okonjo Structural Partners, a consultancy headquartered in Manchester, England, with an initial staff of 12 engineers. The firm was acquired by Mott MacDonald in March 2019 for approximately 45 million pounds, after which Okonjo stayed on as a senior advisor for two years. She was elected a Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering in 2015 and, on 9 October 2022, received the International Structural Award from the International Association for Bridge and Structural Engineering during a ceremony in Zurich. Okonjo is married to fellow engineer Thomas Reyes, whom she met while working on the Cascadia Tower project; the couple has one daughter, Amara Reyes, born in 1995 in Manchester. Okonjo currently serves on the advisory board of the University of Lagos and continues to consult on seismic safety standards for the International Organization for Standardization.

No cases of tuberculosis reactivation or serious opportunistic infection were observed. Dr. Sundaram presented the findings on March 2, 2024, at the American College of Rheumatology's annual meeting in Chicago, Illinois. Verantis Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by immunologist Dr. Marcus Feld, stated it plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the fourth quarter of 2024. The company raised $85 million in Series C funding last year, led by venture firm Larkspur Capital, to support late-stage development. If approved, tolerimab would compete directly with AbbVie's adalimumab and Amgen's etanercept in the crowded autoimmune therapeutics market. Analysts at Jefferies estimate peak annual sales could reach $1.2 billion by 2029, pending successful Phase III trials expected to begin enrollment in early 2025 at sites including Toronto General Hospital.

Pixelverse Labs, a startup headquartered in Austin, Texas, launched the Aurora Q3 headset on September 12, 2024, promising a lighter alternative to Meta's Quest 3. I tested the device for two weeks at the company's downtown office and came away impressed, if not entirely converted. The Aurora Q3 weighs just 320 grams, roughly 40 percent lighter than its closest rival, thanks to a magnesium-alloy frame designed by lead engineer Priya Nandakumar. Priya, who previously spent six years at Valve Corporation in Bellevue, Washington, told me the team rebuilt the optical stack from scratch to cut weight without sacrificing a 110-degree field of view. Pricing starts at $499 for the base model with 128GB of storage, undercutting the Quest 3 by $150. Battery life is the weak spot: the headset lasted just 1.8 hours in our mixed-use test, well short of Pixelverse's advertised 2.5 hours. Software support is also thin at launch, with only 34 titles available through the Aurora Store compared to over 500 on Meta's platform. Pixelverse Labs was founded in 2021 by Marcus Ohle, a former Oculus engineer, and raised $60 million in Series B funding led by Andreessen Horowitz in March 2023. On October 3, 2024, the company announced a partnership with Qualcomm to co-develop a custom chipset for the next-generation Aurora Q4, expected in 2026. Despite the rough edges, the Aurora Q3 signals that Pixelverse is a legitimate challenger in the mixed-reality space, and I'll be watching closely to see whether battery life and content catch up to its ambitious hardware design.

HARTFORD, Conn. — Meridian Steelworks Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in debt and collapsing demand for industrial fasteners. The filing was made in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Connecticut.

CEO Daniel Ostrander told reporters at a press briefing in Hartford that the company will continue operating its plant in Waterbury while it restructures under new ownership. "We owe it to our 1,200 employees to fight for this company," Ostrander said.

Meridian Steelworks was founded in 1962 by Walter Ostrander, Daniel's grandfather, and grew into one of the largest fastener manufacturers in New England. The company supplies bolts and rivets to Pratt & Whitney and several other aerospace firms.

Analysts say the bankruptcy follows a failed acquisition attempt last year, when rival firm Corbin Fasteners offered $210 million to buy Meridian's Waterbury facility, a deal that collapsed in March after regulators raised antitrust concerns.

The Connecticut Department of Labor said roughly 400 jobs could be at risk if a buyer is not found by January 15, 2025. Governor Lena Marsh issued a statement Tuesday evening pledging $15 million in state transition funds to support affected workers.

Meridian's stock, delisted from the Nasdaq in 2023, last traded at 42 cents per share. Creditors, including Fifth Harbor Bank, are expected to meet with company lawyers in Hartford next week to discuss repayment terms.

On March 14, 2024, Judge Wendell Ashford presided over the sentencing hearing of Marcus Delaine Whitfield, 41, former controller at Bayshore Logistics Inc., a freight company headquartered in Oakland, California. Whitfield was convicted on February 2, 2024 of wire fraud after prosecutors from the Alameda County District Attorney's Office, led by Deputy District Attorney Renata Cho, proved he diverted $612,400 from company accounts between June 2021 and August 2023 to fund personal real estate purchases in Reno, Nevada.

Judge Ashford sentenced Whitfield to 54 months in federal custody at Dublin Federal Correctional Institution, followed by three years of supervised release, and ordered restitution of $612,400 payable to Bayshore Logistics Inc. Defense attorney Priya Nair argued for leniency, citing her client's cooperation and lack of prior record, but the court noted the prolonged duration of the scheme as an aggravating factor.

Bayshore Logistics Inc., a subsidiary of Meridian Transport Holdings, employed Whitfield from January 2016 until his termination in September 2023, when internal auditor Sandra Kowalski first flagged irregular wire transfers to an account at Desert Ridge Savings Bank. The case was investigated jointly by the FBI's San Francisco Field Office and the California Department of Justice. Whitfield must surrender to custody no later than April 30, 2024. His attorney indicated an appeal is under consideration.

Ilse Van Damme (born 14 March 1958 in Ghent, Belgium) is a Belgian materials scientist known for pioneering work in graphene-based battery electrodes. She earned a doctorate in chemistry from Ghent University in 1984 and joined Philips Research in Eindhoven the same year as a research chemist. In 1991 Van Damme left Philips Research to become head of the Materials Division at Solvay, a chemicals company headquartered in Brussels, Belgium.

During her fifteen years at Solvay, she led a team that developed a lithium-sulfur cathode later licensed to the automaker Renault for use in electric vehicle batteries. In 2006 Van Damme founded her own company, Carbonova NV, in Antwerp, Belgium, to commercialize the technology. Carbonova was acquired by the German chemical giant BASF in October 2014 for approximately 340 million euros, after which Van Damme served briefly as a scientific advisor to BASF before retiring in 2016.

Van Damme's contributions were recognized in 2011 when she received the Solvay Prize for Innovation from the Solvay Institutes in Brussels. She has authored more than 90 peer-reviewed papers and holds 22 patents. She married fellow chemist Marc Dujardin in 1985; their son, Tom Dujardin, is now a professor of physics at KU Leuven. Van Damme currently lives in Ghent, where she continues to consult for renewable-energy startups and lectures occasionally at Ghent University.

CINCINNATI, OH — September 9, 2024 — Meridian Foods Corporation announced today that it has acquired Bellwether Snacks LLC, a Portland, Oregon-based maker of organic tortilla chips, for $142 million in cash. The transaction, finalized on September 6, 2024, marks Meridian's third acquisition since 2021 and is expected to close fully by October 15, 2024.

Under the terms of the deal, Bellwether Snacks will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Foods, retaining its Portland production facility and its 210 employees. Bellwether founder and Chief Executive Officer Dana Ferris will remain with the company, assuming the newly created role of Vice President of Innovation, reporting directly to Meridian CEO Robert Halloway.

"Bellwether has built a loyal following with its Pacific Northwest-inspired flavors, and we intend to scale that success nationally," said Halloway, speaking at a press briefing held at Meridian's headquarters in Cincinnati, Ohio.

Ferris, who founded Bellwether Snacks in 2015, said the merger would allow the brand to reach grocery chains across 38 states by mid-2025, up from its current 14-state footprint. Meridian Foods, which is headquartered in Cincinnati and trades on the NASDAQ under the ticker MFCO, reported $1.3 billion in revenue last fiscal year.

Analysts at Whitcombe Capital noted the deal positions Meridian to compete more directly with Golden Valley Snack Co., the current market leader in the premium organic snack segment. Regulatory filings related to the acquisition were submitted to the Federal Trade Commission on September 3, 2024.

The Ontario Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks announced on May 14, 2024 that it will invest $42 million to upgrade wastewater treatment facilities in Thunder Bay and Sudbury over the next three years. Minister Andrea Whitfield said the funding, drawn from the province's Clean Water Infrastructure Fund, will reduce untreated sewage discharges into Lake Superior by an estimated 65 percent by 2027. The announcement was made at the Thunder Bay Waterfront Recreation Facility, where Whitfield was joined by Mayor Ken Boshcoff and representatives from the engineering firm Hatch Ltd., which will oversee construction. Boshcoff called the investment "a turning point for our shoreline communities." Under the plan, the city of Sudbury will receive $18 million to replace aging pipes installed in 1968, while Thunder Bay will receive $24 million for a new treatment plant expected to open in September 2026. The ministry noted that similar upgrades completed in Sault Ste. Marie in 2021 cut phosphorus runoff by 40 percent within two years. Opposition critics, including MPP Sara Delacroix of the New Democratic Party, welcomed the funding but argued that an additional $120 million is still needed province-wide to meet federal water quality standards set by Environment and Climate Change Canada. The ministry expects construction crews to begin site preparation in Thunder Bay by July 2024, with Hatch Ltd. submitting final engineering plans to the province by October 1, 2024.

Pixelworks Labs, a design studio based in Portland, Oregon, unveiled the Aurora Slate 5 tablet on June 11, 2024, positioning it as a mid-range competitor to Samsung's Galaxy Tab line. The device, priced at $449, features a 10.9-inch OLED display, a MediaTek Dimensity 9200 processor, and 8GB of RAM. I tested the Aurora Slate 5 for three weeks in Seattle, running errands, editing photos, and streaming through the Aurora OS 2.1 software layered atop Android 14.

Battery life impressed me most: the tablet lasted roughly 11 hours of continuous video playback, beating the 9 hours advertised by Lenovo for its Tab P12 series. Camera performance, however, remains mediocre, with the 8-megapixel rear sensor struggling in low light.

Chen, who serves as Chief Executive Officer, told reporters at a press briefing in San Jose on June 12 that the firm plans to expand into the European market by early 2025. Notably, Foxconn Technology Group manufactures the Aurora Slate 5 under a supply agreement signed last October.

On the software side, Aurora OS 2.1 supports a stylus called the Aurora Pen, sold separately for $59. Overall, despite its camera shortcomings, the Aurora Slate 5 delivers strong value at its price point, making it one of the more compelling budget tablets of 2024.

Waterford Grain Corp. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, October 15, in federal court in Wichita, Kansas, after a sharp decline in commodity prices left the company unable to service $340 million in debt. Chief Executive Officer Marcus Delaney told reporters the filing would allow the 78-year-old grain processor to restructure while continuing operations at its three facilities in Kansas and Nebraska. "We intend to keep paying our 620 employees and honoring contracts with local farmers," Delaney said during a press conference at the company's headquarters in Wichita. Court documents show Waterford Grain owes $92 million to lender Prairie National Bank and an additional $54 million to supplier Heartland Seed Co. Analysts at Cormier Ridge Partners, an investment firm based in Chicago, Illinois, said the bankruptcy reflects broader stress in the agricultural sector following two consecutive years of drought across the Midwest. Waterford Grain was founded in 1946 by Elias Waterford and had been family-owned until it was acquired by private equity firm Hollis Bridge Capital in 2011 for $410 million. Delaney, who joined the company in 2018, said Waterford Grain expects to emerge from bankruptcy by March 2025. MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT PRESS STATEMENT
Nairobi, Kenya — 4 March 2024

The Ministry of Transport announced today that the Nairobi Expressway Authority will receive a grant of 850 million Kenyan shillings from the African Development Bank to fund repairs on the Thika Superhighway following flood damage recorded in early February. Transport Secretary Kipchoge Mwangi confirmed the allocation during a press briefing at Uhuru Highway offices, stating that construction firm China Road and Bridge Corporation has been contracted to complete the repairs by 30 June 2024.

"This funding demonstrates our commitment to restoring critical infrastructure for the 4.4 million residents of Nairobi County," said Mwangi, who assumed the position of Transport Secretary on 12 January 2023 after being appointed by President William Ruto.

The Kenya National Highways Authority, headquartered in Nairobi, will oversee daily inspections. Engineer Faith Wanjiru, who leads the Authority's Infrastructure Division, noted that similar flooding damaged the same stretch of highway in 2021, prompting calls for a permanent drainage upgrade.

The African Development Bank previously provided a loan of 1.2 billion Kenyan shillings in 2019 for the initial construction of the Nairobi Expressway, which was completed and opened to the public in May 2022. Officials expect repair work to begin on 15 March 2024, with lane closures affecting commuters travelling between Mlolongo and Westlands.

The Ministry urged the public to report additional damage through its toll-free hotline before the rainy season intensifies in April.

Pixel Buds Pro 2, Google's latest wireless earbuds, went on sale in San Francisco on October 4, 2024, priced at $199. After two weeks of daily use, I'm impressed but not floored. Google, headquartered in Mountain View, California, packed the tiny A1 chip into each earbud, and the active noise cancellation is noticeably stronger than the original Pixel Buds Pro from 2022. Battery life reaches 8 hours with ANC on, according to Google's product lead, Sarah Kim, who demonstrated the earbuds at a press event attended by roughly 40 journalists.

Comfort is where these buds shine. Google redesigned the silicone tips after customer complaints about the first generation, and the new oval shape stayed secure through a 5-mile run along the Embarcadero. Bluetooth 5.3 connectivity paired instantly with both a Pixel 9 phone and a MacBook Pro, though switching between them still lags by about 2 seconds.

The $199 price tag puts the Pixel Buds Pro 2 in direct competition with Apple's AirPods Pro, which retail for $249, and Samsung's Galaxy Buds3 Pro, priced at $219. Sony, another rival in the space, has yet to announce a 2024 flagship earbud.

Minor gripes: the charging case only supports Qi wireless charging at 5W, slower than competitors, and the companion app on Android occasionally fails to show battery percentage. Still, for anyone inside Google's ecosystem, the Pixel Buds Pro 2 are an easy recommendation at this price point.

Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1958 in Turin, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques for historic masonry buildings. She earned a degree in civil engineering from the Politecnico di Torino in 1981 and later completed a doctorate at ETH Zurich in 1986. In 1990 Marchetti founded Studio Marchetti Ingegneria, a structural engineering firm headquartered in Turin, Italy, which grew to employ over 120 engineers across three offices. Her firm served as a key supplier of retrofit designs to the Italian Ministry of Cultural Heritage during the reconstruction of L'Aquila following the 2009 earthquake. In 2011 Marchetti was appointed Chief Structural Engineer of the Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore restoration project in Florence, a position she held until 2018. For this work she received the Gustave Eiffel Medal from the International Association for Bridge and Structural Engineering in Zurich in September 2015. Marchetti married fellow engineer Paolo Ricci in 1992; their daughter, Sofia Ricci, later joined Studio Marchetti Ingegneria as a project manager in 2016. In 2020, Studio Marchetti Ingegneria was acquired by the multinational firm Arup for an undisclosed sum, becoming a subsidiary of Arup Italia. Marchetti stepped down as chief executive in December 2021 but remains a senior advisor. She continues to lecture part-time at the Politecnico di Torino and lives in Turin with her husband.

MANCHESTER, England — Aston Villa striker Marcus Idris scored twice on Saturday to lead his side to a 3-1 victory over Everton at Villa Park, moving Villa into fifth place in the Premier League table. Idris opened the scoring in the 14th minute with a low left-footed strike, then added a second just before halftime after a defensive error by Everton captain Declan Rourke. Everton pulled one back through substitute Tomas Vidic in the 68th minute, but a late header from defender Sam Okafor sealed the win in the 84th minute. The match drew a crowd of 41,200, and Villa manager Petra Lindqvist praised her squad's discipline afterward. "We stayed patient and trusted the plan," Lindqvist told reporters at the post-match press conference. Everton manager Rafael Costa admitted his team lacked concentration in the final third. The result lifts Aston Villa to 38 points from 22 matches, while Everton remains in 15th place with 21 points. Villa will next travel to London on November 9 to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, while Everton hosts Newcastle United on November 10 at Goodison Park. Aston Villa's chairman, Robert Sung, confirmed the club has begun contract talks with Idris, whose current deal expires in June 2026. Sung called the striker "a generational talent worth protecting." The Premier League confirmed the match statistics on Sunday, noting Idris has now scored 11 goals this season, the most of any Villa player.

MANCHESTER, England — October 14, 2023. Manchester City midfielder Kevin De Bruyne scored twice as City defeated Everton 4-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, extending their unbeaten Premier League run to nine matches. Manager Pep Guardiola praised his squad's discipline after the match, calling it "one of our most complete performances this season." Erling Haaland opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a header from a Bernardo Silva cross, before De Bruyne struck twice in a five-minute span midway through the first half. Everton manager Sean Dyche admitted his side "struggled to cope with City's tempo," after Dominic Calvert-Lewin pulled one back in the 63rd minute. The win moves City to 21 points, three clear of second-placed Arsenal, who face Chelsea on Sunday at Stamford Bridge. Attendance at the Etihad Stadium was announced at 53,112. City's next fixture is away to RB Leipzig in the UEFA Champions League on October 17, a match that will be crucial after their 2-1 defeat in the reverse fixture last month. Guardiola confirmed that defender Ruben Dias, who missed Saturday's game with a hamstring injury, is expected to be fit for the Leipzig trip. City's chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak was present at the Etihad, along with club sponsor Etihad Airways representatives, celebrating the club's 10th consecutive home victory this season.

DETROIT, Mich. — Ferravale Motors Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Bronson Battery Systems, a Toledo-based maker of lithium-ion cells, for approximately $740 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by December 15, 2024, marks Ferravale's largest acquisition since its founding in 1987 by industrialist Walter Hain.

Under the agreement, Ferravale will pay Bronson shareholders $58 per share, a 22 percent premium over Monday's closing price. Bronson Battery Systems, founded in 2011 by engineer Priya Nandakumar, employs roughly 1,200 workers at its Ohio plant and supplies battery packs to several electric-vehicle manufacturers, including Solvane Motors, a Ferravale competitor.

CEO Marcus Delgado said the acquisition would let Ferravale bring battery production in-house ahead of its planned Aurora EV sedan launch in 2025. "This is about controlling our supply chain at a moment when demand for electric vehicles is accelerating," Delgado told reporters at a press briefing in Detroit.

Ferravale shares rose 4.3 percent to $91.20 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of rival automaker Solvane Motors dipped 1.8 percent amid concern over its battery supply.

Analyst Grace Whitfield of Meridian Capital Partners called the deal "a smart hedge against raw-material volatility," noting that Bronson's patented cathode chemistry could cut battery costs by 15 percent. Nandakumar will join Ferravale's board as Chief Technology Officer once the transaction closes, according to a company statement released Wednesday.

Voltique employs 240 people and will retain its Austin office as a standalone research unit under the Ferra Energy division. Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google's Wearable Finally Feels Complete

MOUNTAIN VIEW, October 14, 2024 - Google's Pixel Watch 3, released on September 20, 2024, is the most convincing case yet that the company can compete with Apple in the wearables market. I've worn the 45mm LTE model, priced at $429.99, for three weeks alongside my Pixel 9 Pro, and the improvements over the Pixel Watch 2 are immediately noticeable.

The standout upgrade is the display, now 20 percent brighter at peak output, which makes outdoor readability far less of a struggle. Battery life has also improved meaningfully; Google claims 24 hours with the always-on display enabled, and in my testing around Shoreline Park in Mountain View, California, that held up even during a 90-minute run tracked via GPS.

Software remains the differentiator. Wear OS 5, developed jointly by Google and Samsung Electronics, powers the device, and the new Loss of Pulse Detection feature, built with guidance from Mass General Brigham, adds a genuine safety case that competitors like the Apple Watch Series 10 and the Samsung Galaxy Watch 7 don't fully match.

Not everything is perfect. The watch still can't match the seven-day battery life of the Amazfit Balance, and Google's fitness coaching, powered by its Fitbit subsidiary, occasionally repeats advice I'd already logged. Still, at $429.99, this is the first Pixel Watch I'd recommend without hesitation.

Rating: 4 out of 5 stars.

AUSTIN, TEXAS -- November 14, 2023 -- Helios Grid Systems, Inc. announced today that it has acquired Bluewave Energy Storage, a battery-technology startup based in Denver, Colorado, for $340 million in cash and stock. The acquisition, expected to close by December 20, 2023, will fold Bluewave's 210-employee workforce into Helios Grid's growing storage division.

Helios Grid, headquartered in Austin, Texas, was founded in 2016 by Priya Nair, who currently serves as Chief Executive Officer. "Bluewave's lithium-iron-phosphate battery platform accelerates our roadmap by at least two years," Nair said during a press briefing held at the company's Austin headquarters on Tuesday.

Under the terms of the deal, Bluewave founder and CEO Marcus Feld will join Helios Grid as Executive Vice President of Storage Technology, reporting directly to Nair. Feld co-founded Bluewave in 2018 alongside his sister, Dana Feld, who will remain in Denver as Vice President of Manufacturing.

Helios Grid's board of directors approved the transaction on November 10, 2023, and financing was arranged through a $150 million credit facility provided by Meridian Capital Partners. input: Ingrid Halvorsen (born 12 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cold-water coral ecosystems. She earned a doctorate in oceanography from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø the same year as a research scientist. In 1994 Halvorsen became Head of the Deep-Sea Ecology Division at the institute, a position she held for over a decade. Her fieldwork aboard the research vessel Johan Hjort documented extensive Lophelia pertusa reef systems off the coast of Trondheim, findings she published in the 1998 monograph The Hidden Gardens of the North Sea. In 2003 she left the institute to become Professor of Marine Biology at the University of Tromsø, a post she held until her retirement in 2021. Halvorsen married fellow oceanographer Erik Solheim in 1986; the couple had two children, Kristin and Mats. In 2010 she received the Nansen Award from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to marine conservation. She also served as a scientific advisor to the World Wildlife Fund from 2012 to 2019, warning repeatedly about the effects of bottom trawling on deep-sea habitats. Halvorsen currently lives in Tromsø, where she continues to write popular science books about the Arctic Ocean.

input: MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City clinched a dramatic 2-1 victory over Liverpool FC at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, with midfielder Kevin De Bruyne scoring the winning goal in the 89th minute. The result lifted City to the top of the Premier League table with 22 points after nine matches. Erling Haaland opened the scoring for City in the 34th minute, converting a penalty after being fouled inside the box, but Liverpool responded through Mohamed Salah just before halftime to level the score at 1-1. Manager Pep Guardiola praised his squad's resilience after the match, telling reporters, "We showed character today, and Kevin's goal was pure class." Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp expressed disappointment, noting that his side had conceded a needless penalty. The match, watched by 53,000 fans, was City's fourth consecutive win in all competitions. Referee Michael Oliver booked three players during the contest, including Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk for a late challenge in the 76th minute. City's chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak was present at the stadium and later congratulated the team on social media. The victory also extended City's unbeaten home record to 18 matches. Next weekend, Manchester City will travel to London to face Arsenal at Emirates Stadium on October 21, in what promises to be a pivotal clash for the Premier League title race.

Marguerite Okafor (born 14 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-British structural engineer known for pioneering seismic retrofitting techniques in West African construction. She earned a degree in Civil Engineering from the University of Lagos in 1980 before relocating to London, where she joined Ove Arup & Partners in 1984 as a Junior Engineer. By 1993, Okafor had risen to Principal Engineer, and in 1998 she left Ove Arup & Partners to found Okafor Structural Consultants, headquartered in Manchester, United Kingdom.

Her firm gained international attention after leading the reconstruction of the Bamenda Central Market Complex in Cameroon following a fire in 2003. In 2011, Okafor Structural Consultants was acquired by the multinational firm Arcadis for an undisclosed sum, though industry sources estimated the deal at roughly 12 million pounds. Okafor remained with Arcadis as Director of African Operations until her retirement in 2019.

In 2015, she received the Royal Academy of Engineering's Africa Prize for Engineering Innovation, awarded in Nairobi, Kenya, for her work on low-cost earthquake-resistant housing. Okafor is married to Nigerian architect Chidi Nwosu, whom she met in 1986 while working on a joint housing project in Lagos; the couple has two children. She currently lives in Manchester and serves on the board of trustees for the Institution of Structural Engineers.

HARTFORD, Conn. — Meridian Freight Corp., a regional trucking company headquartered in Hartford, Connecticut, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $47 million in unpaid debts and a sharp decline in shipping demand. The filing, submitted in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Connecticut, comes just eight months after CEO Rebecca Norton took over the company from founder Walter Ganz, who stepped down as chief executive in March.

"We are doing everything possible to protect jobs and keep trucks on the road," Norton said.

The bankruptcy filing follows a turbulent year for the freight industry, with diesel prices rising 18 percent since January and consumer shipping volumes down nearly 9 percent, according to the American Trucking Association. Analysts at Fitch Ratings warned that at least three more mid-sized carriers could face insolvency by the end of 2024 if fuel costs remain elevated.
