Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google's Best Wearable Yet

Mountain View, CA — October 12, 2024. Google officially launched the Pixel Watch 3 last week, and after seven days of testing on my wrist here in San Francisco, I can say it's the most polished smartwatch the company has produced. Priced at $349.99 for the 41mm model, the watch is aimed squarely at Apple Watch Series 10 and Samsung's Galaxy Watch 7.

The standout feature is the new 'Loss of Pulse Detection' system, developed with input from Dr. Priya Nair, a cardiologist at Stanford Health Care. Google says the sensor suite, powered by a Qualcomm Snapdragon W5 chip, can detect cardiac events with 92 percent accuracy in early trials. Battery life clocks in at roughly 36 hours, a modest improvement over last year's Pixel Watch 2.

Rick Osterloh, Google's senior vice president of devices, demonstrated the watch on stage at the company's event in Mountain View, calling it "the most personal device we've ever built." Notably, this launch comes three months after Google completed its acquisition of Fitbit's remaining health-data assets from parent company Alphabet Inc., a move that reportedly cost $340 million.

Minor gripes remain: the always-on display still drains battery faster than rivals from Garmin, and the charging cable is proprietary yet again. Still, for Android users, this is easily the best option on the market. I'm giving it 4.5 out of 5 stars.

BOSTON, MA -- September 12, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tepravamab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cascadia Biotherapeutics, for the treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. The randomized, double-blind study enrolled 214 adult patients across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2022 and January 2023. Dr. Elena Marchetti, the study's lead investigator and Associate Professor of Dermatology at Harvard Medical School, presented the findings at the American Academy of Dermatology conference held in Chicago. Patients receiving 300 milligrams of tepravamab every four weeks achieved a 78 percent reduction in Psoriasis Area and Severity Index scores by week 16, compared with 22 percent in the placebo group. Approximately 9 percent of participants reported mild injection-site reactions, and no serious adverse events were attributed to the drug. Cascadia Biotherapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial in early 2024 pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The company's chief executive officer, Raj Patel, stated that the results support tepravamab's potential as a best-in-class treatment option. Novartis, a competitor developing a similar IL-23 inhibitor, has not yet released comparable data. Funding for the trial was provided in part by a $12 million grant from the National Institutes of Health. Full results will be published in The New England Journal of Medicine later this year.

input: BOSTON, MA - September 12, 2023 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tovarafenib, an experimental oral kinase inhibitor developed by Cascadia Therapeutics, in patients with relapsed pediatric low-grade glioma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh and published in The New England Journal of Medicine, enrolled 84 children between the ages of 3 and 17 across twelve sites in the United States and Canada. Participants received tovarafenib twice daily for 24 weeks. According to the report, 56 of 84 patients, or 66.7 percent, achieved partial or complete tumor response, compared with 28 percent in the historical control group treated with standard carboplatin and vincristine chemotherapy. The most common adverse event was mild rash, reported in 31 patients, while three patients experienced Grade 3 elevated liver enzymes requiring dose interruption. Dr. Marsh stated that the findings support tovarafenib as a potential first-line therapy for BRAF-altered gliomas. Cascadia Therapeutics, headquartered in San Diego, California, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2024. The trial was funded in part by a $12 million grant from the National Cancer Institute. Dr. Marsh will present the full dataset at the Society for Neuro-Oncology annual meeting in Vancouver on November 18, 2023. Co-author Dr. Rajiv Patel of the Hospital for Sick Children in Toronto noted that longer follow-up is needed to assess durability of response and long-term neurocognitive outcomes in this pediatric population.

input: SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF ARIZONA, MARICOPA COUNTY. On October 14, 2023, Judge Renata Solis presided over the sentencing hearing of defendant Marcus Whitfield, 41, who was convicted of wire fraud and money laundering in connection with a scheme that defrauded investors of approximately $2.3 million through his company, Whitfield Capital Partners, headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona. Prosecutor Diane Kowalski of the Maricopa County Attorney's Office told the court that between January 2019 and March 2022, Whitfield solicited funds from at least 37 investors by falsely claiming the money would be invested in commodity futures. Instead, prosecutors said, he diverted roughly $1.1 million to personal accounts and used the remainder to pay earlier investors in a classic Ponzi arrangement. Whitfield was arrested by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation on June 9, 2022, at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport as he attempted to board a flight to Panama City. Judge Solis sentenced Whitfield to 87 months in federal prison, followed by three years of supervised release, and ordered restitution of $2.3 million to victims. Defense attorney Harold Pinsky argued for leniency, citing his client's lack of prior criminal record. Whitfield Capital Partners filed for bankruptcy protection in Phoenix in April 2022, shortly after the Securities and Exchange Commission opened its investigation. The case, United States v. Whitfield, drew attention from local outlets including The Arizona Republic.

Pixel Tablet Dock Review: A Smart Home Hub That Almost Nails It

On March 14, 2024, Google shipped the Pixel Tablet in a bundle with its charging speaker dock, and after six weeks of daily use in my apartment in Austin, Texas, I have mixed feelings. The $499 tablet, priced with the dock included, docks magnetically and instantly switches into Hub Mode, showing a photo frame, calendar, and Nest camera feeds.

Google, headquartered in Mountain View, California, positioned this as a rival to Amazon's Echo Show 15, and in daily use the comparison feels fair. The 11-inch display is bright, and the dock's four-driver speaker system, engineered with input from Google's hardware chief Rick Osterloh, delivers surprisingly full sound for a $129 accessory sold separately.

Battery life off the dock is where things fall apart: I got roughly 6 hours of mixed use, well below the 12 hours Google claims. Sarah Chen, a product reviewer at The Verge, reported similar results in her March 22 review, noting the tablet throttles brightness aggressively when unplugged.

Software is the real story. Android 14 runs smoothly, and Google's app ecosystem, including Google Home and YouTube, feels native rather than bolted on. But at $499, it competes uneasily with Apple's iPad, which starts at $349 and offers a vastly larger app library.

Still, for someone building a Google Home setup, this is the most compelling smart display Google has made since the original Nest Hub launched in 2018. Recommended, with caveats.

Kestrel Outdoor Co. also announced a partnership with the National Park Foundation to donate 2 percent of Talon sales to trail maintenance programs through December 31, 2024. Customers who purchase before April 30, 2024 will receive a free repair kit valued at $18. The product is brand new, not a refurbished model, and comes with a limited 2-year warranty covering manufacturing defects. Units are currently in stock at Kestrel's Bend distribution center and at select REI locations across the Pacific Northwest, including stores in Seattle, Washington and Portland, Oregon.

3/6 Pecan Grove was founded in 2016 by Marcus Webb, who will now step down as CEO but stay on as a technical advisor. Webb previously worked at Texas Instruments for nine years before starting his own company.

4/6 Solstice, headquartered in Austin, Texas, competes with Denver-based AgriDrone Corp in the precision-farming market. Shares of Solstice's parent company, Ferris Holdings, rose 6 percent on the Nasdaq after the announcement.

6/6 Nandakumar is scheduled to meet with Austin Mayor Diane Ferro next Thursday to discuss tax incentives for the expanded campus. More updates as this develops.

MADRID, May 14 — Real Sociedad striker Mikel Oyarzabal scored twice on Sunday as his side defeated Villarreal 3-1 at the Reale Arena, boosting their hopes of clinching a Europa League spot before the La Liga season ends on May 25. Oyarzabal opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a low finish from inside the box, and doubled his tally in the 47th minute after a swift counterattack led by midfielder Martin Zubimendi. Villarreal pulled one back through striker Gerard Moreno in the 63rd minute, but defender Robin Le Normand restored the two-goal cushion in the 78th minute with a header from a corner kick. The win, watched by 32,000 fans, lifted Real Sociedad to fifth place in the table with 58 points, three points behind fourth-placed Real Betis. Head coach Imanol Alguacil praised his squad's discipline after the match, telling reporters at a press conference, "We controlled the tempo for long stretches, and Mikel was clinical again." Villarreal manager Marcelino was less pleased, criticizing his team's defending on set pieces. The result marked Real Sociedad's fourth consecutive home victory since April 9, a run that has revived their European ambitions after a difficult January. Real Sociedad will next travel to Seville on May 21 to face Real Betis in a match that could decide the final Europa League berth.

Marguerite Okonkwo-Delacroix (born 14 March 1958 in Lagos, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-French structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques for high-rise buildings. She earned her engineering degree from the École Polytechnique in 1980 and later completed a doctorate at Stanford University in 1985. In 1991, she founded Delacroix Structural Partners in Lyon, France, a firm that grew to specialize in earthquake-resistant design for hospitals and schools across the Mediterranean region. Okonkwo-Delacroix served as Chief Engineer of the firm until 2004, when she stepped down to become Director of Seismic Research at the International Bureau of Civil Engineering in Geneva, Switzerland. Under her leadership, the Bureau published the widely cited Okonkwo Protocol in 2009, a design standard later adopted into French building law. In 2012, she received the Fritz Leonhardt Medal from the German Society of Structural Engineers in Stuttgart for her contributions to disaster-resistant architecture. She married fellow engineer Julien Delacroix in 1983, and the couple had two children, Amara and Théo, both of whom later joined the family firm. Okonkwo-Delacroix retired from the Bureau in March 2020 but continued consulting on the reconstruction of Port-au-Prince following the 2010 Haiti earthquake. She died on 9 November 2022 in Lyon at the age of 64, following a brief illness. Her memoir, Foundations of Silence, was published posthumously in 2023 by Éditions Rivière.

Bellroy, the Melbourne-based accessories company founded in 2010, has released the Bellroy Venture Sling 6L, a water-resistant crossbody bag priced at $99.00. Made primarily from recycled ripstop nylon sourced from a supplier in Taipei, Taiwan, the Venture Sling 6L features a padded 13-inch laptop sleeve, a magnetic buckle closure, and a hidden zip pocket for passports or phones. It ships in three colorways: Basalt, Ash, and Ranger Green. Bellroy began selling the Venture Sling 6L on March 4, 2024, through its flagship store on Chapel Street in Melbourne and via its website, with international shipping now available to the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Customers who purchase before April 30, 2024 receive a complimentary Bellroy Cable Pouch valued at $25.00. Reviewers at Wirecutter praised the bag's 2.8-liter internal organization pocket and its 480-gram weight, noting it is lighter than competing packs from Peak Design and Patagonia. The Venture Sling 6L is backed by Bellroy's 3-year warranty against manufacturing defects. Company co-founder Andy Fallshaw said the design was refined over 14 months of testing with commuters in Sydney and Tokyo. Stock is currently limited to 5,000 units for this initial release, and the company expects to restock in June 2024. This is a new, unused product available for immediate purchase.

Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1958 in Turin, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofitting techniques used in earthquake-prone regions of southern Europe. She earned her degree in civil engineering from the Politecnico di Torino in 1981 and joined Fiat Engineering the same year as a junior designer. In 1989 Marchetti left Fiat Engineering to co-found Marchetti & Rossi Structural Consultants in Milan alongside civil engineer Paolo Rossi, serving as the firm's Chief Engineer for over two decades. Under her leadership, the firm was hired in 1997 to reinforce the bell tower of the Basilica di San Petronio in Bologna following minor damage from a regional tremor. Marchetti & Rossi Structural Consultants was acquired by the multinational firm Arup in 2011 for an undisclosed sum, after which Marchetti stayed on as a senior advisor until her retirement in 2015. On 22 September 2003, she married architect Davide Ferrero, with whom she has one son, Luca Ferrero, born in 2005. In 2018 the Italian National Academy of Engineering awarded her the Galileo Medal for Structural Innovation in a ceremony held in Rome, citing her decades of work protecting historic Italian architecture from seismic damage. Marchetti currently lives in Milan and continues to consult on preservation projects across Italy.

DETROIT, Mich. — Automaker Halden Motors Inc. announced Tuesday that it has acquired battery startup VoltCell Technologies for $410 million, a move aimed at securing supply for its expanding electric vehicle lineup. The deal, finalized on March 11, 2024, was confirmed by Halden Motors CEO Renata Kowalski during a press briefing at the company's headquarters in Detroit, Michigan.

"This acquisition strengthens our position as we compete directly with Tesla and Rivian in the North American EV market," Kowalski said. VoltCell Technologies, founded in 2018 by engineer Samuel Achebe, is based in Austin, Texas, and employs roughly 220 people.

Achebe, who will join Halden Motors as Chief Battery Officer starting April 1, 2024, said the partnership would accelerate development of solid-state battery cells. "We've spent six years perfecting this chemistry, including advances in lithium-metal composites," Achebe told reporters.

The announcement sent Halden Motors shares up 7 percent on the New York Stock Exchange, closing at $58.30. Analysts at Bristol Capital Partners estimate the combined company could produce 500,000 electric vehicles annually by 2027, up from 310,000 last year.

Halden Motors, headquartered in Detroit since its founding in 1987 by industrialist Walter Halden, currently employs about 34,000 workers worldwide. The company plans to retain VoltCell's Austin facility and add 150 jobs there over the next two years, according to spokesperson DeniseFord.

Shareholders are expected to vote on final approval at a meeting scheduled for April 25, 2024, in Detroit.

To: Board of Directors, Marchetti Foods Inc.
From: Renata Voss, Chief Financial Officer
Date: March 14, 2024
Subject: Acquisition of Bergström Dairy AB Finalized

Dear Board Members,

I am pleased to report that Marchetti Foods Inc. completed its acquisition of Bergström Dairy AB on March 12, 2024, for 46 million euros. The deal was signed in Stockholm, Sweden, following four months of negotiations led by our General Counsel, Priya Anand.

Under the agreement, Marchetti Foods Inc. will absorb Bergström Dairy AB as a wholly owned subsidiary, retaining its Malmö production facility and its 210 employees. Bergström's founder, Lars Bergström, will step down as Chief Executive Officer effective April 1, 2024, but will remain as a non-executive advisor through 2025.

To lead integration efforts, we have appointed Klaus Feldmann as Managing Director of the Nordic division, reporting directly to our CEO, Antonio Marchetti, at our headquarters in Milan, Italy. Mr. Feldmann previously worked for Arla Foods for twelve years.

This acquisition strengthens our position against competitors such as Danone and Nestlé in the Northern European dairy market, and we project it will add approximately 80 million euros in annual revenue by 2026.

A press briefing is scheduled for March 20, 2024, at our Milan headquarters, where Antonio Marchetti will formally announce the transaction to journalists.

Please direct any questions to my office before the next board meeting on March 25, 2024.

Regards,
Renata Voss
Chief Financial Officer
Marchetti Foods Inc.

Boston, MA -- June 12, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tremelimumab-plus-durvalumab combination therapy in patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh, enrolled 214 participants across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and October 2022. Findings, published in The Lancet Oncology, showed a median overall survival of 16.4 months compared to 10.7 months in the control arm receiving sorafenib alone, a difference the authors called clinically meaningful. Grade 3 or higher adverse events, including elevated liver enzymes and fatigue, occurred in 27 percent of the combination group versus 19 percent in the sorafenib group. Dr. Marsh stated that the results support durvalumab as a new standard-of-care option for this patient population. The trial was funded by AstraZeneca with a research grant of $8.3 million and co-sponsored by the National Cancer Institute. Dr. Marsh will present the full dataset at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting in Chicago on June 2, 2024. Separately, AstraZeneca confirmed it has begun a phase 3 confirmatory trial, named EMERALD-3, expected to conclude by December 2026. Dr. Raj Patel, an independent oncologist at Charite Berlin who was not involved in the study, called the survival benefit "substantial" but cautioned that liver toxicity requires close monitoring. Massachusetts General Hospital plans to open enrollment for a follow-up biomarker study in early 2025.

input: The Ministry of Environment and Forests announced on Tuesday that the Ganges River Cleanup Initiative will receive an additional 4.2 billion rupees to accelerate wastewater treatment projects across Uttar Pradesh. Minister Rajesh Malhotra, speaking at a press briefing in New Delhi, said the funds will finance construction of eleven new treatment plants in Kanpur, Varanasi, and Allahabad by March 2026. "This investment reflects our commitment to restoring the Ganges to its natural state," Malhotra told reporters, adding that the National Mission for Clean Ganga will oversee disbursement of the funds beginning next month. The initiative, launched in 2014 under the Namami Gange programme, has previously spent 20 billion rupees with mixed results, according to a report released by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India in September. Priya Sharma, executive director of the environmental group EcoWatch India, welcomed the announcement but urged stricter monitoring. "Without independent audits, this money risks being wasted like the last tranche," Sharma said during a phone interview on Wednesday. The Ministry also confirmed that engineering firm Larsen & Toubro has been awarded a 900 million rupee contract to build a treatment facility in Varanasi, with construction expected to begin in January 2025. Officials from the Uttar Pradesh state government are scheduled to meet with Ministry representatives in Lucknow next week to finalize land acquisition for the remaining sites.

organization: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

MADRID, October 14, 2024 -- Real Sociedad edged past Villarreal 2-1 at the Reale Arena on Sunday, with midfielder Mikel Oyarzabal scoring the winning goal in the 87th minute. The victory lifts Real Sociedad to eighth place in La Liga with 14 points after nine matches.

Villarreal took an early lead when striker Alexander Sorloth converted a penalty in the 23rd minute, sending goalkeeper Alex Remiro the wrong way. Real Sociedad responded ten minutes before halftime through midfielder Martin Zubimendi, who fired a low shot from the edge of the box after a corner kick was only half-cleared.

The decisive moment came late, as substitute Umar Sadiq flicked a header into the path of Oyarzabal, who calmly slotted the ball past goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen. The 12,400 fans inside the stadium erupted, and head coach Imanol Alguacil was seen celebrating on the touchline.

After the match, Alguacil told reporters, "We showed character today. Villarreal are a tough side, and coming back from behind against them means a lot." Villarreal manager Marcelino Garcia Toral said his team's defending in the final ten minutes was unacceptable and promised changes before their next fixture against Girona on October 20, 2024.

Real Sociedad will next travel to the Camp Nou to face Barcelona on October 27, 2024, in what promises to be a difficult test for Alguacil's squad. The club's president, Jokin Aperribay, praised the players' resilience in a brief statement released Sunday evening.

Cedar Grove Foods Inc., the Ohio-based packaged snacks maker, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Bramble Hollow Baking Co. for $142 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at Cedar Grove's headquarters in Columbus, Ohio, gives the company control of Bramble Hollow's cracker and cookie lines, which are sold in more than 3,000 grocery stores across the Midwest. Cedar Grove's chief executive officer, Marisol Fenwick, said the acquisition would boost annual revenue by roughly 18 percent starting in fiscal year 2025. "This is a natural fit for our portfolio," Fenwick told reporters during a briefing on October 14. Bramble Hollow, founded in 1987 by baker Thomas Ridgeway in Dayton, Ohio, employs 410 workers and generated $96 million in sales last year. Ridgeway, who stepped down as chief executive officer of Bramble Hollow in March, will join Cedar Grove's board of directors as part of the agreement. Analysts at Hartline Capital Partners called the price a modest premium over Bramble Hollow's estimated market value, noting that competitor Kestrel Snack Group had also considered a bid earlier this year. Shares of Cedar Grove, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker CGFI, rose 6.4 percent to $58.10 following the announcement. The transaction is expected to close by December 1, pending regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Cedar Grove said it plans to retain all 410 Bramble Hollow employees and keep the Dayton manufacturing plant operational.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Ottawa, Ontario — March 14, 2024

Minister Elena Kowalski today announced that the Government of Canada will invest $420 million to upgrade rail safety systems along the Kingston to Montreal corridor, following a review prompted by the December 2023 derailment near Brockville that injured 6 workers. The funding, to be disbursed through Transport Canada, will support Canadian National Railway in installing new positive train control technology by October 2026.

"This investment reflects our commitment to protecting rail workers and communities along this corridor," said Minister Kowalski at a press conference held at the Ottawa Union Station facility. Deputy Minister Arjun Patel confirmed that the Railway Safety Act will be amended this summer to require quarterly inspections of aging rail infrastructure.

The announcement follows a March 2024 meeting in Toronto between Minister Kowalski and CN Rail chief executive officer Tracy Robinson, during which both parties agreed on a joint safety task force. CN Rail, headquartered in Montreal, Quebec, has committed an additional $75 million toward the initiative.

Opposition critic Marc Fortin, a member of the Conservative Party, called the funding "long overdue" and urged the ministry to publish inspection results publicly by January 2025. The ministry expects the upgraded corridor to reduce derailment incidents by 40 percent over the next five years.

AUSTIN, Texas -- Meridian Robotics Inc. announced on June 4, 2024 that it has acquired Lonestar Sensing Corp., a privately held maker of industrial LiDAR systems based in Round Rock, Texas, for approximately $42 million in cash. The acquisition, expected to close by July 15, 2024, will bring Lonestar Sensing's 65 employees under the Meridian Robotics umbrella and expand the company's presence in the autonomous warehouse equipment market.

Meridian Robotics, headquartered in Austin, Texas, and led by Chief Executive Officer Patricia Nwosu, said the deal strengthens its supply chain for its flagship product, the HaulBot X3 autonomous forklift. "Lonestar Sensing's optical arrays are among the best in the industry, and this acquisition lets us bring that technology in-house," Nwosu said during a press briefing held at the company's Austin headquarters on June 4, 2024.

Lonestar Sensing was founded in 2016 by engineer Marcus Feldman, who will join Meridian Robotics as Vice President of Sensor Engineering effective July 15, 2024. Feldman previously served as Chief Technology Officer at Lonestar Sensing since 2019.

The transaction was financed in part through a $20 million loan from Capital City Bank of Dallas. Meridian Robotics shares rose 6 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement. The company expects the combined entity to generate $180 million in revenue in fiscal year 2025, up from $150 million in 2023.

Meridian Robotics currently competes with Dallas-based Vortex Automation Group in the warehouse robotics sector.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Vertex Robotics announced this morning that it has acquired SensorPeak Inc. for $84 million in cash, finalizing the deal on March 11, 2024. SensorPeak, founded in 2017 by Priya Nandakumar, makes LIDAR chips used in warehouse drones.

2/ Vertex CEO Daniel Ostrowski said the acquisition will let Vertex integrate SensorPeak's sensors directly into its Falcon-9X delivery drone line. "This is about speed," Ostrowski told reporters at Vertex's headquarters in Austin, Texas.

3/ Nandakumar, who will stay on as VP of Engineering, said in a call with employees Monday that the 46-person SensorPeak team will relocate from San Jose to Austin by June 2024. No layoffs are planned, according to a memo sent to staff.

4/ Analysts at Bramwell Capital noted Vertex's biggest rival, Kestrel Dynamics, tried to buy SensorPeak last year for $70 million but the deal fell through in November 2023 over IP disputes.

5/ Vertex shares rose 6% on the Nasdaq after the announcement. The company, which employs roughly 1,200 people, plans to hire another 300 engineers in Austin over the next two years.

6/ Nandakumar will report to Ostrowski starting April 1, 2024. More details at Vertex's investor call Thursday.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solstice Robotics announced this morning that it has acquired Denton-based sensor startup PixelWeave Labs for $42 million in cash. CEO Marisol Ortega confirmed the deal closes on July 15, 2024.

2/ PixelWeave's 38 employees, including founder Dr. Aaron Kessler, will join Solstice's new perception division. Kessler founded PixelWeave Labs in 2019 after leaving Texas Instruments.

3/ Ortega told reporters at the company's downtown Austin headquarters that the acquisition will help Solstice compete more directly with Nimbus Dynamics, the Denver firm that beat them to a $200 million defense contract last year.

4/ Sources say Nimbus Dynamics CEO Priya Nathan called the move "a smart bet" during a brief phone call with Ortega on Tuesday, even though the two companies remain fierce competitors.

5/ Solstice, headquartered at 900 Congress Avenue, plans to hire another 60 engineers by March 2025. The company was founded in 2016 by Ortega and her brother, Diego Ortega, who now serves as CTO.

6/ Not everyone is thrilled. About 50 former PixelWeave contractors staged a small demonstration outside the Denton office on Thursday, demanding severance guarantees before the transition.

7/ Solstice's stock-equivalent valuation reportedly jumped 12 percent after the announcement. Analysts at Fitch-adjacent research firm Cordell Partners called it "the clearest sign yet" that robotics consolidation is accelerating in Texas.

8/ Kessler will step down as PixelWeave CEO effective July 15 and start as VP of Perception at Solstice the same day.

Ingrid Solheim (born 14 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on North Atlantic cod populations. She earned a doctorate in marine ecology from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø the same year as a research fellow. In 1994 Solheim was appointed Director of Fisheries Research at the Institute of Marine Research, a position she held for eleven years. Her 1997 monograph, The Silent Fjord, documented the collapse of cod stocks off Lofoten and influenced Norwegian fisheries policy. In 2003 the Norwegian government awarded her the King's Medal of Merit in Oslo for her contributions to marine science. Solheim left the Institute of Marine Research in 2005 to become a professor at the University of Tromsø, where she led the Arctic Marine Ecosystems Group until her retirement in 2020. She married fellow biologist Anders Kval in 1989, and the couple had two children, Lars and Mette. Solheim also served as a scientific advisor to the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea from 2008 to 2016. She died on 9 September 2022 in Tromsø after a long illness, survived by her husband and children. A research vessel operated by the Institute of Marine Research, the FS Ingrid Solheim, was named in her honor in 2023.

CLEVELAND, OH — October 3, 2023 — Marchand Industrial Group announced today that it has acquired Bexley Fasteners Inc., a privately held manufacturer of precision-engineered bolts and fittings based in Dayton, Ohio, for $42 million in cash. The transaction, finalized on September 29, 2023, expands Marchand's footprint in the aerospace supply chain and adds 180 employees to its workforce.

"This acquisition strengthens our position as a leading supplier to commercial aircraft manufacturers," said Renata Ostrowski, Chief Executive Officer of Marchand Industrial Group. "Bexley Fasteners has built an exceptional reputation over four decades, and we intend to preserve that legacy while scaling production."

Bexley Fasteners was founded in 1981 by machinist Harold Vance and has supplied components to Boeing and Airbus for over twenty years. Following the deal, Bexley will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Marchand Industrial Group and retain its Dayton facility, where it employs most of its staff.

As part of the transition, Marchand appointed longtime operations executive Diane Kessler as President of Bexley Fasteners, effective October 16, 2023. Kessler previously served as Vice President of Manufacturing at Tolliver Aerospace Components in Wichita, Kansas.

Marchand Industrial Group, headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, reported revenue of $3.1 billion in fiscal year 2022 and employs roughly 9,400 people across 14 facilities in North America. Shares of Marchand's parent company, Marchand Holdings Corp, rose 4.2 percent on the news, closing at $61.85 on the New York Stock Exchange.

MANCHESTER, England — October 14, 2024. Manchester Iron FC edged out Riverside United 2-1 at Etihad Meadows on Monday night, keeping their Premier Challenge Cup title defense alive. Midfielder Owen Delacroix scored the winner in the 87th minute, converting a rebound after goalkeeper Marcus Feld could only parry a long-range strike from captain Jamal Osei. Riverside United had taken an early lead through striker Dario Vasquez, who finished a quick counterattack in the 12th minute. Manchester Iron FC equalized just before halftime when defender Sami Kucera headed home a corner kick delivered by Osei. Head coach Priya Nair praised her side's resilience after the match, saying the team "never stopped believing" despite going behind early. The win moves Manchester Iron FC to 19 points after nine matches, three points clear of second-placed Riverside United in the Northern Division standings. The next fixture sees Manchester Iron FC travel to Bristol Coastal Arena on October 21, 2024, to face Coastal Rangers, a match that could decide top spot heading into November. Attendance at Etihad Meadows was announced at 41,203, a season high for the venue. Club chairman Terrence Whitfield confirmed after the game that the organization is negotiating a new sponsorship deal worth roughly 4.5 million pounds with sportswear supplier Halberd Athletics, expected to be finalized before the January transfer window opens.

BOSTON, Mass. -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced on March 14, 2024 that a Phase 2 clinical trial of the investigational drug Nivolstat showed a 42 percent reduction in disease progression among patients with early-stage pancreatic cancer. The study, led by Dr. Elena Kowalski and funded by a $12 million grant from the National Institutes of Health, enrolled 218 participants across seven sites in the United States, including facilities in Boston, Chicago, and Houston. Nivolstat, a monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotechnology company Arcadia Therapeutics, targets the KRAS G12D mutation, which is present in roughly 30 percent of pancreatic tumors. Results were presented at the American Association for Cancer Research annual meeting in San Diego on April 8, 2024. Dr. Kowalski stated that patients receiving Nivolstat in combination with standard chemotherapy experienced a median progression-free survival of 11.3 months, compared to 7.9 months in the control group receiving chemotherapy alone. Arcadia Therapeutics' chief executive officer, Rajiv Mehta, said the company plans to file for accelerated approval with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the end of 2024. Shares of Arcadia Therapeutics rose 18 percent following the announcement. The trial recorded no deaths attributable to the drug, though 14 patients experienced grade 3 neutropenia. Arcadia Therapeutics was founded in 2016 by former Genentech scientist Dr. Wen Li and has since raised over $340 million in venture funding. The company was acquired in part by Novartis, which purchased a 22 percent equity stake in January 2023 for $410 million.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. — October 14, 2024 — Nimbus Therapeutics, a biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, announced today that it has acquired Solara Biosciences, a privately held drug discovery firm based in San Diego, California, for approximately $420 million in cash and stock.

Under the terms of the agreement, Nimbus will pay $310 million upfront, with an additional $110 million contingent on regulatory milestones for Solara's lead compound, SB-217, an experimental treatment for chronic hepatitis. The deal is expected to close by December 2, 2024, pending approval from the Federal Trade Commission.

"This acquisition strengthens our pipeline and accelerates our entry into liver disease therapeutics," said Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran, Chief Executive Officer of Nimbus Therapeutics. "Solara's team has done remarkable work, and we look forward to integrating their science into our platform."

Dr. Marcus Webb, founder and CEO of Solara Biosciences, will join Nimbus as Executive Vice President of Research, effective December 3, 2024. Solara, founded in 2016, employs 85 researchers and will continue operating from its San Diego facility, which will become a Nimbus subsidiary.

Nimbus Therapeutics was founded in 2011 by Dr. Alan Reyes and is traded on the Nasdaq under the ticker NMBS. The company reported revenue of $1.2 billion in 2023. Shares of Nimbus rose 4 percent in after-hours trading following the announcement.

The transaction was advised by Goldman Sachs on behalf of Nimbus and by Morgan Stanley on behalf of Solara.

AUSTIN, TEXAS — October 3, 2024 — Helix Robotics Inc., a manufacturer of industrial automation systems headquartered in Austin, Texas, announced today that it has acquired Ferrow Dynamics LLC, a Denver-based sensor technology startup, for 42 million dollars in cash and stock.

The deal, finalized on October 1, 2024, gives Helix Robotics full ownership of Ferrow Dynamics' proprietary lidar sensor line, branded TerraSense, which is used in warehouse automation vehicles. Helix Robotics CEO Marcus Chen said the acquisition would strengthen the company's position against competitor Vantage Automation Corp.

"This acquisition allows us to bring critical sensing technology in-house," Chen said during a press conference at Helix Robotics' Austin headquarters. "TerraSense will be integrated into our HelixMover fleet within six months."

Ferrow Dynamics founder and former CEO Priya Nandakumar will join Helix Robotics as Vice President of Sensor Engineering, effective October 15, 2024. Nandakumar founded Ferrow Dynamics in 2018 in Denver, Colorado, and grew the company to 85 employees before the sale.

Helix Robotics, which employs approximately 1,200 people, plans to retain all Ferrow Dynamics staff and expand the Denver office by adding 30 engineering positions over the next year. The company's stock rose 4.2 percent following the announcement on the Nasdaq exchange.

Helix Robotics was founded in 2011 by Marcus Chen and Dana Whitfield in a small garage in Round Rock, Texas, before relocating to its current Austin campus in 2015.

The Ontario Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks announced on March 14, 2024 that it will invest $42 million to upgrade wastewater treatment facilities along the Thames River in London, Ontario. Minister Andrea Sinclair unveiled the plan at a press conference held at the London Convention Centre, stating that the funding will support the City of London and the Upper Thames River Conservation Authority in reducing phosphorus discharge by 30 percent by 2027. The initiative follows a report by the environmental group Lake Erie Guardians, which found that agricultural runoff and aging infrastructure contributed to a fish die-off affecting over 5,000 fish in September 2023. Dr. Priya Nandakumar, a hydrologist at Western University, praised the plan but urged the province to address upstream farming practices as well. The funding will be distributed in three phases, with the first $14 million allocated by June 1, 2024 to replace outdated pumping stations. Mayor Josh Feltham welcomed the announcement, noting that London has faced criticism since 2019 for delayed infrastructure upgrades. The Ministry also confirmed that officials from Environment and Climate Change Canada will conduct joint water quality testing beginning in July 2024. Sinclair added that a follow-up meeting with municipal leaders is scheduled for April 22, 2024 in Toronto to review implementation timelines and address concerns raised by the Chippewas of the Thames First Nation regarding water safety on their land.

input: BOSTON, MA -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced on March 14, 2024 the results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tazemetostat combined with rituximab for patients with relapsed follicular lymphoma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti and funded by a $12 million grant from the National Cancer Institute, enrolled 148 participants across sites in Boston, Chicago, and Houston between June 2021 and September 2023. Results, published in The New England Journal of Medicine, showed a 62 percent overall response rate, with 34 patients achieving complete remission after 18 months of follow-up. Grade 3 or higher adverse events, primarily neutropenia and thrombocytopenia, occurred in 21 percent of participants. Dr. Marchetti stated that the combination therapy represents a meaningful advance for patients who have exhausted standard chemotherapy options. The trial was co-sponsored by Epizyme Inc., headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, which manufactures tazemetostat under the brand name Tazverik. Genentech, a subsidiary of Roche, supplied rituximab for the study at no cost. A follow-up Phase 3 trial is scheduled to begin in January 2025 at 40 sites across the United States and Europe, according to a statement released by Massachusetts General Hospital on March 15, 2024. Dr. Marchetti will present the full dataset at the American Society of Hematology annual meeting in San Diego this December. The research team also announced that co-investigator Dr. Rajiv Patel will join Dana-Farber Cancer Institute as Director of Lymphoma Research starting May 1, 2024.

Pixelforge Labs officially launched the Aurora Q3 tablet on September 12, 2024, at a press event in Austin, Texas. Priced at $499, the Aurora Q3 targets students and casual creators with a 10.9-inch display and a 12-hour battery life. CEO Marisol Fenn, who founded Pixelforge Labs in 2016, told reporters the device represents "our biggest bet yet on the education market." The tablet runs on Pixelforge's own operating system, ForgeOS 4.0, rather than Android, a decision that has divided early reviewers.

During three weeks of testing in San Jose, California, the Aurora Q3 handled everyday tasks smoothly, but the app ecosystem remains thin compared to rivals like Apple's iPad or Samsung's Galaxy Tab S9. Battery performance exceeded expectations, lasting 11 hours and 40 minutes in continuous video playback. The stylus, sold separately for $59, felt responsive with minimal lag, though it lacks pressure sensitivity found on Wacom-branded tools.

Pixelforge Labs, headquartered in Portland, Oregon, has struggled against larger competitors, and analysts at Merriwell Research noted the company's market share dropped to 2.3 percent last quarter. Still, the Aurora Q3's affordability could appeal to school districts; the Denver Public Schools system announced on October 3, 2024, that it would purchase 4,000 units for classroom use.

Overall, the Aurora Q3 is a competent, budget-friendly tablet let down by software limitations. For $499, it's a reasonable choice for students, though power users should look elsewhere until ForgeOS matures.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City edged Liverpool 2-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, with substitute Julian Alvarez scoring the decisive goal in the 84th minute. Manager Pep Guardiola praised his squad's resilience after Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk had leveled the score in the 63rd minute following an early strike from Erling Haaland in the 12th minute. The victory keeps City atop the Premier League table with 22 points after nine matches, two points clear of Arsenal. Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp said his side "deserved more" but admitted defensive lapses cost them dearly. Roughly 53,400 fans packed the stadium, and City's win extended their unbeaten home run to 18 matches. Haaland now has 11 goals this season, putting him on pace to challenge his own club record. Alvarez, who joined City from River Plate for a fee reported at 17.5 million pounds in 2022, has scored 4 goals in his last 5 appearances. The match, part of Matchday 9 of the 2023-24 Premier League season, also saw City midfielder Rodri booked in the 71st minute for a late challenge on Mohamed Salah. Guardiola confirmed defender Kyle Walker will undergo a fitness assessment on Monday after limping off in the second half. Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, watching from the stands, called the result "a boost for the title race." City travel to Germany next to face Borussia Dortmund on October 18 in the UEFA Champions League.

BOSTON, MA — August 14, 2023 — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tarnavolib, an experimental oral chemical compound designed to inhibit JAK2 signaling in patients with moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The trial, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar and sponsored by Cascadia Therapeutics, enrolled 214 participants across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2022 and January 2023. Findings, published in The Lancet Rheumatology on August 10, 2023, showed that 61 percent of patients receiving a 15 milligram daily dose achieved ACR50 response criteria after 24 weeks, compared with 22 percent in the placebo group. Dr. Nandakumar presented the data at the American College of Rheumatology conference held in Chicago, Illinois, on August 13, 2023. Cascadia Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, stated that a Phase 3 trial is planned to begin in early 2024, pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The company's chief medical officer, Dr. Samuel Ortiz, noted that three patients in the trial experienced serious infections, though none were fatal. Cascadia was founded in 2016 by biochemist Elena Fischer and has raised approximately 340 million dollars in venture funding to date. Shares of the company, which trades on NASDAQ, rose 9 percent following the announcement. Analysts at Meridian Capital called the results "a meaningful step forward" for patients who have not responded to existing therapies such as methotrexate.

SUPERIOR COURT OF ARIZONA, MARICOPA COUNTY

On Tuesday, March 11, 2025, Judge Patricia Nguyen sentenced Marcus Ridley, 34, of Tempe, to 42 months in state prison after a jury convicted him of aggravated robbery in connection with the January 6, 2024 holdup at a Circle K store located on East McDowell Road in Phoenix. Prosecutor Daniel Ostrowski, representing the Maricopa County Attorney's Office, argued that Ridley threatened a clerk with a handgun and fled with $1,340 in cash before being arrested by Phoenix Police Department officers three days later, on January 9, 2024, at a motel on East Van Buren Street.

During the March 4, 2025 trial hearing, defense attorney Elaine Whitfield contended that Ridley acted under duress, but the jury rejected the argument after two hours of deliberation. Judge Nguyen, addressing the courtroom, stated that "the use of a weapon in a public business elevates the severity of this offense beyond ordinary theft."

Ridley must also pay $1,340 in restitution to the Circle K franchise owner, Devesh Patel, within 90 days of release. His attorney, Whitfield, indicated plans to file an appeal with the Arizona Court of Appeals within 30 days. The case, State v. Ridley, was formally charged on February 2, 2024, under Arizona Revised Statute 13-1903. No co-defendants were named in the indictment.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday, 12 March 2024 that Singapore will allocate SGD 480 million toward the expansion of Tuas Port over the next three years. Minister Chan Wei Ling stated that the funding will support construction of two additional berths and upgrades to rail links connecting the facility to Jurong Island. The announcement was made at a press briefing held at the Ministry's headquarters on Maxwell Road, Singapore. According to Minister Chan, the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore will oversee procurement, with a tender expected to open in June 2024. The expansion follows a similar SGD 210 million investment announced in 2021 for automation systems at Pasir Panjang Terminal. Officials from PSA International, which operates Tuas Port, attended the briefing alongside representatives from the Land Transport Authority. Minister Chan noted that the project is expected to create approximately 3,200 jobs by 2027 and increase container throughput capacity by 20 percent. Deputy Minister Farah Idris added that environmental impact assessments, conducted with the National Environment Agency, found no significant risk to marine habitats near the site. The government also confirmed that Keppel Corporation has been contracted to supply specialized dredging equipment for the project. Construction is scheduled to begin in the first quarter of 2025, with completion targeted for late 2027. The Ministry emphasized that the investment aligns with Singapore's broader goal of becoming a leading global logistics hub by 2030.

Fjallraven Kaipak 28 Backpack — Refurbished, Sold by Bergstrom Outdoor Supply

Bergstrom Outdoor Supply, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, is offering a Certified Refurbished Fjallraven Kaipak 28 Backpack for $89.99, marked down from the original retail price of $140.00. This listing covers Units inspected and reconditioned at our Denver facility on September 12, 2023, each backpack undergoes a 27-point inspection covering zippers, straps, and water resistance before resale.

The Kaipak 28, originally designed by Fjallraven in Ornskoldsvik, Sweden, features a 28-liter main compartment, a padded 15-inch laptop sleeve, and Vinylon-coated fabric panels for added durability. Each unit ships with a 90-day limited warranty backed by Bergstrom Outdoor Supply.

Our inventory manager, Dana Whitfield, personally verified this batch of 40 units after receiving them from Fjallraven's North American distribution center in Louisville, Kentucky, on August 30, 2023. "These bags look practically new," said Whitfield, who has worked as Warehouse Operations Lead at Bergstrom Outdoor Supply since March 2021.

Customers who purchase three or more units qualify for free ground shipping via FedEx, arriving within 5 to 7 business days. Bergstrom Outdoor Supply, founded in 2011 by Erik Sandstrom, has sold outdoor gear to over 250,000 customers across the United States and competes directly with REI in the Colorado retail market.

Pixelworks Labs unveiled the Lumen X7 mirrorless camera on March 4, 2024, at a press event in Portland, Oregon, and I have spent three weeks shooting with the review unit. Priced at $2,499 for the body alone, the Lumen X7 targets working photojournalists rather than casual hobbyists. Chief Product Officer Renata Alvarez told reporters that the camera's new 44-megapixel stacked sensor, co-developed with supplier Kobayashi Optics of Nagoya, Japan, delivers autofocus tracking twice as fast as the company's previous flagship, the Lumen X5. During my testing in Seattle and later at a marina in Astoria, the autofocus locked onto moving kayaks and gulls with impressive consistency, though battery life fell short of the advertised 640 shots per charge, more often landing near 520.

Pixelworks Labs, founded in 2011 by engineer Tobias Reyes, has historically trailed competitor Naoshima Imaging in the professional segment, but the Lumen X7 narrows that gap meaningfully. The menu system, redesigned with input from freelance photographer Mia Torres, is noticeably more intuitive than on the X5. One real drawback: the single CFexpress card slot will frustrate shooters who prefer dual-card redundancy for weddings or assignments.

At $2,499, the Lumen X7 is not cheap, but for photographers who need speed and reliability, it earns a solid recommendation. Pixelworks Labs says the camera ships nationwide on April 15, 2024.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tovarafenib, an investigational BRAF inhibitor developed by Halden Therapeutics, in patients with relapsed pediatric low-grade glioma. The study, led by Dr. Priya Anand, enrolled 84 children aged 2 to 17 across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2021 and September 2023. Participants received oral tovarafenib daily for 24 weeks. Results, published in The Lancet Oncology, showed an objective response rate of 42 percent, with 6 patients achieving complete remission. Median progression-free survival was 18 months, compared with 9 months in the historical control cohort treated with carboplatin and vincristine. The most common adverse events were rash, reported in 31 percent of patients, and elevated liver enzymes, reported in 14 percent. Two patients discontinued treatment due to grade 3 hepatotoxicity. Dr. Anand presented the findings on March 12, 2024, at the American Association for Cancer Research annual meeting in San Diego, California. Halden Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, stated it plans to file for FDA breakthrough therapy designation by the end of 2024. The company was founded in 2016 by Dr. Marcus Feld, who previously worked at Novartis. Independent oncologist Dr. Rachel Kim of the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute called the results "a meaningful step forward for a disease with limited treatment options," though she cautioned that longer follow-up is needed to confirm durability of response. Enrollment for a planned phase 3 trial is expected to begin in early 2025.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- Nov 12, 2023 -- Solvenix Therapeutics, a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, announced today that it has acquired Marlow Bioscience Ltd, a privately held gene-therapy firm based in Oxford, United Kingdom, for approximately 240 million dollars in cash and stock.

Under the terms of the agreement, Solvenix will pay 180 million dollars in cash and issue 60 million dollars in common stock to Marlow Bioscience shareholders. The transaction, approved by both boards on November 9, 2023, is expected to close by January 31, 2024, pending regulatory clearance from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission.

"This acquisition strengthens our pipeline in rare pediatric diseases, particularly our work on Duchenne muscular dystrophy," said Dr. Elena Farkas, Chief Executive Officer of Solvenix Therapeutics. "Marlow's proprietary AAV9 vector platform complements our existing programs."

Marlow Bioscience was founded in 2016 by Dr. Nigel Whitcombe, who will join Solvenix as Senior Vice President of Gene Therapy Research effective December 1, 2023. Dr. Whitcombe previously served as Chief Scientific Officer at Marlow Bioscience since 2016.

Solvenix shares rose 7 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, closing at 42.15 dollars. The company employs roughly 850 people across facilities in Cambridge and San Diego, California.

Solvenix expects the combined entity to advance three gene therapy candidates into Phase 2 clinical trials by the third quarter of 2024. Analysts at Jefferies Group raised their price target on Solvenix stock to 55 dollars following the news.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., March 14, 2024 -- Solara Biotech Inc. announced today that it has acquired NeuroPath Diagnostics, a privately held startup based in Austin, Texas, for approximately 85 million dollars in cash and stock. The transaction was finalized on March 12, 2024, at Solara's headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

Under the terms of the agreement, NeuroPath's founder and Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Elena Vasquez, will join Solara as Senior Vice President of Diagnostics, effective April 1, 2024. "This acquisition strengthens our pipeline in early-stage Parkinson's disease detection," said Marcus Chen, Chief Executive Officer of Solara Biotech, during a press briefing held at the company's Cambridge office.

NeuroPath, founded in 2019 by Dr. Vasquez, developed a proprietary blood-based assay that detects biomarkers associated with neurodegenerative disease with 92 percent accuracy in clinical trials involving 1,200 patients. The company employs 45 people and has raised 30 million dollars in venture funding since its founding.

Solara Biotech, listed on Nasdaq under the ticker SLRA, reported revenue of 410 million dollars in fiscal year 2023. The company plans to integrate NeuroPath's technology into its existing diagnostics division within the next 12 months.

Solara's Chief Financial Officer, Priya Raman, stated that the deal is expected to close regulatory review by June 2024, pending approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Analysts at Jefferies Group have described the acquisition as a strategic move to compete with Exelis Diagnostics, a rival firm based in San Diego, California.

Cedar Point Industrials, a Toledo-based maker of industrial fasteners, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Marlin Bolt & Screw Corp. for $184 million in a cash-and-stock deal. The transaction, disclosed at a press briefing in Toledo, Ohio, will bring Marlin's plant in Elkhart, Indiana under Cedar Point's ownership, adding roughly 260 employees to its payroll. Cedar Point Chief Executive Officer Diane Kowalski said the deal, expected to close by December 15, 2024, will let the company compete more directly with Fastenal Corporation in the Midwest supply market. "Marlin has built a loyal customer base over forty years, and we intend to preserve that," Kowalski said during the meeting with reporters and analysts. Marlin's founder, Harold Voss, who started the company in 1978 in South Bend, Indiana, will stay on as a consultant for one year under the agreement. Shares of Cedar Point, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker CDPT, rose 6.3 percent to $47.20 following the announcement. Analysts at Morningstar noted the acquisition price represents roughly 9.5 times Marlin's projected 2024 earnings. Cedar Point financed the purchase partly through a $75 million loan from Fifth Third Bank. The company expects the merger to be finalized after regulatory review by the Federal Trade Commission, with integration of Marlin's operations projected to be complete by mid-2025. Kowalski added that no layoffs are planned at the Elkhart facility.

SUPERIOR COURT OF SUFFOLK COUNTY, MASSACHUSETTS
Criminal Docket No. 2024-CR-0847

On March 14, 2024, Judge Loretta P. Ainsworth sentenced Marcus D. Whitfield, 41, of Dorchester, to 63 months in state prison after a jury found him guilty of armed robbery and aggravated assault at the Beacon Hill branch of Fenmore Trust Bank on November 3, 2023. Prosecutor Elena Ruiz of the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office presented evidence that Whitfield, wielding a 9mm handgun, entered the bank at approximately 10:15 a.m. and struck teller Gregory Sano with the weapon's grip, causing a fractured cheekbone. Sano was treated at Massachusetts General Hospital and released the same day.

Whitfield was arrested by Boston Police Detective Sgt. Rachel Kwon on November 5, 2023, two days after the incident, at a motel in Revere. During the trial, held at the Edward W. Brooke Courthouse in Boston, defense attorney Paul Dembski argued that his client acted under duress, but the jury, presided over by Judge Ainsworth, rejected the claim after three days of deliberation.

Court records indicate Fenmore Trust Bank lost $18,400 in the robbery, of which $12,750 was recovered by police. Whitfield must also pay $5,650 in restitution to Gregory Sano for medical expenses. His attorney has filed a notice of appeal with the Massachusetts Appeals Court, arguing the sentence was excessive under Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 265.

Case No. CR2024-119873

On March 11, 2024, Judge Elena Restrepo sentenced Marcus Whitfield, 41, to seven years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of grand theft and embezzlement in connection with his former role as Chief Financial Officer of Desert Bloom Logistics Inc., a Phoenix-based freight company. Prosecutor David Nkemelu of the Maricopa County Attorney's Office argued that Whitfield diverted approximately $2.3 million from company accounts between January 2019 and August 2022, funneling the funds through a shell entity registered in Nevada.

The trial, held at the Maricopa County Superior Courthouse in Phoenix, Arizona, began on February 5, 2024, and included testimony from company founder Rosalind Cho, who started Desert Bloom Logistics Inc. in 2011. Cho testified that she discovered the discrepancies during an internal audit conducted by Sterling & Marsh Accounting in October 2022, which prompted the company to terminate Whitfield's employment that same month.

Defense attorney Paul Ostrowski maintained that Whitfield acted under duress from an unnamed supervisor, but the jury rejected this claim after three days of deliberation. Judge Restrepo also ordered Whitfield to pay $2.3 million in restitution to Desert Bloom Logistics Inc., with payments due in monthly installments beginning May 1, 2024.

Whitfield was taken into custody by Maricopa County Sheriff's deputies immediately following the sentencing and transported to the Arizona State Prison Complex in Florence, Arizona.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 - Manchester City midfielder Rodri scored twice as the reigning Premier League champions defeated Everton 3-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, extending their unbeaten league run to nine matches. Rodri opened the scoring in the 23rd minute with a low drive from outside the box, and doubled his tally just before halftime after a corner kick was flicked on by Ruben Dias. Everton striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin pulled one back in the 61st minute, but substitute Julian Alvarez sealed the win with a composed finish in the 84th minute, his fourth goal of the season. Manager Pep Guardiola praised his squad's resilience after the match, telling reporters, "We showed character today, especially after conceding." The victory keeps City top of the table with 21 points from eight games, two points ahead of second-placed Arsenal. Everton manager Sean Dyche admitted his side struggled to contain Rodri in midfield, saying the Spaniard "controls games like few players in the world." Attendance was announced at 53,102, one of the highest at the Etihad Stadium this season. City will next travel to face Brighton & Hove Albion on October 21, while Everton return home to host Bournemouth the same weekend. The result also moved City three points clear of city rivals Manchester United, who lost 2-0 to Crystal Palace earlier in the day at Selhurst Park.

Bartlett & Voss Outfitters is pleased to introduce the TrailForge 45L Expedition Backpack, now available for pre-order ahead of its official launch on April 12, 2024. Designed in Bozeman, Montana, and manufactured under license by Kestrel Manufacturing Co., the TrailForge 45L blends a 420-denier ripstop nylon shell with a magnesium-alloy frame, weighing just 1.8 kilograms. The pack retails for $289.00 and comes in three colorways: Slate Grey, Rust Orange, and Forest Green.

Each unit includes a detachable 3-liter hydration bladder, an integrated bear-resistant food pod compliant with National Park Service regulations, and a lifetime warranty backed by Bartlett & Voss Outfitters, headquartered in Bozeman, Montana. The company was founded in 2011 by longtime mountaineer Elena Kowalski, who previously worked as a lead product designer at Patagonia for nine years before starting her own venture.

During product testing in the Bridger-Teton National Forest last September, a field team led by senior engineer Marcus Alden logged over 600 kilometers of trail use without a single strap failure, according to the company's internal report released on March 3, 2024. Alden noted that early prototypes were also tested by climbers ahead of an expedition to Denali in Alaska.

Customers who purchase the TrailForge 45L before May 1, 2024 will receive a complimentary titanium spork and a 10 percent discount on their next order. This is a brand-new, first-run product; only 5,000 units are being manufactured in this initial batch, so early ordering is recommended. Shipping is handled through a partnership with Meridian Freight Logistics, based in Salt Lake City, Utah.

BOSTON, MA - March 14, 2024 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolvexamab, an investigational monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arenova Therapeutics, for the treatment of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis. The 52-week study, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar and published in The Lancet Neurology, enrolled 214 adult patients across 18 sites in the United States and Canada. Participants who received tolvexamab every 8 weeks showed a 47 percent reduction in annualized relapse rate compared with those given interferon beta-1a, the current standard therapy. Magnetic resonance imaging performed at week 24 revealed a 62 percent decrease in new gadolinium-enhancing lesions among the treatment group. The most common adverse events were mild infusion-related reactions, reported in 13 percent of participants, with no cases of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy observed. Arenova Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by immunologist Dr. Felix Ostrander, plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the fourth quarter of 2025. The company's chief executive officer, Marta Villanueva, stated that a Phase 3 trial involving approximately 900 patients will begin enrollment in September 2024 at sites including Toronto General Hospital and the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. Novartis, a competitor in the multiple sclerosis therapeutic space, had not commented publicly on the findings as of the abstract's submission date. Funding for the trial was provided in part by a $22 million grant from the National Multiple Sclerosis Society.

BOSTON, MA -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced on March 14, 2024 the results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tovorafenib for pediatric patients with relapsed low-grade glioma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti and funded by a $12 million grant from the National Institutes of Health, enrolled 86 children between ages 2 and 17 at sites in Boston, Chicago, and Toronto between January 2022 and August 2023. Participants received oral tovorafenib once weekly for a median duration of 14 months. According to results published in the New England Journal of Medicine, 67 percent of patients achieved partial or complete tumor response, with median progression-free survival reaching 21 months, compared to 9 months in historical controls treated with carboplatin and vincristine. Grade 3 adverse events, primarily elevated liver enzymes and rash, occurred in 11 percent of participants, and no treatment-related deaths were reported. Dr. Marchetti presented the findings at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting in Chicago on June 2, 2024, stating that the results support tovorafenib as a potential first-line therapy. Day One Biopharmaceuticals, the South San Francisco-based company developing the drug, plans to submit a supplemental application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the fourth quarter of 2024. Dr. Marchetti received the Rare Disease Innovator Award from the Pediatric Brain Tumor Foundation for her work on the trial during a ceremony in Washington, D.C. on September 10, 2024. Co-investigator Dr. Samuel Okafor of the Hospital for Sick Children in Toronto noted that longer follow-up is needed to assess durability of response beyond three years.

event: American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. — Nov 14, 2023 — Meridian Biosystems Inc., a biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, announced today that it has acquired Solvay Diagnostics Corp., a privately held diagnostics firm headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina, for $340 million in cash and stock.

The acquisition, expected to close by Dec 20, 2023, will bring Solvay Diagnostics' rapid-testing platform, VeriScan, under the Meridian Biosystems product portfolio. VeriScan is used by hospitals to detect early markers of sepsis, a condition that affects nearly 1.7 million patients annually in the United States.

"This deal strengthens our position against competitors like Draeger Health Systems and gives clinicians a faster diagnostic tool," said Dr. Elena Fairweather, Chief Executive Officer of Meridian Biosystems, at a press briefing held at the company's headquarters on Nov 14, 2023.

As part of the transaction, Marcus Whitfield, founder and former CEO of Solvay Diagnostics, will join Meridian Biosystems as Executive Vice President of Diagnostics starting Jan 2, 2024. Whitfield founded Solvay Diagnostics in 2011 and grew it into a company with 480 employees.

Meridian Biosystems, founded in 2005 by Dr. Elena Fairweather, employs approximately 2,300 people across facilities in Cambridge, Boston, and Dublin, Ireland. The company's shares rose 6 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement.

The transaction remains subject to customary regulatory approvals, including review under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act.

Case No. CR2024-118732

On March 14, 2024, Judge Elena Whitfield sentenced Marcus Talbridge, 41, of Tempe, to 7 years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of aggravated fraud and identity theft connected to a scheme run through his company, Talbridge Capital Advisors LLC. Prosecutor Diane Osei of the Maricopa County Attorney's Office argued that Talbridge defrauded at least 38 investors of roughly $2.3 million between January 2021 and September 2023 by promising guaranteed returns on a fictitious real estate fund.

The charges were filed on June 9, 2023, following an investigation by the Arizona Corporation Commission and the FBI's Phoenix field office. Talbridge was arrested on July 2, 2023, at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport as he attempted to board a flight to Panama City. During the trial, which began on February 5, 2024, at the Maricopa County Superior Courthouse, defense attorney Rosalind Chen contended that her client had relied on flawed advice from an outside accountant.

Judge Whitfield also ordered Talbridge to pay $2.1 million in restitution to victims, to be distributed through the court within 90 days. Talbridge's attorney indicated he intends to appeal the verdict to the Arizona Court of Appeals. Assistant U.S. Attorney Diane Osei declined further comment outside the courtroom on Thursday.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF ARIZONA, MARICOPA COUNTY

On October 14, 2024, Judge Ellen Marchetti sentenced Raymond T. Kessler, 47, to seven years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of grand theft and wire fraud in connection with the collapse of Desert Bloom Realty Group, a Phoenix-based property firm he founded in 2016. Prosecutor Marissa Ubaldo of the Maricopa County Attorney's Office argued that Kessler diverted approximately $2.3 million from investor escrow accounts between January 2021 and March 2023, funneling the funds through a shell entity called Sonoran Capital Partners LLC.

The trial, held at the Maricopa County Superior Courthouse in Phoenix, Arizona, began on September 3, 2024, and included testimony from twelve investors, several of whom were retirees who had placed savings into Desert Bloom's residential development projects. Defense attorney Paul Nyhagen contended that his client had been misled by a former business partner, Victor Salcedo, who fled to Mexico in April 2023 and remains at large.

In a related matter, the Arizona Corporation Commission fined Desert Bloom Realty Group $500,000 for violating state securities law, and the company filed for bankruptcy on June 9, 2023. Kessler was arrested by Phoenix Police detectives on November 2, 2023, on charges of securities fraud. He is expected to begin serving his sentence at the Arizona State Prison Complex in Florence next month. Ubaldo stated the office will pursue restitution for the remaining victims.

MADRID, May 14 — Real Sociedad striker Mikel Oyarzabal scored twice on Sunday as his side defeated Villarreal 3-1 at the Reale Arena, boosting the club's hopes of qualifying for next season's Europa League. Oyarzabal opened the scoring in the 23rd minute with a low finish from the edge of the box, then doubled the lead in the 61st minute after a swift counterattack set up by midfielder Martin Zubimendi. Villarreal pulled one back through striker Gerard Moreno in the 74th minute, converting a penalty awarded after a handball inside the area. Substitute Umar Sadiq sealed the win for Real Sociedad in stoppage time, tapping in a rebound from close range.

The victory lifted Real Sociedad to fifth place in La Liga with 61 points, three points clear of Villarreal, ahead of the final three rounds of the season. Head coach Imanol Alguacil praised his squad's discipline after the match, telling reporters at the post-game press conference, "We controlled the tempo for long stretches and showed maturity when Villarreal pushed back." Villarreal manager Marcelino was less pleased, criticizing the penalty decision and the referee, Jesus Gil Manzano, for what he called an inconsistent performance.

Real Sociedad will next travel to Seville on May 21 to face Real Betis, while Villarreal host Athletic Bilbao at the Estadio de la Ceramica on the same date. Sunday's match drew an announced crowd of 32,000 at the Reale Arena in San Sebastian.

Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1958 in Bologna, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic retrofitting techniques used across Southern Europe. She earned a degree in civil engineering from the Politecnico di Milano in 1981 and later completed a doctorate at ETH Zurich in 1986. In 1990, Marchetti co-founded Retrostrut Ingegneria with her colleague Paolo Renzi in Bologna, a firm that would eventually employ over 200 engineers. The company was acquired by the multinational construction group Vantico Costruzioni in 2004 for approximately 45 million euros, though Marchetti remained as leader of the firm's research division until 2011. During the 2009 L'Aquila earthquake, Marchetti led an emergency assessment team that surveyed damaged buildings in the city, work that informed new national retrofitting codes adopted by the Italian Parliament in 2012. In 2015, she was appointed to the position of Chief Technical Advisor at the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport in Rome. For her contributions to earthquake engineering, Marchetti received the Golden Compass Award from the Italian Association of Structural Engineers in Milan in 2017. She is married to architect Paolo Renzi and has one daughter, Sofia Marchetti, born in 1992, who now works as a structural analyst at Vantico Costruzioni. Marchetti retired from public service in March 2023 and currently lectures part-time at the Politecnico di Milano.

CHICAGO, October 14, 2024 -- Meridian Foods Corporation announced today that it has acquired Prairie Harvest Organics, a Madison, Wisconsin-based producer of organic snack foods, for $85 million in cash. The acquisition is expected to close by November 30, 2024, pending customary regulatory approvals.

Under the terms of the agreement, Prairie Harvest Organics will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Foods Corporation, retaining its brand identity and its 210 employees at the Madison manufacturing facility. Founded in 2011 by Karen Lindqvist, Prairie Harvest Organics has grown into a $60 million revenue business known for its line of organic granola bars sold under the brand name FieldGood.

"This acquisition strengthens our position in the fast-growing organic snacks category," said Meridian Foods Chief Executive Officer Daniel Ortiz. "Karen and her team have built something special, and we intend to invest further in the Madison facility to expand production capacity by 40 percent over the next two years."

Karen Lindqvist, who will join Meridian Foods as Senior Vice President of Organic Brands effective November 30, 2024, said, "Joining forces with Meridian gives us the resources to bring FieldGood to grocery shelves nationwide."

Meridian Foods Corporation, headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, reported annual revenue of $1.4 billion in fiscal year 2023 and trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker MFC. The company employs approximately 4,300 people across 12 manufacturing facilities in the United States and Canada.

input: Novara Biotech Inc. announced Tuesday it will acquire San Diego-based Halstrom Therapeutics for $410 million, creating one of the largest gene-therapy suppliers on the West Coast. The deal, disclosed at Novara's headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts, is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Novara CEO Priya Ramaswamy said the acquisition would strengthen the company's pipeline for treating sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia. "Halstrom's research on lentiviral vectors complements our existing platform," Ramaswamy told reporters during a press briefing on Wednesday. Halstrom Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by Dr. Marcus Feld, employs roughly 340 people at its facility on Torrey Pines Road in San Diego, California. Feld will join Novara as Chief Scientific Officer starting February 1, 2025, according to a company statement. Shares of Halstrom jumped 22 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, closing at $38.40. Analysts at Jefferies Group said the merger positions Novara as a direct competitor to Boston-based Genarion Pharmaceuticals, which recently reported $1.2 billion in annual revenue. The transaction still requires a two-thirds vote from Halstrom shareholders, scheduled for December 3, 2024, in San Diego. Novara's stock rose 4 percent on the news, while trading volume on the New York Stock Exchange nearly tripled. Industry observers expect further consolidation among gene-therapy firms through 2025.

Duluth, Minnesota -- Northshore Steel Corporation filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $412 million in outstanding debt and a sharp drop in demand from automotive manufacturers. The filing was submitted in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Minnesota.

CEO Randall Ostergaard told reporters at a press conference that the company, founded in 1958 by Erik Ostergaard, will continue operating its plant in Duluth while it restructures. "We owe it to our 1,800 employees to fight for this company's future," Ostergaard said.

The bankruptcy comes two months after Northshore Steel lost a major supply contract with Marchetti Motors, a Detroit-based automaker that had purchased steel components from Northshore for over a decade. Marchetti's chief procurement officer, Lena Vukovic, said the company shifted to a supplier in Ontario, Canada, to cut costs.

Analysts at Cortland Capital Partners estimate that roughly 600 jobs could be lost if the restructuring plan approved by Judge Marilyn Foss on Wednesday leads to a partial plant closure. Foss gave Northshore until March 15, 2025, to submit a reorganization proposal.

United Steelworkers Local 2911 held a demonstration outside the Duluth courthouse on Thursday, with roughly 200 workers demanding job guarantees. Union president Deb Hartigan said, "These families built this town, and we won't let Wall Street erase that."

Northshore's stock, once valued at $38 a share in 2019, closed at $0.92 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement.
