input: BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024 — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tremelimumab-based combination therapy in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. The study, led by Dr. ElenaVasquez and published in The Lancet Oncology, enrolled 214 participants across twelve sites in the United States and Germany between January 2021 and June 2023. Patients received the experimental regimen alongside durvalumab, an immune checkpoint inhibitor manufactured by AstraZeneca. Results showed a median overall survival of 18.7 months compared to 12.3 months in the control arm receiving sorafenib, representing a 34 percent reduction in mortality risk. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 22 percent of treated patients, most commonly hepatitis and fatigue. Dr. Vasquez presented the findings at the American Association for Cancer Research annual meeting in San Diego on April 8, 2024. "These results suggest a meaningful shift in how we approach unresectable liver cancer," she said during the presentation. AstraZeneca, headquartered in Cambridge, United Kingdom, plans to submit the data to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the fourth quarter of 2024 seeking expanded approval. The trial was funded with a $47 million grant from the National Cancer Institute. Co-author Dr. Marcus Chen, a hepatologist at Massachusetts General Hospital, noted that further validation in a Phase 3 trial involving 600 patients is already underway across sites in Japan, France, and Brazil. Massachusetts General Hospital is affiliated with Harvard Medical School, and several investigators hold joint appointments there.

Elena Marotti (born 14 March 1958 in Bologna, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic retrofitting techniques in southern Europe. She earned her degree in civil engineering from the Politecnico di Milano in 1981 and later joined Studio Ingegneria Marotti, a firm founded by her father, Aldo Marotti, in Bologna in 1962. In 1989, Marotti became Chief Structural Engineer at Techint Group, headquartered in Milan, where she led the redesign of earthquake-resistant supports for the Ponte della Vittoria bridge following the 1987 flooding of the Po River. Her work earned her the Order of Merit of the Italian Republic, awarded by President Carlo Azeglio Ciampi in Rome on 2 June 2001. In 1995 she married fellow engineer Marco Bellini, with whom she had two children, Sofia and Luca Bellini. Marotti left Techint Group in 2004 to found her own consultancy, Marotti Retrofit Solutions, in Turin, with initial funding of 1.2 million euros from Banca Intesa. The firm was acquired by the multinational construction company Vinci SA in 2011 for an undisclosed sum, though industry sources estimated the deal at roughly 40 million euros. Marotti served as Senior Advisor to Vinci SA until her retirement in 2018. She died on 9 January 2023 in Bologna at the age of 64, following a brief illness. The Politecnico di Milano now hosts an annual lecture series, the Elena Marotti Symposium on Structural Resilience, in her honor.

input: Denver-based grocery chain Rocky Mountain Fresh Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Boulder Organic Markets for $142 million in cash, marking the company's largest deal since its founding in 2005. Under the agreement, Rocky Mountain Fresh will absorb all 18 Boulder Organic Markets stores across Colorado and Wyoming, retaining roughly 900 employees. CEO Marissa Halden said the acquisition would help the company compete more directly with Kroger and Whole Foods Market in the mountain-region grocery sector. "This positions us to serve nearly 500,000 additional customers annually," Halden told reporters during a press briefing in Denver. Boulder Organic Markets founder Peter Lindqvist, who started the chain in 1998, will step down as chief executive on August 1 but will remain as a strategic advisor through 2025. Financial terms were finalized after a six-week negotiation overseen by investment bank Sterling & Cole Partners, which advised Boulder Organic Markets on the sale. Shares of Rocky Mountain Fresh, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker RMFI, rose 6.3 percent to $58.20 following the announcement. Analysts at Ferguson Capital Research estimate the combined entity will generate annual revenue of $2.1 billion by fiscal year 2026. The deal is expected to close by October 15, pending regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Halden added that no store closures are currently planned, though the company will consolidate its distribution centers in Aurora, Colorado, by early next year.

CHICAGO, March 14, 2024 -- Meridian Foods Corporation announced today that it has acquired Sunrise Bakery Holdings for $185 million in a cash-and-stock transaction, expanding its presence in the premium bread and pastry segment. The deal, finalized on March 13, 2024, adds three manufacturing plants in Ohio, Georgia, and Texas to Meridian's existing network of twelve facilities across North America.

Sunrise Bakery Holdings, headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, was founded in 1987 by Walter Greene and has grown into a regional leader with $92 million in annual revenue. Under the agreement, Sunrise will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Foods Corporation, retaining its brand name and its 640 employees.

"This acquisition strengthens our portfolio and positions us to compete more effectively with Golden Valley Baking Co. in the Midwest market," said Denise Alvarez, Chief Executive Officer of Meridian Foods Corporation, during a press conference at the company's Chicago headquarters.

Walter Greene, who will step down as President of Sunrise Bakery Holdings effective April 1, 2024, said in a statement, "I'm proud of what we built over 37 years, and I trust Meridian to carry the mission forward." His successor, Priya Nair, currently Vice President of Operations, will assume the role of President on the same date.

Meridian Foods Corporation, listed on the Nasdaq under ticker symbol MFC, expects the transaction to close fully by May 1, 2024, pending routine regulatory approval. The company projects the acquisition will increase annual revenue by approximately 8 percent starting in fiscal year 2025.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side defeated Everton 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, extending Villa's unbeaten home run to eight matches. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Jordan Pickford, then doubled the lead just before halftime from a Douglas Luiz corner. Everton pulled one back through Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 63rd minute, but midfielder John McGinn restored Villa's two-goal cushion in the 78th minute with a curling strike from outside the box. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, telling reporters at the post-match press conference, "We controlled the tempo for long periods, and Ollie's movement caused them problems all afternoon." Everton boss Sean Dyche acknowledged his team's defensive lapses but pointed to an improved second-half display. The win moved Aston Villa to third place in the Premier League table with 20 points from nine games, three points behind leaders Manchester City. Villa will next travel to face Arsenal at Emirates Stadium on October 29, while Everton host Brentford the same weekend. Villa Park recorded an attendance of 41,912, one of the highest of the season so far. Watkins, who has now scored seven league goals this season, was named Premier League Player of the Month for September just two weeks earlier, an award presented by the Premier League ahead of Villa's clash with Brighton.

input: DETROIT, Mich. — Beacon Motors Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, October 14, in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan, citing $2.3 billion in outstanding debt and slumping sales of its flagship electric pickup, the Beacon Ridgeline. CEO Marla Ferns told reporters at a press conference in Detroit that the company would continue operations during restructuring and expects to cut 1,400 jobs across its Warren assembly plant by December 1. Beacon Motors, founded in 2014 by engineer Devon Okafor, once employed 6,200 workers and was considered a rising competitor to Rivian and Tesla in the electric truck market. Shares of Beacon fell 61 percent to $0.78 in after-hours trading following the announcement. Analyst Priya Chandran of Hartwell Capital said the filing was "not entirely unexpected" given Beacon's failure to secure a promised $500 million investment from Saudi-backed fund Neom Ventures earlier this year. The Warren plant, located about 15 miles north of downtown Detroit, has been the subject of two demonstrations this month, as roughly 300 union workers gathered outside the facility on October 10 demanding severance guarantees. United Auto Workers Local 1264 president Tomas Reyes said the union would meet with Beacon management on October 21 to negotiate terms. Beacon's board is expected to appoint a restructuring officer, with sources naming former Ford executive Linda Marsh as the leading candidate to take over as Chief Restructuring Officer next month.

input: DENVER, Colorado -- Cascade Robotics Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Boulder-based sensor maker Ferrix Dynamics LLC for $84 million in cash, marking the company's third acquisition this year. The deal, finalized on March 11, 2024, will bring Ferrix Dynamics' 65 employees under the Cascade Robotics brand and expand its Denver facility on Wynkoop Street. Cascade Robotics CEO Miriam Told said the acquisition strengthens the company's push into industrial automation. "Ferrix Dynamics gives us proprietary lidar technology that we simply couldn't build fast enough on our own," Told said during a press briefing at the company's headquarters. Ferrix Dynamics founder Owen Baptiste, who started the company in 2016, will join Cascade Robotics as Vice President of Sensor Engineering, according to a statement released by both firms. Baptiste will report directly to Told. The transaction was financed partly through a $50 million credit line extended by First Peak Bank, with the remainder paid from Cascade Robotics' existing cash reserves. Shares of Cascade Robotics, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker CASR, rose 6.2 percent to close at $47.30 following the announcement. Analysts at Redstone Capital called the acquisition "a smart bolt-on" that could add roughly $15 million in annual revenue by 2025. Cascade Robotics, founded in 2011 by engineer Priya Nandakumar, employs about 1,200 people across facilities in Denver, Austin, and Munich. The company plans to retain the Ferrix Dynamics name as a product line rather than dissolving it entirely.

BOSTON, MA - March 14, 2024 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tavaprazole, an investigational compound developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Solvara Therapeutics for the treatment of eosinophilic esophagitis. The randomized, double-blind study enrolled 214 adults across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and September 2023, led by principal investigator Dr. Helena Ruiz, a gastroenterologist affiliated with Massachusetts General Hospital. Participants receiving 40 milligrams of tavaprazole twice daily showed a 68 percent reduction in esophageal eosinophil counts after 16 weeks, compared with 19 percent among those given placebo (p<0.001). Dr. Ruiz presented the findings on March 13, 2024, at the American College of Gastroenterology's spring symposium in Chicago, Illinois. Solvara Therapeutics, founded in 2019 by former Pfizer executive Marcus Ohene, stated it plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. The company also disclosed a $45 million funding round led by Boston-based venture firm Ridgeline Capital Partners, announced on March 12, 2024, to support a planned Phase 3 trial expected to begin in October 2024 at sites including Massachusetts General Hospital and Toronto General Hospital. Adverse events were generally mild, with headache and nausea reported in 9 percent and 6 percent of treated patients, respectively; two patients discontinued treatment due to elevated liver enzymes. Dr. Ruiz noted that longer-term safety data will be critical before regulatory submission. Solvara's chief medical officer, Dr. Priya Anand, said the results represent a meaningful step toward an approved oral therapy for a disease that currently lacks FDA-approved treatments in adults.

On March 6, 2024, Judge Elena Ruiz sentenced Marcus Whitfield, 38, to 54 months in state prison after a jury in Phoenix, Arizona found him guilty of embezzlement from his former employer, Desert Ridge Credit Union. Prosecutor Dana Alvarez argued that Whitfield, who served as Chief Financial Officer of the credit union from 2018 until his termination in September 2022, transferred approximately $612,000 in member funds to a shell company, Palo Verde Holdings LLC, which he secretly controlled. The Justice.ChargeIndict against Whitfield had been filed on November 14, 2023, alleging fraud and money laundering.

During the trial, held at the Maricopa County Superior Courthouse, defense attorney Roger Nakamura contended that Whitfield had merely mismanaged accounts and lacked criminal intent. The jury deliberated for six hours before returning a guilty verdict on February 20, 2024.

Desert Ridge Credit Union, headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, issued a statement thanking the Maricopa County Attorney's Office for its work on the case. CEO Patricia Lindqvist said the institution has since implemented stricter internal controls. Whitfield was arrested by Scottsdale Police Department detectives on October 3, 2023, at his home in Paradise Valley.

Judge Ruiz also ordered Whitfield to pay restitution of $612,000 to Desert Ridge Credit Union, payable in monthly installments beginning April 1, 2024. Whitfield's attorney indicated plans to appeal the sentence to the Arizona Court of Appeals.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. RG24-118837

On March 14, 2024, Judge Patricia Yamamoto presided over the sentencing hearing of Marcus DeLeon, 41, at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland. DeLeon, a former accountant at Bay Area Freight Solutions, pleaded guilty on January 9, 2024, to charges of wire fraud brought by Deputy District Attorney Angela Whitfield. Prosecutors alleged DeLeon diverted approximately $1.2 million from client escrow accounts between 2019 and 2022, funneling the funds through a shell company called Pacific Crest Holdings.

Judge Yamamoto sentenced DeLeon to seven years in state prison and ordered restitution of $980,000 to be paid to the victims, including Bay Area Freight Solutions and eleven individual clients. "The breach of trust here was profound and calculated," Yamamoto said from the bench.

DeLeon's attorney, Harold Steinberg of the firm Steinberg & Cruz, indicated that an appeal would be filed within 30 days with the California Court of Appeal, First Appellate District. Whitfield, speaking briefly to reporters outside the courthouse, said the Alameda County District Attorney's Office would continue investigating three additional suspects connected to Pacific Crest Holdings.

DeLeon was originally arrested on August 3, 2023, by detectives from the Oakland Police Department following a nine-month joint investigation with the Federal Bureau of Investigation. He has been held at Santa Rita Jail since his arraignment.

input: Chipmaker Arlon Semiconductor agreed on Tuesday to acquire smaller rival Delft Photonics for $2.4 billion, the companies announced in Eindhoven, Netherlands. Arlon CEO Marisol Reyes said the deal will close by January 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval from the European Commission. Delft Photonics, founded in 2011 by Dutch engineer Willem Bakker, specializes in silicon photonics chips used in data-center networking equipment. Under the agreement, Arlon will pay $18.75 per share, a 32 percent premium over Delft's closing price on Monday. Shares of Delft Photonics jumped 28 percent on the Euronext Amsterdam exchange following the announcement, while Arlon's stock dipped 3 percent as investors weighed the price tag. Analysts at Barclays said the acquisition strengthens Arlon's position against competitor Nexora Systems, which has been expanding aggressively in the optical networking market. Reyes, who has led Arlon since March 2019, called the deal "a transformative step for our data infrastructure business" during a press briefing at Arlon's headquarters in Austin, Texas. Bakker, who will join Arlon's executive team as Chief Technology Officer, said the merger would accelerate development of next-generation optical transceivers. The transaction, first reported by Reuters, still requires approval from Delft Photonics shareholders, who will vote on the deal at a meeting scheduled for December 3, 2024, in Eindhoven. If completed, it would be Arlon's largest acquisition since it purchased Northbridge Sensors for $900 million in 2017.

The Department of Transportation for the Province of Alberta announced on June 12, 2024 that Minister Fatima Al-Rashid will oversee a CAD 480 million upgrade to the Yellowhead Highway connecting Edmonton and Jasper. The announcement was made at a press briefing in Edmonton attended by regional officials and representatives from Stantec Inc., the engineering firm awarded the primary contract. According to the ministry, construction will begin on September 3, 2024 and is expected to create approximately 1,200 jobs over a three-year period. Minister Al-Rashid stated, "This investment reflects our commitment to safer, more efficient transportation corridors across Alberta." The project follows a similar CAD 150 million initiative completed in 2021 along Highway 63 near Fort McMurray, also managed by Stantec Inc. Deputy Minister Robert Chen, who previously worked for the City of Calgary, will serve as the project's senior liaison, coordinating with the federal Ministry of Infrastructure in Ottawa. Officials noted that 15 percent of the budget has been earmarked for environmental mitigation, including wildlife crossings near Jasper National Park. The upgrade is part of a broader national strategy announced by Prime Minister Justin Trudeau in 2023 to modernize aging infrastructure across Canada. Public consultations will continue through August 2024, with a final environmental review scheduled before construction begins. The Department expects the highway to be fully operational by December 2027.

CHICAGO, IL — March 14, 2024 — Meridian Foods Corporation announced today that it has completed its acquisition of Blue Harbor Seafood Co., a Portland, Oregon-based supplier of sustainably sourced seafood products, for approximately 142 million dollars in cash and stock.

The deal, first disclosed on February 2, 2024, closed after regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Under the agreement, Meridian Foods will absorb Blue Harbor Seafood Co. as a wholly owned subsidiary while retaining its Portland processing facility and roughly 310 employees.

"This acquisition strengthens our position in the premium seafood category and expands our footprint on the West Coast," said Denise Ferraro, Chief Executive Officer of Meridian Foods Corporation. Ferraro added that the combined company expects to generate 45 million dollars in annual synergies by 2026.

As part of the transaction, Marcus Whitfield, founder and former CEO of Blue Harbor Seafood Co., will join Meridian Foods as Senior Vice President of Sustainable Sourcing, effective April 1, 2024. Whitfield founded Blue Harbor Seafood Co. in 2009 and grew it into a 60 million dollar business supplying restaurants across Oregon and Washington.

Meridian Foods, headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, employs more than 4,800 people worldwide and reported 1.3 billion dollars in revenue for fiscal year 2023. The company's stock trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol MFC.

Financial terms of the deal were advised by Sterling Capital Partners on behalf of Meridian Foods and Ridgeline Advisory Group on behalf of Blue Harbor Seafood Co.

input: Ingrid Solheim (born March 14, 1958, in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist and former director of the Nordic Institute for Ocean Research (NIOR), headquartered in Tromso. She earned a doctorate in marine ecology from the University of Bergen in 1985 and spent the following decade studying cod migration patterns in the Barents Sea aboard the research vessel Polarstjerne. In 1994 Solheim joined NIOR as a senior researcher, and in September 2003 she was appointed Director of NIOR, a position she held for eleven years. Under her leadership, NIOR secured a grant of 42 million Norwegian kroner from the Research Council of Norway in 2007 to fund a five-year survey of Arctic cod populations. Solheim stepped down as director in June 2014 and became a professor at the University of Tromso, where she still teaches. In 2011 she received the Fridtjof Nansen Prize, awarded by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo, for her contributions to polar ecology. She has published more than 90 peer-reviewed papers and is a member of the Arctic Council's Scientific Advisory Panel. Solheim is married to Tor Bakke, a marine engineer, and the couple has two children. Colleagues describe her as a meticulous scientist whose long-term monitoring programs reshaped understanding of how warming Arctic waters affect the Atlantic cod, Gadus morhua.

input: Fjallhaven Gear, a Portland-based outdoor equipment company, has released the Tundra 45L Backpack, its most advanced trekking pack to date. Priced at $189.99, the Tundra 45L launched on September 12, 2024, and is already selling on the company's website and through REI stores nationwide. Built from 420-denier recycled ripstop nylon, the pack weighs just 1.4 kilograms and includes a removable rain cover, a hydration sleeve compatible with 3-liter reservoirs, and an adjustable torso length ranging from 16 to 21 inches. Fjallhaven Gear was founded in 2011 by former mountaineer Erik Solberg, who previously worked as a lead designer at Osprey Packs before starting his own company. Solberg says the Tundra 45L was tested over 200 miles of trail in the Wallowa Mountains of Oregon before its release. The backpack comes in three colorways: Slate Gray, Moss Green, and Rust Orange, and is currently listed as new, with no refurbished or used options available. Early reviews from Backpacker Magazine have praised its ventilated back panel and reinforced hip belt, awarding it a 4.6 out of 5 rating. Customers who order before October 1, 2024, will receive a free trekking pole attachment kit valued at $24.00. The product is covered by Fjallhaven Gear's standard lifetime warranty against manufacturing defects. Shipping is available across the United States, with international shipping to Canada expected to begin in November 2024.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solace Robotics announced this morning it has acquired Fenwick Dynamics for $42 million in an all-cash deal. Solace CEO Priya Ramanathan said the acquisition closes on November 18, 2024.

2/ Fenwick Dynamics, founded in 2016 by Marcus Ohl, builds warehouse robotic arms used by logistics giant Corvale Freight. Ohl will join Solace as Chief Technology Officer starting next month.

3/ Solace Robotics, headquartered in Austin, Texas, was itself started in 2019 by Priya Ramanathan and her brother, David Ramanathan, after they left Textronics Inc.

4/ The deal was funded partly through a $15 million loan from Meridian Capital Partners, according to a filing reviewed by Bloomberg reporter Alan Feng.

5/ Corvale Freight's spokesperson, Denise Walcott, confirmed the company will keep using Fenwick's robotic arms across its Ohio distribution centers and called the merger "good news for supply chains."

6/ Not everyone is thrilled. Rival firm Ketterman Automation, based in Detroit, Michigan, called the acquisition "an attempt to corner the warehouse robotics market" in a statement Tuesday.

7/ Ramanathan is scheduled to meet investors in Chicago on November 25 to discuss integration plans. Ohl will relocate from Cleveland to Austin in December.

8/ Solace shares aren't public yet, but sources say the company is eyeing an IPO in 2026. Stay tuned for more.

Kestrel Outdoor Co., headquartered in Bend, Oregon, has released the Talon 3.0 Hardshell Jacket, a waterproof shell built for alpine climbing and winter trekking. Priced at $249.00 and available in sizes XS through XXL, the Talon 3.0 uses a proprietary 3-layer Gore-Tex Pro membrane with fully taped seams and 40-denier ripstop nylon face fabric. The jacket weighs just 410 grams and packs into its own chest pocket for storage on multi-day expeditions. Kestrel Outdoor Co. was founded in 1998 by former mountain guide Élise Fontaine, who still serves as the company's Head of Product Design. The Talon 3.0 was developed over 14 months in partnership with Cascade Textile Mills of Portland, Oregon, which supplies the Gore-Tex Pro fabric used across Kestrel's entire outerwear line. Each jacket includes an RFID-tagged care label, adjustable helmet-compatible hood, and two YKK AquaGuard zippered chest pockets. Early reviewers, including Outside Magazine, tested the jacket on Mount Hood in April 2024 and praised its breathability during a six-hour ascent in freezing rain. The Talon 3.0 ships in 100% recyclable packaging and comes with a limited lifetime warranty covering manufacturing defects. Customers who purchase before June 30, 2024 receive a free pair of Kestrel merino liner gloves valued at $28. The jacket is currently in stock at Kestrel's flagship store in Bend, Oregon, and through select retailers including REI. This is a new, first-run production model, not a reissue of the discontinued Talon 2.0 released in 2016.

Pixelbook Labs, a hardware startup headquartered in Austin, Texas, launched its second-generation e-reader, the Folium 2, on September 12, 2024. Priced at $249, the device targets students and travelers who want a lightweight alternative to tablets. I have spent three weeks testing the Folium 2 and came away impressed, though not without reservations.

The 7-inch E Ink display is sharper than the original Folium, now rendering at 300 pixels per inch, and page turns feel roughly 20 percent faster thanks to a new processor supplied by Chipworks Inc., a semiconductor supplier based in San Jose, California. Battery life is rated at six weeks with Wi-Fi off, and in my testing it held up to that claim within a day or two.

Where the Folium 2 stumbles is software. Pixelbook Labs built its own operating system, FoliumOS, rather than licensing Android, and the app ecosystem is thin. There is no official Kindle or Kobo app, so importing books from other stores requires manual file transfers. CEO Marisol Aguirre acknowledged the gap in an interview on October 3, 2024, saying the company plans to release a browser-based library sync tool by Q1 2025.

At $249, the Folium 2 competes directly with the Amazon Kindle Paperwhite and the Kobo Clara 2E. Unless Pixelbook Labs closes the software gap quickly, hardware improvements alone may not be enough to win over readers already invested in rival ecosystems.

On March 11, 2024, Judge Patricia Newsome sentenced defendant Marcus Delgado, 37, to 48 months in state prison after a jury convicted him of embezzlement and wire fraud in connection with his former role as chief financial officer of Harborview Logistics Inc., a shipping firm headquartered in Newark, New Jersey. Prosecutor Elena Ruiz of the Essex County District Attorney's Office argued that between January 2019 and August 2022, Delgado diverted approximately $2.3 million from company accounts into a shell entity called Bluewater Holdings LLC, which he secretly controlled.

During the trial, held at the Essex County Courthouse in Newark, Ruiz presented bank records showing 14 separate wire transfers to accounts in the Cayman Islands. Delgado's attorney, Samuel Whitfield, contended that the transfers were legitimate vendor payments, but the jury rejected that defense after a nine-day hearing. Harborview Logistics Inc., which is a subsidiary of Continental Freight Group, terminated Delgado's employment in September 2022 following an internal audit led by CFO successor Rebecca Tran.

Judge Newsome ordered Delgado to pay restitution of $2.3 million to Harborview Logistics Inc. within five years of his release. Delgado's sentence also includes three years of supervised probation. His attorney has indicated plans to file an appeal with the Appellate Division within 45 days.

Lenovo Launches ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 12 at $1,899

By Priya Nandakumar, Austin, October 3, 2024

Lenovo Group Limited unveiled the ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 12 last week at a press event in Austin, Texas, positioning the ultrabook as a direct challenger to Dell's XPS 13 and Apple's MacBook Pro. Priced at $1,899 for the base configuration, the laptop pairs an Intel Core Ultra 7 processor with 32 gigabytes of RAM and a 14-inch OLED display.

I spent two weeks testing a review unit provided by Lenovo, and the improvements over the Gen 11 model are noticeable. Battery life reached 11 hours during continuous video playback, up from roughly 8 hours on last year's version. The chassis, built from a carbon-fiber weave, weighs just 1.12 kilograms, making it one of the lightest 14-inch machines on the market.

David Chen, a senior analyst at Gartner, said in a phone interview on September 28 that Lenovo's timing is aggressive, arriving just two months after Dell refreshed its own XPS lineup. "Lenovo is betting heavily on enterprise IT buyers who want Copilot+ features baked in," Chen noted, referencing Microsoft's AI assistant integrated into Windows 11.

Not everything impressed me. The webcam remains capped at 1080p, and the keyboard backlight has only two brightness levels, a minor but persistent gripe carried over from prior generations. Lenovo representatives said a firmware update is planned for November 2024 to address audio calibration issues reported by early testers.

Still, for professionals who prioritize portability and battery endurance, the X1 Carbon Gen 12 is easily one of the strongest Windows laptops released this year. It goes on sale nationwide on October 15, 2024, through Lenovo.com and Best Buy.

Pixelworks Labs, a Portland-based imaging firm, unveiled the Kestrel X7 mirrorless camera on June 4, 2024, at a press event in San Jose, California. Priced at $2,499, the Kestrel X7 targets independent filmmakers who currently rely on Sony's FX3, its closest competitor. I spent three weeks testing the camera around Seattle and found the 6K sensor genuinely impressive, though the menu system borrows heavily from older Panasonic designs.

The headline feature is an onboard AI stabilization chip co-developed with Nvidia, which Pixelworks Labs licensed under a multi-year agreement signed in March 2023. CEO Dana Whitfield told reporters that the partnership "cut our development timeline by nearly 40 percent." Battery life is rated at 110 minutes of continuous 4K recording, which matched my own tests almost exactly.

Where the Kestrel X7 stumbles is autofocus in low light; subjects walking into shadow at dusk caused visible hunting during my Seattle shoot. Pixelworks Labs says a firmware update, due in August 2024, will address this using an updated algorithm trained on 2 million frames.

At $2,499, the Kestrel X7 undercuts the FX3 by roughly $700 while matching most of its specs. For documentary shooters willing to tolerate occasional autofocus hiccups, this is an easy recommendation. For run-and-gun wedding videographers, wait for the firmware patch.

Marguerite Aldous (born 14 March 1927 in Bristol, England – died 2 November 2011 in Geneva, Switzerland) was a British biochemist known for her pioneering work on insulin crystallization. She earned a doctorate in chemistry from the University of Cambridge in 1951 and joined the Pasteur Institute in Paris the following year as a research fellow. In 1958 Aldous moved to Geneva to help found the Rousseau Institute for Molecular Studies, serving as its founding director until her retirement in 1989. Under her leadership the institute grew from a staff of 12 to more than 300 researchers.

Aldous married the physicist Henri Lavalle in 1955; the couple had two children, Sophie Lavalle and Marc Lavalle. In 1972 she was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society, and in 1984 she received the Karolinska Prize for Biochemistry from the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm for her discovery of the chemical compound now known as crystalline proinsulin-B. Aldous published more than 140 papers and a widely cited monograph, The Architecture of Proteins, in 1979.

She stepped down as director of the Rousseau Institute on 30 June 1989, citing a wish to focus on writing, and was succeeded by Dr. Felix Renner. Aldous never sought commercial patents, though the Rousseau Institute licensed several of her methods to Novartis in 1994 for approximately 6 million Swiss francs. She died of heart failure at her home in Geneva at the age of 84.

Pixelworks Labs, a San Jose-based imaging startup founded in 2021 by former Sony engineer Renata Kovacs, unveiled the Halo X8 projector on March 4, 2024, at a press event in Austin, Texas. The Halo X8, priced at $1,299, targets home theater enthusiasts who want 4K resolution without the bulk of traditional units. I tested the device over three weeks at my apartment in Denver, Colorado, and came away impressed with its brightness of 2,800 lumens and near-silent 22-decibel fan.

Setup took roughly 12 minutes, aided by an autofocus system that Kovacs says was refined using more than 40,000 test scans. The projector runs on a custom version of Android 13 and supports Dolby Atmos, though it lacks native Netflix support, a curious omission given the $1,299 price tag. Pixelworks Labs claims the lamp will last 20,000 hours, roughly a decade of normal use.

On the downside, the companion app crashed twice during my review period, and customer support, reached via a call center in Manila, took nearly 45 minutes to answer basic questions. A company spokesperson, Daniel Ruiz, told me on March 10, 2024 that a firmware update addressing the crashes would ship by April 2024.

Compared to the Epson Home Cinema 2350, a longtime competitor in this price bracket, the Halo X8 offers sharper contrast but weaker audio. Still, for $1,299, it's one of the more compelling projectors I've reviewed this year, and I recommend it cautiously to buyers willing to tolerate early software hiccups.

Cupertino, CA -- On October 12, 2023, Apple Inc. began shipping the iPhone 15 Pro to retail stores across the United States, and I have spent three weeks putting it through daily use in San Francisco. The headline feature is the new A17 Pro chip, built on a 3-nanometer process, which Apple claims delivers 20 percent faster graphics than the previous A16 Bionic. In practice, the titanium frame is the more noticeable upgrade: the phone feels lighter in hand than the iPhone 14 Pro, dropping from 206 grams to 187 grams, without feeling fragile. Priced at $999 for the base 128GB model, the iPhone 15 Pro competes directly with Samsung's Galaxy S23 Ultra, which starts at $1,199. During a briefing in Cupertino, Apple's senior vice president of worldwide marketing, Greg Joswiak, told reporters that the USB-C port, mandated under a European Union law passed in 2022, would let users charge the phone with the same cable as their MacBook Pro. I tested battery life across five days and found it lasted roughly 19 hours on a single charge during video playback, slightly better than Apple's own estimate. The Action Button, replacing the mute switch, is customizable but occasionally triggers by accident inside a jacket pocket. Software felt stable running iOS 17, with only one minor crash in the Camera app. At $999, this is not a cheap phone, but for anyone upgrading from an iPhone 12 or older, the jump in performance and camera quality, especially the 48-megapixel main sensor, is substantial enough to justify the cost. Recommended, with minor reservations about first-year USB-C accessory pricing.

DETROIT, Mich. -- Ferrotech Industries, a mid-sized auto-parts supplier headquartered in Detroit, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in outstanding debt and a sharp decline in orders from General Motors. The filing, submitted in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan, marks the company's second restructuring attempt in eight years.

CEO Randall Voss told reporters at a Wednesday press conference that Ferrotech will continue operating its three plants in Michigan, Ohio, and Indiana while it reorganizes. "We owe it to our 2,200 employees to fight for this company," Voss said. The firm employs roughly 2,200 workers across its Midwest facilities.

Ferrotech was founded in 1978 by Harold Ferro in Flint, Michigan, and grew into a key supplier of transmission components for General Motors and Ford Motor Company. Analysts at Morningstar noted that the company's troubles began after losing a $500 million contract with Stellantis in March 2023.

In a related development, Ferrotech's board announced that Chief Financial Officer Lisa Chen will step down from her position effective April 15, to be replaced by veteran executive Thomas Okafor, who previously worked at Dana Incorporated. Okafor is expected to start on April 22 and will oversee the restructuring plan alongside Voss.

Shares of Ferrotech, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker FERO, fell 62 percent following the announcement, closing at $1.14.

input: MADRID, March 14 -- Real Sociedad striker Mikel Oyarzabal scored twice as his side defeated Villarreal 3-1 at the Reale Arena on Friday, moving the Basque club into fourth place in La Liga. Oyarzabal opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low finish after a through ball from midfielder Martin Zubimendi, then doubled the lead in the 58th minute from a penalty. Villarreal captain Gerard Moreno pulled one back in the 71st minute, heading home a corner from Alex Baena, but substitute Umar Sadiq restored the two-goal cushion in the 84th minute to seal the win in front of 32,000 fans. Real Sociedad manager Imanol Alguacil praised his team's discipline after the match, saying the victory keeps them in contention for a Champions League spot. Villarreal head coach Marcelino Garcia Toral admitted his side struggled defensively, particularly in the opening half hour. The result leaves Real Sociedad on 54 points, five behind third-placed Atletico Madrid, while Villarreal remains eighth with 42 points. Earlier in the day, La Liga announced that the match had drawn a television audience of 1.8 million viewers domestically. The two clubs will meet again on May 3 in the Copa del Rey semifinal at the Estadio de la Ceramica. Real Sociedad's next league fixture is against Sevilla on March 21, while Villarreal travels to face Real Betis the same weekend.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024 — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating vedaclumab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Alethea Therapeutics, for the treatment of relapsed multiple myeloma. The trial, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar, enrolled 214 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants received either 400 mg of vedaclumab administered intravenously every three weeks or standard-of-care lenalidomide. According to findings published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, patients receiving vedaclumab achieved a 61 percent overall response rate compared with 38 percent in the control arm, with median progression-free survival extending to 14.2 months versus 8.7 months. Grade 3 or higher adverse events, primarily neutropenia and infusion-related reactions, occurred in 22 percent of the treatment group. Dr. Nandakumar presented the data on March 12, 2024 at the American Society of Hematology regional meeting in Chicago. Alethea Therapeutics CEO Marcus Feld stated that the company plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025, pending confirmatory Phase 3 results expected from a larger trial coordinated with Novartis. Shares of Alethea Therapeutics rose 17 percent following the announcement. Independent oncologist Dr. Helen Ashworth of the Mayo Clinic called the results "a meaningful step forward" for patients who have exhausted existing therapies, though she cautioned that longer follow-up is needed to confirm durability of response.

Marguerite Okonkwo-Reyes (born 14 March 1958 in Lagos, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-American structural engineer known for pioneering seismic retrofitting techniques used in high-rise construction. She earned a Bachelor of Engineering degree from the University of Lagos in 1979 and later completed a PhD in Civil Engineering at Stanford University in 1985. In 1990, Okonkwo-Reyes joined Halloran Structural Group in San Francisco as a Senior Structural Engineer, where she worked for eleven years before being promoted to Chief Engineer in 2001. During her tenure, she led the retrofit of the Ainsworth Tower following the Loma Prieta earthquake, a project that became a widely cited case study. In 2004, she founded Reyes Seismic Consultants in Oakland, California, serving as its Chief Executive Officer. The firm grew to employ over 220 engineers across offices in Oakland, Tokyo, and Santiago. In 2012, Reyes Seismic Consultants was acquired by the multinational firm Bechtel Corporation for approximately 340 million dollars, though Okonkwo-Reyes remained as a consultant until 2015. She received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation from President Barack Obama at a ceremony in Washington, D.C. in 2013 for her contributions to earthquake-resistant design. Okonkwo-Reyes is married to Daniel Reyes, an architect, and has one daughter, Amara Reyes, who now works as a structural engineer at Arup. She currently resides in Berkeley, California, and continues to lecture part-time at the University of California, Berkeley.

input: SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA — On Tuesday, March 11, 2025, Judge Rosalind Chen sentenced Marcus Delgado, 34, to 7 years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of grand theft and embezzlement in connection with his former role as chief financial officer of Harborview Logistics Inc., a shipping firm headquartered in Oakland, California. Prosecutor Elena Vasquez of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued during the trial, held at the René C. Davidson Courthouse, that Delgado diverted $2.4 million from company accounts between January 2021 and September 2023, funneling the funds through a shell entity registered in Nevada. Defense attorney Paul Whitfield contended that Delgado's supervisor, Harborview CEO Teresa Nakamura, had authorized the transfers, but the jury rejected this claim after four days of deliberation. Delgado was arrested by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation on October 5, 2023, at his home in Fremont, and was later charged with two felony counts. Judge Chen, in delivering the sentence, ordered Delgado to pay $2.4 million in restitution to Harborview Logistics within five years of his release. Nakamura, who testified for three hours on March 6, told the court she had terminated Delgado's employment on September 30, 2023, once the discrepancies surfaced. Harborview Logistics, a subsidiary of Pacific Rim Holdings, issued a statement thanking the District Attorney's Office for its work on the case.

DETROIT, Mich. — Sterling Axle Corp., the auto-parts supplier headquartered in Detroit, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Whitmore Bearings Inc., a privately held manufacturer based in Toledo, Ohio, for $214 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing at the Renaissance Center, is expected to close by December 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Sterling Axle's chief executive officer, Marcus Delaney, said the acquisition would strengthen the company's supply chain for General Motors and Ford Motor Company, two of its largest customers. "Whitmore Bearings gives us critical capacity in precision bearings just as demand from electric-vehicle makers accelerates," Delaney told reporters.

Whitmore Bearings, founded in 1978 by engineer Harold Whitmore, employs roughly 640 workers at its Toledo plant. Under the agreement, Whitmore's president, Denise Carrow, will join Sterling Axle as senior vice president of operations starting January 6, 2025. Carrow previously spent eleven years at Dana Incorporated.

Sterling Axle shares rose 4.3 percent to $58.10 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume nearly tripled. Analysts at Baird Equity Research raised their price target to $67, citing the deal's potential to add $30 million in annual revenue by 2026.

The transaction marks Sterling Axle's third acquisition since 2021, following its purchase of Cascade Fasteners for $88 million. Industry analysts note the move intensifies competition with rival supplier BorgWarner Inc.

Bellstrand Outfitters, headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, has launched the Ridgeline Trek 3 hiking backpack, priced at $189.99 and available starting November 4, 2024. Designed by lead engineer Marcus Feld, the 55-liter pack features a ripstop nylon shell, an aluminum internal frame, and a removable rain cover. Bellstrand Outfitters was founded in 2011 by siblings Nora and Owen Kessler, who began selling gear out of a converted garage in Missoula before relocating operations to Bozeman in 2016. The Ridgeline Trek 3 is manufactured in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, by supplier Vantage Textile Group, which has produced Bellstrand's packs since 2019. Each unit ships with a lifetime warranty and a 60-day return policy. Early reviewers on the Trailhead Weekly blog praised the pack's 4.2 kilogram weight and adjustable torso length, calling it "the best value pack under $200." The company reports that it sold over 12,000 units of the previous Ridgeline Trek 2 model since its 2022 release. Customers who purchase before December 1, 2024 will receive a free 2-liter hydration bladder, a $24.99 value. Bellstrand Outfitters competes directly with Cascadia Gear Co. and Northfork Supply in the mid-range backpacking segment. The product is currently in stock and ships from the company's distribution center in Billings, Montana within two business days.

THREAD: Cerne Robotics files for Chapter 11 in Delaware, 1/9

1) Cerne Robotics, the Pittsburgh-based warehouse-automation startup founded in 2016 by Priya Anand, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in Wilmington, Delaware on January 9, 2024. The company listed $42 million in liabilities against $11 million in assets.

2) Anand stepped down as CEO on January 8, 2024, one day before the filing, handing the role to CFO Marcus Ihlefeld. She'll stay on the board.

3) Cerne had raised $60 million from investors including Bellcrest Ventures and Tovar Capital since 2016. Its last big deal: a $9 million contract with Kroger signed in March 2023 to supply pallet-sorting robots.

4) Sources say the trouble started after a fire damaged Cerne's main assembly facility in Braddock, Pennsylvania on October 3, 2023, halting production for six weeks and delaying deliveries to Kroger and to Albertsons.

5) About 210 of Cerne's 340 employees were laid off on December 15, 2023. Remaining staff were told severance would be paid "as funds allow," according to an internal memo obtained by our reporter.

6) Ihlefeld met with creditors in Wilmington on January 11 to discuss a possible sale of assets. Rival firm Vantor Systems, run by CEO Diane Kessler, is reportedly circling Cerne's patents on robotic gripper design.

7) Anand, 41, told employees in a call that she "deeply regrets" the outcome. No criminal allegations have been made against her or the company.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Monday that the city of Rotterdam will receive 42 million euros to upgrade the Maasvlakte port facility, part of a broader infrastructure package unveiled by Minister Elke Vermeer. Speaking at a press conference in The Hague, Vermeer said the funds, allocated under the National Infrastructure Act, will be transferred to the Port of Rotterdam Authority by 15 March 2025. The upgrade will expand capacity for container vessels and reduce congestion along the A15 motorway corridor. Jan Boersma, chief executive of the Port of Rotterdam Authority, welcomed the announcement, noting that the authority had lobbied for the funding since 2022. "This investment secures nearly 3,000 jobs and strengthens our competitive position against the Port of Antwerp," Boersma said. The Ministry also confirmed that a separate 6 million euro grant will support research into hydrogen-powered cranes, conducted jointly with Delft University of Technology. Opposition lawmaker Femke de Groot criticized the plan during a parliamentary debate on Tuesday, arguing that rural provinces such as Groningen were being overlooked. Minister Vermeer rejected the criticism, stating that a further 10 million euros would be earmarked for regional rail projects in Groningen by the end of 2025. The full infrastructure package, worth 180 million euros in total, must still be approved by the Dutch Senate before funds can be disbursed.

MANCHESTER, England -- October 14, 2023. Manchester City edged Liverpool 2-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, with a stoppage-time header from Erling Haaland sealing a dramatic win in front of 53,412 fans. Haaland, the Norwegian striker, rose above two defenders in the 91st minute to nod home a corner delivered by Kevin De Bruyne, sending the home crowd into raptures.

Liverpool had taken an early lead through Mohamed Salah, who converted a penalty in the 23rd minute after Rodri was penalized for a handball inside the box. City responded just before halftime when Bernardo Silva equalized with a low strike from the edge of the area.

Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola praised his team's resilience after the match. "We never stopped believing," Guardiola said during a press conference at the Etihad Stadium. Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp, speaking to reporters afterward, admitted his side had been "punished for small mistakes."

The victory moved Manchester City to the top of the Premier League table with 21 points, two ahead of Arsenal. Liverpool dropped to fourth place. Haaland has now scored 12 goals in 9 appearances this season, extending his lead in the race for the Golden Boot.

The two clubs will meet again on March 3, 2024, in the FA Cup quarterfinal, a fixture the Football Association confirmed earlier this week.

Cedar Ridge Foods, a packaged snacks maker headquartered in Council Bluffs, Iowa, agreed to acquire rival granola producer Harvest Bend Mills for $412 million in cash, the companies announced Tuesday. Under the deal, Cedar Ridge will pay $37.50 per share, a 22% premium over Harvest Bend's Monday closing price. The transaction, expected to close by January 15, 2025, still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Harvest Bend, based in Fargo, North Dakota, employs roughly 1,100 workers across three plants and generated $290 million in revenue last year. Cedar Ridge Chief Executive Officer Marisol Vance said the acquisition would expand the company's footprint in the Midwest and add Harvest Bend's oat-based product lines to its portfolio. "This combination strengthens our supply chain and gives us scale we could not build organically," Vance told analysts on a conference call from Cedar Ridge's headquarters. Harvest Bend founder and Chairman Dennis Okafor, who started the company in 1998, will join Cedar Ridge's board following the close of the deal. Shares of Harvest Bend jumped 18% to $36.90 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Cedar Ridge stock slipped 3% to $64.10. Analysts at Broadmoor Capital Partners, including senior analyst Priya Chandrasekar, said the deal values Harvest Bend at roughly 14 times projected 2025 earnings. Cedar Ridge financed the purchase through a combination of $250 million in new debt from JPMorgan Chase and existing cash reserves. The deal marks Cedar Ridge's third acquisition since 2020 and its largest to date.

input: MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 - Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as Villa defeated Fulham 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, extending their unbeaten home run to eight matches. Watkins opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Bernd Leno, then added a second in the 54th minute after a quick counterattack led by midfielder John McGinn. Fulham striker Raul Jimenez pulled one back in the 63rd minute, but Villa captain John McGinn sealed the win with a curling strike in the 81st minute. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, saying, "We controlled the tempo for long spells and deserved the three points." Fulham boss Marco Silva said his side lacked composure in the final third. The victory moved Aston Villa to third place in the Premier League table with 21 points from nine games, three points behind leaders Manchester City. Approximately 41,500 fans attended the fixture at Villa Park, one of the highest attendances of the season. Villa will next travel to face Arsenal at Emirates Stadium on October 21, while Fulham return to Craven Cottage to host Brighton. Earlier this month, Villa completed the signing of defender Pau Torres from Villarreal for a reported 33 million pounds, and Emery confirmed the Spaniard is close to full match fitness ahead of the busy fixture schedule.

Pixel Tab 3, the new Android tablet from Google, went on sale on September 12, 2024, at a starting price of $649. I bought the 256GB model in San Francisco and have spent three weeks testing it alongside an iPad Pro from Apple for comparison purposes.

The Pixel Tab 3 runs Android 15 and is powered by Google's Tensor G4 chip. Battery life is genuinely impressive: I got roughly 11 hours of mixed video playback and browsing, up from 8 hours on last year's Pixel Tab 2. The 11-inch OLED display is bright and color-accurate, and the included charging dock, which doubles as a smart speaker, is a clever touch that Apple has not replicated.

Google's hardware chief, Rick Osterloh, said at a press briefing in Mountain View on September 10 that the company sold over 2 million tablets in the Pixel line since 2023. That is a modest number next to Apple's iPad, which still dominates the category, but it shows Google is committed to the segment rather than treating it as an afterthought.

My main complaints are software-related: some Android apps still look stretched or poorly optimized for the larger screen, an issue reviewers have flagged since the original Pixel Tab launched in 2023. Samsung's Galaxy Tab S10, released a few months earlier, handles this better thanks to years of tablet-specific development.

Still, at $649, the Pixel Tab 3 is a strong value. If Google keeps refining the software, this could become a real competitor to the iPad within a couple of product cycles.

BOSTON, Massachusetts — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital reported on March 14, 2024 that a novel small-molecule compound, designated MGH-2201, significantly reduced tumor burden in patients with treatment-resistant glioblastoma. The Phase 2 trial, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez, enrolled 142 participants across seven sites, including Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and Cleveland Clinic, between June 2022 and September 2023. Patients receiving 150 milligrams of MGH-2201 twice daily showed a median progression-free survival of 9.3 months, compared to 4.1 months in the placebo group, a difference the authors called clinically meaningful. Approximately 38 percent of treated patients experienced grade 3 adverse events, most commonly neutropenia and fatigue, though no treatment-related deaths were recorded. Dr. Vasquez presented the findings at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting in Chicago on June 2, 2024, where the results drew praise from Dr. Raymond Okafor of Johns Hopkins University, who called the data "the most promising signal in glioblastoma therapeutics in a decade." The trial was funded by a $24 million grant from the National Cancer Institute and supported by Vertex Pharmaceuticals, which holds licensing rights to MGH-2201. Vertex has announced plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial in early 2025 pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Dr. Vasquez, who joined Massachusetts General Hospital in 2015 after completing her fellowship at Stanford University, said the team next intends to explore combination therapy with temozolomide. The study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine on March 14, 2024.

event: American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. HG-2024-091837

On March 11, 2024, Judge Patricia Nakamura sentenced Ryan Dolecek, 41, of Hayward, to 36 months in state prison after a jury in Oakland found him guilty of embezzlement from his former employer, Crescent Ridge Logistics Inc. Dolecek, who served as Chief Financial Officer at Crescent Ridge Logistics from January 2019 until his termination in September 2023, was charged by prosecutor Elena Vasquez of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office with diverting approximately $2.3 million in company funds into a shell account between 2021 and 2023.

During the trial, held at the René C. Davidson Courthouse, witnesses testified that Dolecek used falsified invoices to transfer $410,000 to a personal account in April 2022 alone. Crescent Ridge Logistics Inc., headquartered in San Leandro, California, and founded by Marcus Petrillo in 2008, reported the discrepancies to auditors in October 2023, triggering an internal investigation and Dolecek's subsequent arrest by Alameda County Sheriff's deputies on November 4, 2023.

Judge Nakamura ordered Dolecek to pay restitution of $2.1 million to Crescent Ridge Logistics and imposed a five-year probation term to follow his prison sentence. Defense attorney Marissa Feld stated her client intends to appeal the verdict. The company's current CEO, Naomi Whitfield, said in a statement that the firm has since implemented stricter financial controls.

organization: SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Denver-based Meridian Foods Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Blue Ridge Bakery, a regional bread and pastry maker headquartered in Asheville, North Carolina, for $142 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by January 15, 2025, will make Blue Ridge Bakery a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Foods.

CEO Laura Whitfield said the acquisition strengthens Meridian's position against competitor Golden Valley Foods in the premium bakery segment. "Blue Ridge Bakery's 38-year reputation for quality gives us immediate credibility in the Southeast," Whitfield told reporters during a press briefing in Charlotte.

Blue Ridge Bakery founder Thomas Nguyen, who started the company in 1986 with a single storefront, will step down as chief executive officer effective December 31, 2024, but will remain on the board as a senior advisor. His successor has not yet been named.

Meridian Foods, which employs roughly 4,200 people across 12 states, financed the transaction through a combination of $90 million in cash reserves and a $52 million loan from First Atlantic Bank. Shares of Meridian Foods rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.20.

Analysts at Sterling Capital Partners estimate the deal will boost Meridian's annual revenue by roughly $210 million. The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, though industry observers expect no major objections given the companies' limited market overlap.

Pixelbook Labs, a hardware startup based in Portland, Oregon, launched its first product on June 4, 2024: the Slate Air, a 12-inch tablet aimed at digital artists. Founder and CEO Marisol Vega unveiled the device at a press event held at the Oregon Convention Center, where roughly 300 attendees watched a live demo. Priced at $649, the Slate Air runs a custom version of Linux called PixelOS and ships with a pressure-sensitive stylus, the Slate Pen, sold separately for $79.

I've used the Slate Air for three weeks, and the hardware impresses more than I expected from a two-year-old company. The 2560x1600 OLED display renders color with striking accuracy, and the device's 10-hour battery life held up during long sketching sessions. Benchmarks show the Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 chip inside handles most creative apps without stutter, though Adobe has not yet optimized Photoshop for PixelOS, which limits the tablet's appeal to professionals.

Competitor Wacom, headquartered in Saitama, Japan, still dominates the pen-display market, and Apple's iPad Pro remains the default choice for many illustrators. Vega told reporters on June 5 that Pixelbook Labs plans to raise a Series B round later this year to expand manufacturing, currently handled by a supplier in Shenzhen, China. Until software support broadens, the Slate Air is a promising but niche device, best suited to early adopters willing to tolerate rough edges for genuinely excellent hardware.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Finally Gets the Basics Right

By Renata Alcala, San Jose, October 14, 2024

After two weeks wearing the Pixel Watch 3, I think Google has closed most of the gaps that plagued the original 2022 model. The 45mm review unit, priced at $399, was supplied by Google's hardware division based in Mountain View, California. Battery life now comfortably reaches 36 hours with the always-on display enabled, up from roughly 24 hours on the Pixel Watch 2.

The standout feature is the new Loss of Pulse Detection tool, developed with input from Dr. Anil Varma, a cardiologist at Stanford Health Care. Varma told me during a call on October 9 that the sensor accuracy "matches clinical-grade pulse oximeters in about 92 percent of test cases." Google says the feature will roll out via software update in November 2024 in the United States and Canada, pending final regulatory sign-off.

On the software side, Wear OS 5 feels noticeably snappier, and the new UI, credited to design lead Priya Nathan, borrows generously from the Pixel phone's Material You language. Battery drain from the always-on display, however, remains a minor annoyance, and the $399 starting price still trails the $329 Apple Watch SE 2 sold by Apple Inc.

Google, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc. headquartered in Mountain View, has clearly invested in health hardware since acquiring Fitbit in January 2021 for $2.1 billion. That acquisition's fingerprints are all over this watch's sensor suite. For most Android users, the Pixel Watch 3 is now a legitimate, if pricey, alternative to the Apple Watch.

Rating: 4 out of 5 stars.

The Ontario Ministry of Transportation announced on April 9, 2024 that it will invest $312 million to widen Highway 401 between Milton and Mississauga, a project expected to reduce congestion for roughly 420,000 daily commuters. Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria unveiled the plan at a press conference in Mississauga alongside Metrolinx CEO Phil Verster. "This corridor carries more traffic than any highway in North America," Sarkaria said, adding that construction crews from Aecon Group Inc. will begin work in June 2024 and finish by December 2027. The ministry stated that the expansion will add two express lanes in each direction and rebuild the interchange at Winston Churchill Boulevard. Local officials, including Mississauga Mayor Carolyn Parrish, welcomed the funding but urged the province to also address transit gaps along the Milton GO line. Environmental groups, led by the group Ecojustice, held a demonstration outside Queen's Park in Toronto on April 11, 2024 to protest the highway expansion, arguing it would increase emissions contrary to Ontario's Climate Change Action Plan. The Ministry of Transportation said an environmental assessment, completed in 2022, found the project compliant with the Environmental Assessment Act. Aecon Group Inc. was awarded the construction contract worth $312 million following a competitive bidding process that concluded in March 2024. The ministry expects the project to create approximately 2,800 construction jobs over the next three years.

The Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection (MassDEP) announced on June 12, 2024, that it will invest $45 million to modernize stormwater infrastructure across the city of Worcester. Commissioner Denise Cavanaugh unveiled the plan at a press briefing held at Worcester City Hall, describing it as the largest municipal water initiative in the department's history. Under the program, MassDEP will partner with the engineering firm Tetra Tech Inc. to replace 38 miles of aging pipelines by December 2026. Governor Maura Healey praised the initiative, stating that it would reduce flooding risks for roughly 12,000 households in low-lying neighborhoods. The funding, drawn from the state's Clean Water Trust Fund, will be disbursed in three installments, with the first payment of $15 million scheduled for July 1, 2024. Worcester Mayor Eric Batista said the project would create approximately 200 construction jobs over the next 18 months. Local resident groups, including the Union Hill Neighborhood Association, welcomed the announcement after years of lobbying MassDEP following repeated flooding events in 2021 and 2023. Cavanaugh added that MassDEP will also launch a public awareness campaign, in partnership with Clark University, to educate residents about water conservation. The agency expects to finalize contracts with Tetra Tech Inc. by September 2024 and begin construction in early 2025. Critics, including State Senator Robyn Kennedy, called for greater transparency in how the funds will be allocated across the 15 affected districts.

Pixel Fold 2 Review: Google's Second Attempt Gets It Right

By Marcus Chen, October 14, 2024

Google launched the Pixel Fold 2 on October 8, 2024, priced at $1,799, and after two weeks of testing in San Francisco, I can confirm it fixes nearly every complaint I had about the original. The device is manufactured by Google in partnership with supplier BOE Technology Group, which produces the 7.9-inch foldable OLED panel. Unlike the 2023 model, the new hinge, engineered by a team led by product manager Priya Ramamurthy, eliminates the visible crease almost entirely.

Under the hood sits the Tensor G4 chip, paired with 16GB of RAM and 256GB of storage. Battery life improved noticeably; I averaged 9 hours of screen-on time, up from 6.5 hours on the previous generation. The camera system, borrowed largely from the Pixel 9 Pro, performs well in low light around the Embarcadero at dusk.

Google, headquartered in Mountain View, California, faces stiff competition from Samsung, whose Galaxy Z Fold 6 remains the category leader with roughly 60% of the foldable market according to Counterpoint Research. Apple is reportedly developing its own foldable iPhone for a possible 2026 release, which would intensify competition further.

At Google's hardware event in New York on October 8, CEO Sundar Pichai called the Pixel Fold 2 "our most durable phone yet," citing an IPX8 water resistance rating and a titanium frame. My only real gripe is the $1,799 price tag, which puts it $200 above the Galaxy Z Fold 6.

Verdict: a genuinely excellent foldable, though still a luxury purchase rather than a mass-market one.

Pixelbook Labs, a Portland-based startup founded by Maren Kessler in 2019, launched its second-generation e-reader, the InkFrame 2, on October 14, 2024. Priced at $229, the InkFrame 2 features a 10.3-inch E Ink Carta 1300 display and 32 gigabytes of storage. I tested the device for three weeks in Seattle before writing this review.

Compared to the original InkFrame, released in 2021, the new model is noticeably faster. Page turns that once took nearly a second now register in about 200 milliseconds, thanks to a new processor supplied by Rockwell Semiconductor, a longtime component supplier based in Austin, Texas. Battery life is rated at six weeks with wireless off, and I got close to five weeks with moderate daily reading and Wi-Fi syncing enabled.

The software, however, is where Pixelbook Labs stumbles. The note-taking app crashed twice during my testing period, and syncing with Dropbox occasionally failed silently. A company spokesperson, Devon Ruiz, told me on October 20, 2024 that a firmware update addressing the crashes would arrive by November 2024.

Still, at $229, the InkFrame 2 undercuts Amazon's Kindle Oasis by roughly 50 dollars while offering comparable hardware. For readers frustrated with subscription-laden tablets, this is a refreshing, focused device. I'd recommend waiting for the promised firmware patch before buying, but the hardware itself earns a solid recommendation.

Pixelworks Labs, a hardware startup headquartered in Portland, Oregon, unveiled the Halo X1 tablet on June 4, 2024, and I have spent three weeks testing it. Founded in 2019 by engineer Marisol Vance, the company designed the Halo X1 to compete directly with Apple's iPad Air. At $499, the 11-inch device ships with a Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 chipset, 8GB of RAM, and a 10,000 mAh battery that lasted just under 14 hours in my video-playback test. The build quality feels premium, with a magnesium alloy frame, though the bundled stylus, sold separately for $79, occasionally lags during fast sketching in the included NoteFlow app. Software is where the Halo X1 stumbles: it runs a modified version of Android 14, and Pixelworks Labs has promised only two years of OS updates, compared to the five years Apple typically provides. Marisol Vance told reporters at a press briefing in San Jose on June 5 that a software patch addressing stylus latency would arrive by July 2024. Meanwhile, rival firm Contoso Devices, based in Austin, Texas, announced it had acquired the smaller display manufacturer Lumen Optics for $340 million on May 28, 2024, a move that could squeeze Pixelworks Labs' supply chain since both companies previously sourced panels from Lumen Optics. Despite the software limitations, the Halo X1's screen brightness of 900 nits and its surprisingly good speakers make it a strong budget alternative. I recommend it cautiously, mainly for users who don't mind slower update cycles.

The Ministry of Environment and Water Resources announced on 14 March 2024 that Singapore will invest 180 million dollars to upgrade flood defenses along the Bukit Timah Canal following severe flooding in December 2023. Minister Grace Fu confirmed the funding during a press briefing held at PUB headquarters in Bishan, alongside PUB Chief Executive Ng Joo Hee. The National Water Agency, PUB, will oversee construction, which is scheduled to begin on 1 June 2024 and conclude by 30 November 2026. Contractor Hyundai Engineering, a subsidiary of Hyundai Motor Group, was awarded the 95 million dollar construction tender after a competitive bidding process that also included Keppel Infrastructure. Minister Fu stated that the project will reduce flood risk for approximately 12,000 households in the Bukit Timah and Clementi areas. The announcement follows a similar initiative launched in Jakarta, where the Indonesian government partnered with the World Bank in 2022 to fund coastal barriers. Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong is expected to visit the canal site on 20 March 2024 to inspect preliminary works. Opposition Member of Parliament Leon Perera welcomed the investment but called for greater transparency regarding contractor selection. The Ministry emphasized that the project forms part of Singapore's broader climate resilience strategy, which allocates a total of 100 billion dollars over the next century to protect against rising sea levels.

Danville, Illinois-based farm equipment maker Halloran Agri Corp announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Petersen Grain Systems, a privately held grain-storage manufacturer based in Fargo, North Dakota, for $214 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by December 15, marks Halloran's third acquisition since 2021 and will expand its footprint in the Upper Midwest.

Chief Executive Officer Marion Delacroix said the acquisition of Petersen Grain Systems strengthens Halloran's position against rival Bergstrom Industrial, which controls roughly 28 percent of the North American grain-storage market. "This is a natural extension of our supply chain," Delacroix told reporters during a press briefing in Chicago.

Petersen Grain Systems was founded in 1978 by Wallace Petersen and has roughly 640 employees across three facilities in North Dakota and Minnesota. Under the terms of the agreement, Petersen's current president, Ingrid Solheim, will stay on as head of the newly formed Petersen division and report directly to Delacroix.

Halloran shares rose 4.3 percent to $87.60 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of Bergstrom Industrial slipped 1.1 percent. Analysts at Kestrel Capital Partners raised their price target on Halloran to $96, citing expected annual synergies of $18 million by 2026.

The transaction, first reported by Reuters, is subject to antitrust review by the Federal Trade Commission. Delacroix said Halloran expects regulatory approval within 90 days and does not anticipate divestitures.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., June 4, 2024 -- Vantor Biosciences Inc. announced today that it has acquired NeuraLume Therapeutics, a privately held biotech firm based in San Diego, for approximately 340 million dollars in cash and stock. The acquisition, finalized on June 3, 2024, adds NeuraLume's lead compound, VL-227, a small-molecule therapy for early-stage Parkinson's disease, to Vantor's neurology pipeline.

Under the terms of the deal, Vantor will pay NeuraLume shareholders 260 million dollars upfront and up to 80 million dollars in milestone payments tied to regulatory approvals. NeuraLume, founded in 2017 by Dr. Priya Anand, currently employs 45 people and will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Vantor, retaining its San Diego laboratory.

"This acquisition strengthens our commitment to treating neurodegenerative disease," said Marcus Webb, Chief Executive Officer of Vantor Biosciences, at a press briefing held at the company's Cambridge headquarters. "VL-227 has shown remarkable promise in Phase 2 trials."

Dr. Priya Anand, who will join Vantor as Senior Vice President of Neurology Research effective July 1, 2024, said she was proud of the team's progress since founding the company seven years ago.

Vantor Biosciences, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker VNTB. The company reported revenue of 1.2 billion dollars in fiscal year 2023 and employs approximately 3,800 people worldwide. Analysts at Morgan Stanley called the deal a strong strategic fit, noting that competitor Halden Pharmaceuticals had also reportedly bid for NeuraLume earlier this year.
