THREAD: Novara Robotics files for Chapter 11

1/ Big news out of Pittsburgh today. Novara Robotics, the warehouse-automation startup founded by Priya Desai in 2016, filed for bankruptcy protection this morning at the federal courthouse downtown.

2/ Novara had raised $42 million from investors including Cascade Ventures, but a botched expansion into Ohio and rising steel costs left it unable to pay suppliers like Kessler Manufacturing.

3/ CEO Priya Desai stepped down as chief executive officer on Tuesday, just two days before the filing. Board member Tomas Reyes will take over as interim CEO effective November 4, 2024.

4/ Sources say Novara owes roughly $6.3 million to Kessler Manufacturing alone. A Novara spokesperson said the company plans to sell its Pittsburgh facility to cover part of the debt.

5/ In a statement, Reyes said: "We are committed to protecting the 210 jobs at our Braddock plant while we restructure."

6/ Rival firm Atlas Logistics, based in Columbus, Ohio, has reportedly approached Novara about acquiring its remaining patents for an undisclosed sum.

7/ Desai told reporters she still believes in the technology: "I built this company from a garage in Squirrel Hill. It's not the end."

8/ Analysts at Meridian Capital expect a decision on the asset sale by January 15, 2025. More updates as this develops.

MERIDIAN CHEMICALS TO ACQUIRE RIVERTON POLYMERS FOR $410 MILLION

CLEVELAND, Ohio -- Meridian Chemicals Inc. announced Tuesday that it will acquire Riverton Polymers LLC in a deal worth $410 million, marking the company's largest acquisition since its founding in 1987. The agreement was signed at Meridian's headquarters in Cleveland by Chief Executive Officer Laura Bennett and Riverton's founder, Marcus Feld.

Under the terms of the deal, Meridian will pay $410 million in cash for Riverton Polymers, a specialty plastics manufacturer based in Akron, Ohio, that employs roughly 620 workers. The transaction is expected to close by November 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission.

"This acquisition strengthens our position in the automotive supply chain," Bennett said during a press conference at Meridian's Cleveland facility on Tuesday afternoon. Riverton currently supplies polymer components to Ford Motor Company and General Motors.

Feld, who launched Riverton Polymers in 2003, will join Meridian's board of directors as part of the agreement. He is expected to start his new role on December 1, 2024.

Analysts at Sterling Capital Partners estimate the merger could increase Meridian's annual revenue by 18 percent. Shares of Meridian Chemicals rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $74.20.

The deal still requires approval from Riverton's minority shareholders, who will vote on the proposal at a meeting scheduled for October 30, 2024, in Akron.

Bergen Outdoor Supply, headquartered in Bend, Oregon, is now shipping the TrailForge 45L Backpack, a rugged pack engineered for multi-day alpine trekking. Launched on March 12, 2024, the TrailForge 45L retails for $189.99 and is currently in stock as a brand-new item. Designed by lead engineer Marisol Vance, the pack features a ripstop nylon shell, an aluminum internal frame, and a hydration bladder compartment that holds up to 3 liters. Bergen Outdoor Supply was founded in 2011 by former mountaineer Tomas Ridley, who remains the company's Chief Executive Officer. The TrailForge line has become a direct competitor to Black Canyon Gear's popular Summit 40 pack, though reviewers at Trailhead Monthly magazine noted the TrailForge's superior weight distribution in a review published on April 2, 2024. Each backpack ships from the company's distribution center in Boise, Idaho, and typically arrives within 5 business days. Customers who purchase before June 30, 2024 will receive a free rain cover valued at $24.00. The pack is available in three colors: Slate Gray, Forest Green, and Rust Orange, and comes with a 2-year manufacturer warranty. Over 3,200 units have been sold since launch, according to a statement from Bergen Outdoor Supply's marketing director, Priya Chandran. "We built the TrailForge for people who actually live outdoors," Chandran said during an interview at the Outdoor Retailer Summer Market trade show in Denver, Colorado on June 5, 2024. Bergen Outdoor Supply also confirmed plans to open a new flagship store in Seattle, Washington later this year.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Press Statement — 14 March 2024

The Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure today announced that the Port of Halden Bay expansion project will proceed following approval from the National Infrastructure Board in Canberra. Minister Ellen Marsdale confirmed that AUD 420 million will be allocated to the project, with construction beginning on 3 June 2024 and completion expected by December 2026.

The funding will be disbursed by the Treasury Department to Halden Bay Port Authority in three installments over the next 30 months. The first tranche of AUD 140 million is scheduled for release on 1 July 2024. Contractor Bremner Civil Works, headquartered in Adelaide, was selected following a competitive tender process that concluded last month.

Speaking at a press conference in Canberra, Minister Marsdale stated, "This investment will create approximately 1,200 jobs and increase container throughput by 35 percent by 2027." She was joined by Deputy Secretary Owen Fairweather, who will oversee compliance with the new Maritime Infrastructure Safety Act.

The National Infrastructure Board, led by Chairwoman Priya Nathan, will review progress quarterly. Local residents held a demonstration outside Parliament House on 12 March 2024, protesting potential environmental impacts on the nearby Halden Wetlands Reserve. The Ministry has committed to an independent environmental audit before construction begins.

input: The Ontario Ministry of Transportation announced on May 14, 2024, that it will invest 128 million dollars to upgrade Highway 401 between Milton and Mississauga, citing chronic congestion that costs commuters an estimated 45 minutes daily. Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria confirmed the funding at a press conference held at the Milton Operations Centre, alongside Mayor Zeeshan Hamid of Milton and Metrolinx CEO Phil Verster. The project, awarded to contractor Aecon Group Inc., will add two express lanes in each direction and is scheduled for completion by December 2027. Sarkaria stated that the expansion follows a 2023 traffic study showing a 22 percent increase in freight volume through the corridor since 2019. The Ministry also confirmed that construction crews will begin mobilizing equipment on June 3, 2024, with lane closures expected overnight only to minimize disruption. Approximately 340 workers employed by Aecon will be deployed across four work zones. Opposition critic Marit Stiles questioned the timeline during a legislative session in Toronto on May 16, 2024, arguing that similar projects along Highway 407 were delayed by more than a year. The Ministry responded that lessons from that delay, attributed partly to supply shortages of asphalt binder, have been incorporated into the new contract terms. Residents of Milton have been invited to a public information session on May 30, 2024, at the Milton Centre for the Arts to review construction schedules and noise mitigation plans.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as Villa defeated Fulham 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, moving the club into fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Bernd Leno, then doubled his tally in the 58th minute after a swift counterattack led by midfielder Douglas Luiz. Fulham briefly leveled through a penalty from Andreas Pereira in the 63rd minute, but substitute Leon Bailey restored Villa's lead in the 79th minute with a curling shot from 20 yards. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, saying the win showed "real maturity" against a well-organized Fulham side coached by Marco Silva. The victory extended Aston Villa's unbeaten home run to eight matches, a club record since the 2019-20 season. Approximately 41,500 fans attended the match at Villa Park, generating an estimated £2.1 million in matchday revenue for the club, according to a statement released by Aston Villa's commercial department on Monday. Villa will next travel to face Tottenham Hotspur on October 21 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, a fixture that could push them into the Champions League qualification spots. Meanwhile, Fulham, who dropped to 11th place, will host Chelsea on October 22 at Craven Cottage as they look to bounce back under Silva's guidance.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side defeated Newcastle United 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, moving Villa into fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute, converting a low cross from midfielder John McGinn, before doubling his tally just before halftime with a header from a corner. Newcastle striker Alexander Isak pulled one back in the 58th minute, but substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win with a curling effort in the 81st minute. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, telling reporters at a press conference, "We controlled the game for long periods, and Ollie's movement was outstanding today." Newcastle boss Eddie Howe, appointed to the role in November 2021, admitted his team struggled defensively in the opening half. The victory extended Aston Villa's unbeaten home run to eight matches and lifted the club above Tottenham Hotspur on goal difference. Villa Park, which holds approximately 42,000 spectators, recorded an attendance of 41,832 for the fixture. Aston Villa will next travel to face Arsenal at Emirates Stadium on October 21, while Newcastle United host Crystal Palace at St James' Park three days later. The result marked Emery's fifteenth win since taking charge at Villa in November 2022, further strengthening his reputation as one of the Premier League's most effective coaches this season.

MERIDIAN FALLS, Ohio — Blackstone Robotics Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $42 million in unpaid supplier debts and a collapsed acquisition deal, according to court filings submitted in Cleveland. The company, headquartered in Meridian Falls since its founding in 2014 by engineer Dana Whitfield, laid off 310 employees the same day. CEO Marcus Reyner, who took over as chief executive in March 2021, told reporters at a press conference that talks with rival firm Talon Automation Corp. to acquire Blackstone's assembly division had fallen through the previous week. "We simply ran out of runway," Reyner said outside the company's headquarters on Foundry Street. Talon Automation, based in Columbus, had offered $18 million for the division but withdrew after an internal audit flagged irregularities in Blackstone's 2023 financial statements. Judge Ellen Marsh of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Ohio is scheduled to hold an initial hearing on October 9 to review the restructuring plan. Whitfield, who stepped down as chairman in 2022, said in a phone interview that she was "devastated but not surprised," pointing to years of declining orders from automotive clients. Blackstone's shares, once valued near $30 a share on private markets, are now considered worthless by analysts at Fenwick Capital Partners. Local officials in Meridian Falls estimate the closure will cost the region roughly $9 million in annual tax revenue.

organization: U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Ohio

MERIDIAN FALLS, Ohio, Nov. 14 -- Danfield Robotics Inc. announced Thursday it has acquired local competitor Voss Automation LLC for $42 million in cash, a deal expected to close by Dec. 20. The acquisition, disclosed at a press briefing at Danfield's Meridian Falls headquarters, will bring Voss Automation's 130 employees under the Danfield umbrella, including its founder and chief executive, Renata Voss.

"This merger strengthens our supply chain and doubles our manufacturing footprint in the Midwest," said Danfield CEO Owen Kessler, who founded the company in 2011. Kessler added that Renata Voss will join Danfield as Executive Vice President of Operations starting Jan. 5, 2025.

Voss Automation, headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, has supplied precision robotic arms to automakers including Falcon Motors for the past six years. Analysts at Kessler's rival Bramwell Robotics called the deal a direct threat to their market share in industrial automation.

The transaction, financed partly through a $15 million loan from Great Lakes Capital Bank, still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission. A spokesperson for the FTC, Marisol Trent, said the agency expects to complete its review within 60 days.

Shares of Danfield Robotics, traded publicly since 2019, rose 8 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement. Voss said in a statement, "I'm proud of what we built, and I'm confident this partnership will accelerate our technology."

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solace Robotics announced this morning that it has acquired Pemberton Sensing for $42 million in cash. The deal closed Tuesday, June 4th, 2024.

2/ Solace CEO Priya Nathwani said the acquisition will fold Pemberton's lidar tech directly into Solace's warehouse robots. Pemberton founder Colin Reyes will join Solace as VP of Hardware starting July 1st.

3/ Pemberton Sensing was founded in 2018 by Reyes out of a garage in Round Rock, Texas. The company had just 34 employees but held 12 patents in short-range lidar.

4/ Solace Robotics, headquartered in Austin, Texas, currently supplies automation systems to logistics giant Farrow & Kane, which operates 6 distribution centers across the Midwest.

5/ Nathwani told reporters at a press briefing at the Driskill Hotel that Solace expects revenue to grow 18 percent by Q1 2025 because of the deal. She declined to comment on layoffs.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google's Refined Wearable Finally Gets It Right

By Renee Castillo, September 12, 2024

Google launched the Pixel Watch 3 on September 10, 2024, at a press event in Mountain View, California, and after two weeks of testing, I'm convinced it's the company's most polished wearable yet. The new Loss of Pulse Detection feature, developed with input from cardiologist Dr. Amara Okafor of Johns Hopkins Hospital, worked reliably during a simulated test, though I hope I never need it for real.

Google's Rick Osterloh, senior vice president of devices and services, said in a briefing that the Pixel Watch 3 represents "the biggest leap in Fitbit-powered coaching we've shipped." Fitbit, which Google acquired in 2021 for $2.1 billion, now powers nearly every metric on the watch, from readiness scores to running form analysis.

My only real complaint is storage: 32GB feels stingy compared to the Apple Watch Series 9, its clearest competitor. Still, at under $350, the Pixel Watch 3 undercuts Apple by roughly $50 while matching most of its health features.

Verdict: 4.5 out of 5 stars. Recommended for Android users who want serious health tracking without switching ecosystems.

Ingrid Halvorsen (born 14 March 1957 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her studies of cold-water coral reefs in the North Atlantic. She earned a doctorate in oceanography from the University of Bergen in 1984 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø the same year as a research scientist. In 1996 Halvorsen was appointed Director of the Institute's Deep Sea Ecology Division, a position she held for eleven years. Her 1999 expedition aboard the research vessel Nordkapp documented previously unmapped Lophelia pertusa reefs off the coast of Trøndelag, work later cited in the founding charter of the Sula Reef Marine Protected Area, established in 2003. Halvorsen left the Institute of Marine Research in 2007 to become a professor at the University of Bergen, where she still teaches marine ecology. In 2011 she received the Fridtjof Nansen Award for Environmental Research from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo, recognizing three decades of coral conservation research. She married fellow biologist Erik Solheim in 1985, and the couple's daughter, Maren Solheim, was born in Tromsø in 1988 and later became a marine policy advisor for the European Commission. Halvorsen has published more than 70 peer-reviewed papers and served on the advisory board of the International Coral Reef Society from 2005 to 2015. She currently resides in Bergen.

Pixelbook Labs, a small hardware startup based in Austin, Texas, launched the Fenwick S2 wireless earbuds on October 14, 2024, and after three weeks of daily use, I have mixed feelings. Founded in 2021 by former Dell engineer Priya Ramaswamy, Pixelbook Labs positioned the $179 earbuds as a rival to the Sony WF-1000XM5 and Apple's AirPods Pro 2. The Fenwick S2 delivers genuinely impressive noise cancellation, rated at 38 decibels of attenuation, and battery life stretches to 9 hours per charge, roughly 20 percent longer than the Sony model. Bluetooth 5.3 connectivity felt stable throughout my testing in Austin and during a trip to Chicago.

However, the companion app, built on a proprietary protocol called FenLink, crashed twice on my Samsung Galaxy S23 and once on an iPhone 14. Customer support, reached via email, took four days to respond. Priya Ramaswamy told Wired magazine on October 20, 2024, that a software patch would arrive by November 5, 2024, though as of this writing the update has not appeared.

At $179, the Fenwick S2 competes directly with Sony and Bose, yet lacks the polish of either. The hardware shows real promise, with a comfortable ergonomic fit and surprisingly rich bass response, but the software feels unfinished. Pixelbook Labs still has an opportunity here, particularly given its price advantage of nearly $130 under Bose's flagship QuietComfort Ultra. For now, I would recommend waiting for the promised update before buying, unless aggressive noise cancellation at a low price is your only priority.

Mireille Auclair (born 4 March 1948 in Lyon, France) was a French biochemist best known for her pioneering work on insulin synthesis. She earned her doctorate at the Sorbonne in 1973 and joined the Pasteur Institute in Paris as a research fellow the same year. In 1981 Auclair became Director of Molecular Biology at the Pasteur Institute, a position she held for nineteen years. Her laboratory's 1987 discovery of a synthetic pathway for recombinant insulin, published in the journal Nature, was later licensed by the pharmaceutical company Sanofi for 42 million francs in 1989. Auclair was elected to the French Academy of Sciences in 1994 and received the Louis Pasteur Medal from the Pasteur Institute in Paris in 1996. She stepped down from her directorship in 2000 to become a scientific advisor to the World Health Organization in Geneva. Auclair married fellow biochemist Jean-Marc Fournier in 1975; the couple had two children, Claire and Thomas Fournier. She died on 12 September 2015 in Paris at the age of 67 after a long illness. In her honor, the University of Lyon established the Mireille Auclair Fellowship in 2016 to support young women entering biochemistry research.

2/ Solstice CEO Naomi Ferris said the acquisition will let the company ship its new AutoCart-9 pallet robot with in-house sensors by Q3. "We've been buying LIDAR from three suppliers for two years. Now we control our own roadmap," Ferris told employees at the Austin headquarters.

3/ Pemberton founder Raj Malhotra, who started the company in 2016 with his sister Anjali Malhotra, will join Solstice as VP of Sensing. Anjali is staying on as an independent consultant. Both were present at the announcement event held at Solstice's East 6th Street facility.

4/ Reaction from competitor Vantage Autonomy was blunt. Spokesperson Derek Olsen called the deal "a defensive move" and noted Vantage shipped 1,200 warehouse robots last quarter alone.

5/ Solstice's stock-equivalent valuation (it's still private) reportedly rose 18 percent among existing investors after the news, according to a memo seen by Reuters reporter Lianne Cho.

6/ Ferris will present the integrated AutoCart-9 at the Modex Supply Chain Expo in Atlanta on April 9, 2024. Analysts expect at least 40 companies to attend.

Bergstrom Outdoors is proud to launch the TrailForge X2 hiking backpack, now available for $189.99 through the company's online store. Designed in Bozeman, Montana, and manufactured in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, the TrailForge X2 features a 65-liter capacity, a reinforced aluminum frame, and a lifetime warranty against manufacturing defects. Bergstrom Outdoors was founded in 2011 by Anders Bergstrom, a former mountaineering guide who wanted to create gear tough enough for the Rocky Mountains yet light enough for weekend trips. The company, headquartered in Bozeman, sold over 40,000 units of its previous flagship, the TrailForge X1, since its release in September 2019. This new model was unveiled on March 14, 2024, at the Outdoor Retailer trade show in Denver, Colorado, where it won the Best New Gear award from the Outdoor Industry Association. Customers who order before April 30, 2024 will receive a complimentary rain cover worth $24.99. The backpack comes in three colorways: Slate Gray, Forest Green, and Rust Orange. Each unit weighs approximately 2.1 kilograms and includes a hydration bladder compartment compatible with most 3-liter reservoirs. Early reviewers, including Outside Magazine, praised the TrailForge X2's hip belt padding and adjustable torso length, ranging from 16 to 22 inches. Bergstrom Outdoors currently competes directly with Patagonia and Osprey Packs in the premium backpack segment. Orders ship from the company's distribution center in Salt Lake City, Utah, within three business days.

DETROIT, Oct 9 - Ferrous Dynamics Inc, a mid-sized auto-parts supplier based in Warren, Michigan, announced Wednesday it has acquired Bellhaven Tooling Corp, a Toledo, Ohio-based maker of stamping dies, for $142 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by December 15, will make Bellhaven a wholly owned subsidiary of Ferrous Dynamics, expanding its footprint in the Midwest tooling market.

CEO Marcus Reyes said the acquisition strengthens Ferrous Dynamics' position as a supplier to General Motors and Stellantis, both of which rely on Bellhaven's dies for body panel production. "This is about scale and speed," Reyes told reporters during a press briefing at the company's Warren headquarters. "Bellhaven gives us capacity we simply didn't have."

Bellhaven's founder, Diane Kowalski, will step down as president effective November 1 after 27 years leading the firm, though she will remain as a board advisor. Her successor, Paul Ostrowski, previously an operations director at Magna International, will join Ferrous Dynamics as Executive Vice President of Manufacturing on November 1.

Ferrous Dynamics financed the purchase through a $90 million term loan from Comerica Bank and existing cash reserves. Shares of Ferrous Dynamics, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker FRDY, rose 6.3 percent to $34.10 following the announcement. Analysts at Baird noted the deal could add roughly $28 million in annual revenue starting in fiscal year 2025.

The transaction is subject to standard regulatory review and is not expected to trigger antitrust concerns given the fragmented nature of the tooling sector.

Danvers Chemical Corp. Files for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy After Plant Explosion

DANVERS, Ohio, March 14 — Danvers Chemical Corp. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Thursday, less than two weeks after an explosion at its manufacturing plant killed three workers and injured eleven others. The blast occurred on March 2 at the company's facility on Route 9, when a tank containing anhydrous ammonia ruptured during a routine maintenance procedure.

CEO Marisol Ferrante announced the filing in a statement released from the company's headquarters in Danvers, Ohio, saying the firm owed more than $42 million to creditors, including supplier Blackstone Polymers LLC. "We are committed to compensating the families affected by this tragedy," Ferrante said.

The Occupational Safety and Health Administration launched an investigation on March 3 and cited the company for eight safety violations. OSHA regional director Thomas Whitfield said inspectors found that emergency shutoff valves had not been tested since 2021.

Among the deceased were plant operator Raymond Cole, 47, and technicians Denise Ochoa and Frank Bellamy. Families of the victims have retained attorney Susan Marchetti, who said she plans to file a wrongful-death lawsuit against Danvers Chemical Corp. within thirty days.

Danvers Chemical Corp., founded in 1978, employs roughly 620 people and supplies chemicals to agricultural firms across the Midwest. Trading in its parent company, Heartland Industrial Holdings, was halted briefly on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024 — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating darolutinib, an experimental oral therapy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez and published in The Lancet Oncology, enrolled 214 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between January 2022 and September 2023. Participants receiving darolutinib in combination with standard androgen deprivation therapy showed a median progression-free survival of 19.8 months, compared with 11.3 months in the placebo arm, representing a 42 percent reduction in disease progression risk. Grade 3 or higher adverse events, primarily fatigue and hypertension, occurred in 27 percent of treated patients. Dr. Vasquez presented the findings at the American Urological Association annual meeting in San Antonio on May 3, 2024. Novaris Therapeutics, the Cambridge-based biotechnology company that developed darolutinib, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. Novaris was founded in 2015 by former Pfizer executive Richard Kwan and has raised $340 million in venture funding to date. Company spokesperson Maria Torres stated that a confirmatory Phase 3 trial, involving approximately 600 patients, will begin enrollment in Toronto and Chicago this summer. Analysts at Jefferies Group estimate peak annual sales for darolutinib could reach $1.2 billion if approved. Independent oncologist Dr. Samuel Okafor of the Mayo Clinic called the results "a meaningful advance" but cautioned that longer follow-up is needed to confirm overall survival benefit.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Sharpens Its Wearable Ambitions

Mountain View, October 14, 2024 -- Google officially launched the Pixel Watch 3 last week, and after six days of testing, it's clear the company has addressed most complaints leveled at the original Pixel Watch back in 2022. The new model, priced at $349 for the 41mm variant and $399 for the 45mm version, ships with a brighter 2,000-nit LTPO OLED display and a Snapdragon W5 chip supplied by Qualcomm.

I tested the 45mm unit in Matte Black, paired with a Pixel 9 Pro purchased at a Best Buy store in San Jose. Battery life improved noticeably, lasting roughly 36 hours with the always-on display enabled, up from about 24 hours on the previous generation. Fitbit, the Google subsidiary that supplies much of the health-tracking software, added a new Loss of Pulse Detection feature that can alert emergency contacts within 30 seconds of detecting a cardiac event.

Rick Osterloh, Google's Senior Vice President of Devices and Services, said during the September 10 launch event in Mountain View that the Pixel Watch line has now sold over 3 million units worldwide. Competing directly with the Apple Watch Series 10 and Samsung's Galaxy Watch 7, the Pixel Watch 3 undercuts Apple's pricing by roughly $50 while offering comparable fitness metrics.

My main complaint remains third-party app support, which still lags behind watchOS. Still, for $349, this is the most polished wearable Google has ever shipped, and I recommend it to any Android user considering an upgrade.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital reported promising results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tebafloxamab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotechnology firm Alderon Therapeutics for the treatment of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis. The trial, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti, enrolled 214 adult patients across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants received either 300 milligrams of tebafloxamab administered intravenously every four weeks or a placebo. After 52 weeks, patients receiving tebafloxamab showed a 47 percent reduction in annualized relapse rate compared with placebo, and 68 percent achieved no evidence of disease activity, versus 31 percent in the control group. The most common adverse events were mild infusion-related reactions, reported in 12 percent of treated patients, and nasopharyngitis. No cases of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy were observed. Dr. Marchetti presented the findings on March 14, 2024, at the American Academy of Neurology annual meeting in Denver, Colorado. Alderon Therapeutics' chief executive officer, Raj Patel, said the company plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial by early 2025 and will seek Breakthrough Therapy designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The study was funded by a $22 million grant from the National Multiple Sclerosis Society and co-sponsored by Alderon Therapeutics. Independent commentary from Dr. Hiroshi Tanaka of the Karolinska Institute described the results as "a meaningful step forward" for patients with limited treatment options. Full trial data will be published in The Lancet Neurology later this year.

The Ministry of Transportation of Ontario announced on June 4, 2024, that it will invest CAD 82 million to widen Highway 7 between Kitchener and Guelph, a project expected to reduce commute times by 18 percent. Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria said the funding, allocated through the Building Highways Fund, will support construction from September 2024 through November 2026. The contract was awarded to Aecon Group Inc., a Toronto-based infrastructure firm, following a competitive bidding process that concluded last month. Aecon's chief executive, John Beck, said the company would begin mobilizing crews at the Highway 7 corridor near Breslau within three weeks. Pixel Tablet Redux: Google's Halo Dock Finally Makes Sense

By Marisol Aguirre, Senior Reviewer, Gadgetline Weekly

MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif., March 4, 2024 -- After two weeks of daily use, I'm convinced the Pixel Tablet, paired with its optional $129 Halo Dock, is the most compelling Android tablet Google has shipped since the ill-fated Pixel C in 2015. Google announced the second-generation Halo Dock at a small press event on February 27, 2024, held at the company's Mountain View campus, where product lead Devon Ashworth demonstrated the accessory's improved Qi2 charging coil and new Nest Hub-style ambient display mode.

The tablet itself starts at $499 for the 128GB model, a $20 increase over last year's price, and is manufactured by Foxconn at a facility in Longtan, Taiwan. Under the hood sits a Tensor G3 chip, the same silicon found in the Pixel 8 Pro, delivering roughly 15 percent faster multi-core performance than its predecessor according to Google's own benchmarks.

Competitively, the Pixel Tablet still trails Apple's iPad in raw app polish, but it beats Samsung's Galaxy Tab S9 on price. I tested the unit alongside a Lenovo Tab P12 borrowed from a colleague, and the Pixel's speaker array, tuned in partnership with audio engineer Priya Chandrasekaran, was noticeably richer.

One caveat: Google has a spotty history with tablets, and I'd wait for a software update cadence before recommending this to enterprise buyers. Still, for $499, this is the first Pixel tablet I'd actually tell a friend to buy.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF ARIZONA, MARICOPA COUNTY

Case No. CR2024-041882

On March 14, 2024, Judge Elena Ruiz sentenced Marcus Delaney, 37, to 5 years in state prison after a jury in Phoenix, Arizona found him guilty of aggravated assault stemming from an incident at the Desert Ridge Marketplace on July 9, 2023. Prosecutor Angela Whitfield of the Maricopa County Attorney's Office argued that Delaney struck victim Roberto Salinas with a metal baseball bat during a dispute in the parking lot, leaving Salinas with a fractured skull. Salinas was hospitalized at Banner Desert Medical Center for eleven days.

Delaney was arrested on July 10, 2023 by Phoenix Police Department officers following a tip from a witness who recorded the altercation on a cell phone. He was indicted on charges of aggravated assault and unlawful use of a weapon on September 2, 2023, before Judge Ruiz at the Maricopa County Superior Court.

During the trial, which began on February 5, 2024, defense attorney Craig Osmond contended that Delaney acted in self-defense after Salinas allegedly threatened him with a knife. The jury deliberated for six hours before returning a guilty verdict on March 1, 2024.

In addition to the prison term, Judge Ruiz ordered Delaney to pay $42,000 in restitution to Salinas for medical expenses. Delaney's attorney has stated he intends to file an appeal with the Arizona Court of Appeals within 30 days.

input: MADRID, June 14 — Real Sociedad striker Mikel Oyarzabal scored twice as Spain edged Croatia 2-1 in a friendly at Estadio Reale Arena on Friday night, boosting confidence ahead of next month's UEFA Nations League finals. Oyarzabal netted in the 23rd minute after a low cross from Nico Williams, then added a second in the 67th minute with a header from a corner kick taken by Dani Olmo. Croatia's Andrej Kramaric pulled one back in the 81st minute, but Spain held on for the win in front of 32,000 fans. Head coach Luis de la Fuente praised his squad's discipline, telling reporters after the match, "We controlled the tempo for long stretches and showed maturity against a tough opponent." Croatia manager Zlatko Dalic said his team lacked sharpness in the final third. The victory was Spain's fourth in a row and extended their unbeaten run to 14 matches. Spain will now travel to Porto on June 18 to face Portugal in another warm-up fixture before the Nations League semifinal against France on June 22 in Munich. Oyarzabal, who joined Real Sociedad's youth academy at age 12, has now scored 18 goals in 62 appearances for the national team. The Spanish Football Federation confirmed that captain Alvaro Morata, sidelined since May 30 with a hamstring injury, is expected to rejoin training in Las Rozas next week. Ticket sales for the France match reportedly exceeded 60,000 within two days of going on sale.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. RG24-118732

On March 14, 2024, Judge Marion T. Whitfield sentenced Defendant Carlos R. Delgado, 41, of Oakland, California, to 36 months in state prison following his conviction for embezzlement in connection with funds taken from Bayview Logistics Inc., a freight company headquartered in Oakland where Delgado worked as a payroll administrator. Prosecutor Elena Faust of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Delgado diverted approximately $412,000 between January 2021 and September 2023 into a personal account at Cascade Union Bank.

The charges, filed on November 2, 2023, alleged violations of California Penal Code Section 503. Delgado was arrested on November 9, 2023, by detectives from the Oakland Police Department at his residence on 14th Street. During the trial hearing held at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland on February 5, 2024, defense attorney Priya Nandakumar argued her client suffered from severe gambling addiction, presenting testimony from Dr. Samuel Ochoa, a psychiatrist retained by the defense.

Judge Whitfield ordered Delgado to pay restitution of $412,000 to Bayview Logistics Inc. and noted the sentence reflected both the scale of the theft and Delgado's lack of prior criminal record. Bayview Logistics Inc., founded in 1998 by Harold Bayview, has not commented publicly on the case. Company spokesperson Renata Cole confirmed internal controls have since been revised.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., March 4, 2024 -- Arden Biotherapeutics, Inc. announced today that it has acquired NovaCell Diagnostics for $340 million in a cash-and-stock transaction expected to close on April 15, 2024. The acquisition strengthens Arden's oncology pipeline by adding NovaCell's proprietary liquid-biopsy platform, ClarityScan, which detects circulating tumor DNA with 94 percent sensitivity in early-stage colorectal cancer.

Under the terms of the agreement, Arden will pay $210 million in cash and issue 3.2 million shares of common stock to NovaCell shareholders. NovaCell, founded in 2016 by Dr. Priya Anand in San Diego, California, employs 85 people and has raised $62 million in venture funding to date.

"This acquisition accelerates our mission to bring earlier cancer detection to patients everywhere," said Marcus Feldman, Chief Executive Officer of Arden Biotherapeutics. "NovaCell's technology, combined with our clinical network, positions us to file for FDA clearance by the third quarter of 2025."

Dr. Anand will join Arden as Chief Scientific Officer, effective April 15, 2024, reporting directly to Feldman. NovaCell's Boston satellite office will remain operational, while its San Diego headquarters will be integrated into Arden's existing facility in Cambridge over the following six months.

Arden Biotherapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, was founded in 2011 and currently employs more than 400 people across three countries. The company's shares trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker ARDX. Analysts at Jefferies raised their price target on Arden to $58 following the announcement.

SUPERIOR COURT OF SANTA CLARA COUNTY — Judge Marion Estrada sentenced Daniel Whitfield, 41, to 27 months in federal prison on Tuesday after he pleaded guilty to wire fraud involving Meridian Capital Partners, a San Jose-based investment firm. Prosecutor Angela Ruiz told the court that Whitfield, formerly a Senior Portfolio Manager at Meridian Capital Partners, diverted $1.4 million from client accounts between March 2021 and August 2022 to fund personal real estate purchases in Lake Tahoe. Whitfield was arrested by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation on November 3, 2022, at his home in Los Gatos, California, after a whistleblower complaint filed by former colleague Priya Nandakumar triggered an internal audit. The indictment, filed in December 2022 by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of California, charged Whitfield with six counts of wire fraud and one count of money laundering. During Tuesday's hearing at the San Jose federal courthouse, Judge Estrada also ordered Whitfield to pay $1.4 million in restitution to Meridian Capital Partners within five years. Defense attorney Carl Osei argued for leniency, citing Whitfield's cooperation with investigators and lack of prior criminal history, but Judge Estrada rejected the request, stating that the breach of client trust warranted a custodial sentence. Meridian Capital Partners, founded in 2009 by Howard Lindqvist, has since implemented new compliance protocols and hired a Chief Compliance Officer, Rebecca Tran, to prevent future incidents. The firm manages approximately $3.2 billion in assets for institutional clients across California and Nevada.

input: The Ministry of Transportation of Ontario announced on Tuesday, June 11, 2024, that it will allocate CAD 42 million to repair the Gardiner Expressway in Toronto following a structural inspection completed last month. Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria said the funding, drawn from the Provincial Infrastructure Fund, will cover repairs to three overpasses damaged after a delivery truck struck a support column near Spadina Avenue on May 3, killing one pedestrian and injuring four others. The victim, identified as 58-year-old construction worker Daniel Whitmore, died at St. Michael's Hospital two days after the crash. Ontario Provincial Police arrested the truck's driver, Marek Nowicki, on May 5 on charges of dangerous driving causing death. Nowicki is scheduled to appear before Justice Elaine Cho at the Ontario Court of Justice in Toronto on July 22 for a preliminary hearing. Premier Doug Ford, speaking alongside Sarkaria at a press conference in Toronto, said the repair project would be carried out by Aecon Group Inc., a construction firm headquartered in Toronto, with work beginning August 1 and expected to conclude by December 15, 2024. "Safety on the Gardiner is non-negotiable," Ford said. The ministry also confirmed that a separate contract worth CAD 6.5 million was awarded to WSP Canada for ongoing structural monitoring of the expressway through 2026. Local advocacy group Toronto Pedestrian Safety Coalition held a demonstration outside Toronto City Hall on June 10, demanding stricter regulations on commercial truck routes through downtown corridors.

Fjallmark Outdoors, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, has launched the Trailhead 45L backpack, priced at $189.00 and available starting November 12, 2024. Designed by lead engineer Ingrid Solvang, the pack features a recycled ripstop nylon shell, an aluminum internal frame, and a 3-liter hydration reservoir compartment. Fjallmark, founded in 2011 by former REI buyer Marcus Teale, has grown into a competitor of Osprey Packs and Gregory Mountain Products within the technical backpacking segment. The Trailhead 45L was field-tested over 6 months by a team of guides in Rocky Mountain National Park before its release. Each unit ships with a lifetime warranty and a detachable rain cover. Reviewers at Backpacker Magazine gave the pack 4.5 out of 5 stars in their October 2024 issue, praising its 2.1-kilogram weight and adjustable torso length ranging from 16 to 22 inches. The backpack is manufactured in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, at a facility supplied by Duratex Fabrics Ltd., a longtime supplier to Fjallmark. Customers who order before December 1, 2024 will receive a free 1-liter Nalgene bottle. The product is currently listed as new and is not available in refurbished or used condition. Fjallmark plans to donate 2 percent of November sales to the Colorado Trail Foundation. Founder Marcus Teale said, "This pack represents everything we've learned since 2011 about building gear that survives real mountains." The Trailhead 45L is sold exclusively through Fjallmark's website and select REI locations across the United States.

Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1968 in Bologna, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for her work on seismic retrofitting of historic buildings. She earned a degree in Civil Engineering from the University of Bologna in 1991 and later joined Politecnico di Milano as a research fellow in 1994. In 1999, Marchetti founded Studio Marchetti Ingegneria, an engineering consultancy headquartered in Milan, Italy, which grew to employ more than 120 engineers by 2015. Her firm led the retrofitting of the Basilica di San Petronio following the 2012 Emilia earthquake, a project completed in October 2015 and funded in part by a grant of 4.5 million euros from the Italian Ministry of Culture. In 2018, Marchetti was elected President of the Italian Association of Structural Engineers in Rome, a position she held until stepping down in March 2022. For her contributions to earthquake-resistant design, she received the Gustav Lindenthal Medal from the International Association for Bridge and Structural Engineering in Zurich in September 2019. Marchetti married fellow engineer Paolo Ricci in 1997; the couple has two children. In 2021, Studio Marchetti Ingegneria was acquired by the multinational firm Arup for an undisclosed sum, becoming a subsidiary while retaining its Milan office. Marchetti continues to serve as a technical advisor to Arup and lectures part-time at Politecnico di Milano.

input: SEOUL, September 12, 2024 -- Samsung Electronics unveiled the Galaxy Ring 2 at a press event held at its Digital City campus, positioning the $349 wearable as a direct challenger to the Oura Ring 4. Company vice president Han Jong-hee told reporters the device now tracks blood oxygen levels continuously, a feature earlier models lacked, thanks to a redesigned sensor supplied by Samsung's own semiconductor division. I tested the ring for eleven days across Seoul and Busan, and battery life consistently hit six days per charge, slightly short of the seven days Samsung advertises. Sleep tracking accuracy impressed me, matching within three percent of readings from a hospital-grade pulse oximeter used at Seoul National University Hospital. The companion app, rebuilt in Kotlin, syncs faster than the previous version but still lacks a working integration with Google Fit, an omission that frustrated me daily. Pricing undercuts the Oura Ring 4's $399 by a modest margin, though Oura still leads on third-party app support. Samsung says the Galaxy Ring 2 will ship globally on October 3, 2024, starting in South Korea, the United States, and Germany. For anyone already inside the Samsung ecosystem, particularly Galaxy S24 owners, this is an easy upgrade. For everyone else, Oura's maturity still makes it the safer bet. Overall, the Galaxy Ring 2 is a genuinely competitive product, held back only by software polish rather than hardware ambition.

DETROIT, Mich. — Automaker Falken Motors filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $2.3 billion in unpaid supplier debt and a sharp decline in electric vehicle sales. The filing was made in federal bankruptcy court in Detroit.

CEO Marcus Whitfield told reporters the company would continue operating its two remaining plants in Ohio and Kentucky while it restructures. "We believe this process will allow Falken Motors to emerge stronger," Whitfield said during a press briefing at the company's headquarters in Dearborn, Michigan.

Falken Motors, founded in 1987 by industrialist Harold Beckett, had struggled since 2022 to compete with Tesla and Rivian in the EV market. Its flagship sedan, the Falken Aurora, saw sales drop 41 percent last year. The company employs roughly 14,000 workers, and analysts at Morgan Stanley estimate up to 3,800 jobs could be cut in the coming months.

Supplier Redline Components, based in Toledo, Ohio, said it is owed $87 million and is evaluating legal options. "This puts real strain on our own operations," said Redline spokesperson Angela Ruiz.

Shares of Falken Motors fell 62 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $1.14. The bankruptcy filing marks the largest by a U.S. automaker since Chrysler's 2009 collapse. A hearing before Judge Elaine Torres is scheduled for March 14 in Detroit to review the reorganization plan.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. — August 14, 2024 — Solara Biotics, Inc. announced today that it has acquired NimbleGene Diagnostics for $210 million in a cash-and-stock transaction, expanding its footprint in precision oncology. The deal closed on August 12, 2024, and was approved by both companies' boards.

Under the agreement, Solara Biotics will pay $150 million in cash and issue $60 million in stock to NimbleGene Diagnostics shareholders. NimbleGene, headquartered in Palo Alto, California, was founded in 2016 by Dr. Priya Anand, who will join Solara Biotics as Chief Scientific Officer effective September 1, 2024. Dr. Anand previously served as Chief Executive Officer of NimbleGene Diagnostics for eight years.

"This acquisition strengthens our diagnostics pipeline and accelerates our entry into liquid biopsy testing," said Marcus Feldman, Chief Executive Officer of Solara Biotics, speaking at a press briefing in Cambridge on Wednesday. "NimbleGene's technology, validated in over 40,000 patient samples, complements our existing platforms."

Solara Biotics, listed on Nasdaq under the ticker SLRA, reported revenue of $1.2 billion in fiscal year 2023. The company employs roughly 3,400 people across facilities in Cambridge, San Diego, and Basel, Switzerland. Analysts at Jefferies noted the deal positions Solara Biotics as a stronger competitor to Guardant Health in the early cancer detection market.

The transaction is expected to close regulatory review by October 2024, pending clearance from the Federal Trade Commission.

HAMBURG, Germany — Norderkette AG, a mid-sized shipping equipment maker, filed for insolvency protection on Tuesday after losing its largest customer, according to a statement released by chief executive Bettina Vogt. The company, headquartered in Hamburg since 1987, employs 640 workers across three facilities in Germany and Poland.

Vogt told reporters at a Hamburg press conference that Norderkette had been struggling since March 2023, when Maersk Line ended a supply contract worth roughly 42 million euros annually. "We exhausted every option before this step," Vogt said. The Hamburg Regional Court confirmed it received the bankruptcy filing on Tuesday morning.

Insolvency administrator Klaus Reiter has been appointed by the court to oversee restructuring efforts over the next 90 days. Reiter said he would seek a buyer for at least two of the company's factories, including the flagship plant in Rostock, to preserve jobs.

Union representative Sabine Krauss criticized the timing, noting that Norderkette had paid a 3.5 million euro dividend to shareholders in December 2023. About 200 employees staged a demonstration outside the company's Hamburg headquarters on Wednesday, demanding guarantees against layoffs.

Analysts at Deutsche Bank said the collapse reflects broader pressure on European maritime suppliers amid rising steel costs and softer shipping demand. Norderkette's shares, traded on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, fell 78 percent following the announcement.

MANCHESTER, England — October 14, 2024 — Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side defeated Everton 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, extending Villa's unbeaten run to six matches in the Premier League. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Jordan Pickford, then doubled his tally in the 58th minute after a swift counterattack led by midfielder Youri Tielemans. Everton pulled one back through Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 71st minute, but substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win with a curling effort in stoppage time. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, telling reporters at the post-match press conference, "We controlled the tempo for long spells, and Ollie's movement was decisive." The victory lifted Aston Villa to second place in the table with 21 points from nine games, three points behind leaders Liverpool. Everton, managed by Sean Dyche, remained in 16th place with just eight points and now face relegation-threatened Nottingham Forest on October 21. Villa Park, which holds approximately 42,000 spectators, recorded an attendance of 41,312 for Saturday's fixture. Watkins, who joined Aston Villa from Brentford for a fee of £28 million in 2020, has now scored seven goals in the league this season. The England international is expected to feature for his country in next month's international fixtures against Greece and the Republic of Ireland.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolzumab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arden Therapeutics, for the treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. The trial, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti, enrolled 214 adult patients across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants received either 150 milligrams of tolzumab or placebo via subcutaneous injection every four weeks for 16 weeks. At the primary endpoint, 68 percent of patients receiving tolzumab achieved at least 90 percent improvement in the Psoriasis Area and Severity Index, compared with 12 percent in the placebo group. Dr. Marchetti presented the findings on March 13, 2024, at the American Academy of Dermatology annual meeting in San Diego, California. Adverse events were generally mild, with nasopharyngitis reported in 9 percent of the tolzumab arm. Arden Therapeutics' chief executive officer, Raymond Ochoa, said the company plans to initiate a Phase 3 program later this year and is seeking a strategic partner to help fund the estimated $180 million cost. Shares of Arden Therapeutics rose 22 percent following the announcement. The study was funded in part by a $4.5 million grant from the National Institutes of Health and was published in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology. Novartis, a competitor developing a similar IL-23 inhibitor, declined to comment on the results.

CEO Marlene Deitrich announced the filing at a press conference at the company's Euclid Avenue plant, saying the firm would continue operations while restructuring under court supervision. The company, founded in 1978 by Harold Vance, employs roughly 640 workers across two facilities in Ohio and Indiana. Deitrich said the bankruptcy court in the Northern District of Ohio approved emergency financing of $6 million from lender Pinnacle Capital Partners to keep operations running through the transition. Union representative Tom Kowalski, of the United Steelworkers Local 1104, said workers were informed of the filing on Monday evening and expressed concern about pension obligations. Cleveland Metal Works supplies steel components to Ford Motor Company and Stellantis, both of which issued statements saying they were monitoring the situation but did not expect immediate supply disruptions. Analysts at Fitch Ratings downgraded the company's credit rating to CCC on Wednesday, citing liquidity concerns. Deitrich said she expects the restructuring process to conclude by March 2025, with no immediate plans for layoffs. Shares of the company's parent, Vance Industrial Holdings, fell 18 percent in after-hours trading following the announcement.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF ARIZONA, MARICOPA COUNTY

Case No. CR2024-118034

On October 3, 2024, Judge Elena Ramos sentenced Marcus Whitfield, 41, to 7 years in state prison after a jury in Phoenix, Arizona found him guilty of embezzlement in connection with funds taken from Desert Ridge Credit Union. Prosecutor Angela Torres of the Maricopa County Attorney's Office argued that Whitfield, a former branch manager, diverted $340,000 from customer accounts between March 2021 and January 2023 to cover personal gambling debts.

Whitfield was arrested on February 14, 2023, by detectives from the Phoenix Police Department after an internal audit at Desert Ridge Credit Union flagged irregular withdrawals. He was charged on March 9, 2023, with one count of embezzlement and two counts of fraud. The trial began on August 12, 2024, before Judge Ramos at the Maricopa County Superior Courthouse.

Defense attorney Paul Kessler had requested leniency, citing his client's cooperation and lack of prior record, but Judge Ramos rejected the request, stating that the breach of trust warranted a substantial sentence. Whitfield was also ordered to pay $340,000 in restitution to Desert Ridge Credit Union within five years of his release.

Desert Ridge Credit Union issued a statement thanking the Phoenix Police Department and the Maricopa County Attorney's Office for their work on the case, noting that new internal controls have been implemented since the incident.

CARY, N.C. — October 14, 2024 — SolarBright Technologies, Inc. announced today that it has acquired NightHawk Sensors LLC, a privately held maker of low-light imaging chips based in Austin, Texas, for approximately $42 million in cash. The transaction, completed on October 11, 2024, is expected to strengthen SolarBright's position in the industrial automation market.

Under the terms of the deal, NightHawk's 65 employees will join SolarBright's Sensor Systems division, and NightHawk co-founder Priya Ramaswami will be appointed Vice President of Product Engineering effective November 1, 2024. "This acquisition allows us to bring advanced imaging capability directly into our automation platforms," said Derek Whitfield, Chief Executive Officer of SolarBright Technologies, speaking at a press briefing in Cary on Monday.

NightHawk Sensors was founded in 2016 by Priya Ramaswami and her brother, Anil Ramaswami, and had previously raised $9 million in venture funding from Blue Ridge Capital Partners. The company's flagship product, the NH-200 imaging sensor, is used in more than 3,000 factories worldwide.

SolarBright, headquartered in Cary, North Carolina, employs roughly 1,400 people and reported revenue of $310 million in fiscal year 2023. The company competes with Denver-based Arclight Systems in the automated sensing market. SolarBright shares rose 4 percent in after-hours trading following the announcement.

The deal is SolarBright's third acquisition since 2021 and is expected to close fully by December 2024, pending routine regulatory review.

BOSTON, MA -- November 12, 2023 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital reported today that a Phase 2 clinical trial of the investigational drug Reventoclib produced a 62 percent reduction in tumor burden among patients with relapsed multiple myeloma. The trial, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar and sponsored by Cascade Therapeutics, enrolled 148 patients across 11 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and June 2023. Participants received intravenous Reventoclib every 21 days for up to twelve cycles. According to results published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, the median progression-free survival reached 14.2 months, compared with 7.8 months in the control arm receiving standard-of-care bortezomib. Grade 3 or higher adverse events, primarily neutropenia and thrombocytopenia, occurred in 23 percent of treated patients. Dr. Nandakumar stated that the findings support advancing Reventoclib into a Phase 3 registration study, which Cascade Therapeutics plans to launch in early 2024 in collaboration with the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. The company's chief medical officer, Dr. Samuel Reyes, said the drug received Breakthrough Therapy designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in September 2023, potentially accelerating its regulatory review. Cascade Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, was founded in 2016 and has raised $340 million in venture funding to date. Analysts at Leerink Partners estimate peak annual sales for Reventoclib could exceed $1.2 billion if approved. The company expects to submit a New Drug Application to the FDA by the fourth quarter of 2025, pending confirmatory Phase 3 data.

Ingrid Solberg (born 4 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cod population decline in the North Sea. She earned a doctorate in marine ecology from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Bergen the same year as a research scientist. In 1994 Solberg was appointed Director of Fisheries Research at the institute, a position she held for eleven years. Her 1998 study on Gadus morhua migration patterns, published in the journal Marine Ecology Progress Series, became a foundational reference for European Union fisheries policy. In 2003 she was awarded the Nansen Prize by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to oceanography. Solberg left the Institute of Marine Research in 2005 to become a professor at the University of Tromso, where she established the Arctic Fisheries Laboratory with a grant of 12 million Norwegian kroner from the Research Council of Norway. She married fellow biologist Erik Fossum in 1988, and the couple have one daughter, Marte Fossum, born in 1991 in Tromso. Solberg retired from active teaching in 2020 but continues to advise the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea on sustainable cod quotas. She currently lives in Tromso, Norway.

4/ Kestrel Dynamics, based in Denver, Colorado, raised $9 million in seed funding back in 2021 but had struggled to land customers, according to a source familiar with the matter.

5/ Nathan will present the combined roadmap at the National Robotics Conference in Chicago on May 3, 2024. Analysts at Jefferies say the deal values Kestrel at roughly 6.4x revenue.

6/ Not everyone's thrilled — about 12 Kestrel employees were laid off yesterday as part of the transition, per an internal memo obtained by TechCrunch reporter Elena Ruiz.

7/ Shares of Solace's largest investor, Sequoia-backed holding firm Vantage Capital, ticked up 3 percent on the news. Nathan called it "the most important deal we've done in five years."

8/ More details expected when Nathan speaks with reporters Friday.

CAMBRIDGE, MA — October 14, 2024 — Solenne Biotherapeutics, Inc. today announced that Novartis AG has agreed to acquire the company for approximately $2.3 billion in cash, in a deal expected to close by December 20, 2024, pending regulatory approval. Under the terms of the agreement, Novartis will pay $48 per share, a 42 percent premium over Solenne's closing price on October 11, 2024.

Solenne, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, was founded in 2016 by Dr. Amara Whitfield and Dr. Julian Roskov and has developed a pipeline of RNA-based therapies for chronic kidney disease, including its lead candidate, Renolix. The drug is currently in Phase 3 trials involving 1,200 patients across sites in the United States and Germany.

"This acquisition validates a decade of scientific work by our team," said Amara Whitfield, Chief Executive Officer of Solenne, speaking at a press briefing in Boston. "We believe Novartis has the global reach to bring Renolix to patients faster."

Vasant Narasimhan, Chief Executive Officer of Novartis, said the acquisition strengthens the company's renal disease portfolio and will add roughly 340 employees to its research division based in Basel, Switzerland. Novartis expects the transaction to be neutral to earnings per share in 2025 and accretive thereafter.

The boards of directors of both companies have unanimously approved the transaction. Goldman Sachs is serving as financial advisor to Solenne, while Morgan Stanley is advising Novartis. Shareholders of Solenne are expected to vote on the merger at a special meeting scheduled for November 25, 2024, in Cambridge.

Marguerite Okonjo (born 14 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-British structural engineer known for pioneering low-carbon concrete alternatives. She earned a Bachelor of Engineering from the University of Lagos in 1980 before moving to London to complete a doctorate at Imperial College London in 1985. In 1991 Okonjo joined Arup as a junior engineer and rose to become Head of Materials Research by 2003. During her tenure at Arup, she led the team that developed Ferrocrete, a low-emission binder later adopted in the construction of the Elizabeth Line stations across London. In 2008 Okonjo left Arup to found Solidus Materials Ltd, a startup headquartered in Bristol, United Kingdom, dedicated to commercializing carbon-reduced cement. Solidus Materials was acquired by the French conglomerate Lafarge Holcim in June 2016 for approximately 42 million pounds, allowing Okonjo to retain a research directorship within the merged division. She married fellow engineer Thomas Reyes in 1994, and the couple has two children. In 2019 Okonjo received the Royal Academy of Engineering's Silver Medal, presented in London by then-president Dame Ann Dowling, in recognition of her contributions to sustainable infrastructure. She currently serves as a visiting professor at Imperial College London and continues to consult for Arup on decarbonization projects. Okonjo has published over 60 peer-reviewed papers and holds three patents related to alternative cement chemistry. She lives in Bristol with her husband.

The Ohio Department of Transportation (ODOT) announced on March 14, 2024, that it will begin a $42 million reconstruction of the Interstate 70 interchange near Zanesville, Ohio, starting April 1, 2024. Director Pamela Boratyn said the project, awarded to Kokosing Construction Company, is expected to be completed by November 2025 and will reduce congestion for roughly 38,000 daily commuters. "This investment reflects our commitment to safer, more efficient infrastructure for Muskingum County residents," Boratyn said during a press briefing at the ODOT District 5 office in Jefferson Township. Funding for the project draws on $30 million in federal highway funds allocated under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, with the remaining $12 million provided by the Ohio state budget. State Senator Tim Schaffer, who represents the 20th District, praised the announcement, noting that similar upgrades along Interstate 70 in Franklin County reduced accident rates by 18 percent after completion in 2022. ODOT officials also confirmed that Kokosing Construction Company will hire approximately 150 additional workers for the duration of the project. Motorists should expect lane closures beginning April 8, 2024, with detour routes posted at all major exits. The agency will hold a public information session on March 28, 2024, at the Zanesville Municipal Building to address community concerns. ODOT emphasized that safety remains its top priority throughout construction.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City midfielder Rodri scored twice on Saturday as City defeated Everton 3-1 at the Etihad Stadium, extending their unbeaten league run to 12 matches. Manager Pep Guardiola praised his team's composure after a slow start that saw Everton striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin open the scoring in the 18th minute.

Rodri equalized in the 34th minute with a low strike from outside the box, then added a second in the 67th minute after a corner delivered by Kevin De Bruyne. Substitute Julian Alvarez sealed the win with a close-range finish in the 82nd minute. The victory keeps Manchester City in second place in the Premier League table, two points behind leaders Arsenal.

Guardiola confirmed after the match that defender Ruben Dias will miss the next three weeks with a hamstring injury sustained in training on Thursday. "It's a blow, but we have players ready to step in," Guardiola told reporters at a press conference inside the Etihad Stadium.

Everton manager Sean Dyche said his side's away form remains a concern after a fourth consecutive loss on the road. The Toffees, who sit 15th in the table, will host Newcastle United on October 21 at Goodison Park.

Manchester City's next fixture is away to RB Leipzig in the Champions League on October 17, a rematch of last season's group stage encounter. Attendance at the Etihad Stadium was announced at 53,112.

To: Board of Directors, Meridian Foods Corp.
From: Sandra Whitfield, Chief Financial Officer
Date: March 11, 2024
Subject: Acquisition of Cascade Bakery Holdings Finalized

Dear Colleagues,

I am pleased to confirm that Meridian Foods Corp. completed its acquisition of Cascade Bakery Holdings on March 8, 2024, for a total price of $42 million. The deal was signed at our headquarters in Portland, Oregon, following four months of negotiations led by our Chief Executive Officer, Marcus Delaney, and Cascade's founder, Elena Vasquez.

Cascade Bakery Holdings, headquartered in Seattle, Washington, will now operate as a subsidiary of Meridian Foods Corp. Elena Vasquez has agreed to stay on as President of the Cascade division for at least eighteen months to ensure a smooth transition. She previously founded the company in 2011 and grew it to 27 retail locations across Washington and Oregon.

To fund the transaction, Meridian secured a $15 million loan from Pacific Crest Bank, with the remainder covered by existing cash reserves. Payment was transferred to Cascade's shareholders on March 8, 2024.

Sandra Whitfield

Meridian Foods Corp.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City edged Liverpool 2-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, with a stoppage-time header from Erling Haaland sealing a dramatic Premier League victory in front of 53,412 fans. Haaland, the 23-year-old Norwegian striker, rose above two defenders in the 91st minute to convert a corner delivered by Kevin De Bruyne, sparking wild celebrations among the home supporters.

Liverpool had taken the lead in the 34th minute through Mohamed Salah, who curled a left-footed shot past goalkeeper Ederson. City responded quickly, with Phil Foden equalizing in the 52nd minute after a swift counterattack. Manager Pep Guardiola praised his squad's resilience afterward, telling reporters at the post-match press conference, "We never stopped believing, even when Liverpool controlled long stretches of the second half."

Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp, who has led the club since 2015, expressed frustration at his team's inability to close out the match. "We conceded a soft goal at the worst possible moment," Klopp said outside the away dressing room.

The result lifts Manchester City to second place in the Premier League table, one point behind leaders Arsenal, while Liverpool drops to fifth. City's next fixture is against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on October 21, 2023. The match also marked Haaland's 15th goal of the season, extending his lead atop the league's scoring charts.

Earlier in the week, the Premier League announced that City's Rodri would miss two matches after picking up a fifth yellow card of the campaign.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating vedostatin-B, an experimental chemical compound targeting inflammatory pathways in patients with early-stage rheumatoid arthritis. The study, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar, enrolled 214 participants across three sites in Boston, Chicago, and Toronto between June 2022 and September 2023. Findings, published in The Lancet Rheumatology, showed a 42 percent reduction in joint swelling among patients receiving 150 milligrams of vedostatin-B daily compared to a placebo group. Dr. Nandakumar, who serves as Chief of Rheumatology at Massachusetts General Hospital, presented the data at the American College of Rheumatology conference held in Chicago on March 12, 2024. Co-author Dr. Felix Wachtel of the University of Toronto noted that 18 patients experienced mild gastrointestinal side effects, while none developed serious infections, a common concern with existing biologic therapies. The trial was funded by a $12 million grant from the National Institutes of Health and sponsored by Aravine Therapeutics, a biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Aravine Therapeutics was founded in 2018 by former Pfizer executive Martin Coelho, who now serves as its Chief Executive Officer. The company plans to begin a larger Phase 3 trial in early 2025, pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Shares of Aravine Therapeutics rose 9 percent following the announcement. If successful, vedostatin-B could become the first oral treatment of its kind approved for rheumatoid arthritis within the next three years, according to Dr. Nandakumar.

Ingrid Voss (born March 14, 1958, in Lübeck, West Germany) is a German biochemist known for pioneering work on lipid nanoparticle delivery systems. She earned her doctorate in biochemistry from the University of Freiburg in 1985 and joined Hoechst AG as a research scientist that same year. In 1994, Voss left Hoechst to co-found Cellivax GmbH alongside chemist Rainer Bergmann, serving as Chief Scientific Officer of the Munich-based biotechnology firm. Under her leadership, Cellivax developed an early mRNA-stabilization technique that later underpinned several vaccine platforms. In 2003, Novartis acquired Cellivax GmbH for 340 million euros, and Voss briefly served as Head of Research at Novartis before stepping down from that position in December 2005. She subsequently accepted a professorship at ETH Zurich, where she taught molecular pharmacology for over a decade. In 2016, the Swiss Academy of Sciences awarded Voss the Marcel Benoist Prize for her contributions to nanomedicine, presented at a ceremony in Bern. Voss is married to physicist Klaus Dittmer, with whom she has one daughter, Lena Dittmer, a researcher at the Max Planck Institute. Voss retired from ETH Zurich in 2020 but continues to chair the scientific advisory board of Cellivax GmbH's successor company, NovaLipid AG, headquartered in Basel, Switzerland.

Pixel Tab Pro Review: Google's Bold Bet on Hybrid Computing

On September 18, 2024, Google launched the Pixel Tab Pro at an event in Mountain View, California, positioning it as a rival to Apple's iPad Pro. I have spent three weeks testing the $899 tablet, and the results are mixed but promising.

The device runs on Google's new Tensor G4X chip, manufactured in partnership with Samsung Electronics, and ships with 12GB of RAM. Battery life impressed me: roughly 14 hours of continuous video playback, up from 10 hours on last year's Pixel Tab. The 11-inch OLED display, sourced from LG Display, is sharp and vibrant, though reflective in sunlight.

Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google, called the Pixel Tab Pro "the clearest expression yet of Android's desktop ambitions" during the keynote. That ambition shows in the new multitasking mode, which lets users run four apps simultaneously, a feature absent from the previous model.

Software remains the weak link. Several third-party apps, including Adobe Photoshop, crashed twice during my testing in San Francisco. Google says a patch is scheduled for October 2024.

At $899, the Pixel Tab Pro undercuts the $999 iPad Pro by $100, and for users embedded in the Android ecosystem, that gap matters. It is not a perfect device, but it is the most serious challenger to Apple's tablet dominance in years. I recommend it cautiously, with the software caveat firmly in mind.

Rating: 7.5/10
