CAMBRIDGE, Mass., April 9, 2024 -- Meridian Biosciences Inc. today announced that it has acquired Novapath Diagnostics Ltd., a Dublin-based developer of rapid molecular testing kits, for approximately $340 million in cash and stock. The transaction closed on April 8, 2024, following approval from regulators in the European Union and the United States.

Under the terms of the deal, Novapath will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Biosciences and retain its 210 employees at its facility in Dublin, Ireland. Dr. Fiona Callaghan, Novapath's founder and chief executive officer, will join Meridian as Senior Vice President of Diagnostics, reporting to Meridian CEO Robert Hansen.

"This acquisition strengthens our position in infectious disease testing at a critical time," said Robert Hansen, speaking at a press briefing in Boston. "Novapath's PCR-based assays for detecting influenza and respiratory syncytial virus complement our existing portfolio."

Novapath was founded in 2016 by Dr. Callaghan and has raised more than $60 million in venture funding from investors including Kernel Capital and Atlantic Bridge. The company's flagship product, the RapidScan RSV Assay, received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in March 2023.

Meridian Biosciences, headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio, reported revenue of $245 million in fiscal year 2023. The company employs roughly 1,800 people across facilities in the United States, Belgium, and China. Shares of Meridian rose 4.2 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement.

Meridian expects the acquisition to be finalized fully integrated by the third quarter of 2024.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT AND INFRASTRUCTURE, Ottawa, Ontario — October 3, 2024

Minister Élise Fontaine announced today that the federal government will allocate $420 million over five years to modernize rail safety systems along the Windsor-Quebec corridor. The funding, approved under the Rail Safety Improvement Act, will be administered through Transport Canada in partnership with Via Rail Canada and Canadian National Railway.

"This investment reflects our commitment to protecting the 4.8 million passengers who travel this corridor annually," said Minister Fontaine during a press conference at Union Station in Toronto. The announcement follows a Transportation Safety Board investigation into a freight derailment near Belleville on July 14, 2024, which injured three workers and prompted renewed scrutiny of aging track infrastructure.

Canadian National Railway CEO Tracy Robinson welcomed the funding, noting that 60 percent of the corridor's track was laid before 1980. Robinson confirmed that her company will match $95 million in federal funds with private capital by March 2025.

Opposition transport critic Daniel Whitfield criticized the timeline, arguing that $420 million is insufficient given the scale of deferred maintenance across 1,200 kilometres of track. The Ministry expects construction crews to begin work near Kingston in January 2025, with completion targeted for December 2029.

A public consultation session will be held in Kingston on November 12, 2024, where residents can submit comments on proposed noise mitigation measures.

SUPERIOR COURT OF ALAMEDA COUNTY, CALIFORNIA — The State of California charged Marcus D. Wheeler, 41, of Oakland, with two counts of grand theft and one count of embezzlement on March 4, 2024, following an investigation into missing funds from Bayview Logistics Inc., where Wheeler worked as Chief Financial Officer until his termination on January 17, 2024. Prosecutor Elena Suarez told Judge Harold T. Bingham during a hearing at the Rene C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland that Wheeler allegedly diverted $612,000 from company accounts between June 2022 and December 2023, transferring the funds to a shell entity called Pacific Crest Holdings LLC. Defense attorney Rosa Nunez argued that the transfers were authorized under a consulting agreement and requested dismissal of the charges. Judge Bingham denied the motion and scheduled a trial hearing for September 9, 2024. Bayview Logistics Inc., headquartered in San Leandro, California, is a subsidiary of Meridian Transport Group, which reported the discrepancy to the Alameda County District Attorney's Office in November 2023 after an internal audit by KPMG flagged irregular wire transfers. If convicted on all counts, Wheeler faces up to nine years in state prison and restitution of the full stolen amount. A pretrial status conference is set for April 22, 2024, at 9:00 a.m. Wheeler was released on $150,000 bail on March 6, 2024, pending trial. The District Attorney's Office confirmed that no additional employees of Bayview Logistics Inc. are currently under investigation.

SUPERIOR COURT OF SUFFOLK COUNTY
Criminal Term, Part 12

Case No. SC-2024-11987: State of Massachusetts v. Darnell Ogunwe

On March 14, 2024, Judge Patricia Vance presided over the sentencing hearing of defendant Darnell Ogunwe, 34, at the Suffolk County Courthouse in Boston, Massachusetts. Ogunwe was convicted on February 9, 2024 of grand larceny after prosecutors from the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office, led by Assistant District Attorney Michael Renna, proved he embezzled $412,000 from his former employer, Coastal Freight Logistics Inc., between June 2021 and October 2023. Company president Linda Petracek testified that Ogunwe, who held the position of senior accounts manager, funneled the funds through a shell vendor called Harbor Supply Partners LLC.

Judge Vance sentenced Ogunwe to seven years in state prison, followed by three years of supervised probation, and ordered restitution of $412,000 payable to Coastal Freight Logistics Inc. Defense attorney Rosalind Cho argued for leniency, citing her client's lack of prior record, but the request was denied.

Separately, the court noted that Ogunwe was arrested by Boston Police detectives on November 2, 2023 at his residence in Quincy, Massachusetts, shortly after the company's internal auditors flagged irregular wire transfers. The case drew attention from local business groups, including the Massachusetts Freight Association, which called the verdict a warning to employers about internal fraud controls.

The sentence will take effect April 1, 2024, according to court clerk Teresa Wu.

To: Board of Directors, Halloway Instruments Inc.
From: Priya Nandakumar, Chief Financial Officer
Date: March 14, 2024
Subject: Acquisition of SensorTech Dynamics and Related Financing

Dear Board Members,

I am writing to confirm that Halloway Instruments Inc., headquartered in Austin, Texas, completed its acquisition of SensorTech Dynamics on March 11, 2024. Under the terms of the agreement, Halloway Instruments paid $42 million in cash to SensorTech's founder, Marcus Webb, who will remain as Vice President of Engineering for a transition period of eighteen months.

To finance the deal, Wells Fargo extended a credit facility of $30 million to Halloway Instruments on March 8, 2024. The remaining balance was drawn from existing reserves.

Separately, I want to update you on a personnel change. Effective April 1, 2024, Daniel Ostrowski will step down as Chief Operating Officer to pursue an opportunity with a firm in Denver, Colorado. The board is expected to meet on March 25, 2024, in our Austin headquarters to elect his successor, and I understand Grace Lindqvist, currently Director of Manufacturing, is the leading candidate for the role.

On a related note, SensorTech's flagship product, the FlowSense X200 pressure sensor, will now be marketed under the Halloway brand starting in June 2024. We anticipate this will strengthen our position against competitors such as Bristow Automation, based in Portland, Oregon.

Please let me know if you have questions before the March 25 meeting.

Best regards,
Priya Nandakumar
Chief Financial Officer
Halloway Instruments Inc.

Redmond, Wash. — On November 14, 2024, Microsoft Corporation formally launched Surface Laptop Studio 3, a $2,199 convertible workstation aimed at creative professionals. I have spent three weeks with the device, purchased at a Best Buy store in Bellevue, Washington, and the results are mostly impressive.

The laptop pairs a 14.4-inch PixelSense display with Intel's new Core Ultra 9 285H processor and an Nvidia RTX 4070 mobile GPU, delivering noticeably smoother performance in Adobe Premiere Pro than last year's model. Battery life reached 9 hours during video playback, slightly below Microsoft's advertised 11-hour claim.

Panos Panay, who now serves as Chief Product Officer at Amazon after leaving Microsoft in 2023, does not appear in this generation's marketing, a notable shift from prior launches. Instead, Microsoft's current devices chief, Pavan Davuluri, presented the hardware at an event in New York City, emphasizing on-device AI features powered by Copilot.

One caveat: two units in our test batch, sourced separately from a distributor in Austin, Texas, suffered unexpected shutdowns under heavy load, an issue Microsoft acknowledged on December 2, 2024, promising a firmware fix within weeks. That defect, combined with the $2,199 starting price, tempers enthusiasm.

Still, for editors and designers already inside the Windows ecosystem, this is the most capable Surface yet. Competitors like Apple's MacBook Pro and Dell's XPS 16 remain worth cross-shopping, but Microsoft has closed the performance gap considerably.

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY — On October 14, 2024, Judge Marlene Ostrowski sentenced Darnell Pickett, 37, of Newark, to 8 years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of aggravated arson and insurance fraud. Prosecutor Elena Vasquez of the Essex County Prosecutor's Office argued that Pickett deliberately set fire to a warehouse owned by Garrison Textile Supply on Ferry Street on March 3, 2023, causing $2.4 million in damages, in order to collect a $500,000 insurance payout from Meridian Casualty Insurance Co. No injuries were reported, though firefighter Thomas Reyes suffered smoke inhalation while battling the blaze and was treated at University Hospital in Newark. During the two-week trial, held at the Wilentz Justice Complex, defense attorney Carla Nunn maintained that Pickett was framed by a former business partner, but the jury of twelve deliberated for only six hours before returning a unanimous verdict on September 20, 2024. Judge Ostrowski, addressing the courtroom, stated that "the calculated destruction of a livelihood for personal gain warrants the maximum penalty permitted under New Jersey statute 2C:17-1." Pickett's attorney has already filed notice of appeal with the Appellate Division. The Essex County Prosecutor's Office confirmed that Meridian Casualty Insurance Co. never paid the disputed claim after fraud investigators flagged inconsistencies in Pickett's financial records.

input: Boston, MA - November 12, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tenafexor, an oral chemical compound designed to inhibit fibrosis progression in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh and funded by a $14.2 million grant from the National Institutes of Health, enrolled 236 participants across seven sites in the United States and Canada between March 2021 and August 2022. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of tenafexor daily showed a 31 percent reduction in disease progression compared to placebo over 52 weeks, according to findings published in The New England Journal of Medicine. Dr. Marsh presented the data at the American Thoracic Society conference held in San Diego on November 10, 2023. "These results represent a meaningful step forward for patients who currently have few treatment options," Marsh said during the presentation. Pharmaceutical company Aravex Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the second quarter of 2024. Aravex was founded in 2015 by biochemist Raymond Oduya, who currently serves as Chief Executive Officer. The company's stock rose 18 percent following the announcement. Aravex also disclosed a $40 million supply agreement with Kestrel Biologics to secure raw materials for large-scale production. Roughly 100,000 people in the United States are diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis each year, and median survival after diagnosis remains three to five years without intervention.

input: The Ministry of Environment and Water Resources announced on 14 March 2024 that the Department of Public Works will allocate 42 million dollars to upgrade flood defenses along the Mekong River near the city of Kratie, Cambodia. The announcement was delivered by Minister Sopheak Chan at a press briefing held at the National Assembly Building in Phnom Penh. According to Minister Chan, the funds will be transferred from the National Treasury to the Kratie Provincial Authority by 30 April 2024 to finance the construction of 12 kilometers of reinforced levees. The project follows severe flooding in September 2023 that displaced roughly 8,000 residents and damaged over 1,500 homes along the riverbank. Deputy Minister Ratana Sok, who previously served as Director of the Hydrology Department, will oversee implementation and coordinate with engineers from the Cambodian National Mekong Committee. The World Bank has pledged an additional 15 million dollars in supplementary financing, pending approval from its board in Washington on 10 May 2024. Minister Chan stated, "This investment reflects our commitment to protecting vulnerable communities from future disasters." Construction is expected to begin in June 2024 and conclude by December 2025. Local officials in Kratie have welcomed the plan, noting that similar floods in 2011 caused an estimated 60 million dollars in damage. The Ministry will submit quarterly progress reports to the National Assembly starting in July 2024.

input: DENVER, Colorado — Trailhead Energy Corp. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Basin Rock Resources LLC for $412 million in a cash-and-stock deal, expanding its footprint in the Permian Basin. The agreement, disclosed at Trailhead's headquarters in Denver, will see Basin Rock shareholders receive $27.50 per share, a 19 percent premium over Monday's closing price. Trailhead's chief executive officer, Marina Delgado, said the acquisition would add roughly 45,000 net acres and boost daily production by 38,000 barrels of oil equivalent. "This transaction strengthens our position as a top-tier operator in West Texas," Delgado told reporters during a call. Basin Rock's founder and outgoing CEO, Walter Higgins, will step down once the deal closes, expected by March 15, 2025, pending approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Higgins, who started Basin Rock in 2011, will join Trailhead's board of directors as a senior advisor. Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimate the combined company will generate $1.3 billion in annual revenue. Shares of Trailhead Energy Corp. rose 6 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Basin Rock's stock jumped nearly 18 percent. The deal marks the third major acquisition in the Permian Basin this year, following similar moves by competitor Odessa Petroleum Inc. Trailhead plans to fund the purchase through a combination of existing cash reserves and a new $200 million credit facility arranged by JPMorgan Chase.

DETROIT, Mich. — Sterling Bancorp announced Tuesday that it has acquired Meridian Robotics Inc., a Detroit-based startup specializing in warehouse automation, for $340 million in cash and stock. The deal, finalized on March 11, 2024, marks Sterling Bancorp's largest acquisition to date and is expected to close by June 2024 pending regulatory approval.

Meridian Robotics, founded in 2018 by engineer Priya Nataraj, employs 210 people at its headquarters on Woodward Avenue in Detroit. Nataraj will remain with the company as Chief Technology Officer, according to a statement released by Sterling Bancorp CEO Warren Halloway.

"This acquisition strengthens our position against competitors like Vantage Logistics and gives us a foothold in automated supply chains," Halloway said during a press conference at Sterling Bancorp's headquarters in Chicago, Illinois.

Shares of Sterling Bancorp rose 4.2 percent following the announcement, closing at $87.65 on the New York Stock Exchange. Analysts at Fenwick Capital Partners noted the deal reflects growing interest among financial firms in robotics and automation technology.

Nataraj, a naturalized U.S. citizen originally from Bengaluru, India, said the partnership would allow Meridian to scale production of its flagship product, the HaulBot 3000, a self-driving warehouse cart. Sterling Bancorp expects the integration to be complete by the fourth quarter of 2024, with 50 additional jobs to be created in Detroit over the next year.

HARTFORD, Conn. — Meridian Health Systems announced Tuesday it will acquire Colton Regional Medical Center for $412 million, a deal that will expand its footprint across New England. The acquisition, expected to close by March 15, 2025, was confirmed by Meridian CEO Denise Alvarado during a press conference at the company's Hartford headquarters.

Colton Regional, a 340-bed hospital based in Colton, Connecticut, has struggled financially since filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in August 2023. Its board chairman, Walter Higgins, said the sale would preserve roughly 2,800 jobs and keep the emergency department operating without interruption.

Alvarado, who became CEO of Meridian in June 2021, said the merger reflects broader consolidation in the healthcare industry. "This partnership strengthens access to care for patients across Hartford County," she told reporters. Meridian, headquartered in Hartford, currently operates 14 hospitals across Connecticut and Massachusetts and competes directly with Stamford-based Nutmeg Health Partners.

The deal still requires approval from the Connecticut Attorney General's office and the Federal Trade Commission, which has scrutinized similar hospital mergers in recent years. Analysts at Bristow Capital estimate the transaction could close within four months if regulators raise no objections.

Colton Regional employs roughly 3,100 people and was founded in 1958 by Dr. Eleanor Vance. Higgins said Vance's family had been consulted throughout negotiations and supported the transition. Meridian shares rose 6 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement.

Ingrid Sallmann (born 12 March 1958 in Graz, Austria) is an Austrian materials scientist known for pioneering low-temperature ceramic sintering techniques. She earned a doctorate in chemistry from the University of Vienna in 1984 and joined Siemens AG in Munich the same year as a Research Engineer. In 1991 Sallmann left Siemens AG to co-found Ceravantis GmbH alongside engineer Hartmut Rieger, establishing the company's headquarters in Salzburg, Austria. Under her leadership as Chief Technology Officer, Ceravantis GmbH developed a widely used piezoelectric ceramic called TheraFlex, produced by Ceravantis GmbH and adopted by medical device makers across Europe.

In 2003 Ceravantis GmbH was acquired by the German conglomerate Wentroff Industries for 78 million euros, and Sallmann was appointed Vice President of Materials Research at Wentroff Industries, a position she held until 2011. That year she stepped down from Wentroff Industries to accept a professorship at ETH Zurich in Switzerland, where she has since mentored more than 40 doctoral students.

Sallmann received the European Ceramics Innovation Prize from the European Ceramic Society in 2015 in Barcelona, Spain, for her contributions to biomedical ceramics. She married fellow scientist Dr. Klaus Bergmann in 1989; the couple has one daughter, Lena Bergmann, born in 1993 in Salzburg. Sallmann continues to publish on sustainable ceramic manufacturing and serves on the advisory board of the Fraunhofer Institute for Ceramic Technologies.

Bellroy, the Australian accessories brand headquartered in Fitzroy, Melbourne, has released the Venture Ready Backpack, a 22-liter travel pack built for commuters and light travelers. Priced at $189.00 USD, the bag is now available on Bellroy's online store as of March 4, 2024. Constructed from a 900D recycled polyester shell, the Venture Ready Backpack features a padded 16-inch laptop sleeve, a magnetic buckle closure system, and a hidden passport pocket lined with ripstop nylon. Bellroy sourced the main zippers from YKK, a Japanese supplier known for durable hardware used across the outdoor gear industry. The bag weighs 1.3 kilograms and comes in three colorways: Basalt, Neptune, and Black. According to Bellroy's product director, Ash Faulkner, the backpack underwent 14 months of testing with commuters in Melbourne and Osaka before launch. Approximately 60 percent of the shell material is made from post-consumer plastic bottles. Customers who purchase the Venture Ready Backpack before April 1, 2024 will receive a complimentary luggage tag worth $15.00. Early reviewers on Bellroy's site have given the product an average rating of 4.7 out of 5 stars, praising its organization pockets but noting the base could be more reinforced. The bag is currently listed as a new item and ships from Bellroy's distribution center in Port Melbourne within two business days of ordering.

SUPERIOR COURT OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

On March 14, 2024, Judge Patricia Nakamura sentenced Ramon Duarte, 41, to 7 years in state prison after a jury convicted him of grand theft and embezzlement in connection with his former role as Chief Financial Officer at Bayview Logistics Inc., a freight company headquartered in Oakland, California. Prosecutor Diane Colston of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Duarte diverted approximately $2.3 million from company accounts between January 2019 and October 2022, funneling the funds through a shell entity called Harborline Trading LLC. Duarte was arrested by Oakland Police Department detectives on November 8, 2022, at his residence in Piedmont, California, following a six-month investigation triggered by an internal audit.

During the trial, held at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, defense attorney Marcus Feld contended that his client had been authorized by former CEO Wallace Ito to make the transfers as part of an off-book vendor arrangement. Ito, who resigned from Bayview Logistics in May 2023, denied the claim under cross-examination. The jury deliberated for eleven hours before returning its verdict on February 27, 2024.

Judge Nakamura also ordered Duarte to pay restitution of $2.3 million to Bayview Logistics and imposed a $50,000 fine. Duarte's attorney has indicated he will file an appeal with the California Court of Appeal within 60 days. Bayview Logistics released a statement thanking the Alameda County District Attorney's Office for its diligence.

AUSTIN, TEXAS -- May 14, 2024 -- Silverline Robotics Inc., a fast-growing manufacturer of warehouse automation systems, announced today that it has acquired Vantage Sensing LLC, a Denver-based maker of industrial lidar sensors, for $42 million in cash and stock. The deal, which closed on May 10, 2024, is expected to strengthen Silverline's product lineup ahead of the launch of its next-generation autonomous forklift, the HaulBot X2.

Under the agreement, Vantage Sensing's 65 employees will join Silverline's engineering division in Denver, Colorado, and the unit will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary under the name Silverline Sensing. Dr. Priya Nandakumar, Vantage Sensing's founder and chief executive officer, will become Silverline's new Vice President of Sensor Engineering, reporting directly to Silverline CEO Marcus Feld.

"This acquisition gives us the depth of sensing technology we need to compete with Kestrel Automation and Norrick Robotics," said Marcus Feld, speaking at a press briefing held at Silverline's Austin headquarters. "Priya and her team have built something remarkable, and we're thrilled to bring them into the Silverline family."

Founded in 2016, Silverline Robotics is headquartered in Austin, Texas, and employs more than 900 people across facilities in Texas, Colorado, and Ohio. The company reported $310 million in revenue for fiscal year 2023 and expects the HaulBot X2 to enter production by the third quarter of 2025.

Financial terms of the transaction were advised by Bracton Capital Partners, which represented Vantage Sensing in the negotiations.

Introducing the Kestrel Aero 700, a carbon-fiber road bike from Denver-based Vantage Cycles, now available for pre-order starting September 12, 2024. Priced at $3,499, the Aero 700 features a Shimano Ultegra Di2 groupset, a 700c wheelset, and a frame weight of just 950 grams. Vantage Cycles, founded in 2016 by former professional cyclist Marco Delvecchio, has shipped over 40,000 bikes worldwide from its facility in Boulder, Colorado. The Aero 700 was engineered in partnership with aerodynamicist Dr. Elena Farrow, whose wind-tunnel testing at the University of Michigan reduced drag by 8 percent compared to the previous Kestrel Aero 600 model. Each frame is hand-finished in Vantage's Boulder workshop and undergoes a 200-point quality inspection before shipping. Customers who order before October 1, 2024 will receive a complimentary Vantage hydration kit worth $75. The bike ships in three colorways: Obsidian Black, Alpine White, and Crimson Red, and is available in five frame sizes ranging from 48cm to 61cm. Vantage Cycles offers a limited lifetime warranty on the frame and a two-year warranty on components. Early reviewers, including cycling journalist Priya Nakamura of VeloEdge Magazine, praised the Aero 700's stiffness-to-weight ratio, calling it "the most responsive climbing bike under $4,000." Units are expected to begin shipping from the Boulder facility in late October 2024, with international shipping to Canada, the United Kingdom, and Australia starting in November.

The Ontario Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks announced on March 4, 2024 that it will invest $42 million to modernize wastewater treatment facilities in Thunder Bay and Sudbury. Minister Andrea Kowalski unveiled the plan at a press conference held at Thunder Bay City Hall, emphasizing that the funding will address aging infrastructure exposed after heavy flooding damaged the Current River treatment plant in September 2023. "This investment reflects our commitment to protecting the Great Lakes watershed," Kowalski said, flanked by Thunder Bay Mayor Ken Boshcoff. Under the program, the City of Sudbury will receive $18 million to replace corroded pipelines dating to 1968, while Thunder Bay will receive $24 million for a new filtration system expected to be operational by December 2025. The Ministry stated that Veolia Canada, a subsidiary of Veolia Environnement, has been selected as the primary engineering contractor following a competitive bidding process that concluded in January 2024. Opposition critic Marit Stiles, leader of the Ontario New Democratic Party, questioned whether the funding was sufficient, noting that similar upgrades in Ottawa cost $60 million in 2022. The Ministry countered that economies of scale and standardized equipment sourced from supplier Xylem Inc. would keep costs lower. Construction crews are scheduled to begin work in Sudbury on April 15, 2024, with the Thunder Bay project following in May. Residents can submit questions to the Ministry's public engagement office through June 30, 2024.

Fjällkorn Outdoors, headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, has released the Trollveggen 45L Alpine Pack, a lightweight backpack designed for multi-day mountaineering trips. Priced at $289.00, the Trollveggen 45L is constructed from 210-denier Cordura fabric and weighs just 1.4 kilograms. The pack debuted on September 12, 2024, at the Outdoor Retailer Summer Market in Denver, Colorado, where company founder Ingrid Halvorsen demonstrated its modular hip-belt system to a crowd of retailers. Halvorsen, a former competitive alpinist from Norway, founded Fjällkorn Outdoors in 2016 after a difficult climb of Mount Rainier convinced her that most packs on the market were poorly suited to technical terrain. The Trollveggen 45L includes a detachable 2-liter hydration bladder, an integrated ice-axe loop, and three external compression straps rated to hold 25 kilograms of gear. Early reviewers, including Backpacker Magazine, praised its 92 percent customer satisfaction rating in initial trials of 150 units sold through REI stores in Seattle and Portland. The pack is available in two colorways, Glacier Gray and Ember Orange, and ships within 5 business days of ordering. Fjällkorn Outdoors currently competes directly with Norwegian rival Norrøna and American brand Osprey Packs in the technical mountaineering segment. Customers who purchase before October 31, 2024 will receive a complimentary Fjällkorn trekking pole worth $45. The product is new and currently in stock, with over 3,000 units already shipped to retailers across North America and Europe.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solace Robotics announced this morning it has acquired Fenwick Sensors for $42 million in cash, closing the deal on March 14, 2024. Solace CEO Renata Kowalski says the buy strengthens their warehouse-automation line.

2/ Fenwick Sensors, founded in 2016 by Devon Ashcroft, was headquartered in Boulder, Colorado. Ashcroft will stay on as VP of Engineering under Solace, according to a memo sent to staff Thursday.

3/ Kowalski told Reuters, "This isn't just a bolt-on acquisition, it's the backbone of our next-gen platform." She spoke from Solace's Austin headquarters during a press call Friday afternoon.

4/ Industry watchers note Solace now directly competes with Chicago-based Marlow Automation, which itself absorbed a smaller rival, GridPoint Robotics, back in 2021.

5/ Solace shares jumped 11 percent on the Nasdaq after the announcement, giving the company a market value near $1.3 billion.

Cleveland-based Parkline Industrial Corp. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Boyd Machining Group, a Wichita, Kansas-based supplier of precision-milled components, for $142 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by December 15, 2024, will make Boyd Machining a wholly owned subsidiary of Parkline Industrial. Chief Executive Officer Marissa Tolan said the acquisition strengthens Parkline's position in the aerospace-parts market, where it competes with Danfield Aerotech and Ruskin Manufacturing. "Boyd Machining brings forty years of manufacturing expertise and a loyal customer base in the defense sector," Tolan said during a call with investors from Parkline's headquarters in Cleveland, Ohio. Boyd Machining's founder, Walter Boyd, who started the company in 1984, will stay on as a senior advisor through 2025. Parkline shares rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.20. Analysts at Greenpoint Capital, including senior analyst Rajiv Mehta, said the deal could add roughly $30 million to Parkline's annual revenue. The transaction, funded partly through a $90 million loan from First Meridian Bank, marks Parkline's third acquisition in two years, after purchasing Talbot Fasteners in 2022 and Colston Hydraulics in 2023. Parkline employs about 4,200 workers across twelve facilities in the United States and Mexico. The company plans to retain all 310 Boyd Machining employees at its Wichita plant. Trading of Parkline stock was heavier than usual, with over 2.1 million shares changing hands by early afternoon.

DENVER, Colorado -- Rocky Mountain Brewing Co. announced Tuesday that it has acquired Front Range Ciderworks, a smaller craft producer based in Boulder, for $42 million in cash and stock. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing on October 14, marks Rocky Mountain Brewing's third acquisition since 2021 and is expected to close by December 1, pending regulatory approval.

CEO Marisol Andrade said the acquisition will expand the company's distribution network across Colorado, Utah, and New Mexico, adding roughly 3.2 million cases of annual production capacity. "Front Range Ciderworks built something special over the last nine years, and we intend to preserve that identity," Andrade told reporters gathered at the company's headquarters in Denver.

Front Range Ciderworks founder Tobias Wren, who started the company in 2015 with his sister Elena Wren, will stay on as an advisor for eighteen months under the terms of the agreement. Elena Wren, who currently serves as head of production, is expected to leave the company in January to launch a new venture.

Analysts at Highline Capital Partners estimate the combined company could generate $310 million in revenue next year, up 18 percent from current levels. Shares of Rocky Mountain Brewing, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker RMBC, rose 6.4 percent to $28.90 following the announcement. Competitor Alpine Peak Beverages, headquartered in Fort Collins, declined to comment on the deal.

DETROIT, Mich. — Vantage Motors Inc. announced Tuesday that it will acquire electric-vehicle battery maker Solaris Cell Corp. for $2.4 billion, in a deal expected to close by December 15, 2024. The agreement, disclosed at a press conference in Detroit, marks Vantage Motors' largest acquisition since its founding in 1987 by industrialist Harold Bregman.

Under terms of the deal, Vantage Motors will pay Solaris Cell shareholders in a mix of cash and stock. Solaris Cell, headquartered in Austin, Texas, was founded in 2015 by engineer Priya Nandakumar, who will join Vantage Motors as Chief Technology Officer effective January 6, 2025. Nandakumar previously served as Solaris Cell's Chief Executive Officer for nine years.

"This acquisition strengthens our supply chain and accelerates our transition to electric vehicles," said Marcus Webb, Chief Executive Officer of Vantage Motors, during the announcement.

Solaris Cell employs roughly 1,200 workers across two facilities, including its main plant in Round Rock, Texas. Analysts at Bristow Capital Partners estimate the deal could raise Vantage Motors' market share in the battery sector by 8 percent. Shares of Vantage Motors rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Solaris Cell's private valuation reportedly climbed to match the offer price.

Regulators at the Federal Trade Commission are expected to review the transaction before final approval. Vantage Motors said it does not anticipate antitrust concerns given limited market overlap between the two companies.

Case No. RG24-118834

On March 14, 2024, Judge Marlene Whitfield presided over the sentencing hearing of defendant Trevor Ashcombe, 41, at the Rene C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, California. Ashcombe, former Chief Financial Officer of Baycrest Logistics Inc., pleaded guilty on January 9, 2024, to one count of wire fraud in violation of federal law after prosecutor Diane Kessler of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office presented evidence that he diverted $2.3 million from company accounts between 2019 and 2022.

Judge Whitfield sentenced Ashcombe to 46 months in federal prison followed by three years of supervised release, and ordered restitution of $2.1 million to Baycrest Logistics Inc. Defense attorney Roland Pierce argued for leniency, citing his client's cooperation with investigators from the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

Baycrest Logistics Inc., headquartered in San Leandro, California, is a subsidiary of Meridian Transport Group. Company spokesperson Ana Reyes stated that the firm has since implemented new internal controls. The case was investigated jointly by the FBI and the California Department of Justice, with agents arresting Ashcombe on October 3, 2023, at his residence in Pleasanton on charges of wire fraud and embezzlement.

Ashcombe is scheduled to report to a federal facility in Lompoc by April 15, 2024. His attorney has indicated an intent to appeal the restitution order.

Pixelbook Labs, a Portland-based startup founded by Nadia Ferris in 2019, launched its second-generation e-reader, the Quillion Slate 2, on March 11, 2024. Priced at $249, the device features a 10.3-inch E Ink screen, 32 GB of storage, and a battery Pixelbook Labs claims lasts six weeks on a single charge. I tested the Quillion Slate 2 for three weeks in Portland, Oregon, and came away impressed, though not without reservations.

The screen is genuinely excellent, rendering text with a crispness that rivals Amazon's Kindle Oasis. Page turns feel instantaneous, a marked improvement over the original Quillion Slate, which shipped in 2021 with a noticeably sluggish refresh rate. Pixelbook Labs also added USB-C charging, finally abandoning the micro-USB port that frustrated reviewers two years ago.

Where the Quillion Slate 2 stumbles is software. The store interface, built on a customized version of Android, crashed twice during my testing, once while I was browsing titles from Penguin Random House. Customer support, reached by phone on March 20, told me a patch was already in development.

At $249, the Quillion Slate 2 competes directly with the $269 Kobo Libra Colour and undercuts the $299 Kindle Oasis. CEO Nadia Ferris told me in an interview that Pixelbook Labs sold 40,000 units in the first week alone, a figure that, if accurate, suggests real momentum for a company competing against giants like Amazon and Rakuten's Kobo. For readers willing to tolerate occasional software hiccups, the Quillion Slate 2 is, on balance, a strong value.

input: Pixel Watch 3, Google's latest wearable, went on sale at Best Buy stores across the United States on September 10, 2024, priced at $349.99 for the 41mm Wi-Fi model. I have worn the review unit, provided by Google's Mountain View headquarters, for eleven days while training for the Chicago Marathon, and the improvements over the Pixel Watch 2 are noticeable but incremental. Rick Osterloh, Google's senior vice president of devices, told reporters at a briefing in San Francisco that the new Actua 360 display is 10 percent brighter than last year's panel, and battery life now stretches to 36 hours with the always-on screen disabled. Loss of Pulse Detection, a feature that automatically contacts emergency services, worked as advertised during a treadmill test at a gym in Austin, Texas, though it took nearly ninety seconds to trigger. The included charging cable is now magnetic and charges the device to 50 percent in about thirty minutes, a genuine improvement over the old puck. Fitbit, a Google subsidiary based in San Francisco, supplies the health-tracking software that powers sleep scores and cardio load metrics. My chief complaint is price: at $349.99, the watch costs $50 more than the Apple Watch Series 9 sold by Apple Inc, and the Wear OS 5 app ecosystem still lags behind watchOS. For runners already inside the Google ecosystem, the Pixel Watch 3 is a solid, if expensive, upgrade; for everyone else, the competition remains more compelling.

Marguerite Ferrand (born 14 March 1927 in Lyon, France; died 8 September 2011 in Geneva, Switzerland) was a French-Swiss biochemist known for isolating the enzyme complex later marketed as Lyzavor. She earned her doctorate in biochemistry from the University of Lyon in 1951 and joined the Pasteur Institute in Paris as a research fellow the following year. In 1958 Ferrand moved to Geneva to take up a position as Director of Research at Novabiotique SA, a pharmaceutical firm headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, founded in 1949 by industrialist Henri Lachaux. Under her leadership, Novabiotique SA developed Lyzavor, an antibacterial compound that received approval from Swiss health authorities in 1963 and generated an estimated 40 million Swiss francs in revenue by 1970. Ferrand married fellow chemist Paul Ferrand in 1955, and the couple had one daughter, Claire Ferrand, born in 1959 in Geneva. In 1972 Novabiotique SA was acquired by the German conglomerate Baumeister Chemie AG for 210 million Swiss francs, after which Ferrand resigned from her post, citing disagreements over research funding. She subsequently became a professor at the University of Geneva in 1973, a position she held for two decades. In 1988 she received the Marcel Benoist Prize for her contributions to pharmaceutical science, awarded in Bern by the Swiss federal government. Ferrand retired in 1993 and remained in Geneva until her death at age 84.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Aston Villa defeated Chelsea 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, powered by a second-half brace from striker Ollie Watkins. The 27-year-old forward scored in the 58th and 71st minutes, taking his Premier League tally to eight goals this season. Midfielder Youri Tielemans opened the scoring for Villa in the 22nd minute with a curling shot from outside the box, before Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson equalized in the 40th minute. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's resilience after the match, telling reporters, "We showed character today, and Ollie was clinical when it mattered." Chelsea head coach Mauricio Pochettino acknowledged his team's defensive lapses, saying the club must "fix these mistakes quickly" ahead of their Champions League fixture against RB Leipzig on October 24. The win moved Aston Villa to third place in the Premier League table with 21 points from nine games, three points behind leaders Manchester City. Villa Park, which holds just over 42,000 spectators, was near capacity with an announced attendance of 41,912. Aston Villa's next league match is scheduled for October 21 against Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium in west London. Meanwhile, Chelsea, who have now lost four of their opening nine matches, face mounting pressure, with the London club currently sitting twelfth in the standings under owner Todd Boehly.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., June 4, 2024 - Meridian Biotherapeutics, Inc. announced today that it has acquired NovaGen Diagnostics, a privately held genomics startup based in Austin, Texas, for approximately $340 million in cash and stock. The transaction closed on June 3, 2024, following approval from regulators at the Federal Trade Commission.

Under the agreement, Meridian Biotherapeutics will integrate NovaGen Diagnostics as a wholly owned subsidiary, retaining its Austin facility and its 210 employees. Dr. Priya Nathan, founder and chief executive officer of NovaGen Diagnostics, will join Meridian Biotherapeutics as Executive Vice President of Genomic Sciences, reporting directly to Meridian's chief executive officer, Thomas Reilly.

"This acquisition strengthens our diagnostics pipeline and accelerates our entry into precision oncology," said Thomas Reilly, speaking at a press conference held at Meridian's headquarters in Cambridge. "Priya and her team have built something remarkable, and we are thrilled to welcome them."

NovaGen Diagnostics was founded in 2016 by Dr. Priya Nathan and Dr. Samuel Ortiz, who previously worked together at Stanford University. The company's flagship product, the GenoScan 3000, is used in more than 400 hospitals across North America to detect early-stage genetic mutations linked to breast cancer.

Meridian Biotherapeutics, listed on the Nasdaq under ticker symbol MDBT, reported revenue of $1.2 billion in fiscal year 2023. The company expects the NovaGen deal to add $85 million in annual revenue beginning in fiscal year 2025. Analysts at Goldman Sachs called the acquisition "a shrewd strategic move" in a note published Tuesday.

Ingrid Falk (born 12 March 1958 in Malmö, Sweden) is a Swedish biochemist known for her contributions to enzyme engineering. She earned a doctorate in biochemistry from Lund University in 1985 and joined Novo Nordisk in Bagsværd, Denmark as a Research Scientist in 1988. In 1994 Falk was promoted to Director of Enzyme Research, a position she held for eleven years while leading studies on lipase catalysis published in the Journal of Molecular Catalysis.

In 2001 Falk co-founded Nordic Enzymatics AB in Lund together with her colleague Dr. Peter Ahlgren, aiming to commercialize industrial biocatalysts. The company was acquired by Novozymes A/S for 340 million Swedish kronor in September 2006, after which Falk left Novo Nordisk to become Chief Scientific Officer at Novozymes, headquartered in Bagsværd. She held that role until her retirement in 2015.

Falk was married to fellow chemist Dr. Erik Falk from 1983 until his death in 2010; the couple had one son, Anders Falk, born in 1986. In 2012 she received the Anders Jahre Award for Medical Research from the University of Oslo in recognition of her enzyme research, presented at a ceremony in Oslo. Falk is a member of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences and continues to lecture occasionally at Lund University. She currently resides in Malmö, Sweden.

DETROIT, Sept. 12 -- Stellantis NV said Thursday it will acquire EV battery startup Voltaris Energy Inc. for $1.2 billion in cash, a move aimed at securing lithium-ion supply for its Jeep and Ram truck lines. Chief Executive Carlos Tavares announced the deal at a press conference in Auburn Hills, Michigan, alongside Voltaris founder and CEO Renee Okafor, who will join Stellantis as Senior Vice President of Battery Technology starting October 1.

Under the agreement, Stellantis will pay $800 million upfront and the remaining $400 million tied to production milestones through 2027. Voltaris, founded in 2019 in Palo Alto, California, operates a 300,000-square-foot factory in Reno, Nevada, that currently supplies battery cells to competitor Rivian Automotive. Analysts at Morgan Stanley said the acquisition would give Stellantis roughly 40 percent of the battery capacity it needs for North American EV output by 2028.

Shares of Stellantis rose 3.4 percent to $18.75 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of privately held Voltaris were not publicly traded. The transaction, expected to close by December 15, still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Tavares said the Reno plant would add 650 jobs over the next two years, with hiring to begin in January.

Okafor, a former Tesla battery engineer, said the deal would let Voltaris scale production "far faster than we could alone." Stellantis, headquartered in Amsterdam, Netherlands, also owns brands including Chrysler, Dodge, and Peugeot.

DETROIT, Mich. — Automotive supplier Cascade Axle Corp. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $410 million in outstanding debt and a sharp decline in orders from General Motors, one of its largest customers. The filing was submitted in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan.

Cascade Axle, headquartered in Warren, Michigan, employs roughly 2,300 workers across four plants in Michigan, Ohio, and Indiana. CEO Martin Feld told reporters the company plans to continue operations during restructuring and expects to emerge from bankruptcy by early 2026. "We are committed to protecting jobs while we restructure our balance sheet," Feld said during a press briefing at the company's Warren headquarters.

The bankruptcy follows a turbulent year for Cascade Axle, which lost a supply contract with Ford Motor Company in March after a dispute over part defects that led to a recall of 85,000 F-150 trucks. Analysts at Moody's downgraded the company's credit rating twice in 2024.

United Auto Workers Local 1264 President Denise Okafor said the union would fight to preserve pension benefits for retirees. "Our members built this company," Okafor said Wednesday outside the Warren plant. "They deserve better than layoffs."

General Motors said in a statement it is monitoring the situation but has already begun shifting some axle orders to a competing supplier, Linden Drivetrain Systems, based in Toledo, Ohio. Cascade Axle's stock, which traded at $2.15 per share Monday, fell 61 percent to $0.84 after the announcement.

Defense attorney Marcus Feld had requested leniency, citing his client's lack of prior convictions, but Judge Marquez rejected the request, calling the attack "calculated and brutal." Calloway was arrested by Phoenix Police detectives on October 12, 2023, three days after the assault, following a tip from a pawn shop employee who recognized stolen tools matching the warehouse inventory. Sonora Freight Logistics, headquartered in Tucson, issued a statement thanking the Phoenix Police Department and the Maricopa County Attorney's Office for their work on the case.

Halcyon, founded in 2016 by Dr. Vasquez, employs 85 researchers and holds three patents related to its lead compound, HX-221, currently in Phase II clinical trials. Meridian expects the transaction to close fully by October 1, 2024, pending customary regulatory approvals.

DETROIT, Mich. — Vantis Motors announced Tuesday it will acquire electric drivetrain startup CoreVolt Systems for $412 million in cash, a move the automaker says will accelerate its transition to electric vehicles. The deal, disclosed at a press conference at Vantis Motors' headquarters in Dearborn, Michigan, is expected to close by December 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Vantis Motors CEO Elena Marsh said the acquisition of CoreVolt Systems, founded in 2018 by engineer Raj Patel, would bring roughly 340 employees and 12 patents into the company. "CoreVolt's battery management technology is years ahead of anything we've built internally," Marsh told reporters.

CoreVolt Systems, based in Austin, Texas, has supplied battery components to smaller manufacturers including Halden Auto and Persio Electric since 2021. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners estimate the deal values CoreVolt at nearly 18 times its 2023 revenue of $23 million.

Shares of Vantis Motors rose 6.4 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.10. Patel, who will join Vantis as Chief Technology Officer effective January 6, 2025, said the merger would let his team "scale battery innovation to millions of vehicles."

The move intensifies competition with rival automaker Northgate Auto, which last month announced its own $300 million investment in solid-state battery research. Vantis Motors expects the CoreVolt deal to reduce battery production costs by roughly 15 percent within two years.

Pixel Fold 2 Review: Google Refines the Formula

Mountain View, CA -- On October 3, 2024, Google released the Pixel Fold 2, its second-generation foldable smartphone, priced at $1,899 for the 256GB model. I have used it daily for three weeks and came away impressed, though not without reservations.

The hinge, redesigned by Google's hardware team in Taiwan, feels sturdier than the original 2023 Pixel Fold. Rick Osterloh, Google's Senior Vice President of Devices and Services, said in a briefing at the Mountain View campus that the company "rebuilt the durability testing rig from scratch" after customer complaints last year. The device runs on the Tensor G4 chip, manufactured by Samsung Foundry in South Korea, and ships with Android 15.

Battery life is the standout upgrade: 5,015 mAh, up 18 percent from last year's 4,300 mAh cell, giving roughly 26 hours of mixed use. The 8-inch inner display and 6.3-inch cover screen are both bright enough for outdoor use in direct sunlight, something I tested extensively near San Francisco Bay.

Competition is fierce. Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 6, released in July 2024, remains the market leader, and Honor's Magic V3 undercuts both on weight. Still, Google's software polish, including seamless multitasking between the two screens, gives the Pixel Fold 2 an edge for anyone already inside the Google ecosystem.

At $1,899, this is not a casual purchase. But for enthusiasts wanting a genuine flagship foldable from Google, this is the most complete effort yet. I'm giving it 4 out of 5 stars.

input: MANCHESTER, England -- October 14, 2024 -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side defeated Newcastle United 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, moving Villa into fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 12th minute, converting a low cross from midfielder Youri Tielemans, before doubling his tally just before halftime with a header from a corner kick. Newcastle pulled one back through striker Alexander Isak in the 58th minute, but substitute Leon Bailey restored Villa's two-goal cushion in the 81st minute with a curling effort from outside the box. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his team's discipline after the match, telling reporters at the post-match press conference, "We controlled the tempo for long periods, and Ollie's movement was outstanding." Newcastle manager Eddie Howe acknowledged his side's slow start, saying the team would review the performance before their next fixture against Chelsea on October 21. The win extended Aston Villa's unbeaten run to eight matches across all competitions, a stretch that began in August. Villa Park, which holds just over 42,000 spectators, recorded an attendance of 41,875 for the fixture. Aston Villa's next match will be a UEFA Champions League group stage clash against Bayern Munich on October 29 in Munich, Germany.

Rocky Peak, founded in 2011 by entrepreneur Daniel Ortiz in Boulder, Colorado, employs 210 people and operates a single production facility in Longmont. Whitfield added that Meridian plans two more acquisitions in the natural foods space before the end of next year.

Ingrid Halvorsen (born 14 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cold-water coral reefs. She earned a doctorate from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Norwegian Institute of Marine Research the same year as a research scientist. In 1994 Halvorsen became Head of the Deep-Sea Ecology Division, a position she held for eleven years. Her fieldwork off the coast of Trondheim led to the 1998 discovery of an extensive Lophelia pertusa reef system, later protected under Norway's Marine Resources Act. Halvorsen married fellow oceanographer Erik Solberg in 1990; their daughter, Kaja Solberg, was born in Bergen in 1993 and now works as a marine policy advisor for the European Commission in Brussels. In 2003 Halvorsen received the Nansen Award from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to deep-sea conservation. She stepped down from her division role in 2005 to become a professor at the University of Bergen, a post she held until her retirement in 2020. During her academic career she published more than 90 papers and mentored dozens of graduate students. In 2011 she was elected to the Royal Norwegian Society of Sciences and Letters. Halvorsen currently resides in Bergen, where she continues to advise the Institute of Marine Research on conservation policy for Norway's continental shelf.

BOSTON, Massachusetts -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital reported on March 14, 2024 that a novel oral compound, designated MGH-2201, reduced fasting glucose levels by 38 percent in a Phase 2 trial involving 214 adults with type 2 diabetes. The randomized, double-blind study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez and funded by a $12 million grant from the National Institutes of Health, was conducted across three sites: Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston, Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles, and the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. Participants received either MGH-2201 or a placebo daily for 24 weeks. Dr. Vasquez, an endocrinologist and professor at Harvard Medical School, presented the findings at the American Diabetes Association's annual meeting in Chicago on June 21, 2024. "We observed a statistically significant reduction in HbA1c levels among patients treated with MGH-2201, with minimal gastrointestinal side effects compared to metformin," Vasquez said. The compound, a small-molecule inhibitor of the SGLT2 protein, was originally synthesized by chemist Raj Patel at Cambridge-based biotech firm Glyphex Therapeutics, which licensed the molecule to Massachusetts General Hospital for clinical development in 2021. Novartis has since expressed interest in acquiring exclusive commercialization rights, according to a person familiar with the negotiations. If approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, MGH-2201 could become a competitor to Jardiance, manufactured by Boehringer Ingelheim. A Phase 3 trial enrolling 1,800 patients is expected to begin in January 2025 at sites across the United States and Germany. The research team also reported two serious adverse events, including one case of ketoacidosis, though investigators concluded the events were not directly attributable to the drug. Full results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine on June 22, 2024.

SUPERIOR COURT OF SANTA CLARA COUNTY, CALIFORNIA

Case No. 24-CV-118823

On March 11, 2024, Judge Patricia Alvarado presided over a sentencing hearing in the matter of the State of California v. Dennis Whitfield at the San Jose Hall of Justice in San Jose, California. Dennis Whitfield, 47, formerly a senior accountant at Meridian Capital Group, was convicted on February 6, 2024 of embezzlement after prosecutor Gregory Nunes of the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office proved that Whitfield diverted $1,240,000 from client accounts between January 2019 and October 2023.

Judge Alvarado sentenced Whitfield to six years in state prison and ordered restitution of $980,000 to be paid to the victims, including retiree Helen Cortez of Sunnyvale. Defense attorney Rosalind Park argued for leniency, citing her client's cooperation with investigators, but the court rejected the request.

Meridian Capital Group, headquartered in Palo Alto, California, issued a statement confirming that Whitfield was terminated from his position as Senior Accountant on November 2, 2023, immediately after the firm's internal audit uncovered irregularities. The company said it had already reimbursed $600,000 to affected clients through its insurer, Pacific Assurance Corporation.

Whitfield was arrested by detectives of the San Jose Police Department on November 15, 2023, at his residence in Los Gatos. He will be transferred to Elmwood Correctional Facility to begin serving his sentence.

DENVER, Colorado -- Trailhead Robotics Inc., a maker of autonomous warehouse forklifts, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired competitor PalletWorks Systems LLC for $142 million in cash and stock. The deal, disclosed at Trailhead's headquarters in Denver, is expected to close by November 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Under the agreement, Trailhead will pay PalletWorks shareholders $95 million in cash and issue roughly $47 million worth of Trailhead common stock. PalletWorks, founded in 2016 by engineer Marisol Vega, employs about 210 people at its facility in Austin, Texas, and generated $38 million in revenue last year.

"This acquisition strengthens our supply chain and lets us scale faster," said Dennis Okafor, Trailhead's chief executive officer, during a press call from Denver. Okafor added that PalletWorks' chief technology officer, Priya Ramaswamy, will join Trailhead as senior vice president of engineering starting December 1, 2024.

Trailhead's shares rose 6.3 percent on the Nasdaq exchange following the announcement, closing at $54.10. Analysts at Kestrel Capital Partners called the move a defensive play against larger rival Boston Dynamics, which has expanded aggressively into logistics automation.

The combined company will operate under the Trailhead Robotics name and will maintain offices in both Denver and Austin. Vega, who will step down as PalletWorks' chief executive officer once the deal closes, said in a statement that she plans to start a new venture focused on agricultural robotics in 2025.

Trailhead was founded in 2011 by siblings Carla and Jonah Whitfield and currently employs 1,400 people worldwide.

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY

On March 14, 2024, Judge Patricia Neal Aldrich sentenced Marcus D. Ellery, 41, of Newark, New Jersey, to seven years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of aggravated assault stemming from an incident outside the Ironbound Athletic Club on October 2, 2023. Prosecutor Denise Farrow of the Essex County Prosecutor's Office argued that Ellery struck victim Raymond Colt Whitfield with a tire iron during a dispute in the parking lot, causing a fractured skull and permanent hearing loss. Whitfield, 37, was hospitalized at University Hospital in Newark for eleven days.

Ellery was arrested on October 5, 2023, by detectives from the Newark Police Department after Whitfield identified him from surveillance footage. He was formally charged on November 1, 2023, with aggravated assault and possession of a weapon for unlawful purposes. During the trial, which opened on February 12, 2024, defense attorney Gordon Pelham of Pelham & Ruiz LLP contended that Ellery acted in self-defense, but the jury, under Judge Aldrich's instruction, rejected the claim after four hours of deliberation.

In addition to the prison term, Judge Aldrich ordered Ellery to pay $85,000 in restitution to Whitfield for medical expenses and lost wages. The New Jersey Department of Corrections confirmed Ellery will be held at Northern State Prison in Newark. Farrow stated the sentence "reflects the severity of the injuries inflicted" and thanked the Newark Police Department for its investigation.

input: Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1958 in Turin, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques for historic masonry buildings. She earned her Laurea in Civil Engineering from the Politecnico di Torino in 1981 and later completed a doctorate at ETH Zurich in 1986. In 1990 Marchetti joined Studio Ingegneria Rossi in Milan as a Senior Structural Engineer, where she worked for eleven years on infrastructure projects across northern Italy. In 2001 she left the firm to found Marchetti & Partners, an engineering consultancy headquartered in Bologna, Italy, focused on retrofitting bridges and cathedrals damaged by earthquakes. Her firm led the reinforcement of the Basilica di San Petronio following the 2012 Emilia earthquake, a project funded in part by a grant of 4.2 million euros from the Italian Ministry of Culture. In 2015 Marchetti was elected President of the European Association for Earthquake Engineering during its congress in Istanbul, Turkey, a position she held until 2019. For her contributions to seismic safety, she received the Fritz London Award from the International Society for Structural Engineers in Vienna, Austria, on 9 October 2018. Marchetti married fellow engineer Paolo Conti in 1988; the couple have one son, Marco Conti, born in 1991. She currently lives in Bologna and continues to consult for UNESCO on the preservation of earthquake-prone heritage sites in the Mediterranean region.

DENVER, Colorado — Sterling Ridge Foods Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Boulder Grain Collective LLC, a privately held organic pasta maker, for $142 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing at the company's headquarters in Denver, is expected to close by March 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Under the terms of the agreement, Sterling Ridge will pay Boulder Grain Collective's founder and chief executive officer, Marcus Whitfield, $38 million personally as part of the transaction, according to filings reviewed by Reuters. Whitfield founded Boulder Grain Collective in 2011 and grew the company into a supplier for regional retailers including Front Range Markets.

"This acquisition strengthens our position in the premium organic segment," said Elena Vasquez, chief executive officer of Sterling Ridge Foods, during the briefing. Vasquez, who has led Sterling Ridge since 2019, added that the combined company expects annual revenue of roughly $610 million.

Analysts at Highgate Capital Partners estimated the deal represents a 22 percent premium over Boulder Grain Collective's most recent private valuation. Shares of Sterling Ridge Foods, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker SRFI, rose 4.6 percent to $57.20 following the announcement.

Whitfield is expected to join Sterling Ridge's board of directors and will step down as chief executive officer of Boulder Grain Collective once the deal closes. The company plans to retain all 260 employees at Boulder Grain Collective's production facility in Longmont, Colorado.

Portland-based Cascade Robotics Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Nimbus Drone Systems, a Seattle drone-technology startup, for $84 million in cash and stock. Nimbus Drone Systems, founded in 2018 by engineer David Okafor, employs 62 people and specializes in autonomous delivery drones used by logistics firms across the Pacific Northwest. Tan said the acquisition will let Cascade Robotics expand into commercial aerial logistics, a market it currently does not serve. "Nimbus brings technology we simply could not build fast enough on our own," Tan said during a press briefing at Cascade Robotics' headquarters in Portland, Oregon. Meredith Okafor (born March 14, 1968, in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-British structural engineer known for pioneering earthquake-resistant design in West African construction. She earned her degree in civil engineering from Imperial College London in 1990 and joined Arup in 1993 as a junior engineer. In 2001 Okafor left Arup to found Terraform Structural Consultants, headquartered in Lagos, Nigeria, with an initial team of eleven engineers. Under her leadership as Managing Director, the firm designed the retrofitting of the Third Mainland Bridge in 2007 and later expanded operations to Accra, Ghana in 2012. Terraform Structural Consultants merged with the British firm Hendricks & Vane in Lagos in March 2015, forming Hendricks Terraform Ltd. Okafor became Chief Executive Officer of the merged entity, a position she held until stepping down in June 2019 to join the University of Lagos as a professor of civil engineering. In November 2020, Okafor received the Prince Philip Medal from the Royal Academy of Engineering in London for her contributions to sustainable infrastructure in developing economies. She is married to architect David Bello, whom she met while working on the Third Mainland Bridge project, and the couple has two children. Okafor currently divides her time between Lagos and Cambridge, where she holds a visiting fellowship at Cambridge University. She has published over forty papers on seismic-resistant design and continues to advise the Nigerian Ministry of Works on national infrastructure standards.

BOSTON, MA -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced on March 14, 2024 the results of a phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolerabin-9, an experimental chemical compound designed to inhibit tumor growth in patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The trial, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Germany between January 2022 and September 2023. According to the study published in The Lancet Oncology, patients receiving tolerabin-9 in combination with gemcitabine showed a median overall survival of 11.4 months, compared to 7.8 months in the control group receiving standard chemotherapy alone, representing a 32 percent reduction in mortality risk. Dr. Marchetti presented the findings at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting in Chicago on June 2, 2024. "These results suggest a meaningful shift in how we approach pancreatic cancer treatment," she said during the press briefing. The trial was funded by a $48 million grant from the National Institutes of Health and co-sponsored by Vertex Pharmaceuticals, a biotechnology company headquartered in Boston. Dr. Rajiv Nair, chief medical officer at Vertex Pharmaceuticals, stated that the company plans to file for FDA approval by early 2025. Adverse events included grade 3 neutropenia in 18 percent of patients and mild peripheral neuropathy in 9 percent. No treatment-related deaths were reported. Vertex shares rose 6 percent following the announcement. The research team plans a phase 3 trial involving approximately 600 patients beginning in November 2024, with additional sites planned in France and Japan.

input: The Ontario Ministry of Transportation announced on June 4, 2024 that it will invest $128 million to rehabilitate the Garden City Skyway in St. Catharines, a critical bridge along the Queen Elizabeth Way. Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria said the project, to be carried out by Aecon Group Inc., will begin on July 15, 2024 and is expected to conclude by October 2026. "This funding reflects our government's commitment to keeping Ontario moving," Sarkaria told reporters at a press conference in Niagara Falls. The bridge, built in 1963, carries approximately 55,000 vehicles daily and has shown signs of structural deterioration, according to a 2023 inspection report from the ministry's engineering division. Aecon Group Inc. was selected following a competitive bidding process that concluded in March 2024, beating out rival firm Dufferin Construction. Under the contract, Aecon will replace deck joints, repair concrete piers, and install a new drainage system. Local officials, including St. Catharines Mayor Mat Siscoe, welcomed the announcement, noting that lane closures during construction will be minimized during peak summer tourist season. The Ministry of Transportation noted that similar rehabilitation work was completed on the Burlington Bay James N. Allan Skyway in 2021 at a cost of $92 million. Sarkaria added that the province has allocated a further $2.1 billion for bridge and highway maintenance across Ontario through 2027, as part of the broader Building Ontario's Future plan announced last year.

input: BOSTON, MA - September 12, 2023 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced today the results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolerabine, an experimental small-molecule inhibitor developed by Cambridge-based biotechnology firm Solenta Therapeutics, for the treatment of moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The randomized, double-blind study enrolled 214 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2021 and June 2022. Dr. Amara Chen, the trial's principal investigator and a professor of rheumatology at Harvard Medical School, reported that 61 percent of patients receiving tolerabine achieved a 50 percent reduction in disease activity by week 24, compared with 23 percent in the placebo group. The most common adverse events were mild headache and nausea, with only 4 percent of participants discontinuing treatment due to side effects. Solenta Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by immunologist Dr. Rafael Ortiz, raised $85 million in a Series C funding round led by Kestrel Capital Partners in January 2023 to support late-stage development of the drug. The company plans to begin a Phase 3 trial in early 2024, pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Dr. Chen presented the findings on September 11, 2023 at the American College of Rheumatology's annual meeting in San Diego, California, where the data were met with cautious optimism from attending specialists. Novartis, a competitor developing a similar JAK-inhibitor class drug, declined to comment on the results. If approved, tolerabine would become Solenta's first commercial product since the company's inception seven years ago.

event: American College of Rheumatology's annual meeting

input: Kestrel Optics of Bend, Oregon introduces the Talon X4 Rangefinder Binoculars, launching October 14, 2024 at a retail price of $449.99. Built for hunters and competitive shooters, the Talon X4 pairs 10x42 magnification with a laser rangefinder accurate to 1,200 yards. The rugged magnesium-alloy housing is rated IPX7 waterproof and has survived internal drop tests from 5 feet onto concrete. Each unit ships with a padded case, a microfiber cloth, a CR2 battery, and a limited 3-year warranty. Kestrel Optics was founded in 2011 by former Bushnell engineer Marcus Iverson, who serves as the company's Chief Product Officer. Early reviewers, including outdoor writer Dana Whitfield of Field & Stride Magazine, praised the Talon X4's fast target acquisition, noting it locks onto a deer-sized target in under 0.3 seconds. The unit weighs just 26 ounces and includes Bluetooth 5.0 connectivity, allowing hunters to sync range data to the companion app on iOS and Android devices. Kestrel Optics currently sells the Talon X4 exclusively through its website and at Cabela's stores across the United States, with plans to expand distribution to Canada by early 2025. Customers who purchase before November 1, 2024 will receive a free carrying harness worth $29.99. Stock is limited to 5,000 units for this initial release, and the company expects a second production run in Q1 2025 to meet demand following strong preorder numbers of over 1,800 units in the first week alone.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tovorafenib, an oral RAF kinase inhibitor, in pediatric patients with relapsed low-grade glioma. The study, led by Dr. Priya Nathan and presented at the American Association for Cancer Research annual meeting in San Diego, enrolled 76 children between ages 2 and 17 across 14 sites in the United States and Canada. Participants received 380 mg/m2 of tovorafenib weekly for up to 24 months. According to the report, 51 patients, or 67 percent, achieved a confirmed objective response, with a median duration of response of 16.6 months. The most common adverse events were elevated liver enzymes and hair color changes, reported in roughly 30 percent of patients; three children discontinued treatment due to grade 3 toxicity. Dr. Nathan noted that tovorafenib, developed by Day One Biopharmaceuticals of Brisbane, California, received accelerated approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration on April 23, 2024, under the brand name Ojemda, marking the first systemic therapy specifically approved for this pediatric population. Day One Biopharmaceuticals was founded in 2018 by Jeremy Bender and is headquartered in Brisbane, California. The company's shares rose 12 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement. Co-investigator Dr. Samuel Okafor of the Hospital for Sick Children in Toronto said longer follow-up is needed to assess durability of response and long-term neurocognitive outcomes. Funding for the trial was provided by the National Cancer Institute and Day One Biopharmaceuticals under a $14 million research grant.

input: Ingrid Solberg (born 14 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist and oceanographer best known for her research on cold-water coral ecosystems in the North Atlantic. She earned her doctorate in marine biology from the University of Bergen in 1986 and joined the Institute of Marine Research (Havforskningsinstituttet) in Bergen the same year as a research scientist. In 1994, Solberg became Head of the Deep-Sea Ecology Department at the Institute of Marine Research, a position she held for eleven years. Her 1999 monograph, The Hidden Reefs, documented the discovery of a 40-kilometer coral reef system off the coast of Trondheim and is widely credited with prompting Norway to establish the Sula Reef Marine Protected Area in 2002. In 2007, Solberg left the Institute of Marine Research to become a professor at the University of Tromso, where she led the Arctic Benthic Ecosystems research group. She married fellow oceanographer Torstein Aas in 1990, and the couple had one daughter, Kari Aas, born in 1993 in Tromso. In November 2015, Solberg received the Nansen Award, presented by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo, for her contributions to marine conservation. She retired from active fieldwork in 2020 but continues to publish, and in 2023 she was appointed as an advisor to the Norwegian Ministry of Climate and Environment.
