Sacramento Sting Ends Drought With Overtime Thriller

SACRAMENTO, Calif. — October 14, 2023 — The Sacramento Sting defeated the Portland Timberwolves 89-86 in overtime on Saturday at Golden Oak Arena, snapping a seven-game losing streak that had stretched back to September 2nd. Point guard Malik Foreman scored a career-high 27 points, including the go-ahead three-pointer with 12 seconds left in the extra period.

Head coach Denise Aldridge, who took over the Sting in July 2022, praised her team's defense after the game. "We finally executed down the stretch," she said in a postgame press conference. "This win belongs to the guys who kept believing."

The Timberwolves, led by forward Curtis Brannigan's 24 points, had a chance to win at the buzzer, but Brannigan's fadeaway shot rimmed out. Portland general manager Selena Whitfield declined to comment on whether the loss would affect coach Terry Nakamura's job security.

The victory improved Sacramento's record to 3-8 on the season, while Portland fell to 6-5. The Sting's next game is scheduled for October 19 against the Denver Peaks at the Mile High Pavilion in Denver, Colorado. League officials from the National Basketball Confederation confirmed that Saturday's attendance of 14,320 set a new record for Golden Oak Arena.

Foreman, a 24-year-old guard originally from Baton Rouge, Louisiana, was named the game's Most Valuable Player by broadcaster SportsNet West, earning a $500 bonus under his contract incentive clause.

Lenovo launched the ThinkPad X1 Fold Gen 3 on September 12, 2024, at an event in Chicago, and I have spent three weeks testing the $2,499 unit provided by the company. The 16.3-inch OLED panel folds into a 12.7-inch tablet, and Lenovo's engineering lead, Priya Nandakumar, told reporters the hinge was rated for 30,000 folds. Under the hood sits a Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite chip paired with 32GB of RAM, delivering roughly 14 hours of battery life in my mixed-use tests, a modest 8 percent improvement over last year's Gen 2 model. Lenovo, headquartered in Beijing, faces stiff competition from HP and its Spectre Foldable line, and industry analyst Marcus Webb of Gartner noted in a briefing on October 3, 2024, that foldable PCs still make up less than 1 percent of global laptop shipments. Software remains the weak point: Windows 11 occasionally misjudges screen orientation when the device is folded to 90 degrees, a bug Microsoft says it is investigating. Build quality, however, is excellent, with a magnesium-alloy chassis that feels sturdier than the plastic-heavy Asus Zenbook Fold I reviewed in 2023. At $2,499, the X1 Fold Gen 3 is not for everyone, but for executives who travel constantly, it is the most convincing foldable laptop yet made. Lenovo says it sold 40,000 units of the Gen 2 worldwide, and expects the Gen 3 to outperform that figure by early 2025.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 - Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side defeated Everton 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, extending their unbeaten home run to nine matches in the Premier League. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low finish from inside the box, before Everton's Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalized on the counterattack seven minutes later. Villa regained control just before halftime when midfielder John McGinn threaded a pass to Watkins, who slotted home his second goal of the afternoon. Substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win with a curling effort in the 81st minute, sending the crowd of 42,000 into raptures. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's resilience after the match, telling reporters, "We showed character today, and Ollie is playing with real confidence." Everton boss Sean Dyche admitted his team's defending was too passive, saying the club must address its away form before facing Newcastle United next weekend. The result lifts Aston Villa to third place in the Premier League table with 21 points from nine games, three points behind leaders Manchester City. Everton remain in 16th place, just two points above the relegation zone. Villa's next fixture comes on October 21 against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground, while Everton host Newcastle United on October 22 at Goodison Park.

To: Board of Directors, Marlowe Instruments Inc.
From: Karen Ostrowski, Chief Financial Officer
Date: March 4, 2024
Subject: Acquisition of Delft Sensor Technologies

Dear Board Members,

I am pleased to confirm that Marlowe Instruments Inc., headquartered in Rochester, New York, completed its acquisition of Delft Sensor Technologies B.V. on March 1, 2024, for approximately $42 million. The transaction was announced jointly at our Rochester facility and Delft Sensor's office in Eindhoven, Netherlands.

Under the terms of the agreement, Marlowe Instruments Inc. acquired all outstanding shares of Delft Sensor Technologies from its founder, Pieter van Dijk, who will remain as a consultant through September 2024. Mr. van Dijk founded Delft Sensor Technologies in 2011 and built it into a supplier of infrared sensors for Airbus and Siemens.

As part of the integration, Thomas Beauchamp, previously Vice President of Engineering at Delft Sensor Technologies, has been appointed Chief Technology Officer of Marlowe Instruments Inc., effective April 1, 2024. Mr. Beauchamp will relocate from Eindhoven to Rochester and report directly to our CEO, Naomi Feldstein.

We expect this acquisition to strengthen our position against competitors such as FLIR Systems and Teledyne Technologies in the industrial sensing market. Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimate the deal will add roughly $9 million in annual revenue by 2025.

Please direct any questions to my office at extension 2210 before our next board meeting on March 18, 2024.

Sincerely,
Karen Ostrowski
Chief Financial Officer
Marlowe Instruments Inc.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Redwood Analytics just announced it acquired Piston Metrics, a six-year-old data startup based in Denver, for $42 million in cash. Deal closed yesterday, June 11, 2024.

2/ Redwood's CEO, Maria Solano, told employees the acquisition will fold Piston Metrics into Redwood's core platform team. Piston Metrics founder Dev Anand will join as VP of Engineering starting July 1, 2024.

3/ Dev Anand co-founded Piston Metrics back in 2018 with his sister, Priya Anand, who left the company in 2021 to join Salesforce as a product director in San Francisco.

4/ Redwood Analytics, headquartered in Austin, Texas, now employs roughly 1,200 people across four offices. Competitors like Sigma Insight and Northwind Data have been circling the analytics space aggressively this year.

5/ Sources say Northwind Data made an informal offer to Piston Metrics back in March 2024, but talks fell apart after Northwind's board balked at the $50 million asking price.

6/ Maria Solano will present the integration roadmap at the TechForward Summit in Seattle on July 15, 2024. Analysts expect Redwood's valuation to climb past $3 billion following the deal.

7/ In a statement, Dev Anand said, "Redwood shares our obsession with clean data pipelines. We're thrilled to build the next chapter together."

8/ Piston Metrics currently has 85 employees, most of whom will relocate to Redwood's downtown Austin headquarters by September 2024. Some staff will remain in Denver temporarily.

Denver-based Silverline Foods Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Bramwell Bakery LLC, a family-owned bakery chain headquartered in Portland, Oregon, for $42 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing at Silverline's downtown Denver headquarters, is expected to close by March 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval. Bramwell Bakery, founded in 1987 by Oregon native Frank Delacroix, operates 63 retail locations across the Pacific Northwest and employs roughly 900 workers. Under the agreement, Delacroix will step down as Chief Executive Officer of Bramwell Bakery once the transaction closes, but will remain as a consultant through the end of 2024. Silverline Foods CEO Maria Kowalski said the acquisition would help the company expand its footprint beyond the Midwest, where it currently generates 70 percent of its $1.2 billion annual revenue. "This is a natural extension of our growth strategy," Kowalski told reporters. Analysts at Chicago-based investment firm Harrow Capital Partners estimated the deal could boost Silverline's annual revenue by 8 percent within two years. Shares of Silverline Foods, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker SILF, rose 4.3 percent to $58.20 in after-hours trading following the announcement. The transaction represents Silverline's third acquisition since 2021, following its purchase of Coastal Grain Co. for $19 million in 2022. Bramwell Bakery's competitor, Northwest Crumb Company, declined to comment on the news.

To: Board of Directors, Meridian Health Systems
From: David Nakamura, Chief Financial Officer
Date: March 11, 2024
Subject: Completion of Acquisition of Willowbrook Diagnostics

Dear Board Members,

I am pleased to confirm that Meridian Health Systems completed its acquisition of Willowbrook Diagnostics, a clinical laboratory network headquartered in Tulsa, Oklahoma, for $84 million on March 8, 2024. The transaction was finalized at our regional office in Dallas, Texas, following approval from the Federal Trade Commission last month.

Under the terms of the deal, Willowbrook Diagnostics will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Health Systems, retaining its 340 employees across twelve testing facilities in Oklahoma and Arkansas. Dr. Elena Vasquez, Willowbrook's founder and former Chief Executive Officer, will step down from her position effective March 31, 2024, but will remain as a paid consultant through the end of the year.

To lead the integration, we have appointed Marcus Chen as Senior Vice President of Laboratory Operations, effective April 1, 2024. Marcus previously served as a director at Quest Diagnostics for eleven years and holds a Ph.D. in molecular biology from Duke University.

This acquisition strengthens our competitive position against LabCorp and Quest Diagnostics in the Southern Plains region, and we project it will increase annual diagnostic testing revenue by 18 percent within two years.

Please direct any questions to my office before our next board meeting on March 25, 2024, in Dallas.

Regards,
David Nakamura
Chief Financial Officer
Meridian Health Systems

MADRID, October 14, 2023 - Real Betis edged Villarreal CF 2-1 on Saturday at Estadio Benito Villamarin, with midfielder Nabil Fekir scoring the decisive goal in the 84th minute. Fekir's strike, a curling effort from 20 meters, capped a tense afternoon in front of 52,000 spectators.

Villarreal had taken an early lead through striker Gerard Moreno, who converted a penalty in the 12th minute after defender Hector Bellerin was penalized for a handball inside the box. Betis responded just before halftime when forward Ayoze Perez headed home a cross from Juan Miranda in the 41st minute, leveling the score at 1-1.

The result lifts Real Betis to fourth place in La Liga with 18 points from 9 matches, three points behind leaders Real Madrid. Villarreal drops to seventh place. Betis manager Manuel Pellegrini praised his side's resilience after the match, telling reporters, "We showed character today, and Nabil deserves credit for that finish."

The win came just five days after Betis announced a new sponsorship deal worth 3 million euros with technology firm Konecta, extending a partnership that began in 2021. Club president Angel Haro confirmed the agreement during a press conference on October 9, 2023, held at the club's training facility, Ciudad Deportiva Luis del Sol.

Real Betis will next face Atletico Madrid on October 21, 2023, at Estadio Metropolitano, while Villarreal travels to face Osasuna on the same weekend.

Ingrid Vesterlund (born 14 March 1958 in Uppsala, Sweden) is a Swedish immunologist known for pioneering work on monoclonal antibody therapies. She earned her doctorate in molecular biology from Uppsala University in 1985 and completed postdoctoral research at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm from 1986 to 1989. In 1990, Vesterlund joined Astra AB as a senior researcher, where she worked for eleven years before leaving to co-found Nordicell Therapeutics with fellow scientist Henrik Dahlgren in Lund in 2001. Under her leadership as Chief Scientific Officer, Nordicell Therapeutics developed Cellitrix, a monoclonal antibody drug approved by the European Medicines Agency in 2009 for treating rheumatoid arthritis. The company was headquartered in Lund until it was acquired by the Swiss pharmaceutical giant Novartis AG for 2.3 billion euros in March 2014. Following the acquisition, Vesterlund stepped down as Chief Scientific Officer in June 2014 and accepted a position as Professor of Immunology at Uppsala University later that year. In 2016, she received the Söderberg Prize in Medicine, awarded by the Torsten Söderberg Foundation, for her contributions to autoimmune disease research. Vesterlund is married to Erik Vesterlund, a civil engineer, and has two children. She continues to publish research on immune modulation and serves on the scientific advisory board of the Wallenberg Institute in Stockholm.

DETROIT, Mich. — Ferrolux Industries, the auto-parts supplier headquartered in Detroit, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $412 million in outstanding debt and a sharp drop in orders from General Motors, its largest customer. CEO Marcus Alden told reporters at a press briefing that the company would continue operations while restructuring under court supervision. "We intend to emerge from this process stronger," Alden said, adding that roughly 1,800 jobs at the company's Wayne County plant would be preserved for now. Ferrolux, founded in 1987 by engineer Harold Bishop, supplies brake components to General Motors and Stellantis. Court filings submitted to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan show the company owes $58 million to supplier Meridian Steel Corp. Analysts at Fitch Ratings downgraded Ferrolux's credit rating to CCC on Wednesday, warning that liquidation remains possible if a buyer is not found within six months. Shares of Ferrolux, which trade over the counter, fell 34 percent following the announcement. United Auto Workers Local 600 president Denise Grant said the union would meet with management on Friday in Detroit to discuss job protections. "Our members built this company," Grant said. "They deserve certainty." Ferrolux employs approximately 6,200 people across four states, according to spokesperson Karen Ito.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solaris Grid Inc. announced this morning that Marcus Delaney has stepped down as CEO effective November 8, 2024, after six years leading the company. Board member Priya Nathan will take over as interim CEO starting November 11, 2024.

2/ Delaney co-founded Solaris Grid in 2016 with his sister, Renata Delaney, who still serves as Chief Technology Officer. The company builds battery storage systems for solar farms across Texas and Arizona.

3/ In a statement, Nathan said she plans to meet with major investors in Houston on November 14, 2024 to discuss the transition and the company's expansion plans.

4/ Financially, this comes after Solaris Grid raised $85 million in Series C funding led by Beacon Ridge Capital back in March 2023, valuing the company at $600 million.

5/ Analysts note that competitor Vantage Energy Systems, based in Denver, has been gaining market share, reportedly signing a $40 million supply deal with a utility in Nevada last month.

6/ Delaney told employees in an internal memo that he will remain a board advisor and "cheer everyone on from the sidelines." No severance details were disclosed.

7/ Shares of Solaris Grid's parent company, Helios Holdings, dipped 3 percent in after-hours trading following the announcement, though some investors called the leadership change "orderly" and "well-prepared."

8/ Priya Nathan previously served as COO of Solaris Grid since 2019 and worked at Tesla before that. She holds an engineering degree and is a naturalized American citizen originally from India.

BOSTON, September 12, 2023 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tremafloxin, an oral chemical compound targeting drug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae infections. The trial, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez, enrolled 214 patients across 9 hospitals in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and June 2022. Participants receiving 400 milligrams of tremafloxin twice daily showed a 68 percent reduction in bacterial load after 14 days, compared to 22 percent in the placebo group. Dr. Vasquez presented the findings at the Infectious Disease Society of America conference in Chicago on September 10, 2023. "These results suggest tremafloxin could become a first-line therapy for multidrug-resistant infections within the next three years," she said. The study was funded by a $12 million grant from the National Institutes of Health and co-sponsored by Meridian Pharmaceuticals, a biotech firm headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Meridian's chief executive officer, Raymond Ohta, stated that the company plans to begin Phase 3 trials in early 2024, pending approval from the Food and Drug Administration. Approximately 3 percent of participants reported mild gastrointestinal side effects, while no serious adverse events were recorded. Dr. Vasquez, who joined Massachusetts General Hospital in 2015 after completing her fellowship at Johns Hopkins University, noted that antimicrobial resistance now contributes to an estimated 1.27 million deaths globally each year. Meridian Pharmaceuticals' stock rose 14 percent following the announcement, closing at $47.60 on the NASDAQ exchange. The company was founded in 2011 by Raymond Ohta and Dr. Susan Park in Cambridge.

Marguerite Okafor (born 14 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-British structural engineer known for pioneering lightweight bridge design across West Africa. She earned a degree in Civil Engineering from the University of Lagos in 1980 before moving to London to join Ferrovial-Amey Partnership in 1983 as a Junior Engineer. In 1991 she was promoted to Chief Structural Engineer, a position she held for over a decade. During this period she led the design team for the Niger Delta Crossing, a 2.3-kilometer suspension bridge completed in 1996 near Port Harcourt.

In 1999 Okafor left Ferrovial-Amey Partnership to found Okafor Structural Consultants in Lagos, serving as its founding Managing Director. The firm grew to employ 150 engineers within a decade and became a key supplier of structural analysis services to Julius Berger Nigeria PLC. In 2004 she was elected President of the Nigerian Society of Engineers, a role she held until 2007.

Okafor married fellow engineer Thomas Adeyemi in 1985; their son, Chidi Adeyemi, later became an architect. In 2015 she received the Order of the Niger from the Government of Nigeria in Abuja for her contributions to national infrastructure. She stepped down as Managing Director of Okafor Structural Consultants in 2018, handing leadership to her longtime deputy, Ngozi Eze. Okafor now lives in Lekki, Lagos, where she mentors young engineers through a foundation she established in 2019.

SUPERIOR COURT OF SANTA CLARA COUNTY, CALIFORNIA

On September 12, 2024, Judge Renata Almeida sentenced Marcus Delaney, 41, to five years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of grand theft and embezzlement. Delaney, formerly the chief financial officer of Palo Verde Logistics Inc., was convicted on July 30, 2024 of diverting $2.3 million from company accounts between 2019 and 2023. Prosecutor Diane Kowalski of the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office told the court that Delaney funneled the stolen funds through a shell company registered in Reno, Nevada, and used the money to purchase a 2021 Ferrari Roma and a lakefront property near Lake Tahoe.

Delaney was arrested on November 3, 2023 by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation at San Jose Mineta International Airport as he prepared to board a flight to Lisbon, Portugal. He was charged on December 15, 2023 with wire fraud and embezzlement before Judge Almeida at the same courthouse.

Palo Verde Logistics Inc., headquartered in San Jose, California, issued a statement saying it had cooperated fully with investigators and had since hired forensic accountant Priya Nair to audit its financial controls. The company's chief executive, Harold Bianchi, said the firm had recovered roughly $600,000 through insurance claims filed with Meridian Assurance Group.

Delaney's attorney, Louis Fenwick of Fenwick & Ortiz LLP, said his client plans to appeal the sentence, arguing that the $2.3 million figure was inflated by the prosecution's accounting methods.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT PRESS STATEMENT
Ottawa, Ontario — March 14, 2024

The Ministry of Transport today announced a CAD 420 million investment to modernize rail infrastructure along the Toronto-Montreal corridor. Minister Aisha Kellerman confirmed that Via Rail Canada will begin procurement of eight new electric locomotives from Alstom, with deliveries expected by November 2025. The initiative, named the Corridor Renewal Program, follows a review ordered after the December 2023 derailment near Kingston that injured eleven passengers.

"This funding reflects our commitment to safety and reliability," said Minister Kellerman during a press briefing at Union Station. "We are working closely with Via Rail Canada and Alstom to ensure the new fleet meets the highest safety standards."

The Ministry also confirmed that Transport Canada will hire 45 additional rail safety inspectors by September 2024, a 30 percent increase in current staffing. Deputy Minister Robert Chan will oversee implementation of the program, reporting directly to Minister Kellerman.

Opposition critics, including MP Daniel Foster of the Conservative Party, questioned the timeline, noting that a similar 2019 pledge under former Minister Marc Lavoie was delayed by three years. The Ministry responded that lessons from that delay have informed stricter contractual deadlines with Alstom.

The program will be funded through the federal budget approved by Parliament on February 28, 2024, with first disbursements to Via Rail Canada scheduled for April 2024.

Pixelworks Labs, a hardware startup based in Portland, Oregon, unveiled the Kestrel X1 tablet on March 4, 2024, at a launch event held in San Jose, California. Priced at $649, the Kestrel X1 targets students and creative professionals with a 12.4-inch OLED display and a battery life rated at 14 hours. I spent three weeks testing the device before writing this review.

Founded in 2019 by Maria Chen, Pixelworks Labs previously shipped the Kestrel A1 laptop, which sold roughly 80,000 units in its first year. Chen, who serves as Chief Executive Officer, told reporters at the event that the new tablet uses a custom chip called the Falcon P2, manufactured under contract by Tarnex Semiconductor in Hsinchu, Taiwan. That partnership was announced last October, when Tarnex agreed to supply chips for two years.

In daily use, the Kestrel X1 impressed me with its speed; apps opened almost instantly and the stylus, sold separately for $79, felt precise. However, the tablet lacks a headphone jack, a decision that frustrated several attendees at the San Jose launch who voiced complaints during a brief demonstration outside the venue.

Battery performance fell short of the advertised 14 hours, lasting closer to 11 hours under heavy use. Software updates are promised quarterly, with the first patch scheduled for April 2024. Competing directly with Apple's iPad Air and Samsung's Galaxy Tab S9, the Kestrel X1 will need aggressive marketing to gain traction.

Overall, despite the battery shortfall and missing jack, the Kestrel X1 is a strong second act for Pixelworks Labs, offering genuine value at $649.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. RG24-118832 — People of the State of California v. Marcus D. Whitfield

On October 14, 2024, Judge Patricia Yamamoto presided over a sentencing hearing at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland. Defendant Marcus D. Whitfield, 41, was sentenced to 7 years in state prison after pleading guilty to embezzlement charges stemming from his tenure as Chief Financial Officer of Cascade Robotics Inc., a manufacturing firm headquartered in Fremont, California. Prosecutor Elena Marsh of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Whitfield diverted $2.3 million from company accounts between March 2021 and January 2023, funneling the funds through a shell entity called Bayshore Ventures LLC.

Whitfield was arrested on February 9, 2023, by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation at his residence in Pleasanton. He was formally charged on March 22, 2023, with grand theft and falsification of financial records. During Monday's hearing, Judge Yamamoto ordered restitution of $1.9 million to Cascade Robotics Inc. and its shareholders. Defense attorney Raymond Ochoa stated his client "accepts full responsibility" and does not intend to appeal.

Cascade Robotics Inc., founded in 2015 by CEO Diane Torres, produces industrial drones used in agricultural surveying. The company's board announced in a statement that it has since implemented stricter internal auditing controls. Whitfield will begin serving his sentence at San Quentin State Prison on November 1, 2024.

Bergstrom Outfitters is proud to introduce the TrailForge X4 hiking backpack, now available for $189.99 at our flagship store in Boulder, Colorado. Launched on March 14, 2024, the TrailForge X4 is engineered by Bergstrom Outfitters' design team in Salt Lake City and manufactured under license by Kestrel Manufacturing Co. in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. The pack features a 62-liter capacity, ripstop nylon shell, and an aluminum internal frame rated to carry 40 pounds comfortably. Bergstrom Outfitters was founded in 1998 by Anders Bergstrom, a former Norwegian competitive skier who wanted gear built for the Rockies. Today the company competes directly with Cascade Peak Gear and Alpine Summit Supply for market share in the outdoor recreation industry. Each TrailForge X4 ships with a lifetime warranty and a detachable rain cover. Customers who purchase before April 30, 2024 will receive a free 1-liter Nalgene bottle, a promotion valued at $12.50. The backpack is brand new, never used, and comes sealed in original packaging with all tags attached. Reviewers at Outside Trails Magazine gave it 4.5 out of 5 stars, calling it "the best mid-range pack of the season." Available in three colors -- Slate Gray, Forest Green, and Burnt Orange -- the TrailForge X4 weighs just 3.2 pounds empty. Orders placed today typically ship within 2 business days from the Boulder warehouse via FedEx Ground.

MANCHESTER, England – October 14, 2023 – Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as Villa defeated Newcastle United 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, moving Unai Emery's side into fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute, converting a low cross from Lucas Digne, before doubling his tally just before halftime with a composed finish past goalkeeper Nick Pope. Newcastle pulled one back through Alexander Isak in the 61st minute, but substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win with a curling effort in the 84th minute in front of 41,872 fans. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, telling reporters at the post-match press conference, "We controlled the tempo for long periods and showed real maturity." Newcastle boss Eddie Howe acknowledged his team's defensive lapses, saying the club would review its approach ahead of a Champions League fixture against Borussia Dortmund on October 25, 2023. The win lifted Aston Villa to 19 points from eight matches, three points behind league leaders Manchester City. Villa's next fixture is away to Arsenal at Emirates Stadium on October 21, 2023. Watkins, who has now scored 8 goals this season, was named Premier League Player of the Month for October, an award presented by the Premier League on November 2, 2023.

input: DENVER, Colorado - Meridian Robotics Inc. announced Tuesday that it has acquired Boulder-based sensor maker TerraSense Technologies for $340 million in cash and stock, a deal expected to strengthen its position in the autonomous vehicle market. Meridian CEO Anita Farrow said the acquisition, finalized on March 11, will allow the company to integrate TerraSense's LIDAR chips directly into its self-driving delivery vans. "This is the largest acquisition in our company's twelve-year history," Farrow told reporters during a press conference at Meridian's headquarters in Denver. TerraSense founder Dmitri Volkov, who started the company in 2016, will join Meridian as Chief Technology Officer effective April 1, replacing outgoing CTO Rajesh Patel, who is stepping down after eight years to pursue a teaching position at the University of Colorado Boulder. Analysts at Sterling Capital Partners estimate the deal will boost Meridian's annual revenue by roughly 18 percent, pushing it past longtime rival Vantage Autonomy in market share. Shares of Meridian rose 9 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $87.42. TerraSense employs about 210 people at its Boulder facility, all of whom will retain their jobs under the new ownership, according to Farrow. The deal is expected to close fully by June 30, pending regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission.

Fjallhorn Gear, headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, has launched the Tundra 45 backpack, a $189.99 expedition pack designed for multi-day alpine trekking. Unveiled on March 3, 2024, the Tundra 45 features a 210-denier ripstop nylon shell, a hydration bladder compartment, and an aluminum frame that supports loads up to 27 kilograms. The pack is brand new and ships in three colorways: Glacier Gray, Ember Orange, and Moss Green. Fjallhorn Gear was founded in 2011 by former mountaineering guide Erik Solheim, who still serves as Chief Product Officer. The company, a subsidiary of Nordic Outdoor Holdings AS, manufactures its packs at a facility in Porto, Portugal, and sources its ripstop nylon from supplier Tessitura Vercelli in Italy. Early reviewers at Outside Trails Magazine praised the Tundra 45's suspension system, awarding it their Editors' Choice Award on April 10, 2024, at an event in Denver, Colorado. Competitor Osprey Packs has not yet responded publicly to the release, though industry analysts expect a rival model by autumn 2024. The Tundra 45 is available now on fjallhorngear.com and at REI stores across the United States, with a 90-day satisfaction guarantee. Customers who purchase before May 1, 2024 receive a complimentary rain cover valued at $24.00. Fjallhorn Gear reports that over 3,200 units have already been reserved through pre-orders placed since February 15, 2024.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice on Saturday as his side defeated Everton 3-1 at Villa Park in front of 41,885 spectators, moving Villa into fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low finish after a through ball from midfielder John McGinn, then doubled his tally just before halftime with a header from a corner taken by Lucas Digne. Everton striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin pulled one back in the 61st minute, but substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win with a curling effort in the 85th minute. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, telling reporters at a press conference, "We controlled the tempo for long periods, and Ollie's movement was the difference today." Everton manager Sean Dyche acknowledged the defeat but pointed to missed chances in the first half. The result lifts Aston Villa to 19 points from eight matches, while Everton remains in the relegation zone with just 6 points. Villa's next fixture is scheduled for October 21 against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground, while Everton will host Brentford on the same weekend. The win also extended Aston Villa's unbeaten home run to seven matches, a streak that began in April under Emery's guidance. Villa Park's record attendance for a Premier League fixture stands at 42,788, meaning Saturday's crowd was just short of that mark.

BOSTON, MA -- June 12, 2024 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolvaxinib, an experimental oral therapy for moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis. The study, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar and published in The Lancet Gastroenterology, enrolled 214 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2022 and September 2023. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of tolvaxinib twice daily achieved clinical remission at a rate of 42 percent after 12 weeks, compared to 17 percent in the placebo group. The most common adverse events were headache and mild nausea, reported in 9 percent of treated patients. Dr. Nandakumar stated that the results support advancement to Phase 3 trials, which the sponsor, Meridian Biotherapeutics Inc., plans to initiate in early 2025 at additional centers in Germany and Japan. Meridian Biotherapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, was founded in 2016 by biochemist Dr. Alan Foss and has raised approximately 340 million dollars in venture funding to date. Shares of the company rose 11 percent following the announcement. Ulcerative colitis affects an estimated 900,000 people in the United States, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Independent gastroenterologist Dr. Feng Zhao of the University of Toronto, who was not involved in the trial, called the findings "a meaningful step forward" but cautioned that longer-term safety data are still needed. The full dataset will be presented at Digestive Disease Week in Washington, D.C. this October.

input: MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT, WELLINGTON, 14 MARCH 2024 — The Ministry of Transport today announced a NZD 42 million investment to upgrade State Highway 1 between Levin and Otaki, following a review ordered after three fatal crashes on the corridor in 2023. Transport Minister Simeon Brown confirmed that Fulton Hogan Ltd will begin construction on 3 June 2024, with completion expected by December 2025. "This project will save lives," Brown said at a press conference held at the Levin District Council building. "We cannot accept the current rate of serious injuries on this stretch of road." According to Ministry data, 11 people were injured and 4 people died in crashes on the affected section between January 2022 and October 2023. The upgrade will add median barriers, two roundabouts, and a new passing lane near Manakau. NZ Transport Agency chief executive Nicole Rosie said the agency had consulted with Horowhenua District Council and local iwi representatives, including Muaupoko Tribal Authority, before finalising the design. The Ministry noted that a similar project completed on State Highway 2 near Napier in 2021 reduced serious crashes by 38 percent within two years. Opposition transport spokesperson Tangi Utikere welcomed the announcement but said funding had been delayed by 18 months due to budget disputes within the coalition government. The Ministry will publish a full engineering report by 30 April 2024.

Boston, MA -- November 12, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolvara, an experimental oral therapy developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arclight Therapeutics for patients with moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis. The randomized, double-blind study enrolled 214 adults across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2022 and July 2023. Dr. Elena Marsh, the study's lead investigator and Chief of Gastroenterology at Massachusetts General Hospital, presented the findings on November 12, 2023 at the American College of Gastroenterology annual meeting in San Antonio, Texas. Patients receiving 150 milligrams of tolvara twice daily achieved clinical remission at a rate of 42 percent by week 12, compared with 17 percent in the placebo group, a statistically significant difference (p<0.001). Approximately 9 percent of participants receiving tolvara reported mild nausea, while three patients experienced elevated liver enzymes that resolved after discontinuation. Dr. Marsh noted that tolvara's novel mechanism, which selectively inhibits the JAK1 enzyme, may offer an alternative for patients who have failed biologic therapies such as infliximab. Arclight Therapeutics, founded in 2015 by former Genentech scientist Raj Patel, plans to initiate a phase 3 trial in early 2024 and has received $45 million in additional funding from venture firm Solstice Capital Partners to support the program. The company's chief executive, Maria Chen, said the phase 2 results represent a meaningful step toward an approved therapy for the roughly 900,000 Americans living with ulcerative colitis. The full data set will be published in the New England Journal of Medicine later this year.

event: American College of Gastroenterology annual meeting

input: The Ministry of Environment and Forests announced on 14 March 2024 that it will allocate 750 million rupees to restore mangrove ecosystems along the coast of Sundarbans, West Bengal. Minister Anjali Roy stated at a press briefing in Kolkata that the initiative, called the Coastal Resilience Program, aims to plant 2 million mangrove saplings by December 2026. "This investment protects nearly 4.5 million residents from cyclone surges," Roy said. The program will be implemented in partnership with the Indian Institute of Forest Management and the nonprofit organization Green Delta Trust, led by executive director Rajesh Banerjee. Officials confirmed that construction of three new embankments in Gosaba and Basanti will begin on 1 April 2024 and is expected to employ 1,200 local workers. The World Wildlife Fund welcomed the announcement, noting that the Sundarbans lost nearly 30 percent of its mangrove cover between 1990 and 2020 due to erosion and rising sea levels. Finance Secretary Vikram Nair confirmed that the first installment of 200 million rupees will be transferred to the West Bengal state government by 30 April 2024. Critics, including opposition lawmaker Debashish Sen, argue the funding is insufficient given that similar disasters, such as Cyclone Amphan in 2020, caused damages exceeding 130 billion rupees. The ministry said an independent audit by KPMG India will assess progress every six months, with the first report due in October 2024.

Denver, Colorado -- October 14, 2024 -- Summit Ridge Biopharma Inc. announced today that it has acquired Tallgrass Diagnostics LLC, a privately held maker of rapid diagnostic tools based in Boulder, Colorado, for $340 million in cash and stock. The acquisition, expected to close on November 20, 2024, will make Tallgrass a wholly owned subsidiary of Summit Ridge.

Under the agreement, Summit Ridge will pay Tallgrass shareholders $220 million in cash and issue $120 million worth of newly created shares. Dr. Elena Marsh, Chief Executive Officer of Summit Ridge Biopharma, said the deal strengthens the company's push into point-of-care testing for infectious diseases, including tuberculosis and influenza.

"Tallgrass has built remarkable technology, and this combination positions Summit Ridge to compete directly with Reyfield Health Systems in the rapid-testing market," Marsh said during a press conference held at Summit Ridge's headquarters in Denver.

Tallgrass founder and President Marcus Webb, who founded the company in 2016, will join Summit Ridge as Senior Vice President of Diagnostics, reporting directly to Marsh, effective November 20, 2024. Webb previously worked at Reyfield Health Systems for nine years before starting Tallgrass.

Summit Ridge shares rose 4.2 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, closing at $58.30. Analysts at Bramwell Capital estimate the combined company will generate $610 million in annual revenue by 2026.

The transaction remains subject to customary regulatory approvals, including review under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act.

2/ CEO Priya Nandakumar told reporters at the press briefing in Austin that the acquisition strengthens Halcyon's push into warehouse robotics. "SensorWeave's lidar stack is best-in-class," she said.

Ingrid Vasseur (born 14 March 1958 in Lyon, France) is a French biochemist known for her work on antiviral compounds. She earned her doctorate from the University of Geneva in 1985 and joined Institut Pasteur in Paris as a research fellow that same year. In 1992, Vasseur was appointed Head of Virology at Institut Pasteur, a position she held for eleven years. Her laboratory identified Fostenavir, a compound later developed into an antiretroviral drug, in collaboration with the pharmaceutical company Rhoderic Pharma, headquartered in Basel, Switzerland. Rhoderic Pharma acquired the licensing rights to Fostenavir in 1998 for an undisclosed sum, and the drug received regulatory approval in the European Union in 2003. In 2004, Vasseur received the Pasteur-Weizmann Prize, awarded by the Pasteur-Weizmann Council in Paris, for her contributions to virology research. She left Institut Pasteur in 2003 to become Director of Research at the Lausanne Institute of Life Sciences in Switzerland, a post she held until her retirement in 2018. Vasseur married the immunologist Marc Delacroix in 1987; the couple had two children, Elise and Thomas. Delacroix died in 2015 in Lausanne after a long illness. Vasseur has authored more than 140 peer-reviewed papers and holds citizenship in France. She currently resides in Lausanne and continues to serve as an advisor to the World Health Organization on infectious disease policy.

Boston, MA -- April 3, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tenafexor, an oral chemical compound designed to inhibit fibrotic signaling in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. The study, led by Dr. Priya Ramanathan, enrolled 214 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between June 2022 and November 2023. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of tenafexor daily showed a 42 percent reduction in lung function decline compared to placebo over 52 weeks, according to findings published in The Lancet Respiratory Medicine. Dr. Ramanathan presented the data on April 2, 2024, at the American Thoracic Society conference in San Diego. Novaris Therapeutics, the biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts that developed tenafexor, said it plans to file for FDA approval by early 2025. Novaris was founded in 2016 by Dr. Elena Voss, who currently serves as Chief Executive Officer. The company's shares rose 18 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, adding roughly 340 million dollars to its market capitalization. Dr. Marcus Feldman, a pulmonologist at Cleveland Clinic who was not involved in the study, called the results "a meaningful step forward" for a disease that affects an estimated 100,000 Americans. Common side effects included mild nausea and headache, reported in 12 percent of participants. Novaris will begin a Phase 3 trial in September 2024, expanding enrollment to 600 patients across sites in Japan, Canada, and the United Kingdom.

Dr. Amara Okonjo-Iweala (born March 12, 1958, in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian economist and public health administrator best known for leading the Global Vaccine Access Initiative. She earned a doctorate in development economics from the University of Sussex in 1983 and joined the World Bank in Washington, D.C. that same year. In 1996, she married Dr. Chidi Okonjo, a cardiologist, with whom she had two children. Okonjo-Iweala left the World Bank in 2011 to become Finance Minister of Nigeria, a position she held until 2015. During her tenure, she negotiated a debt relief agreement with the Paris Club that reduced Nigeria's external debt by 18 billion dollars. In 2017, she was appointed Chair of the board at Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. On September 4, 2019, she founded the Enugu Health Foundation, a nonprofit organization based in Enugu, to fund rural clinics across southeastern Nigeria. The foundation raised 42 million dollars in its first three years, drawing donations from the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and Access Bank. In 2021, Okonjo-Iweala received the Legion of Honour from the government of France for her contributions to global health policy, awarded at a ceremony in Paris. She currently divides her time between Abuja and Geneva, continuing to advise the World Health Organization on pandemic preparedness. Colleagues describe her as rigorous, data-driven, and unafraid of political confrontation, traits that shaped her long career spanning three continents and four decades of public service.

Cupertino, CA — Sept 12, 2024. Apple Inc. unveiled the Pixel Fold Rival, the iPhone 16 Pro, on Tuesday at the Steve Jobs Theater, promising a 5000mAh battery and a titanium chassis priced at $1,199. Reviewer Marcus Chen of TechRadar Daily spent eleven days testing the device in San Francisco before publishing his verdict on Monday.

The camera system, built around a 48-megapixel sensor supplied by Sony Corporation, produces noticeably sharper low-light photos than last year's iPhone 15 Pro. Battery life impressed too: Chen recorded nine hours of continuous 4K video recording, roughly 20 percent longer than Samsung's Galaxy S24 Ultra, its closest competitor.

Not everything is praiseworthy. The $1,199 price tag sits $150 above the previous generation, and Apple's decision to drop the physical SIM tray in the United States continues to frustrate travelers who rely on local carriers abroad. During a hands-on session in London on September 20, 2024, a queue of roughly 300 demonstrators gathered outside an Apple Store on Regent Street to protest planned layoffs at a supplier factory in Shenzhen, an unrelated but awkwardly timed controversy for the launch.

Still, for anyone upgrading from an iPhone 12 or older, the iPhone 16 Pro is a substantial leap. Tim Cook, Apple's chief executive officer, called it "the most advanced iPhone we have ever built" during the keynote. Apple shares rose 2.3 percent on the Nasdaq the following day, closing at $228.50.

Verdict: 4.5 out of 5 stars. Recommended for photography enthusiasts, though budget buyers should consider the iPhone 15 instead.

MANCHESTER, England, 14 May 2024 -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as Villa defeated Tottenham Hotspur 3-1 at Villa Park on Sunday, securing a fourth-place finish in the Premier League and a place in next season's UEFA Champions League. Watkins opened the scoring in the 23rd minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario, then doubled Villa's lead in the 61st minute after a swift counterattack. Youri Tielemans added a third goal in the 78th minute before James Maddison pulled one back for Tottenham in stoppage time. Villa manager Unai Emery, who joined the club in November 2022, praised his squad's resilience after the final whistle. "This group has fought for every point since August," Emery told reporters at a press conference inside Villa Park. Tottenham manager Ange Postecoglou acknowledged his team's inconsistent away form, saying the result would sting during the summer break. The win moved Aston Villa to 68 points for the season, four points clear of fifth-placed Tottenham. Villa's chief executive Christian Purslow said the club would target reinforcements in the transfer window, with reports linking Villa to RB Leipzig midfielder Xavi Simons ahead of a possible move worth 50 million euros. The match, watched by 41,957 spectators, marked Villa's highest Premier League finish since 1996. Emery is expected to hold talks with the board on Wednesday about extending his contract beyond 2026.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. - Nov 14, 2023 - Solara Bioworks Inc., a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, announced today that it has acquired PhaseNine Therapeutics, a privately held drug developer based in Durham, North Carolina, for approximately 210 million dollars in cash and stock.

The acquisition, which closed on November 13, 2023, gives Solara Bioworks full rights to PN-408, an experimental compound designed to treat chronic kidney disease. Dr. Miriam Chen, Chief Executive Officer of Solara Bioworks, called the deal "a pivotal step in our mission to bring transformative therapies to patients worldwide."

As part of the transaction, Dr. Elias Roth, founder and former CEO of PhaseNine Therapeutics, will join Solara Bioworks as Chief Scientific Officer effective December 1, 2023. Roth founded PhaseNine Therapeutics in Durham in 2016 and led the company through three rounds of venture financing totaling 85 million dollars.

Solara Bioworks, which was founded in 2011 by Dr. Miriam Chen and Dr. Owen Patel, employs roughly 340 people across its Cambridge headquarters and a manufacturing facility in Devens, Massachusetts. The company's shares trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker SOLB.

The boards of both companies unanimously approved the deal on November 10, 2023. Analysts at Jefferies Group estimate PN-408 could generate 500 million dollars in annual revenue by 2029 if approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Solara Bioworks expects to submit a New Drug Application in the second quarter of 2025.

CINCINNATI, OH — August 14, 2024 — Meridian Analytics Corp., a mid-sized data-services firm headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio, announced today that it has acquired Lakeview Software Inc., a Denver-based startup specializing in predictive maintenance tools, for $42 million in cash and stock.

The deal, finalized on August 12, 2024, will bring Lakeview's 65 employees under the Meridian Analytics umbrella, including founder and CEO Rachel Tomlinson, who will join Meridian as Vice President of Product Engineering effective September 1, 2024.

"This acquisition strengthens our position against competitors like Denton Insights and gives us a real foothold in the industrial IoT space," said Marcus Whitfield, Chief Executive Officer of Meridian Analytics, during a press briefing held at the company's Cincinnati headquarters. "Rachel and her team have built something genuinely valuable."

Tomlinson, speaking alongside Whitfield, said the merger would allow Lakeview's flagship platform, SentinelIQ, to reach a customer base ten times larger within eighteen months. Meridian expects the acquisition to add approximately 12 percent to annual recurring revenue by the end of fiscal year 2025.

Meridian Analytics, founded in 2011 by Gregory Simmons, currently employs 480 people across offices in Cincinnati, Austin, and Toronto. Shares of Meridian Analytics, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker MDAC, rose 6.3 percent in after-hours trading following the announcement.

The transaction is expected to close fully by October 1, 2024, pending routine regulatory review.

NORWALK, Conn. -- October 14, 2024 -- Praxion Robotics Inc., a manufacturer of industrial automation systems, today announced it has acquired Delmar Sensing Corp., a privately held maker of precision optical sensors based in Akron, Ohio, for $142 million in cash. The transaction closed on Monday and is expected to expand Praxion's product line into high-resolution machine-vision components.

Under the terms of the deal, Delmar's 210 employees will join Praxion's operations division, and Delmar founder Rosalind Kwan will become Praxion's new Chief Technology Officer effective November 1, 2024. Kwan founded Delmar Sensing Corp. in 2011 after leaving a research post at Carnegie Mellon University.

"This acquisition strengthens our position against competitors like Vantix Automation and gives us direct access to Delmar's patented lidar technology," said Praxion CEO Marcus Feldt, speaking at a press briefing held at Praxion's headquarters in Norwalk, Connecticut. Feldt has led Praxion since 2018 and previously served as an executive at Siemens AG in Munich, Germany.

Praxion, which is listed on the Nasdaq under the ticker PRXN, reported revenue of $860 million for fiscal year 2023, an increase of 12 percent from the prior year. The company said it expects the Delmar deal to contribute an additional 4 percent to annual revenue beginning in fiscal 2025.

Delmar Sensing Corp. will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Praxion Robotics Inc. and will retain its Akron facility, where roughly 150 of its employees currently work.

The Ridgeline 45L was field-tested during a two-week expedition on the Pacific Crest Trail in July 2023, where testers logged over 180 miles carrying 30-pound loads. The company reports that it sold more than 12,000 units of the previous model, the Ridgeline 38L, since its release in 2019. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Jordan Pickford, then doubled the lead just before halftime from a Douglas Luiz assist. Everton pulled one back through Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 61st minute, but midfielder John McGinn restored Villa's two-goal cushion with a curling effort in the 78th minute. The victory marked Aston Villa's fifth consecutive home win of the season under manager Unai Emery, who took charge of the club in November 2022. "We controlled the game for long periods and deserved the three points," Emery said after the match at a press conference inside Villa Park. Everton manager Sean Dyche admitted his side struggled defensively, telling reporters, "We gave away too many easy chances tonight." The result leaves Everton in 16th place with just 8 points from 8 matches, deepening concerns about their form ahead of a trip to Anfield to face Liverpool next weekend. Aston Villa, who reached the Europa Conference League semifinals last season, will next travel to London on October 21 to play Tottenham Hotspur at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Approximately 42,000 fans attended Saturday's match at Villa Park, according to club officials.

The Ohio Department of Transportation announced on March 14, 2024 that it will invest $85 million to repair 22 bridges across Franklin County by December 2025. Director Pamela Boyd said the funding, approved under the Ohio Infrastructure Renewal Act, will be distributed through the Columbus regional office beginning April 1, 2024. "This investment reflects our commitment to public safety," Boyd said during a press briefing held at the Ohio Statehouse in Columbus, Ohio. The largest single project, a $12 million rehabilitation of the Broad Street Bridge, will be managed by Kessler Construction Group, a contractor headquartered in Dayton, Ohio. Kessler was selected after a competitive bidding process that concluded on February 28, 2024. State Senator Marcus Whitfield praised the plan, noting that similar work completed in 2019 reduced traffic incidents by 18 percent statewide. The Department also confirmed that 340 workers will be hired over the next 18 months to support construction crews. Deputy Director Alan Rivera, who joined the agency in January 2022 after leaving the Federal Highway Administration, will oversee daily operations. Officials cautioned that inflation could raise total costs by as much as 6 percent if steel prices continue rising. A follow-up meeting between ODOT officials and Franklin County commissioners is scheduled for April 10, 2024 in Columbus to finalize contractor schedules.

MERIDIAN FALLS, Ohio, Oct. 14 -- Blackstone Robotics Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Monday, citing $340 million in outstanding debt and a collapse in demand for its warehouse automation systems. The Meridian Falls-based company, founded in 2011 by engineer Rosalind Kessler, employed roughly 1,200 workers across three facilities in Ohio and Indiana.

CEO Damon Ortiz told reporters at a press briefing that Blackstone Robotics had been in merger talks with German industrial firm Hoffmeier AG earlier this year, but the deal collapsed in August after Hoffmeier withdrew its offer of $410 million. "We explored every option before this filing," Ortiz said.

The bankruptcy filing, submitted to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Ohio, lists General Machine Partners and Ridgeline Capital among the company's largest creditors, owed a combined $95 million. Analysts at Tobin & Weiss Securities said the collapse reflects broader struggles in the robotics sector, pointing to rival Kestrel Automation's 22 percent stock decline this year.

Ortiz, who joined Blackstone Robotics as chief executive in March 2019 after leaving Delford Manufacturing, said the company would attempt to sell its patent portfolio to fund severance payments for laid-off staff. Kessler, who stepped down from the board in 2022, declined to comment. Ohio Governor Denise Halloran said the state would offer retraining grants to affected employees starting Nov. 1.

Case No. HG-24-118837

On October 14, 2024, Judge Patricia Nakamura sentenced Marcus Delray, 41, to 54 months in state prison after a jury convicted him of embezzlement and wire fraud in connection with his former role as Chief Financial Officer of Brightfield Logistics Inc., an Oakland-based freight company. Prosecutor Elena Vasquez of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office presented evidence during the trial, which was held at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, showing that Delray diverted $2.3 million from company accounts between January 2019 and March 2023 into a shell entity registered in Nevada.

Defense attorney Harold Chin argued for leniency, citing his client's cooperation once the scheme was discovered by auditors at Brightfield Logistics Inc. Judge Nakamura also ordered Delray to pay restitution of $2.1 million to Brightfield Logistics Inc., payable within five years.

Delray was arrested on June 9, 2023, by agents of the FBI at his home in Piedmont, California, following a referral from the company's board. He was charged on July 18, 2023, with three counts of wire fraud and one count of grand theft. Brightfield Logistics Inc., which was acquired by Meridian Transport Group in 2021, has since implemented new internal audit controls. Company spokesperson Denise Farrow said the firm "is relieved this chapter is closed" and reaffirmed confidence in current leadership under CEO Alan Truitt.

MANCHESTER, England -- October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City edged Liverpool 2-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, with a stoppage-time winner from midfielder Rodri sealing a dramatic victory in front of 53,412 fans. Erling Haaland opened the scoring in the 23rd minute, converting a penalty after defender Ibrahima Konate was penalized for a foul inside the box. Liverpool responded through forward Mohamed Salah, who equalized in the 61st minute with a low strike from the edge of the area. The match appeared headed for a draw until Rodri struck in the 92nd minute, finishing a rebound after a save by goalkeeper Alisson Becker. Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola praised his team's resilience after the final whistle, saying the club had shown "character built over five years together." Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp acknowledged the loss but pointed to positives, noting his side created "enough chances to win two games." The victory moved Manchester City to 22 points after nine matches in the Premier League, three points clear of second-placed Arsenal. Liverpool dropped to fourth place with 17 points. The two clubs are scheduled to meet again on March 10, 2024, at Anfield in Liverpool for the reverse fixture. City's next match comes on October 21, 2023, against Brighton & Hove Albion at the Amex Stadium.

MANCHESTER, England — October 14, 2024. Manchester City edged Aston Villa 2-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, with a stoppage-time header from Erling Haaland sealing the win in front of 53,412 fans. The Norwegian striker rose above two defenders in the 91st minute to convert a corner from Kevin De Bruyne, sparking wild celebrations among the home supporters. Villa had taken an early lead through Ollie Watkins in the 12th minute, finishing a swift counterattack, before Rodri equalized for City just before halftime with a low strike from the edge of the box. Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola praised his side's resilience after the match, telling reporters, "We never stopped believing, even when Villa were pressing us hard." Aston Villa boss Unai Emery countered that his team "deserved at least a point" given their first-half performance. The victory moved Manchester City to the top of the Premier League table with 21 points from eight games, one point ahead of Liverpool. Haaland's goal was his ninth of the season, extending his lead in the race for the Golden Boot. The match, played at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, was overseen by referee Michael Oliver, who booked four players including Villa captain John McGinn for a late challenge in the 67th minute. Manchester City will next travel to London on October 21 to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, while Aston Villa host Bournemouth the same weekend at Villa Park.

Roswell Industrial Group announced Tuesday that it will acquire Denton Fabrication Corp for $214 million, marking the largest equipment-manufacturing deal in the region this year. The transaction, disclosed at a press conference in Akron, Ohio, will bring Denton's 1,300 employees under the Roswell umbrella and expand its footprint into precision metal parts for the aerospace sector.

Roswell CEO Marta Villanueva said the acquisition, expected to close by January 15, 2025, will help the company compete more effectively with rivals such as Cascade Steelworks. "Denton has spent thirty years building a reputation for quality, and we intend to honor that legacy," Villanueva told reporters.

Denton Fabrication, founded in 1994 by engineer Harold Denton, has been based in Canton, Ohio since its earliest days. Harold Denton, now 71, said he plans to retire once the deal is finalized. "It's time to pass the torch," he said in a brief statement released by the company.

Analysts at Sterling Capital Partners estimated the deal values Denton at roughly 9 times its 2023 earnings. Shares of Roswell Industrial Group rose 4 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.20.

The deal still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, a process expected to take up to ninety days. If approved, Roswell said it would retain Denton's manufacturing plant in Canton and add roughly 200 new jobs by the end of 2025.

AUSTIN, Texas -- October 14, 2024 -- Halcyon Robotics Inc., a leading manufacturer of industrial automation systems, announced today that it has acquired Vantage Sensor Technologies LLC, a privately held sensor manufacturer based in Round Rock, Texas, for approximately $84 million in cash and stock.

The acquisition, which closed on October 11, 2024, is expected to strengthen Halcyon Robotics' position in the industrial automation market. Vantage Sensor Technologies, founded in 2011 by engineer Priya Nandakumar, employs 140 people and generated $22 million in revenue last year.

"This acquisition allows us to integrate advanced sensing capabilities directly into our robotic arms," said Marcus Webb, Chief Executive Officer of Halcyon Robotics, during a press conference held at the company's Austin headquarters. "Priya and her team have built something remarkable, and we're thrilled to welcome them aboard."

As part of the transaction, Priya Nandakumar will join Halcyon Robotics as Vice President of Sensor Engineering, effective November 1, 2024. She will report directly to Marcus Webb and will relocate her core team to Halcyon's facility in Austin.

Halcyon Robotics, headquartered in Austin, Texas, was founded in 2005 by Marcus Webb and currently employs approximately 1,200 people worldwide. The company competes directly with Denver-based Ironclad Automation Corp. in the industrial robotics sector.

Financial terms of the deal were advised by Sterling & Cross Capital Partners, which served as exclusive financial advisor to Vantage Sensor Technologies.

On September 12, 2024, Judge Priscilla Owens sentenced Marcus Delaney, 41, of Oakland, to 36 months in state prison after a jury in Oakland convicted him of grand theft and embezzlement. Prosecutor Angela Ruiz of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office had charged Delaney on March 3, 2024, alleging he diverted $412,000 from his former employer, Bayview Logistics Inc., between 2021 and 2023 while serving as Chief Financial Officer.

The trial, held at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, began on July 8, 2024, and lasted eleven days. Testimony showed that Delaney transferred company funds to a shell entity called Coastal Trade Partners LLC, which he secretly controlled. Bayview Logistics Inc., headquartered in Fremont, California, is a subsidiary of Harmon Freight Group.

Defense attorney Walter Song argued that his client acted under duress from a former business partner, but the jury rejected the claim after two days of deliberation. Judge Owens also ordered Delaney to pay restitution of $412,000 to Bayview Logistics Inc. within five years of his release.

Angela Ruiz told reporters outside the courthouse that the sentence "sends a clear message to corporate officers who abuse their position of trust." Delaney's attorney said he intends to file an appeal with the California Court of Appeal within 60 days.

MANCHESTER, England — October 14, 2023. Aldergrove United clinched a dramatic 2-1 victory over Portsmith Rovers at Bramwell Park on Saturday, keeping their unbeaten home record intact this season. Striker Kofi Anane scored twice, including a stoppage-time winner in the 91st minute, sending the crowd of 24,300 into raptures.

The visitors had taken an early lead through midfielder Diego Salcedo in the 12th minute, but Anane equalized just before halftime with a low finish from inside the box. His second goal, a header from a corner delivered by captain Liam Foxwell, sealed the win.

Aldergrove United manager Petra Vintner praised her side's resilience after the match. "We showed real character tonight," she told reporters at the post-match press conference held inside Bramwell Park. "Kofi has been outstanding all season, and this performance shows why he deserves recognition."

The result moves Aldergrove United to second place in the Northern Championship table, three points behind leaders Castlebridge FC. Portsmith Rovers manager Owen Whitlock admitted his team's defending was costly. "We gave away two soft goals," he said.

Anane, who joined Aldergrove United in July 2021 from Riverside Athletic for a reported fee of 3.2 million pounds, was named Man of the Match by the Northern Championship board. The league also confirmed that Anane will receive the Player of the Month award for October, to be presented at Bramwell Park on November 3.

Aldergrove United next travel to Castlebridge FC on October 21 for a top-of-the-table clash.

Danville, Ohio — Meridian Foods Corp. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Blue Ridge Snack Co., a privately held pretzel and chip maker based in Roanoke, Virginia, for $340 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by December 15, marks Meridian's third acquisition in two years as the packaged-foods giant seeks to expand its presence in the salty-snacks category.

Under the agreement, Blue Ridge Snack Co. will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Foods Corp., retaining its factory in Roanoke and its 410 employees. Blue Ridge founder and chief executive officer Harlan Voss will step down once the transaction closes, according to a company statement. Voss, who started the company in 1997 with his sister Denise Voss, said the sale would "give the brand the resources to grow nationally."

Meridian's chief executive officer, Priya Nathan, said the acquisition would add roughly $95 million in annual revenue and strengthen the company's supply relationship with regional grocery chain Harlow Markets, which carries Blue Ridge products in over 600 stores across the Mid-Atlantic. Shares of Meridian Foods Corp., which trades on the Nasdaq, rose 4.2 percent to $58.30 on Wednesday following the announcement.

Analysts at Carrow & Bell Securities in Chicago said the purchase price represented roughly 9 times Blue Ridge's estimated EBITDA. The transaction still requires clearance from the Federal Trade Commission, which Meridian expects to obtain before the end of the first quarter of next year.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. — October 3, 2024 — Arcadia Biosystems Inc., a biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, announced today that it has acquired Nordlund Therapeutics AB, a Swedish biotech firm based in Uppsala, Sweden, for approximately $340 million in cash and stock.

The acquisition, expected to close by December 15, 2024, will give Arcadia Biosystems full ownership of Nordlund's lead compound, ARB-217, an experimental treatment for chronic hepatitis B currently in Phase 2 trials. Dr. Helena Moritz, Chief Executive Officer of Arcadia Biosystems, called the deal "a pivotal step in our mission to combat viral liver disease worldwide."

As part of the transaction, Nordlund Therapeutics founder Dr. Sven Lindqvist will join Arcadia Biosystems as Chief Scientific Officer, effective November 1, 2024. Lindqvist founded Nordlund Therapeutics in 2016 and has led its hepatitis B research program since then.

Arcadia Biosystems, listed on the Nasdaq under ticker ARCB, will fund the acquisition through a combination of $200 million in cash reserves and $140 million in newly issued common shares. The company's board of directors, led by Chairman Robert Fennimore, approved the transaction unanimously on September 28, 2024.

Arcadia Biosystems employs roughly 1,200 people across facilities in Cambridge, San Diego, and Basel, Switzerland. Following the merger, the combined company expects to retain all 85 Nordlund employees at its Uppsala research site.

Shares of Arcadia Biosystems rose 6.4 percent following the announcement, closing at $47.82 on the Nasdaq.

MANCHESTER, England — Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as Villa defeated Everton 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, lifting the club to fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a low finish after a through ball from midfielder John McGinn, then doubled the lead in the 41st minute with a header from a corner. Everton pulled one back in the 58th minute through striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin, but substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win with a curling effort in the 84th minute in front of 41,235 fans.

Villa manager Unai Emery praised his team's discipline after the match, saying the victory keeps Villa in contention for a Champions League spot. "We controlled the tempo for long periods," Emery told reporters at Villa Park. Everton manager Sean Dyche admitted his side struggled defensively, particularly against Watkins, who has now scored 14 goals this season.

The result extended Villa's unbeaten home run to seven matches. Villa will next travel to London on November 9 to face Tottenham Hotspur at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, while Everton return to Goodison Park to host Newcastle United on November 10. Villa currently sit on 27 points, five behind league leaders Manchester City, who defeated Brighton 2-0 earlier on Saturday. Emery, who joined Villa in November 2022, has overseen a marked improvement in the club's fortunes since taking charge.

HARTFORD, Conn. — Meridian Steelworks Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in outstanding debt and a sharp decline in industrial demand. The Hartford-based manufacturer, founded in 1962 by Walter Osgood, employs roughly 2,200 workers across three plants in Connecticut and Ohio.

CEO Marissa Kellerman told reporters at a press briefing that the company would continue operations during restructuring. "We intend to emerge stronger by early 2026," Kellerman said. The filing was made in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Connecticut.

Meridian's troubles deepened after rival Titan Alloy Corp. undercut steel prices last year, and after a fire damaged the company's Youngstown, Ohio facility in March, injuring four employees. Analysts at Brookline Capital Partners estimate creditors may recover only 40 percent of what they are owed.

The United Steelworkers union, representing 1,800 Meridian employees, announced a demonstration outside the Hartford headquarters on Thursday to protest potential layoffs. Union president Daniel Reyes said workers "built this company for six decades and deserve better."

Meridian's board also disclosed that Kellerman will step down as CEO effective January 15, 2026, to be replaced by current COO Priya Nandakumar. Shares of Meridian, which trade over the counter, fell 62 percent following the bankruptcy announcement. The company's next hearing before Judge Elaine Foster is scheduled for December 3.

On Tuesday, March 4, 2025, Judge Marion Coates sentenced Devon Ratliff, 37, of Oakland, to 48 months in state prison after a jury convicted him of grand theft and embezzlement in connection with his former position as Chief Financial Officer of Bayline Freight Partners, a logistics firm headquartered in Emeryville, California. Defense attorney Simon Okafor had requested probation, citing his client's lack of prior record.

Ratliff was arrested on October 14, 2023, by investigators from the Alameda County Sheriff's Office after Bayline Freight Partners' new controller, Priya Menon, discovered irregular wire transfers during a routine audit. He was formally charged on November 2, 2023, with one count of grand theft and two counts of embezzlement.

During Monday's hearing at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, Judge Coates also ordered Ratliff to pay restitution of $612,000 to Bayline Freight Partners within five years of his release. Ratliff's employment with the company, where he had worked since March 2016, ended immediately following his arrest. Company founder Harlan Voss issued a statement thanking the Sheriff's Office and the District Attorney's Office for their work on the case.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday, March 11, 2025, that it will allocate 240 million euros to upgrade the aging rail network connecting Lyon and Marseille. Transport Minister Élise Rambert unveiled the plan during a press briefing at the ministry's headquarters in Paris, describing it as the largest infrastructure investment in the region since 2010. According to Rambert, the funds will be distributed to SNCF Réseau, the state-owned rail infrastructure operator, over a period of three years beginning in June 2025. The project will replace roughly 180 kilometers of track and modernize 14 stations, including the facility at Gare de Lyon-Part-Dieu. Deputy Minister Antoine Ferrand, who joined the briefing, stated that the initiative is expected to reduce travel time between the two cities by 25 percent and create approximately 3,200 construction jobs. The announcement follows a report published last month by the National Audit Office, which criticized the ministry for delays affecting nearly 60 percent of regional rail projects since 2018. Opposition lawmaker Camille Dubois, a member of the National Assembly, welcomed the funding but urged the ministry to publish quarterly progress reports. SNCF Réseau chief executive Marc Villeneuve is scheduled to meet with regional officials in Marseille on April 2, 2025, to finalize construction timelines. The government said a second phase, covering the Marseille-Nice corridor, will be considered pending an independent review due by December 2025.

THREAD: Kodiak Robotics just laid off 62 employees at its Mountain View facility, effective November 4, 2024. CEO Don Burnette announced the cuts in an internal memo obtained by TechCrunch, citing a slowdown in autonomous trucking contracts. This is the second round of layoffs this year after 40 workers were cut in March.

Sources say the company is burning through cash faster than expected after losing a supply deal with Daimler Truck North America last quarter. Kodiak's main rival, Aurora Innovation, poached three senior engineers from the Mountain View office just last week, including lead perception engineer Priya Nair, who starts at Aurora's Pittsburgh office on November 18, 2024.

Despite the layoffs, Kodiak raised $50 million in a bridge round led by Koch Disruptive Technologies back in August 2024, according to filings reviewed by Bloomberg. Investors reportedly pushed for the cuts to extend runway into 2025.

Employees affected will receive severance through January 2025, per a company spokesperson. One laid-off engineer, Marcus Webb, tweeted: "Six years at Kodiak and I find out via a 7am email. Brutal."

Kodiak was founded in 2018 by Don Burnette and Paz Eshel in Mountain View, California, and has focused on driverless trucks for logistics giants like US Xpress. No word yet on whether the Daimler contract loss triggers further restructuring.

Will update this thread as more details emerge. #layoffs #autonomoustrucking #SiliconValley

Boston, MA -- November 12, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tirzepatide-based therapy for patients with early-stage nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh and published in The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology, enrolled 214 participants across seven sites in the United States and Canada between January 2021 and March 2023. Patients received weekly subcutaneous injections of the compound, developed by Eli Lilly and Company, over a 52-week period. Results showed a 63 percent reduction in liver fat content among treated patients compared to 12 percent in the placebo group, with 41 participants achieving complete resolution of steatohepatitis without worsening fibrosis. Dr. Marsh presented the findings at the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases meeting in Boston on November 10, 2023. "These results suggest a meaningful shift in how we approach metabolic liver disease," Marsh said during the presentation. Co-author Dr. Rajiv Patel of the University of Toronto noted that three patients experienced moderate gastrointestinal side effects requiring dose adjustment, but no serious adverse events were reported. Eli Lilly and Company plans to launch a Phase 3 trial in early 2024, pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimated the drug could generate $4.2 billion in annual revenue by 2027 if approved for NASH treatment, a condition affecting an estimated 5 percent of adults in the United States. The trial was funded by a $38 million grant from the National Institutes of Health.
