Pixelworks Labs, a Portland-based imaging firm, unveiled its Halo X8 projector on June 3, 2024, at a press event in San Jose, California. Priced at $1,299, the Halo X8 targets home theater enthusiasts who want 4K output without the bulk of traditional units. I tested the unit for two weeks at my apartment in Austin, Texas, and came away impressed, though not without reservations.

The Halo X8 uses a proprietary chip called VisionCore 3, developed in-house by Pixelworks Labs, which the company claims cuts input lag by 40 percent compared to its previous model, the Halo X6. Brightness peaks at 2,200 lumens, enough for moderately lit rooms, and the built-in speaker system, co-engineered with Boston-based audio company Cambridge Acoustics, delivers surprisingly full sound for a device this size.

CEO Diane Marsh, who founded Pixelworks Labs in 2016, told reporters that the company plans to ship 50,000 units by December 2024, with an eye toward competing directly with Anker's Nebula line. "We think the Halo X8 undercuts Nebula on price while matching it on brightness," Marsh said during the Q&A session.

Setup took under ten minutes, and the companion app, available for iOS and Android, handled focus and keystone correction automatically. My main complaint: the fan noise becomes noticeable during dark scenes. At $1,299, the Halo X8 isn't cheap, but it undercuts most 4K rivals by roughly $300. For buyers craving portability without sacrificing picture quality, this is one of the more compelling projectors of 2024.

Ministry of Environment and Water Resources, Nairobi, 14 March 2024 - The Government of Kenya today announced a new regulatory framework aimed at reducing plastic pollution in Lake Victoria and the wider Rift Valley basin. Cabinet Secretary Amina Otieno stated that the National Environmental Management Authority (NEMA) will enforce the Plastic Waste Management Act starting 1 July 2024, imposing fines of up to 500,000 Kenyan Shillings on manufacturers found violating packaging standards. Speaking at a press briefing in Nairobi, Otieno confirmed that NEMA has already inspected 42 factories across Kisumu and Nakuru counties since January, resulting in the suspension of operating licenses for three companies, including Lakeview Plastics Ltd. The ministry will also partner with the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) to fund a 3 billion Shilling cleanup initiative along the Winam Gulf, expected to begin in September 2024. Deputy Director John Mwangi noted that roughly 60 percent of solid waste collected from the lake shoreline consists of single-use plastic bottles. Local fishermen in Kisumu, represented by the Lake Victoria Fisherfolk Association, welcomed the move, saying declining fish stocks have been linked to pollution over the past decade. President William Ruto is expected to sign supplementary regulations during a visit to Kisumu on 22 April 2024. Otieno urged private sector stakeholders, including Bidco Africa and East African Breweries, to accelerate adoption of biodegradable packaging ahead of the July deadline.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. — October 14, 2024 — Solara Biotics, Inc. announced today that it has acquired NeuroPath Diagnostics, a privately held startup based in Austin, Texas, for approximately $92 million in cash and stock. The acquisition, expected to close on November 30, 2024, will strengthen Solara's presence in neurological disease screening.

NeuroPath Diagnostics, founded in 2018 by Dr. Priya Kapoor, developed a portable blood-based assay for early detection of Alzheimer's disease. The device, marketed as NeuroScan-100, has been used in clinical trials across 14 hospitals in the United States.

"This acquisition allows us to bring life-changing diagnostic tools to patients faster," said Marcus Ellery, Chief Executive Officer of Solara Biotics, during a press briefing held at the company's headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts. "Dr. Kapoor and her team have built something remarkable."

As part of the deal, Dr. Kapoor will join Solara Biotics as Senior Vice President of Diagnostics, effective December 1, 2024. She will report directly to Ellery and oversee a team of 45 researchers currently based in Austin.

Solara Biotics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs over 1,200 people worldwide and trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker SLRA. The company reported $410 million in revenue for fiscal year 2023, a 12 percent increase from the previous year.

The transaction is subject to customary regulatory approvals, including review under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act.

Boston, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tovirimab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Aldebaran Therapeutics, for treatment of chronic hepatitis D infection. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti and published in The New England Journal of Medicine, enrolled 214 adult patients across sites in Boston, Toronto, and Berlin between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants received either 300 milligrams of tovirimab administered intravenously every four weeks or a placebo. After 48 weeks, 62 percent of patients receiving tovirimab achieved undetectable hepatitis D virus RNA levels, compared with 11 percent in the placebo group. The most common adverse event was mild injection-site reaction, reported in 18 percent of treated patients; no cases of severe liver injury were recorded. Dr. Marchetti stated that the findings support advancement to a Phase 3 trial, which Aldebaran Therapeutics plans to initiate in early 2025 with an estimated budget of $47 million. The company, founded in 2018 by immunologist Dr. Rajiv Nair, has received $120 million in venture funding from Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz. Hepatitis D, caused by the hepatitis D virus, affects an estimated 12 million people worldwide and can lead to cirrhosis and liver failure if untreated. Aldebaran Therapeutics' chief executive officer, Priya Subramaniam, said the company is also exploring combination therapy with bulevirtide, a drug already approved in the European Union. The full trial data will be presented at the European Association for the Study of the Liver congress in Vienna on June 5, 2024.

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY

On October 14, 2024, Judge Marlene Whitfield sentenced Anthony Ruiz, 37, of Newark, to 8 years in state prison after a jury convicted him of aggravated arson in connection with a fire at the Beacon Street Warehouse in Newark on March 2, 2023. Prosecutor Diane Kessler of the Essex County Prosecutor's Office argued that Ruiz deliberately set the blaze using gasoline, causing an estimated $650,000 in damages and injuring firefighter Paul Doyle, who suffered smoke inhalation while battling the flames.

Ruiz was arrested on March 9, 2023, by detectives from the Newark Police Department following a two-week investigation. He was formally charged on April 3, 2023, with arson and reckless endangerment. During the trial, held at the Essex County Courthouse in Newark between September 16 and September 20, 2024, defense attorney Louis Bartram maintained that his client was elsewhere at the time.

Judge Whitfield, in delivering the sentence, cited the severity of the injury to Doyle and the destruction of the warehouse, which was owned by Meridian Logistics Inc. The company's president, Carol Nunziato, testified that the property loss forced the layoff of 42 employees. Ruiz's sentence will run concurrently with a separate 2-year term for a probation violation in Union County. His attorney has indicated plans to appeal the verdict to the New Jersey Appellate Division within 45 days.

DETROIT, Feb. 9 — Meridian Motors Inc. announced Friday it will acquire electric-vehicle battery maker VoltCore Technologies for $1.2 billion, a deal the companies say will secure supply chains ahead of new federal emissions rules taking effect in 2027. Meridian CEO Nathan Alvarez said the acquisition, expected to close by June 15, will let the Dearborn-based automaker build batteries domestically for its Pulsar EV lineup. VoltCore, headquartered in Austin, Texas, was founded in 2016 by engineer Priya Raman, who will join Meridian's executive team as Chief Battery Officer once the deal closes. The announcement was made at a press conference at Meridian's Dearborn headquarters, where Alvarez stood alongside Raman and Meridian board chairman Douglas Feenan. Shares of Meridian rose 6 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the news, while shares of rival automakerHarrow Auto Group fell 2 percent. Analysts at Kessler Brothers Capital said the deal positions Meridian to compete more directly with Tesla and Harrow in the EV market. VoltCore employs roughly 900 workers across two facilities in Austin and a research site in Boulder, Colorado. Under the agreement, Meridian will retain all VoltCore staff and keep the Austin plant operating for at least three years. The deal still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which Alvarez said he expects within 90 days.

1/6 Big update from Portland: TriMet's board voted Tuesday to approve a $340 million contract with Kiewit Corporation to extend the MAX Orange Line by 4.2 miles into Milwaukie by 2028. Announced this morning at TriMet HQ on NE Holladay Street.

input: The Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks announced on April 9, 2024 that it will invest $42 million to upgrade flood-control infrastructure along the Grand River near Cambridge, Ontario. The funding, unveiled by Minister Andrea Kowalski at a press briefing in Kitchener, follows the severe flooding of March 2024 that displaced roughly 1,200 residents and damaged 340 homes in the region. Kowalski stated that the province will partner with the Grand River Conservation Authority to construct a new retention basin near Highway 8 and reinforce four aging levees by December 2025. "Families in Cambridge deserve certainty that their homes will not be underwater every spring," Kowalski said. The Conservation Authority's chief engineer, Rajiv Mehta, confirmed that construction crews from Bexley Contracting Ltd. will begin site preparation on May 20, 2024. Bexley Contracting, headquartered in Guelph, Ontario, was awarded the $18 million construction contract following a competitive tender process that concluded in February 2024. Opposition critics, including MPP Daniel For-tin of the Ontario New Democratic Party, argued the funding arrives too late for families still living in temporary shelters. The ministry noted that a separate $6 million grant will be distributed directly to affected homeowners through the Disaster Recovery Assistance Program starting June 1, 2024. Premier Doug Ford is expected to visit the site on May 15, 2024 to formally launch the project alongside Kowalski and Mehta.

Case No. RG24-118837

On March 14, 2024, Judge Marcia Feldstein presided over the sentencing hearing of Defendant Oscar Trujillo, 41, in Department 12 of the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, California. Trujillo pleaded guilty on January 9, 2024 to one count of grand theft under California Penal Code Section 487, stemming from the embezzlement of $186,450 from his former employer, Bayview Logistics Inc., where he served as Chief Financial Officer between June 2019 and August 2023.

Deputy District Attorney Lauren Kessler argued for the maximum term, citing the prolonged nature of the fraud, while defense counsel Marcus Whitfield requested probation, noting Trujillo's cooperation and full restitution offer. Judge Feldstein sentenced Trujillo to 3 years in state prison and ordered restitution of $186,450 to Bayview Logistics Inc., payable within 18 months of his release.

Bayview Logistics Inc., headquartered in Fremont, California, is a subsidiary of Delacroix Holdings, a supply-chain conglomerate founded by Henri Delacroix in 1998. Company spokesperson Priya Nandakumar stated the firm has since implemented new internal audit controls, including quarterly reviews conducted by outside accounting firm Whitmore & Cole LLP.

Trujillo is scheduled to report to San Quentin State Prison on April 1, 2024. His attorney has indicated an intention to appeal the restitution order within 30 days.

On March 14, 2024, Judge Miriam Escobar sentenced Darnell Cooper, 37, to 46 months in state prison after a jury found him guilty of embezzlement in connection with funds taken from Pacific Crest Credit Union, headquartered in San Jose, California. Prosecutor Alan Reyes of the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office argued that Cooper, who worked as a Senior Accounts Manager at Pacific Crest Credit Union from January 2019 until his termination in August 2023, diverted approximately $612,000 in member deposits into a shell company registered under his cousin's name, Trevor Cooper.

The trial, held at the Santa Clara County Hall of Justice in San Jose, began on February 5, 2024, and lasted eleven days. Defense attorney Priya Nair contended that Cooper had been coerced by a former supervisor, but the jury rejected this claim on March 8, 2024, convicting him on four counts of embezzlement and one count of falsifying financial records.

Pacific Crest Credit Union CEO Marlene Huang told reporters outside the courthouse that the institution had already reimbursed all 214 affected members and had strengthened internal audit controls. "We take full responsibility for the lapses that allowed this to happen," Huang said.

Cooper is scheduled to begin serving his sentence at San Quentin State Prison on April 1, 2024. His attorney has indicated plans to appeal the verdict to the California Court of Appeal within 60 days.

input: Ingrid Solberg (born 14 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her work on cod population dynamics in the North Sea. She earned a doctorate from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø that same year as a Research Fellow. In 1994 Solberg became Director of Fisheries Science at the Institute of Marine Research, a position she held for eleven years. Her 1997 book, The Silent Fjord, documented declining herring stocks and was translated into six languages. Solberg's research contributed to the establishment of the Barents Sea Cod Management Plan, adopted by Norwegian authorities in 2001. In 2003 she received the Nansen Award from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to marine ecology. She left the Institute of Marine Research in 2005 to found the nonprofit organization OceanFuture in Bergen, which advocates for sustainable fishing practices across Scandinavia. Solberg married fellow biologist Anders Kval in 1982, and the couple had two children, Marte and Sindre Kval. She served on the board of the World Wildlife Fund Norway from 2008 to 2016. Now retired, Solberg lives in Bergen and continues to publish articles on ocean acidification in the journal Marine Ecology Progress Series.

input: BOSTON, MA – April 9, 2024 – Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tirvametol, an oral small-molecule chemical developed by Cambridge-based biotechnology firm Aldrix Therapeutics, for the treatment of relapsed acute myeloid leukemia. The 18-month study, led by Dr. Priya Ramaswami and presented at the American Society of Hematology meeting in Chicago, enrolled 214 adult patients across 12 sites in the United States and Germany. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of tirvametol twice daily showed a 46 percent overall response rate, compared with 19 percent in the placebo group, according to data published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology. Dr. Ramaswami stated that the drug's mechanism, which inhibits the FLT3 enzyme pathway, appeared to reduce disease progression without the severe cardiotoxicity observed with earlier agents such as quizartinib. Aldrix Therapeutics was founded in 2016 by former Genentech scientist Dr. Marcus Ellery, who now serves as Chief Executive Officer. The company, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, raised $85 million in a Series C funding round led by Sequoia Capital in March 2023 to support late-stage trials. Aldrix plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the fourth quarter of 2025. Competitor Daiichi Sankyo, which markets quizartinib, said it would continue independent trials of its own FLT3 inhibitor. The National Cancer Institute provided a $6.2 million grant supporting the trial's biomarker analysis. Full results will be presented at the European Hematology Association congress in Madrid this June.

DETROIT, Mich. — Ferrostal Dynamics Inc., a mid-sized auto-parts supplier headquartered in Detroit, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in outstanding debt and a sharp drop in orders from General Motors. The filing was submitted to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan.

CEO Marta Kowalski told reporters at a press conference that the company would continue operating during restructuring, with plans to cut 1,200 jobs across its three Michigan plants by January 15, 2025. "This was an extremely difficult decision, but it gives us a path forward," Kowalski said.

Ferrostal Dynamics was founded in 1987 by engineer Harold Voss and has supplied brake components to General Motors and Ford Motor Company for over three decades. Industry analyst Priya Nandakumar of Whitfield Capital said the bankruptcy reflects broader turmoil in the automotive supply chain, worsened by rising steel prices and a seven-week strike last year.

General Motors, based in Detroit, issued a statement Wednesday saying it does not expect the filing to disrupt production at its Lansing Grand River plant. Ford Motor Company declined to comment.

Court documents show Ferrostal owes $52 million to steel supplier Nucor Corporation. A hearing before Judge Rebecca Alston is scheduled for December 4, 2024, to review the company's reorganization plan.

DETROIT, Mich. — Nov 14, 2023 — Autoparts supplier Ridgeline Components Inc. announced Tuesday it has acquired Bakerton Hydraulics LLC, a privately held manufacturer of hydraulic braking systems based in Toledo, Ohio, for approximately $142 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by Jan 15, 2024, will make Bakerton Hydraulics a wholly owned subsidiary of Ridgeline Components, headquartered in Detroit, Mich.

Ridgeline Components' chief executive officer, Marcus Fenwick, said the acquisition would strengthen the company's position against rival Torrance Brake Systems Corp., which has grown rapidly in the Midwest market. "This transaction gives us direct access to Bakerton's patented braking technology and a loyal customer base among commercial truck manufacturers," Fenwick told reporters during a briefing at Ridgeline's Detroit headquarters.

Bakerton Hydraulics, founded in 1987 by engineer Diane Sorrell, employs roughly 340 workers at its Toledo plant. Sorrell, who stepped down as chief executive officer in 2019, remains a minority shareholder and will join Ridgeline's advisory board next month.

Ridgeline shares rose 6.2 percent to $58.30 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume nearly tripled. Analysts at Hargrove Capital Partners called the deal "a smart, defensively minded move" in a note published Wednesday. The combined company will employ more than 4,800 people across facilities in Michigan, Ohio, and Indiana. Ridgeline expects the acquisition to add $65 million in annual revenue starting in fiscal year 2024.

Kansas City, MO -- October 14, 2024 -- Trailing by seven points with under three minutes remaining, quarterback Derek Halloway threw a 22-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Marcus Ibe to lift the Kansas City Wolverines past the Denver Stallions, 27-24, at Arrowhead Commons on Monday night. The victory extended the Wolverines' winning streak to six games and kept them atop the Midwest Division standings.

Halloway finished 24 of 33 for 289 yards and two touchdowns, while Ibe hauled in eight receptions for 112 yards. Running back Tyrell Nash added 94 rushing yards on 19 carries, including a crucial 14-yard scramble that set up the game-winning drive. Head coach Bill Renfro praised his offensive line after the game, saying the unit "controlled the trenches all night long."

Denver's quarterback, Sam Okafor, threw for 301 yards and three touchdowns but was intercepted twice, including once by Wolverines safety Julian Cross with 1:47 left to seal the outcome. Stallions head coach Priya Deshmukh acknowledged the defensive lapse, telling reporters, "We simply couldn't get a stop when it mattered."

The win improved the Wolverines to 6-1 on the season, while the Stallions dropped to 4-3. Kansas City will next travel to Chicago on October 21 to face the Chicago Marauders, a matchup that could decide the division's top seed. Approximately 61,500 fans attended Monday's contest, according to Arrowhead Commons officials.

Bellroy, the Melbourne-based accessories brand, has launched the Venture Ready Backpack, a 22-liter travel pack designed for digital nomads and available now for $199 at bellroy.com. Built from a 900-denier recycled polyester shell, the bag features a padded 16-inch laptop sleeve, a hidden passport pocket, and a magnetic strap system Bellroy calls QuickCinch. The Venture Ready Backpack was designed by Bellroy's product team in Fitzroy, Victoria, and manufactured under contract by Huafeng Textiles in Dongguan, China. According to Bellroy co-founder Andy Fallshaw, the pack underwent 14 months of field testing with travelers in Tokyo, Lisbon, and Vancouver before its release on March 3, 2024. The company reports that early reviews from Wirecutter and Outside Magazine praised the backpack's water-resistant YKK zippers and its 2.3 kilogram weight. Bellroy, founded in 2010 by Andy Fallshaw and Steve Fallshaw, is headquartered in Collingwood, Australia, and competes directly with Peak Design and Tortuga in the premium travel-bag market. The Venture Ready Backpack comes in three colorways -- Basalt, Cherry Cola, and Forest -- and ships with a lifetime warranty covering manufacturing defects. Customers who purchase before April 30, 2024 will receive a complimentary packing cube set worth $35. Bellroy processed over 40,000 pre-orders in the first 48 hours after the product page went live, according to a statement from marketing director Priya Raman. The backpack is not currently compatible with Bellroy's older Transit Sling accessory line, though a redesigned clip adapter is expected in June 2024.

MADRID, Spain, June 8 — Real Madrid claimed a record-extending fifteenth Champions League title on Saturday, defeating Borussia Dortmund 2-0 in front of 87,000 fans at Wembley Stadium in London. Striker Vinícius Júnior scored the opening goal in the 25th minute, latching onto a pass from Jude Bellingham, before midfielder Dani Carvajal added a second in the 83rd minute to seal the victory.

Head coach Carlo Ancelotti, who now holds a record for most Champions League titles as a manager, praised his squad's resilience after the match. "This group never stops believing," Ancelotti told reporters at the post-match press conference. "Winning this competition for a fifth time is something I could never have imagined when I started coaching."

Borussia Dortmund manager Edin Terzić accepted the defeat gracefully, noting that his young side had matched Real Madrid for long spells before conceding twice in the second half. Dortmund captain Emre Can was named among the tournament's best defenders despite the loss.

The victory extended Real Madrid's dominance in European football, with club president Florentino Pérez confirming plans to celebrate the title with a parade through Madrid on Sunday, expected to draw tens of thousands of supporters to the Plaza de Cibeles. UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin presented the trophy to Real Madrid captain Nacho Fernández immediately after the final whistle.

Real Madrid will begin their title defense next season on August 17 against newly promoted side Real Sociedad B.

OTTAWA, September 12, 2023 — The Ministry of Environment and Climate Change today announced a new $240 million investment to accelerate the closure of coal-fired power plants across Alberta and Saskatchewan by 2027. Minister Elena Choquette said the funding, administered through the Clean Energy Transition Fund, will support retraining for approximately 3,200 workers and finance the construction of two new solar facilities near Medicine Hat and Estevan. "This is a concrete step toward meeting our commitment under the Paris Agreement," Choquette told reporters at a press conference held at the National Press Theatre. The announcement follows a report published last month by the Pembina Institute, which found that Canada's coal sector emitted 38 megatonnes of carbon dioxide in 2022 alone. TransAlta Corporation, which operates three of the affected plants in Alberta, welcomed the funding but warned that the 2027 timeline could strain regional electricity supply during winter months. Premier Danielle Smith criticized the plan on Tuesday, calling it "an unfunded mandate that ignores Alberta's energy realities." The federal government said additional details, including a facility-by-facility closure schedule, will be released by Environment Canada before December 1, 2023. Opposition critic Pierre Lavoie of the Conservative Party demanded an independent audit of the fund's disbursement process, arguing that similar programs in Ontario had faced delays exceeding 18 months.

CLEVELAND, OH — October 14, 2024 — Halbrook Industrial Group announced today that it has acquired Vantex Machining Corp., a Dayton-based precision parts manufacturer, for $86 million in cash. The transaction, finalized on October 11, 2024, expands Halbrook's footprint in the aerospace supply chain and adds Vantex's 340 employees to Halbrook's workforce of roughly 4,200.

Under the terms of the deal, Vantex will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary and retain its Dayton facility on Kettering Boulevard. Halbrook CEO Marion Alvarado said the acquisition strengthens the company's ability to supply titanium components to Boeing and other aerospace customers. "Vantex has built a 30-year reputation for precision, and we intend to invest an additional $12 million in new equipment over the next two years," Alvarado said during a press briefing held at Halbrook's headquarters in Cleveland.

As part of the transition, Vantex founder and longtime president Gerald Nkemelu will step down from his role effective November 1, 2024, and will be succeeded by current Halbrook vice president Sylvia Truong, who will relocate to Dayton to lead the newly formed Halbrook Aerospace Components division.

Halbrook, headquartered in Cleveland since its founding in 1978 by industrialist Walter Ostrowski, reported $1.4 billion in revenue last year. The company's stock rose 3.2 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners called the move a strong signal that Halbrook intends to compete more directly with Rockwell Precision Systems in the North American aerospace components market.

DENVER, Colorado -- Mountain Peak Resources Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Blackstone Ridge Mining Corp. for $412 million in a cash-and-stock deal, expanding its footprint in the lithium extraction business. The agreement, disclosed at a press briefing at the company's headquarters in Denver, will see Mountain Peak pay $260 million in cash and issue 4.8 million shares to Blackstone Ridge shareholders.

CEO Diane Farrow said the acquisition, expected to close by January 15, 2025, positions Mountain Peak as a top-three lithium supplier in North America. "This deal strengthens our supply chain and accelerates our push into battery-grade materials," Farrow told reporters. Blackstone Ridge's outgoing chief executive, Marcus Ohlin, will step down from his position once the transaction closes, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Analysts at Redwood Capital Partners, a financial advisory firm based in Chicago, estimate the combined entity will generate roughly $1.3 billion in annual revenue by 2026. Shares of Mountain Peak rose 7 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Blackstone Ridge stock climbed 11 percent.

The deal still requires approval from regulators, including the Federal Trade Commission, and is subject to a 60-day review period. Mountain Peak, founded in 2011 by geologist Peter Vance, operates six mining sites across Nevada and Arizona. Blackstone Ridge, headquartered in Reno, Nevada, employs approximately 1,450 workers.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Press Statement
Ottawa, Ontario — March 14, 2024

Minister Cynthia Alaverdian announced today that the federal government will allocate $420 million over four years to upgrade the Trans-Canada Highway between Sudbury and Thunder Bay, a stretch spanning approximately 680 kilometres. The funding, approved under the National Infrastructure Renewal Act, follows a report by the Canadian Highway Safety Board that documented 37 fatal collisions along the corridor since 2019.

"This investment will save lives," said Minister Alaverdian during a press conference held at the Sudbury Community Arena. "We cannot continue to accept preventable deaths on a route that carries over 12,000 vehicles daily."

The project will be managed by Halcyon Infrastructure Group, a subsidiary of Bellwood Construction Corp headquartered in Mississauga, Ontario. Halcyon was awarded the contract on February 2, 2024, after a competitive bidding process that also included bids from Redgate Civil Works and Northstar Paving Ltd. Construction is scheduled to begin on May 6, 2024, and is expected to employ 1,400 workers across the province.

Deputy Minister Farooq Bhatti confirmed that the Ontario Ministry of Transportation will contribute an additional $95 million toward the widening of Highway 17 near Nipigon. Officials from both ministries met with representatives of the Thunder Bay Chamber of Commerce on March 12, 2024, to discuss local hiring commitments.

The government expects the project to reduce collision rates by 40 percent upon completion in late 2028.

BOSTON, MA -- November 4, 2023 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital reported promising results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating vidarapan, an oral chemical compound targeting IL-17 signaling, in patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh, an associate professor of dermatology, enrolled 214 participants across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between January 2022 and March 2023. Participants received either 30 milligrams of vidarapan daily or placebo for 16 weeks. According to results published in The Journal of Clinical Dermatology, 68 percent of patients receiving vidarapan achieved at least a 75 percent reduction in psoriasis severity, compared with 19 percent in the placebo group. Dr. Marsh presented the findings on November 3, 2023, at a meeting of the American Academy of Dermatology held in Chicago, Illinois. "These results suggest vidarapan could become a valuable oral alternative to injectable biologics," Marsh said during her presentation. The trial was funded by Solenta Pharmaceuticals, a biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, which plans to begin a Phase 3 trial in early 2024 involving approximately 900 patients. Solenta's chief executive officer, Raj Patel, stated the company intends to seek approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by 2026. Common side effects included mild headache and nasal congestion, with no serious adverse events reported. Dr. Marsh noted that longer-term data are needed to assess durability of response and safety beyond one year. The research was supported in part by a grant from the National Institutes of Health.

CAMBRIDGE, MA, September 9, 2024 -- Arcadia BioWorks Inc., a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, announced today that it has acquired Northport Therapeutics LLC, a privately held gene-therapy startup based in Durham, North Carolina, for approximately 240 million dollars in cash and stock.

The acquisition, expected to close on October 15, 2024, will give Arcadia BioWorks full rights to NPX-118, Northport's lead investigational therapy for sickle cell disease, currently in Phase 2 trials. Dr. Helena Marsh, Chief Executive Officer of Arcadia BioWorks, said the deal strengthens the company's pipeline in rare genetic disorders.

"Northport's work on NPX-118 represents exactly the kind of innovation we want to bring to patients faster," Marsh said during a press briefing in Boston on Monday.

As part of the transaction, Dr. Raymond Osei, founder and former CEO of Northport Therapeutics, will join Arcadia BioWorks as Chief Scientific Officer effective October 16, 2024. Osei founded Northport Therapeutics in 2016 in Durham with an initial investment of 3 million dollars from local backers.

Arcadia BioWorks, founded in 2011 by Helena Marsh and listed on the Nasdaq under ticker ARCB, reported revenue of 512 million dollars in fiscal year 2023. The company employs roughly 1,400 people across facilities in Cambridge, San Diego, and Basel, Switzerland.

Shares of Arcadia BioWorks rose 6 percent in after-hours trading following the announcement. The combined company plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the third quarter of 2025.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solstice Robotics announced today it has acquired Pecan Labs, a 40-person startup building warehouse-picking arms, for $78 million in cash and stock. Deal closes November 15, 2024.

2/ Pecan Labs was founded in 2019 by Maria Torres, a former Tesla engineer, and has been quietly supplying pick-and-place modules to three of the top five US grocery chains.

3/ Solstice CEO Daniel Whitfield said in a call with reporters this morning that Torres will join Solstice as Chief Robotics Officer starting December 2, 2024, reporting directly to him.

4/ "This isn't about headcount, it's about the 12 patents Pecan Labs holds on gripper sensing," Whitfield told CNBC. Solstice shares rose 6% on the Nasdaq after the announcement.

5/ Worth noting: Solstice competes head-to-head with Berkshire Robotics and Nordic Autonomy Group in the fulfillment-automation space, and this buy narrows the gap significantly.

6/ Torres posted on X: "Proud of what we built in Boston since 2019. Excited to scale this inside Solstice." Pecan Labs will operate as a subsidiary based in Boston for now.

7/ Solstice, headquartered in Austin, Texas, employs about 1,100 people and last year reported $310 million in revenue. Analysts at Morgan Stanley called the deal "a smart, if pricey, bolt-on."

8/ No layoffs are planned, per an internal memo sent to staff Tuesday.

HARTFORD, Conn. — Meridian Steelworks Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in outstanding debt and collapsing demand from the automotive sector. The filing, submitted in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Hartford, comes two years after the company's CEO, Diane Kowalski, took over from founder Robert Alden.

Meridian Steelworks, headquartered in New Haven, Connecticut, employs roughly 2,100 workers across three plants in Ohio, Pennsylvania and Indiana. Kowalski told reporters the company plans to keep all facilities operating during restructuring, though she did not rule out layoffs. "We intend to emerge leaner and more competitive by early 2026," she said during a press conference at the company's New Haven headquarters.

The bankruptcy follows a steep decline in orders from General Motors, one of Meridian's largest customers, after the automaker shifted sourcing to Nucor Corporation last year. Analysts at Fitch Ratings downgraded Meridian's credit rating to CCC in September, citing liquidity concerns.

Meridian's shares, traded on the Nasdaq under the ticker MRSW, fell 62 percent to $1.15 after the announcement. The United Steelworkers union, which represents about 1,400 Meridian employees, said it would seek assurances that pension obligations remain protected. A hearing before Judge Patricia Nunez is scheduled for November 14 to review the company's reorganization plan.

THREAD: Layoffs + a bright spot 1/6

Starting today, Vantage Robotics Inc. is cutting 240 jobs at its Fremont, California plant, according to CEO Marisol Ortega. The company filed a WARN notice on June 3, 2024, citing weaker demand from Nordic Freight Group, its biggest customer since 2021.

2/6 Ortega told employees in an email obtained by our newsroom: "This is not the outcome we wanted." Vantage was founded in 2015 by Ortega and her brother Diego Ortega in a garage in Palo Alto before moving to Fremont in 2018.

3/6 On the brighter side, Vantage announced it acquired Kestrel Vision Labs, a Boston-based startup, for $38 million on May 29, 2024. The deal brings 45 engineers into Vantage's autonomy division led by CTO Priya Nandakumar.

4/6 Priya Nandakumar will present the combined roadmap at the Robotics World Summit in Austin, Texas on July 14, 2024. She joined Vantage in 2019 after leaving Boston Dynamics.

5/6 Meanwhile, about 60 laid-off workers gathered outside Fremont City Hall this morning to demand severance guarantees. Organizer Luis Bautista said negotiations with management are ongoing.

6/6 Vantage's stock (ticker VRBT) dropped 7% in early Nasdaq trading. Analysts at Fenwick Capital, including Tom Reyes, expect a rebound once Kestrel's lidar tech ships in Q4.

CLEVELAND, Ohio — Federated Steel Corp., the century-old manufacturer headquartered in Cleveland, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $412 million in outstanding debt and a sharp decline in orders from the automotive sector. CEO Marlene Ostrowski told reporters at a Contact.Communicate-style press briefing at the company's downtown headquarters that the filing would allow Federated Steel to restructure operations while continuing to pay its 2,300 employees.

The bankruptcy filing, submitted in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Ohio, comes three weeks after rival producer Ardmore Metals acquired Federated's smaller competitor, Buckeye Alloy Works, for $89 million. Analysts at Fitch Ratings said Federated Steel had struggled since 2019 to compete with cheaper imported steel from China and Vietnam.

Ostrowski, who became chief executive in March 2021, said the company would close its Youngstown plant by January 15, 2025, eliminating roughly 640 jobs. "This is not the outcome we wanted, but it gives us a path forward," she said during the briefing, which was attended by union representative Gary Halvorsen of the United Steelworkers.

Federated Steel's stock, which trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker FDST, fell 47 percent in early trading following the announcement. The company's board, led by chairman Thomas Reyes, is expected to meet again next week to review a proposed $150 million debtor-in-possession loan from JPMorgan Chase.

Ingrid Solheim (born 14 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist and former Director-General of the Institute of Marine Research in Bergen. She earned a doctorate in oceanography from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research as a researcher the same year. In 1998 Solheim was appointed Director-General of the Institute of Marine Research, a position she held for sixteen years. During her tenure she led a 2003 expedition aboard the research vessel Johan Hjort to study cod stocks in the Barents Sea, work that informed Norway's 2006 fisheries quota reforms. Solheim also served as a scientific advisor to the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea, headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, from 2001 to 2009. In 2012 she received the Nansen Award from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to marine ecosystem research. Solheim stepped down as Director-General in July 2014 and was succeeded by Erik Fossum. She subsequently joined the University of Bergen as a professor of marine biology in September 2014. Solheim is married to Torbjørn Aas, a former naval officer, and the couple has two children. Her memoir, Cold Currents, published in 2019 by Aschehoug, describes her research voyages in the Arctic. She currently lives in Bergen and continues to publish on climate change effects on North Atlantic fish populations.

input: Voltrek Outdoors, headquartered in Bend, Oregon, has launched the TrailBlazer X4, a 4-person waterproof tent designed for backcountry camping. Priced at $349.99, the TrailBlazer X4 is available now on Voltrek's website and at REI stores across the United States starting November 12, 2024. The tent weighs 8.2 pounds and features a ripstop nylon shell rated for winds up to 45 mph. Voltrek Outdoors was founded in 2016 by former Patagonia engineer Daniel Ruiz, who serves as the company's Chief Product Officer. According to Ruiz, the TrailBlazer X4 underwent 18 months of field testing in the Cascade Range before release. Each tent ships with a lifetime warranty and a repair kit manufactured by supplier Gorilla Fabrics Inc., based in Portland, Oregon. Early reviewers, including outdoor journalist Priya Nair of Backpacker Magazine, praised the tent's 60-second setup time and called it "a genuine upgrade over the discontinued TrailBlazer X3." Voltrek Outdoors reported that pre-orders reached 3,200 units within the first 72 hours, generating roughly $1.1 million in revenue. The company plans to donate 2 percent of December sales to the Pacific Crest Trail Association. Customers can choose from three colorways: Slate Gray, Forest Green, and Sunrise Orange. This is a new, first-generation product with no prior model recalls, and Voltrek is offering a 30-day money-back guarantee for all purchases made before January 15, 2025.

BOSTON, MA — March 4, 2024. Researchers at Beacon Hill Therapeutics announced Phase 2 trial results for BHT-221, an oral small-molecule inhibitor developed to treat moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis. The 24-week, randomized, placebo-controlled study enrolled 312 adults across 41 sites in the United States and Germany, led by Dr. Priya Sundaram, the company's Chief Medical Officer. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of BHT-221 twice daily achieved clinical remission at a rate of 38 percent, compared with 14 percent for placebo, a difference the authors called statistically significant (p<0.001). Endoscopic improvement was observed in 45 percent of treated patients versus 19 percent of controls. The most common adverse events were headache and mild nausea; three patients discontinued treatment due to elevated liver enzymes. Dr. Sundaram presented the findings on March 4 at Digestive Disease Week in Chicago, Illinois, noting that BHT-221 could offer an alternative to biologic therapies such as infliximab for patients who fail conventional treatment. Beacon Hill Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, was founded in 2016 by Dr. Marcus Feldman and is backed by venture funding from Sequoia Capital. The company plans to begin a Phase 3 program in the third quarter of 2024, pending discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Shares of Beacon Hill Therapeutics, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker BHTX, rose 22 percent following the announcement. Analysts at Jefferies Group estimated peak annual sales potential of $1.8 billion if the drug receives approval by late 2026.

DETROIT, Mich. — Auto parts maker Halden Industries filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in outstanding debt and a sharp decline in orders from General Motors and Ford Motor Company. The filing, submitted in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan, marks the third bankruptcy in the auto supply sector this year.

CEO Marcus Feldman told reporters at a press briefing in Detroit that the company would continue operations during restructuring, with roughly 2,200 employees remaining on payroll at plants in Toledo, Ohio and Kokomo, Indiana. "This is a painful but necessary step to preserve jobs and modernize our supply chain," Feldman said.

Halden Industries, founded in 1978 by engineer Walter Halden, has supplied brake components to Ford Motor Company for over three decades. Shares of the company, traded on Nasdaq under the ticker HLDN, fell 62 percent to $1.14 in after-hours trading following the announcement.

Analysts at Morningstar said the bankruptcy reflects broader turmoil in the industry as automakers shift toward electric vehicles, reducing demand for traditional combustion parts. Halden's largest creditor, JPMorgan Chase, is owed approximately $118 million and will participate in restructuring talks scheduled for November 14 in Detroit.

Feldman added that no immediate layoffs are planned, though the company may close a smaller facility in Flint, Michigan by early 2025.

DENVER, Colorado — Rockwell Midstream Partners announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Basin Gathering LLC, a privately held pipeline operator based in Midland, Texas, for $740 million in cash and stock. The deal, confirmed by Rockwell Midstream chief executive officer Diane Fasano, is expected to close by December 15, 2024, pending approval from the Federal Trade Commission.

Under the terms of the agreement, Rockwell Midstream will pay $520 million in cash and issue 6.3 million shares of common stock to Basin Gathering's owner, Terrence Cole, who founded the company in 2011. The acquisition adds roughly 900 miles of natural gas pipelines across the Permian Basin to Rockwell Midstream's existing network.

"This transaction strengthens our footprint in West Texas and positions us to compete more directly with Enterprise Products Partners," Fasano said during a call with analysts on Wednesday.

Rockwell Midstream, headquartered in Denver, also announced that Marcus Webb, previously senior vice president of operations, will step down from his role effective November 1, 2024, to pursue what the company described as a new opportunity. He will be succeeded by Priya Nandakumar, who joins from Enbridge Inc.

Shares of Rockwell Midstream rose 4.2 percent to $58.90 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement. Analysts at Morgan Stanley raised their price target on the stock to $65, citing the deal's expected contribution of $85 million in annual free cash flow starting in 2025.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday, 14 May 2024 that it will invest 420 million euros to upgrade regional rail infrastructure across Bavaria, Germany. Speaking at a press conference in Munich, Transport Minister Elena Vogt said the funding will modernize 38 stations and replace aging signal systems along the Nuremberg-Munich corridor by December 2026. Deutsche Bahn, the state-owned rail operator headquartered in Berlin, will oversee construction, with subcontractor Alstom SE supplying new signaling equipment. Minister Vogt stated, "This investment will cut average delays by 30 percent and create roughly 1,200 jobs in the region." The announcement follows a report by the German Federal Audit Office, which found that 22 percent of regional trains were delayed by more than ten minutes in 2023. Opposition lawmaker Klaus Richter criticized the plan, arguing that similar promises made in 2019 were only partially fulfilled, with just 60 percent of the promised stations completed. Local officials in Nuremberg welcomed the funding, noting that Nuremberg Central Station, built in 1900, urgently needs renovation. The Ministry expects construction to begin in September 2024, pending approval from the Bavarian state parliament, which is scheduled to vote on 3 June 2024. If approved, this would represent the largest single rail investment in Bavaria since reunification, according to Ministry spokesperson Anna Keller.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- Nov 14, 2023 -- Arkview Biotech, Inc. announced today that it has acquired PathoSense Diagnostics Ltd, a Dublin-based developer of rapid pathogen-detection tools, for $145 million in cash. The acquisition is expected to close by Dec 20, 2023, pending regulatory approval.

Under the agreement, Arkview will pay PathoSense shareholders $145 million, funded through existing cash reserves and a $50 million credit facility arranged with Meridian National Bank. PathoSense, founded in 2016 by Dr. Fiona Callahan, employs 82 people at its headquarters in Dublin, Ireland, and has developed a diagnostic platform capable of detecting the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis within 90 minutes.

"This acquisition strengthens our infectious disease portfolio and accelerates our path to market," said Arkview CEO Raymond Doust, who will oversee integration alongside Dr. Callahan, who is joining Arkview as Chief Scientific Officer effective Jan 2, 2024.

Arkview Biotech, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, currently employs 340 people and posted revenue of $210 million in fiscal year 2023. The company's shares (NASDAQ: ARKV) rose 6.2 percent in after-hours trading following the announcement.

The deal was advised by Whitcombe & Rourke LLP, serving as legal counsel to Arkview, while PathoSense was represented by Dublin-based Farrow Kent Solicitors. Analysts at Braddon Securities project the combined entity could capture an additional 12 percent share of the tuberculosis diagnostics market by 2026, intensifying competition with rival firm Genscape Diagnostics.

DETROIT, Nov. 14 -- Ferrous Dynamics Inc., a Michigan-based auto parts supplier, announced Tuesday it has acquired Whitlock Brake Systems LLC for $215 million in cash, expanding its footprint in the electric vehicle components market. The deal, confirmed by Ferrous Dynamics chief executive officer Renata Cole, is expected to close by January 31, 2025, pending regulatory approval.

Whitlock Brake Systems, headquartered in Toledo, Ohio, employs roughly 640 workers and supplies regenerative braking components to General Motors and Rivian. Cole said the acquisition would help Ferrous Dynamics compete more directly with Bosch and Continental AG in the fast-growing EV supply chain.

"This is a pivotal step in our strategy to dominate the next generation of braking technology," Cole told reporters during a press briefing at the company's Dearborn headquarters.

Ferrous Dynamics, founded in 1987 by engineer Harold Whitfield, reported revenue of $3.1 billion last fiscal year, a 6 percent increase from 2022. Shares of the company rose 4.8 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.32.

Whitlock's founder, Marcus Whitlock, will step down as president once the transaction closes, according to a company filing. He plans to join the board of a nonprofit focused on manufacturing education in Ohio.

Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimated the deal could add $180 million in annual revenue to Ferrous Dynamics by 2026, though they cautioned that integration costs may weigh on margins through mid-2025.

The Ontario Ministry of Transportation announced on June 12, 2024 that it will invest $180 million to upgrade Highway 401 between Milton and Mississauga, Ontario, aiming to reduce congestion by 15 percent within three years. Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria, speaking at a press conference in Toronto, said the project will begin construction on September 3, 2024 and is expected to create 1,200 jobs. "This investment reflects our commitment to keeping goods and people moving across the Greater Toronto Area," Sarkaria said. The funding will be administered through a new agreement with Aecon Group Inc., a Toronto-based construction firm that was awarded the contract following a competitive bidding process managed by Infrastructure Ontario. Aecon's chief executive, Jean-Louis Servranckx, welcomed the announcement, noting that the company had previously completed the Highway 407 expansion in 2019. The Ministry also confirmed that the Canadian Union of Public Employees held a demonstration outside Queen's Park on June 10, 2024 to protest potential job losses among provincial maintenance crews, though officials stated no layoffs are planned. Environmental groups, including Ontario Nature, have raised concerns about wetland disruption near the Credit River. The Ministry stated that an environmental assessment, required under the Environmental Assessment Act, will be completed by January 2025 before construction proceeds further. Premier Doug Ford is expected to visit the site next month to review progress.

Anker Innovations today launched the SoundCore Trek Pro Backpack, a 32-liter travel backpack with a built-in Bluetooth speaker, priced at $149.99 and available exclusively through Amazon starting October 14, 2024. Designed by a small team in Changsha, China, the Trek Pro Backpack integrates two 15-watt drivers, a USB-C fast-charging port rated at 65 watts, and a weatherproof RF-shielded compartment for laptops up to 16 inches. Anker representative Diane Holloway said the product targets commuters and outdoor enthusiasts who want audio on the move without carrying a separate speaker. Early reviewers on Amazon have given the bag an average of 4.6 stars after roughly 1,200 ratings, and a limited batch of 5,000 units sold out within 48 hours of launch in the United States. The backpack comes in three colorways: Slate Gray, Forest Green, and Midnight Black, and includes a 2-year limited warranty covering the electronics. Customers who purchase before November 1, 2024 receive a free 10,000mAh power bank, a $39.99 value. Anker Innovations, headquartered in Shenzhen, competes directly with Bose and JBL in the portable audio accessories market. The company was founded in 2011 by Steven Yang and has since expanded into robotics vacuums, home security cameras, and charging solutions sold in over 100 countries.

Bellwood Outfitters is now shipping the Kestrel 3.0 Trail Runner, a lightweight hiking boot designed and manufactured by Bellwood Outfitters at its facility in Bend, Oregon. Launched on March 14, 2024, the Kestrel 3.0 replaces the original Kestrel model and features a Vibram Megagrip outsole, a recycled-polyester upper, and a waterproof membrane rated for conditions down to -10 degrees Celsius. Each pair weighs 340 grams and is priced at $189.00, available in sizes 6 through 13. Bellwood Outfitters was founded in 2011 by Colin Marsh, a former competitive trail runner, and is headquartered in Portland, Oregon. The company sold roughly 42,000 pairs of its previous Kestrel line last year alone, according to a statement released by spokesperson Denise Ruiz on March 18, 2024. The Kestrel 3.0 is currently listed as new inventory and ships within 3 business days via FedEx Ground. Customers who purchase before April 1, 2024 will receive a complimentary pair of Merino wool socks, a promotion the company says is meant to compete directly with Salomon and Merrell in the crowded trail-running footwear market. Reviewers from Outside Magazine gave the boot 4.5 out of 5 stars, praising its grip on wet granite during test hikes near Smith Rock State Park. Bellwood Outfitters accepts returns within 30 days of purchase for a full refund, provided the boots show no signs of outdoor use.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester United striker Marcus Rashford scored twice on Saturday to lead his club to a 3-1 victory over Everton at Old Trafford, snapping a four-match winless run in the Premier League. Rashford opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low left-footed strike, then added a second from the penalty spot just before halftime after Everton defender James Tarkowski was penalized for a handball inside the box. Bruno Fernandes sealed the win with a header in the 78th minute. Everton's lone goal came from striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 65th minute. The victory lifted Manchester United to eighth place in the table with 13 points from eight matches. Manager Erik ten Hag praised his team's response after a difficult September, telling reporters, "We showed character today, and Marcus was outstanding." Roughly 73,500 fans packed Old Trafford for the match, the second-largest home crowd of the season. Everton manager Sean Dyche said his side would review defensive mistakes ahead of their next fixture against Newcastle United on October 21, 2023. Manchester United will travel to Denmark on October 24, 2023, to face FC Copenhagen in the UEFA Champions League. The club confirmed that midfielder Mason Mount, sidelined since August with a knee injury, could return to training within two weeks, according to a statement released by the club's medical staff.

DETROIT, Mich. — Meridian Motors Inc. announced Tuesday that it has acquired battery startup VoltCore Technologies for $420 million, in a deal aimed at accelerating its electric vehicle production ahead of a planned 2026 launch. The agreement, signed at Meridian's headquarters in Detroit, was confirmed by CEO Rachel Ostrowski during a press briefing attended by roughly 40 reporters. "VoltCore's solid-state battery technology will cut charging times by 60 percent," Ostrowski said. VoltCore, founded in 2019 by engineer Daniel Feng, employs 210 people at its facility in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Feng will join Meridian as Chief Technology Officer starting November 1, replacing outgoing CTO Priya Sharma, who is stepping down after eight years to pursue a teaching position at the University of Michigan. Meridian shares rose 7 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.30. Analysts at Bardwell Capital said the acquisition positions Meridian as a stronger competitor to Tesla and Rivian in the EV market. The deal is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Meridian, headquartered in Detroit since its founding in 1987 by industrialist Walter Kessler, currently produces the Meridian Falcon sedan and the Meridian Atlas SUV. Ostrowski said the company plans to unveil a new EV model, tentatively named the Meridian Volt, at the Detroit Auto Show next April.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday, June 11, 2024, that it will invest 450 million euros to upgrade rail infrastructure across the Lombardy region. Minister Elena Ferraro unveiled the plan at a press conference in Milan, stating that the funds will modernize 120 kilometers of track between Milan and Bergamo by December 2026. The initiative, known as the Lombardy Rail Renewal Program, will be carried out by Ferrovie Italiane S.p.A., the state-owned rail operator headquartered in Rome. Ferraro said the project will create approximately 3,000 jobs and reduce commuter travel times by 25 percent. The announcement follows a series of delays that frustrated residents; in March 2024, roughly 800 commuters staged a demonstration outside Milano Centrale station to protest chronic train cancellations. Deputy Minister Paolo Grassi, who joined Ferraro at the event, confirmed that construction will begin on September 1, 2024, and that the first phase will be completed within 18 months. The Ministry also signed a supply agreement with Alstom S.A., a French rail manufacturer, to provide 40 new electric trains valued at 600 million euros. Ferraro, who has led the Ministry since her appointment in January 2023, emphasized that the investment reflects the government's broader climate strategy under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan. Local officials in Bergamo welcomed the announcement, though some environmental groups called for greater transparency on procurement contracts.

Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1958 in Bologna, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic retrofitting techniques used across southern Europe. She earned her doctorate in civil engineering from the Politecnico di Milano in 1984 and joined Studio Marchetti, a Milan-based engineering consultancy founded by her father, Aldo Marchetti, in 1961.

In 1992 Marchetti was appointed Chief Structural Engineer at Bechtel Italia, where she led the retrofit of the Teatro Massimo in Palermo following damage assessments conducted after the 1990 Sicily earthquake. Her methods, later codified in the technical guideline Eurocode 8 Annex C, were adopted by the Italian Ministry of Infrastructure in 1998.

Marchetti left Bechtel Italia in 2003 to found her own firm, Marchetti Structural Group, headquartered in Turin, with initial capital of 2.3 million euros. The company grew to employ 140 engineers by 2010 and was acquired by the French conglomerate Vinci SA for 78 million euros in November 2011.

In 2015 Marchetti received the Golden Compass Award from the Associazione per il Disegno Industriale in Milan for her contribution to earthquake-resistant public architecture. She married fellow engineer Paolo Ricci in 1986; their son, Marco Ricci, is now a bridge designer at Arup in London.

Marchetti retired from active practice in 2020 and currently serves as an honorary professor at the Politecnico di Milano.

CHICAGO, September 12, 2024 — Meridian Foods Corporation announced today that it has acquired Prairie Harvest Bakeries, a regional bakery chain based in Madison, Wisconsin, for $85 million in cash. The acquisition, expected to close by October 30, 2024, will add 22 retail locations and a 140,000-square-foot production facility to Meridian's portfolio.

Under the terms of the agreement, Prairie Harvest founder and Chief Executive Officer Linda Vance will step down from her role but will remain as a consultant through March 2025. Meridian's Chief Executive Officer, Robert Aldana, said the deal strengthens the company's presence in the Midwest.

"Prairie Harvest has built a beloved brand over 35 years, and we intend to preserve its recipes and its people," Aldana said during a press conference held at Meridian's headquarters in Chicago, Illinois.

Meridian Foods Corporation, headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, currently employs approximately 4,300 people across 12 states and reported revenue of $1.2 billion in fiscal year 2023. The company also owns Golden Valley Snacks, acquired in 2019, and competes with national players such as Sunrise Baking Company.

As part of the transition, Meridian will appoint David Chen, currently Vice President of Operations, to the newly created position of General Manager of the Midwest Division, effective November 1, 2024. Chen previously worked at Sunrise Baking Company for eight years.

Meridian's stock traded up 3 percent following the announcement. The transaction remains subject to customary regulatory approval.

input: Vantage Outdoor Co., headquartered in Bend, Oregon, has released the Ridgeline 45L backpack, a lightweight touring pack designed for multi-day treks. Priced at $189.00, the Ridgeline 45L is constructed from 210-denier recycled nylon and weighs just 1.4 kilograms. Vantage Outdoor Co. was founded in 2011 by former REI product manager Dana Kowalski, who now serves as Chief Design Officer. The pack officially launched on September 9, 2024, at the Outdoor Retailer Summer Market trade show in Denver, Colorado. Each Ridgeline 45L includes an internal hydration sleeve, adjustable torso length from 16 to 22 inches, and a lifetime warranty against manufacturing defects. According to Vantage Outdoor Co. spokesperson Marcus Feld, the company sold over 3,000 units in the first two weeks after launch, generating roughly $567,000 in revenue. The backpack is manufactured in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, at a facility operated by longtime supplier Thanh Long Textiles, and is shipped to warehouses in Portland, Oregon before distribution across North America. Competitor Osprey Packs has already responded with a promotional discount on its similar Exos 48 model, though industry analyst Priya Ramachandran of Outside Business Journal noted that the Ridgeline 45L's price point undercuts most rivals by roughly 15 percent. The Ridgeline 45L is available now in three colorways: Slate Gray, Moss Green, and Rust Orange, exclusively through Vantage Outdoor Co.'s website and select REI locations nationwide.

BOSTON, MA -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital reported on March 14, 2024 that a Phase 2 trial of the investigational drug pentraxamib reduced hospitalizations among patients with moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis by 42 percent over 24 weeks. The randomized, double-blind study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez and sponsored by Cambridge-based Solara Therapeutics, enrolled 318 participants across 11 clinical sites in the United States and Germany between June 2022 and January 2024. Participants received either 150 milligrams of pentraxamib or placebo administered subcutaneously once weekly. Results, published in The Lancet Rheumatology, showed a statistically significant reduction in serum C-reactive protein levels compared with placebo (p<0.001). Dr. Vasquez presented the findings at the American College of Rheumatology annual meeting in San Diego on March 15, 2024. "These data suggest pentraxamib could become a first-line option for patients who fail methotrexate," she said. Solara Therapeutics' chief executive, Marcus Feldman, announced that the company plans to file for FDA approval by the fourth quarter of 2025. The trial was funded in part by a $12 million grant from the National Institutes of Health. Solara Therapeutics, founded in 2018 by Feldman and immunologist Dr. Priya Nair, was acquired by Novartis in a $2.3 billion deal completed in September 2023, though it continues to operate as an independent subsidiary. Side effects reported included mild injection-site reactions and headache; no serious adverse events attributable to pentraxamib were recorded. A Phase 3 trial is expected to begin enrollment in early 2025 at additional sites in France and Japan.

event: American College of Rheumatology annual meeting

input: SUPERIOR COURT OF ARIZONA, MARICOPA COUNTY — On October 14, 2024, Judge Renata Solis sentenced Marcus Delaney, 41, to seven years in state prison after a jury convicted him of aggravated robbery and assault with a deadly weapon. The charges stemmed from an incident on March 3, 2023, at a Circle K convenience store on East Van Buren Street in Phoenix, in which Delaney struck clerk Priya Nanda with a metal pipe and fled with approximately $860 in cash. Prosecutor Diane Kessler of the Maricopa County Attorney's Office argued that Delaney posed an ongoing danger to the public, citing a prior 2019 conviction for burglary. Defense attorney Harold Beckmann countered that his client suffered from untreated schizophrenia and requested placement in a treatment-focused facility rather than a standard correctional institution. Judge Solis, presiding at the Maricopa County Superior Courthouse, denied the request but ordered that Delaney receive psychiatric evaluation within 30 days of intake. Nanda, who suffered a fractured wrist in the attack, read a victim impact statement describing lasting anxiety and medical bills exceeding $4,200. Detective Omar Fields of the Phoenix Police Department, who arrested Delaney on April 9, 2023, testified that surveillance footage from the store was central to the case. The sentencing concludes a case first filed in Maricopa County Superior Court in June 2023 under case number CR2023-004471.

Reuters, DETROIT — Auto parts maker Delphi Technologies filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, October 14, citing $2.3 billion in outstanding debt and slumping demand for combustion-engine components. The filing was made in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware. Chief Executive Officer Marcus Whitfield told reporters at a press conference in Detroit that the company would continue operations at its 47 manufacturing plants worldwide while it restructures. "This is a difficult but necessary step to secure Delphi's long-term future," Whitfield said. The company employs roughly 18,000 workers across 18 countries, including large operations in Michigan, Poland, and Mexico. Delphi Technologies, which was spun off from Delphi Automotive PLC in 2017, has struggled as automakers including Ford Motor Company and Stellantis shift toward electric vehicles. Shares of Delphi fell 62% in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement. Analyst Rebecca Chen of Morgan Stanley said the bankruptcy reflects broader turmoil in the internal combustion supply chain. Delphi's largest creditor, JPMorgan Chase, has agreed to provide $450 million in debtor-in-possession financing to keep operations running during restructuring. A bankruptcy hearing before Judge Laurie Selber Silverstein is scheduled for November 3 in Wilmington, Delaware. Whitfield added that no immediate layoffs are planned, though the company may sell its brake systems division as part of the restructuring plan.

1/ Big news from Austin: Solstice Robotics announced this morning that it has acquired Marrow Labs, a 40-person startup building soft-tissue surgical grippers, for $58 million in cash and stock. Deal closed Tuesday, June 11.

2/ Solstice CEO Priya Nandakumar said the acquisition will let the company fold Marrow Labs' gripper tech directly into the Talon-9 surgical arm, which already ships to 120 hospitals across the US and Canada.

3/ Marrow Labs was founded in 2019 by Dr. Aaron Feld, a former Johns Hopkins researcher, in a small lab space in Cambridge, Massachusetts. He'll join Solstice as Chief Medical Officer starting July 1.

4/ Solstice, headquartered in Austin, Texas, employs about 340 people and competes directly with Meridian Surgical Systems, which controls roughly 22% of the soft-tissue robotics market.

5/ Analysts at Baird Capital estimate Solstice's revenue will grow 15% next fiscal year on the strength of the merged product line. Shares of Solstice (ticker SLST) rose 4.3% in early trading Wednesday.

6/ Not everyone's thrilled. Outside Solstice's Austin headquarters, about 30 gig-worker contractors protested Tuesday afternoon, demanding full-time status after the acquisition news raised fears of layoffs.

7/ Nandakumar told reporters at a press briefing in Austin that no current Marrow Labs staff will be let go before 2025. We'll keep watching this one closely.

MANCHESTER, England -- October 14, 2024 -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as Villa defeated Manchester City 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, handing Pep Guardiola's side their second Premier League loss of the season. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute, converting a low cross from midfielder John McGinn, before doubling his tally in the 51st minute with a curling finish past goalkeeper Ederson. Erling Haaland pulled one back for City in the 63rd minute, heading home a corner delivered by Kevin De Bruyne, but substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win for Villa in stoppage time. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, saying the team had "executed the game plan perfectly." The victory lifted Aston Villa to second place in the Premier League table with 21 points from 8 matches, three points behind leaders Liverpool. Manchester City, chasing a fifth consecutive league title, dropped to fourth place with 16 points. The match, played in front of 42,000 spectators at Villa Park, was Watkins' first career brace against City. Guardiola confirmed after the game that defender Kyle Walker would undergo further scans on a hamstring injury sustained in the second half. Aston Villa will next travel to face Bologna in the UEFA Champions League on October 22, while City host Wolverhampton Wanderers on October 19.

Marguerite Okafor (born 14 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-British structural engineer known for pioneering lightweight bridge designs across West Africa. She emigrated to the United Kingdom in 1979 to study at Imperial College London, earning a degree in Civil Engineering in 1983. In 1991 Okafor joined Bexley & Hart Engineering in London as a junior associate, rising to the position of Chief Structural Engineer by 1998. She left Bexley & Hart in 2004 to found Okafor Bridgeworks Ltd, headquartered in Bristol, United Kingdom, a firm specializing in modular pedestrian bridges. Under her leadership, the company designed the Kaduna River Footbridge, completed in 2011 at a cost of 2.4 million pounds, which won the Institution of Civil Engineers' Global Award in 2012 in London. Okafor married fellow engineer Thomas Reyes in 1996; the couple has one daughter, Amara Reyes, born in 2001 in Bristol. In 2015, Okafor Bridgeworks Ltd was acquired by the multinational firm Halloway Infrastructure Group for 18 million pounds, though Okafor remained as a consultant until her retirement in 2020. She was appointed a Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering in 2013. Okafor currently resides in Bristol and continues to lecture part-time at the University of Bath. Her memoir, Spanning Rivers, was published in 2021 by Fenwick Press.

Portland, Oregon-based Cascade Robotics Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Willamette Sensor Systems, a privately held maker of industrial lidar components, for $142 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by January 15, 2025, will make Willamette Sensor Systems a wholly owned subsidiary of Cascade Robotics.

Chief Executive Officer Maria Ferreira said the acquisition strengthens Cascade Robotics' position against rival Denver-based Highline Automation Corp. in the warehouse robotics market. "This gives us the sensing technology we need to compete at scale," Ferreira told reporters during a briefing at the company's headquarters.

As part of the transaction, Willamette Sensor Systems founder and Chief Technology Officer David Okafor will join Cascade Robotics as Senior Vice President of Sensing Technology, effective January 15, 2025. Okafor founded Willamette Sensor Systems in Eugene in 2016 after leaving Intel Corporation, where he had worked as a research engineer for nine years.

Cascade Robotics shares rose 6.3 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, closing at $58.14. Analysts at Blackstone Capital Advisors said the deal values Willamette Sensor Systems at roughly 9 times projected 2025 revenue of $15.8 million.

The transaction will be funded through $90 million in existing cash reserves and a new $52 million credit facility arranged by First Republic Bank. Cascade Robotics expects the acquisition to add approximately $4 million to operating expenses in the first two quarters of 2025 before becoming profitable by the fourth quarter.

Regulatory filings are expected to be submitted to the Federal Trade Commission within thirty days.

input: Bergstrom Outdoor Supply is now shipping the Kestrel 3200 Insulated Backpack, a 32-liter daypack engineered for alpine trekking in temperatures as low as -20 degrees Celsius. Designed by lead engineer Naomi Cargill at the company's Bozeman, Montana workshop, the Kestrel 3200 features a ripstop nylon shell, a hydration bladder compartment, and a magnetic sternum strap. Bergstrom Outdoor Supply, founded in 2011 by Anders Bergstrom, sources its waterproof zippers from Fujita Textile Corporation, a supplier based in Osaka, Japan. The Kestrel 3200 launched on September 14, 2023, and is priced at $189.00. It is available in three colors: Slate Gray, Forest Green, and Rust Orange. Each unit ships with a lifetime warranty and a 60-day return policy. Customer reviews on the Bergstrom website praise the pack's durability, with one reviewer, hiking guide Marcus Feldt of Denver, Colorado, noting he used it during a 9-day trek across the Torres del Paine circuit in Chile without a single seam failure. The company reports it sold 4,700 units in the first month alone, prompting Bergstrom Outdoor Supply to expand production capacity at its Bozeman facility by 30 percent. Retailers interested in wholesale pricing can contact the sales department at wholesale@bergstromoutdoor.com. This is a brand-new product, not a refurbished or used model, and is currently in stock for immediate delivery.

Duluth, Minnesota — Northern Ore Mining Corp., a mid-sized iron-ore producer based in Duluth, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing a $340 million debt load and collapsing taconite prices. The filing, submitted to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Minnesota, lists roughly 1,200 employees whose jobs are now at risk.

CEO Randall Petersen told reporters at the company's headquarters that the decision followed months of failed negotiations with lenders led by Great Lakes Capital Partners. "We fought to keep this company alive, but falling steel demand and a 22 percent drop in ore prices left us no choice," Petersen said.

The bankruptcy comes three months after Northern Ore's chief rival, Superior Range Minerals, acquired the smaller Vermilion Iron Company for $85 million, further tightening competition in the region. Analysts at Fitch Ratings warned the restructuring could ripple through Minnesota's Iron Range, an area already struggling with mine closures since 2019.

Governor Elena Marsh said Wednesday she would meet with union representatives from the United Steelworkers in St. Paul on Friday to discuss emergency aid. "These are hardworking families, and the state will not abandon them," Marsh said in a statement.

Northern Ore's stock, which traded at $12 a share in January, closed at 41 cents on Tuesday. Court documents indicate a reorganization plan could be presented by March 2025.

organization: U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Minnesota
