SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. HG-24-118872 — People of the State of California v. Marcus D. Whitfield

On Tuesday, June 11, 2024, Judge Elena R. Suarez presided over the sentencing hearing of Marcus D. Whitfield, 41, a former financial analyst at Cornerstone Capital Partners, at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, California. Whitfield was convicted on May 2, 2024 of wire fraud and embezzlement after prosecutors from the Alameda County District Attorney's Office, led by Deputy District Attorney Priya Chandrasekaran, proved he diverted $2.3 million from client accounts between 2019 and 2023.

Judge Suarez sentenced Whitfield to 78 months in state prison and ordered restitution of $2.3 million to be paid to the twenty-two victims, most of whom were retirees living in Fremont and San Leandro. Defense attorney Gerald T. Munoz argued for leniency, citing his client's lack of prior record, but the court rejected the request.

Cornerstone Capital Partners, headquartered in San Francisco, was fined $500,000 by the Securities and Exchange Commission in a separate civil action filed on March 14, 2024, after regulators found the firm failed to supervise Whitfield's trading activity. The firm's chief executive, Daniel Ostrowski, issued a statement saying Cornerstone had strengthened internal compliance controls since the incident came to light in 2023.

Whitfield is expected to begin serving his sentence at San Quentin State Prison next week.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF SANTA CLARA — On October 14, 2024, Judge Marcia Ellenbogen sentenced defendant Raymond Tolliver, 47, to 5 years in state prison after a jury convicted him of grand theft and securities fraud in connection with the collapse of his investment firm, Tolliver Capital Partners, headquartered in San Jose, California. Prosecutor Anita Reyes, representing the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office, told the court that Tolliver had defrauded at least 32 investors of approximately $4.2 million between March 2019 and June 2023, funneling client funds into a shell company called Westbridge Holdings. The trial, which began on September 3, 2024 at the Santa Clara County Superior Courthouse, included testimony from forensic accountant Diane Kowalski, who traced wire transfers totaling $1.8 million to an account in the Cayman Islands. Defense attorney Marcus Webb argued that Tolliver's business partner, Sean Farrelly, had orchestrated the scheme without his client's knowledge, but the jury rejected this claim after eleven days of deliberation. Judge Ellenbogen also ordered Tolliver to pay $4.2 million in restitution to victims, payable within 90 days of his release. Tolliver Capital Partners filed for bankruptcy in Santa Clara in August 2023, shortly after the California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation opened an investigation. Reyes stated that a related case against Farrelly, who fled to Panama in 2023, remains under Justice.ChargeIndict review, with a warrant issued by Judge Ellenbogen for his arrest.

Anker unveiled the Soundcore Frames 2 on March 11, 2024, at a press event in San Jose, California, positioning the $179 audio sunglasses as a rival to Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses. I tested a pair loaned by Anker's PR team for two weeks around Austin, Texas, and came away impressed by battery life but let down by the companion app.

The Frames 2 pack open-ear speakers into a lightweight acetate frame weighing 34 grams, with Bluetooth 5.3 connecting to an iPhone 14 in under three seconds. Anker claims 8 hours of continuous playback, and in my testing I got roughly 7.5 hours before needing a recharge from the included USB-C case, which adds another 24 hours of backup power. Audio quality is surprisingly full for open-ear design, though bass thins out above 60% volume.

Where the product stumbles is software. The Soundcore app crashed three times during setup, and pairing with a Samsung Galaxy S23 took four attempts. Anker's product manager, Elena Fisk, told me the company is aware of the bug and plans a firmware update by April 2024.

At $179, the Frames 2 undercut the $299 Ray-Ban Meta glasses made by EssilorLuxottica, though they lack a camera entirely. For anyone who just wants music and calls without earbuds, that trade-off might be worth 120 dollars in savings. I'd recommend waiting for the software patch before buying, but the hardware itself earns a cautious thumbs-up.

The Ministry of Environment and Water Resources announced on Tuesday that Singapore will invest 240 million dollars over the next five years to upgrade coastal flood defenses along the East Coast. Minister Grace Fu unveiled the plan at a press conference held at the Marina Barrage facility, describing it as part of the national Coastal Protection Strategy. According to the ministry, the funding will support the construction of a new tidal gate near Marina Bay and the reinforcement of sea walls in Pasir Ris. Dr. Tan Wei Ming, chief engineer at the Public Utilities Board, said the project will begin in March 2025 and is expected to be completed by December 2028. The announcement follows a review conducted after Tropical Storm Linfa caused flooding in low-lying areas of Singapore last November, affecting more than 3,000 residents. The Public Utilities Board will oversee construction alongside contractor Hyundai Engineering, which was awarded the tender last week. Minister Fu also confirmed that the National Environment Agency will monitor sea-level data monthly and report findings to Parliament every six months. Opposition Member of Parliament Leong Mun Wai welcomed the funding but urged the ministry to accelerate timelines given rising climate risks. The plan forms part of Singapore's broader commitment under the Paris Agreement to strengthen resilience against extreme weather events. Officials estimate the project will protect over 80,000 households by 2030.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Cedar Peak Robotics announced this morning it has acquired Vantage Sensing Inc. for $42 million in an all-cash deal. Cedar Peak CEO Marisol Vega confirmed the acquisition closed on June 3, 2024.

2/ Vantage Sensing, founded in 2016 by former NASA engineer Ted Okafor, makes LIDAR modules used in warehouse drones. Cedar Peak plans to fold the 38-person team into its Perception division.

3/ Okafor will step down as Vantage's CEO effective June 3, 2024, and join Cedar Peak as Vice President of Sensing Technology, reporting directly to Vega.

4/ Cedar Peak, headquartered in Austin, Texas, competes with Denver-based Halcyon Robotics for contracts with logistics giant Fenwick Freight.

5/ Sources say Halcyon was also bidding for Vantage but was outpaced by Cedar Peak's offer. A Halcyon spokesperson declined to comment.

6/ Vega told reporters at a press briefing in downtown Austin on Tuesday that the deal "strengthens our supply chain against competitors like Halcyon." Fenwick Freight currently sources sensors from both companies.

7/ Analysts at Bramwell Capital estimate the combined entity could reach $310 million in annual revenue by 2026, up from roughly $190 million last year.

8/ Vantage will officially become a subsidiary of Cedar Peak Robotics, retaining its brand name for existing customer contracts through 2025.

End of thread.

Denver-based Ridgeline Foods Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Blue Mesa Snacks LLC, a privately held maker of tortilla chips based in Albuquerque, New Mexico, for $142 million in cash and stock. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing in Denver, Colorado, is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval.

Ridgeline's chief executive officer, Marisol Vance, said the acquisition would expand the company's presence in the Southwest and add roughly 3,400 retail accounts across Texas and New Mexico. "Blue Mesa has built a loyal following over the past 22 years, and we intend to keep production in Albuquerque," Vance told reporters.

Blue Mesa founder Hector Delgado, who started the company in 2002 with his sister Renata Delgado, will join Ridgeline as senior vice president of Southwest operations, effective February 1, 2025. Renata Delgado will step down from her role as chief operating officer at Blue Mesa the same week.

Shares of Ridgeline Foods rose 6.8 percent to $58.10 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume topped 2.1 million shares, nearly triple the daily average. Analyst Priya Ramaswamy of Cascade Capital Partners called the price "a fair multiple" given Blue Mesa's estimated $38 million in annual revenue.

Ridgeline plans to fund the purchase through a combination of $90 million in cash reserves and a new credit facility arranged by First Continental Bank. The company expects the deal to be accretive to earnings within 18 months.

input: Fjallraven Kanken 16L Backpack, sold by Cedarwood Outdoors of Portland, Oregon, is now available for $89.99, down from $110.00 through November 30, 2024. Introduced in Sweden in 1978, the Kanken has become a wardrobe staple across Scandinavia and beyond. This listing covers the Ox Red colorway, crafted from Vinylon F fabric for water resistance and durability. The pack measures 16 liters, weighs 410 grams, and includes two front pockets, padded shoulder straps, and a reflective logo patch. Cedarwood Outdoors purchased its current inventory of 500 units directly from Fjallraven AB, headquartered in Ornskoldsvik, Sweden, in a wholesale deal finalized on September 12, 2024. The bag is brand new, unused, and ships in original packaging with tags attached. Customers who order before 2:00 PM Pacific Time on weekdays will receive same-day shipping via UPS Ground. Cedarwood Outdoors, founded in 2015 by Marcus Whitfield, has built a loyal following among Pacific Northwest hikers and students at Reed College. The company reports that Kanken backpacks account for roughly 18 percent of its total annual sales. Reviewers on the site have praised the bag's minimalist design, with one customer, Priya Nandakumar of Seattle, Washington, calling it "the perfect everyday carry for grad school." Stock is limited to 500 units, and Cedarwood Outdoors does not expect a restock before January 2025.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- Aurelia Biosciences Inc. announced on June 4, 2024 that it has acquired NovaGene Diagnostics Ltd, a Dublin-based genomics startup, for approximately 240 million dollars in a cash-and-stock transaction. The deal, finalized at Aurelia's headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts, is expected to close by August 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Aurelia CEO Dr. Marcus Reinholt said the acquisition will strengthen the company's diagnostics pipeline, particularly its work on early detection of pancreatic cancer. "NovaGene's proprietary sequencing platform, GeneTrack, complements our existing portfolio and accelerates our timeline by roughly eighteen months," Reinholt said during a press briefing in Boston on June 4.

NovaGene, founded in 2016 by geneticist Dr. Fiona Callaghan, employs 85 people across its Dublin and London offices. Callaghan will join Aurelia as Chief Scientific Officer, effective July 1, 2024, reporting directly to Reinholt. She will step down from her current role as NovaGene's Chief Executive Officer.

Under the terms of the agreement, Aurelia will pay 180 million dollars in cash and issue stock valued at 60 million dollars to NovaGene shareholders. Aurelia's board, led by Chairwoman Elena Petrov, approved the transaction unanimously on May 30, 2024.

Aurelia, listed on the Nasdaq under ticker ARLB, reported revenue of 1.2 billion dollars in fiscal year 2023, a 14 percent increase over the previous year. Shares of Aurelia rose 3 percent in after-hours trading following the announcement.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side defeated Everton 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, moving Villa into fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Jordan Pickford, and added a second just before halftime after a quick counterattack led by midfielder John McGinn. Everton's Dominic Calvert-Lewin pulled one back in the 63rd minute, heading home from a corner, but substitute Leon Bailey restored Villa's two-goal cushion in the 81st minute to seal the 3-1 win. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, saying, "We controlled the tempo for long periods and showed real maturity." Everton boss Sean Dyche admitted his team's defending was too passive in the first half. The victory lifted Aston Villa to 19 points from eight matches, three points behind leaders Manchester City. Villa's next fixture is away to Arsenal at Emirates Stadium on October 29, while Everton will host Brentford the same weekend. Attendance at Villa Park was recorded at 41,912, one of the highest gates of the season so far. Watkins, capped 12 times for the England national team, has now scored six league goals this season, putting him among the Premier League's top scorers alongside Erling Haaland.

DETROIT, Oct. 14 -- Falcon Motors Inc. announced Monday it will acquire EverCharge Systems LLC, a privately held battery-technology supplier based in Austin, Texas, for $740 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by December 2024, marks Falcon's largest acquisition since it was founded in 1998 by engineer Rosalind Chu. Under the agreement, EverCharge founder and Chief Executive Officer Marcus Petrov will join Falcon Motors as Senior Vice President of Battery Engineering, reporting directly to Falcon CEO Diane Okafor. Petrov stepped down from his role at EverCharge effective Friday to prepare for the transition. 'This combination strengthens our supply chain and accelerates our electric vehicle roadmap by at least two years,' Okafor told reporters during a press briefing at Falcon's headquarters in Detroit, Michigan. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners estimate the merged battery division could generate $1.2 billion in annual revenue by 2027. Falcon shares rose 6.3 percent to $58.42 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of rival automaker Bramwell Motors dipped slightly amid concerns over EverCharge's exclusive supply contracts. EverCharge, which employs roughly 850 workers across three facilities in Texas and Nevada, has supplied lithium-ion battery cells to Falcon since 2019. The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, with a decision expected in early 2025. Rosalind Chu, now Falcon's board chair, called the acquisition 'a defining moment for American manufacturing.'

Pixelworks Labs, a design studio in Portland, Oregon, unveiled the Streamline S7 mirrorless camera on June 4, 2024, and it has quickly become my favorite travel companion. Priced at $1,899, the S7 pairs a 33-megapixel sensor with an in-house image processor called Halo IQ, delivering noticeably cleaner low-light shots than its predecessor, the S6. I tested the camera over three weeks in Kyoto, Japan, shooting everything from narrow alleyways at dusk to the Arashiyama bamboo grove at noon. Autofocus locked on moving subjects in under 0.2 seconds, a claim Pixelworks Labs first made at a press briefing in San Jose on May 14, 2024.

CEO Marissa Tan, who founded Pixelworks Labs in 2016, told reporters the S7 represents "the biggest sensor jump we've shipped in eight years." The company, a longtime competitor of Fujifilm, sources its lens glass from Schott AG in Germany, and battery cells are supplied by Ambr Energy of Seoul, South Korea. Pixelworks Labs was acquired by Nikkei Optics Holdings for $410 million in March 2023, though it continues to operate under its original name.

My only complaints: the menu system borrows too heavily from the older S5, and the $199 leather strap feels overpriced. Still, at under two pounds with the 24mm kit lens attached, the Streamline S7 is the most compelling mirrorless option I've handled this year, and I'd recommend it without hesitation to enthusiasts upgrading from a Streamline S6.

MANCHESTER, England, 14 October 2024 - Aston Villa striker Jhon Duran scored twice on Sunday to lead his side to a 3-1 victory over Everton at Villa Park, extending Villa's unbeaten run to seven matches in the Premier League. Duran opened the scoring in the 23rd minute with a curling strike from outside the box, and doubled his tally in the 61st minute after a swift counterattack set up by midfielder Youri Tielemans. Everton pulled one back through Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 74th minute, but a late header from defender Ezri Konsa in stoppage time sealed the win for the home side. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his team's discipline after the match, saying the squad had 'grown into a unit capable of competing for a top-four finish.' The result lifted Aston Villa to third place in the table with 18 points from eight games, three points behind leaders Liverpool. Everton, managed by Sean Dyche, remain in 15th place with just nine points and have now lost four of their last five away fixtures. Villa Park, which holds 42,682 spectators, was sold out for the fixture, with several thousand fans arriving early to mark the club's 150th anniversary celebrations. Villa will next travel to face Bournemouth on 26 October, while Everton host Brighton on the same weekend.

CLEVELAND, OH -- October 14, 2024 -- Halloran Industrial Group announced today that it has acquired Bexford Sensor Technologies, a privately held manufacturer of industrial pressure sensors based in Akron, Ohio, for approximately $84 million in cash. The transaction, which closed on October 11, 2024, marks Halloran's third acquisition in two years and strengthens its position in the automation equipment market.

Under the agreement, Bexford will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Halloran and retain its 210 employees at its Akron manufacturing facility. Bexford's founder and chief executive officer, Marcus Whitfield, will join Halloran as Vice President of Sensor Technologies, reporting directly to Halloran CEO Diane Ostrowski.

"Bexford has built an exceptional reputation over the past eighteen years for precision engineering," said Ostrowski, speaking at a press briefing held at Halloran's headquarters in Cleveland. "This acquisition allows us to expand our footprint in the Midwest and compete more directly with Tolvane Corp."

Whitfield, who founded Bexford in 2006, said the deal would provide the resources needed to scale production. "We've outgrown our current capacity," he said. "Partnering with Halloran gives us access to global distribution."

Halloran Industrial Group, headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, reported revenue of $1.2 billion in fiscal year 2023 and employs roughly 4,300 people across North America. The company's stock trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker HIG.

Case No. RG23-118876. On March 14, 2024, Judge Patricia Menendez sentenced Darnell Ogundipe, 34, to 6 years in state prison after a jury in Oakland convicted him of grand theft and embezzlement from his former employer, Coastline Freight Logistics. Prosecutor Anthony Wu of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Ogundipe, who worked as a warehouse manager at Coastline Freight Logistics, diverted $412,000 in company funds between January 2021 and September 2022 by falsifying invoices tied to shipments moved by leased Freightliner Cascadia trucks.

Ogundipe was arrested on October 3, 2022, at his home in Hayward by detectives from the Alameda County Sheriff's Office after an internal audit flagged irregularities. He was charged on November 15, 2022, with one count of grand theft and two counts of embezzlement. During the trial, which began February 5, 2024, at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, defense attorney Miriam Castellanos maintained that her client had authorization from company vice president Gregory Talbot.

Judge Menendez rejected that defense, citing bank records showing transfers to an account held by Ogundipe's sister, Renata Ogundipe. Coastline Freight Logistics, headquartered in San Leandro and a subsidiary of Meridian Supply Chain Group, issued a statement thanking the Sheriff's Office and the District Attorney. Ogundipe must also pay $412,000 in restitution within five years of his release.

MERIDIAN CITY, Ohio — Kessler Industrial Group announced Tuesday that it has acquired Bramwell Fasteners LLC, a family-owned manufacturer based in Toledo, Ohio, for $84 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing at Kessler's headquarters, marks the company's third acquisition in two years and expands its footprint in the automotive supply chain.

Kessler CEO Renata Foss said the acquisition of Bramwell, which employs 310 workers and supplies steel fasteners to Ford Motor Company and General Motors, will strengthen the company's position against rival Danforth Manufacturing. "Bramwell's engineering team is among the best in the Midwest," Foss said. "This is about long-term supply reliability, not just volume."

Bramwell founder Harold Voss, 68, who started the company in 1979 with his brother Edwin Voss, will step down as president effective March 1, 2025, but will remain on the board as a senior advisor. His son, Peter Voss, currently the plant's operations manager, is expected to be named site director in the coming weeks.

The transaction, first reported by the Toledo Blade, still requires clearance from the Federal Trade Commission, though analysts do not expect regulators to object given Bramwell's relatively small market share. Shares of Kessler Industrial Group rose 4.2 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $57.30.

The deal is expected to close by April 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval.

DETROIT, Mich. — Meridian Motors Inc. announced Tuesday that it has acquired Voltec Battery Systems, a Troy, Michigan-based startup specializing in solid-state battery technology, for $410 million in cash. The deal, finalized on March 11, 2024, is expected to close by the end of April.

Meridian Motors CEO Ellen Whitaker said the acquisition would help the automaker cut electric vehicle production costs by 18 percent over the next three years. "Voltec's technology gives us a real competitive edge over Tesla and Rivian," Whitaker told reporters during a press conference at Meridian's headquarters in Dearborn.

Voltec Battery Systems was founded in 2019 by engineer Raj Patel, who previously worked at Panasonic. Patel will join Meridian as Chief Battery Officer starting April 15, 2024, according to a company statement. Voltec currently employs 260 people and operates a research facility in Troy.

The announcement sent Meridian Motors' stock up 6.2 percent on the New York Stock Exchange, closing at $87.40 per share. Analysts at Morgan Stanley called the acquisition "a bold bet on next-generation battery chemistry," noting that solid-state batteries could extend EV range by up to 40 percent compared to current lithium-ion designs.

Meridian has not disclosed whether Voltec's 260 employees will retain their positions, though Whitaker indicated most staff would transition to Meridian's payroll. The deal still requires approval from federal antitrust regulators, with a decision expected by June 2024.

Chief Executive Officer Marcus Delaney said the purchase will help Faraday Motors secure a stable supply of lithium-ion cells for its upcoming electric pickup, the Faraday Ranger, set to launch in late 2025. Lumen Cells, based in Reno, Nevada, was founded in 2016 by engineer Priya Nandakumar, who will join Faraday Motors as Senior Vice President of Battery Engineering effective November 1, 2024. Shares of Faraday Motors rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.20. Analysts at Whitcombe Research noted that the acquisition strengthens Faraday's position against competitor Sable Auto Corp, which last month unveiled its own battery plant in Georgia. Delaney, speaking at a press conference in Detroit, said, "This is a pivotal moment for Faraday Motors as we accelerate our transition to electric vehicles." Lumen Cells employs 340 people and reported revenue of $89 million last year. The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which has increased scrutiny of battery-sector consolidation in recent months.

MADRID, April 12 - Real Sociedad edged past Villarreal 2-1 at the Reale Arena on Saturday, with midfielder Mikel Oyarzabal scoring the decisive goal in the 84th minute. The victory, watched by 32,000 fans, lifted Real Sociedad to fourth place in La Liga, three points ahead of Real Betis.

Villarreal had taken an early lead through striker Gerard Moreno, who converted a penalty in the 12th minute after a foul inside the box. Real Sociedad responded before halftime when defender Robin Le Normand headed home a corner kick in the 39th minute, leveling the score at 1-1.

The match, refereed by Jesus Gil Manzano, saw two yellow cards issued, including one to Villarreal captain Dani Parejo for dissent. Real Sociedad manager Imanol Alguacil praised his team's resilience after the game, telling reporters, "We fought until the final whistle, and Mikel's goal was the reward for that effort."

The result keeps Real Sociedad in contention for a Champions League spot with six matches remaining this season. Villarreal, meanwhile, dropped to eighth place, three points behind Athletic Bilbao. Villarreal coach Marcelino Garcia Toral acknowledged the loss was costly, noting that his side must win at home against Sevilla on April 20 to stay in the European qualification race.

Real Sociedad will next travel to face Atletico Madrid at the Civitas Metropolitano on April 19, while Villarreal hosts Sevilla the following day. Both clubs are owned by ownership groups based in Spain, with Real Sociedad remaining a member-owned club, unlike privately held Villarreal.

On March 6, 2024, Judge Patricia Nakamura sentenced Marcus Ellery Boone, 41, to 54 months in state prison after a jury in Oakland found him guilty of embezzling $2.3 million from Crestline Capital Partners, a boutique investment firm headquartered in San Francisco. Prosecutor Diane Whitfield of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Boone, who served as Chief Financial Officer of Crestline Capital Partners from January 2019 until his termination in August 2022, diverted client funds into a shell company called Bramwell Holdings LLC.

During the four-day trial, which concluded on March 4, 2024, at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, defense attorney Samuel Ortiz contended that Boone had authorization from founder Harold Wexler to reallocate the funds. The jury rejected this claim and convicted Boone on charges of grand theft and securities fraud.

Boone was originally arrested on November 12, 2022, by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation at his residence in Piedmont, California, following a tip from an internal auditor. He was released on $500,000 bail pending trial.

Judge Nakamura ordered Boone to pay restitution of $2.3 million to Crestline Capital Partners and its clients, with payments beginning April 1, 2024. Whitfield stated after the hearing that the sentence "sends a clear message to financial professionals who abuse positions of trust." Boone's attorney has filed notice of intent to appeal the conviction to the California Court of Appeal.

MANCHESTER, England -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice on Saturday to lead his club to a 3-1 victory over Everton at Villa Park, moving Villa into fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 14th minute with a low finish after a through ball from midfielder John McGinn, then added his second just before halftime with a header from a corner kick. Everton pulled one back in the 63rd minute through striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin, but defender Ezri Konsa restored Villa's two-goal cushion in the 78th minute. The match, watched by 41,234 fans, was Villa's fifth win in six matches under manager Unai Emery. Emery, who took charge of Aston Villa in November 2022, praised his squad's discipline after the final whistle. "We controlled the tempo for large spells and Ollie was clinical again," Emery told reporters at a press conference inside Villa Park. Everton manager Sean Dyche said his side's second-half performance gave him hope despite the defeat. The result lifts Aston Villa to 52 points from 27 games, six points behind leaders Manchester City. Everton, meanwhile, remain in 15th place with 26 points. Villa will next travel to London on Wednesday to face Tottenham Hotspur, while Everton host Newcastle United on Saturday at Goodison Park.

Ingrid Halvorsen (born March 14, 1958, in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on cod population decline in the North Sea. She earned a doctorate in oceanography from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromso the same year as a research fellow. In 1994 Halvorsen was appointed Director of Fisheries Research at the Institute of Marine Research, a position she held for eleven years. Her 1997 study, published in the work of art titled The Silent Depths, linked overfishing to a 40 percent drop in cod stocks between 1980 and 1995. In 2003 she was awarded the Nansen Prize by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to marine ecology. Halvorsen left the Institute of Marine Research in 2005 to found the nonprofit organization Ocean Futures Norway, headquartered in Bergen, which advocates for sustainable fishing quotas across Scandinavia. She married fellow scientist Erik Solberg in 1988, and the couple had two children, Kristin and Lars. Halvorsen retired from active fieldwork in 2019 but continues to serve on the advisory board of the European Marine Board in Ostend, Belgium. She died on August 9, 2022, in Bergen following a brief illness, at the age of 64.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., June 4, 2024 - Solara Biotics Inc., a clinical-stage biotechnology company, today announced that it has acquired Vantage Pharmatech Ltd., a privately held drug-delivery firm based in Dublin, Ireland, for $340 million in cash and stock.

Under the terms of the agreement, Solara Biotics will pay $210 million in cash and issue approximately 2.1 million shares of common stock to Vantage Pharmatech's shareholders. The transaction closed on June 3, 2024, following approval from Ireland's Competition and Consumer Protection Commission.

"This acquisition strengthens our pipeline for chronic kidney disease treatments," said Dr. Elena Marsh, Chief Executive Officer of Solara Biotics, who joined the company in March 2019. "Vantage Pharmatech's nanoparticle delivery platform is exactly what we needed to advance SLR-402 into Phase 3 trials."

Vantage Pharmatech was founded in 2011 by Dr. Conor Byrne, who will remain in Dublin as Senior Vice President of Research and Development, reporting to Dr. Marsh. The company employs 85 researchers and holds 12 patents related to lipid nanoparticle formulations.

Solara Biotics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs roughly 640 people worldwide and trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker SLRA. The company's shares rose 14 percent on the announcement, closing at $38.60.

Goldman Sachs advised Solara Biotics on the deal, while Vantage Pharmatech was represented by William Fry, a Dublin-based law firm.

Solara Biotics expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive to revenue and plans to retain all Vantage Pharmatech employees. The combined company will report fourth-quarter 2024 earnings on February 11, 2025.

input: Sonos launched the Ace headphones on June 5, 2024, priced at $449 and manufactured in Vietnam. I bought a pair at the Sonos store in Boston on July 12, 2024, and have used them daily since. Sound quality is excellent, with deep bass and crisp highs that rival the Bose QuietComfort Ultra, though Sonos' longtime competitor Sony still leads in noise cancellation according to reviewers at The Verge. Patrick Spence, the Chief Executive Officer of Sonos, said in an interview in Santa Barbara that the Ace represents the company's first major push beyond speakers. Sonos, headquartered in Santa Barbara, California, was founded by John MacFarlane in 2002. Battery life is rated at 30 hours, and in my testing over two weeks I got roughly 28 hours per charge, which is impressive for a $449 product. The companion app, however, crashed twice on my iPhone 15 running iOS 17.5, requiring a restart both times. Customer support, reached by phone on July 20, 2024, resolved the issue within 15 minutes by walking me through a firmware update. At $449, the Ace is not cheap, and it faces stiff competition from Apple's AirPods Max, which Apple sells for $549. Still, for anyone already invested in the Sonos ecosystem of speakers like the Sonos Arc, the Ace is a compelling addition. I'd rate it 4 out of 5 stars and recommend it to serious audiophiles willing to pay a premium.

BOSTON, MA - September 12, 2023 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced today the results of a Phase II clinical trial evaluating tebentafusp-vaxx, an experimental immunotherapy for patients with metastatic uveal melanoma. The study, led by Dr. Anita Kowalski and published in The New England Journal of Medicine, enrolled 214 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between January 2021 and March 2023. Participants receiving the drug showed a median overall survival of 21.7 months compared to 13.2 months in the control group, a difference the authors called statistically significant. Approximately 62 percent of treated patients experienced grade 1 or 2 cytokine release syndrome, while 4 percent discontinued treatment due to adverse events. Dr. Kowalski stated, "These results represent the most meaningful advance in uveal melanoma treatment in over a decade." The trial was funded by a $47 million grant from the National Cancer Institute and co-sponsored by Immunocore Holdings plc, the British biotechnology company that manufactures tebentafusp-vaxx. Immunocore's chief executive, Bahija Jallal, said the company plans to submit an expanded application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2024, seeking approval for broader use in ocular oncology. Massachusetts General Hospital, part of Mass General Brigham, will continue follow-up monitoring of trial participants through 2026. Independent oncologist Dr. Samuel Nwosu of Johns Hopkins University, who was not involved in the study, called the findings "encouraging but requiring longer-term validation." The research was presented Monday at the European Society for Medical Oncology Congress in Madrid, Spain, drawing attention from clinicians worldwide.

CHICAGO, Nov. 14 -- Deere & Company said Tuesday it will acquire GreenField Robotics, a Kansas-based agtech startup, for $180 million in cash, expanding its push into autonomous weeding technology. The deal, announced at Deere's headquarters in Moline, Illinois, is expected to close by January 2025, pending regulatory approval.

GreenField Robotics, founded in 2019 by engineer Priya Chandran, makes small robotic units that mechanically weed cover crops between rows, reducing herbicide use for row-crop farmers. The company employs about 45 people in Great Bend, Kansas.

"This acquisition strengthens our autonomy roadmap and helps farmers cut input costs," said John May, Deere's chief executive officer, in a statement. Priya Chandran will join Deere as vice president of autonomous systems once the transaction closes, according to the company.

Deere shares rose 2.3 percent to $412.18 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement. Analysts at Morgan Stanley, including Angela Ford, raised their price target on Deere stock to $460, citing the deal's strategic fit with the company's existing See & Spray platform.

The acquisition marks Deere's third robotics purchase since 2021, following its earlier purchase of Bear Flag Robotics for $250 million. Competitor AGCO Corporation, based in Duluth, Georgia, has also been investing heavily in autonomous equipment, intensifying competition in the precision-agriculture sector.

Deere plans to integrate GreenField's technology into its 8R tractor line by the 2026 planting season, executives said Tuesday.

DETROIT, Mich. — Vantage Motors Inc. announced Tuesday that it has acquired battery startup CellCore Technologies for $412 million, a move the automaker says will accelerate production of its electric pickup truck, the Ranger EV. The deal, finalized on March 11, 2024, was confirmed by Vantage Motors CEO Diane Holbrook during a press conference at the company's Detroit headquarters. "CellCore's solid-state battery technology gives us a two-year lead over competitors," Holbrook told reporters. CellCore Technologies, founded in 2019 by engineer Marcus Feng in Palo Alto, California, employs 340 people and holds 27 patents related to lithium-ion cell design. Feng will join Vantage Motors as Chief Battery Officer starting April 1, 2024, according to a statement released by the company. Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimate the acquisition could boost Vantage Motors' stock price by 8 percent over the next quarter. Rival automaker Bolt Dynamics, headquartered in Austin, Texas, declined to comment on the deal. Vantage Motors' shares closed at $58.30 on the New York Stock Exchange Tuesday, up 3.4 percent from Monday's close of $56.38. The company plans to integrate CellCore's Palo Alto facility into its existing supply chain, retaining all current employees. Production of the updated Ranger EV, featuring the new battery packs, is expected to begin at Vantage Motors' Toledo, Ohio plant in early 2025.

Pixelforge Labs, a game studio based in Austin, Texas, released its long-awaited title Emberfall Chronicles on October 14, 2024, for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, and Windows PC. Priced at $59.99, the open-world action RPG has already sold 1.2 million copies in its first two weeks, according to a statement from CEO Marisol Vega on October 29, 2024.

I spent roughly 40 hours with Emberfall Chronicles and came away impressed by its combat system, which blends real-time swordplay with a delayed-cast magic mechanic borrowed loosely from FromSoftware's Elden Ring. The world of Thareth is genuinely striking, rendered in Unreal Engine 5.3, though the game suffered from noticeable frame drops on the base PlayStation 5 during large battle sequences until a 4GB day-one patch smoothed things out.

Pixelforge Labs, founded in 2016 by Marisol Vega and Daniel Osei, was acquired by Meridian Interactive for $340 million in March 2023, a deal that initially worried longtime fans who feared corporate meddling. Those fears proved mostly unfounded; Meridian largely left the 85-person Austin studio alone, and the result is the most ambitious project of Pixelforge's eight-year history.

My main complaints are minor: the inventory UI is clunky, and one questline in the region of Caldross failed to trigger properly, forcing a restart from an earlier save. Still, at $59.99, Emberfall Chronicles is easily one of 2024's best RPGs, and I recommend it without hesitation to fans of the genre.

Pixelworks Labs, a display-technology unit based in San Jose, California, unveiled the Aurora X7 tablet on October 14, 2024, positioning it as a rival to Apple's iPad Air. Priced at $499, the Aurora X7 features a 10.9-inch OLED panel, a MediaTek Kompanio 930 chipset, and a 9,200 mAh battery that the company claims delivers 14 hours of video playback. I tested the tablet for three weeks in Portland, Oregon, and came away impressed by its color accuracy, though the 8-megapixel rear camera feels dated for a device at this price.

During a briefing, Pixelworks Labs' Chief Product Officer, Rachel Ilinski, told me the Aurora X7 was built to compete directly with Samsung's Galaxy Tab S9 lineup. "We wanted a premium feel without the $700 markup," Ilinski said. The tablet ships with Android 14 and promises two years of software updates.

Battery life in my tests hovered around 12.5 hours of mixed use, slightly below the marketing claim but still strong. The included stylus, sold separately for $59, uses Bluetooth 5.3 and offers minimal input lag. Build quality is solid, with an aluminum unibody, though the speakers sound tinny at high volume.

Pixelworks Labs was founded in 2016 by former Sony engineer David Okafor and has since grown to 340 employees. Last month the company announced it acquired a small audio-software startup, Clarasound, for $22 million, a move meant to improve the tablet line's speaker tuning in future models.

Overall, the Aurora X7 is a strong value pick for anyone priced out of the premium tablet market, even if it doesn't quite dethrone the industry leaders.

BOSTON, September 12, 2023 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tirzepatide-based therapy for patients with moderate-to-severe non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh and published in the Journal of Hepatology, enrolled 214 participants across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2021 and July 2022. Participants received weekly subcutaneous injections of the compound MGH-2201, a glucagon-like peptide receptor agonist developed in collaboration with Cambridge-based biotech firm Solara Therapeutics. After 52 weeks, 61 percent of patients receiving the highest dose (15 milligrams) achieved resolution of steatohepatitis without worsening of fibrosis, compared to 22 percent in the placebo group. Liver enzyme levels, specifically alanine aminotransferase, dropped by an average of 38 units per liter. Dr. Marsh noted that three patients experienced serious adverse events, including one case of acute pancreatitis, prompting temporary suspension of dosing in that cohort. Solara Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by biochemist Raj Patel, plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial in early 2024 involving approximately 1,200 patients across 90 sites globally. The company received $45 million in funding from Meridian Ventures in August 2023 to support the expanded trial. Analysts at Deutsche Bank estimate that if approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, the therapy could generate $2.3 billion in annual revenue by 2028. The findings were presented at the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases meeting in San Francisco on November 10, 2023.

Elena Marceau (born March 14, 1958, in Lyon, France) is a French-Canadian biochemist known for her pioneering work on enzyme catalysis. She earned her doctorate at McGill University in 1984 and joined the University of Toronto as an assistant professor later that year. In 1991, Marceau founded Biothera Labs in Montreal, a company focused on developing industrial enzymes for pharmaceutical manufacturing. Under her leadership as Chief Executive Officer, Biothera Labs grew to employ over 300 scientists by 2005.

In 2003, Marceau was elected president of the Canadian Society of Biochemistry, a position she held until 2007. She received the Gairdner International Award in 1999 for her discovery of a novel bacterial enzyme, Lyseprotease-7, in collaboration with Dr. Henri Dubois. The award was presented in Toronto by the Gairdner Foundation.

Biothera Labs was acquired by the multinational pharmaceutical company Novaris AG for approximately $420 million in 2011, after which Marceau stepped down as CEO and became a senior advisor to Novaris AG. She retired from active research in 2015.

Marceau married fellow scientist Dr. Henri Dubois in 1986; the couple had two children. She currently resides in Montreal, Quebec, where she continues to mentor young researchers at McGill University. Her memoir, "Molecules and Memory," was published in 2020 by Éditions du Fleuve.

MADRID, October 14, 2023 - Real Sociedad edged Villarreal 2-1 at the Reale Arena on Saturday, moving up to third place in La Liga with 19 points after nine matches. Midfielder Mikel Merino scored the opener in the 23rd minute, converting a low cross from Takefusa Kubo, before Villarreal's Gerard Moreno equalized with a penalty in the 51st minute. Substitute Umar Sadiq settled the contest in the 78th minute, heading home a corner delivered by Andoni Gorosabel in front of 32,000 spectators.

Real Sociedad head coach Imanol Alguacil praised his squad's resilience after the match, telling reporters, "We suffered, but we found a way to win against a very difficult opponent." Villarreal manager Marcelino Garcia Toral, whose side dropped to eighth place, said his team lacked sharpness in the final third.

The win extended Real Sociedad's unbeaten home run to seven matches and boosted their hopes of qualifying for the UEFA Champions League next season. The club's sporting director, Roberto Olabe, confirmed that Kubo has agreed to a new contract extension through 2027, a deal reportedly worth 4 million euros annually.

Elsewhere in La Liga on Saturday, Girona thrashed Celta Vigo 4-0 at Montilivi Stadium, with striker Artem Dovbyk netting a hat-trick. Girona now sits atop the table with 22 points, two ahead of leaders Real Madrid heading into next weekend's fixtures.

Kestrel Outdoors of Bend, Oregon introduces the Talus 45 backpacking pack, now available for pre-order at $219.00 and shipping starting November 14, 2024. Designed by lead engineer Marisol Vance, the Talus 45 features a 45-liter main compartment, a torso-adjustable aluminum frame, and a waterproof 210-denier ripstop nylon shell. At just 2.3 pounds, it is among the lightest packs in its class, undercutting the competing Osprey Exos 48 by roughly 0.4 pounds while offering comparable load capacity of up to 35 pounds.

Each Talus 45 ships with a detachable hip-belt pouch, two aluminum trekking-pole loops, and a lifetime warranty covering manufacturing defects. Kestrel Outdoors, founded in 2016 by former REI buyer Daniel Ostrowski, manufactures the pack at a facility in Boise, Idaho and tests every unit on trails in the Cascade Range before release. The company sold its 500,000th pack earlier this year, a milestone celebrated with a limited-edition orange colorway sold exclusively through its website.

Customers who order before October 30, 2024 will receive a free 2-liter Kestrel hydration bladder, a $28 value. The Talus 45 is available in three sizes (Small, Medium, Large) and two colors, Slate Gray and Moss Green. Reviewers at Backpacker Magazine gave the pack 4.5 out of 5 stars, praising its durability and comfortable suspension system, though noting the hip belt padding is thinner than that of the Gregory Paragon 48.

Marguerite Élise Fontaine (born 14 March 1927 in Lyon, France; died 2 September 2011 in Geneva, Switzerland) was a French-Swiss biochemist known for her pioneering work on insulin crystallization. She earned her doctorate in chemistry from the University of Lyon in 1951 and joined the Pasteur Institute in Paris the same year as a research assistant. In 1958 Fontaine moved to Geneva to take a position as Senior Researcher at the Firmenich Laboratories, where she remained until her retirement in 1989. During her tenure, she co-founded the Geneva Institute for Molecular Biology in 1963 alongside Dr. Henri Laurent, a collaboration that produced over 40 peer-reviewed papers. In 1972 Fontaine was elected President of the Swiss Society of Biochemistry, a position she held for six years. She married physicist Bernard Roussel in 1955, and the couple had two children, Claire Roussel and Marc Roussel. In 1981 Fontaine received the Marcel Benoist Prize, Switzerland's most prestigious science award, presented to her in Bern by the Swiss Federal Council for her contributions to protein chemistry. She published her memoir, "Crystals of Memory," in 1998 through Éditions Payot. Fontaine was also a vocal advocate for women in science, founding the Geneva chapter of Women in Chemistry in 1975. She died at age 84 following a brief illness at Geneva University Hospital, survived by her husband and children. A commemorative symposium was held in her honor at the University of Geneva in 2012.

To: Marcus Feldman, VP of Operations, Brightwell Logistics
From: Elena Cho, General Counsel, Brightwell Logistics
Date: March 14, 2024
Subject: Acquisition of Harrow Freight Solutions Finalized

Marcus,

I'm pleased to confirm that Brightwell Logistics, headquartered in Portland, Oregon, completed its acquisition of Harrow Freight Solutions on March 12, 2024, for $47 million in cash. The deal closed at Harrow's headquarters in Tacoma, Washington, following six months of negotiations that began after our initial meeting with Harrow's founder, David Okonkwo, last September in Seattle.

As part of the transaction, Harrow's fleet of 32 delivery trucks and its warehouse facility on Marginal Way will transfer to Brightwell by April 1, 2024. David Okonkwo will step down as CEO of Harrow Freight Solutions effective March 31, 2024, and will join Brightwell as Senior Advisor for Integration, reporting directly to you.

We also need to notify the Washington State Department of Revenue of the ownership change within 15 days, per state law. I've asked our outside counsel, Priya Ramaswamy of Ferris & Cole LLP, to handle that filing by March 27, 2024.

Separately, please note that Brightwell's board approved a $2.3 million retention bonus pool for the 40 Harrow employees who will remain through the transition period ending June 30, 2024.

Let me know if you'd like to discuss the integration timeline before our next board meeting on March 20, 2024.

Best regards,
Elena Cho
General Counsel, Brightwell Logistics

Marguerite Okonjo-Vance (born 14 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-British materials scientist known for pioneering work on graphene-based battery membranes. She earned a degree in chemistry from the University of Ibadan in 1979 before moving to the United Kingdom to complete a PhD at Imperial College London in 1984. In 1991 she joined Cavendish Energy Systems, a battery research firm headquartered in Cambridge, as a Senior Research Fellow. She was appointed Chief Technology Officer of Cavendish Energy Systems in 1998, a position she held for eleven years. During her tenure, the company partnered with Nissan Motor Corporation to supply lithium-ion cell components, and Cavendish Energy Systems was later acquired by the German conglomerate Voltarion AG for 340 million euros in 2006. Okonjo-Vance left Cavendish Energy Systems in 2009 to found Solvex Membranes Ltd in Oxford, serving as its founding Chief Executive Officer. In 2015 she received the Royal Society's Davy Medal for her contributions to electrochemistry, presented to her in London. She married physicist Dr. Thomas Vance in 1986, and the couple has one son, Michael Vance, born in 1990 in Oxford. Okonjo-Vance holds citizenship in both Nigeria and the United Kingdom, and continues to publish on sustainable battery chemistry. She currently resides in Oxford, where Solvex Membranes Ltd remains headquartered.

Pixelworks Labs, a hardware startup based in Portland, Oregon, launched the Argon X7 mirrorless camera on June 4, 2024, promising professional photographers a lighter alternative to Canon's EOS R5. I have spent three weeks shooting with the Argon X7 around Multnomah County, and the results are mostly encouraging. The 45-megapixel sensor, built in partnership with Sony Semiconductor Solutions, delivers sharp detail even at ISO 6400, and the body weighs just 620 grams, roughly 15 percent lighter than comparable full-frame rivals. Founder Renata Sokolova, who previously worked as an engineer at Nikon, told me in an interview at the company's headquarters that the Argon X7 was designed specifically for travel photographers who dislike bulky gear. The autofocus system, powered by a custom chip called NeuroFocus, tracks moving subjects impressively well, though it occasionally hunts in low light. Battery life is rated at 480 shots per charge, which fell short in my testing, closer to 410 shots during a hike near Mount Hood. At $3,199, the Argon X7 costs $400 more than the Sony Alpha 7 IV, a tough sell given Sony's larger lens ecosystem. Pixelworks Labs says it will ship a firmware update in August 2024 to improve low-light autofocus performance. For photographers already invested in Sony or Canon lenses, switching may not be worth the premium yet, but for newcomers building a kit from scratch, the Argon X7 is a compelling, if pricey, option.

Vera Almstedt (born 4 March 1958 in Uppsala, Sweden) is a Swedish biochemist known for pioneering work on lipid signaling. She earned a doctorate in biochemistry from Uppsala University in 1985 and completed postdoctoral research at the Max Planck Institute for Biophysical Chemistry in Göttingen from 1986 to 1989. In 1990, Almstedt joined AstraZeneca as a Research Scientist, later becoming Head of Molecular Pharmacology in 1997. During her tenure she led the team that identified the enzyme phospholipase D2 as a target for inflammatory disease, a discovery published in the journal Nature Medicine in 1999. In 2004, she left AstraZeneca to found Lipidion Therapeutics, a biotechnology company headquartered in Lund, Sweden, focused on developing drugs for chronic inflammatory conditions. Under her leadership as Chief Executive Officer, Lipidion raised 45 million euros in venture funding by 2008 and advanced its lead compound, LX-204, into Phase II clinical trials for rheumatoid arthritis. In 2015, the pharmaceutical company Novartis acquired Lipidion Therapeutics for 310 million euros, and Almstedt stepped down as CEO shortly afterward. She was elected a member of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in 2011 and received the Anders Jahre Award for medical research in Oslo, Norway, in 2013. Almstedt married fellow chemist Erik Sandberg in 1988; the couple has two children. She currently serves as an adjunct professor at Karolinska Institutet in Stockholm.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT PRESS STATEMENT
Ottawa, Ontario -- September 12, 2024

The Ministry of Transport today announced a $340 million investment to upgrade rail safety infrastructure along the Halifax-to-Montreal corridor following a freight derailment near Levis, Quebec on August 29, 2024 that injured three workers. Minister Priya Nandakumar confirmed the funding will be distributed to Canadian National Railway over the next 18 months, with the first installment of $85 million disbursed by October 31, 2024.

"This corridor carries roughly 40 percent of eastern Canada's freight volume, and we cannot allow another incident like the one in Levis," said Minister Nandakumar during a press briefing at the Montreal Central Station. She was joined by Deputy Minister Alain Fortier and Canadian National Railway's Chief Safety Officer, Grace Whitfield, who outlined a plan to replace 1,200 kilometers of aging track and install 60 new sensor stations by March 2026.

The announcement follows a two-week review conducted by the Transportation Safety Board of Canada, which found that a cracked rail component caused the derailment. Opposition critic Marcus Delaney, speaking on behalf of the Conservative Party, called the funding "long overdue" and urged the Ministry to accelerate inspections at 15 additional high-risk crossings identified in the Board's report.

Minister Nandakumar is scheduled to meet with provincial transportation officials in Quebec City on September 25, 2024 to finalize implementation details.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Finally Gets Battery Life Right

Mountain View, October 12, 2024 -- After two generations of disappointing endurance, Google's Pixel Watch 3, released on September 10, 2024, finally addresses the battery complaints that plagued its predecessors. I have worn the 45mm LTE model for three weeks, and the results are genuinely impressive.

The Pixel Watch 3 ships with a 420mAh battery, up from 306mAh in the Pixel Watch 2, and Google claims up to 36 hours of use on a single charge. In my testing at home in Austin, Texas, I consistently hit 30 hours with the always-on display enabled, which is a meaningful jump from last year's model. The watch is priced at $349.99 for the 41mm Wi-Fi version, with the 45mm LTE unit I tested retailing for $499.99.

Google's hardware chief, Rick Osterloh, said at a briefing in San Francisco that the company "listened closely to feedback from Fitbit users" following Google's acquisition of Fitbit for $2.1 billion back in 2019. The new Loss of Pulse Detection feature, built with input from cardiologists at the Cleveland Clinic, is a standout addition, though it isn't yet available in the European Union pending regulatory approval.

Compared to the Apple Watch Series 10, produced by Apple Inc. and headquartered in Cupertino, the Pixel Watch 3 still trails slightly in third-party app support. But for Android users, particularly those with a Pixel 9 in their pocket, this is the most complete smartwatch Google has ever made. Recommended, with minor reservations about app selection.

The Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources of Kenya announced on 14 March 2024 that it will allocate 2.3 billion Kenyan shillings toward flood recovery efforts in Nairobi and Mombasa following heavy rains that displaced more than 45,000 residents last month. Speaking at a press conference in Nairobi, Cabinet Secretary Amina Wanjiru stated that the funds will be disbursed through the Kenya Red Cross Society and the National Drought Management Authority beginning 1 April 2024. "This disaster has tested our infrastructure, but the government of President William Ruto remains committed to rebuilding stronger," Wanjiru said. The ministry also confirmed that engineers from the state-owned Kenya Urban Roads Authority will begin repairing the Mbagathi Bridge, which collapsed on 9 March 2024, killing three people and injuring eleven others. Construction is expected to conclude by 30 June 2024, at a projected cost of 480 million shillings. Separately, the World Bank pledged an additional 15 million dollars in emergency assistance, to be transferred to the National Treasury by 20 March 2024. Opposition leader Raila Odinga welcomed the aid package but criticized the government's earlier response time during a rally held in Kisumu on 16 March 2024. The Ministry noted that a full audit of drainage systems in Nairobi County will be completed by the newly formed Flood Resilience Task Force before the next rainy season begins in October.

input: CHICAGO, June 12 — Deere & Company said Wednesday it has agreed to acquire GrainTrack Analytics Inc., a Minneapolis-based agricultural software startup, for $410 million in cash, as the farm equipment maker pushes deeper into precision agriculture technology. The deal, announced by Deere Chief Executive John May, is expected to close in the third quarter of 2024, pending regulatory approval. GrainTrack Analytics, founded in 2016 by former agronomist Sarah Kessler, employs 140 people and produces software that helps farmers track soil health and crop yields using satellite imagery. Kessler will join Deere as Vice President of Digital Agriculture once the transaction closes, according to a statement released in Moline, Illinois, where Deere is headquartered. Shares of Deere rose 2.3 percent to $392.18 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of rival Caterpillar Inc. slipped slightly amid investor speculation about competitive pressure in the agricultural technology sector. Analyst Mark Feldman of Baird & Co. called the acquisition "a smart bolt-on that strengthens Deere's data ecosystem." This marks Deere's third acquisition in the software space since 2021, following its purchase of Bear Flag Robotics for $250 million. The GrainTrack deal comes as commodity prices remain volatile, with corn futures down 8 percent this year, prompting equipment makers to seek new revenue streams beyond hardware sales. Deere's board approved the transaction on Monday, and the company expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive to earnings by fiscal 2025.

BOSTON, MA -- November 4, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced the results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating durvamicin, an experimental chemical compound targeting treatment-resistant tuberculosis. The 14-month study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez, enrolled 236 adult patients across sites in Boston, Nairobi, and Manila. According to the report, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases, 68 percent of participants receiving durvamicin achieved culture conversion by week 12, compared with 41 percent in the control arm receiving standard rifampicin therapy. Dr. Vasquez, an infectious disease specialist affiliated with Harvard Medical School, presented the findings on November 3, 2023, at a Contact.Communicate-style briefing for journalists in Cambridge. "These results suggest durvamicin could become a critical tool against drug-resistant tuberculosis strains within five years," she said. The trial was funded by a $12 million grant from the Gates Foundation and co-sponsored by Novara Biotech, a Cambridge-based pharmaceutical company that first synthesized durvamicin in 2019. Novara Biotech's chief executive, Mr. Thomas Reyes, stated the company plans to file for regulatory approval with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. Three patients in the trial developed severe liver toxicity and were hospitalized in Nairobi, though all recovered after discontinuation of the drug. Independent reviewers from the World Health Organization, including Dr. Amara Okafor, called the results "promising but preliminary," noting that larger Phase 3 trials involving an estimated 1,500 patients will be required before durvamicin can be considered for widespread clinical use.

BOSTON, MA - March 14, 2024 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tenaplavir, an experimental antiviral chemical compound developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arborvax Therapeutics, for treatment of chronic hepatitis D infection. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti, enrolled 214 adult patients across eight sites in the United States and Germany between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants receiving 400 milligrams of tenaplavir daily for 24 weeks showed a 62 percent reduction in viral load compared to 18 percent in the placebo group, according to findings published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. Dr. Marchetti stated that three patients experienced serious adverse events, including one case of acute liver injury, though no deaths were reported during the trial period. Arborvax Therapeutics, founded in 2018 by former Pfizer executive Raymond Ochoa, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. The company raised $85 million in Series C funding last month, led by venture firm Kestrel Capital Partners, to support a planned Phase 3 trial expected to begin at facilities in Toronto and Berlin in July 2024. Hepatitis D affects an estimated 12 million people worldwide and currently has limited treatment options. Dr. Marchetti will present the full dataset at the European Association for the Study of the Liver conference in Vienna on April 10, 2024.

event: European Association for the Study of the Liver conference

AUSTIN, Texas -- Meridian Robotics Inc., a manufacturer of industrial automation systems, announced on June 4, 2024 that it has acquired Fenwick Sensor Technologies, a privately held sensor startup based in Boulder, Colorado, for 42 million dollars. The acquisition, completed on June 3, 2024, will bring Fenwick's 65 employees under the Meridian Robotics brand and expand the company's product line beyond its flagship RoboArm X200 industrial arm.

Meridian Robotics CEO Diane Sorensen said the deal strengthens the company's position against competitor Halden Automation, which is headquartered in Munich, Germany. "Fenwick's proximity sensors are the missing piece in our RoboArm X200 platform," Sorensen said during a press briefing in Austin on June 4, 2024.

As part of the transaction, Fenwick founder Marcus Whitfield will join Meridian Robotics as Vice President of Sensor Engineering, a newly created position, effective July 1, 2024. Whitfield founded Fenwick Sensor Technologies in 2016 and grew it into a supplier for three Fortune 500 manufacturers before the acquisition.

Meridian Robotics, which is publicly traded and headquartered in Austin, Texas, reported 310 million dollars in revenue last year. Shares of Meridian Robotics rose 4 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement. The company expects the Fenwick integration to be complete by the fourth quarter of 2024, and plans to unveil an upgraded RoboArm X300 model incorporating Fenwick's sensor technology at the National Robotics Expo in Chicago in October 2024.

DETROIT, Mich. — Faircrest Motors Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $2.3 billion in outstanding debt after a sharp decline in electric vehicle sales. The filing, submitted to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Detroit, marks the largest auto industry collapse since 2009.

CEO Daniel Whitfield told reporters the company would continue operating its Warren, Michigan assembly plant while it restructures. "We intend to emerge from this process as a leaner, more competitive company," Whitfield said during a press briefing at Faircrest's headquarters on Woodward Avenue.

The bankruptcy comes just eight months after Faircrest acquired battery maker Ionix Power Systems for $410 million, a deal that analysts now say strained the automaker's cash reserves. Ionix, based in Austin, Texas, will reportedly be sold off as part of the restructuring plan, according to court filings reviewed Wednesday.

Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimate roughly 4,800 jobs could be affected nationwide, including 1,200 positions at the Warren plant alone. United Auto Workers Local 412 president Renee Castillo said the union would fight to protect member benefits and pensions.

Faircrest's stock, which traded above $38 a share in early 2022, closed at $0.62 on the New York Stock Exchange Tuesday. Founded in 1987 by industrialist Harold Faircrest, the company had been a fixture of Michigan manufacturing for nearly four decades.

A bankruptcy hearing is scheduled for March 14 before Judge Elaine Prescott.

DETROIT, Mich. — Meridian Motors Inc. announced Tuesday it will acquire Larkspur Battery Systems, a Toledo-based manufacturer of lithium-ion battery packs, for $740 million in cash and stock. The deal, disclosed at a press conference at Meridian's Detroit headquarters, is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission.

Meridian CEO Rachel Ostrander said the acquisition would allow the automaker to bring battery production in-house as it races to compete with Nova Electric Corp. and Halden Vehicles. "This is about controlling our supply chain," Ostrander told reporters. "Larkspur's technology cuts charging time by 30 percent."

Larkspur Battery Systems was founded in 2016 by engineer Devon Prescott, who will join Meridian as Vice President of Battery Engineering once the deal closes. Prescott previously worked at Halden Vehicles for six years before starting Larkspur in Toledo, Ohio.

Shares of Meridian Motors rose 8 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $54.20. Analysts at Brightline Capital noted the deal marks the largest battery-sector acquisition in the Midwest since 2021.

The combined company will employ roughly 3,200 workers across Ohio and Michigan. Meridian said no layoffs are planned. Larkspur's 210,000-square-foot plant in Toledo will continue operating under its current name for at least two years, according to the agreement filed with regulators late Tuesday.

Fjallraven Kajka 65 Trekking Backpack — Refurbished, Sold by Backcountry Gear Exchange (Denver, CO)

Backcountry Gear Exchange is offering a refurbished Fjallraven Kajka 65 trekking backpack for $189.00, marked down from the original retail price of $340.00. This unit was originally purchased on March 14, 2022 from an REI store in Boulder, Colorado and was returned to Fjallraven's service center in Ulricehamn, Sweden for a full inspection after a zipper failure was reported. Technicians replaced the main compartment zipper, cleaned the aluminum frame, and re-waterproofed the G-1000 fabric using Fjallraven's proprietary Greenland Wax. The backpack has a 65-liter capacity, weighs 2.7 kilograms, and includes an adjustable torso length ranging from 45 to 52 centimeters, making it suitable for multi-day expeditions such as the Kungsleden trail in Swedish Lapland.

Backcountry Gear Exchange, founded in 2015 by former mountain guide Elena Whitfield, has processed over 4,000 refurbished outdoor items since opening its Denver warehouse. The company is not affiliated with Fjallraven AB but is an authorized reseller. Each unit ships within 3 business days via UPS Ground and includes a 90-day limited warranty. Customer service representative Marcus Boyle noted that fewer than 2 percent of refurbished Kajka packs are returned a second time, calling the model "remarkably durable for backcountry use." Orders placed before 2:00 PM Mountain Time on weekdays ship the same day from the Denver facility.

DETROIT, Mich. — Auto parts maker Corvane Industries filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $410 million in outstanding debt and slumping orders from major automakers. The filing was submitted in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan.

Corvane, headquartered in Detroit since its founding in 1987 by engineer Harold Beswick, employs roughly 3,200 workers across four plants in Michigan and Ohio. CEO Denise Patrone told reporters at a press conference that the company plans to continue operations during restructuring and expects to emerge from bankruptcy by March 2025.

"We are not walking away from our workforce," Patrone said. "This filing gives us the breathing room to renegotiate supplier contracts and restructure roughly $150 million in bond obligations."

Corvane supplies braking systems to Ford Motor Company and General Motors, both of which issued statements saying they do not expect immediate disruption to production lines. Analysts at Baird Capital noted that Corvane's troubles stem partly from a costly 2021 acquisition of Ohio-based Lindmark Brake Technologies, which added $90 million in debt without generating expected revenue growth.

The United Auto Workers union, which represents about 2,400 Corvane employees, said it would meet with management in Toledo on Thursday to discuss protections for pensions and healthcare benefits. Local union president Marcus Ivey said workers "deserve certainty, not just promises."

Shares of Corvane, which trades over the counter, fell 62 percent in early trading following the announcement.

input: The Ministry of Transport of Ontario announced on May 14, 2024 that it will invest 220 million dollars to upgrade Highway 407 between Mississauga and Oshawa. Minister Priya Nathwani confirmed the funding during a press conference held at Queen's Park in Toronto, stating that construction will begin in September 2024 and is expected to create 1,800 jobs. The project, known as the Highway 407 Corridor Expansion, will be carried out by contractor Aecon Group Inc., headquartered in Toronto, which was awarded the contract following a competitive bidding process against rival firm SNC-Lavalin. According to Minister Nathwani, the expansion will add two additional lanes across a 35-kilometre stretch and is projected to reduce commute times by 20 percent by 2027. The Ontario government previously faced criticism after the 2019 tolling policy led to public demonstrations outside Queen's Park organized by the Ontario Motorists Coalition. Deputy Minister Faisal Rahman, who joined the ministry in March 2023, said the new investment reflects lessons learned from that dispute. The province will also allocate 15 million dollars to environmental mitigation measures along the Highway 407 corridor, in partnership with the Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks. Premier Doug Ford is expected to visit the construction site in October 2024 to mark the official groundbreaking.

input: The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday that the City of Rotterdam will receive 42 million euros to upgrade flood barriers along the Nieuwe Maas after last month's severe storm damaged three pumping stations. Minister Els Vermeulen confirmed the funding during a press briefing at The Hague, stating that construction firm Van Oord will begin reinforcement work on 14 April 2024 and complete the project by December 2025. The initiative follows a joint inspection by the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management and engineers from Deltares, which found that the pumping station near Feijenoord had failed during the storm surge on 3 March 2024, flooding roughly 1,200 homes. Vermeulen, who took over as Minister of Transport in January 2023, said the government will also allocate an additional 8 million euros to the Rotterdam Port Authority for emergency dredging equipment. Rijkswaterstaat, the executive agency overseeing water management, will supervise the contract and report progress to Parliament every quarter. Opposition lawmaker Bram de Groot welcomed the announcement but questioned why similar funding had not been approved after a comparable flood in 2021. The Ministry noted that a further review, led by Professor Hanneke Bos of Delft University of Technology, will assess long-term risks posed by rising sea levels along the Dutch coast by mid-2026.
