input: MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City edged Liverpool 2-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, with a stoppage-time header from defender Ruben Dias sealing a dramatic Premier League victory in front of 53,412 fans. The result lifted City to second place in the table, three points behind leaders Arsenal, while Liverpool slipped to fifth after their first away defeat of the season. Erling Haaland opened the scoring in the 23rd minute, tapping in from close range after a low cross from Kevin De Bruyne. Mohamed Salah equalized for Liverpool in the 61st minute with a curling effort from the edge of the box, silencing the home crowd briefly before Dias struck in the 91st minute off a corner kick taken by Bernardo Silva. Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola praised his side's resilience after the match, telling reporters, "We suffered, but this team never stops believing." Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp said his players deserved more from the contest, citing a missed penalty by Darwin Nunez in the 78th minute as the turning point. The win extended Manchester City's unbeaten home run to 19 matches. City will next travel to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on October 21, while Liverpool return to Anfield to host Everton on the same date. The Football Association confirmed no disciplinary action would follow a minor confrontation between Rodri and Nunez after the final whistle.

DENVER, Colorado -- Sept. 12, 2024 -- Aurora Solar Technologies Inc. announced Thursday that it has acquired Boulder-based battery startup VoltCore Systems for $340 million in a cash-and-stock deal, marking the largest transaction in the solar equipment maker's 15-year history. Under the terms of the agreement, Aurora Solar will pay $220 million in cash and issue $120 million worth of shares to VoltCore's shareholders. The deal is expected to close by Nov. 30, 2024, pending regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Aurora Solar's chief executive officer, Marcus Whitfield, said the acquisition would allow the company to integrate VoltCore's proprietary lithium-ion storage technology into its residential solar panel lineup. "This is a transformative step for our company and for the renewable energy sector," Whitfield said during a press conference at Aurora Solar's headquarters in Denver. VoltCore Systems, founded in 2016 by engineer Priya Nandakumar, employs roughly 480 people and generated $95 million in revenue last year. Nandakumar will join Aurora Solar's executive team as Chief Technology Officer starting Oct. 1, 2024. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners called the deal a strong strategic fit, noting that Aurora Solar's stock rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement. Aurora Solar shares closed at $58.42, up from $54.97 the previous day. The company, which competes directly with SunPeak Energy Corp., expects the acquisition to boost annual revenue by 12 percent by 2026.

Fjallrunner Gear, headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, has launched the Talus 42 backpack, a rugged alpine touring pack built for multi-day backcountry trips. Priced at $289.00 and available in three colorways, the Talus 42 is now shipping to customers across the United States and Canada as of March 18, 2024. Constructed from 210-denier recycled ripstop nylon, the pack weighs just 1.9 kilograms and includes a detachable avalanche safety pocket, a padded hip belt rated for loads up to 25 kilograms, and a hydration sleeve compatible with a 3-liter reservoir. Fjallrunner Gear was founded in 2016 by former ski patroller Nadia Kessler, who still serves as the company's Chief Design Officer. The Talus 42 was engineered in partnership with Ostberg Materials Lab, a Norwegian textile research firm based in Trondheim, which supplied the ripstop fabric under a multi-year agreement. Early reviewers at Backcountry Journal praised the pack's ventilation system but noted the $289.00 price tag places it above competitors like Osprey and Gregory. Each Talus 42 comes with a limited lifetime warranty and a 60-day return window through Fjallrunner Gear's website or its flagship store in Bozeman. The company reports it sold out its first production run of 4,000 units within eleven days of the November 2023 pre-order launch, prompting a second manufacturing batch at a facility in Ho Chi Minh City. Customers who purchase before April 1, 2024 will receive a free rain cover valued at $18.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT PRESS STATEMENT
Nairobi, 14 March 2024

The Ministry of Transport today announced that Kenya Railways Corporation will begin construction of the Naivasha Inland Container Depot expansion on 1 April 2024, following approval of a KSh 4.2 billion budget allocation by the National Treasury. Transport Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen confirmed the funding during a briefing at Railway Headquarters in Nairobi, stating that the project will create approximately 1,200 jobs over an 18-month period.

The expansion, contracted to China Road and Bridge Corporation, will increase container handling capacity by 60 percent and is expected to reduce freight transit time between Mombasa and Naivasha by three days. Secretary Murkomen noted that the agreement was signed on 11 March 2024 by Kenya Railways Managing Director Philip Mainga and CRBC regional director Li Wenhua.

"This investment reflects our commitment to positioning Kenya as East Africa's premier logistics hub," Murkomen said. He added that the Ministry will conduct a public forum in Naivasha on 22 March 2024 to address concerns raised by local farmers regarding land compensation.

The Kenya National Farmers Federation had earlier organized a demonstration outside Railway Headquarters on 5 March 2024, with roughly 300 participants demanding clearer compensation timelines before construction begins. The Ministry has pledged to disburse KSh 500 million in compensation payments by 30 April 2024.

For further information, contact the Ministry of Transport communications office in Nairobi.

Boston, MA - November 4, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital reported positive results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tirzomab, an investigational monoclonal antibody developed by Cascadia Therapeutics, for the treatment of moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis. The 24-week, double-blind study enrolled 312 adult patients across 18 sites in the United States and Canada, including facilities in Toronto and Chicago. Dr. Elena Marchetti, the trial's lead investigator, presented the findings at the American College of Rheumatology annual meeting held in San Diego. Patients receiving 150 milligrams of tirzomab every four weeks showed a 62 percent reduction in disease activity scores compared to 24 percent in the placebo group, a difference that was statistically significant (p<0.001). Approximately 8 percent of participants receiving tirzomab experienced mild injection-site reactions, while no serious adverse events were reported. Cascadia Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial in early 2024 and has already secured $45 million in additional funding from venture firm Northbridge Capital to support the program. The company's chief executive officer, Raj Patel, stated that the drug could reach the market by 2026 if regulatory approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration is granted. Rheumatoid arthritis affects an estimated 1.3 million adults in the United States, and current biologic therapies, including adalimumab, do not achieve adequate response in nearly 40 percent of patients. The study was published on November 3, 2023, in the New England Journal of Medicine and funded in part by a grant from the National Institutes of Health.

input: Novara Pharma Inc. agreed to acquire Beacon Biotherapeutics Corp. for $2.4 billion in cash, the two companies announced Tuesday in Boston, Massachusetts. Under the deal, Novara Pharma will pay $58 per share, a 32 percent premium over Beacon Biotherapeutics' closing price last Friday. The acquisition, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2024 pending regulatory approval, will give Novara Pharma control of Beacon Biotherapeutics' experimental drug for pancreatic cancer, tentatively named BX-410. Novara Pharma CEO Helena Ruiz said the deal strengthens the company's oncology pipeline. "Beacon Biotherapeutics has built something remarkable, and we intend to accelerate BX-410 through clinical trials," Ruiz said during a press conference at the Boston Harbor Hotel. Beacon Biotherapeutics founder and chairman Dr. Owen Mercer, who started the company in 2015, will join Novara Pharma's board of directors as part of the agreement. Mercer is expected to step down as Beacon Biotherapeutics chairman once the transaction closes. Shares of Beacon Biotherapeutics jumped 28 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Novara Pharma shares dipped 3 percent. Analysts at Fairview Capital Partners called the price a fair valuation given BX-410's promising Phase 2 results. The deal marks Novara Pharma's third acquisition in five years, following its 2021 purchase of Delran Genomics for $900 million. Regulators at the Federal Trade Commission are expected to review the merger for antitrust concerns before final approval.

AUSTIN, Texas — October 14, 2024 — Helios Grid Systems Inc., a renewable energy technology firm headquartered in Austin, Texas, announced today that it has acquired Meridian Battery Works LLC, a Denver-based manufacturer of lithium-ion storage units, for 210 million dollars in cash and stock.

input: BOSTON, MA — March 4, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolvarocin, an experimental oral chemical compound targeting drug-resistant tuberculosis, in a study published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. The trial, led by Dr. Helena Marsh, an infectious disease specialist, enrolled 214 adult patients across sites in Nairobi, Kenya and Manila, Philippines between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants received either 400 milligrams of tolvarocin daily or a placebo for 16 weeks. According to the findings, 78 percent of patients in the tolvarocin arm achieved sputum culture conversion by week 12, compared to 41 percent in the placebo group. Dr. Marsh stated that the drug was generally well tolerated, with only 6 percent of participants discontinuing treatment due to adverse events, primarily mild gastrointestinal symptoms. The research was funded by a $12 million grant from the Gates Foundation and conducted in partnership with the Kenya Medical Research Institute. Novaris Therapeutics, the Cambridge-based biotechnology company that developed tolvarocin, plans to seek approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in early 2025. Dr. Marsh will present the full dataset at the International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease conference in Paris on November 18, 2024. Company spokesperson Daniel Reyes said Novaris has already begun manufacturing scale-up at its facility in Hyderabad, India in anticipation of regulatory approval. Public health officials, including WHO tuberculosis program director Dr. Amara Chukwu, called the results "a meaningful step forward" for a disease that killed an estimated 1.3 million people worldwide in 2022.

The transaction is expected to close by December 1, 2025, pending regulatory clearance.

Solera founder Declan Meagher, who launched the company in Dublin in 2016, will join Vantix as Senior Vice President of Diagnostics Engineering, reporting directly to Holloway. Meagher stepped down as Solera's chief executive officer effective October 13, 2025, ahead of the deal's announcement.

Vantix, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs approximately 1,400 people worldwide and reported $640 million in revenue last fiscal year. input: MANCHESTER, England — October 14, 2023 — Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as Villa defeated Fulham 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, extending manager Unai Emery's unbeaten home run in the Premier League to nine matches. Watkins opened the scoring in the 12th minute, converting a low cross from midfielder John McGinn, before Fulham's Raul Jimenez equalized just before halftime with a header from a corner kick. Villa regained control early in the second half when Watkins struck again in the 58th minute, and substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win with a curling effort in the 84th minute in front of 41,782 spectators. Emery, speaking after the match, praised the squad's resilience, saying the team had 'grown enormously' since he joined the club in November 2022. Fulham manager Marco Silva called the defeat 'frustrating' and confirmed that defender Tosin Adarabioyo will undergo a scan on Monday after limping off in the 70th minute with an apparent hamstring injury. The result lifts Aston Villa to third place in the Premier League table with 21 points from nine games, three points behind leaders Manchester City. Villa's next fixture is away to Arsenal at Emirates Stadium on October 21, while Fulham will host Chelsea at Craven Cottage the same weekend. Villa's chief executive Christian Purslow said the club remains focused on qualifying for the UEFA Champions League this season.

Denbury Outdoor Gear, headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, has released the TrailForge 45L backpack, priced at $189.99 and available starting November 3, 2023. Designed by lead engineer Marcus Whitfield, the TrailForge 45L features a ripstop nylon shell, an aluminum internal frame, and a hydration bladder compartment that holds up to 3 liters. The pack weighs just 2.1 kilograms and comes in three colorways: Slate Gray, Alpine Green, and Rust Orange. Denbury Outdoor Gear was founded in 2011 by former REI buyer Colleen Marsh, and the company now competes directly with Osprey Packs and Gregory Mountain Products in the technical backpacking segment. Each TrailForge 45L undergoes a 72-hour field test at the company's testing facility near Bridger Bowl before shipping. The product ships new, unused, and includes a lifetime warranty covering manufacturing defects. Customers who purchased the pack during the launch week reported high satisfaction, with early reviewer Priya Nandakumar calling it "the most comfortable 45-liter pack I've carried on the Pacific Crest Trail." Denbury Outdoor Gear plans to donate 5 percent of November sales to the Montana Wilderness Association. The TrailForge 45L is available exclusively through Denbury's website and select retailers including Sunlight Sports in Cody, Wyoming. A men's and women's fit are both offered, and the company recommends the pack for multi-day trips of 3 to 7 days.

2/ Solterra CEO Priya Nandakumar said the acquisition will let the company build its own actuators in-house instead of relying on supplier Denko Motion Corp. Shares of Solterra rose 6% on the Nasdaq after the announcement.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City clinched a 3-1 victory over Aston Villa at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, extending their unbeaten Premier League run to eleven matches. Erling Haaland opened the scoring in the 23rd minute with a close-range finish, his twelfth goal of the season, before Kevin De Bruyne doubled the lead just before halftime with a curling strike from outside the box. Aston Villa pulled one back through Ollie Watkins in the 61st minute, but Phil Foden restored City's two-goal cushion with a composed finish in the 78th minute. Manager Pep Guardiola praised his squad's resilience after the match, telling reporters, "We controlled the tempo even when they scored, and that shows our maturity." Aston Villa boss Unai Emery acknowledged the gap in quality, saying his side would regroup before hosting Brighton on October 21. The win kept City atop the Premier League table with 24 points, two clear of Arsenal, who defeated Everton 2-0 earlier in the day at Goodison Park. Approximately 53,000 fans attended the match at the Etihad Stadium, with City captain Kyle Walker returning from a hamstring injury sustained last month. City's next fixture is a Champions League clash against RB Leipzig on October 18, while Aston Villa will look to bounce back domestically. The victory marked Guardiola's 250th win as Manchester City manager, a milestone celebrated by fans inside the stadium.

The Ontario Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks announced on April 9, 2024 that it will invest 42 million dollars to upgrade wastewater treatment facilities in Sudbury following elevated phosphorus levels detected in Lake Wanapitei. Minister Andrea Khanjin stated at a press briefing in Toronto that the funding, administered through the Ontario Clean Water Agency, will support a 14-month retrofit of the Sudbury Water Pollution Control Plant beginning May 15, 2024. The project follows a March 2024 inspection by the Ministry that found ammonia discharge levels exceeding provincial limits by 18 percent. Greater Sudbury Mayor Paul Lefebvre welcomed the announcement, noting that the city had petitioned the province for support since 2021. Under the plan, the Ontario Clean Water Agency will oversee construction contracts, while engineering firm Stantec Consulting will provide technical design services. The Ministry expects the upgrades to reduce phosphorus runoff into Lake Wanapitei by 60 percent by 2026. Officials also confirmed that a public consultation session will be held in Sudbury on April 25, 2024, allowing residents to raise concerns about the Sudbury Water Pollution Control Plant expansion. The Ontario government said the initiative forms part of the broader Clean Water Act compliance strategy, which mandates municipalities to report contamination incidents within 48 hours. Minister Khanjin added that similar upgrades are planned for facilities in Thunder Bay and Sault Ste. Marie pending budget approval in the fall legislative session.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., March 4, 2024 -- Solara Biotech Inc., a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, today announced that it has acquired NovaGene Therapeutics for $340 million in cash and stock, expanding its pipeline of gene-editing treatments for sickle cell disease.

Under the terms of the agreement, Solara Biotech will pay $210 million in cash and issue approximately 3.2 million shares of common stock to NovaGene Therapeutics shareholders. The deal, announced Monday, is expected to close by May 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

"This acquisition strengthens our position in genetic medicine," said Dr. Elena Marsh, Chief Executive Officer of Solara Biotech, in a statement from the company's headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts. "NovaGene's CRISPR-based platform complements our existing programs targeting rare blood disorders."

NovaGene Therapeutics, founded in 2018 by Dr. Rajiv Patel in Boston, Massachusetts, employs 95 people and has developed a lead therapy currently in Phase 2 trials. Dr. Patel will join Solara Biotech as Chief Scientific Officer effective April 1, 2024, according to the release.

Solara Biotech's shares rose 6.3 percent following the announcement on the Nasdaq exchange. The company, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, employs approximately 1,200 people worldwide and reported revenue of $780 million in 2023.

The transaction was advised by Morgan Stanley on behalf of Solara Biotech, and by Goldman Sachs on behalf of NovaGene Therapeutics. Both companies expect the combined entity to accelerate development of treatments for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia.

Ingrid Halvorsen (born 14 March 1958 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on North Atlantic cod populations. She earned her doctorate from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Nordnes as a research scientist that same year. In 1998, Halvorsen was appointed Director of Fisheries Science at the institute, a position she held for eleven years. Her 2003 study on cod migration patterns, published in the work of art "Currents of the North", influenced fishing quotas set by the Norwegian Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries. In 2011, Halvorsen left the Institute of Marine Research to become a professor at the University of Tromso, where she leads a laboratory studying ocean acidification. She married fellow biologist Johan Kristiansen in 1990, and the couple has two children. In 2015, Halvorsen received the Nansen Award from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to fisheries research. She has also served as a scientific advisor to the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea, headquartered in Copenhagen, since 2012. Colleagues describe her as meticulous and deeply committed to sustainable fishing practices. Halvorsen currently lives in Tromso with her husband and continues to publish on the effects of warming seas on fish stocks, warning in a 2022 interview that cod populations could decline by 40 percent within three decades if current trends continue.

input: DETROIT, Mich. — Sept. 12, 2024 — Ridgeline Motors Inc. announced Thursday it will acquire electric-drivetrain supplier VoltCore Systems LLC for $410 million in cash, a move the automaker says will accelerate production of its upcoming Aurora EV sedan. The deal, expected to close by Nov. 30, 2024, was disclosed in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission and confirmed by Ridgeline chief executive officer Marcus Feldman during a press briefing in downtown Detroit. "VoltCore's battery-management technology fills a critical gap in our supply chain," Feldman told reporters. VoltCore, founded in 2016 by engineer Priya Anand in Austin, Texas, currently supplies components to three other automakers, including Ridgeline's rival, Halden Auto Group. Anand will join Ridgeline as chief technology officer once the transaction closes, according to the companies. Ridgeline shares rose 6.2 percent to $58.40 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume topped 4.3 million shares, roughly triple the daily average. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners raised their price target on Ridgeline to $70, citing the deal's potential to cut battery costs by 18 percent within two years. VoltCore employs about 640 workers across facilities in Austin and Reno, Nevada, all of whom are expected to remain with the company. Ridgeline, headquartered in Detroit since its founding in 1998 by industrialist Walter Greene, has faced pressure from investors to expand its EV lineup after losing market share to competitors including Halden Auto Group and Sunspire Motors over the past three years.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solstice Robotics announced this morning it has acquired Marlow Dynamics, a 40-person warehouse-automation startup based in Denver, for $58 million in cash and stock. Deal closes March 15, 2024.

2/ Solstice CEO Priya Nandakumar said the acquisition gives the company access to Marlow's pick-and-place arms, used by clients like Fenwick Logistics. "This is about speed," she told me at their office on Congress Avenue yesterday.

3/ Marlow founder Tomas Reyes, who started the company in 2019 with his sister Elena Reyes, will join Solstice as VP of Hardware Engineering effective April 1. Elena is staying on as an advisor.

4/ Solstice itself was founded in 2015 by Priya Nandakumar and Hank Ostrowski in a garage in Round Rock, Texas. It now employs 620 people and is headquartered in Austin.

6/ Meanwhile, roughly 200 gig workers gathered outside GreenAxle's Chicago facility on Tuesday to demand better pay, unrelated to the Solstice deal but adding to a rough week for the sector.

7/ Nandakumar will present the integration roadmap at the RoboCon 2024 conference in Las Vegas on May 9. Investors seem cautiously optimistic; Solstice stock rose 3 percent in early trading.

BOSTON, MA - September 14, 2023 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tremelanib, an experimental chemical compound targeting non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), in a study of 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Germany. Dr. Elena Vasquez, the trial's principal investigator, presented findings at the American Society of Clinical Oncology conference in Chicago on September 12, 2023. Patients receiving tremelanib in combination with pembrolizumab showed a median progression-free survival of 11.3 months, compared to 6.8 months in the control group receiving standard chemotherapy alone, representing a 41 percent reduction in disease progression risk. The trial, sponsored by Novara Therapeutics, a biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, enrolled patients between March 2021 and January 2023. Dr. Vasquez noted that 18 percent of patients experienced grade 3 adverse events, primarily neutropenia, though no treatment-related deaths were reported. Novara Therapeutics' chief executive officer, Marcus Feldman, stated the company plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the second quarter of 2024. The study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine on September 13, 2023, and was funded by a $42 million grant from the National Cancer Institute. Novara Therapeutics shares rose 9 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement. Dr. Vasquez, who joined Massachusetts General Hospital in 2015 after completing her fellowship at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, said larger Phase 3 trials are expected to begin in early 2024 across sites in France, Japan, and Canada.

input: The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday, June 11, 2024, that it will allocate 450 million euros to upgrade rail infrastructure along the Rotterdam-Antwerp corridor. Minister Elke Vandenberg confirmed the funding during a press briefing in The Hague, stating that the project aims to reduce freight congestion by 30 percent by 2028. The initiative, formally named the North Sea Rail Renewal Program, will be jointly overseen by NS Groep and Infrabel, with construction managed by contractor Volkerwessels. Vandenberg noted that the first phase will begin in September 2024 near the port city of Rotterdam, involving the replacement of 60 kilometers of aging track. Local officials, including Rotterdam Mayor Ahmed Aboutaleb, welcomed the announcement, saying it would create approximately 1,200 jobs over the next three years. The Ministry also disclosed that a parallel agreement was signed last week between NS Groep and Siemens Mobility for the supply of 40 new electric freight locomotives, valued at 210 million euros. Opposition lawmaker Peter de Groot criticized the timeline as overly optimistic, citing prior delays in the Betuweroute expansion completed in 2007. The Ministry of Transport is headquartered in The Hague and reports directly to the Dutch parliament. A follow-up review of the program's progress is scheduled for March 2025 in Brussels, where representatives from Infrabel and the Belgian federal government will attend.

Pixelbook Labs, a hardware startup based in Austin, Texas, launched its second-generation e-reader, the InkSlate 3, on March 4, 2024. Priced at $229, the device weighs 152 grams and uses a 7-inch E Ink Carta 1300 display. I have spent three weeks testing a review unit supplied by the company, and the improvements over the original InkSlate are substantial.

Founded in 2021 by former Amazon engineer Priya Raman, Pixelbook Labs has stayed lean, employing just 34 people as of January 2024. Raman, who now serves as the company's Chief Executive Officer, told reporters at a press briefing in Austin on March 5 that the InkSlate 3 was built to compete directly with the Kindle Paperwhite, made by Amazon, and the Kobo Clara 2E, produced by Rakuten.

Battery life is the standout feature: Pixelbook Labs claims 10 weeks on a single charge, and my own testing over 21 days of moderate use suggests that figure is realistic. The page-turn latency, a persistent complaint with the first InkSlate, has dropped from 300 milliseconds to roughly 90 milliseconds, a 70 percent improvement that makes reading feel noticeably smoother.

The InkSlate 3 does have drawbacks. It lacks physical page-turn buttons, and the microUSB port feels dated compared to the USB-C connectors now standard on competitors. Pixelbook Labs says a firmware update in April will add support for Spanish and French menus, expanding beyond English.

At $229, the InkSlate 3 is not cheap, but for readers who prioritize battery life and display quality over bells and whistles, it earns a solid recommendation.

Nakamura Bikeworks of Portland, Oregon is now shipping the Trailhawk GX2, a full-suspension gravel bike engineered for riders who split time between pavement and singletrack. Priced at $2,899, the Trailhawk GX2 features a Reynolds 725 chromoly frame, a Shimano GRX 400 drivetrain, and 45mm WTB Riddler tires mounted on 700c alloy rims. Nakamura Bikeworks, founded in 2016 by former racer Elena Vasquez, began as a two-person workshop in Beaverton before expanding into a 12,000-square-foot facility in 2021. The Trailhawk GX2 was designed by lead engineer Marcus Feldt and tested over 3,200 miles across the Oregon Coast Range prior to its August 14, 2024 launch. Each frame is hand-welded in the company's Portland facility and covered by a limited lifetime warranty. Customers who order before October 1, 2024 receive a free Blackburn Outpost cargo rack, a $65 value. The bike ships in one of three colorways: Slate Gray, Rust Orange, and Forest Green, and is available in five frame sizes ranging from 48cm to 61cm. Nakamura Bikeworks competes directly with Salsa Cycles and All-City Cycles in the drop-bar adventure segment, but distinguishes itself with direct-to-consumer pricing that cuts out traditional bike shop markups. Reviewers at Bicycling Magazine praised the Trailhawk GX2's stability on loose gravel, awarding it a 4.5 out of 5 rating in their September 2024 gear roundup. Orders placed by 2 p.m. Pacific ship the same day from the Portland warehouse via FedEx Ground, typically arriving within 3 to 5 business days across the continental United States.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Manchester City edged Liverpool 2-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, with Erling Haaland scoring twice to move his season tally to 11 goals in the Premier League. Liverpool's Mohamed Salah pulled one back in the 78th minute, but manager Jurgen Klopp's side could not find an equalizer despite four minutes of stoppage time.

The match drew 53,412 spectators, and City manager Pep Guardiola praised his squad's discipline afterward, calling the win "one of our most complete performances this season." The result lifted Manchester City to second place in the Premier League table, three points behind leaders Arsenal.

Haaland's opening goal came in the 22nd minute, a close-range finish set up by Kevin De Bruyne, while his second, a penalty in the 55th minute, followed a foul on Jack Grealish inside the box. Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk was booked for the challenge.

In a post-match press conference at the Etihad Stadium, Klopp confirmed that midfielder Alexis Mac Allister will undergo a scan on Monday after limping off in the second half with a suspected hamstring injury. "We will know more in the next 48 hours," Klopp said.

Manchester City will next travel to Germany to face Borussia Dortmund in the UEFA Champions League on October 24, while Liverpool host Everton at Anfield on October 21. The Premier League confirmed both fixtures will kick off at 8:00 PM local time.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT PRESS STATEMENT
Ottawa, October 14, 2024

The Ministry of Transport today announced that Minister Sophie Laurendeau will allocate CAD 42 million to upgrade the Highway 7 corridor between Kingston and Ottawa, following a structural assessment that identified deterioration in three bridge spans. The funding, approved under the Federal Infrastructure Renewal Act, will be disbursed to the Ontario Ministry of Transportation beginning November 1, 2024.

"This investment reflects our commitment to safety and economic connectivity," said Minister Laurendeau during a press briefing at the Ottawa Convention Centre. She was joined by Deputy Minister Rajiv Chandra, who confirmed that construction firm Bouchard Infrastructure Group has been selected as the lead contractor. Work is expected to begin on April 6, 2025, and conclude by September 2026.

The announcement follows a February 2024 incident in which a section of the Highway 7 overpass near Perth partially collapsed, injuring two maintenance workers employed by Bouchard Infrastructure Group. No fatalities were reported. The Transportation Safety Board of Canada, led by Chair Elena Wu, is expected to release its final findings on November 20, 2024.

Opposition critic Marcus Delaine, Member of Parliament for Kingston and the Islands, welcomed the funding but urged the ministry to expedite inspections of similar structures across Ontario. The Ministry of Transport confirmed that fourteen additional bridges will undergo review by January 2025.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Finally Gets the Basics Right

Mountain View, October 14, 2024 -- Google launched the Pixel Watch 3 on September 10, 2024, priced at $349.99 for the 41mm model, and after four weeks of daily wear I think it is the company's most polished wearable yet. I tested the unit purchased directly from the Google Store in San Francisco, California.

The standout upgrade is battery life. Google's hardware chief, Rick Osterloh, claimed at the launch event in Mountain View that the watch would last up to 36 hours, and in my testing with the always-on display enabled I consistently got 28 hours, a meaningful jump from the Pixel Watch 2. The 45mm variant, reviewed briefly at a Best Buy demo table in Chicago, felt noticeably lighter than last year's model, dropping about 10 percent in weight.

Software remains the differentiator. Wear OS 5, co-developed with Samsung, now handles background sync far more efficiently, and Fitbit's redesigned dashboard finally surfaces useful morning summaries instead of a wall of numbers. Loss of Pulse Detection, a new safety feature, automatically contacted emergency services during a treadmill test at a gym in Austin, Texas, which was unsettling but reassuring.

At $349.99, the Pixel Watch 3 competes directly with the Apple Watch Series 10 and the Samsung Galaxy Watch 7. Apple still wins on app selection, but Google has closed the gap considerably. If you already own a Pixel 9 phone, this is an easy recommendation; for iPhone owners, stick with Apple.

Rating: 4 out of 5 stars.

Pixelbook Labs, a hardware startup based in Austin, Texas, launched the Fenwick S1 tablet on March 12, 2024, priced at $649. I have spent three weeks testing the device and came away impressed, though not without reservations. The Fenwick S1 uses a 10.9-inch OLED panel supplied by Hansol Display, a South Korean manufacturer, and runs on a custom chip called the Orion X2, designed in-house by Pixelbook Labs engineers led by Chief Technology Officer Priya Nandakumar. Battery life is rated at 14 hours, and in my usage it held up to roughly 12 hours of mixed video playback and web browsing. The build quality feels premium, with a magnesium alloy chassis that undercuts the weight of Apple's iPad Pro by 38 grams. Software is where the S1 stumbles. It ships with FenOS 2.1, a lightly modified version of a Linux-based operating system, and several third-party apps I tried, including a banking app from Meridian Bank, crashed on first launch. Pixelbook Labs says a patch is coming on April 5, 2024. The company, founded in 2021 by former Dell engineer Marcus Ojeda, has raised $40 million in venture funding, according to a statement from spokesperson Elena Vasquez. Ojeda told me in a phone interview last week that Pixelbook Labs plans to open a second office in Berlin by the end of 2025 to serve European customers. For $649, the Fenwick S1 offers strong hardware let down by unfinished software, making it a promising but risky purchase for early adopters.

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY

On September 12, 2023, Judge Marlene Whitfield sentenced Anthony Delgado, 41, of Newark, to seven years in state prison after he pleaded guilty to aggravated assault stemming from an incident at the Ironbound Tavern on East Ferry Street on March 3, 2023. Prosecutor Diane Restrepo told the court that Delgado struck victim Harold Kessler with a beer bottle during an argument, causing severe lacerations that required Kessler to be transported to Newark Beth Israel Medical Center for treatment.

Delgado was arrested by Newark Police Department officers on March 4, 2023, and was later charged with aggravated assault by the Essex County Prosecutor's Office. The trial hearing, held at the Essex County Courthouse in Newark, concluded on August 21, 2023, when Delgado entered his guilty plea before Judge Whitfield.

In addition to the prison term, Judge Whitfield ordered Delgado to pay $12,500 in restitution to Kessler for medical expenses. Defense attorney Samuel Ortiz argued for a reduced sentence, citing his client's lack of prior convictions, but the court found the severity of Kessler's injuries warranted the full term.

The case, formally titled State of New Jersey v. Anthony Delgado, drew attention from local advocacy group Newark Safe Streets Coalition, which has pushed for stricter penalties in bar-related violence cases across Essex County.

7/ Whitfield told reporters, "We built something real in Denton, and I want to make sure the people who built it with me land somewhere good." More updates as this develops.

AUSTIN, Texas -- Meridian Robotics Inc. announced on June 12, 2024 that it has acquired Corvus Dynamics LLC, a privately held sensor-fusion startup based in Boulder, Colorado, for $85 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by August 1, 2024, will bring Corvus Dynamics' 42 employees and its LiDAR-based navigation platform, TerraSense, under the Meridian Robotics brand.

Meridian Robotics, headquartered in Austin, Texas, is a leading manufacturer of autonomous warehouse vehicles, including its flagship AGV model, the HaulerX200. Chief Executive Officer Priya Nandakumar said the acquisition would let the company integrate TerraSense sensors directly into the HaulerX200 line, reducing collision rates by an estimated 30 percent.

"Corvus Dynamics has spent five years perfecting perception software that rivals anything on the market," Nandakumar said during a press briefing at Meridian's Austin headquarters. "This partnership accelerates our roadmap by at least two years."

Corvus Dynamics was founded in 2019 by Dr. Samuel Okafor, who will join Meridian Robotics as Vice President of Perception Engineering effective July 1, 2024. Okafor previously worked at Bosch as a senior research scientist.

Meridian Robotics, a competitor of Chicago-based Vantage Autonomy Corp., expects the transaction to add $40 million in annual revenue starting in fiscal year 2025. The combined company will employ roughly 610 people across facilities in Austin, Boulder, and a new distribution center planned for Reno, Nevada, slated to open in early 2025.

HARTFORD, Conn. — Meridian Rail Corp. announced Tuesday it will acquire regional freight operator Nutmeg Line Holdings for $412 million, a deal expected to close by January 15, 2025. The agreement was disclosed at a press briefing in Hartford by Meridian CEO Denise Halloran, who said the acquisition would expand the company's East Coast freight network by nearly 30 percent.

Nutmeg Line, headquartered in New Haven, operates 18 locomotives and serves ports across Connecticut and Rhode Island. Its founder and outgoing chief executive, Marcus Whitfield, will step down from his role effective December 1, 2024, but will remain as a senior advisor through mid-2025.

"This merger strengthens our position against competitors like Palmetto Freight Systems," Halloran said during Tuesday's announcement. "Nutmeg's port access in New Haven is exactly what we need."

Shares of Meridian Rail rose 6.4 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.20. Analysts at Brightwater Capital, a Boston-based investment firm, said the deal reflects growing consolidation in the Northeast freight sector after three smaller rail carriers filed for bankruptcy protection over the past two years.

The transaction still requires approval from the U.S. Surface Transportation Board, which is expected to review the filing by early February 2025. Halloran added that roughly 240 Nutmeg employees would be retained, though the company's New Haven headquarters will eventually be consolidated into Meridian's Hartford offices.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. RG24-118872

On March 11, 2024, Judge Patricia Something Well, presiding over Department 17 of the Alameda County Superior Court in Oakland, sentenced Marcus Delaney, 41, to 54 months in state prison after a jury found him guilty of embezzlement from his former employer, Bayline Freight Solutions. Prosecutor Angela Reyes of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Delaney, who worked as a Senior Accounts Manager at Bayline Freight Solutions from June 2018 until his termination in September 2022, diverted approximately $412,000 in client payments into a shell account registered under the name Delaney Logistics LLC.

The scheme was uncovered in October 2022 when an internal audit ordered by Bayline's chief financial officer, Howard Chen, flagged irregularities in invoices tied to a longtime client, Pacific Rim Textiles. Delaney was arrested by Oakland Police Department detectives on January 9, 2023, at his residence in Fremont and was later charged with grand theft and money laundering under California Penal Code Section 503.

Defense attorney Louis Barrera had requested probation, citing Delaney's lack of prior convictions, but Judge Well rejected the request, noting the sustained duration of the fraud. Bayline Freight Solutions, headquartered in San Leandro, has since implemented new financial controls. Delaney must also pay restitution of $412,000, to be determined at a separate hearing scheduled for April 22, 2024.

Cedar Point Logistics, a freight-forwarding company headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Blue Ridge Trucking Inc. for $142 million in cash. The deal, disclosed by Cedar Point chief executive officer Marcus Feldman during a press briefing at the company's Charlotte headquarters, is expected to close by November 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval. Blue Ridge Trucking, based in Knoxville, Tennessee, operates a fleet of roughly 1,200 tractor-trailers and employs about 3,400 people across the southeastern United States. Feldman said the acquisition will let Cedar Point expand into refrigerated freight, a segment currently dominated by rival Arctic Transport Group. "This gives us the scale to compete directly with Arctic Transport Group in perishable goods hauling," Feldman told reporters. Blue Ridge founder and outgoing chief executive Rita Alvarez will step down from her post once the transaction closes, though she has agreed to serve as a consultant through March 2025. Analysts at Sterling Capital Partners, including senior analyst David Wong, said the price represents a 22 percent premium over Blue Ridge's estimated market value. Cedar Point shares rose 4.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.10. The company financed the purchase through a combination of $90 million in cash reserves and a $52 million loan from First National Bank of the Carolinas. Cedar Point expects the combined entity to generate $1.1 billion in annual revenue by fiscal year 2025.

input: Hélène Dubreuil (born 14 March 1952 in Lyon, France) is a French microbiologist known for her work on antibiotic resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae. She earned her doctorate from the University of Paris in 1978 and joined the Institut Pasteur that same year as a research scientist. In 1991, Dubreuil was appointed Director of the Department of Microbial Genetics at the Institut Pasteur, a position she held for over two decades. Her 1985 paper describing the plasmid-mediated transfer of resistance genes, published in the journal Nature, became a foundational reference in the field and has been cited more than 4,000 times. In 1998, Dubreuil co-founded the biotechnology company MicroGenix in Strasbourg with her colleague Dr. Bernard Faucher, aiming to commercialize rapid diagnostic tools for hospital-acquired infections. MicroGenix was acquired by the Swiss pharmaceutical giant Novartis in 2006 for an undisclosed sum, though industry sources estimated the deal at roughly 45 million euros. Dubreuil stepped down from her Institut Pasteur post in 2013 and became a professor emeritus at Sorbonne University. In 2015, she received the Legion of Honour from the French government in a ceremony held in Paris, recognizing her contributions to public health. She married fellow scientist Dr. Marc Talbot in 1980, and the couple had two children. Dubreuil currently resides in Lyon, where she continues to advise the World Health Organization on antimicrobial resistance policy.

Pixelworks Labs, a hardware startup based in Portland, Oregon, launched its new smart camera, the LumaCube 4K, on March 3, 2024. Founded in 2019 by engineer Rosa Delgado, the company has focused on affordable imaging tools for independent filmmakers. The LumaCube 4K retails for $649 and includes a detachable gimbal, a 1-inch sensor, and 10-bit color depth. I tested the camera for three weeks in Seattle, Washington, shooting a short documentary about the Duwamish River cleanup.

Compared to the Sony ZV-E1, which costs $2,199, the LumaCube 4K is a bargain, though its autofocus lags noticeably in low light. Battery life is rated at 90 minutes, and in practice I got closer to 75 minutes with Wi-Fi streaming enabled. The companion app, LumaSync, crashed twice during a 40-minute recording session, which was frustrating during a client shoot.

Rosa Delgado told me in a phone interview on March 10, 2024, that a firmware update is expected in April to fix the crashing bug. She also mentioned that Pixelworks Labs is in talks with B&H Photo to expand retail distribution beyond its current online store. For $649, the LumaCube 4K delivers surprisingly sharp 4K footage and a genuinely useful gimbal, but the buggy software holds it back from being a must-buy. I'd recommend waiting for the April firmware patch before purchasing.

Elena Marcheva (born 14 March 1958 in Plovdiv, Bulgaria) is a Bulgarian-American structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques used in high-rise construction. She earned a degree in civil engineering from the Sofia University of Architecture and Civil Engineering in 1981 before emigrating to the United States in 1984. In 1990, Marcheva joined Halden & Ross Structural Partners in Chicago as a junior engineer, and by 1998 she had risen to Chief Structural Engineer. In 2003 she left Halden & Ross to found Marcheva Dynamics LLC, a firm headquartered in San Francisco specializing in earthquake-resistant design for skyscrapers. The company's signature achievement came in 2011, when its damping system was installed in the Cortland Tower, a 62-story building in Los Angeles. Marcheva Dynamics LLC was acquired by Kessler Infrastructure Group for 340 million dollars in September 2016, though Marcheva remained as a consultant until 2019. On 8 May 2014, Marcheva received the Global Resilience Award from the International Council on Structural Safety at a ceremony in Geneva, Switzerland, recognizing her contributions to disaster-resistant architecture. She is married to fellow engineer Dimitar Nikolov, with whom she has one son, Aleksandar Nikolov, born in Chicago in 1993. Marcheva became a naturalized United States citizen in 1996. She currently serves on the advisory board of the American Society of Civil Engineers and lectures occasionally at Stanford University. In interviews, she has cited the 1979 Montenegro earthquake as the formative event that drew her toward seismic engineering.

organization: Sofia University of Architecture and Civil Engineering

input: Fjallraven Kanken 16L Backpack is now available at Nordstrom Rack in Seattle, Washington, priced at $79.99. This refurbished unit was originally sold new for $110.00 by Fjallraven, a Swedish outdoor equipment company founded in 1960 by Ake Nordin. The backpack features Vinylon F fabric, a water-resistant material developed to withstand rain in the Nordic climate, and includes two front pockets, padded shoulder straps, and a laptop sleeve that fits up to a 15-inch device. Nordstrom Rack acquired this batch of 250 units directly from Fjallraven's Stockholm distribution center on March 3, 2024, as part of a clearance partnership announced earlier that year. Each unit has been inspected by certified technicians at the Seattle facility and shows only minor cosmetic wear on the base panel. The color options include Ox Red, Fog, and Navy, though only Fog and Navy remain in stock as of April 10, 2024. Customers who purchase before April 30, 2024 will receive a 10% discount at checkout using code SPRING10. Reviews from verified buyers, including Seattle resident Maria Lindqvist, praised the bag's durability, with Lindqvist noting she has used hers daily since 2021 without a single tear. Shipping is handled by FedEx and typically takes 3 to 5 business days within the continental United States. Returns are accepted within 30 days at any Nordstrom Rack location.

Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1958 in Bologna, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques used across southern Europe. She earned her degree in civil engineering from the University of Bologna in 1981 and later completed a doctorate at ETH Zurich in 1986. In 1990, Marchetti founded Marchetti Structural Associates in Milan, a firm that grew to employ 340 engineers by 2010. The company was acquired by the multinational conglomerate Vertex Infrastructure Group in July 2011 for approximately 220 million euros, after which Marchetti stayed on as Chief Technical Officer until her retirement in 2019. Her most cited project, the retrofit of the Basilica di San Petronio following the 2012 Emilia earthquake, reduced structural vulnerability by an estimated 60 percent according to independent assessors. In 2015, Marchetti received the Golden Compass Award from the Italian Ministry of Infrastructure in Rome for her contributions to public safety engineering. She is married to fellow engineer Paolo Ricci, with whom she has two children, Sofia and Marco Ricci. Marchetti currently serves as a visiting professor at Politecnico di Milano, where she lectures on earthquake-resistant design. She remains a member of the International Association for Earthquake Engineering and continues to consult on infrastructure projects throughout Italy and Greece.

Pixelbook Forge Review: Google's New Chromebook Struggles to Justify Its $1,299 Price

Seattle, October 14, 2023 - Google unveiled the Pixelbook Forge last month at an event in Mountain View, California, and after two weeks of daily use, I remain unconvinced it deserves a spot in anyone's bag. The laptop, manufactured by Quanta Computer under contract for Google, pairs a 13-inch OLED display with an Intel Core Ultra 7 processor and 16 gigabytes of RAM. Build quality is excellent, and the keyboard is among the best I've tested this year, but the $1,299 asking price puts it in direct competition with Apple's MacBook Air and Dell's XPS 13, both of which offer longer battery life.

Sundar Pichai, Google's chief executive officer, called the Forge "a statement product" during the launch keynote, and Rick Osterloh, senior vice president of devices at Google, told reporters that the company sold roughly 40,000 units in the first week. That figure sounds respectable until you consider that Samsung sold over 500,000 Galaxy Book4 laptops in the same period, according to data from Counterpoint Research analyst Priya Nandakumar.

Battery life clocked in at just 7 hours in my testing, well short of Google's claimed 11 hours. Software issues were also frustrating: ChromeOS 118 crashed twice during video calls on Google Meet. For $1,299, I expected fewer compromises. Unless Google issues a significant price cut or a battery-focused firmware update, I'd steer most buyers toward the cheaper Acer Chromebook Spin 714 instead.

CHICAGO, Oct 14 - Archer Grain Corp announced Tuesday it will acquire Midwest Silo Systems Inc for $412 million in cash, expanding its footprint in grain storage infrastructure across the Midwest. The deal, expected to close by January 2025, will make Archer Grain the largest operator of silo networks in Illinois and Iowa.

Under the agreement, Archer Grain will pay Midwest Silo Systems shareholders $58 per share, a 22 percent premium over Monday's closing price. Chief Executive Officer Laura Hutchins said the acquisition strengthens Archer Grain's supply chain and reduces reliance on third-party storage providers such as Prairie Bulk Holdings.

"This transaction positions us to serve customers more efficiently while cutting logistics costs by roughly 15 percent," Hutchins told analysts during a conference call from the company's headquarters in Chicago, Illinois.

Midwest Silo Systems, founded in 1987 by Gerald Voss, operates 46 grain elevators across six states. Voss, who retired as chairman in 2019, praised the deal as a validation of the company's long-term strategy.

Archer Grain's shares rose 6.4 percent to $91.20 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Midwest Silo Systems shares jumped 19 percent to $57.85. Analysts at Blackstone Ridge Capital raised their price target on Archer Grain to $105, citing improved margins.

The transaction, funded through a combination of cash reserves and a $250 million term loan from First Continental Bank, still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission. Archer Grain expects the review process to conclude within 90 days.

Peloton Interactive unveiled the Row+, its second-generation rowing machine, at a press event in Brooklyn on September 10, 2024. Priced at $3,295, the Row+ adds a swiveling 23.8-inch touchscreen and a magnetic resistance system with 32 levels, up from 16 on the original Row launched in 2022. I tested the unit for three weeks at my apartment in Queens, New York, and the improvements are noticeable immediately. The screen now rotates 180 degrees so users can follow floor workouts without dismounting, a complaint CEO Barry McCarthy acknowledged during the Brooklyn launch.

Performance-wise, the drag chain feels smoother than the 2022 model, and the companion app, updated to version 4.7, syncs stroke-rate data to Apple Health and Garmin Connect within seconds. Peloton says the Row+ will ship starting October 1, 2024, initially to customers in the United States and Canada, with United Kingdom availability slated for early 2025.

Competitors are already circling. Hydrow, based in Boston, Massachusetts, cut the price of its Wave rower by $200 the same week, a move analysts at Morgan Stanley called a direct response to Peloton's announcement. Meanwhile, Peloton's stock rose 4 percent on the Nasdaq following the unveiling, a welcome sign for a company that reported a $167 million net loss last quarter.

My main gripe is the $44 monthly subscription required to unlock live classes, pushing the effective first-year cost past $3,800. For serious rowers with the budget, though, the Row+ is the most polished machine Peloton has built.

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT — PUBLIC NOTICE
Jakarta, 4 March 2024

The Ministry of Transport of Indonesia today announced a $420 million infrastructure package to upgrade regional ferry terminals across Sulawesi and the Maluku Islands. Minister Budi Karya Sumadi confirmed that PT Pelni, the state-owned shipping operator, will receive 60% of the funding to modernize eleven port facilities by December 2026. "This investment will cut travel times by nearly 30 percent for over 2.3 million passengers annually," Minister Sumadi said during a press briefing at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport.

The announcement follows a review ordered after the ferry KM Sinar Bangun capsized near Lake Toba in 2018, an incident that prompted stricter safety regulations under the National Shipping Safety Law of 2019. Director General Antoni Arif Priadi stated that the Directorate General of Sea Transportation will deploy 45 new safety inspectors to fifteen provinces starting 1 April 2024.

Opposition lawmaker Fadli Zon criticized the timeline, arguing that similar pledges made in 2021 were only 40 percent completed. The Ministry responded that a supplementary budget of Rp 1.2 trillion, approved by the House of Representatives on 28 February 2024, will accelerate procurement of new vessels from PT PAL Indonesia, a state shipbuilder based in Surabaya.

The Ministry expects the first upgraded terminal, in Bau-Bau, to open by June 2025, with full completion targeted for 15 December 2026.

HARTFORD, Conn. — Meridian Steelworks Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in outstanding debt and collapsing demand from the automotive sector. The filing, submitted in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Connecticut, marks the end of a 68-year run for the Hartford-based manufacturer, which once employed 4,200 workers across three states.

CEO Diane Kowalski told reporters at a press briefing that the company had explored a merger with rival Blackstone Alloys Corp. earlier this year, but talks collapsed in March after the two sides could not agree on valuation. "We fought to save these jobs until the last possible moment," Kowalski said outside the company's headquarters on Prospect Avenue.

Meridian's board voted Monday to appoint restructuring specialist Raymond Ochoa as chief restructuring officer, effective immediately, to oversee the wind-down of operations. Ochoa previously guided Delphi Manufacturing through its 2019 bankruptcy.

About 1,100 employees at the Hartford plant will be laid off by December 15, according to a filing with the Connecticut Department of Labor. Union representatives from United Steelworkers Local 447 gathered outside the courthouse Tuesday afternoon to protest the layoffs, holding signs and chanting for severance guarantees.

Meridian's stock, which traded at $2.15 on the New York Stock Exchange before the announcement, fell 61 percent in after-hours trading. Analysts at Fitch Ratings downgraded the company's credit rating to D, citing "no viable path to solvency."

organization: U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Connecticut

Dr. Amara Foster (born March 14, 1958, in Lagos, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-British immunologist known for her contributions to malaria vaccine research. Foster earned her medical degree from the University of Ibadan in 1981 before relocating to the United Kingdom, where she completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford in 1986. In 1990, she joined the Wellcome Trust Centre for Human Genetics as a research fellow, and by 1997 she had risen to the position of Director of Immunology.

In 2003, Foster co-founded ImmunoVax Therapeutics, a biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, United Kingdom, alongside her longtime collaborator Dr. Peter Nkemelu. The company focused on developing next-generation vaccines for malaria and tuberculosis. Under her leadership, ImmunoVax Therapeutics grew to employ over 400 scientists before it was acquired by Genexis Pharmaceuticals for $1.2 billion in September 2015.

Foster received the Lasker-DeBakey Clinical Medical Research Award in 2011 for her work on the RTS,S malaria vaccine candidate, presented to her in New York City. In 2018, she stepped down as Chief Scientific Officer of Genexis Pharmaceuticals to become a visiting professor at Imperial College London.

Foster married fellow researcher Dr. Peter Nkemelu in 1995; the couple has two children. She continues to advocate for expanded vaccine access across sub-Saharan Africa and serves on the board of the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria.

DETROIT, Mich. — Automaker Ferris Motors announced Tuesday that it has acquired battery startup VoltCore Technologies for $740 million, a move aimed at accelerating production of its electric pickup truck lineup. The deal, finalized at Ferris Motors' headquarters in Detroit, was confirmed by Chief Executive Officer Diane Kessler during a press briefing attended by roughly 60 reporters and analysts.

"VoltCore's solid-state battery technology will let us cut charging times by nearly 40 percent," Kessler said. VoltCore Technologies, founded in 2018 by engineer Marcus Oyelaran in Austin, Texas, employs about 210 people and has been a key supplier to several mid-sized automakers over the past three years.

Under the agreement, VoltCore will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Ferris Motors, retaining its Austin facility while adding 150 new jobs in Detroit by March 2025. Oyelaran will join Ferris Motors as Chief Technology Officer starting January 6, replacing outgoing CTO Harold Nguyen, who is stepping down after eight years to pursue a teaching position at the University of Michigan.

Shares of Ferris Motors rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of rival automaker Bramwell Auto Group dipped 1.8 percent. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners called the acquisition "a decisive bet on next-generation battery supply chains." Regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission is expected by February 2025, according to a company statement released Tuesday afternoon.

The Ministry of Environment and Water Resources of Ghana announced on 14 March 2024 that it will invest 85 million cedis to rehabilitate flood defenses along the Odaw River in Accra following the disaster that displaced roughly 3,200 residents last September. Minister Kwabena Otieno-Mensah told reporters at a press briefing in Accra that the funds, drawn from the National Disaster Management Fund, would be disbursed to the Accra Metropolitan Assembly by 30 April 2024. "This is a direct response to the flooding that struck the Alajo and Avenor communities," Otieno-Mensah said. "We cannot allow another disaster of this scale." The rehabilitation contract has been awarded to Buildcon Ghana Ltd, a subsidiary of the South African firm Stratcon Holdings, which will begin construction on 1 May 2024 and complete the project within eighteen months. The Ghana Meteorological Agency, headquartered in Legon, has warned that the upcoming rainy season could bring rainfall 20 percent above the historical average. Deputy Minister Ama Serwaa Adjei, who assumed her post in January 2023, confirmed that a parallel early-warning system will be installed in partnership with the United Nations Development Programme. Opposition lawmaker Kojo Ansah-Boateng criticized the timeline as too slow, noting that residents of Alajo have already endured two flooding events since 2021. The Ministry stated that a public forum will be held in Accra on 5 April 2024 to address community concerns before construction begins.

SUPERIOR COURT OF ARIZONA, MARICOPA COUNTY

On September 12, 2024, Judge Elena Ruiz sentenced Marcus Whitfield, 41, to seven years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of embezzlement and wire fraud in connection with his former position at Sonoran Trust Bank in Phoenix, Arizona. Prosecutor Daniel Ochoa of the Maricopa County Attorney's Office argued that Whitfield, who worked as a Senior Financial Officer at the bank between 2017 and 2023, diverted approximately $2.3 million from client accounts into shell companies registered in Nevada. The scheme was uncovered in March 2023 when internal auditors at Sonoran Trust Bank flagged irregular transfers totaling $410,000 made over a single weekend. Whitfield was arrested by Phoenix Police Department detectives on June 4, 2023, at his residence in Scottsdale, Arizona, and was charged with fraud on June 9, 2023, following an indictment presented to Judge Ruiz. During the trial, which began on August 5, 2024, at the Maricopa County Superior Courthouse, defense attorney Priya Nandan contended that her client had acted under duress from a former supervisor, though the jury rejected this argument after four days of deliberation. Sonoran Trust Bank, a subsidiary of Desert Financial Holdings, issued a statement confirming that restitution proceedings would begin in October 2024, with the bank seeking to recover the full $2.3 million from Whitfield's remaining assets. Judge Ruiz ordered Whitfield to pay restitution of $1.8 million in addition to his prison sentence.

BOSTON, MA - September 12, 2023 - Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital reported promising Phase 2 trial results for tavelumab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arcadia Therapeutics for the treatment of relapsing multiple sclerosis. The study, led by Dr. Helena Ruiz, an associate professor of neurology, enrolled 214 patients across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and July 2022. Participants receiving 300 milligrams of tavelumab every four weeks experienced a 47 percent reduction in annualized relapse rate compared to placebo, according to findings published in The Lancet Neurology. Secondary endpoints showed a 31 percent decrease in new brain lesions detected by MRI. The most common adverse events were mild infusion-site reactions and headache, reported in 12 percent of participants; no cases of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy were observed. Arcadia Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by former Genentech scientist Dr. Marcus Weill, plans to initiate a Phase 3 trial in early 2024 involving approximately 900 patients. The company's chief medical officer, Dr. Priya Nair, stated that tavelumab could represent a meaningful advance for patients who have not responded to existing therapies such as ocrelizumab. Arcadia's stock rose 18 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement. The National Multiple Sclerosis Society welcomed the results, noting that multiple sclerosis affects an estimated 1 million people in the United States. Full data will be presented at the ECTRIMS Congress in Milan, Italy, on October 14, 2023.

Bellroy Studio, a design-led accessories brand headquartered in Fitzroy, Australia, has launched the Kanto Weekender Bag, a 42-liter travel duffel crafted from water-resistant recycled polyester. Priced at $189.00, the bag is now available on Bellroy Studio's website and through select retailers including Nordstrom in Seattle, Washington. The Kanto Weekender debuted on March 14, 2024, and has already sold more than 3,000 units in its first month, according to spokesperson Maya Renwick. "We designed this bag for people who travel two or three times a month," Renwick said during a press briefing in Melbourne on March 20, 2024. The duffel features a padded 15-inch laptop sleeve, a detachable shoulder strap rated for 20 kilograms, and a hidden shoe compartment. It comes in three colorways: Slate Grey, Rust Orange, and Midnight Black. Bellroy Studio was founded in 2010 by Andy Fallshaw and Steve Fallshaw, brothers who started the company in a small workshop in Fitzroy before expanding internationally. The brand is a subsidiary of Ferro Design Holdings, a private manufacturing group based in Singapore. Reviewers at Wirecutter awarded the Kanto Weekender their Editors' Choice Award on April 2, 2024, citing its durability and organizational pockets. The bag ships within 5 business days and includes a 3-year warranty against manufacturing defects. Customers who purchase before April 30, 2024 receive a complimentary luggage tag valued at $15.

SUPERIOR COURT OF ORANGE COUNTY, CALIFORNIA
Case No. 30-2024-CV-01187

On March 11, 2024, the Superior Court of Orange County entered a judgment against Marcus Whitfield, former Chief Financial Officer of Solaris Harbor Inc., following a bench trial presided over by Judge Elena Torres. Prosecutor Daniel Ruiz, representing the Orange County District Attorney's Office, charged Whitfield with wire fraud and embezzlement stemming from the diversion of $2.4 million in company funds between January 2019 and October 2021. Solaris Harbor Inc., headquartered in Irvine, California, is a subsidiary of Pacifica Energy Group.

According to trial testimony, Whitfield transferred the misappropriated funds to a shell company, Redwood Capital Partners, registered in Delaware, using wire transfers routed through First National Bank of Anaheim. Company auditor Priya Nandakumar first flagged irregularities in the ledger during a routine review in September 2021, prompting an internal investigation.

Judge Torres sentenced Whitfield on March 11, 2024, to seven years in state prison and ordered restitution of $2.4 million payable to Solaris Harbor Inc. Whitfield's attorney, Gregory Hale, indicated an appeal would be filed with the California Court of Appeal within thirty days.

The case was investigated jointly by the Orange County District Attorney's Office and the Federal Bureau of Investigation, whose Los Angeles field office assisted in tracing the fraudulent transfers. Company spokesperson Lena Ortiz stated that Solaris Harbor Inc. has since implemented new financial oversight controls under its current CFO, Thomas Reyes, who assumed the position in November 2021.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. RG24-118832

On March 11, 2025, Judge Marion T. Whitfield presided over the sentencing hearing of Defendant Carlos Neri Vasquez in Department 17 of the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland. Vasquez, 41, was convicted on February 3, 2025, of grand theft and embezzlement following a jury trial in which Deputy District Attorney Elaine Sorrento served as prosecutor. Evidence at trial showed Vasquez, a former bookkeeper at Harmon & Reyes Logistics Inc., diverted approximately $412,000 from company accounts between June 2021 and August 2023.

Judge Whitfield sentenced Vasquez to four years in state prison and ordered restitution of $412,000 payable to Harmon & Reyes Logistics Inc. Defense attorney Priya Kapoor argued for probation, citing her client's lack of prior record, but the court denied the motion. Vasquez was remanded into custody immediately following the hearing by Alameda County Sheriff's deputies.

In a related civil matter, Harmon & Reyes Logistics Inc. filed suit against Vasquez on September 9, 2023, seeking damages; that case was stayed pending the criminal proceeding and is expected to resume in Alameda County Superior Court later this year.

Court spokesperson Denise Farrow confirmed the sentence would be entered into the record by March 18, 2025. Vasquez's attorney indicated an appeal may be filed with the California Court of Appeal, First Appellate District, within 60 days.

input: Cedar Point Logistics, a Nashville-based freight brokerage, announced on Tuesday that it has acquired regional carrier Blue Ridge Transport for $84 million in a cash-and-stock deal. The acquisition, disclosed at a press briefing in Nashville, Tennessee, marks Cedar Point's third purchase since 2021 and expands its footprint into the Southeast trucking corridor. Blue Ridge Transport, headquartered in Asheville, North Carolina, operates a fleet of roughly 340 tractor-trailers and employs about 620 drivers and staff. Under the terms of the agreement, Blue Ridge founder Martin Reyes will step down as chief executive officer effective November 1, 2024, while remaining as a strategic advisor for one year. Cedar Point's CEO, Dana Whitfield, said the deal would close by December 15, 2024, pending regulatory review by the Federal Trade Commission. "This gives us the scale to compete directly with Landstar System and J.B. Hunt in the Carolinas," Whitfield told reporters. Shares of Cedar Point, which trades privately, are not publicly listed, but the company's bondholders reacted positively, with its 2027 notes rising 1.3 percent in early trading. Analysts at Merrick Capital Partners estimated the combined entity could generate $410 million in annual revenue, up from Cedar Point's current $290 million. The deal follows a wave of consolidation in freight brokerage, as smaller carriers struggle with fuel costs and driver shortages. Reyes, who founded Blue Ridge Transport in 1998, said he was proud of the company's growth over twenty-six years.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., March 4, 2024 -- Nimbus Therapeutics, Inc. announced today that it has acquired Solvex Biosciences Ltd. for $340 million in a deal expected to close on April 15, 2024. The acquisition will strengthen Nimbus's pipeline of treatments for chronic kidney disease and give the company access to Solvex's proprietary compound, SVX-221, currently in Phase 2 trials.

Under the terms of the agreement, Nimbus will pay $250 million in cash and $90 million in stock to Solvex's shareholders. The transaction was unanimously approved by both companies' boards of directors and is subject to customary regulatory clearance.

"This acquisition represents a pivotal step in our strategy to become a leader in renal disease treatment," said Dr. Helena Ruiz, Chief Executive Officer of Nimbus Therapeutics. "Solvex's research team, led by Dr. Marcus Feldt, has made remarkable progress on SVX-221, and we look forward to accelerating its development."

Dr. Feldt, who founded Solvex Biosciences in 2016 in Cambridge, will join Nimbus as Senior Vice President of Research starting April 15, 2024. He will report directly to Dr. Ruiz.

Solvex, headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, currently employs 85 researchers and support staff, most of whom are expected to relocate to Nimbus's Cambridge campus by June 2024.

Nimbus shares rose 6.2 percent following the announcement, closing at $58.30 on the Nasdaq exchange. Analysts at Everstone Capital called the deal "a smart bet on a crowded but lucrative therapeutic market."

The combined company will employ approximately 640 people across its Cambridge and Boston facilities.

DENVER, Oct. 14 - Rocky Mountain Energy Corp. announced Monday it has acquired Sable Basin Resources LLC for $612 million in cash and stock, expanding its footprint in the Permian Basin. The deal, expected to close in December, was disclosed in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Under the agreement, Rocky Mountain Energy will pay $410 million in cash and issue 6.2 million shares to Sable Basin's shareholders. Sable Basin, headquartered in Midland, Texas, produces roughly 38,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day across 45,000 net acres.

"This transaction strengthens our position as a leading independent producer," said Karen Whitfield, Chief Executive Officer of Rocky Mountain Energy, during a call with analysts. Whitfield added that the company expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive to cash flow.

Sable Basin's founder and outgoing CEO, Marcus Delgado, will step down once the deal closes and will not join the combined company. Delgado founded Sable Basin Resources in 2011 with backing from private equity firm Coldwater Partners.

Analysts at Fairmont Securities, including Priya Nataraj, said the price represents an 18 percent premium over Sable Basin's last private valuation. Shares of Rocky Mountain Energy rose 4.3 percent to $57.20 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement.

The combined company will control more than 210,000 acres and is projected to generate $1.4 billion in annual revenue. Rocky Mountain Energy said it will fund the cash portion of the deal through a new $350 million term loan arranged by Highbridge Capital Bank.
