AUSTIN, Texas -- November 14, 2023 -- Meridian Robotics Inc., a manufacturer of industrial automation systems, announced today that it has acquired Prescott Vision Systems LLC, a privately held machine-vision startup based in Boulder, Colorado, for approximately 42 million dollars in cash and stock.

Under the terms of the agreement, Prescott Vision Systems will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Robotics, retaining its 58 employees and its facility in Boulder. The deal is expected to close on December 5, 2023, pending customary regulatory approvals.

"This acquisition strengthens our position against competitors like Danforth Automation and accelerates our roadmap for AI-driven inspection tools," said Meridian Robotics Chief Executive Officer Laura Ibsen, who will present the integration plan to shareholders at the company's Austin headquarters on November 20, 2023.

Prescott Vision Systems was founded in 2016 by Dr. Samuel Ortiz, who will join Meridian Robotics as Vice President of Machine Vision, reporting directly to Ibsen. Ortiz previously worked at Lockheed Martin for nine years before starting his own company.

Meridian Robotics, which employs roughly 1,200 people worldwide, posted revenue of 310 million dollars in its most recent fiscal year. Shares of the company, which trades under the ticker MRDN, rose 4 percent following the announcement.

The combined entity will showcase its new inspection platform, VisionCore 3, at the National Robotics Expo in Chicago in February 2024.

Pixelnest Labs, a Portland startup founded in 2019 by former Intel engineer Rosa Delgado, launched its long-awaited handheld gaming device, the Nova Deck, on June 4, 2024. Priced at $429, the Nova Deck runs a custom build of Linux and ships with a 7-inch OLED screen, 16GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD. I have spent three weeks with the review unit, and the results are genuinely impressive for a first-generation product.

Battery life stands out immediately: roughly 6 hours of continuous play in demanding titles like Elden Ring, compared to the 4 hours typical of the Steam Deck OLED, made by Valve Corporation, its closest competitor. The 720p display gets bright enough for outdoor use, and the haptic triggers feel more precise than those on the ASUS ROG Ally.

Delgado told reporters at a press event in San Francisco that Pixelnest plans to ship 200,000 units by December 2024, with a European launch to follow in early 2025. The company also announced a partnership with AMD, which will supply the custom Zen 4 chip powering the device.

The Nova Deck isn't perfect. Its trackpads are cramped, and the fan grows audible under load. But at $429, it undercuts rivals by nearly $120 while offering comparable performance. For handheld PC gaming enthusiasts, the Nova Deck is a serious, budget-friendly contender that deserves attention.

Marguerite Okonkwo-Lindqvist (born 14 March 1958 in Lagos, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-Swedish structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques in West Africa. She earned a degree in Civil Engineering from the University of Lagos in 1980 and later a doctorate from the Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm in 1986. In 1991, Okonkwo-Lindqvist joined Skanska AB in Stockholm as a Senior Structural Engineer, where she worked for eleven years. In 2002, she left Skanska AB to found Baobab Structural Consultants, headquartered in Lagos, Nigeria, serving as its Chief Executive Officer. Under her leadership, the firm designed the retrofit of the Third Mainland Bridge completed in 2009, a project praised by the Nigerian Society of Engineers. In 2014, Baobab Structural Consultants merged with the Stockholm-based firm Nordisk Bygg AB to form Baobab Nordisk Engineering, with headquarters in both Lagos and Stockholm. Okonkwo-Lindqvist stepped down as Chief Executive Officer in March 2020, remaining on the board as a non-executive director. In November 2021, she received the Prince Philip Medal from the Royal Academy of Engineering in London for her contributions to sustainable infrastructure in developing nations. She married Erik Lindqvist, a fellow engineer, in 1985, and the couple has two children, Adaeze and Bjorn. Okonkwo-Lindqvist currently divides her time between Lagos and Stockholm, continuing to consult on infrastructure projects across Nigeria, Ghana, and Kenya. She holds citizenship in both Nigeria and Sweden.

MANCHESTER, England – October 14, 2024 – Manchester City extended its unbeaten home run to eleven matches on Saturday, defeating Aston Villa 3-1 at the Etihad Stadium in front of 53,412 spectators. Norwegian striker Erling Haaland scored twice in the first half, netting in the 12th minute and again in the 34th minute, before Belgian midfielder Kevin De Bruyne added a third goal in the 61st minute. Aston Villa's lone reply came from Ollie Watkins in the 78th minute.

Manager Pep Guardiola praised his squad's discipline after the match, telling reporters at the post-match press conference, "We controlled the tempo for ninety minutes, and that is exactly what we needed against a team like Villa." Villa boss Unai Emery countered that his side "competed well but lacked the final ball in the box."

The win moved Manchester City to 22 points after eight matches, two points clear of second-placed Arsenal, who defeated Everton 2-0 earlier in the day at Emirates Stadium. Liverpool sits third with 19 points following a goalless draw against Brighton on Friday.

City midfielder Rodri, last year's Ballon d'Or winner, was substituted in the 70th minute as a precaution due to a minor knee complaint, according to the club's medical staff. Guardiola confirmed Rodri would be assessed ahead of City's Champions League fixture against RB Leipzig on October 22, 2024.

The Premier League's next round of fixtures begins October 19, 2024, with City traveling to face Wolverhampton Wanderers at Molineux Stadium.

Pixelbook Forge 14 Review: Google's Priciest Chromebook Yet

Mountain View, CA -- On March 11, 2024, Google launched the Pixelbook Forge 14, a $1,299 flagship Chromebook aimed squarely at Apple's MacBook Air. I have spent three weeks with the review unit supplied by Google, and the verdict is mixed.

The Forge 14 pairs a 3K OLED display with an Intel Core Ultra 7 155H chip and 16GB of RAM. Benchmarks from Anandtech last month confirmed battery life of just over 11 hours, respectable for a machine this thin. Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google, called the laptop "the clearest signal yet that ChromeOS can compete at the premium tier" during a briefing at the company's Mountain View headquarters.

Still, software remains the bottleneck. Android app scaling is inconsistent, and offline support for Google Docs lags behind Microsoft's OneDrive integration on Windows machines. A firmware update pushed on March 20, 2024 fixed a trackpad stutter that plagued early units, but users on Reddit report a new Bluetooth bug affecting the Forge 14's pairing with Sony WH-1000XM5 headphones.

Competing devices, including the Asus Chromebook Plus CX34 and Lenovo's ThinkPad Chromebook, undercut the Forge 14 by roughly $400, raising questions about whether Google can justify the premium. Google spokesperson Maria Chen said the company plans a software update in June 2024 to address the Bluetooth issue.

For buyers who live inside Google's ecosystem and value display quality above all, the Forge 14 is compelling. For everyone else, $1,299 is a steep ask for a Chromebook.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Finally Gets the Basics Right

By Marcus Feldman, October 14, 2024

Google launched the Pixel Watch 3 on September 20, 2024, at a starting price of $349.99, and after three weeks of daily wear in Austin, Texas, I can say it fixes most of my complaints about the original. The 45mm model I tested, on loan from Google's press office, uses a 3nm Snapdragon W5 chip supplied by Qualcomm, and battery life stretched to roughly 36 hours with the always-on display enabled.

The biggest improvement is brightness: at 2,000 nits, the display is finally readable under direct sunlight, something reviewers criticized harshly when the first Pixel Watch debuted in 2022. Google also added a Loss of Pulse Detection feature, developed in partnership with Fitbit, which the company acquired back in 2021. During a hiking trip near Zilker Park, the watch's fall-detection alert triggered a test call to emergency contacts within nine seconds, which felt reassuring rather than gimmicky.

Software-wise, Wear OS 5 feels noticeably snappier than the version shipped last year, and Google says over 60% of battery drain complaints reported after the Pixel Watch 2 launch have been resolved through firmware updates. My one gripe is the $349.99 price still undercuts the Apple Watch Series 10 by only $50, making the competitive gap narrower than Google probably wants.

Overall, this is the most polished wearable Google has shipped, and it finally feels like a genuine rival to Samsung's Galaxy Watch 7 rather than a footnote in the smartwatch market.

input: The Ministry of Environment and Water Resources of Ghana announced on 9 April 2024 that it will invest 42 million cedis to rehabilitate flood defenses along the White Volta River near Tamale. Minister Kwabena Osei-Mensah stated the funding, released through the National Disaster Management Organisation, follows the March 2024 floods that displaced roughly 6,500 residents in the Northern Region. "We cannot allow another disaster like the one that struck Yendi to repeat itself," Osei-Mensah told reporters during a briefing at the ministry's headquarters in Accra. The project, to be carried out by contractor Bimbilla Construction Ltd, will begin on 1 June 2024 and is expected to conclude within eighteen months. According to engineer Adjoa Frimpong, who leads the technical review team, the new levees will be built two meters higher than the previous structures destroyed in the flooding. The ministry also confirmed it has signed a memorandum of understanding with the World Bank, which will contribute an additional 15 million dollars toward long-term watershed management under the Ghana Resilient Rivers Programme. Osei-Mensah added that a public consultation session will be held in Tamale on 20 April 2024 to gather input from local chiefs and farmers affected by the disaster. Opposition lawmaker Sarah Boateng criticized the timeline as too slow, arguing that families in Yendi have already waited nearly two months without adequate shelter. The ministry says it remains committed to completing the rehabilitation before the next rainy season begins in late June.

Watkins opened the scoring in the 14th minute with a low finish after a through ball from midfielder John McGinn, then doubled his tally in the 52nd minute with a header from a corner kick. Everton pulled one back through striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 63rd minute, but defender Ezri Konsa restored Villa's two-goal cushion in the 78th minute with a close-range volley. The match, played in front of 41,000 spectators, was overseen by referee Michael Oliver. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his team's discipline after the game, telling reporters, "We controlled the tempo for large stretches, and Ollie's movement caused them problems all afternoon." Everton manager Sean Dyche said his side had conceded soft goals at crucial moments. The win moved Aston Villa to 62 points, four points behind fourth-placed Tottenham Hotspur with six matches remaining this season. Villa's next fixture is scheduled for April 21 against Brighton & Hove Albion at the American Express Stadium. Watkins, who has now scored 22 goals this season, was named Premier League Player of the Month for March by the league on Monday, an award presented at a ceremony in London.

input: CLEVELAND, Ohio -- Cedar Point Manufacturing filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $340 million in outstanding debt and a sharp drop in orders for industrial fasteners. The company, headquartered in Cleveland since 1978, employs roughly 1,200 workers across three plants in Ohio and Indiana. CEO Marcus Whitfield told reporters at a press briefing that the filing would allow Cedar Point to restructure while continuing daily operations. "We intend to keep every plant running through this process," Whitfield said. Court records filed in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Ohio show the company's largest creditor is Fifth Third Bank, owed approximately $95 million. Industry analyst Renata Sokolova of Great Lakes Capital Partners said the bankruptcy reflects broader stress in the automotive supply chain, noting that Cedar Point's biggest customer, Detroit-based Harlow Motors, cut orders by 22 percent last quarter. Whitfield, 54, took over as chief executive in March 2019 after founder Diane Kessler stepped down following a 41-year career at the firm. Kessler founded Cedar Point Manufacturing in 1978 with her late husband, Robert Kessler. Local officials expressed concern about the region's economy. Cleveland Mayor Priya Nair said the city would work with the company to protect jobs. A hearing before Judge Elaine Marsh is scheduled for November 14 in Cleveland to review the restructuring plan.

input: The Ontario Ministry of Transportation announced on May 14, 2024 that it will invest $220 million to widen Highway 401 between Milton and Mississauga, a project expected to reduce commuter delays by 18 percent once completed. Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria stated at a press conference in Toronto that construction will begin in September 2024 and continue through late 2027. The project, named the 401 Expansion Initiative, will be carried out by Aecon Group Inc., a construction firm headquartered in Toronto that was awarded the contract following a competitive bidding process. Aecon Group Inc. previously completed the Highway 407 interchange upgrade in 2019. Deputy Minister Doug Jones said the ministry will also allocate $15 million toward noise barriers for residents in Milton, a response to concerns raised by the Milton Residents Coalition during a demonstration held outside Queen's Park on April 3, 2024. Approximately 300 demonstrators gathered to protest construction noise and property devaluation. Sarkaria confirmed that the Ministry of Transportation will hold a public consultation in Mississauga on June 10, 2024 to address further concerns. The provincial government expects the expansion to accommodate 40,000 additional vehicles daily by 2030, supporting Ontario's growing population and easing congestion across the Greater Toronto Area.

DETROIT, Mich. — Novum Motors Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired battery-technology startup CellCore Systems for $412 million in cash, a move the automaker says will accelerate its shift toward electric vehicles. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing at Novum's headquarters in Detroit, is expected to close by March 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval.

Under the agreement, CellCore's 220 employees, including founder and Chief Executive Officer Dr. Elena Marsh, will join Novum's newly formed battery division. Marsh, who founded CellCore in 2018 in Austin, Texas, will take on the role of Chief Technology Officer at Novum, reporting directly to Novum CEO Raymond Ortiz.

"This acquisition gives us direct control over solid-state battery production, something our competitor Halden Auto has been racing to secure as well," Ortiz said during the briefing. Shares of Novum Motors rose 6.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $58.94.

Analysts at Kessler Bradshaw Partners estimated the deal values CellCore at nearly 18 times its projected 2025 revenue. The transaction will be funded through a combination of $250 million in cash reserves and a $162 million bridge loan from Meridian Trust Bank.

Novum, which employs roughly 31,000 people worldwide, has faced pressure from investors to reduce its reliance on third-party battery suppliers such as PowerLinx Corp. Ortiz said the CellCore deal marks the company's largest acquisition since it purchased chip designer Trellix Semiconductor in 2021 for $780 million.

Sacramento, Calif. — Delta Grid Corp., a mid-sized utility holding company headquartered in Sacramento, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $2.3 billion in wildfire liability claims stemming from the Butte Canyon Fire in September 2023. The filing was submitted to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in the Eastern District of California.

CEO Marisol Fenwick told reporters at a press conference that the company would continue operating during restructuring and that no customers would lose power. "This is a painful but necessary step to ensure Delta Grid can compensate victims fairly," Fenwick said.

Attorney Ramon Ibarra, representing 300 fire victims, said his clients would fight to be prioritized in bankruptcy proceedings. "Families lost everything. They cannot be treated like ordinary creditors," Ibarra said.

Shares of Delta Grid, traded as DGRD, fell 42 percent to $3.10 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement. VoltCore's founder and chief executive, Raj Patel, will join Meridian as Chief Technology Officer starting January 6, 2025, according to a statement from the company.

The deal still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which has scrutinized similar mergers in the auto sector. Analysts at Bristow Capital said the transaction could position Meridian as a stronger competitor to Tesla Inc. and Rivian Automotive in the electric truck market.

Shares of Meridian Motors rose 8 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while privately held VoltCore's investors, including venture firm Alden Ridge Partners, are expected to receive a payout as part of the deal. Meridian said it plans to retain all 340 VoltCore employees at their existing Austin facility, with no immediate layoffs planned.

The announcement comes amid a wave of consolidation in the EV industry, as traditional automakers race to close the technology gap with newer entrants.

DETROIT, Nov. 14 - Blue Anchor Motors Inc. announced Tuesday it has acquired Lansing-based battery startup VoltCell Technologies for $412 million in cash, marking the automaker's largest acquisition since 2019. Chief Executive Officer Karen Mistry said the deal, expected to close by January 15, 2025, will let Blue Anchor build lithium iron phosphate battery packs domestically rather than sourcing them from suppliers in South Korea. VoltCell, founded in 2016 by engineer Daniel Okafor, employs 340 people at its facility in Lansing, Michigan, and reported revenue of $58 million last year. Under the agreement, Okafor will join Blue Anchor as Senior Vice President of Battery Engineering, reporting directly to Mistry. Shares of Blue Anchor rose 6.3 percent to $71.20 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of rival automaker Harrow Dynamics fell 1.8 percent amid concerns about the company's competitiveness in electric vehicles. Analysts at Ridgeline Capital Partners called the acquisition "a strategic masterstroke" in a note to clients, projecting the deal could reduce battery costs by 22 percent within three years. Blue Anchor, headquartered in Detroit, Michigan, plans to fund the purchase through a combination of $250 million in cash reserves and a new credit facility arranged by Meridian Bank. The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which is expected to review the filing over the next 60 days. If approved, VoltCell will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary under the new name Blue Anchor Battery Solutions.

input: MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side defeated Newcastle United 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, moving Villa up to fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute, converting a low cross from midfielder John McGinn, before Newcastle's Alexander Isak equalized just before halftime. In the second half, Watkins struck again in the 61st minute, and substitute Leon Bailey added a third in stoppage time to seal the win in front of 42,000 fans. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his team's resilience after the match, telling reporters, "We showed character today, and Ollie is playing with great confidence." Newcastle boss Eddie Howe acknowledged his side's defensive lapses, saying the team must improve before hosting Arsenal on October 21. The victory extended Aston Villa's unbeaten home run to eight matches this season and lifted the club above rivals Tottenham Hotspur on goal difference. Watkins, who has now scored seven goals in nine appearances for Villa this campaign, was named Premier League Player of the Month for September earlier this week, an award presented by the Premier League at a ceremony in London. Villa will next travel to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on October 29, while Newcastle return to action against Arsenal at St James' Park. Aston Villa's chief executive, Christian Purslow, said the club's ambitions this season include qualifying for the Champions League for the first time in over four decades.

input: Ingrid Falk (born 14 March 1958 in Malmö, Sweden) is a Swedish biochemist known for her contributions to enzyme engineering. She earned a PhD in Biochemistry from Lund University in 1986 and joined Karolinska Institutet as a postdoctoral researcher the following year. In 1994 Falk founded Novazym AB, a biotechnology company headquartered in Solna, Sweden, focused on developing industrial enzymes for detergent manufacturing. Under her leadership as Chief Executive Officer, Novazym AB grew to employ 210 people by 2003. That year, the company was acquired by Danish conglomerate Chr. Hansen Holding for 340 million Swedish kronor, a deal announced in Copenhagen on 9 September 2003. Falk stepped down as CEO in October 2003 but remained on the board as a scientific advisor. In 2008 she was appointed Professor of Molecular Biotechnology at Uppsala University, a position she held until her retirement in 2020. Falk received the Göran Gustafsson Prize in Biochemistry in 1999, awarded by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm, for her work on lipase stabilization. She has published more than 90 papers on protein engineering and holds seven patents related to enzyme catalysis. Falk married fellow researcher Anders Björk in 1990; the couple has two children. She currently resides in Uppsala, where she continues to consult for biotechnology startups.

Elena Vasquez (born March 14, 1968, in Bilbao, Spain) is a Spanish-American structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-resistant designs in high-rise construction. She earned a degree in Civil Engineering from the Universidad Politécnica de Madrid in 1990 before immigrating to the United States, where she became a naturalized citizen in 1998. Vasquez joined Kessler & Hart Engineering in Chicago in 1993 as a junior structural analyst, rising to Chief Engineer by 2005. In that role she led the design of the Meridian Tower in San Francisco, completed in 2011, which withstood a magnitude 5.4 earthquake near Oakland in 2014 without structural damage. In 2016 Vasquez left Kessler & Hart to found Terrastable Structures, a consultancy headquartered in Seattle, Washington, that develops base-isolation systems for earthquake-prone regions. The company was acquired by Obayashi Corporation in 2021 for an undisclosed sum, though industry sources estimated the deal at 40 million dollars. Vasquez continued as President of the Seattle division following the acquisition. In 2019 she received the Nakamura Prize for Structural Innovation from the International Association for Earthquake Engineering at a ceremony in Tokyo, Japan. She has published over 30 papers in the Journal of Structural Engineering and holds three patents related to viscoelastic dampers. Vasquez is married to architect Thomas Reyes, with whom she has two children, Mateo and Sofia. She currently resides in Seattle and serves on the advisory board of the American Society of Civil Engineers.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolvirumab, an investigational monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arcadia Therapeutics, for the treatment of relapsing multiple sclerosis. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants receiving 300 milligrams of tolvirumab every eight weeks showed a 42 percent reduction in annualized relapse rate compared to placebo, according to findings published in The New England Journal of Medicine. Dr. Marsh stated that the drug also reduced new brain lesions detected via MRI by 58 percent over the 18-month study period. Arcadia Therapeutics, founded in 2015 by immunologist Dr. Rajiv Patel, plans to seek approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. The company's chief executive officer, Susan Okafor, said Arcadia has invested approximately 340 million dollars in the tolvirumab program to date. Novartis, a competitor in the multiple sclerosis therapeutic space, has expressed interest in licensing agreements, though no deal has been finalized. Common adverse events included mild upper respiratory infections and headache, reported in 19 percent of treated patients; no serious safety signals emerged. The trial was funded in part by a 25 million dollar grant from the National Institutes of Health. Dr. Marsh presented the full dataset at the American Academy of Neurology annual meeting in Denver, Colorado, on April 16, 2024.

1/ Big week for Denver's tech scene: Fenwick Robotics announced this morning it has acquired Boulder-based sensor startup Traxion Labs for $42 million in an all-cash deal. Fenwick CEO Marisol Ortega confirmed the news in a call with reporters at 9am MT on Tuesday.

2/ Ortega said Traxion's founder, Dr. Amit Chandra, will join Fenwick as Chief Technology Officer effective March 3rd. Chandra founded Traxion Labs back in 2017 with just three employees in a Boulder garage.

3/ The deal was funded partly through a $15 million bridge loan from Highline Capital, a Denver-based venture firm. Highline partner Greg Tanaka will also take a seat on Fenwick's board.

4/ Fenwick Robotics, headquartered in Denver, Colorado, makes industrial inspection drones used by pipeline operators across Texas and Oklahoma. Traxion's LIDAR sensors are expected to be integrated into Fenwick's next drone model, the Falcon-9X, launching in Q3.

5/ Not everyone is thrilled. Rival firm Ashgrove Dynamics called the acquisition "a consolidation move that hurts competition" in a statement released Wednesday afternoon.

6/ Chandra, who is originally from Pune, India, and became a U.S. citizen in 2019, said he's excited to scale the technology. "We built Traxion to solve a hard problem. Now we get to solve it at scale," he told a small crowd gathered at Fenwick's headquarters.

7/ Analysts expect Fenwick to file paperwork with the SEC within 30 days. Shares of publicly traded competitor Deltron Systems dipped 3.2% on the news.

CHICAGO, Nov. 14 -- Deere & Company announced Tuesday that it has completed the acquisition of Blue River Robotics Inc., a Sunnyvale-based agricultural technology startup, for $305 million in cash. The deal, first disclosed on October 3, closes a partnership that began three years earlier when the two companies co-developed weed-detection cameras for tractors. Deere's chief executive officer, John May, said the acquisition would accelerate the rollout of autonomous spraying equipment across North America and Brazil. "This purchase strengthens our precision agriculture platform and reduces herbicide use for farmers," May told reporters during a press briefing at Deere's headquarters in Moline, Illinois. Blue River's co-founder and outgoing chief executive, Priya Nathan, will step down from her post on December 1 and join Deere as vice president of autonomy engineering, according to a company statement. Analysts at Morgan Stanley raised their price target on Deere shares by 8 percent following the announcement, citing the strategic fit with rival Caterpillar's ongoing automation push. Deere stock rose 3.2 percent to $412.50 on the New York Stock Exchange after the news broke. The company also confirmed it will retain roughly 140 Blue River employees at their existing Sunnyvale office rather than relocating operations to Illinois. Blue River, founded in 2011 by Nathan and Jorge Heraud, had previously raised $30 million from venture investors including Khosla Ventures before its first partnership with Deere in 2017. The transaction is expected to close fully by January 15, pending routine regulatory review.

DETROIT, Mich. — Onyx Motors Corp. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan, citing $2.3 billion in outstanding debt tied to its stalled electric truck program. Chief Executive Marcus Feld told reporters at the company's Detroit headquarters that Onyx would continue operations during restructuring and expects to emerge from bankruptcy by June 2025. The filing comes two years after Onyx acquired battery maker Solara Cells for $410 million, a deal that Feld once called the cornerstone of the company's shift toward electric vehicles. Analysts at Fenwick Partners said the Solara acquisition strained cash reserves as production delays mounted at Onyx's Flint assembly plant. Shares of Onyx Motors, which trades under the ticker ONXM, fell 34 percent in after-hours trading following the announcement. Rival automaker Berrington Auto, headquartered in Warren, Michigan, said it does not expect the bankruptcy to affect supply agreements between the two firms. Onyx employs roughly 8,400 workers across three states, and the United Auto Workers union said it would seek assurances that no plant closures are planned before contract talks resume next month. Feld, 52, founded Onyx Motors in 2011 alongside co-founder Priya Nandakumar, who left the company in 2019 to launch her own startup. A bankruptcy court hearing is scheduled for March 14 in Detroit.

Duluth, Minnesota — October 14, 2024 — Lakeshore Robotics Inc. announced today that it has acquired Ironclad Sensors LLC, a Milwaukee-based manufacturer of industrial proximity sensors, for $42 million in cash. The acquisition, which closed on October 11, 2024, is expected to strengthen Lakeshore Robotics' position in the automated warehouse equipment market.

Under the terms of the agreement, Ironclad Sensors will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Lakeshore Robotics, retaining its 85 employees and its facility on Lincoln Avenue in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Ironclad Sensors founder and Chief Executive Officer Marta Kowalski will join Lakeshore Robotics as Vice President of Sensor Technology, reporting directly to Lakeshore Robotics CEO David Chen.

"This is a pivotal moment for our company," said Chen during a press briefing held at Lakeshore Robotics' headquarters in Duluth. "Ironclad's LIDAR-based sensor arrays will be integrated into our HaulerBot 200 platform within the next two quarters."

Kowalski, who founded Ironclad Sensors in 2009, said the deal would allow her team's technology to reach a broader customer base. Lakeshore Robotics, which reported $310 million in revenue last year, expects the acquisition to increase annual sales by approximately 12 percent by the end of 2025.

The transaction was financed through a combination of cash reserves and a $20 million credit facility provided by Great Northern Bank. Lakeshore Robotics' shares rose 4.3 percent following the announcement, closing at $58.91 on the Nasdaq.

CINCINNATI, OH -- July 9, 2024 -- Meridian Foods Corporation announced today that it has completed its acquisition of Blue Ridge Roasters, a specialty coffee producer based in Asheville, North Carolina, for approximately 142 million dollars in cash. The transaction closed on July 8, 2024, following approval from the Federal Trade Commission.

Under the agreement, Meridian Foods will absorb Blue Ridge Roasters as a wholly owned subsidiary while retaining its Asheville roasting facility and its 210 employees. Blue Ridge Roasters was founded in 2011 by Clara Whitfield, who will remain with the company as Vice President of Product Innovation.

"This acquisition strengthens our position in the premium coffee segment and complements our existing portfolio," said Marcus Delgado, Chief Executive Officer of Meridian Foods, at a press briefing held at the company's headquarters in Cincinnati. "Blue Ridge Roasters has built a loyal following, and we intend to expand distribution of its flagship product, the Appalachian Reserve blend, into 3,000 additional grocery stores by the end of the fourth quarter."

Clara Whitfield added, "Joining Meridian gives us the resources to scale production while preserving the craftsmanship our customers expect."

Meridian Foods, headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio, is a publicly traded consumer goods company with annual revenue exceeding 3.4 billion dollars. The company competes directly with Sunrise Beverage Group in the specialty foods market. Analysts at Hartwell Capital project the deal will boost Meridian's beverage division revenue by 8 percent within two years.

DETROIT, Mich. — Reliant Motors Corp. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $2.3 billion in unpaid supplier debts and a sharp decline in electric vehicle sales. The filing, submitted to the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Michigan, marks the end of a turbulent two-year run for the once-promising automaker founded in 2016 by entrepreneur Marcus Feld.

CEO Elena Voss told reporters at a press conference in Detroit that the company would continue operating its Warren, Michigan assembly plant while it restructures. "We owe it to our 4,800 employees to find a path forward," Voss said. Reliant's main lender, Cascade Bank, is owed roughly $780 million and has agreed to provide $150 million in debtor-in-possession financing to keep operations running through March 2025.

The bankruptcy follows a steep drop in demand for Reliant's flagship sedan, the Aurora EV, after two battery fires last year prompted a recall of 38,000 vehicles. Analysts at Baird Securities said the company's market share fell from 6 percent to under 1 percent in eighteen months, as competitors Tesla and Rivian expanded their lineups.

Marcus Feld stepped down as chairman in September 2023 and was replaced by Voss, a former Ford executive. Reliant's stock, once valued near $40 a share, closed Tuesday at 12 cents on the Nasdaq before trading was halted. Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer said the state would work with federal officials to protect jobs at the Warren facility.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solstice Robotics announced today it has acquired Denton-based sensor startup PixelHawk Systems for $42 million. CEO Marisol Torres said the deal closes by March 15, 2025.

2/ PixelHawk, founded in 2019 by engineer Aaron Feld, makes lidar sensors used in warehouse robots. Feld will join Solstice as VP of Sensor Engineering, reporting directly to Torres.

3/ Solstice, headquartered in Austin, Texas, has raised $310 million total and competes directly with Chicago-based Ferrum Automation for retail logistics contracts.

4/ Torres told reporters at a press event in downtown Austin on Tuesday that the combined company plans to hire 150 engineers by the end of 2025.

5/ Not everyone is thrilled. About 60 warehouse workers gathered outside Solstice's headquarters on Wednesday to protest potential automation-driven layoffs at partner facility Meridian Logistics in Round Rock.

6/ Meridian's spokesperson, Dana Ruiz, said no layoffs are planned this year, but declined to comment on 2026.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF ARIZONA, MARICOPA COUNTY — On October 14, 2024, Judge Rosalind Hartley sentenced Daniel Okafor, 41, to 7 years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of wire fraud and embezzlement stemming from his tenure as Chief Financial Officer of Sonoran Grain Cooperative, a Phoenix-based agricultural supplier. Prosecutor Marisol Vega of the Maricopa County Attorney's Office argued that Okafor diverted $2.3 million from the cooperative's accounts between March 2019 and August 2022, funneling the funds through a shell company, Desert Ridge Holdings LLC, before purchasing a 2021 Bentley Continental and a lakefront property in Show Low, Arizona. The trial, held at the Maricopa County Superior Courthouse in Phoenix, began on September 3, 2024, and concluded after eleven days of testimony from forensic accountant Priya Nandakumar and cooperative board chair Walter Fenwick. Defense attorney Sam Rosetti maintained that Okafor's actions were authorized by the board, but the jury rejected that claim on October 9, 2024. Sonoran Grain Cooperative, which supplies wheat and sorghum to distributors across Arizona and New Mexico, reported losses that pushed it toward Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings filed in December 2022. Okafor was arrested by agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation on January 17, 2023, at his residence in Scottsdale on charges of wire fraud. He will begin serving his sentence at the Arizona State Prison Complex in Florence.

Pixelbook Labs, a Portland-based startup founded in 2019 by Maria Whitfield, launched its second-generation tablet, the Slate Pro 2, on June 4, 2024. Priced at $649, the Slate Pro 2 targets professionals who need a lightweight device for sketching and note-taking. I have spent three weeks testing the 11-inch model, and the results are largely positive.

The Slate Pro 2 runs on a custom chip called Fenrir X1, developed in-house after Pixelbook Labs acquired chipmaker Northwind Semiconductor for $42 million in March 2023. Battery life is rated at 14 hours, and in my testing it consistently lasted 12 hours under heavy use, including video calls in Chrome and Figma sketching sessions. The 2560x1600 OLED display is noticeably brighter than the panel on the original Slate Pro, which shipped in 2021.

Whitfield, who serves as Chief Executive Officer, told reporters at a press event in San Francisco on June 3, 2024, that the company sold 30,000 units in the first 48 hours. That is a modest number compared to competitor Anveo Inc., whose Anveo Slate 3 reportedly sold 200,000 units last quarter, but Whitfield insists Pixelbook Labs is focused on quality over volume.

One real drawback: the included stylus, the Slate Pen 2, is sold separately for $89, which feels stingy at this price point. Software support is another concern, since Pixelbook Labs has a history of abandoning updates after eighteen months.

Still, for $649, the Slate Pro 2 is one of the more compelling tablets I have reviewed this year, and I recommend it cautiously to creative professionals.

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY
Criminal Division

Case No. ESX-2024-CR-01187

On March 14, 2024, defendant Marcus T. Ivey, 37, of Newark, New Jersey, appeared before Judge Regina Alvarado for a sentencing hearing after pleading guilty to one count of aggravated assault and one count of unlawful possession of a weapon. The charges stemmed from an incident on November 9, 2023, in which Ivey allegedly struck victim Daniel Wozniak with a tire iron outside a bar on Bloomfield Avenue in Newark, leaving Wozniak with a fractured jaw. Prosecutor Angela Fine of the Essex County Prosecutor's Office argued for a nine-year sentence, citing Ivey's prior conviction in 2019 for the same offense category.

Judge Alvarado sentenced Ivey to seven years in state prison, with credit for 128 days already served, to be followed by three years of parole supervision. The court also ordered Ivey to pay $4,500 in restitution to Wozniak for medical expenses incurred at St. Michael's Medical Center.

Defense attorney Louis Berardi stated his client accepted responsibility and would not appeal the sentence. Ivey was remanded to the custody of the New Jersey Department of Corrections immediately following the hearing. Wozniak, reached by phone, said he was relieved the case had concluded and hoped to return to work as a machinist by June 2024.

The case was formally docketed under New Jersey statute 2C:12-1b, governing aggravated assault.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. RG24-118732

On March 14, 2024, Judge Nora Estevez presided over the sentencing hearing of Defendant Marcus Whitfield, 41, at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, California. Whitfield was convicted on February 9, 2024, of embezzlement after prosecutors from the Alameda County District Attorney's Office, led by Deputy District Attorney Priya Nair, proved he diverted $412,000 from his former employer, Coastal Ridge Logistics Inc., between 2019 and 2022. Judge Estevez sentenced Whitfield to 36 months in state prison and ordered restitution of $412,000 payable to Coastal Ridge Logistics Inc.

Defense attorney Gerald Ostrowski argued for leniency, citing his client's lack of prior record, but the court noted the scale of the fraud warranted incarceration. Whitfield was arrested on November 3, 2023, by investigators from the Oakland Police Department after an internal audit at Coastal Ridge Logistics Inc. flagged irregular wire transfers to an account in Reno, Nevada.

Coastal Ridge Logistics Inc., headquartered in San Leandro, California, issued a statement thanking the District Attorney's Office and confirmed that Whitfield had served as the company's Chief Financial Officer from January 2017 until his termination in October 2022. The company said it has since implemented new internal controls. Whitfield's attorney indicated an appeal would be filed with the California Court of Appeal within 60 days.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2023 -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side defeated Fulham 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, moving Villa into fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Bernd Leno, before Fulham midfielder Andreas Pereira equalized in the 38th minute with a free kick from 25 meters. Villa captain John McGinn restored the lead just before halftime, and Watkins added his second goal in the 67th minute to seal the win in front of 41,912 fans. Aston Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's resilience after the match, telling reporters, "We showed character today, and Ollie's movement caused Fulham problems all afternoon." Fulham boss Marco Silva said his team's defending in the final third needed improvement ahead of their next fixture against Chelsea on October 21. The victory extended Aston Villa's unbeaten home run to seven matches this season. Villa will next travel to London to face Arsenal at Emirates Stadium on October 29, while Fulham return to Craven Cottage to host Chelsea. With the win, Aston Villa climbed above Tottenham Hotspur on goal difference, marking their best start to a Premier League campaign in over a decade.

Osprey Gearworks of Bend, Oregon has released the Talus 42 Hauler, a carbon-fiber cargo rack built for the Ford Maverick and priced at $389.00. Launched on September 9, 2024, the Talus 42 Hauler holds up to 250 pounds and mounts directly to the factory bed rails without drilling. Osprey Gearworks, founded in 2016 by former Bactrack Industries engineer Priya Nakamura, tested the rack for six months at a proving ground near Prineville, Oregon before bringing it to market. According to lead product manager Jonas Reitmeyer, the Talus 42 Hauler underwent 1,200 miles of washboard-road trials and a 40-percent overload test to meet internal safety margins. The rack ships in Matte Graphite or Desert Tan finishes and includes a 5-year limited warranty. Osprey Gearworks competes directly with Yakima and Rhino-Rack in the overlanding accessories space, though the Talus 42 Hauler undercuts comparable Yakima racks by roughly $60. Each unit weighs 34 pounds and arrives with a torque wrench, mounting hardware, and a laminated installation guide. Customers who purchased the Redwood Roof Basket, an earlier Osprey Gearworks product, can use a $25 trade-in credit through October 31, 2024. Units are currently in stock at REI stores in Portland and Seattle, with nationwide shipping available from the company's warehouse in Bend. Early reviewers, including automotive writer Carla Denison of Overland Journal, praised the rack's low profile and called it "the best bed-mounted hauler under $400."

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. RG24-118834

In the matter of People v. Derrick Osei, the Alameda County District Attorney's Office announced that Derrick Osei, 41, was sentenced on March 6, 2024, to 54 months in state prison after pleading guilty to grand theft under California Penal Code Section 487. Judge Patricia Lynwood presided over the hearing at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, California.

Prosecutors, led by Deputy District Attorney Miriam Solache, argued that Osei, a former warehouse supervisor at Fairmont Logistics Inc., diverted approximately $210,000 worth of imported electronics between June 2022 and October 2023. Defense attorney Gregory Nunn contended his client cooperated fully once arrested by Oakland Police Department detectives on November 14, 2023, following a joint investigation with the Alameda County Sheriff's Office.

According to court filings, Osei was charged on December 1, 2023, and appeared for a trial hearing on February 5, 2024, before Judge Lynwood entered the guilty plea agreement. Fairmont Logistics Inc., headquartered in San Leandro, California, stated it has since implemented new inventory-tracking software supplied by Meridian Systems Corp.

Osei must also pay $210,000 in restitution to Fairmont Logistics Inc. within five years of his release. He is scheduled for parole eligibility review in 2028.

Kessler Pharmaceuticals Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, citing $410 million in outstanding debt following a failed clinical trial for its flagship diabetes drug, Glucavex. The filing was submitted in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware in Wilmington.

CEO Miriam Voss announced the decision at a press briefing in Newark, New Jersey, where Kessler is headquartered. "This restructuring will allow us to protect roughly 1,200 jobs while we renegotiate terms with creditors," Voss said. The company's shares, traded on the Nasdaq under the ticker KSPH, fell 62 percent to $1.15 before trading was halted.

Kessler's troubles began in March 2024, when the Food and Drug Administration rejected Glucavex over safety concerns tied to elevated liver enzyme readings in trial participants. The company had spent an estimated $780 million developing the drug over eight years.

Analysts say Kessler now faces pressure from larger competitor Halden Biosciences, which controls nearly 40 percent of the diabetes-treatment market. Halden's chief executive, Peter Dunmore, declined to comment on whether his company would consider acquiring any of Kessler's remaining assets.

Creditors, led by Ridgeview Capital Partners, are expected to meet with Kessler executives in Wilmington on November 18 to discuss a restructuring plan. A federal bankruptcy judge, the Honorable Susan Fairweather, will oversee the proceedings. Kessler's stock has lost more than 90 percent of its value since January.

input: The Ministry of Environment and Water Resources announced on Tuesday that the Republic of Ghana will receive $42 million in grant funding from the World Bank to upgrade flood defenses along the Volta River. Minister Cecilia Abena Dapaah confirmed the agreement during a press briefing held at the Accra International Conference Centre. The funds, to be disbursed by 15 March 2024, will finance the construction of three new drainage channels in the Ashanti Region, a project expected to protect roughly 120,000 residents from seasonal flooding. World Bank Country Director Pierre Laporte, who signed the agreement on behalf of the institution, stated that the initiative aligns with the Ghana Resilience and Adaptation Programme launched in 2021. Dapaah noted that the flooding of September 2023, which displaced over 8,000 people in Kumasi, underscored the urgency of the investment. The Ministry also confirmed that engineering firm Vasco Consult Ltd, headquartered in Accra, has been contracted to oversee construction, with work scheduled to begin on 1 April 2024. President Nana Akufo-Addo is expected to visit the Ashanti Region next month to formally launch the project. Officials from the National Disaster Management Organisation will monitor progress alongside World Bank auditors. The Ministry emphasized that transparency measures, including quarterly public reporting, will accompany the disbursement of funds to prevent misuse.

input: BOSTON, MA -- November 12, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase II clinical trial evaluating tavolimab, an investigational monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotechnology firm Nuvara Therapeutics for the treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. The randomized, double-blind study enrolled 214 adult patients across 18 sites in the United States and Canada between March 2022 and January 2023. Dr. Elena Marsh, the trial's principal investigator and a professor of dermatology at Harvard Medical School, presented findings at the American Academy of Dermatology conference in Chicago on November 10, 2023. Patients receiving 300 milligrams of tavolimab every four weeks achieved a 78 percent reduction in Psoriasis Area and Severity Index scores at week 16, compared with 22 percent among those given placebo. Approximately 9 percent of participants in the treatment arm reported mild injection-site reactions, while no serious adverse events were attributed to the drug. Nuvara Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by immunologist Raj Patel, plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by mid-2024. The company's chief executive officer, Sandra Voss, stated that a Phase III trial involving 900 patients is scheduled to begin in Toronto and Berlin in January 2024. Shares of Nuvara Therapeutics rose 14 percent following the announcement. Analysts at Merrimack Capital noted that competitor Aclyris Biosciences, which markets a similar interleukin inhibitor, may face pricing pressure if tavolimab receives approval. The full results were published in The Journal of Clinical Dermatology on November 12, 2023.

Fjord & Pine, a Portland, Oregon-based furniture maker, has launched the Kettering Reading Chair, a mid-century-inspired lounge chair priced at $649.00 and available exclusively through the company's online store starting November 4, 2024. Built with solid white oak sourced from a supplier in Eugene, Oregon, and upholstered in Belgian linen, the chair comes in three colors: Slate Gray, Oat, and Rust. Each unit is hand-assembled at Fjord & Pine's workshop on Southeast Division Street and ships within 7 business days. The company's founder, Marta Solheim, said the design was inspired by her grandfather's reading nook in Bergen, Norway, and that only 500 units will be produced in this first run. Fjord & Pine was founded in 2016 and has since become a competitor to larger brands like Article and West Elm in the affordable modern furniture market. The Kettering Reading Chair weighs 38 pounds and holds up to 300 pounds. Customers who order before November 15, 2024 will receive a complimentary wool throw blanket worth $75. Returns are accepted within 30 days of delivery, and the chair carries a 5-year structural warranty. Reviewers from Dwell magazine praised the chair's craftsmanship after testing a prototype in September 2024. Shipping is available across the continental United States, with delivery typically taking 10 to 14 days. For bulk orders of 10 units or more, interested buyers can contact Fjord & Pine's sales team directly at sales@fjordandpine.com.

MANCHESTER, England, September 14, 2024 - Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice as his side defeated Everton 3-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, moving Villa to fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Jordan Pickford, then doubled his tally in the 38th minute from close range after a corner from midfielder Youri Tielemans. Everton pulled one back through Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 55th minute, but substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win with a curling strike in the 82nd minute. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, saying the team had "controlled the tempo for long spells." Everton boss Sean Dyche admitted his side struggled to contain Watkins, who has now scored 6 goals in his last 5 appearances for Villa. The victory lifts Aston Villa to 13 points from five matches, while Everton remain in the relegation zone with just 3 points. Villa Park, which holds approximately 42,000 spectators, was sold out for the fixture, with attendance reported at 41,832. The result continues a strong start for Villa under Emery, who took charge of the Birmingham-based club in November 2022. Villa will next travel to London on September 21 to face Arsenal at Emirates Stadium, while Everton host Crystal Palace the same day.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Finally Gets the Basics Right

By Renata Salvi, October 14, 2024

After two years of testing wearables from Mountain View, I can say the Pixel Watch 3 is the first one worth recommending without caveats. Google launched the device on September 10, 2024, at a press event in New York City, pricing the 45mm LTE model at $429.

The watch pairs with Google's Fitbit app, and battery life has finally improved to a genuine 36 hours under normal use, up from the 24 hours I measured on the Pixel Watch 2 last year. The AMOLED display is now 25 percent brighter, which mattered during a hike near Boulder, Colorado, where direct sunlight used to wash out the screen entirely.

Google's hardware chief, Rick Osterloh, told reporters at the launch that the company built the new sensor array specifically for runners, and it shows. Heart-rate accuracy during a 10K I ran in Golden Gate Park matched a chest strap from Polar within two beats per minute.

The watch isn't perfect. Software still lags behind Apple's watchOS 11 in third-party app support, and Samsung's Galaxy Watch 7, released in July 2024, remains a stronger value at $299. Still, at $429, the Pixel Watch 3 is a legitimate alternative for Android users who stuck with Fitbit trackers for years.

Google, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc., says it sold out of initial stock within 48 hours, according to a company spokesperson in Mountain View, California.

Ingrid Solheim (born March 4, 1958, in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist and former director of the Sørfjord Oceanographic Institute. She earned a doctorate in marine ecology from the University of Bergen in 1985 and joined the Institute for Marine Research the following year as a research scientist. In 1994 Solheim became head of the Sørfjord Oceanographic Institute, a position she held for twenty-two years.

Solheim is best known for documenting the collapse and recovery of herring stocks in the Norwegian Sea during the 1990s, work published in her 1998 monograph "Silent Currents." In 2003 she was elected to the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo. For this research, she received the Nansen Prize from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Bergen in November 2005.

In 2011 Solheim co-founded Nordvann Marine Consulting AS with her former student Petter Aasgard, advising fisheries companies across Scandinavia. The firm was acquired by the Dutch conglomerate Deltamare Group for 40 million kroner in June 2016, after which Solheim stepped down as director of the Sørfjord Oceanographic Institute.

She married oceanographer Halvor Lie in 1988; the couple have two children, Erik and Freya. Solheim currently lives in Bergen and continues to serve as an adjunct professor at the University of Bergen.

input: The Ontario Ministry of Transportation announced on April 9, 2024 that it will invest 240 million dollars to widen Highway 401 between Milton and Mississauga, a project expected to reduce congestion for roughly 300,000 daily commuters. Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria unveiled the plan at a press conference in Toronto alongside Metrolinx CEO Phil Verster. "This corridor is the busiest highway in North America, and drivers deserve relief," Sarkaria said. Construction, to be carried out by Aecon Group Inc., is scheduled to begin in June 2024 and finish by the fall of 2027. The ministry stated that Aecon was selected following a competitive bidding process that concluded in March 2024. Local officials in Mississauga, including Mayor Carolyn Parrish, welcomed the announcement, though the Peel Environmental Coalition held a demonstration outside Mississauga City Hall on April 11, 2024 to protest the highway's expansion, arguing it will increase carbon emissions rather than reduce them. The Ministry of Transportation countered that the project includes 15 kilometres of new dedicated bus lanes intended to encourage public transit use. Funding will be drawn jointly from the provincial budget and a 90 million dollar contribution from the federal government under the National Infrastructure Fund. Sarkaria added that a similar expansion for Highway 400 near Barrie is under review for 2025.

Frankfurt-based Deutsche Chemie AG announced on Tuesday that it has acquired specialty coatings maker NovaPoly GmbH for approximately 640 million euros, expanding its footprint in industrial adhesives. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing in Frankfurt, values NovaPoly at roughly 9 times projected 2025 earnings, according to CFO Martina Reuss. Deutsche Chemie shares rose 4.2 percent to 87.60 euros on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume more than doubled compared with the previous session. NovaPoly, founded in 1998 by engineer Lukas Brenner, employs about 1,200 workers across three plants in Germany and Poland and reported revenue of 310 million euros last year. Reuss said the acquisition, expected to close by December 15, 2024 pending regulatory approval, will be funded through a combination of cash reserves and a new 400 million euro bond issuance. Analysts at Commerzbank welcomed the move, noting that NovaPoly's customer base overlaps with rival BASF SE in the automotive coatings segment. "This transaction strengthens our position against BASF and other European competitors," said Deutsche Chemie CEO Helga Wentzel during the briefing. Brenner will step down as NovaPoly's managing director once the deal closes, handing operations to current deputy Sabine Kohl. The German Federal Cartel Office confirmed it will review the merger over the coming weeks, a process regulators estimate could take up to 90 days. Shareholders of both companies are expected to vote on final terms in January 2025.

Anker unveiled the Soundcore Space One Pro headphones on March 14, 2024, at a launch event in San Jose, California, pricing the noise-cancelling model at $149.99. I have spent three weeks testing a review unit shipped from Anker's Seattle distribution center, and the results are mostly impressive. Battery life reaches 40 hours with ANC enabled, beating the 30-hour figure Sony quotes for its WH-1000XM5, a direct competitor at $399. The adaptive noise cancellation, tuned by Anker's audio team led by engineer Priya Nandakumar, handles airplane cabin noise well, though it struggles with sudden sounds like barking dogs. Bluetooth 5.3 connectivity paired instantly with an iPhone 15 and a Dell XPS 13 laptop during my tests in Portland, Oregon. Anker, headquartered in Shenzhen, China, and founded by Steven Yang in 2011, says the Space One Pro uses recycled aluminum in its hinges, part of a sustainability pledge the company announced last year. At $149.99, the headphones undercut Sony and Bose by a wide margin while matching most of their features. Minor gripes include a plastic carrying case that feels cheaper than the $150 price suggests and an companion app, Soundcore, that occasionally fails to save custom EQ settings. Still, for shoppers deciding between flagship-priced options and something more affordable, the Space One Pro is easily the best value I have tested this year. Anker plans to ship the model to retailers including Best Buy on April 2, 2024.

To: Marcus Feldt, Chief Financial Officer, Brannigan Steelworks
From: Ivy Chen, Deal Counsel, Whitcombe & Ross LLP

Re: Closing of Asset Purchase from Delridge Fabrication

Under the terms finalized last week, Brannigan Steelworks paid $18.4 million in cash to Delridge's sole shareholder, Harold Ganz, for substantially all operating assets, including the Youngstown, Ohio fabrication plant and associated equipment.

Wire funds were transferred from Brannigan Steelworks' account at Keystone National Bank to Delridge Fabrication's escrow account at Third Union Trust on March 3, 2024, satisfying the full purchase price.

Separately, please note that Delridge's outgoing plant manager, Renata Solis, will step down from her position effective March 15, 2024, and will not be joining the combined entity. Brannigan Steelworks has appointed Devon Okafor as the new plant manager, starting March 18, 2024, reporting directly to you.

One open item: the Youngstown facility experienced a minor equipment fire on February 27, 2024, which injured one technician, Sam Kowalski, who was treated for smoke inhalation at Mercy Health St. Elizabeth. Please confirm whether Delridge's insurer, Ohio Mutual Casualty, has finalized the claim before we release the final escrow holdback of $250,000.

Please call me at (412) 555-0134 with any questions before Friday.

BOSTON, MA -- November 12, 2023 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tarlorafenib, an experimental oral kinase inhibitor developed by Cambridge-based biotechnology firm Solstice Therapeutics, for the treatment of relapsed acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The study, led by Dr. Elena Marchetti, enrolled 142 adult patients across 9 medical centers in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and July 2022. Participants received 200 milligrams of tarlorafenib daily for 24 weeks. According to findings published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, 61 percent of patients achieved complete remission, compared with 28 percent in the control arm receiving standard cytarabine chemotherapy. Grade 3 adverse events, primarily neutropenia and fatigue, occurred in 19 percent of the treatment group. Dr. Marchetti presented the data at the American Society of Hematology conference in San Diego on December 9, 2023. "These results suggest tarlorafenib could become a meaningful option for patients who have exhausted first-line therapies," she said. Solstice Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by former Novartis executive Raj Patel, plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by mid-2024. The company's shares rose 14 percent following the announcement. Rival firm Aravex Pharmaceuticals, which is developing a competing AML treatment, declined to comment. The trial was funded in part by a $22 million grant from the National Institutes of Health. Independent oncologists, including Dr. Samuel Okafor of the Mayo Clinic, called the results "promising but preliminary," noting that longer follow-up data are needed before the drug can be considered a standard therapy.

DENVER, Colorado -- Sept. 12, 2024 -- Rocky Mountain Coffee Roasters Inc. announced Thursday that it has acquired Boulder-based Alpine Bean Company for $42 million in cash, in a deal aimed at expanding its footprint across the Mountain West. The acquisition, which closed earlier this week, adds Alpine Bean's three roasting facilities in Colorado and Utah to Rocky Mountain's existing network of nine plants.

CEO Marisol Vance said the deal would boost annual revenue by roughly 18 percent, pushing the combined company past $310 million in sales for fiscal 2025. "Alpine Bean has built a loyal customer base over the past twenty-two years, and we intend to preserve that identity while scaling distribution nationally," Vance told reporters during a briefing at the company's headquarters in Denver.

Alpine Bean founder Tomas Reyes, who started the company in 2002 with his sister Elena Reyes, will stay on as Vice President of Sourcing for at least two years, according to the merger agreement. Elena Reyes, who previously served as Chief Operating Officer, stepped down from that role last month and will not join the combined entity.

Analysts at Highline Capital Partners, a Chicago-based investment firm, called the transaction a smart bet on premium coffee demand, noting that Rocky Mountain's stock rose 6 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement. The deal is expected to be finalized administratively by October 1, pending routine regulatory filings with the Colorado Secretary of State.

Sarah Mensah scored twice as the Portland Thorns defeated the Chicago Red Stars 3-1 at Providence Park on Saturday, October 12, 2024, keeping their playoff hopes alive in the National Women's Soccer League. Mensah opened the scoring in the 18th minute with a left-footed strike from outside the box, then added a second goal in the 54th minute after a quick counterattack set up by midfielder Olivia Rowe. Forward Camila Torres netted the Thorns' third goal in the 71st minute, converting a penalty kick awarded after a handball inside the area. Chicago's lone response came from striker Beatriz Nunes, who scored in the 63rd minute to briefly cut the deficit to one goal. Thorns head coach Rebecca Dolan praised her team's composure after the match, telling reporters, "We knew Chicago would push hard in the second half, but our defense held firm when it mattered." The win lifts Portland to 41 points, moving them into third place in the league table with two matches remaining. Chicago, coached by interim manager Frank Ilic, drops to ninth place with 27 points, all but ending their postseason ambitions. The Thorns will next travel to Kansas City on Saturday, October 19, to face the Current, while the Red Stars host the Orlando Pride the same day at SeatGeek Stadium. Attendance at Providence Park was announced at 18,442, a season high for the venue.

Introducing the Kessler Voyager 3 Trail Hiking Boot, engineered by Kessler Outdoor Co. of Bend, Oregon and released on March 14, 2024. Priced at $189.99, these boots are brand new and ship directly from the Kessler Outdoor Co. warehouse in Bend within 48 hours of purchase. The Voyager 3 features a waterproof Cordura Flex upper, a Vibram Megagrip outsole, and a proprietary EchoFoam midsole that Kessler engineers developed over 2 years of testing in the Cascade Mountains. Each pair weighs approximately 850 grams and is available in sizes 7 through 13, including half sizes. Customers who purchased the earlier Voyager 2 model report that the Voyager 3 offers 30 percent more ankle support and a noticeably lighter feel on long treks. Kessler Outdoor Co., founded in 2011 by former REI product designer Marcus Aldridge, has sold over 1.2 million pairs of hiking footwear since launching its flagship Trailhawk line in 2013. The Voyager 3 is already outselling comparable models from competitor Salomon in the North American market, according to a company statement issued last week. Every purchase includes a lifetime sole-replacement warranty and a free pair of Merino wool socks valued at $18. Orders over $150 qualify for free two-day shipping within the continental United States. The boots are covered under U.S. Patent No. 11,234,567 for the EchoFoam compression technology. For questions, contact customer support at support@kessleroutdoor.com or call 1-800-555-0199.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. RG24-118832

On Tuesday, March 11, 2025, Judge Patricia Nakamura sentenced defendant Marcus Ellery Todd, 41, to 36 months in state prison after a jury found him guilty of grand theft and embezzlement in connection with his former position at Coastal Ridge Logistics Inc., a freight brokerage headquartered in Oakland, California. Prosecutor Denise Whitfield of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Todd, who served as Chief Financial Officer of Coastal Ridge Logistics Inc. from January 2019 until his termination in August 2023, diverted approximately $612,000 in company funds into a shell account registered under his brother's name, Gregory Todd. The scheme was uncovered during an internal audit ordered by CEO Renata Alvarez in September 2023, after which Coastal Ridge Logistics Inc. reported the discrepancy to the Oakland Police Department. Todd was arrested on November 4, 2023, at his residence in Pleasanton by detectives from the Oakland Police Department on charges of embezzlement and falsifying corporate records. During the trial, which began on February 3, 2025, at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, defense attorney Harold Simms maintained that Todd had authorization for the transfers, but the jury rejected this claim on February 27, 2025. Judge Nakamura also ordered Todd to pay $612,000 in restitution to Coastal Ridge Logistics Inc. within five years. Ms. Whitfield stated afterward that the sentence "reflects the seriousness of betraying corporate trust." Todd's attorney indicated he intends to file an appeal with the California Court of Appeal, First Appellate District.

input: Meridian Outdoor Supply is now shipping the Kestrel 40L Alpine Backpack, a rugged trekking pack engineered by former REI product designer Sarah Voss and manufactured in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Priced at $189.99, the Kestrel 40L features a ripstop nylon shell, an aluminum internal frame, and a 15-liter hydration bladder compartment. Meridian Outdoor Supply, headquartered in Bozeman, Montana, launched the product line on March 3, 2024, after two years of field testing in the Bridger Mountains. Company founder Tomas Reyes said the pack was tested by a team of 12 guides on Mount Kilimanjaro and in Patagonia before final production began. Each backpack ships with a lifetime warranty and a detachable rain cover. The company reports that over 4,600 units have already been sold to retailers including Backcountry.com and Moosejaw since the launch. Customers who purchase before June 30, 2024 will receive a free titanium spork valued at $12. Reviewers at Outside Magazine gave the Kestrel 40L a 4.5 out of 5 rating, praising its 2.1-kilogram weight and adjustable torso length. The backpack is available in three colorways: Slate Gray, Forest Green, and Desert Tan. Meridian Outdoor Supply competes directly with Osprey Packs and Gregory Mountain Products in the North American trekking gear market. Orders placed after 2 p.m. Mountain Time ship the same day from the company's distribution center in Billings, Montana.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. — October 3, 2023 — Solara Biotics, Inc., a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, today announced that it has acquired Vantix Therapeutics for approximately $340 million in cash and stock. The transaction, finalized on September 29, 2023, gives Solara Biotics full rights to Vantix's lead compound, SLX-221, an experimental treatment for chronic kidney disease currently in Phase 2 trials.

Under the terms of the agreement, Solara Biotics will pay Vantix Therapeutics shareholders $12.50 per share, representing a 45 percent premium over Vantix's closing price on September 28, 2023. Dr. Elena Marsh, Chief Executive Officer of Solara Biotics, called the acquisition "a pivotal step in our mission to address unmet needs in renal medicine."

As part of the deal, Dr. Raymond Ito, founder and former CEO of Vantix Therapeutics, will join Solara Biotics as Chief Scientific Officer effective October 16, 2023. Vantix, founded in 2016 and based in Boston, Massachusetts, employs 85 researchers who will relocate to Solara's Cambridge campus by early 2024.

Solara Biotics expects the acquisition to close regulatory review by the Federal Trade Commission within 60 days. The company's shares, traded on the Nasdaq under the ticker SLRA, rose 6 percent following the announcement. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners project the combined pipeline could generate $1.2 billion in annual revenue by 2028.

Solara Biotics will host an investor call on October 5, 2023, at 9:00 a.m. Eastern Time to discuss the acquisition in greater detail.

Dr. Amara Solheim (born March 14, 1958, in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian-American marine biologist known for her research on Arctic phytoplankton. She earned her doctorate in oceanography from the University of Washington in 1986 and joined the Scripps Institution of Oceanography in La Jolla, California, as a research fellow that same year. In 1994 Solheim became the leader of the Arctic Ecosystems Laboratory, a position she held for eleven years while publishing extensively on Emiliania huxleyi, a species of calcifying algae central to carbon-cycle studies. In 2003 she co-founded Polarforsk AS, a Norwegian environmental research firm headquartered in Tromsø, alongside her longtime collaborator Dr. Henrik Aasland, whom she later married in 2006. Their daughter, Ingrid Aasland, was born in 2008 and has followed her mother into marine science. In November 2011, Solheim left Scripps Institution of Oceanography to become director of the Norwegian Polar Institute, a government agency based in Tromsø. She received the Volvo Environment Prize in Stockholm on October 9, 2015, in recognition of her work documenting a 22 percent decline in Arctic phytoplankton biomass since 1990. Polarforsk AS was acquired by the multinational firm Veolia Environnement for approximately 40 million dollars in 2019. Solheim retired from the Norwegian Polar Institute in June 2023 and now serves as an emeritus advisor to the European Environment Agency in Copenhagen.

Redmond, WA -- Microsoft Corporation began shipping the Surface Laptop 7 to retail partners on October 3, 2024, and after four weeks of daily use, the $1,499 configuration has earned a cautious recommendation. The unit tested pairs a Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite processor with 32 gigabytes of RAM, delivering roughly 20 hours of battery life on a single charge, according to lab tests run in Seattle by reviewer Alicia Tran. Panos Panay, who once led Surface hardware at Microsoft before departing for Amazon in 2023, is notably absent from the marketing materials, replaced by current devices chief Pavan Davuluri.

Competitor Apple Inc., headquartered in Cupertino, California, still holds an edge in raw single-core performance with its M3 chip, but Microsoft's new Copilot+ features, including live caption translation across 40 languages, feel genuinely useful rather than gimmicky. During a demo at Microsoft's campus on September 25, 2024, the translation lag was under one second when converting spoken Japanese to English captions.

Build quality remains excellent, though the 1080p webcam is disappointing at this price point, especially compared with the Dell XPS 13 reviewed last March. Storage options top out at 1 terabyte, and the entry model starts at $999.

Overall, the Surface Laptop 7 is a 9 out of 10 for professionals already inside the Microsoft ecosystem, but shoppers should wait for Black Friday discounts expected around November 29, 2024 before buying.

NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- August 14, 2024 -- Meridian BioWorks, Inc. today announced that it has acquired Calloway Diagnostics LLC, a privately held maker of rapid pathogen-detection kits based in Durham, North Carolina, for $85 million in cash and stock.

Under the terms of the agreement, Meridian BioWorks will pay $60 million upfront and up to $25 million in milestone payments tied to regulatory approvals from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The transaction is expected to close by October 1, 2024, pending customary regulatory review.

"This acquisition strengthens our diagnostics portfolio and accelerates our entry into infectious disease testing," said Dr. Elena Farrow, Chief Executive Officer of Meridian BioWorks, who founded the company in 2011 in Nashville. "Calloway's flagship product, the RapidScreen CT-9 assay, has already been used in more than 2 million tests across 40 hospital networks."

Calloway Diagnostics was founded in 2016 by Dr. Marcus Whitfield, who will join Meridian BioWorks as Senior Vice President of Diagnostics Innovation effective September 3, 2024. Whitfield stepped down as Chief Executive Officer of Calloway Diagnostics on August 14, 2024.

Meridian BioWorks, headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee, employs approximately 1,400 people and reported revenue of $410 million last year. The company's shares trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol MRBW.

Calloway Diagnostics employs 210 people and will continue operating from its Durham facility, which Meridian BioWorks plans to expand by 15 percent over the next two years.

For more information, contact Rachel Osei, Vice President of Communications, at rosei@meridianbioworks.com.
