DETROIT, Mich. — Aug 14, 2024 — Meridian Auto Group announced Wednesday that it has acquired Bellweather Components Inc., a Toledo-based supplier of braking systems, for $412 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at a press briefing at Meridian's headquarters on Woodward Avenue, is expected to close by October 1, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Meridian's chief executive officer, Rachel Ostrander, said the acquisition will strengthen the company's supply chain amid rising demand for electric vehicles. "Bellweather's expertise in regenerative braking technology fits perfectly with our EV roadmap," Ostrander told reporters. Bellweather's founder, Timothy Kessler, will join Meridian as senior vice president of engineering starting September 3, 2024, according to a statement issued by the company.

Meridian, which employs roughly 18,000 people across North America, has been expanding aggressively since 2021, when it purchased a 40 percent stake in Swedish battery maker Voltrix AB for 1.1 billion Swedish krona. Analysts at Larchmont Capital Partners in Chicago said the Bellweather deal values the smaller firm at nearly 14 times its projected 2025 earnings.

Shares of Meridian Auto Group rose 6.3 percent to $87.42 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while shares of rival automaker Draycott Motors fell 2.1 percent amid concerns over competitive pressure. Bellweather, which was founded in 1998 and employs 2,200 workers in Toledo, will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian.

Pixel Tab 3, Sunnyvale-based Google's first cellular tablet in nearly a decade, hit shelves on September 12, 2024, priced at $499 for the 128GB Wi-Fi model. I have spent three weeks with the device, and it mostly delivers on its promise of blending Android 15 with genuine productivity chops. The 11-inch OLED panel, manufactured by Samsung Display in South Korea, gets bright enough for outdoor reading, and the Tensor G4 chip handles multitasking without the stutter that plagued the 2018 Pixel Slate. Google's hardware chief, Rick Osterloh, told reporters at a briefing in Mountain View that the company designed the Tab 3 specifically to compete with Apple's iPad Air and Samsung's Galaxy Tab S9. Battery life is the standout: I got just over 11 hours of mixed video and browsing use, beating Apple's claimed 10 hours for the iPad Air. The included Pixelbook Keyboard, sold separately for $149, feels cramped for anyone with larger hands, and the stylus, oddly, is not included at all. Software support is generous, with Google promising five years of OS updates through 2029. My main complaint is the speaker array, which sounds tinny compared to the iPad Air's quad speakers. At $499, the Pixel Tab 3 undercuts Samsung's $599 Galaxy Tab S9 while offering comparable performance, making it an easy recommendation for anyone already inside the Google ecosystem. Retailers including Best Buy began accepting preorders on September 5, 2024.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

Case No. HG-24-119837

On March 11, 2024, Judge Patricia Wollman sentenced Marcus Delgado, 41, to 54 months in state prison after a jury in Oakland found him guilty of embezzlement and wire fraud in connection with his former position at Redstone Capital Partners, a private equity firm headquartered in San Francisco. Prosecutor Angela Chu of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Delgado, who served as Chief Financial Officer of Redstone Capital Partners from January 2018 until his termination in September 2022, diverted approximately $2.3 million in client funds to a shell company registered in Nevada.

The trial, held at the René C. Davidson Courthouse, began on February 5, 2024, and included testimony from forensic accountant Sarah In, who traced the transferred money to accounts controlled by Delgado's brother, Ricardo Delgado. Ricardo Delgado was not charged. Defense attorney Howard Pratt maintained that his client acted under duress from the firm's founder, Nathaniel Voss, though the jury rejected this argument.

Judge Wollman also ordered Delgado to pay restitution of $2.1 million to Redstone Capital Partners and its affected clients within five years. Delgado was taken into custody immediately following the sentencing and is scheduled to be transported to San Quentin State Prison next week. His attorney stated he intends to file an appeal with the California Court of Appeal within 60 days.

Chicago-based Meridian Foods Corp. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Dakota Grain Alliance, a regional grain processing company based in Fargo, North Dakota, for approximately $340 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by December 15, 2024, will make Meridian Foods the third-largest grain processor in the Midwest, according to CEO Rachel Ostrander. Dakota Grain Alliance, founded in 1987 by Thomas Kellerman, operates six processing facilities across North Dakota and Minnesota and reported revenue of $210 million last year. "This acquisition strengthens our supply chain and positions us to compete more directly with Cargill and Archer-Daniels-Midland," Ostrander said during a press conference at Meridian's headquarters in Chicago, Illinois. Kellerman, who will step down as Chief Executive Officer of Dakota Grain Alliance once the transaction closes, said he plans to join the board of a nonprofit agricultural foundation. Meridian Foods will fund the purchase through a combination of $200 million in cash reserves and a $140 million loan from First Prairie Bank. Shares of Meridian Foods rose 6.2 percent to $58.40 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while analysts at Morgan Stanley raised their price target to $65. The transaction still requires approval from the Federal Trade Commission, which is expected to review the deal over the next 90 days. If approved, roughly 1,200 Dakota Grain employees will transition to Meridian Foods payroll starting in January 2025.

CLEVELAND, OH — October 3, 2024 — Parkview Industrial Group, a diversified manufacturer headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, today announced it has acquired Bexley Fastener Corporation, a privately held maker of precision fasteners based in Akron, Ohio, for $142 million in cash. The transaction closed on October 1, 2024.

Under the agreement, Parkview will absorb Bexley Fastener as a wholly owned subsidiary, retaining its 310 employees and its manufacturing plant in Akron. Bexley Fastener's founder and chief executive officer, Marcus Whitfield, will step down from his role effective October 31, 2024, and will be succeeded by longtime Parkview executive Renata Alvarez, who was named President of Bexley Fastener on October 3, 2024.

"This acquisition strengthens our supply chain and positions Parkview to better serve customers in the aerospace and automotive sectors," said Douglas Kim, Chief Executive Officer of Parkview Industrial Group, during a press briefing held at the company's Cleveland headquarters. Kim added that Bexley Fastener has long been a key supplier to Parkview's automotive division and that the deal removes a layer of procurement complexity.

Parkview financed the acquisition through a combination of $90 million in existing cash reserves and a $52 million term loan arranged by First Merit Capital Partners. The company expects the deal to add approximately $38 million in annual revenue beginning in fiscal year 2025.

Parkview Industrial Group, founded in 1978 by industrialist Harold Penrose, employs roughly 4,600 people across 12 facilities in the United States and Mexico. Shares of Parkview traded up 3.2 percent following the announcement.

DENVER, Colorado — Frontier Grain Corp announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Blue Mesa Milling LLC, a privately held wheat processor based in Pueblo, Colorado, for $142 million in cash. The deal, disclosed by chief executive officer Marion Halstead during a press briefing at Frontier Grain's headquarters, marks the company's third acquisition since 2021 and expands its footprint into the Rocky Mountain corridor.

Under the terms of the agreement, Blue Mesa Milling's roughly 210 employees will remain in place, and founder Estelle Ruiz will stay on as plant director for at least eighteen months. Halstead said the transaction, expected to close on November 15, will be financed through a combination of existing cash reserves and a new credit facility arranged by Summit National Bank.

"This acquisition strengthens our supply chain and gives us direct access to high-protein wheat sourced from southern Colorado farms," Halstead told reporters. Frontier Grain, headquartered in Denver since its founding in 1998 by siblings Daniel and Priya Okafor, posted revenue of $890 million last fiscal year, a 6 percent increase over the prior period.

Shares of Frontier Grain, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker FRGN, rose 4.3 percent to $58.20 following the announcement. Analysts at Cedar Ridge Capital, including senior analyst Tomas Lindqvist, said the purchase price represented roughly 9 times Blue Mesa Milling's annual EBITDA, calling it a reasonable multiple given current commodity market conditions. The deal still requires clearance from the Federal Trade Commission, which Frontier Grain expects to receive by early December.

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY

On September 12, 2024, Judge Marion Feldt sentenced Raymond Ostroff, 47, of Newark, to 63 months in federal-equivalent custody after a jury in Newark found him guilty of wire fraud and embezzlement connected to his former role as Chief Financial Officer of Palisade Freight Corp. Prosecutor Denise Whitfield of the Essex County District Attorney's Office argued that Ostroff diverted $2.4 million from company accounts between March 2019 and November 2022, funneling the funds through a shell entity called Harborline Logistics LLC. Defense attorney Carl Mendoza contended his client had been coerced by former Palisade Freight CEO Anthony Guerra, who was charged separately last month and is scheduled for a trial hearing on October 30, 2024, before Judge Feldt at the Essex County Courthouse in Newark.

According to testimony, Ostroff was arrested on January 8, 2023, by agents of the Newark Field Office after a whistleblower, former controller Lisa Han, alerted regulators to irregular transfers. Han testified that Ostroff authorized a $410,000 wire transfer to Harborline Logistics LLC on June 14, 2021, disguised as a supplier payment. Palisade Freight Corp., headquartered in Newark, New Jersey, and a subsidiary of Meridian Holdings Group, suspended Ostroff in December 2022 and later cooperated fully with investigators.

Judge Feldt ordered restitution of $2.4 million payable to Palisade Freight Corp. within five years. Ostroff's sentence begins immediately at Northern State Correctional Facility.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Finally Gets the Basics Right

Mountain View, October 14, 2024 -- After two disappointing generations, Google's Pixel Watch 3 feels like the smartwatch the company should have shipped in 2022. I have worn the 45mm model, priced at $399.99, for three weeks in San Francisco, and it addresses nearly every complaint I had about the Pixel Watch 2.

The headline upgrade is battery life. Google claims 36 hours on a single charge, and in my testing with always-on display enabled, I consistently hit 30 hours before needing the included fast charger. The display itself is now 10% brighter at 2,000 nits, making it far more legible under direct sunlight along the Embarcadero.

Software remains the differentiator. Wear OS 5, developed jointly by Google and Samsung, powers the device, and Fitbit's loss-of-pulse detection feature, a first for the platform, could genuinely save lives for runners training alone. Sundar Pichai, Google's CEO, mentioned the feature during a Google Store event in New York on September 10, 2024, calling it "one of the most meaningful health features we've ever built."

Not everything is perfect. The watch still lacks a rotating crown, a design choice reviewers have criticized since 2022, and the $399.99 starting price undercuts the Apple Watch Series 10 by only $10, keeping Google in a tough competitive position against Apple and Samsung.

Still, for Android users deciding between the Pixel Watch 3 and the Galaxy Watch 7, this is the first Pixel Watch I'd recommend without hesitation.

Bergstrom Outdoor Gear of Bozeman, Montana is now shipping the Cascadia Trail 45 backpack, launched on March 3, 2024. Priced at $189.99, the Cascadia Trail 45 is built with 210-denier recycled ripstop nylon and features a 45-liter main compartment, a removable rain cover, and an aluminum internal frame that supports loads up to 18 kilograms. Each unit weighs 1.6 kilograms and comes in three colorways: Slate Gray, Moss Green, and Rust Orange. The pack is manufactured under contract by Highland Textile Works in Da Nang, Vietnam, a longtime supplier to Bergstrom Outdoor Gear since 2016. Company founder Elena Marsh designed the Cascadia Trail 45 after a 2019 trek through Patagonia, aiming to create a durable option for backpackers on multi-day routes. "We tested more than 40 prototypes before settling on this frame geometry," said Marsh, who serves as Chief Product Officer at Bergstrom Outdoor Gear. The backpack ships with a 5-year limited warranty and is compatible with Bergstrom's optional hydration bladder, sold separately for $24.99. Customers who order before April 15, 2024 will receive a free trekking pole set worth $35. Units are currently in stock at the company's flagship store in Bozeman and through its website, with international shipping available to Canada, the United Kingdom, and Australia. Early reviewers on the Trailhead Forum have praised the pack's ventilated back panel, though a few noted the hip belt padding feels thin on loads over 15 kilograms. Bergstrom Outdoor Gear expects to sell 12,000 units in the first year.

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solaris Grid Corp announced this morning it has acquired Pecan Street Battery Inc for $340 million in an all-cash deal. CEO Marisol Trent confirmed the acquisition will close by January 15, 2025.

2/ Pecan Street Battery, founded in 2018 by engineer Dev Okafor, builds sodium-ion storage units used by utilities across Texas. Okafor will stay on as Chief Technology Officer at Solaris Grid.

3/ Solaris Grid, headquartered in Austin, Texas, says the deal adds 1,200 employees and three manufacturing plants in Waco, Lubbock, and El Paso. Shares of Solaris Grid rose 8 percent on the NASDAQ after the announcement.

4/ Analyst Priya Chandrasekaran of Fenwick Capital called it "the biggest energy storage deal of the year," noting rival NovaCharge Systems had reportedly offered $290 million last month but was rejected.

5/ Regulators aren't done yet. The Federal Trade Commission said Thursday it will review the merger for antitrust concerns before it can be finalized.

6/ In related news, Solaris Grid's board elected former Tesla executive Hannah Reyes as Chief Financial Officer, effective March 3, 2025, replacing outgoing CFO Marcus Whitfield, who is retiring after eleven years.

7/ Meanwhile in Sacramento, about 400 workers from the union representing battery plant employees gathered outside the California State Capitol on Tuesday to demand stronger safety protections following two injuries at a Fresno facility last week.

8/ Stay tuned — we'll have more on the Solaris Grid-Pecan Street deal as the FTC review unfolds.

To: Board of Directors, Meridian Capital Partners
From: Sarah Whitfield, Chief Financial Officer
Date: March 14, 2024
Re: Acquisition of Danforth Logistics Corp.

Dear Board Members,

I am writing to formally update you on the acquisition of Danforth Logistics Corp. by Meridian Capital Partners, which closed yesterday, March 13, 2024, in Chicago, Illinois. The transaction, valued at $42 million, was finalized after four months of negotiations led by our General Counsel, Mr. Robert Alvarez.

Under the terms of the deal, Meridian acquired 100% of Danforth's outstanding shares from founder and CEO Marcus Danforth, who will remain as a consultant through September 2024. Danforth Logistics, headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, operates a fleet of 85 delivery trucks and employs approximately 210 staff across three regional warehouses.

As part of the transition, Elena Ruiz will step down from her role as Chief Operating Officer effective April 1, 2024, and will be succeeded by James Whitaker, formerly of Continental Freight Systems. Mr. Whitaker previously served as Vice President of Operations at Continental Freight Systems in Detroit, Michigan, for six years.

We anticipate this acquisition will strengthen our position against competitors such as Pinnacle Transport Group, particularly in the Midwest distribution market. Integration efforts will begin on April 15, 2024, with a joint town hall meeting scheduled for employees of both companies at the Cleveland facility.

Please let me know if you have any questions ahead of our next board meeting on March 28, 2024.

Best regards,
Sarah Whitfield
Chief Financial Officer
Meridian Capital Partners

MUNICH, March 14 - German automaker Bayerische Werke AG announced Thursday it will acquire electric vehicle battery startup VoltCore GmbH for 480 million euros, in a deal expected to close by June 2024. The acquisition, confirmed by CEO Markus Ehrlich at a press conference in Munich, marks Bayerische Werke's largest purchase in a decade. VoltCore, founded in 2018 by engineer Lena Fischer, employs 340 people at its Stuttgart facility and supplies battery cells to several European carmakers. Fischer will join Bayerische Werke as Head of Battery Innovation, according to a statement released by the company. Industry analyst Peter Wollmann of Deutsche Bank said the deal signals accelerating consolidation in the EV sector, noting that competitor Rheinmetall Motors has also explored similar acquisitions this year. Shares of Bayerische Werke rose 6 percent on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading in VoltCore's private shares was reportedly frozen pending regulatory approval. The German Federal Cartel Office said Friday it would review the transaction to ensure compliance with antitrust law before final approval. If approved, the merger would combine VoltCore's 12 patents in solid-state battery technology with Bayerische Werke's manufacturing network across Germany, Austria, and the Czech Republic. Ehrlich told reporters the company aims to produce 500,000 EV battery packs annually by 2027, positioning it against rivals Tesla and BYD in the global electric vehicle race.

The Ontario Ministry of Transportation announced on April 9, 2024 that Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria will allocate CAD 42 million to repair Highway 401 between Milton and Cambridge following a structural inspection conducted by SNC-Lavalin. The funding, approved during a cabinet meeting in Toronto, follows an inspection that found deterioration in three overpasses near Milton. Deputy Minister Renu Kulendran stated that construction will begin on June 3, 2024 and is expected to last fourteen months, affecting an estimated 190,000 daily commuters. The ministry also confirmed that Aecon Group Inc. was awarded the primary construction contract worth CAD 31 million, with work to be completed by August 2025. Minister Sarkaria met with Cambridge Mayor Jan Liggett on April 8, 2024 in Cambridge to discuss traffic mitigation measures, including temporary detours through Regional Road 24. The Ministry emphasized that safety remains the top priority, noting that a similar overpass failure in Winnipeg in 2019 caused significant public concern nationally. Local business owners, including members of the Cambridge Chamber of Commerce, expressed cautious support for the project, citing potential short-term disruptions to freight traffic along the Highway 401 corridor. The Ministry of Transportation will provide monthly progress updates beginning July 2024, and residents can submit feedback through the ministry's online portal until May 15, 2024. Premier Doug Ford praised the initiative as "critical infrastructure renewal for southern Ontario" during a press briefing at Queen's Park on April 10, 2024.

Braxton Dynamics, a mid-sized aerospace supplier headquartered in Wichita, Kansas, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday after months of declining orders from Boeing. The filing, submitted in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware, lists debts of roughly $340 million owed to creditors including First Prairie Bank and Meridian Capital Partners.

CEO Renata Alvarez told employees in an internal memo that the company would continue operations during restructuring and does not plan immediate layoffs. "We intend to emerge from this process as a leaner, more competitive supplier," Alvarez said in a statement released Wednesday. Braxton Dynamics, founded in 1987 by aerospace engineer Harold Finch, employs approximately 2,200 workers across facilities in Wichita and Tulsa, Oklahoma.

The bankruptcy comes two months after Braxton lost a $500 million contract to rival supplier Kestrel Aerostructures, based in Everett, Washington. Analysts at Fitch Ratings had downgraded Braxton's credit rating in September, citing supply chain disruptions and rising titanium costs.

Boeing spokesperson Daniel Ochoa said the company is "monitoring the situation closely" and working with alternative suppliers to avoid production delays on the 737 MAX line. A bankruptcy court hearing is scheduled for November 14 in Wilmington, Delaware, where a judge will review Braxton's proposed reorganization plan.

Meridian Capital Partners, one of Braxton's largest creditors, has reportedly expressed interest in providing $75 million in debtor-in-possession financing to keep the company afloat during proceedings.

Sonos launched the Ace headphones on June 5, 2024, priced at $449, positioning the product against Apple's AirPods Max and Bose's QuietComfort Ultra. I tested the Ace for three weeks in Austin, Texas, commuting on the MetroRapid bus line and working from a co-working space downtown. The headphones weigh 312 grams and deliver roughly 30 hours of battery life on a single charge, matching Sonos's own marketing claims almost exactly.

Sound quality is excellent, with a warm low end that outperforms the AirPods Max in bass-heavy tracks, though Bose still edges ahead in raw noise cancellation. The companion app, Sonos S2, occasionally failed to pair reliably with my iPhone 15, forcing two restarts during the review period. Patrick Spence, Sonos's chief executive officer, told Bloomberg on June 10, 2024, that the Ace represents "the company's most ambitious audio product since its founding in 2002 by John MacFarlane in Santa Barbara, California." Sonos is headquartered in Santa Barbara and competes directly with Bose Corporation, based in Framingham, Massachusetts, and Apple Inc., headquartered in Cupertino, California.

At $449, the Ace is not cheap, and the swappable ear cushions add another $49 each. Still, after three weeks I found myself reaching for them daily. For anyone already inside the Sonos ecosystem, the seamless handoff to a Sonos Arc soundbar via TV Swap is a genuinely useful trick no competitor offers yet. Recommended, with the caveat that first-generation software bugs may frustrate early adopters.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., June 4, 2024 -- Solstice Biopharma Inc. today announced that it has acquired Verdant Neuroscience Ltd., a Dublin-based clinical-stage biotech focused on treatments for Parkinson's disease, for $410 million in cash and stock. The deal is expected to close by August 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Under the terms of the agreement, Solstice will pay Verdant shareholders $18.50 per share, a 42 percent premium over Verdant's closing price on the Nasdaq on June 3. Verdant's lead compound, a small-molecule therapy called VRD-207, is currently in Phase 2 trials across 14 sites in the United States and Ireland.

"This acquisition strengthens our neuroscience pipeline and positions Solstice as a leader in neurodegenerative disease research," said Dr. Priya Ramaswamy, Chief Executive Officer of Solstice Biopharma, in a statement from the company's headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

Verdant was founded in 2016 by Dr. Owen Fitzgerald, who will join Solstice as Senior Vice President of Neuroscience Research effective September 1, 2024. Dr. Fitzgerald previously served as Verdant's Chief Scientific Officer for eight years.

Solstice's board of directors approved the transaction on May 30, 2024. The company expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive to earnings, adding approximately $60 million in annual revenue. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners, including senior analyst Thomas Ng, called the move "a bold but well-timed bet on the neurodegenerative disease market."

Solstice shares rose 6 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, closing at $94.20.

Pixel Fold 2 Review: Google's Second Attempt Finally Sticks

Mountain View, June 12, 2024 -- Google unveiled the Pixel Fold 2 at its I/O campus event last month, and after three weeks of daily use, I can say it corrects nearly every complaint I had about the original 2023 model. The $1,899 device, manufactured in partnership with supplier BOE Technology Group in Chengdu, China, features a 7.9-inch inner display with a nearly invisible crease, an improvement Google's hardware chief Rick Osterloh called "the result of 400 engineering changes" during his keynote.

I tested the phone in San Francisco and on a short trip to Austin, Texas, running Android 15 the entire time. Battery life is the standout upgrade: the 4,900 mAh cell comfortably lasted 14 hours of mixed use, up from roughly 9 hours on last year's unit. The Tensor G4 chip, co-developed with Samsung, handles multitasking well, though it still trails Apple's A17 Pro in raw benchmark scores by about 18 percent.

Google acquired Fitbit back in 2021, and that lineage shows here: the Pixel Fold 2 integrates sleep-tracking features directly into the cover screen, a first for the lineup. Competitor Samsung, maker of the Galaxy Z Fold 6, remains the category leader by shipment volume, but Google's software polish narrows the gap.

Minor gripes: the $1,899 price undercuts Samsung's flagship by only $100, and the included 30-watt charger feels stingy in 2024. Still, for anyone burned by the 2023 original, this is the foldable that finally justifies the price. I'm giving it 4 out of 5 stars.

Ilse Brandt (born 14 March 1952 in Leipzig, East Germany) is a German biochemist known for her research on enzyme kinetics. She earned her doctorate from Humboldt University of Berlin in 1978 and joined the Max Planck Institute for Biophysical Chemistry in Göttingen as a research fellow that same year. In 1985, Brandt was appointed Head of the Enzymology Division at the institute, a position she held for over two decades. Her most cited work, published in the journal Nature in 1991, described the crystallographic structure of the enzyme aspartate transcarbamoylase, advancing understanding of allosteric regulation. Brandt became a naturalized citizen of the United States in 1994 while conducting a two-year sabbatical at Stanford University, though she retained her German citizenship as well. In 2003, she left the Max Planck Institute to found BioKinetix GmbH, a biotechnology company headquartered in Munich that develops diagnostic assays for metabolic disorders. The company was acquired by Roche Holding AG in 2011 for an undisclosed sum, after which Brandt served as a scientific advisor to Roche until her retirement in 2016. She married fellow chemist Werner Faust in 1980; their daughter, Dr. Petra Faust-Brandt, is now a professor of molecular biology at ETH Zurich. In 2009, Brandt received the Leibniz Prize from the German Research Foundation in Bonn for her contributions to structural biochemistry. She currently resides in Göttingen, where she continues to lecture occasionally at the University of Göttingen.

input: Panasonic unveiled its latest home robotics product, the Panasonic HomeGuard S3, at a press event in Osaka, Japan on March 14, 2024. Priced at $899, the HomeGuard S3 is a refurbished unit built from returned first-generation models that failed initial quality checks last year. Company spokesperson Naomi Fujimoto, who serves as Senior Product Manager at Panasonic, demonstrated the device's new obstacle-avoidance system, which uses LIDAR sensors and a proprietary chemical coating called PolyGuard-7 to resist dust buildup. Fujimoto claimed the HomeGuard S3 reduces cleaning time by 40 percent compared to its predecessor. Analysts from Nomura Research Institute, including senior analyst Kenji Watanabe, attended the demonstration and noted that Panasonic faces stiff competition from iRobot and Xiaomi in the home robotics market. Watanabe pointed out that Xiaomi's Mi Robot Vacuum X10 undercuts the HomeGuard S3 by roughly $300, raising questions about whether Panasonic's refurbished pricing strategy will succeed. Despite the competitive pressure, early reviewers on the tech site Engadget Japan gave the HomeGuard S3 a score of 8.2 out of 10, praising its battery life of six hours per charge. Panasonic plans to begin shipping the HomeGuard S3 to retailers across Japan on April 1, 2024, with a wider Southeast Asia rollout expected later in the year. For consumers weighing a $899 refurbished robot against a cheaper new competitor, the HomeGuard S3 offers solid engineering but an uncertain value proposition.

BOSTON, MA — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced on March 14, 2024 the results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating vedafolimab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Arclight Therapeutics for the treatment of relapsed multiple myeloma. The study, led by Dr. Priya Nakamura, enrolled 214 patients across 12 sites in the United States and Germany between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants received either vedafolimab plus dexamethasone or a placebo plus dexamethasone every 21 days. According to results published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, 61 percent of patients in the treatment arm achieved a partial or complete response, compared with 27 percent in the placebo group. The most common adverse events included neutropenia, reported in 34 percent of patients, and mild infusion-related reactions in 18 percent. Dr. Nakamura stated that the findings support advancement to a Phase 3 trial, which Arclight Therapeutics plans to initiate at facilities in Boston and Munich by early 2025. Arclight Therapeutics, founded in 2018 by former Pfizer executive Daniel Osei, raised $85 million in Series C funding last year to support late-stage development of vedafolimab. The company's chief medical officer, Dr. Helena Vogt, presented the data at the American Society of Hematology annual meeting held in San Diego on December 9, 2023. Analysts at Jefferies noted that a successful Phase 3 outcome could position vedafolimab as a $2 billion annual revenue product, intensifying competition with Bristol Myers Squibb's existing myeloma therapies. The trial was funded in part by a $12 million grant from the National Institutes of Health.

input: DETROIT, Michigan -- Ferrous Dynamics Corp., a mid-sized auto-parts supplier headquartered in Detroit, announced on Tuesday, June 11, 2024, that it has acquired Rollhaus Bearings GmbH, a German precision-bearing maker based in Stuttgart, for $412 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by September 30, 2024, marks Ferrous Dynamics' third acquisition since 2020 and its first move into the European market. CEO Marlene Kowalczyk said the acquisition would strengthen the company's supply chain for electric-vehicle drivetrains and help it compete more directly with Bosch and ZF Friedrichshafen. Rollhaus Bearings, founded in 1978 by engineer Dieter Hausmann, employs roughly 1,400 workers across two plants in Stuttgart and Brno. Under the agreement, Rollhaus will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Ferrous Dynamics and retain its current management team, led by managing director Anke Voss. Shares of Ferrous Dynamics rose 6.8 percent to $58.20 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while analysts at Whitfield Capital Partners raised their price target to $65. The transaction, first reported by Reuters, still requires approval from German antitrust regulators and is subject to a customary 90-day review period. Kowalczyk added that no layoffs are planned and that Voss will join Ferrous Dynamics' executive committee as Senior Vice President of European Operations effective October 1, 2024. Analyst Priya Raman of Whitfield Capital called the deal "a smart, defensively priced bet on EV supply chains."

2/ ClearPath Analytics was founded in 2019 by Marcus Iwu, who previously worked as a Senior Engineer at Tesla. Marcus will join Solera as Vice President of Data Science starting July 1, 2024, reporting directly to Rachel Ostrander.

6/ Congrats to the whole ClearPath team on this milestone!

Fjallraven Kanken Classic 16L Backpack — Ox Red, sold by Backcountry Gear Co. of Boulder, Colorado, is now available for $89.95, marking a $10 discount off the original $99.95 price through November 30, 2024. This brand-new, never-used backpack features Vinylon F fabric, a design originally developed by Fjallraven in Sweden back in 1978. The Kanken Classic includes two front pockets, padded shoulder straps, and a signature Fox logo patch. Backcountry Gear Co. purchased its current inventory of 500 units directly from Fjallraven's distributor, Nordic Outdoor Supply AB, in a deal finalized on September 12, 2024, for a total of $32,000. Customers who order before 5:00 PM MST on any business day will receive free shipping via FedEx Ground, with delivery typically completed within 3 to 5 business days across the continental United States. Reviewer Sarah Kessler, a hiking guide based in Denver, Colorado, rated the bag 5 stars, writing, "I've used this Kanken on trails throughout Rocky Mountain National Park for two years and it still looks new." The backpack is available in 12 colorways, including Ox Red, Frost Green, and Navy. Backcountry Gear Co., founded in 2011 by outdoor enthusiast Mark Delaney, operates two retail locations in Boulder and one in Fort Collins, competing directly with REI for regional market share.

The Ohio Department of Transportation announced on May 6, 2024 that it will invest $340 million to repair the Brent Spence Bridge connecting Cincinnati to Covington, Kentucky. Director Jack Marchbanks stated the project, formally named the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor Project, will begin construction on June 17, 2024 and is expected to conclude by December 2029. The funding combines $80 million in state bonds with $260 million provided by the Federal Highway Administration under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. Governor Mike DeWine praised the agreement, noting that the bridge carries roughly 160,000 vehicles daily and has been rated functionally obsolete since 2015. Kentucky Transportation Cabinet Secretary Jim Gray joined DeWine at a press conference held at the Duke Energy Convention Center in Cincinnati to confirm the two states' cooperation. Approximately 1,200 construction jobs are projected to be created over the five-year timeline, according to ODOT spokesperson Breanna Badanes. The agency also announced that Kokosing Construction Company, headquartered in Fredericktown, Ohio, has been selected as the lead contractor following a competitive bidding process completed in March 2024. Local officials, including Cincinnati Mayor Aftab Pureval, welcomed the announcement, though several residents attended a demonstration outside City Hall on May 8, 2024 to protest anticipated traffic disruptions. The Ohio-Kentucky Metropolitan Transportation Council will oversee quarterly progress reviews starting in September 2024 to ensure the project remains on schedule and within budget.

CAMBRIDGE, MA — October 14, 2024 — Solara Biotics Inc., a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, announced today that it has acquired Northgate Diagnostics LLC, a privately held maker of rapid diagnostic assays based in Raleigh, North Carolina, for approximately $92 million in cash and stock.

The transaction, which closed on October 11, 2024, adds Northgate's flagship product, the ClearPath HPV Assay, to Solara's portfolio of women's health diagnostics. Dr. Elena Marsh, Chief Executive Officer of Solara Biotics, said the acquisition strengthens the company's position against competitor Vantix Health Corp. "Northgate's technology fills a critical gap in our pipeline," Marsh said during a press briefing in Boston on October 14, 2024.

As part of the deal, Northgate's founder and former CEO, Raymond Okafor, will join Solara as Senior Vice President of Diagnostics, effective November 1, 2024. Okafor founded Northgate Diagnostics in 2016 and grew the company to 140 employees before the sale.

Solara also disclosed that it will retain Northgate's manufacturing facility in Raleigh, which employs 85 people, and expects the deal to add $40 million in annual revenue. The company's shares rose 6 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement.

Solara Biotics is scheduled to report its third-quarter financial results on November 7, 2024. The company was founded in 2011 by Dr. Elena Marsh and is a member of the Massachusetts Biotechnology Council.

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY
Case No. ESX-L-004417-24

On March 6, 2024, Judge Patricia Hollowell sentenced Marcus Deveraux, 41, of Newark, New Jersey, to seven years in state prison after a jury convicted him of aggravated arson at the Ironbound Storage Facility on Ferry Street. Prosecutor Angela Nkemelu of the Essex County District Attorney's Office argued that Deveraux, a former employee of Ferry Street Logistics, deliberately set fire to the warehouse on the night of November 12, 2023, causing an estimated $2.3 million in damages and injuring firefighter Sean Boyle, who suffered smoke inhalation while battling the blaze.

During the two-week trial held at the Essex County Courthouse in Newark, defense attorney Robert Feldstein maintained that his client was at a family gathering in Paterson at the time of the fire. Surveillance footage, however, placed Deveraux's gray Ford pickup truck near the facility at approximately 11:40 p.m.

Deveraux was arrested on December 3, 2023, by detectives of the Newark Police Department on charges of arson and reckless endangerment. He was formally indicted on January 9, 2024, by a grand jury convened under Adjudicator Hollowell.

Following the sentencing, Ferry Street Logistics issued a statement confirming it had filed an insurance claim with Garden State Mutual for $2.1 million. The company's CEO, Diane Whitfield, said the firm plans to rebuild the facility by early 2025.

Pixelbook Labs, a Portland-based startup founded by former Intel engineer Marcus Whitfield, unveiled the Vantage 7 wireless earbuds on September 12, 2024, promising 30 hours of battery life and active noise cancellation for $179. I tested a review unit for two weeks before writing this piece for CircuitDaily.

The Vantage 7 impresses in several ways. Sound quality is rich, especially in the midrange, and the companion app, built for both iOS and Android, offers granular EQ controls rarely seen at this price. Battery claims held up in my tests, hitting roughly 28 hours with the case. At $179, they undercut the Sony WF-1000XM5, which retails for $299, making them a genuine competitor in the mid-range earbud market.

However, call quality disappointed. On a windy afternoon in Portland, my colleague Elena Ruiz could barely hear me during a fifteen-minute call. Pixelbook Labs says a firmware update, planned for October 2024, should address microphone tuning.

Whitfield told me in an interview at the company's Portland office that Pixelbook Labs plans to ship 500,000 units globally by early 2025, with retail partner Best Buy carrying the product starting October 1, 2024. The company, which employs 42 people, raised $12 million in a Series A round led by Cascade Ventures last March.

Overall, the Vantage 7 is a strong value pick despite its call-quality flaw, and I'd recommend it to budget-conscious buyers willing to wait for the firmware fix.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Finally Gets It Right

On October 4, 2024, Google released the Pixel Watch 3 alongside the Pixel 9 lineup, and after three weeks of daily use in San Francisco, I can say it is the company's most polished wearable yet. Priced at $349 for the 41mm model, the watch pairs a brighter 2,000-nit display with a redesigned Wear OS 5 interface that finally feels fast on the Snapdragon W5 chip.

Google's hardware chief, Rick Osterloh, told reporters at a briefing in Mountain View that the team focused heavily on battery life after complaints about the Pixel Watch 2. In my testing, the 41mm unit lasted about 26 hours with the always-on display enabled, a noticeable improvement of roughly 20 percent over last year's model.

The standout new feature is Loss of Pulse Detection, developed with input from cardiologists at Stanford Health Care, which can automatically call emergency services if it detects your heart has stopped. Fitbit, now fully absorbed into Google since the $2.1 billion acquisition finalized in 2021, provides the fitness-tracking backbone, including updated running form coaching.

Competitors haven't stood still. Samsung's Galaxy Watch 7 and Apple's Watch Series 10 both remain strong rivals, and Apple still commands a larger share of the smartwatch market overall. Still, for Android users, the Pixel Watch 3 is the easiest recommendation Google has ever made, minor gripes about third-party band pricing aside.

Denver-based Meridian Foods Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Boulder Crest Bakery, a regional artisan bread maker, for $42 million in cash. The deal, disclosed at Meridian's headquarters in Denver, Colorado, is expected to close by January 15, 2025, pending regulatory approval. Meridian's chief executive officer, Rachel Simmons, said the acquisition would expand the company's presence in the Rocky Mountain region and add three manufacturing plants in Colorado and Wyoming. "Boulder Crest Bakery has built a loyal following over its 28 years in business, and we intend to preserve that legacy," Simmons told reporters during a press briefing on Wednesday. Boulder Crest Bakery was founded in 1996 by Thomas Nolan, who will remain as a consultant through the transition period. The bakery currently employs 310 workers across its facilities in Fort Collins and Cheyenne. Meridian Foods, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker MFI, reported quarterly revenue of $310 million last month, up 6 percent from the same period a year earlier. Analysts at Sterling Capital Partners said the acquisition values Boulder Crest at roughly 1.8 times annual sales, a premium they described as reasonable given the bakery's strong brand loyalty in the Midwest and Mountain West markets. Shares of Meridian Foods rose 4 percent to $57.30 following the announcement, while competitor GrainWorks Holdings saw its stock dip slightly amid concerns over increased competition.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass. — October 3, 2024 — Nimbus Therapeutics, a clinical-stage biotechnology company, announced today that it has acquired Solvent Bio, a Boston-based startup specializing in mRNA delivery systems, for approximately $340 million in cash and stock.

Under the agreement, Nimbus Therapeutics will absorb Solvent Bio's 62 employees and its proprietary lipid nanoparticle platform, known as LipidCore. The deal is expected to close by December 15, 2024, pending regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission.

"This acquisition strengthens our pipeline for treating cystic fibrosis and positions us as a leader in nucleic acid therapeutics," said Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer of Nimbus Therapeutics, during a press briefing held at the company's headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

Solvent Bio was founded in 2019 by Dr. Marcus Chen, who will join Nimbus Therapeutics as Chief Scientific Officer effective November 1, 2024. Dr. Chen previously served as a senior researcher at Moderna.

Nimbus Therapeutics, which employs roughly 410 people, reported revenue of $128 million in its most recent fiscal year. The company is publicly traded on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol NMBT. Shares rose 4.7 percent following the announcement.

The combined entity will operate a new research facility in Somerville, Massachusetts, slated to open in the first quarter of 2025, adding an estimated 150 jobs to the region.

Analysts at Jefferies Group described the transaction as a strategic move to counter competition from Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, a rival in the RNA therapeutics space.

CHICAGO, Nov. 14 -- Archer Grain Systems Inc. agreed to acquire Prairie Silo Technologies LLC for $412 million in cash, the companies announced Tuesday, in a deal expected to close by March 2025. The acquisition, Archer's largest since 2019, will bring Prairie Silo's automated grain-storage software under Archer's industrial division based in Chicago, Illinois. Prairie Silo, founded in 2011 by engineer Renata Osei, employs 340 people at its headquarters in Ames, Iowa. Osei will join Archer as Senior Vice President of Digital Agriculture, reporting to Chief Executive Officer Martin Voss, who has led Archer since 2018. "This combination lets us serve farmers from planting to storage," Voss said during a press call from Archer's Chicago headquarters. Shares of Archer rose 6.2 percent to $88.40 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume reached 3.1 million shares, well above the daily average. Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners called the price "a full but justified premium," noting Prairie Silo's revenue grew 41 percent last year to $96 million. Archer will fund the purchase through a combination of $250 million in cash reserves and a new credit facility arranged by Fentress Bank. The deal still requires clearance from the Federal Trade Commission, which Archer expects within 90 days. Prairie Silo's other co-founder, Daniel Kwarteng, will depart the company once the transaction closes, according to a regulatory filing submitted Tuesday afternoon.

Priced at $189.00, this refurbished-condition unit was originally part of a limited pilot batch manufactured in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, and later returned unused by a corporate buyer, allowing Fieldstock Outfitters to offer it at a reduced rate. The bag features a 22-liter main compartment, a padded 16-inch laptop sleeve, and a weatherproof recycled nylon shell rated for 3 millimeters of hydrostatic resistance. Bellroy, founded in 2010 in Melbourne, Australia, has built a reputation for minimalist design, and the Venture line was developed under the direction of design lead Ana Kovac, who joined the company in March 2019. Fieldstock Outfitters, a retailer headquartered in Portland, Oregon, acquired a small closeout batch of these backpacks directly from Bellroy's Melbourne warehouse in October 2024 for an undisclosed sum. Warranty coverage is limited to 90 days due to the refurbished condition.

Anker's newest charging accessory, the Anker 737 Power Bank, went on sale on March 14, 2024, at retailers across the United States for $99.99. I bought a unit through Best Buy in Austin, Texas, and spent two weeks testing it before writing this review. The device, manufactured by Anker Innovations Limited and headquartered in Shenzhen, China, packs a 24,000mAh battery and a 140W USB-C port that can fast-charge a MacBook Pro from 0 to 50 percent in about 30 minutes. Company spokesperson Wendy Zhao said in an email on March 20, 2024, that the built-in digital display was designed after customer feedback collected through the Anker mobile app. In hands-on use, the power bank charged an iPhone 15 Pro three full times before needing a recharge itself, a noticeable improvement over the older Anker 737 model released in 2022. One caveat: at 1.4 pounds, it is noticeably heavier than the Belkin BoostCharge Pro, a direct competitor to Anker in the portable power segment. Anker Innovations, founded by Steven Yang in 2011, has grown into one of the largest consumer electronics exporters in China, and this launch follows the company's $50 million investment announced last year to expand its research lab in San Jose, California. For frequent travelers who need to keep a laptop and phone alive on a transcontinental flight, the Anker 737 Power Bank is, despite its weight, an easy recommendation.

CHICAGO, Illinois — Nov 14, 2023 — Midwest Grain Holdings Inc. announced Tuesday that it has agreed to acquire Prairie Millworks LLC, a privately held flour and feed producer based in Peoria, Illinois, for $412 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by Jan 31, 2024, would make Midwest Grain the third-largest grain processor in the United States, according to chief executive officer Ellen Marsh.

Under the terms of the agreement, Midwest Grain will pay $310 million in cash and issue roughly 2.6 million new shares valued at $102 million to Prairie Millworks shareholders, led by founder Harold Voss. Voss, who started the company in Peoria in 1987, will join Midwest Grain's board as a senior advisor beginning Feb 1, 2024.

"This acquisition strengthens our supply chain across the Midwest and adds nearly 900 employees to our workforce," Marsh said during a call with analysts in Chicago. Shares of Midwest Grain, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker MWGN, rose 6.3 percent to $58.40 following the announcement.

Analysts at Cedar Point Capital, a Minneapolis-based investment firm, said the merger could pressure competitor Heartland Agri Corp, whose stock fell 2.1 percent on Tuesday. Heartland, headquartered in Des Moines, Iowa, has not yet issued a statement.

Regulatory approval from the Federal Trade Commission is still pending, though Marsh expressed confidence the transaction would clear review without significant delay.

Marguerite Ilena Voss (born 14 March 1937 in Rotterdam, Netherlands) was a Dutch-American structural engineer best known for designing the cantilevered roof of the Halden Transit Terminal in Portland, Oregon. Voss emigrated with her family to the United States in 1951 and became a naturalized citizen in 1959. She earned a degree in civil engineering from the University of Michigan in 1961 and joined Kessler & Bram Associates in Chicago that same year as a junior engineer.

In 1968 Voss left Kessler & Bram to co-found Voss-Halloran Structural Group with her colleague Peter Halloran, headquartered in Portland, Oregon. The firm grew rapidly, and by 1975 it employed more than 200 engineers across three offices. Voss served as Chief Engineer of Voss-Halloran until her retirement in 1994.

Her most celebrated work, the Halden Transit Terminal, opened on 9 May 1979 and was praised for its 45-meter unsupported steel span. In 1981 Voss received the Marchetti Prize for Structural Innovation, awarded by the International Union of Structural Engineers in Geneva, Switzerland.

Voss married fellow engineer Peter Halloran in 1970; the couple had one son, Thomas Halloran, born in 1973 in Portland. Voss-Halloran Structural Group was acquired by the multinational firm Renmark Engineering in 2003 for an undisclosed sum, becoming a subsidiary of Renmark. Marguerite Voss died on 2 November 2011 in Portland, Oregon, at the age of 74.

CHARLOTTE, N.C. — Duke Energy Corp. agreed on Tuesday to acquire Piedmont Solar Holdings LLC for $412 million, the companies announced at a joint press conference in Charlotte. The deal, expected to close by January 15, 2025, will give Duke Energy control of 18 solar farms across North Carolina and South Carolina, adding roughly 900 megawatts of generation capacity.

Duke Energy Chief Executive Officer Harold Weston said the acquisition reflects the utility's push toward renewable energy. "This is the largest solar transaction in our company's history," Weston told reporters. Piedmont Solar founder and President Maria Colston will join Duke Energy as Senior Vice President of Renewable Operations, effective February 1, 2025.

The announcement sent Duke Energy shares up 3.2 percent on the New York Stock Exchange, closing at $104.87. Analysts at Morgan Stanley called the price "fair value," noting Piedmont Solar generated $87 million in revenue last year.

Piedmont Solar, founded in 2011 by Colston in Asheville, North Carolina, employs 240 people and supplies power to more than 60,000 households. The company will operate as a wholly owned subsidiary of Duke Energy under the Piedmont Solar name for at least two years, according to the merger agreement filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Not everyone welcomed the news. The Carolina Ratepayers Alliance, a consumer advocacy group, warned that consolidation could raise electricity prices for residential customers. "We've seen this pattern before," said spokesperson Denise Ruiz. Duke Energy, headquartered in Charlotte, currently serves 8.2 million customers across six states.

MUNICH, Germany — Siemens Energy AG announced Tuesday it will acquire Nordic Turbine Systems, a Danish wind-turbine component maker, for 740 million euros in a deal expected to close by March 2025. The acquisition, disclosed at a press conference in Munich, marks Siemens Energy's largest purchase since 2021 and comes as the German conglomerate seeks to expand its renewable energy portfolio amid growing competition from Vestas Wind Systems and General Electric.

CEO Christian Bruch said the deal would strengthen Siemens Energy's supply chain for offshore wind projects across the North Sea. "Nordic Turbine Systems brings engineering talent and manufacturing capacity we simply don't have in-house," Bruch told reporters. Nordic Turbine Systems, headquartered in Aarhus, Denmark, was founded in 2009 by engineer Lars Holm and employs roughly 1,200 workers.

Under the agreement, Holm will join Siemens Energy's executive board as Chief Innovation Officer starting January 15, 2025, while retaining a seat on Nordic Turbine Systems' advisory board. Shareholders of Nordic Turbine Systems will receive a combination of cash and Siemens Energy stock, according to a filing with the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority.

Analysts at Deutsche Bank estimated the deal values Nordic Turbine Systems at roughly 12 times its 2023 earnings. Shares of Siemens Energy rose 4.3 percent on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Vestas shares dipped 1.8 percent. The transaction still requires approval from European Union antitrust regulators, a process expected to take up to six months.

CLEVELAND, Ohio — Rocket Mortgage announced Tuesday it will acquire fintech startup PayLume Inc. for $340 million in a deal expected to close by January 15, 2025. The acquisition, disclosed by CEO Bill Emerson at a press conference at the company's Cleveland headquarters, will fold PayLume's 210 employees into Rocket Mortgage's digital lending division. PayLume, founded in 2019 by Priya Nandakumar, built software that helps homebuyers pre-qualify for loans within minutes. Nandakumar will join Rocket Mortgage as Senior Vice President of Product Innovation starting December 1, 2024, according to a company statement. "This partnership accelerates our mission to make homeownership simpler for millions of Americans," Emerson said. Analysts at Morningstar noted the deal positions Rocket Mortgage to compete more directly with rival United Wholesale Mortgage, headquartered in Pontiac, Michigan. Shares of Rocket Companies, the parent of Rocket Mortgage, rose 4.3 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement, closing at $12.86. PayLume, based in Austin, Texas, had raised $58 million in venture funding since its founding, backed by investors including Silverline Capital. The company employs roughly 210 people across offices in Austin and Denver. Rocket Mortgage said it does not anticipate layoffs as part of the integration, though two senior PayLume executives, including CFO Daniel Whitfield, are expected to depart once the transaction closes. Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Finally Gets the Basics Right

By Renata Cole, October 14, 2024

After two weeks wearing the Pixel Watch 3 around Austin, Texas, I'm convinced Google has closed most of the gap with the Apple Watch Series 9. The 45mm model, priced at $399, ships with a brighter 2,000-nit display and a noticeably lighter aluminum case compared to the original Pixel Watch that Google launched in 2022.

Google, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc., built the new Loss of Pulse Detection feature in partnership with the American Heart Association, and it worked reliably during a treadmill test at my gym in Austin on October 9, 2024. Battery life stretched to roughly 36 hours with the always-on display enabled, a real improvement over the 24 hours Fitbit-branded Pixel Watch 2 managed last year.

Rick Osterloh, Senior Vice President of Devices and Services at Google, said in a briefing that the Pixel Watch 3 was designed to compete directly with Samsung's Galaxy Watch 7, which debuted in July 2024. Samsung, headquartered in Suwon, South Korea, has sold over 4 million units of the Galaxy Watch 7 globally, according to analysts at Counterpoint Research.

My only complaint: the $399 price tag puts it uncomfortably close to the $429 Apple Watch, and Wear OS 5 still lacks the third-party app polish of watchOS. Still, for Android users in the United States, this is the best Google smartwatch yet, and it earned a Best Wearable nod at the Engadget Awards in San Francisco last month.

job title: Senior Vice President of Devices and Services

input: Manchester City midfielder Rodri scored twice as the reigning champions beat Aston Villa 3-1 at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, extending their unbeaten Premier League run to eleven matches. Manager Pep Guardiola praised his side's composure after Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins had leveled the score in the 38th minute. Rodri restored City's lead just before halftime with a low finish from the edge of the box, then sealed the win with a penalty in the 71st minute after Villa defender Ezri Konsa was penalized for a handball. Erling Haaland opened the scoring for City in the 12th minute, his 19th goal of the season, and now leads the Premier League scoring charts with nineteen goals. Aston Villa manager Unai Emery said his team "competed well but lacked the final touch in key moments." The victory moves Manchester City to 58 points, three points behind league leaders Liverpool, who defeated Everton 2-0 earlier on Saturday at Anfield. City's next fixture is against Chelsea on Wednesday at Stamford Bridge in the League Cup quarterfinal. Villa, meanwhile, will host Brighton on 25 January at Villa Park, hoping to bounce back from their third defeat in five league games. Attendance at the Etihad Stadium was announced at 53,412, one of the highest league gates of the season. City captain Kyle Walker was substituted in the second half after a minor knee knock but is expected to be fit for the Chelsea match.

MANCHESTER, England -- October 14, 2023 -- Fulton City FC edged Riverside United 2-1 at Etihad Park on Saturday, moving into second place in the Northern Premier League table. Striker Marcus Ondiba scored twice in the second half, including a stoppage-time winner in the 91st minute, after Riverside United's Declan Foy had opened the scoring with a free kick in the 23rd minute. The victory extended Fulton City's unbeaten run to eight matches. Head coach Elena Vasquez praised her squad's resilience after the match, telling reporters, "We showed real character tonight, and Marcus deserved that goal after the season he's had." Ondiba, a 26-year-old Kenyan international who joined Fulton City from Dortmund Reserves for approximately 3.2 million pounds in July 2022, has now scored 11 goals in 14 appearances this season. Riverside United manager Paul Hartnett criticized the referee's decision not to award a late penalty when defender Sam Okafor appeared to be fouled inside the box. Fulton City FC, founded in 1904 and based in Manchester, will next travel to Leeds on October 21, 2023 to face Leeds Forge in the League Cup quarterfinal. Approximately 24,500 fans attended Saturday's match at Etihad Park, which has a capacity of 28,000. The result lifted Fulton City to 22 points from 11 matches, three points behind league leaders Camden Athletic.

The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday, April 9, 2024, that it will allocate 120 million euros to upgrade regional rail lines connecting Leiden and Utrecht. Minister Femke Bakker stated during a press briefing in The Hague that the funding, drawn from the National Infrastructure Fund, will finance the replacement of aging signal systems operated by NS, the Dutch national railway company. "This investment will reduce delays by 30 percent within two years," Bakker said. The project, named Rail Renewal 2026, is expected to begin construction on June 1, 2024, and conclude by December 2026. NS spokesperson Willem de Groot confirmed that ProRail, the infrastructure subsidiary responsible for track maintenance, will oversee daily operations alongside contractor VolkerWessels. The Ministry also disclosed that 45 million euros of the total budget will be transferred to VolkerWessels upon completion of the first construction phase, expected in early 2025. Opposition lawmaker Sanne Vermeer criticized the timeline as overly optimistic, noting that a similar 2019 upgrade near Rotterdam was delayed by eighteen months. Bakker responded that lessons from that delay, caused partly by unexpected asbestos removal at Rotterdam Centraal, have been incorporated into the new engineering plans. The Ministry expects roughly 60,000 daily commuters to benefit once the upgraded line opens. Bakker will meet with regional council representatives in Utrecht on April 22, 2024, to discuss further coordination.

MANCHESTER, England -- October 14, 2024 -- Manchester United secured a 2-1 win over Liverpool at Old Trafford on Saturday, snapping a four-match winless streak under interim manager Ruud van Nistelrooy. Marcus Rashford opened the scoring in the 23rd minute, curling a left-footed shot past goalkeeper Alisson Becker. Liverpool equalized through Mohamed Salah in the 41st minute, converting a penalty after a foul by Diogo Dalot inside the box. The decisive goal came in the 78th minute when substitute Alejandro Garnacho headed home a corner delivered by Bruno Fernandes, sending the crowd of 73,412 into raptures.

Van Nistelrooy, appointed on an interim basis last week after Erik ten Hag was dismissed, praised his players' resilience. "We showed character today, and that's exactly what this club needs right now," he told reporters at a post-match press conference. Liverpool manager Arne Slot expressed frustration over the officiating, noting that referee Michael Oliver missed a potential second penalty in stoppage time.

The victory lifts Manchester United to ninth place in the Premier League table with 12 points from eight matches, while Liverpool remains second on 19 points. Manchester United's next fixture is away at Chelsea on October 20, 2024, at Stamford Bridge. The Football Association confirmed no disciplinary action would be taken against either club following the match.

DETROIT, Mich. — Marchetti Industrial Group announced Tuesday it has acquired Blackstone Fasteners Inc. for $412 million, a deal expected to close by December 15, 2024. The agreement, disclosed at a press conference at the Renaissance Center, marks Marchetti's largest purchase since its founding in 1987 by engineer Vittorio Marchetti.

CEO Lorraine Duffy, who has led Marchetti Industrial Group since 2019, said the acquisition will strengthen the company's supply chain across North America. "Blackstone Fasteners brings 38 manufacturing plants and roughly 2,600 employees into our network," Duffy told reporters. Blackstone, headquartered in Toledo, Ohio, has supplied bolts and industrial fasteners to automakers including Ford Motor Company for over three decades.

Analysts at Cortland Capital Partners estimate the merged entity will generate $3.1 billion in annual revenue. Shares of Marchetti Industrial Group rose 6.4 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while Blackstone's private equity owner, Redwood Bridge Capital, confirmed it will exit its stake entirely.

The deal still requires clearance from the Federal Trade Commission, which is expected to review the transaction over the next 90 days. Duffy added that Blackstone's chief executive, Harold Nunez, will join Marchetti's board of directors starting January 6, 2025. Nunez has served as Blackstone's CEO since 2016.

Union representatives from the United Auto Workers said Wednesday they would monitor the transition closely, citing concerns about potential layoffs at two Ohio plants.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tirbanamide, an investigational chemical compound targeting IL-23 signaling, for treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. The study, led by Dr. Elena Vasquez, enrolled 214 adult patients across 12 sites in the United States and Canada between June 2022 and September 2023. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of tirbanamide every four weeks achieved a 78 percent reduction in Psoriasis Area and Severity Index scores at week 16, compared to 22 percent among those given placebo. Dr. Vasquez presented the findings on March 12, 2024 at the American Academy of Dermatology conference in San Diego, California. "These results exceeded our expectations," she said during a press briefing attended by representatives from Novara Therapeutics, the biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts that funded the trial. Novara Therapeutics was founded in 2015 by Dr. Marcus Chen, who currently serves as Chief Executive Officer. The company's stock rose 14 percent following the announcement. Novara plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the fourth quarter of 2024, with a potential launch in early 2025 if approved. Common adverse events included mild headache and nasopharyngitis, reported in fewer than 9 percent of patients; no serious safety signals emerged. Analysts at Kessler Bloom Partners estimate the drug could generate 1.2 billion dollars in annual revenue by 2028 if approved, positioning it as a competitor to AbbVie's Skyrizi. Full trial data will be published in The New England Journal of Medicine later this year.

input: BOSTON, MA — March 12, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced today the results of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolvexamab, an experimental monoclonal antibody developed by Cambridge-based biotechnology company Arcadia Therapeutics, for treatment of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis. The 18-month study, led by Dr. Priya Nathan and published in The New England Journal of Medicine, enrolled 342 patients across 14 sites in the United States and Germany. Participants receiving 150 milligrams of tolvexamab every four weeks showed a 47 percent reduction in annualized relapse rate compared to placebo, according to the report. Dr. Nathan stated that three patients experienced serious infusion-related reactions, though none were fatal. Arcadia Therapeutics, founded in 2016 by immunologist Dr. Samuel Okafor, plans to submit a Biologics License Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by September 2024. The company's shares rose 22 percent on the Nasdaq following the announcement. Novartis, a competitor developing a similar therapy called ofatamab, said it would continue its own Phase 3 trial in Basel, Switzerland. Funding for the Boston trial, totaling $48 million, was provided jointly by the National Institutes of Health and Arcadia Therapeutics. Dr. Nathan is scheduled to present the full dataset at the American Academy of Neurology annual meeting in Denver, Colorado, on April 9, 2024. Patient advocacy group the National MS Society welcomed the results, calling them "a meaningful step forward" for the estimated 1 million Americans living with multiple sclerosis.

Everton had taken a surprise lead in the 23rd minute through striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who converted a penalty after James Tarkowski was fouled inside the box. City manager Pep Guardiola responded by introducing midfielder Mateo Kovacic at halftime, a substitution that shifted momentum. Julian Alvarez equalized in the 68th minute with a low strike from the edge of the area.

"We showed character today," Guardiola told reporters after the match at the Etihad Stadium. "Erling's movement in the box is unmatched."

Everton manager Sean Dyche said his side deserved at least a draw, citing missed chances by Abdoulaye Doucouré in the second half. The result lifts Manchester City to second place in the Premier League table, three points behind leaders Liverpool, while Everton remains 17th after the defeat.

The two clubs will meet again on February 10, 2024, at Goodison Park in the reverse fixture. City's next match comes on Tuesday against RB Leipzig in the UEFA Champions League at the Etihad Stadium.

Voltrek Gear, headquartered in Bend, Oregon, has launched the Ridgeline 3400 hydration backpack, a 34-liter pack built for multi-day alpine trekking. Priced at $189.99, the Ridgeline 3400 is available now on Voltrek's website and at REI stores across the Pacific Northwest starting October 14, 2024. The pack features a welded TPU reservoir sleeve, magnesium-alloy frame stays, and a removable rain fly rated for 3,000mm of waterproofing. Voltrek Gear was founded in 2016 by former mountaineer Elena Kowalski, who serves as the company's Chief Product Officer and led the two-year development effort behind the Ridgeline line. "We tested this pack on Mount Hood and in the Wallowa Mountains before we were satisfied," Kowalski said in a statement released Tuesday. Each Ridgeline 3400 ships with a lifetime warranty against manufacturing defects and a detachable 2-liter Hydrapak bladder. The backpack weighs 1.8 kilograms and comes in three colorways: Basalt Gray, Cascade Green, and Ember Orange. Voltrek Gear reports that roughly 12,000 units have already been pre-ordered ahead of the official launch. Competing brand Osprey Packs, based in Cortez, Colorado, released a similar 32-liter model, the Levitate 32, in March 2024, intensifying competition in the backcountry hydration segment. Customers who purchase the Ridgeline 3400 before November 1, 2024 will receive a free pair of Voltrek trekking poles, a $45 value. This is condition: new, and the product ships from Voltrek's distribution center in Bend within two business days of order confirmation.

DENVER, Colorado — Trailhead Energy Corp. announced Tuesday that it has acquired Summit Ridge Solar LLC, a privately held solar developer based in Boulder, Colorado, for $412 million in cash and stock. The deal, disclosed on October 14, 2025, marks Trailhead's largest acquisition since the company was founded in 2011 by chief executive officer Marcus Whitfield.

Under the terms of the agreement, Trailhead will pay $260 million in cash and issue approximately 3.8 million shares of common stock to Summit Ridge's shareholders, according to a regulatory filing submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission. Summit Ridge, led by founder and president Elena Cortez, operates solar farms across Colorado, Utah, and New Mexico with a combined capacity of 1.2 gigawatts.

"This acquisition strengthens our renewable portfolio and positions Trailhead as a top-five solar operator in the Mountain West," Whitfield said during a call with investors on Wednesday. Analysts at Cascade Capital Partners estimated the transaction could boost Trailhead's annual revenue by 18 percent.

The deal is expected to close by December 1, 2025, pending regulatory approval. Cortez will join Trailhead's board of directors and assume the newly created role of chief sustainability officer, effective upon closing. Trailhead shares rose 6.4 percent to $57.30 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while trading volume topped 2.3 million shares, well above the daily average of 850,000.

Trailhead Energy Corp., headquartered in Denver, employs roughly 4,300 people and reported revenue of $2.1 billion last year.

Chicago-based Meridian Foods Corp. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Prairie Snack Co., a privately held maker of kettle-cooked chips based in Madison, Wisconsin, for $340 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by January 15, 2025, will make Prairie Snack a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Foods. CEO Daniel Whitfield said the acquisition strengthens Meridian's position against rival Golden Valley Snacks Inc. in the competitive salty-snacks market. "Prairie Snack has built a loyal following over 22 years, and this combination lets us scale their production nationally," Whitfield said during a conference call with analysts. Prairie Snack founder and outgoing chief executive Laura Bennett will step down from her role effective February 1, 2025, but will remain as a strategic advisor for six months. Bennett founded Prairie Snack Co. in 2002 in a small facility outside Madison and grew annual revenue to $180 million by 2023. Meridian Foods, which employs roughly 4,200 people across facilities in Illinois, Ohio, and Texas, plans to retain all 310 Prairie Snack employees at the Madison plant. Shares of Meridian Foods rose 6.4 percent to $88.12 on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, while analysts at Baird raised their price target to $95. The transaction is subject to customary regulatory approval, including review by the Federal Trade Commission. Meridian expects the deal to add approximately $0.35 per share to earnings within the first full year after closing.

MANCHESTER, England — October 14, 2024. Manchester United striker Rasmus Hojlund scored twice as United beat Brentford 3-1 at Old Trafford on Saturday, lifting the club to fifth place in the Premier League table. Hojlund opened the scoring in the 23rd minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Mark Flekken, then doubled his tally in the 61st minute after a through ball from midfielder Kobbie Mainoo. Bryan Mbeumo pulled one back for Brentford in the 74th minute, but substitute Alejandro Garnacho sealed the win with a late strike in stoppage time. Manager Erik ten Hag praised the team's resilience after the match, telling reporters at a press conference, "We showed character today, and Rasmus is growing into his role." The victory extended United's unbeaten run to four matches ahead of a Champions League clash against Bayern Munich on October 29 at Allianz Arena in Munich. Brentford manager Thomas Frank said his side would regroup before hosting Liverpool on October 21 at the Gtech Community Stadium. The match drew a crowd of 73,547, one of the largest attendances at Old Trafford this season. United's win moved them to 15 points from eight matches, three points behind fourth-placed Newcastle United. Hojlund, a 21-year-old Danish international who joined United from Atalanta in 2023 for a reported £64 million, has now scored five goals in his last six appearances.

Pixelbook Labs launched the Aria Slate 2 tablet on September 12, 2024, at a press event in Austin, Texas, and after three weeks of daily use, it earns a cautious recommendation. Priced at $649, the Aria Slate 2 pairs a 11-inch OLED display with Qualcomm's Snapdragon X2 Elite chip, and Pixelbook Labs claims 14 hours of battery life. In my testing at a downtown Austin coffee shop, I got closer to 11 hours with the screen at 70 percent brightness. CEO Rania Kessler said during the launch that the company sold 40,000 units in the first week, a figure the firm shared with reporters from The Verge and Engadget. The build quality feels premium, with a machined aluminum chassis, but the software still shows rough edges; the custom OS, called PixelOS 3, crashed twice during a video call over Wi-Fi. Pixelbook Labs, headquartered in San Jose, California, was founded in 2019 by Rania Kessler and Tomás Vidal, and the company acquired the audio startup EchoWave for $28 million in March 2023 to bring better speakers to its lineup. That acquisition shows here: the quad speakers, tuned by EchoWave engineers, are the best I've heard on a tablet under $700. Competitor Samsung's Galaxy Tab S10, released earlier in 2024, still beats it on app optimization. Storage options top out at 512GB, and there's no expandable memory, which feels stingy at this price. If Pixelbook Labs pushes a software update to fix the crashing, the Aria Slate 2 could become the best midrange tablet of 2024. For now, it's a promising but flawed second act.

The Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change announced on Tuesday, June 11, 2024, that it will allocate 2.3 billion rupees to fund flood-mitigation infrastructure along the Brahmaputra River in Assam. Minister Kiran Rijiju, speaking at a press briefing in New Delhi, said the funds will support the construction of 14 new embankments and a early-warning sensor network to be completed by March 2026. The announcement follows the April 2024 floods that displaced roughly 45,000 residents in Dibrugarh district and damaged three major highways. Rijiju stated, "We cannot allow another monsoon season to devastate these communities without adequate protection," during remarks to reporters from Reuters and the Press Trust of India. The National Disaster Management Authority, led by Director General Anil Kumar Sharma, will oversee implementation alongside the Assam State Disaster Management Authority. Contractor Larsen & Toubro Limited, headquartered in Mumbai, has been selected to build the embankments under a contract worth 890 million rupees, with work expected to begin on July 1, 2024. Opposition lawmaker Priya Devi Barman criticized the timeline as insufficient, arguing that 60 percent of the affected villages will remain vulnerable through at least one more monsoon cycle. The ministry confirmed that a follow-up review will be conducted in December 2024 to assess progress and reallocate funds if necessary. Officials emphasized that this initiative forms part of a broader 12 billion rupee national flood-resilience program launched in 2022.
