input: Sonos launched the Ace headphones on June 5, 2024, pricing the over-ear model at $449 and pitching it as a direct competitor to the Bose QuietComfort Ultra. I tested a unit purchased at a Best Buy store in Austin, Texas, over three weeks of daily commuting and travel through Dallas Fort Worth International Airport. The Ace, manufactured by Sonos Inc, headquartered in Santa Barbara, California, uses a custom aluminum driver and supports active noise cancellation rated at roughly 35 decibels of reduction, according to company engineer Priya Nandakumar, who joined Sonos in March 2019 as a senior acoustics designer. Battery life reached about 30 hours in my tests, slightly under the advertised 40-hour figure. A standout feature, TrueCinema, syncs audio with a Sonos Arc soundbar for home theater playback, though it requires a firmware update expected in September 2024. Comfort is excellent for a 320-gram headset, and the case, sold separately for $49, charges the Ace via USB-C. My chief complaint concerns the companion app, which crashed twice on an iPhone 15 running iOS 17.5. Sonos CEO Patrick Spence acknowledged software issues during an earnings call on August 7, 2024, promising a patch within 90 days. Compared with the $429 Bose QuietComfort Ultra, the Ace offers better build quality but weaker noise cancellation. At $449, it is a strong but not flawless debut into personal audio hardware for a company built on speakers.

Pixelbook Labs, a hardware startup based in Austin, Texas, unveiled the Contour X1 laptop on March 4, 2024, and I have spent three weeks putting it through daily work. The Contour X1 costs $1,299 and ships with a 14-inch OLED display, 32GB of RAM, and a 1TB solid-state drive. Founder Renata Osei, who previously worked as a Senior Engineer at Dell Technologies, told me in an interview in Austin that the team built the device to compete directly with the Dell XPS 14 and Apple's MacBook Pro. Battery life is the standout feature: I consistently got 13 hours of mixed use, well above the 9 hours Dell advertises for the XPS 14. The 1080p webcam is merely adequate, and the trackpad occasionally registers phantom clicks, a bug Pixelbook Labs says will be fixed in a firmware update scheduled for April 2024. Performance from the Intel Core Ultra 7 processor was strong in Adobe Premiere export tests, finishing a 10-minute 4K timeline in just under 6 minutes. Pixelbook Labs was founded in 2021 by Renata Osei and Marcus Feld, and the company raised $18 million in Series A funding led by Kestrel Ventures in 2022. At $1,299, the Contour X1 is not cheap, but after three weeks I think it earns the price. It is one of the few Windows laptops I would recommend over a MacBook this year.

MANCHESTER, England, October 14, 2024 — Everton striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored twice as Everton defeated Brighton & Hove Albion 3-1 at Goodison Park on Saturday, lifting the club to eighth place in the Premier League table. Calvert-Lewin opened the scoring in the 23rd minute with a header from a corner delivered by midfielder James Garner, then added a second in the 61st minute after a swift counterattack. Brighton pulled one back through striker Danny Welbeck in the 70th minute, but Everton sealed the win when substitute Beto struck in stoppage time. Everton manager Sean Dyche praised his squad's resilience after the match, telling reporters, "We showed real character today, especially after conceding." Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler admitted his side struggled defensively, saying his team would review the performance before facing Aston Villa next week. Approximately 39,000 fans attended the fixture at Goodison Park, one of the oldest stadiums in English football. The result moves Everton to 12 points from eight matches, while Brighton remain on 11 points. Everton's next match is scheduled for October 21 against Newcastle United at St James' Park. The Premier League confirmed that Saturday's match had no reported incidents of crowd trouble, following increased security measures introduced earlier this season. Calvert-Lewin, who has now scored five goals this season, was named Player of the Match by broadcaster Sky Sports.

BOSTON, MA — March 14, 2024 — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tovorafenib, an oral RAF kinase inhibitor developed by Day One Biopharmaceuticals, in pediatric patients with relapsed low-grade glioma. The trial, led by Dr. Karen Whitfield and presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology meeting in Chicago, enrolled 76 children between ages 2 and 17 across 12 sites in the United States and Canada from June 2021 to September 2023. Among 69 evaluable patients, the objective response rate was 51%, with a median duration of response of 13.8 months. The most common adverse events were elevated creatine kinase levels, seen in 58% of participants, and hair color changes, reported in 41%. Three patients discontinued treatment due to grade 3 hepatotoxicity. Dr. Whitfield stated that the results support tovorafenib as a potential first targeted therapy for this population, which currently relies on chemotherapy regimens largely unchanged since the 1990s. Day One Biopharmaceuticals, headquartered in South San Francisco, California, submitted a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in December 2023, and the agency granted accelerated approval on April 23, 2024, under the brand name Ojemda. The company's chief executive officer, Jeremy Bender, said the approval marks a milestone for children with brain tumors worldwide. Peer-reviewed findings were published in The Lancet Oncology on March 20, 2024. Additional funding was provided by the National Cancer Institute and the Pediatric Brain Tumor Consortium.

Pixel Tab Review: Google's First Real Tablet Bet Since 2018

Mountain View, CA -- August 14, 2024. After a six-year absence from the standalone tablet market, Google returned last week with the Pixel Tab, unveiled by Rick Osterloh, Google's Senior Vice President of Devices and Services, at a press event held at the Shoreline Amphitheatre. The device, manufactured by Google in partnership with supplier Foxconn, ships with an 11-inch OLED display, a Tensor G4 chipset, and a detachable Charging Speaker Dock included in the $499 base price.

I've spent nine days with the 256GB review unit, and the hardware feels like a genuine successor to the discontinued Pixel Slate. Battery life hit 11 hours of mixed use, and the dock's built-in speaker noticeably improves audio when the tablet sits on a kitchen counter running Android 15.

Google says the Pixel Tab will compete directly with Apple's iPad Air and Samsung's Galaxy Tab S9, both of which remain dominant in the category. Analyst Carolina Milanesi of Creative Strategies noted in a research note dated August 16, 2024, that Google faces an uphill battle given Apple's roughly 30 percent share of global tablet shipments.

One caveat: the Pixel Tab launched only in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom, with a wider rollout to Germany and Japan promised for early 2025. Software support is guaranteed for five years, matching Google's Pixel phone policy. At $499, it undercuts the iPad Air by $100, making it the most aggressive pricing Google has offered in this category.

Overall, it's a strong first step, though I'd wait for the software polish to catch up before recommending it over the Galaxy Tab S9.

input: BOSTON, MA -- April 9, 2024 -- Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital reported promising results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tavaprazole, an experimental compound developed to treat chronic gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh, enrolled 214 adults across three sites in Boston, Chicago, and Denver between June 2022 and November 2023. Participants received either 40 milligrams of tavaprazole daily or a placebo for 12 weeks. According to results published in the Journal of Gastrointestinal Medicine, 68 percent of patients receiving tavaprazole reported significant symptom relief, compared with 31 percent in the placebo group. The most common adverse effects included mild headache and nausea, reported by 9 percent of participants; no serious cardiac events were recorded. Dr. Marsh presented the findings on April 8, 2024, at a Contact.Meet-style scientific symposium hosted by the American Gastroenterological Association in Chicago, where she noted that tavaprazole's novel mechanism, which selectively inhibits the H+/K+-ATPase pump, may offer an alternative for patients unresponsive to existing proton pump inhibitors such as omeprazole. The trial was funded by Merrow Biopharmaceuticals, a subsidiary of Halden Life Sciences headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with additional support of $4.2 million from the National Institutes of Health. Merrow's chief executive, Priya Nandakumar, stated that a Phase 3 trial involving 1,800 patients is planned to begin in early 2025 across sites in the United States and Germany. Regulatory submission to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration is anticipated by late 2026 if Phase 3 results confirm the current safety and efficacy profile.

Denver-based Cascade Robotics Inc. announced on Tuesday that it has acquired Millbrook Sensors LLC, a privately held sensor manufacturer based in Ann Arbor, Michigan, for $142 million in cash. The deal, expected to close by December 15, 2024, will bring Millbrook's roughly 210 employees under Cascade's engineering division. Cascade CEO Renata Ibarra said the acquisition strengthens the company's push into industrial automation, noting that Millbrook's lidar sensors are already used by three of the top five automakers in North America. "This is about accelerating our robotics roadmap by at least two years," Ibarra told reporters during a call from Cascade's headquarters. Millbrook founder and outgoing chief executive, Dr. Samuel Wren, will step down from his post on January 5, 2025, after 14 years leading the company he started in 2010. Wren is expected to join Cascade's advisory board instead. Analysts at Fenwick Capital Partners estimate the deal will boost Cascade's annual revenue by 18 percent, pushing it past $1.3 billion for fiscal 2025. Shares of Cascade Robotics, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker CSCR, rose 6.4 percent to $87.20 following the announcement. Rival firm Talon Dynamics, based in Austin, Texas, declined to comment on whether it had also pursued Millbrook. The transaction still requires clearance from the Federal Trade Commission, which Cascade expects within 60 days.

SUPERIOR COURT OF ALAMEDA COUNTY, DEPARTMENT 12 — On October 3, 2024, Judge Marion T. Ellsworth sentenced Dwayne R. Costigan, 41, to 5 years in state prison after a jury convicted him of grand theft and embezzlement from his former employer, Fairhaven Logistics Inc., a freight company headquartered in Oakland, California. Prosecutor Angela Nunez of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office argued that Costigan, who worked as a warehouse manager for Fairhaven Logistics from March 2019 until his termination in June 2023, diverted approximately $187,000 in company funds into a personal account between January 2022 and May 2023. Costigan was arrested by Oakland Police Department detectives on August 14, 2023, at his residence in San Leandro following a six-month internal audit that flagged irregular shipping invoices. During the trial, which began September 9, 2024, at the René C. Davidson Courthouse, defense attorney Priya Raghunathan claimed her client had been coerced by a since-departed supervisor, Terrence Vail, who left the company in 2023 and has not been located. Fairhaven Logistics CEO Marcus Whitfield declined to comment on pending civil claims but confirmed the company has since implemented new auditing software supplied by LedgerGuard Systems, based in Austin, Texas. Judge Ellsworth ordered Costigan to pay $187,000 in restitution, payable in monthly installments beginning January 2025. Costigan's attorney indicated plans to appeal the sentence to the California Court of Appeal, First Appellate District.

AUSTIN, Texas -- Meridian BioLogics, Inc. announced today that it has acquired Corvant Diagnostics for $340 million in cash, expanding its footprint in molecular testing. The deal, finalized on June 12, 2024, at Meridian's headquarters in Austin, Texas, was confirmed by CEO Rachel Tanaka during a press briefing.

"This acquisition strengthens our pipeline in infectious disease detection," said Tanaka, who has led Meridian since 2019. Corvant Diagnostics, based in San Diego, California, specializes in rapid PCR assays for detecting influenza and tuberculosis. Corvant was founded in 2011 by Dr. Elena Vasquez, who will join Meridian as Chief Scientific Officer effective July 1, 2024.

Meridian BioLogics, a subsidiary of Halden Pharmaceutical Group, employs roughly 2,300 people across facilities in Texas, North Carolina, and Ireland. The company posted revenue of $1.2 billion in fiscal year 2023, a 14 percent increase over the prior year.

Analysts at Kessler Ridge Capital noted that the acquisition positions Meridian as a stronger competitor to Rovanta Health Systems in the diagnostics market. Shares of Halden Pharmaceutical Group rose 3.5 percent following the announcement on the New York Stock Exchange.

The transaction is expected to close by August 15, 2024, pending regulatory clearance from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission. Meridian plans to retain all 180 Corvant employees and maintain the San Diego facility as a research hub.

For more information, contact Marcus Ohene, Director of Communications, at press@meridianbio.com.

Danville, PA -- Geisinger Health System announced Tuesday that it will acquire Riverside Regional Medical Center, a 210-bed hospital in Newport News, Virginia, for $340 million. The deal, expected to close by March 15, 2025, will expand Geisinger's footprint beyond Pennsylvania for the first time in its 108-year history. CEO Dr. Terrence Wall said the acquisition would bring advanced cardiology and oncology services to underserved communities in southeastern Virginia. "This partnership allows us to deliver Geisinger's value-based care model to nearly 400,000 additional patients," Wall said during a press conference held at Geisinger's headquarters. Riverside Regional's current owner, Sentara Health, has faced financial pressure after reporting a $92 million operating loss in fiscal year 2024. Sentara CEO Marjorie Alston confirmed the sale, stating the funds would help the nonprofit reduce debt and reinvest in its remaining twelve hospitals across Virginia and North Carolina. The transaction still requires approval from the Virginia State Corporation Commission and federal antitrust regulators, who are expected to review the deal over the next four months. Analysts at Moody's Investors Service said the acquisition reflects a broader wave of hospital consolidation as healthcare systems seek scale to offset rising labor costs. Shares of publicly traded hospital operator HCA Healthcare, a competitor in the region, dipped 1.3 percent following the announcement. Geisinger, founded in 1915 by Abigail Geisinger, currently operates thirteen hospitals across Pennsylvania.

Boston, MA -- May 14, 2024. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tovorafenib, an oral RAF inhibitor, in 84 pediatric patients with relapsed low-grade glioma. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh and published in The Lancet Oncology, reported an overall response rate of 67 percent among participants aged 2 to 18 treated between January 2022 and September 2023 at 12 sites across the United States and Canada. Tumor shrinkage of at least 50 percent was observed in 41 children, while grade 3 adverse events, primarily anemia and elevated liver enzymes, occurred in 9 percent of the cohort. Day One Biopharmaceuticals, headquartered in Brentwood, California, funded the trial and plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by early 2025. Dr. Marsh noted that tovorafenib's selectivity for BRAF-altered tumors distinguishes it from earlier pan-RAF compounds such as dabrafenib. The trial excluded patients with prior exposure to type II RAF inhibitors and those with uncontrolled seizure disorders. Co-investigator Dr. Rajiv Patel of the Hospital for Sick Children in Toronto presented supplementary data at the American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting on June 2, 2024, highlighting durable responses lasting a median of 16.6 months. Day One's stock rose 11 percent following the presentation. The company stated it will pursue accelerated approval and expects a regulatory decision within six months of submission, potentially making tovorafenib the first targeted therapy approved specifically for pediatric low-grade glioma in the United States.

event: American Society of Clinical Oncology annual meeting

1/ Big news out of Austin: Solstice Robotics announced this morning it has acquired Denton-based sensor startup Ferrous Vision for $42 million in cash. Deal closed Tuesday, June 11, 2024. Ferrous Vision's 38 employees will join Solstice's hardware division. #robotics

2/ Solstice CEO Priya Nandakumar told reporters at the company's East 6th Street headquarters that Ferrous Vision's LIDAR chips will be integrated into the SR-9 warehouse robot within a year. "This is the biggest bet we've made since founding Solstice in 2017," she said.

3/ Ferrous Vision was founded in 2019 by Marcus Delgado, a former Texas Instruments engineer. Delgado will stay on as VP of Sensor Engineering under the new arrangement, reporting directly to Nandakumar.

4/ Not everyone's thrilled. About 60 gig workers gathered outside Solstice's headquarters on Wednesday to protest automation-driven layoffs at logistics firm Cargill Transport, a major Solstice customer. Organizer Denise Whitfield said three warehouses in Round Rock already cut 90 jobs this year.

5/ Market reaction was mostly positive — Solstice shares rose 7% on the Nasdaq by Tuesday afternoon. Analyst Tom Reyes at Brightline Capital called the acquisition "a smart vertical play."

6/ Solstice will hold a press briefing Thursday, June 13, 2024 in Austin to answer questions about integration plans and possible additional hiring.

DETROIT, Mich. — Feb 14 — Kessler Automotive Group announced Wednesday that it has acquired Bright Path Robotics, a Pittsburgh-based startup specializing in warehouse automation, for $340 million in cash and stock. The deal, finalized at Kessler's headquarters in Detroit, marks the automaker's largest technology acquisition to date.

Kessler CEO Marisol Vance told reporters the acquisition will accelerate the company's push into automated parts distribution. "Bright Path's robotics platform will cut our logistics costs by nearly 18 percent within two years," Vance said during a press briefing attended by roughly 40 journalists.

Bright Path Robotics was founded in 2017 by engineer Devon Okafor, who will join Kessler as Chief Robotics Officer effective March 1. Okafor previously worked at Carnegie Robotics in Pittsburgh before launching his own venture. The company employs 210 people and will retain its Pittsburgh facility as an East Coast engineering hub.

Industry analysts noted the move intensifies competition with rival automaker Halden Motors, which has invested heavily in its own automation subsidiary, Halden Logistics Solutions. Halden spokesperson Priya Chandrasekaran declined to comment on Wednesday's announcement.

Shares of Kessler Automotive Group rose 6 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the news, closing at $87.42. The transaction is expected to close fully by April 30, pending routine regulatory review.

Pixel Watch 3 Review: Google Finally Gets the Basics Right

By Renata Alcazar, Gearline Magazine, September 12, 2024

Google launched the Pixel Watch 3 on September 10, 2024, at a small press event in Mountain View, California, and after two weeks of daily wear I think it is the company's most convincing wearable yet. The 45mm aluminum model I tested costs $399.99 and ships with a redesigned Actua display that hits 2,000 nits of peak brightness, a genuine improvement over the Pixel Watch 2 I reviewed last year for the same publication.

Battery life is the headline fix. Google claims 36 hours in normal mode, and in my testing with the always-on display enabled I consistently got 28 hours, which is still respectable for a watch this thin. The device runs Wear OS 5 and pairs tightly with a Pixel 9 phone, syncing Fitbit data almost instantly.

On the software side, Sundar Pichai, Google's chief executive, mentioned during the launch that the Pixel Watch line has now sold over 3 million units worldwide since its debut in 2022. That is a modest number next to the Apple Watch, still the category leader made by Apple Inc., but it signals real momentum for Google's hardware division, run by Rick Osterloh out of offices in Mountain View.

A notable weak point: the loop band I received began fraying after ten days, and a Google spokesperson told me on September 20, 2024 that replacement bands would ship free of charge to affected customers.

Recommendation: if you already own a Pixel 9 phone, the Pixel Watch 3 is an easy $399.99 upgrade. If you are starting fresh, I would still nudge cautious buyers toward the Apple Watch Series 9 instead.

Fresno, California -- October 14, 2024 -- Valley Fresh Foods Inc., a mid-sized packaged foods company headquartered in Fresno, California, announced today that it has acquired Golden State Snacks LLC, a Modesto-based maker of tortilla chips, for $42 million in cash. The acquisition is expected to close by November 30, 2024, pending regulatory approval.

Under the terms of the deal, Valley Fresh Foods will retain all 210 Golden State Snacks employees at the company's Modesto production facility. Golden State Snacks founder and CEO Marissa Tran will join Valley Fresh Foods as Vice President of Snack Innovation, effective December 1, 2024.

"This acquisition strengthens our portfolio and gives us immediate access to the fast-growing snack category," said Daniel Ortiz, Chief Executive Officer of Valley Fresh Foods, in a statement released from the company's Fresno headquarters. "Marissa and her team have built something special, and we're excited to invest in their growth."

Golden State Snacks was founded in 2015 by Marissa Tran and has grown to generate approximately $18 million in annual revenue, competing directly with Sun Valley Chips, a rival based in Bakersfield. The company distributes its products across 1,200 grocery stores in California, Nevada, and Arizona.

Valley Fresh Foods, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker VFF, reported $310 million in revenue for fiscal year 2023. The company plans to fund the acquisition using existing cash reserves and a $15 million credit line from Pacific Coast Bank.

Shares of Valley Fresh Foods rose 3.2 percent following the announcement.

Duesenfeld GmbH, a battery-recycling firm headquartered in Wendeburg, Germany, announced Tuesday that it has acquired Nordic Cell Recovery AS, a Norwegian competitor based in Trondheim, for 42 million euros. The deal, confirmed by Duesenfeld chief executive Christian Hanisch, is expected to close by December 15, 2024, pending approval from Norwegian regulators. Hanisch said the acquisition would triple Duesenfeld's processing capacity to 60,000 tons of lithium-ion battery material annually, positioning the company to compete more directly with China's GEM Co. and Belgium's Umicore. Nordic Cell Recovery, founded in 2016 by engineer Ingrid Solberg, employs 130 workers and operates a plant in Trondheim that supplies recycled cobalt and nickel to automakers including Volvo Cars. Solberg will join Duesenfeld's board as chief technology officer starting January 6, 2025. Speaking at a press briefing in Wendeburg, Hanisch said the combined company would be renamed Duesenfeld Nordic and would seek a listing on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2026. Analysts at Berenberg Bank said the deal reflects growing pressure on European recyclers to secure raw materials as demand for electric vehicle batteries rises. Shares of Umicore fell 2.3 percent in Brussels trading following the announcement. The European Commission said it would review the transaction under EU competition law but does not expect it to raise antitrust concerns given the fragmented state of the battery-recycling market.

OTTAWA, March 4 — The Department of Fisheries and Oceans Canada announced today that Minister Diane Lebouthillier will implement a new conservation quota for Atlantic mackerel stocks off the coast of Nova Scotia, effective April 1. Under the plan, the total allowable catch will be reduced by 35 percent, from 8,000 metric tons to 5,200 metric tons, following a stock assessment conducted by scientists at the Bedford Institute of Oceanography in Halifax. The decision follows consultations with the Fundy North Fishermen's Association and representatives from the Maritime Fishermen's Union, who met with department officials on February 19 in Moncton, New Brunswick. "We recognize the economic impact on harvesters, but the science is clear that mackerel populations have declined sharply since 2011," Lebouthillier said in a statement released Tuesday. The department will also allocate CAD 12 million in transition funding to affected fishing communities in Digby and Yarmouth, administered through the Atlantic Fisheries Fund. Industry groups have until March 25 to submit written comments before the regulation is finalized under the Fisheries Act. Separately, the department confirmed that a research vessel, the CCGS Hudson, will depart from Dartmouth on March 12 to conduct further surveys of herring populations in the Gulf of St. Lawrence. Officials noted that similar quota reductions in 2022 helped stabilize cod stocks near Newfoundland, and they expect comparable results for mackerel by 2027 if compliance remains high among commercial fleets.

Elena Marchetti (born 14 March 1958 in Trieste, Italy) is an Italian structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques used in earthquake-prone regions across Southern Europe. She earned her degree from the Politecnico di Milano in 1981 and joined Ansaldo Costruzioni as a junior engineer that same year. In 1989 Marchetti left Ansaldo Costruzioni to co-found Marchetti & Rossi Engineering with colleague Paolo Rossi, headquartered in Bologna, Italy. The firm quickly gained recognition after its retrofit of the Basilica di San Petronio following minor structural damage identified in 1991.

In 1997, Marchetti was appointed Chief Structural Engineer at Studio Ingegneria Nervi, a position she held for eleven years. During her tenure, she led the design team for the Ponte della Libertà reconstruction in Venice, completed in 2003 at a cost of 42 million euros. She left Studio Ingegneria Nervi in 2008 to become a professor at the Politecnico di Torino, where she has taught since.

Marchetti received the Gustavo Colonnetti Prize from the Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei in Rome in 2011 for her contributions to seismic safety. She married fellow engineer Marco Fabbri in 1985, and the couple has one son, Luca Fabbri, born in 1990 in Bologna. Marchetti currently resides in Turin and continues to consult for the World Bank on infrastructure resilience projects in Southeast Asia.

MANCHESTER, England — October 14, 2024. Manchester City midfielder Rodrigo Alvarez scored twice as City defeated Aston Villa 3-1 at Etihad Stadium on Saturday, extending their unbeaten Premier League run to nine matches. Alvarez opened the scoring in the 22nd minute with a curling shot from outside the box, then added a second just before halftime after a pass from striker Marcus Thibodeaux. Villa pulled one back through defender Callum Foss in the 61st minute, but midfielder Youssef Benali restored City's two-goal cushion with a penalty in the 78th minute after Villa captain Daniel Reyes was penalized for a handball.

Manager Pep Guardiola praised his squad's discipline after the match, telling reporters at the post-game press conference, "We controlled the tempo for ninety minutes. That is exactly what we asked for." Villa manager Unai Emery acknowledged the defeat, saying his team lost focus after conceding the second goal.

The win keeps Manchester City atop the Premier League table with 24 points from 10 games, three points ahead of second-placed Liverpool. City's next fixture is scheduled for October 21 against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. Attendance at Etihad Stadium was announced at 53,412, and the match generated an estimated £2.1 million in matchday revenue for the club, according to a City spokesperson.

SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, COUNTY OF ALAMEDA

On Tuesday, June 11, 2024, Judge Renata Solis presided over the sentencing hearing of Marcus D. Ferrell, 41, at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, California. Ferrell was convicted on May 2, 2024, of grand theft and embezzlement after prosecutors from the Alameda County District Attorney's Office, led by Deputy District Attorney Priya Nandakumar, proved he diverted $412,000 from his former employer, Westbrook Logistics Inc., a freight company headquartered in Fremont, California, between January 2021 and October 2022.

Judge Solis sentenced Ferrell to four years in state prison and ordered restitution of $412,000 to Westbrook Logistics Inc., payable within 90 days of his release. Defense attorney Callum Reyes argued for probation, citing his client's lack of prior convictions, but the court found the scheme, which involved falsified invoices routed through a shell vendor called Harmon Freight Solutions, too calculated for leniency.

Westbrook Logistics Inc. CEO Denise Applewhite issued a statement thanking the District Attorney's Office and confirming the company has since implemented new auditing controls. Ferrell was taken into custody by Alameda County Sheriff's deputies immediately following the hearing and transported to Santa Rita Jail. His attorney stated an appeal would be filed within 60 days with the California Court of Appeal, First Appellate District.

input: MANCHESTER, England -- Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins scored twice on Saturday to lift his side to a 3-1 win over Everton at Villa Park, moving Villa into fourth place in the Premier League table. Watkins opened the scoring in the 12th minute with a low left-footed finish, then doubled his tally in the 54th minute after a swift counterattack set up by midfielder Youri Tielemans. Everton pulled one back through striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the 63rd minute, but substitute Leon Bailey sealed the win with a close-range header in the 81st minute. Villa manager Unai Emery praised his squad's discipline after the match, telling reporters, "We controlled the tempo for large spells and defended set pieces much better than last week." The victory, watched by a crowd of 41,234, extended Aston Villa's unbeaten home run to eight matches. Everton manager Sean Dyche said his team's slow start cost them dearly, adding that he would review the club's pressing structure before their next fixture against Newcastle United on October 28. Aston Villa will travel to face Tottenham Hotspur on November 4 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. The result lifted Villa to 19 points from ten games, three points behind league leaders Manchester City. Aston Villa's owners, V Sports, have targeted a top-four finish this season after investing heavily in the squad since acquiring the club in 2018.

Ingrid Halvorsen (born 14 March 1957 in Bergen, Norway) is a Norwegian marine biologist known for her research on deep-sea coral ecosystems. She earned her doctorate from the University of Bergen in 1984 and joined the Institute of Marine Research in Tromsø the following year as a Research Scientist. In 1991 Halvorsen was appointed Head of Marine Ecology at the same institute, a position she held for eleven years. Her 1996 monograph, The Silent Reefs, documented previously uncatalogued coral formations off the Lofoten archipelago and became a foundational text in cold-water reef studies. In 2003 she left Tromsø to become Professor of Oceanography at the University of Oslo, where she established the Nordic Deep Sea Research Center with funding of 42 million Norwegian kroner from the Research Council of Norway. Halvorsen married fellow oceanographer Johan Fredriksen in 1989; the couple had two children, Kari and Aksel. In 2011 she received the Nansen Award from the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters in Oslo for her contributions to marine ecology. She retired from active fieldwork in 2019 but continues to serve as an emeritus advisor to the Norwegian Environment Agency. Colleagues describe her meticulous cataloguing methods as having reshaped Scandinavian marine science, and in 2022 the research vessel Ingrid Halvorsen was launched in her honor by the Institute of Marine Research, continuing her legacy in Arctic and North Atlantic exploration.

input: The Ministry of Transport announced on Tuesday, March 11, 2025, that it will invest 240 million euros to upgrade rail infrastructure along the coastal corridor between Porto and Lisbon. Minister Helena Cardoso confirmed the funding at a press briefing held at the Ministry headquarters in Lisbon, Portugal. The initiative, named Corredor Atlântico, will be carried out by Infraestruturas de Portugal in partnership with the construction firm Mota-Engil. Work is scheduled to begin on April 7, 2025, and is expected to reduce travel time between the two cities by 25 percent once completed. Minister Cardoso stated that the project will create approximately 3,200 jobs over the next three years and will be financed partly through a 90 million euro grant from the European Investment Bank. Secretary of State João Ferreira, who oversees rail policy, will meet with union representatives from the Federação Nacional dos Sindicatos dos Trabalhadores in Coimbra on March 20, 2025, to discuss labor conditions during construction. Opposition lawmaker Rita Sampaio criticized the announcement, calling the budget insufficient given that similar projects in Spain received 400 million euros last year. The Ministry expects the first phase, covering the Aveiro to Coimbra segment, to be completed by December 2027. Officials noted that Infraestruturas de Portugal previously completed the Norte Line renovation in 2022 without major delays.

DETROIT, Mich. — Nov 14, 2023 — Ferrand Motors Inc., the Detroit-based automaker, announced Tuesday that it will acquire Bright Volt Systems, a battery technology startup headquartered in Austin, Texas, for $740 million in cash and stock. The deal, expected to close by Feb 2024, marks Ferrand Motors' largest acquisition since its founding by industrialist Walter Ferrand in 1958.

Under the agreement, Ferrand Motors will pay $520 million in cash and issue $220 million in newly created shares to Bright Volt Systems' shareholders. Bright Volt Systems, founded in 2016 by engineer Priya Nandan, employs about 340 people and holds 62 patents related to solid-state battery chemistry using lithium and cobalt compounds.

CEO Marcus Whitfield told reporters at a press briefing in Detroit that the acquisition would let Ferrand Motors cut battery costs by 18 percent within three years. "This positions us directly against Tesla and Rivian in the next-generation EV race," Whitfield said.

Priya Nandan, who will join Ferrand Motors as Chief Technology Officer effective Jan 2, 2024, said the merger would accelerate commercialization of her team's research. Shares of Ferrand Motors rose 4.3 percent on the New York Stock Exchange following the announcement, closing at $87.62.

Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners called the deal a strong strategic move, noting that Bright Volt Systems had previously supplied battery cells to Lucid Motors. Ferrand Motors expects the transaction to add $310 million in annual revenue by 2026.

Marguerite Okafor (born 14 March 1958 in Enugu, Nigeria) is a Nigerian-British structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-resistant design in West African construction. She earned a degree in Civil Engineering from the University of Lagos in 1980 before moving to London to join Ove Arup & Partners in 1983. At Arup, Okafor rose to the position of Principal Engineer in 1994, working on the retrofit of the Millennium Bridge following its 2000 closure. In 1998 she co-founded Okafor Structural Consultants with her husband, Bayo Okafor, headquartered in Lagos, Nigeria, focusing on affordable housing resilient to flooding and earthquakes. The firm was acquired by the multinational engineering group WSP Global in 2011 for an undisclosed sum, after which Okafor served as Regional Director for West Africa until stepping down from that position in 2016. Okafor was elected a Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering in 2005 and received the Prince Philip Medal from the Royal Academy of Engineering in London in 2015 for her contributions to sustainable infrastructure. She has published over 40 papers and lectured at Imperial College London. Okafor and Bayo have two children, Ada and Chidi Okafor, both of whom studied architecture at University College London. She currently resides in Lagos, where she mentors young engineers through the foundation she established in 2018, the Okafor Institute for Resilient Design.

BOSTON, MA -- November 12, 2023. Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tarlibrutide, an investigational oral kinase inhibitor developed by Cambridge-based biotech firm Alcova Therapeutics, in patients with relapsed chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). The study, led by Dr. Priya Nandakumar, enrolled 214 adult patients across 18 sites in the United States and Germany between March 2021 and July 2022. Participants received either 200 milligrams of tarlibrutide daily or placebo for 24 weeks. According to results published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, 61 percent of patients receiving tarlibrutide achieved complete remission, compared with 22 percent in the placebo group. The most common adverse event was Grade 2 neutropenia, reported in 14 percent of treated patients. Dr. Nandakumar stated that the findings support tarlibrutide's potential as a first-line therapy for CLL. Alcova Therapeutics was founded in 2016 by former Genentech scientist Dr. Marcus Reyes and is headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The company announced on November 10, 2023, that it had received $85 million in Series C funding led by Sequoia Capital to support a planned Phase 3 trial beginning in early 2024. Alcova's chief executive, Elena Vasquez, said the company plans to submit a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by late 2025. Competing therapies from Pfizer and AbbVie remain the current standard of care for relapsed CLL patients worldwide.

Pixel Fold 2 Review: Google Finally Gets It Right

Mountain View, California -- On October 3, 2024, Google released the Pixel Fold 2, and after two weeks of daily use, I can say it fixes nearly every complaint I had about the original 2023 model. Priced at $1,799, the device is manufactured by Google in partnership with supplier BOE Technology Group, which provides the flexible OLED panel.

The hinge, redesigned by Google's hardware team under Vice President Rick Osterloh, no longer creases visibly under office lighting. Osterloh announced the launch during a press event at the Shoreline Amphitheatre, calling it "the most durable foldable we've ever shipped." Battery life, long a weak point, now stretches to 14 hours of mixed use thanks to a 5,200 mAh cell.

Competitor Samsung, headquartered in Suwon, South Korea, still holds roughly 61 percent of the foldable market, according to a Counterpoint Research report published September 28, 2024. Google's Pixel line, by contrast, holds just 4 percent, though analyst Maria Kwon of Canalys expects that share to grow after this release.

One caveat: the Pixel Fold 2 does not ship with a charger, continuing a trend Apple started in 2020. Software support runs seven years, matching Google's own Pixel 9 promise announced in August 2024.

At $1,799, this is not a budget purchase, but for anyone who folds their phone into a mini tablet daily, it is currently the best option on the market, edging out the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 6.

SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY, ESSEX COUNTY — On March 14, 2024, Judge Marlene Pruitt sentenced Anthony Vasquez, 41, of Newark, New Jersey, to 7 years in state prison after a jury found him guilty of aggravated assault stemming from an incident outside Rico's Tavern on Bloomfield Avenue on September 2, 2023. Prosecutor Deborah Chen of the Essex County District Attorney's Office argued that Vasquez struck victim Harold Tuttle with a baseball bat during a dispute over a parking spot, leaving Tuttle with a fractured skull. Tuttle, 55, was transported by ambulance to University Hospital in Newark, where he remained in critical condition for nine days before being released on September 11, 2023.

Defense attorney Marcus Feldman had requested leniency, citing Vasquez's lack of prior convictions, but Judge Pruitt rejected the request, stating that the severity of Tuttle's injuries warranted a substantial sentence. Vasquez was formally charged on October 5, 2023, with aggravated assault and possession of a weapon for unlawful purposes.

The trial, held at the Essex County Courthouse in Newark, began on February 20, 2024, and concluded after eight days of testimony. Vasquez's attorney has indicated plans to file an appeal with the Superior Court of New Jersey, Appellate Division, within 45 days. Court records show Vasquez was arrested by the Newark Police Department on September 3, 2023, the day after the alleged attack. Tuttle's family, represented by attorney Renata Kowalski, has also filed a separate civil suit seeking $850,000 in damages.

Case No. RG24-118732

On March 14, 2024, Judge Miriam Castellano presided over the sentencing hearing of Devon T. Ashworth, 41, at the René C. Davidson Courthouse in Oakland, California. Ashworth, formerly a senior accountant at Coastline Freight Logistics Inc., was convicted on February 9, 2024 of embezzlement after prosecutor Angela Reyes of the Alameda County District Attorney's Office proved he diverted $612,400 from company accounts between June 2021 and October 2023.

During trial, witness testimony established that Ashworth transferred the funds to a shell entity, Harborview Consulting LLC, which he secretly controlled. Coastline Freight Logistics Inc., headquartered in San Leandro, California, discovered the discrepancy during an internal audit conducted by KPMG in November 2023.

Judge Castellano sentenced Ashworth to 5 years in state prison and ordered restitution of $612,400 to be paid to Coastline Freight Logistics Inc. Ashworth was taken into custody immediately following the hearing by Alameda County Sheriff's deputies. His attorney, Paul Nakamura, stated he intends to file an appeal within 60 days.

The case, People v. Ashworth, drew attention after Coastline Freight Logistics Inc. laid off 38 employees in January 2024, a move the company attributed partly to the financial losses caused by the embezzlement scheme.

Ingrid Vasilenko (born March 14, 1958, in Odessa, Ukrainian SSR) is a Ukrainian-American structural engineer known for pioneering seismic-retrofit techniques for aging bridges. She emigrated to the United States in 1979 and earned a Ph.D. in Civil Engineering from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign in 1985. Vasilenko joined Halcyon Bridgeworks, headquartered in Denver, Colorado, in 1987, where she rose to Chief Engineer in 1994. During her tenure, she led the retrofit of the Larimer Street Viaduct after a magnitude 5.8 earthquake damaged its support columns in 1998. In 2003, Halcyon Bridgeworks was acquired by Meridian Infrastructure Group for 210 million dollars, and Vasilenko was named Vice President of Structural Innovation the same year. She left Meridian in 2011 to found her own consultancy, Vasilenko Structural Partners, in Boulder, Colorado, with backing from former colleague Tomas Reyes. The firm has since consulted on more than 40 bridge projects across North America. In 2016, Vasilenko received the Fritz Leonhardt Prize from the International Association for Bridge and Structural Engineering in Zurich, Switzerland, for her contributions to earthquake-resilient design. She is married to fellow engineer Daniel Osei, whom she met at a conference in 1991, and the couple has one son, Mikael. Vasilenko currently serves as an adjunct professor at the University of Colorado Boulder and continues to publish widely on infrastructure resilience.

Case No. 24-CV-118842

On Tuesday, June 3, 2025, Judge Rosalind Pham convicted Marcus Delaney, 41, of San Jose, on charges of grand theft and embezzlement following a five-day trial at the Santa Clara County Courthouse. Prosecutor Elena Vasquez, representing the District Attorney's Office, argued that Delaney, while employed as chief financial officer at Trellis Logistics Inc., diverted approximately $2.3 million from company accounts between March 2021 and November 2023 into a shell entity called Harbor Point Holdings.

Delaney was arrested by Santa Clara County Sheriff's deputies on December 9, 2023, at his residence on Willow Glen Avenue after a six-month investigation triggered by an internal audit conducted by KPMG. He was formally charged on January 22, 2024.

Judge Pham sentenced Delaney to eight years in state prison and ordered restitution of $2.3 million to Trellis Logistics Inc. Defense attorney Harold Nguyen stated his client intends to appeal the verdict within thirty days, as permitted under California Penal Code Section 1237.

Trellis Logistics Inc., headquartered in Fremont, California, issued a statement through spokesperson Mei-Lin Cho welcoming the verdict and confirming that new financial controls have been implemented under CFO successor Angela Brooks, who assumed the position on February 14, 2024. The company's CEO, Robert Yang, said the ruling "restores confidence among our shareholders and logistics partners across the Bay Area."

CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Piedmont Regional Bank filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Monday after regulators discovered a $340 million shortfall tied to soured commercial real estate loans, according to a statement released by the North Carolina Office of Financial Regulation.

CEO Dana Whitfield told employees at the company's Charlotte headquarters that the bankruptcy filing was necessary to stabilize operations while the bank restructures roughly $1.2 billion in outstanding debt. Whitfield, who has led Piedmont Regional Bank since March 2019, said no branches would close immediately and that customer deposits remain insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation up to $250,000 per account.

The collapse follows a two-year investigation by federal examiners into lending practices at the bank's commercial division, which was headed by former executive Marcus Ruiz until his resignation last October. Ruiz has not been charged with any crime.

Analysts at Meridian Capital Partners said the bankruptcy could trigger a broader review of regional lenders in the Southeast. "This is the largest failure of a mid-sized bank in the Carolinas since 2011," said Meridian analyst Priya Chandrasekaran in a note to investors Tuesday.

Piedmont Regional Bank, founded in 1987 by brothers Harold and Eugene Pruitt, operates 62 branches across North Carolina and South Carolina and employs about 1,400 people. Shares of the bank's parent company, Piedmont Financial Group, fell 78% in early trading Tuesday on the Nasdaq before being halted.

Regulators said a court hearing on the restructuring plan is scheduled for November 14 in federal bankruptcy court in Charlotte.

organization: North Carolina Office of Financial Regulation

input: MADRID, June 14 — Real Sociedad striker Mikel Oyarzabal scored twice on Saturday as Spain defeated Croatia 3-1 in a friendly at the Santiago Bernabeu, boosting confidence ahead of next week's UEFA Nations League opener. Oyarzabal opened the scoring in the 23rd minute with a low finish past goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic, then doubled Spain's lead in the 41st minute from a Pedri corner. Croatia pulled one back through Ivan Perisic in the 58th minute, but substitute Ferran Torres restored the two-goal cushion in the 76th minute after coming on for Alvaro Morata. Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente praised his squad's discipline, telling reporters, "We controlled the tempo for long stretches, and Mikel's movement in the box was decisive." Croatia manager Zlatko Dalic acknowledged his side's slow start but pointed to improvement after halftime. The match, attended by roughly 62,000 fans, was the first meeting between the two nations since a 2022 World Cup group-stage draw in Qatar. Real Federacion Espanola de Futbol confirmed Spain will next face France in Paris on June 19, while Croatia returns home to Zagreb to prepare for a friendly against Poland. Oyarzabal, who now has 14 international goals, said afterward he was "proud to contribute" but stressed the team's collective effort. The Spanish federation also announced that defender Dani Carvajal, who missed the match with a minor knee issue, is expected to be fit for the France fixture.

BOSTON, MA — March 4, 2024 — Researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital announced results from a phase 2 clinical trial evaluating tolvexib, an experimental oral inhibitor developed by Cascade Therapeutics for patients with treatment-resistant type 2 diabetes. The study, led by Dr. Elena Marsh and published in The New England Journal of Medicine, enrolled 214 participants across sites in Boston, Chicago, and Toronto between June 2022 and September 2023. Patients receiving a 50 milligram daily dose of tolvexib showed a mean reduction in HbA1c levels of 1.8 percent over 24 weeks, compared with 0.6 percent in the placebo group. Approximately 12 percent of participants reported mild gastrointestinal side effects, while no cases of severe hypoglycemia were recorded. Dr. Marsh presented the findings at the American Diabetes Association's annual meeting in San Diego on June 21, 2024. Cascade Therapeutics, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, stated that a phase 3 trial involving 3,000 patients is planned to begin in early 2025, pending approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The company's chief executive officer, Raj Patel, said the drug could become available to patients by 2027 if regulatory milestones are met. Novartis, a competitor developing a similar compound called dapaglinix, has also reported promising early-stage results. Funding for the trial was provided in part by a $14 million grant from the National Institutes of Health. Independent experts, including Dr. Susan Wray of Johns Hopkins University, called the results encouraging but urged caution pending longer-term safety data.

input: The Ontario Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks announced on May 14, 2024 a new regulation restricting industrial phosphorus discharge into Lake Erie. Minister Andrea Whitfield, speaking at a press conference in Toronto, said the rule takes effect January 1, 2025 and will apply to roughly 40 facilities across the province, including the Nexcorp Chemical Plant in Windsor. "This regulation will cut phosphorus loading by an estimated 25 percent within three years," Whitfield said. The ministry's Assistant Deputy Minister, Raj Patel, confirmed that Nexcorp Chemical Plant has until March 31, 2025 to submit a compliance plan or face fines of up to CAD 500,000 per violation. Nexcorp's spokesperson, Lena Marsh, stated the company would comply and had already invested CAD 2.3 million in filtration upgrades at its Windsor facility. Environmental group Great Lakes Watch, led by Executive Director Samuel Okafor, praised the announcement but urged the ministry to extend similar rules to Lake Ontario by 2026. The regulation follows a 2023 report by the University of Guelph documenting a 12 percent rise in algal blooms linked to phosphorus runoff. Premier Doug Ford's office issued a statement supporting the measure, noting that CAD 15 million in funding will be allocated to municipalities for wastewater treatment upgrades starting April 2025. The ministry will hold a public consultation in Windsor on June 20, 2024 to gather feedback from residents and industry stakeholders before finalizing enforcement guidelines.
